en_text: “I first made the newspapers when I was nine years old. I made them in every city across the country, most of them on the first page. I even made them internationally. In them I was black and white, blurred a little, my face turned into my father’s chest, people surrounding us. From then on I was shown on TV, in magazines, in more and more papers, always the same photo. I never wanted any of it, I tried to avoid it, but the option wasn’t mine.
zh_text: 「九歲時，我第一次上報。全國各地的報紙都登了我的消息，大多在頭版。我甚至也上了國外的報紙。照片是黑白的，有點模糊，我的臉靠著父親的胸膛，旁邊圍了很多人。然後我還上了電視、雜誌、其他的報紙，都是同一張照片。我根本不想曝光，我很想躲起來，但我無法選擇。」

en_text: “My dad, well, he made the papers too. He was also on the front pages. There were more photos of him than of me, because he was the one being arrested. I was just along for the ride, trying to fight off the police as they came to take him away. I didn’t know any better. Mum peeled me away from his side as I cried. The police handcuffed him, and I never saw him again until this week. He was my dad, sure, but it was pretty easy to stop loving the guy when it turned out he was never really the man we thought he was. Dad got himself arrested because he had tastes other people didn’t look too kindly on—not even the people of Christchurch.
zh_text: 「再說我爹吧，他也上報了，而且總在頭版。他的照片比我多，因爲他才是被捕的罪犯。我只是在警察要把他帶走時想把他們推開，結果也跟著上報。我不知道發生了什麼事。媽媽把我從爹身邊拉開，我哭了。警察幫他戴上手銬，從此我再也沒見過他，一直到這個星期才再度見面。當然，他是我爹，但當他不是表面上那個人的時候，要放棄對他的愛意其實很容易。爹被逮捕，因爲他的興趣在別人眼中非常不可取——連基督城的居民都無法苟同。」

en_text: “Mum was dead a year later. She took cocktails of poisons and pills to escape the hate and the accusations from the public. That left me with the doctors and psychiatrists to study me. They were curious about me. Everybody was. My dad was a man of blood. He had murdered eleven prostitutes over a period of twenty-five years, and that got some of the good people of Christchurch wondering whether I’d turn out the same way. Dad was so subtle nobody even realized Christchurch had a serial killer. He didn’t advertise the fact, he just did his thing, no fuss, no real mess, sometimes they were found and sometimes they weren’t, and those that weren’t were never reported missing. He was a family man who loved us, who would do everything for us. He never laid a finger on my mother or my sister or me, he worked hard to put food on our table, to provide what he could to make our lives better than his was growing up. The monster inside him never came home, it was left hidden in the darkness with the blood and the flesh of those it killed, but sometimes—at least eleven times that he admitted to—Dad’d go out at night and meet up with that monster. He wasn’t my dad in those moments, he was something else. I never asked what, exactly. In the beginning I couldn’t. In the beginning I wasn’t allowed to see him, then, when I was old enough to make my own decisions, I didn’t want to.
zh_text: 「一年後，媽媽死了。她吞了一大堆毒藥跟藥丸，逃離大衆的恨意和控訴。因此醫生和心理治療師受命來研究我。他們對我很好奇。大家都很好奇。我父親嗜血如命。在二十五年間，他謀害了十一名妓女，因此基督城的一些好人非常好奇我是否也會走上父親的路。爹的手法夠隱密，沒人發現基督城出了連續殺人魔。他沒有四處宣揚，想殺人就去殺，乾淨俐落，有些屍體被發現了，有些沒被發現，沒被發現的那些，也從來沒有人會去報案說她們失蹤了。爹是一個居家男人，很愛我們，爲了我們什麼都願意。他從來不會動手打我媽媽、我姊姊跟我，他辛勤工作，讓我們三餐無虞，讓我們過著比他小時候更好的生活。他心中的怪獸從不跟他回家，它留在黑暗中，陪著那些被殺妓女的血肉，但有時候至少他承認犯下了十一件謀殺案爹會趁著晚上出門，跟怪獸會合。這時候他就不是我爹了，他變成另一種生物。我從沒問到底是什麼。一開始的時候我問不出口。一開始的時候我不能跟他見面，後來，等我年紀夠大，可以做決定的時候，我已經不想跟他見面了。」

en_text: “I was ten years old when the trial began. It was a circus. My mum was still alive, but my sister and I were struggling. Mum was always yelling at us when she was sober, and crying when she was drunk, and whatever of those two states she was in, you always wished it was the other. Soon the pills and the booze took their toll, but not as quick as she wanted, and when they couldn’t finish the job she used a razor blade. I don’t know how long it took for her to bleed out. She might still have been alive when we found her. I held my sister’s hand and we watched her pale body, the yelling and the crying gone now.
zh_text: 「審判在我十歲的時候開始。整個過程吵吵鬧鬧。我媽那時還在，但我跟姊姊的生活很艱。媽媽清醒的時候對我們大吼大叫，喝醉的時候就哭個不停，她清醒的時候我們希望她喝醉，喝醉的時候我們卻希望她清醒。藥物跟酒精很快就要奪走她的性命，但速度卻不如她期望的快，最後她覺得吃藥喝酒還不夠，用剃刀刀片自殺。我不知道要花多久血才會流乾。我們發現她的時候她可能還活著。我握住姊姊的手，一起看著母親蒼白的身體，她再也不吼了，再也不哭了。」

en_text: “My mum’s family wanted nothing to do with us, but my dad’s parents took us in. The kids at school would tease me, they’d beat me up, they’d steal my bag at least once a week and jam it down a toilet somewhere. The psychiatrist came around every few months with his tests and questions. My photo came up in the papers every now and then, always the same one, though the distance between those occurrences started to stretch. I was almost a celebrity. I was also the son of a serial killer—and some of those good Christchurch people thought I would follow in his footsteps.
zh_text: 「母親那邊的親戚跟我們斷絕往來，但爺爺奶奶收留了我們。學校裡其他的學生會戲弄我，把我揍個半死，一個禮拜偷一次我的書包，然後丢到馬桶裡沖掉。心理醫生每隔幾個月就帶來測試跟問題。我的照片依然會上報，總是同一張照片，只是出現的間隔愈來愈長。我都快變成名人了。我也是連續殺人犯的兒子——基督城也住了好人，他們認爲我會跟父親走上同一條路。」

en_text: “My sister, Belinda, she took the direction of Dad’s victims. She was out fucking for money when she was fourteen. By sixteen she was an addict; her tastes ran to the liquids that could be scored cheap and injected into her veins. By nineteen she was dead. I was the last of my family—Dad’s monster took them all away.
zh_text: 「我的姊姊貝琳達則選了跟那些被害人一樣的路。十四歲她就出去賣身賺錢。不到十六歲就染上毒癮；她偏好能從非法管道便宜買進又能注射到靜脈中的液體。她不到十九歲就死了。我家只剩我一個——爹的怪獸把大家都帶走了。」

en_text: “Of course little Eddie grew up, I have my own family now. A wife. A child. I told my wife who I was not long after we met. It frightened her in the beginning. Thankfully she got to know me. She saw I had no monsters.
zh_text: 「不過小艾迪還是長大了，我成立了自己的家庭。妻子，和小孩。跟妻子認識不久，我就告诉她我是誰。一開始的時候她嚇到了，還好，她仍願意認識我。她看得到我沒有怪獸。」

en_text: “There are those who think what my dad had was a gene, that he’s passed it on to me. There are people who think that I’m destined to be a man of blood too,” I say, and I look at the blood soaking into the upholstery from the woman slumped in the passenger seat, “that the same blood runs through both of us. They’re wrong,” I say, and I take the car up to sixty kilometers an hour and drive straight into the wall.
zh_text: 「有些人認爲我父親的毛病在基因裡，也會遺傳給我。有些人認爲我也一定會變成嗜血之人，」我說，看著癱在副駕駛座上的女人鮮血直流，滲進了座椅裡，「同樣的血流在我們的身体面。他們錯了。」我把車子加速到時速六十公里，直接對著那面牆撞過去。

en_text: The alarm clock dragging me into the Friday morning before the Christmas break sounds like laser fire from an old sci-fi movie, the kind where the special effects budget runs the production company up about a hundred bucks. I manage to open my eyes about halfway. I feel like I have a hangover even though I haven’t had a drink in ages. I reach out and shut off the alarm and am almost asleep when Jodie pushes me in the back. Hopefully this year Santa will bring me an alarm clock that doesn’t make any noise.
zh_text: 耶誕節假期來臨前的那個星期五早上，叫醒我的鬧鈴聲宛若古早科幻電影中的雷射光束，一打就會讓製片公司的特效預算增加好幾百塊錢那種。我的眼皮好不容易掀開了一半，宿醉的感覺揮之不去，可有好一陣子我滴酒不沾了。伸手按掉鬧鐘，差點又隨入夢鄉，這時茱蒂從背後推推我。希望今年耶誕老公給我一個不會發出聲音的鬧鐘當作禮物。

en_text: “You have to get up,” she says.
zh_text: 茱蒂說：「你該起床了。」

en_text: It takes a few seconds to focus on her words, and I let them slide with me toward the dark hole of sleep. “I don’t want to,” I hear myself saying.
zh_text: 過了幾秒，我才注意到她說了什麼，她的話便這麼跟著我流向黑甜鄉。「我不想起床。」我聽見自己說。

en_text: “You have to. It’s your job to get up and then drag me out of bed.”
zh_text: 「你一定要先起來，然後把我拖下床。」

en_text: “I thought it was your turn to drag me out.” I roll over to face her. The sun is bright behind the curtains, beams of light shining onto the ceiling. I close my eyes so I don’t have to see them. I squeeze them tight and pretend it’s nighttime all over again. “Five more minutes. I promise.”
zh_text: 「輪到妳把我拖下床吧。」我翻身對著她。窗簾後的陽光璀璨，一道道光線照向天花板。我閉上眼睛，就看不見陽光。我緊閉雙眼，假裝又是晚上了。「再五分鐘，然後我保證我一定起床。」

en_text: “That’s what you said five minutes ago when you turned it off the first time.”
zh_text: 「五分鐘前你第一次把鬧鐘按掉的時候也這麼說。」

en_text: “There was a first time?”
zh_text: 「第一次？有第一次？」

en_text: “Come on. It’s Friday. We’ve got the whole weekend ahead of us.” “It’s Christmas,” I say. “We’ve got two weeks ahead of us.”
zh_text: 「快點啦，星期五了。馬上可以休息整個周末。」「耶誕節到了，」我說，「可以休息整整兩個星期。」

en_text: “But not yet,” she reminds me, and she pushes me again.
zh_text: 「還沒到。」她提醒我，然後又開始推我。

en_text: I sit on the edge of the bed and yawn for ten seconds before grabbing her hands and trying to drag her out as well, not wanting to go through this nightmare of waking up alone. She hides under the sheets and starts laughing. Sam comes into the room and starts laughing too.
zh_text: 我坐在床沿打了十秒鐘的哈欠，才抓住她的手把她拉下床，我不要一個人面對起床的噩夢。她躲在床單下吃吃笑了起來。小珊跑進我們的房間，也跟著笑了。

en_text: “Mummy’s a ghost,” she says, and jumps on top of her.
zh_text: 「媽媽變成鬼了。」說完，她跳到茱蒂身上。

en_text: From beneath the sheet comes an “oomph,” then more laughing. I leave them to it and go and take a shower, the hot water bringing me fully around. I’m finished and halfway through shaving when Jodie comes in and climbs into the shower behind me.
zh_text: 茱蒂在床單下「噢」了一聲，又笑了起來。我丢下她們兩人走進浴室，沖在身上的熱水讓我完全清醒了。洗過澡後鬍子刮到一半，茱蒂也進了淋浴間，站在我身後。

en_text: “Just four more days of work,” she says, then yawns.
zh_text: 「再工作幾天就好了。」她打了個哈欠。

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text:
“It’s almost the weekend. Then three more days. Not even that. The last day is always a short one.”
“Sounds like you can add.” “It’s an occupational bonus.”
zh_text:
「周末馬上就到，然後再上三天班。其實不到三天，最後一天大家都會提早下班。」「妳的數學還不錯嘛。」
「職業病。」

en_text: The occupational bonus comes about from the fact Jodie is an accountant. Being married to an accountant isn’t the end of the world, but that’s probably because I’m an accountant too. It is, of course, how we met. Accountants are the punch line of a thousand jokes, and our relationship might contribute to those stereotypes—I don’t know.
zh_text: 茱蒂是會計師，所以對數字特別敏感。一般人都覺得跟會計師結婚等於世界末日，沒那麼糟，或者因爲我也是會計師吧。我們怎麼認識的，可想而知。有關會計師的笑話滿坑滿谷，我跟茱蒂結婚，或许也符合别人眼中刻板的印象吧——天曉得。

en_text: Jodie turns on the small bathroom radio which is styled as a penguin. She twists its flipper until she finds a station with something decent to listen to, then its other flipper to increase the volume. She sings along to a Paul Simon song about fifty ways to leave your lover, and the accountant in me wonders how he came to that number, how many he tried out. My dad had his own ways of leaving his lovers—and I’m pretty sure they’re ways that Paul Simon—Slit her wrists, Chris—never factored in. Jodie doesn’t know all the words and fills in the blanks with loud humming.
zh_text: 浴室裡有台企鵝外型的小收音機，茱蒂按下了開關，轉到聽起來還不錯的電台，然後放大了音量。她跟著保羅·賽門的歌聲，唱出離開愛人的五十種方法，我心中的會計師不解，他從哪裡算出這個數字，他自己又試過了多少種。我爸有他獨到的方法來離開愛人——保羅·賽門肯定沒算進去——切開她腕上的動脈，克里斯。茱蒂記不住所有的歌詞，有些地方就大聲哼哼過去。

en_text: I get dressed and head out to the living room. Toys and schoolbooks are scattered across the floor and the TV is going, gay-looking cartoon characters dancing across the screen. Sam is finishing off her homework while watching the TV, developing the whole multitasking skill at the tender age where homework is done mostly with crayons and markers—all kinds of colorful things that make all kinds of colorful messes. The living room is small, especially with the Christmas tree taking up one whole corner. The entire house is getting too cramped, which is why we’re buying a new one. Today is Sam’s last day of school until the end of January and she’s acting like a kid who just discovered caffeine.
zh_text: 穿好衣服後，我走進客廳。地板上亂七八糟丢了玩具跟課本，電視開著，快樂的卡通人物在螢幕上跳舞。小珊邊看電視邊寫功課，小小年紀就懂得一心多用，不過她的作業多半只用到蠟筆和不織布一五彩繽紛的材料，製造出五彩繽紛的混亂。客廳原本就小，現在又被耶誕樹佔滿了一個角落。家裡太擁擠了，所以我們也打算買新房子。今天小珊再上一天課，就可以放假放到月底，她亢奮得要命，表現得像第一次嚐到咖啡因的孩子。

en_text: I open up the curtains and sunlight pours into the living room and the kitchen, bouncing off every metal surface and making the sun appear to be about as far away as my next-door neighbor. The poplar trees lining the street have been defeated by the heat, the burned leaves drooping, front lawns turning crispy brown as the sun beats down on it all. The air-conditioning is working overtime, separating the outside world from the inside by a dozen degrees. Sam’s holidays kick in in about seven hours and her excitement levels are high and my stress levels are high and Jodie has high levels of both. I’m pretty sure the house has a poltergeist living in it; it comes through at night and does its best to make sure there are no straight lines anywhere.
zh_text: 拉開窗簾，陽光湧入客廳和廚房，凡是金屬的表面都閃閃發亮，太陽似乎離我們很近，就跟隔壁的鄰居一樣。街旁的一排白楊樹在熱力下奄奄一息，囇焦的葉子垂下來，在陽光籠罩下，前面的草地也轉成鮮明的褐色。冷氣開太久了，裡面跟外面差了十幾度。再過七個小時，小珊就開始放假，她非常興奮，而我非常緊張，茱蒂則是既興奮又緊張。我們家一定住了頑皮鬼；半夜跑出來使盡全力把家裡搞得天翻地覆。

en_text: I get the kitchen smelling of coffee. Our kitchen is full of modern appliances, most of them were in style back in the fifties and are back in style now, lots of stainless steel and curves everywhere. I pour Sam a bowl of cereal and she works her way through it, and I’m on my second piece of toast when Jodie comes down the hallway into the dining room. Her dark hair hanging around her shoulders is still slightly damp and her skin smells of body wash. She leans in, kisses me on the cheek, and steals the rest of my toast.
zh_text: 我讓廚房裡充滿了咖啡香。我家的廚房放滿了現代化設備，大多是五〇年代的風格，現在又流行回來了，放眼望去都是不鏽鋼和曲線。我幫小珊倒了一碗穀片，她一口一口吃起來，茱蒂穿過走廊來到餐廳時，我已經在吃第二片吐司了。她垂在肩上的黑髮仍然微濕，肌膚散發出沐浴乳的味道。她靠過來親了我的臉頰，然後把吃到一半的吐司拿走。

en_text: “Payment for the kiss,” she whispers, and winks at me.
zh_text: 「親一下，换吐司。」她輕聲說，對我眨了一下眼睛。

en_text: “I should have made you pancakes. They’d have cost you more.”
zh_text: 「我該幫妳煎幾塊鬆餅，交换的代價比較高。」

en_text: Our cat, Mogo, gets under Jodie’s feet before jumping up on the table and staring at me. Mogo is a tabby with way too much personality and nowhere near enough patience. I sometimes think he has similar thoughts to what my dad must have had all those years ago. He never eats when I feed him, and he always waits for Jodie to take care of him. He never hangs around me or wants me to pat him either—but cats never approach me—there’s something about me that they don’t like. Dogs too.
zh_text: 我們的貓咪魔菇走到茱蒂腳邊，然後跳上餐桌盯著我看。魔菇是隻虎斑貓，太有個性又太沒耐心。有時候我覺得，他腦袋瓜裡的東西或許很像多年前我爸一定會想到的事情。我餵他的時候他絕對不吃，一定要等茱蒂來照顧他。他從不在我腳邊轉，也不要我摸他；不過貓咪都不會靠近我，我身上有種牠們不喜歡的氣息。狗也一樣。

en_text: We finish up breakfast and get our gear together. Jodie has her briefcase, Sam her backpack, I have a satchel, and it’s time to go. It’s eight thirty and the Paul Simon song is stuck in my head and heading outside is like walking into a wall of heat. It’s Jodie’s turn to drop Sam at school. There are kisses all around and hugs, then car doors closing and engines turning over and we leave in different directions. The inside of my car is an oven. Neighbors wave while getting their own kids off to school, others out walking before the day gets too hot, some working in the garden. The houses in the neighborhood have recycling bins parked out front, the week’s trash all ready to be picked up and emptied, green bins with yellow lids lining the streets. On the way into town I pass vans on the side of the road with trailers—people in collapsible chairs reading magazines while selling Christmas trees and Christmas lilies.
zh_text: 吃完早餐，拿好我們的裝備：茱蒂的公事包，小珊的背包，我的側背包，该出門了。早上八點三分，保羅·賽門的歌聲還在我腦海中縈繞，走到外面彷彿撞上了一堵熱氣構成的牆。今天換茱蒂送小珊上學。三人親吻擁抱，然後車門關上，引擎開始作響，兩台車駛往不同的方向。車子裡熱得跟烤箱一樣。送小孩上學的鄰居對我揮揮手，有人趕在氣溫變得太熱前出來散步，有人則在整理花園。這一區的房子前面都擺了公家的資源回收箱，本周的垃圾已經收走清乾淨了，街邊有一整排黃色蓋子的綠色垃圾桶。在前往市區的路上，我看到路邊停了加掛拖車的貨車，賣耶誕樹和百合花的攤販坐在折疊椅上讀雜誌。

en_text: The central city is bordered away from the suburbs by four long avenues creating a giant box, within it a network of parallel streets made up in a checkerboard style, the buildings planted among them blending into one of two types—ugly ones built a hundred years ago, and slightly less ugly ones built in the years since. Most of the scenery could be picked up and spliced into a Sherlock Holmes novel without anybody noticing much difference, except for Holmes himself, who would wonder why Baker Street had suddenly turned from a loitering ground for pickpockets and heroin addicts to one of gang members and glue sniffers.
zh_text: 四條大街構成巨大的方格，隔開市區和郊區，方格內彼此平行的街道交錯成棋盤的樣子，插在棋盤中的建築物分成兩種——百年前建造的醜陋房屋，另一類年代沒那嬮久遠也沒那嬮醜。隨便抽一處的景色放到福爾摩斯的小說裡，除了福爾摩斯外，不會有人注意到明顯的差別，而福爾摩斯可能摸不著頭緒，不知道貝克街上徘徊不去的扒手怎麼突然變成幫派分子，吸海洛英的毒蟲則改吸強力膠了。

en_text: The drive-time routines are slipping out of whack as the city crawls toward Christmas, the traffic is thicker than yesterday, but not as thick as it will be tomorrow. There are a few early-morning—or perhaps ultra-late-night—hookers on the corners in town; their lifeless eyes follow me as I drive past, fake smiles on their faces, the makeup smudged and worn after a long night, their clothes short and scented with exhaust fumes and spent exhaustion. I’ve never seen anybody pull over and pick one up at this time of the morning—it would be like screwing something out of Dawn of the Dead. I wonder if they take the holidays off, whether Christmas is a merry time for them, whether they go home and slip into Santa hats and listen to carols and put up decorations.
zh_text: 耶誕節的腳步近了，在路上開車的慣例也變了，今天的路況比昨天更塞，但明天還會比今天更嚴重。街角站了幾個早起（抑或夜班還沒結束）的流鶯；車子開過她們旁邊時，無神的眼睛牢牢盯著我，臉上掛著不由衷的笑容，長長的一夜過去，妝容早已髒污敗壞，身上短短的衣服沾滿了汽車的廢氣。我從沒看過早上這時候有人停車召妓——應該會像找恐怖電影《活人生吃》裡的角色來打一炮。不知道她們會不會放假，不知道在她們心目中耶誕節是不是快樂時光，不知道她們會不會回家戴上耶誕老公公的帽子，聽耶誕歌曲和在家裡擺上耶誕節的裝飾。

en_text: I turn on the radio and have to flick through four stations until I can find a pair of DJs who aren’t laughing at the tired old sex jokes DJs have been making for the last twenty years. The station I settle on mentions it’s already twenty-seven degrees and is only going to get hotter; reminds us all that water restrictions are in place, that global warming is coming, and that Christmas is only seven days away and counting.
zh_text: 我轉開收音機，换了好幾個電台，才找到一對主持人，不會重複過去二十年來廣播主持人琅琅上口的可厭黃色笑話。最後選定的電台說已經二十七度了，溫度還會繼續升高；提醒聽衆限水措施已經開始，全球暖化降臨，再過七天就是耶誕節。

en_text: I strike nearly every red light on the way into town, people sitting in their cars cooking as the temperature rises. It takes me twenty-five minutes to get to the parking building, having survived all the Christchurch Christmas road rage. I drive up to the eighth floor, negotiating the narrow ramps as they wind upward between floors, some drivers taking them more carefully than I do, others treating it as a racecourse. I take the stairs down, breaking into a sweat, and pass a homeless man named Henry at the base of the stairs who tells me I’m a saint after I give him a couple of bucks. Henry has a Bible in his hand so maybe he really does have a keen eye for that kind of thing, or maybe it’s coming from the bottle of cheap vodka in his other hand. From there it’s only a two-minute walk to work. The sidewalks are full of grim-looking people all resigned to the day ahead, in office buildings, retail outlets, or sleeping under park benches. Some of them are waiting for Christmas, some of them excited, some of them probably not even aware of its approach. The sun keeps climbing. There is blue sky in every direction and the overwhelming sense we won’t be seeing any more clouds this year.
zh_text: 在進城的路上，幾乎每個路口都碰到紅燈，溫度不斷上升，駕駛人坐在車子裡烤。我花了二十五分鐘開到停車塔，有驚無險地度過基督城在耶誕節前的混亂路況。我開到八樓，順利通過樓層間環繞向上的狹窄坡道，有些駕駛人比我更小心，有些人則當自己在賽車場上。我走樓梯下去，出了一身汗，走到樓底碰到遊民亨利，我拿了兩塊錢給他，他稱我是聖人。亨利手裡拿了一本聖經，或許他的目光眞鋭利到能看出我是聖人，或許另一隻手裡拿的廉價伏特加叫他要這麼說。從停車塔只要走兩分鐘就到辦公室了。路上人人表情嚴肅，認命面對眼前這一天，或許要去辦公大樓，或許去零售店，或許到公園的長凳上睡覺。有些人在等待耶誕節，有些人很興奮，有些人或许根本沒發現節日要到了。太陽愈爬愈高。抬頭仰望盡是藍天，今年應該不會再看到雲層了，讓人不知該怎麼辦。

en_text: The accountant firm employs almost fifty people, and is one of the bigger and certainly more expensive ones in town—its prestige made obvious by the important-sounding partner names—Goodwin, Devereux & Barclay—and prominent location watching down over the city. It’s in one of the more modern Christchurch buildings, sharing it mostly with lawyers and insurance firms. Our company takes up the top three floors of fifteen—the biggest firm in the building. The foyer is throwing out cold air and people are lining up for the elevator. I take the stairs where the air smells stale and break into even more of a sweat.
zh_text: 會計師事務所的雇員大約有五十名，在城裡算大公司，當然費用也比較貴「古德溫、德弗羅和巴克禮」三個合夥人的名字聽來鏗鏘有力，位於能俯瞰全城的優越地點，因此名聲響亮。辦公室在基督城比較現代的建築物內，仍有律師事務所跟保險公司進駐。這棟樓有十五層，我們在最上面三層，也是這棟樓裡最大的公司。大廳散發出涼爽的空氣，大家排隊等著進電梯。我走樓梯上去，樓梯間的空氣聞起來不太新鮮，我又出了更多汗。

en_text: I work on the thirteenth floor, where the view isn’t as good as the bosses’ above, but better than the lawyers’ below. I go through the early-morning hellos with a few people once I reach my floor, which takes longer this time of the year because people always seem to want to know what everybody else is doing for Christmas. The ones who ask the most seem to be the people with great plans.
zh_text: 我的辦公室在十三樓，風景當然不如上面大老闆的樓層，但比下面的律師事務所好得多。到了我的樓層，我跟幾個人打招呼說早安，最近大家寒暄的時間都比較長，因爲總有人會問起其他人的假期計畫。看來最愛問的人已經做了最棒的計畫。

en_text: Most of us are lucky enough to have our own office—with a few using cubicles. I’m one of the lucky ones, plus my office is at the end of a corridor that doesn’t get a lot of foot traffic. It’s here I deal with taxes and not so much with people. I dump my satchel on my desk and slump in my seat and pull my already damp shirt away from my body. My office is big enough to fit a desk and a person sitting either side of it and not much more. Most spare wall space on the entire floor is covered in school drawings the parents have brought in from their kids—crayon-purple Christmas trees and dogs with seven legs reminding us all we’d rather be somewhere else but here—and my office is the same. I stare at a couple of the drawings Sam has done, taking a few minutes to cool down before throwing myself into the file I’ve been working on—the firm has been hired by a bottled water company, McClintoch Spring Water, searching for tax breaks. It’s a company whose advertising campaign used images of Jesus to make it a lot of money last year.
zh_text: 大多數人都很幸運，一人一間辦公室——少數幾人坐在大隔間裡。我也是其中一名幸運兒，而且我的辦公室在走廊底，很少有人經過。我坐在這裡處理稅務，鮮少與人來往。我把側背包丢在桌上，陷入椅子裡，把汗濕的襯衫脫下來。我的辦公室剛好能裝下一張辦公桌和一邊一張椅子，此外就沒什麼空間了。在這層樓，牆上有空間的地方大多被父母貼了孩子在學校的畫作蠟筆畫的紫色耶誕樹，七條腿的小狗，讓我們只想離開辦公室到別的地方去——我的辦公室也一樣。我凝視著小珊的兩幅畫，花了幾分鐘靜下來，然後才全心投入我正在處理的檔案——麥克林多奇這家瓶裝水公司雇用我們找出節稅的方法。他們的廣告用了耶穌的圖片，去年賺了不少錢。

en_text: I meet Jodie for lunch at twelve thirty outside a café down The Strip, a line of café/bars that double as nightclubs at night, with indoor-outdoor flow and tables spilling out onto the sidewalks. I’m called “sir” because I’m almost thirty years old, but if I came here tonight I’d probably get asked to leave for being too old. The cafés are all at about 90 percent full, some people turning red in the sun, others sitting in the shade of giant umbrellas, the smell of food and cologne thickening the air. The waitresses are all wearing tight black T-shirts. Most of them have their hair pulled back in ponytails that bounce as they walk. On the other side of the road the Avon River is almost at a standstill, bugs attracted by the smell of stagnant river weed and a dead eel floating along belly-up.
zh_text: 我跟茱蒂約了十二點半到長條區的咖啡店一起吃午餐，這裡整條街都是咖啡店和酒吧，晚上就變成夜店，室內室外的分界消失，人行道上也擺了桌子。有人稱我「先生」，因爲我快三十歲了，但如果晚上到這裡來，會有人要求我離開，因爲我太老了。咖啡店的座位快坐滿了，有些人在太陽下曬得皮膚發紅，有些人則坐在大陽傘的陰影裡，食物和古龍水的味道讓空氣更加濁重。女服務生都穿著繫身的黑色T恤，她們大多把頭髮綁成馬尾，走路時馬尾也跟著上下跳動。在馬路另一邊的艾文河幾乎靜止不動，發臭的水藻和翻出白肚的死鰻魚吸引了不少蟲子。

en_text: We talk while we eat, the only subject the new house we’re trying to buy. Jodie picks at a chicken salad which is probably only chicken in name; she can’t seem to find any meat in it. I work at a plate of nachos, the food okay, not great, but priced as if it were the best in the city. Maybe we’re paying a premium to stare at the waitresses in their T-shirts.
zh_text: 我們邊吃邊聊，話題都繞著我們要買的新房子打轉。茱蒂用叉子在她的雞肉沙拉裡挑挑揀揀，雖然名字裡有雞肉，她卻一片也找不到。我點了一盤墨西哥玉米片，味道還行，不算好吃，但價格卻媲美城裡最好的餐點。或许我們付了額外的費用，才能盯著穿T恤的女服務生看。

en_text: The new house will have a spare room big enough for me to put a pool table in, and Jodie wants some aerobic equipment. We’ll probably use neither, but the fun part at this stage is the dreaming. A new house will be exciting for Sam too. But before that we still have to get through the excitement of Christmas. Sam is the perfect age for Christmas—she still believes in Santa.
zh_text: 新房子有間空房，大到可以放一張撞球桌，茱蒂則想買有氧運動的器材。這兩樣東西或許最後都不會放進去，但現在正是做白日夢的時候。小珊應該也很興奮要搬新家了。但搬家前我們仍得先度過耶誕節的興奮。小珊正在熱愛耶誕節的年紀——她仍相信耶誕老人會送禮物來。

en_text: The waitress comes by when both our mouths are full and asks how the meal is and neither of us can answer. She seems to take that as a good sign and moves on to the next table. It’s probably only a couple of degrees away from hitting thirty-five and the waitress is ready to melt into a fleshy puddle when one o’clock rolls around, the umbrellas in danger of catching alight. We pay the bill, and the waitress gives us the smile of the damned.
zh_text: 女服務生過來的時候，我們的嘴巴正好都塞滿了，她問食物怎麼樣，我們兩人都無法回答。她似乎認爲這表示東西很好吃，便移到下一張桌子去。溫度再上升兩度可能就要衝破三十五了，到了下午一點，女服務生已經要融化成一攤肉，遮陽傘也快燒起來了。我們付了帳，女服務生則報以苦笑。

en_text: It’s only a five-minute walk to the bank. One side of the road is warm in the shade, the other almost white hot. The sidewalks are covered in melted chewing gum and teenagers on skateboards wearing loose clothes with hoodies, perfecting the rapist image kids these days love and clothes designers are making millions off. I wonder how hot it has to get before they take their hoodies off. We get stopped every hundred meters or so by people trying to convince us to sign up to save the whales, save the environment, solve world hunger. There’s tinsel hanging from streetlights and building frontages, decorated trees and fake snow on the window-display floors, plastic Santas and reindeer everywhere. People are rushing about on their lunch breaks trying to squeeze in some shopping, some carrying packages and gifts, others wearing lost looks on their faces.
zh_text: 走到銀行只要五分鐘。路的一邊是溫暖的陰影，另一邊則熱到泛白。人行道上到處都是融化的口香糖，以及溜滑板的青少年，他們穿著寬鬆的衣服和連帽外套，完美演出現代小孩熱愛的強暴犯形象，服裝設計師也靠這種風格賺進大筆鈔票。不知道要到多熱他們才會把連帽外套脫下來。每走大約一百公尺就得停下來，有人要我們簽名拯救鯨魚、拯救環境、解決全球飢荒。街燈和大樓前方都掛了金屬彩帶，樹上擺了裝飾品，櫥窗地面上撒了假雪，到處都看得到塑膠耶誕老人和馴鹿。很多人利用午餐時間東奔西跑，想趁機買點東西，有人手上抓滿了包裏和禮物，也有人看起來很失落。

en_text: The bank is pretty much slap bang in the middle of town, a tall building with the ground floor for the public and on the other floors—nobody really knows. It has air-conditioning and about fifty potted plants and a security guard who keeps glancing at his watch. We end up arriving early and are led to a group of comfortable chairs to kill time in. Nobody offers us anything to drink. There are racks full of banking brochures on the wall next to us, plenty of posters advertising interest rates; young families with new homes and new kids and big smiles is the image of choice—which is fine with us. But once you’ve seen one poster there isn’t much more to look at: just more floating and fixed interest rate packages and more smiles from people thrilled to be a slave to their mortgage. There are percentage symbols plastered everywhere.
zh_text: 銀行恰好就在市中心，一棟高大的建築物，一樓供公衆使用，其他樓層不知道幹啥的。裡面有冷氣，還有大概五十盆植物，以及一名不停瞄手錶的保全人員。结果我們還早到了，被領到很舒適的椅子上坐下殺時間。沒有人問我們要喝什麼。旁邊牆上的架子放滿銀行的廣告冊子，也有很多宣傳利率的海報；主角多是新成立的家庭、新房子、剛出生的孩子，大家臉上帶著幸福的微笑——對我們來說還好。但如果你看到一張不值得細看的海報：浮動利率和固定利率，被貸款綁得死死還洋溢著幸福微笑的人兒。你就只會看到百分比符號，到處都是這樣的符號。

en_text: Then, at thirteen minutes past one—two minutes until our appointment with the mortgage consultant—six men carrying shotguns walk calmly through the door.
zh_text: 然後，在一點十三分，還有兩分鐘就是我們跟貸款顧問約定的時間——六個拿著霰彈槍的男人泰然自若地走進了銀行。

en_text: Crime is escalating. Domestic abuse, adolescent street racers running down innocent pedestrians, people stealing and killing—this is the norm in Christchurch, everyday acts happening in an everyday city. Crime escalates like every other statistic, like inflation, cost of living, it ebbs and flows along with gas prices and the real estate market. Same with the murder rate —it can’t be plotted and predicted on a graph, but it stays in line with other crime, a statistic, a percentage.
zh_text: 犯罪率日漸上升。家暴、飆車族撞死無辜的路人、偷竊和兇殺在基督城司空見慣，很普通的城市，發生了很普通的事件。犯罪率就像其他統計數字一樣不斷上揚，比方說通貨膨脹和生活費，也隨著汽油價格和不動產市場起起落落。謀殺案亦然無法用圖表規劃和預測，總跟隨其他的罪行，就是一個統計數字，一個百分比。

en_text: But this . . .
zh_text: 但這個……

en_text: He’s not even sure what this is.
zh_text: 他甚至不確定發生了什麼事。

en_text: Detective Inspector Schroder brings the car to a stop. There are two unmarked patrol cars blocking off the entrance to the alleyway but he can still see the body beyond it. Detective Landry is leaning against one of the cars, jotting down notes and pausing occasionally to cough into his hand as the medical examiner conveys the details with as many hand gestures as he does words. Schroder gets out of the car and walks over.
zh_text: 施羅德探長把車子停下來。兩輛便衣警車堵住了巷子的入口，但他仍看得到後面的屍體。警探藍德里靠在其中一台車子上，聽驗屍官比手畫腳加口述訴說細節，他匆匆寫著筆記，偶爾停下來用手摀著嘴巴咳嗽。施羅德下了車，走到藍德里旁邊。

en_text: “Hell of a show, Carl,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「卡爾，很精采啊。」藍德里說。

en_text: “And you figured I’d want to come take a look.”
zh_text: 「所以你認爲我該過來看看。」

en_text: “Well, sure I did. I thought you could use the fresh air.” “Some air. It must be forty degrees out here.”
zh_text: 「我當真這麼想，你也該呼吸新鮮的空氣了。」「空氣新鮮嗎？這裡應該有四十度吧。」

en_text: “These nor’west winds—don’t know what it is, but they make the crazy even crazier,” Sheldon, the medical examiner, sighs, before taking off his glasses and wiping them with the tail of his shirt. “Don’t discount it,” he adds, “I’ve been doing this long enough to know.”
zh_text: 「誰知道西北風是什麼東西，但風一吹起來，就瘋上加瘋了。」法醫謝爾登嘆了一口氣，然後脫下眼鏡，用襯衫衣角擦了一下。他又說：「別懷疑，我做這一行很久了，我知道。」

en_text: “So what have we got?” Schroder asks, stepping into the alleyway. The body doesn’t look any better than it did from behind his steering wheel. Landry and the ME follow him.
zh_text: 「現在是什麼情況？」施羅德問，走進巷子裡。走近了看，屍體也沒比剛才從方向盤後看到的好看點。藍德里和驗屍官跟在後面。

en_text: Blood has puddled around the dead man, creating a perimeter of about a meter that Schroder can’t cross without contaminating the scene; the footprints already in it are from Sheldon. The victim’s limbs are all twisted up, especially the legs—the left one has bent forward and snapped somewhere in the knee joint so the ankle is tucked up against the front of the groin.
zh_text: 死人身旁積了一灘血，周長大概有一公尺，如果施羅德想穿過去，一定會破壤現場；不過謝爾登已經在裡面留下了腳印。死者的四肢歪扭得厲害，尤其是他的雙腿——左腿向前彎，斷在膝蓋一帶，所以腳踝塞到鼠蹊前方。

en_text: The guy has three suction cups attached to him—one strapped on each hand, the third secured around his right knee. The fourth is resting on the ground about half a meter from the body, the strap broken in the fall.
zh_text: 那人身上黏了三個吸盤，雙手各綁一個，第三個固定在右膝蓋上。第四個則掉在地上，離屍體大約半公尺遠，綁帶在他掉下來時斷掉了。

en_text: The alleyway is cooler than the street, and in complete shade, but the top nine storeys of the ten-storey building are in direct sunlight. Even in this heat the alleyway smells damp. There are recycling bins lining one of the walls, broken wooden pallets and cardboard boxes lining the other. Christchurch alleyways are always full of something—just normally not bodies. He looks up, shielding his eyes against the bright reflection from the windows, then back down at the dead man’s face. A guy with big Vegas-style Elvis sideburns and busted-up features and head wounds that have leaked all over the cracked tarmac.
zh_text: 巷子裡不像街上那麼熱，也曬不到太陽，但旁邊十層樓的建築物除了底層外，上面九層樓都在陽光直射下。雖然溫度很高，巷子裡仍有股濕氣。一邊擺了一排資源回收箱，另一邊則排了殘破的木頭棧板和紙箱。基督城的小巷裡總堆滿東西——但是屍體卻不常見。施羅德抬頭仰望，用手遮住窗戶反射出來的強烈陽光，然後低頭看看死者的臉龐。他的鬢角很顯眼，就像在拉斯維加斯扮演貓王的人，五官支離破碎，頭也爆了，血液腦漿橫流在裂開的柏油路上。

en_text: “See, told you it was a show,” Landry says. “Ain’t much for us to do except wrap Batman up in a bag and take him to the morgue.”
zh_text: 「看吧，就說很精采，」藍德里說，「我們也不能幹嘛，只能把蝙蝠俠裝到袋子裡，送去太平間。」

en_text: “I think he was trying to be more like Spiderman,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我覺得他想扮蜘蛛人。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Either way, the fact he’s naked except for a trench coat tells us he’s a piece of crap.”
zh_text: 「都可以啦，全身光溜溜只穿件雨衣，就知道他是個混蛋。」

en_text: “Maybe.”
zh_text: 「或许吧。」

en_text: “What’s that supposed to mean? For all we know he was on his way to rape somebody,” Landry says. “Dressed like this—he certainly wasn’t trying to watch cable TV for free. I’m thinking he got what he deserved.”
zh_text: 「你想說什麼？我們只知道，他正要找個人來強姦，」藍德里說，「穿成這個樣子，肯定不是爲了免費偷看別人的第四台。我覺得他罪有應得。」

en_text: Schroder nods. Still, if he was planning on peeking into somebody’s apartment—surely there was an easier way.
zh_text: 施羅德點點頭。不論怎麼說，如果他計畫要偷窥別人的公寓，不需要這麼費力吧。

en_text: They all turn as one as the media vans begin their assault on the scene, all pulling up at the same time. The cameramen and reporters climb out and move around the barriers to get closer. Police constables push them back. Cameras are hoisted up onto shoulders and the sun glints off the lenses.
zh_text: 他們轉過頭，看到新聞探訪車開始大舉進攻犯罪現場，所有的車子同時停下來。攝影師和記者爬出車子，在警戒線外挨挨擦擦，想更靠近一點。値勤員警把他們推走。攝影師把機器扛到肩膀上，陽光在鏡頭上閃爍。

en_text: “And the show gets an audience,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「有觀衆了。」藍德里說。

en_text: “We should cover him up,” Schroder says, glancing up at the other tall buildings surrounding them. Landry is right—this is a hell of a show. People are standing in the windows, all staring down and pointing, their faces full of excitement. The reporters scan the buildings for better vantage points to invade the dead man’s privacy from. A constable comes over and goes about covering the victim, a white sheet of canvas hiding the view away from the public. Not all the blood has dried and some of it seeps into the material.
zh_text: 「該把他蓋起來。」施羅德說，抬眼看看旁邊的高樓大廈。藍德里說得對一一的確很精采。不少人站在窗邊對著地面指指點點，滿臉興奮的表情。記者四處查看旁邊的建築物是否有更好的制高點來侵犯死者的隱私。警員走過來，準備蓋住死者，一塊白帆布擋住了公衆的視線。未乾的血液伺機沾上了布料。

en_text: “Anything in his pockets?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「他口袋裡有什麼？」施羅德問。

en_text: “Nothing.”
zh_text: 「什麼也沒有。」

en_text: “I’m all done with him,” Sheldon says. “Pretty obvious what happened, but I’ll know more once we get him back to the morgue. Messed up the way he is, he must have gotten pretty high.”
zh_text: 「我驗完了，」謝爾登說，「案情看來不複雜，不過等我們把他帶回太平間，我可以找出更多資料。像他摔得這麼爛，一定是嗑藥嗑翻了。」

en_text: “I’m not so sure,” Schroder says. “All of this—something here doesn’t add up.”
zh_text: 「我不確定，」施羅德說，「這一切——有些東西不太對勁。」

en_text: Landry and Sheldon glance at the body, at the building, at the body again, then back at Schroder. “You want to elaborate on that, Carl? What exactly are we missing here? A mostly naked dead man with suction cups strapped to him at the base of an apartment building with a couple of hundred windows—what doesn’t add up?”
zh_text: 藍德里和謝爾登看看屍體，看看大樓，又看看屍體，然後看著施羅德。「卡爾，你可以說清楚一點嗎？我們錯過了什麼？一個將近全裸的死人身上綁了吸盤，掉在一棟有兩百扇窗戶的公寓大樓底下還有什麼不對勁的地方？」

en_text: “I don’t get it,” Schroder says. “I mean, it seems a hell of an effort to go to just to peep through some windows. Problem is, all the effort in the world wouldn’t have helped him out. This whole suction cup thing, it’s a myth. You can’t scale buildings like that. Can’t be done.”
zh_text: 「我不懂，」施羅德說，「我的意思是，光爲了偷窺，他這麼搞也太費力了吧？問題在於，就算全世界都幫他的忙，他也不會成功。用吸盤這件事眞的很瞎。怎麼能用吸盤爬大樓？做不到呀。」

en_text: Schroder takes a step back to reduce the glare and gazes up the side of the building. None of the floors have balconies.
zh_text: 施羅德後退了一步，陽光變得沒那麼耀眼，他凝視著眼前的大樓。所有的樓層都沒有陽台。

en_text: “All that means is he started climbing from higher up. Maybe he has an apartment here,” Landry says. “He probably climbed out on the sixth or seventh floor, and fell from the sixth or the seventh floor. Come on, Carl, we didn’t call you down here to try and make us look like idiots—there’s no crime here.”
zh_text: 「這一切表示他不是從地面往上爬。或許他住在其中一棟公寓裡，」藍德里說，「或許他從六樓或七樓爬出來，然後從六樓或七樓掉下來。拜託，卡爾，我們叫你來，不是要你把我們貶低成呆瓜——這人不是被殺的。」

en_text: “If there’s no crime, why did you call me down?”
zh_text: 「如果罪案不成立，叫我來幹嘛？」

en_text: Landry rolls his shoulders back, and when he talks, a vein pops out in his forehead and starts throbbing. “For once the victim is someone who deserved it. For once the victim isn’t some girl who smiled at the wrong guy and got sliced up for it. Come on, Carl, how many times have we seen that, huh? And this time—well, this time it’s score one for the good guys.”
zh_text: 藍德里挺了挺胸膛，等他開口時，額頭上爆起了青筋，還不斷跳動。「我說過，死者活該。我也要說，死者並不是搞錯了調情對象結果被碎屍萬段的女孩。卡爾，拜託你喔，這種事情我們不是第一次碰到了吧？這一次，噯，這一次好人贏了。」

en_text: “How come nobody found him earlier?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「怎麼早一點沒人發現他？」施羅德問。

en_text: “There was a car parked at the front of the alley, blocking the view. Belonged to one of the tenants. He normally leaves it parked here overnight. He only came to move it half an hour ago.”
zh_text: 「巷子前本來停了一輛車子，擋住了視線。車子是住戶的。他晚上都把車子停在這裡，半小時前他才過來移車。」

en_text: “Time of death is about twelve hours,” Sheldon says.
zh_text: 「死亡時間大概是十二個小時前。」謝爾登說。

en_text: “Tell me, when he climbed out last night, before he fell, do you think he closed the window?” “What?” Landry asks.
zh_text: 「告訴我，昨天晚上他爬出來，然後掉下來，你覺得他把窗戶關好了嗎？」「什麼？」藍德里問。

en_text: “None of the windows are open.”
zh_text: 「所有的窗戶都關起來了。」

en_text: They all study the side of the building. There’s no way the victim climbed out and made the effort to close the window behind him. There’s no way he could have gone more than a meter before the suction cups gave way.
zh_text: 三人都仰頭看著大樓。死者不可能爬出來以後還想到要回頭關窗戶。他應該爬不到一公尺，吸盤就失靈了。

en_text: “Shit,” Landry says. He pulls a packet of cigarettes out of his pocket and dances one across his fingers.
zh_text: 「媽的。」藍德里說。他從口袋裡掏出一包香菸，抽出一根在指間跳動。

en_text: “Maybe he managed to climb all the way up from the ground,” Sheldon suggests.
zh_text: 「或許他眞從地面一路爬上去。」謝爾登猜測。

en_text: “It can’t happen,” Schroder says. “Look it up. Try it out. Do whatever you need to, but it doesn’t work.”
zh_text: 「不可能，」施羅德說，「去查查看，試試看。不論你想什麼辦法，就是行不通。」

en_text: “How do you know for sure?” Landry asks.
zh_text: 「你怎麼知道？」藍德里問。

en_text: “I saw it on the Discovery Channel.”
zh_text: 「我在探索频道看到的。」

en_text: “Maybe he took the elevator to the roof and climbed down,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「或許他搭電梯到頂樓，然後爬下來。」藍德里說。

en_text: “Take another look,” Schroder says. Between the roof and the top apartments is about a two-meter strip of concrete. “This isn’t what it seems. This guy was a victim of something.”
zh_text: 「你再看看。」施羅德說。屋頂和最上面那層公寓間有寬約兩公尺的水泥片。「情況不對。這人是受害者。」

en_text: “I still don’t get it,” Landry says, putting the cigarette back. “What you’re saying makes sense, I see that, but there are other alternatives.”
zh_text: 「我還是不懂。」藍德里說，把香菸放回去。「你說得有道理，我同意，但還有其他的解釋。」

en_text: “Like what?” Schroder asks, reaching into his pocket for his ringing cell phone.
zh_text: 「比方說？」施羅德問，同時伸手到口袋裡，拿出鈴聲響起的手機。

en_text: “Like maybe the suction cups worked.”
zh_text: 「比方說，或許吸盤眞能吸得住。」

en_text: “Or maybe somebody dressed him up,” Schroder points out, “and threw him off the roof.” He takes the call. The woman on the other end of the phone talks quickly, and thirty seconds later he’s back in his car, racing toward the bank, fighting for position with the reporters making their way in the same direction.
zh_text: 「或许，有人把他打扮成這樣，」施羅德指出，「然後把他從樓頂丢下來。」他接起電話。電話另一端的女人連珠炮般講了幾句，三十秒後，他已經回到車裡，朝著銀行全速前進，和其他奔往同樣方向的記者爭道。

en_text: It’s a moment in a movie. Something so incredibly implausible and so far away from what I’m thinking about that I can’t even comprehend it. I actually look away for a second, just this normal slice of life in this everyday normal bank where abnormal things don’t happen, back to the family-oriented posters and floating interest rates, back to Jodie sitting opposite me—and then, somehow, somehow, it all becomes real.
zh_text: 跟電影情節一樣。不眞實到令人無法相信的地步，完全與我的思緒背道而馳，我甚至不明白發生了什麼事。事實上我轉過頭看了一下，就在這正常的生活中，在這家普通到不會發生怪事的銀行裡，然後回頭看著牆上的家庭海報和浮動利率，看著坐在我對面的茱蒂一然後，不知怎地，不知道爲什麼，一切就成眞了。

en_text: The doors are two large side-by-side glass doors that open automatically as indiscriminately for these men as they did for me and my wife. The six men enter in three groups of two. The first group goes left, the second, right, and the third, straight ahead. It’s all happening behind Jodie and she has no idea what’s going on. She keeps talking. Most of the people are still talking. Some glance up at the men for a second before returning to what they were doing, then the realization of what they saw kicks in, the disbelief on their faces perhaps comical under other circumstances. Others seem to be noticing immediately, perhaps people who have seen this kind of thing on TV enough times to figure out what happens next. They’re dropping out of sight behind desks. All this and the men haven’t even made a sound.
zh_text: 銀行的入口是兩扇並排的大玻璃門，爲進出的人自動打開，那些人進來的時候，門開了，就跟我們進來的時候一樣。六個男人分成三組，兩兩前進。第一組向左，第二組向右，第三組直走。茱蒂背對門口，不知道發生了什麼事。她沒停下剛才的話題；大多數人也仍在講話。有些人抬頭看了那些男人一眼，然後繼續做自己的事，等領悟到眼前的情况時，他們臉上疑惑的表情如果換個情景，看起來或许有種滑稽的感覺。有些人似乎立刻就注意到了，有可能他們在電視上看了很多次，知道接下來會是什麼情況。他們離開別人的視線，躲到桌子後面。發生了這麼多事，那六個男人卻悄無聲息。

en_text: Jodie watches my face. She hears the collective gasp from everybody else. She twists her head to see what’s happening. A woman screams. The six men are all wearing balaclavas. They’re all wearing black jerseys and black jeans and could all have just come from a heavy metal concert. They move calmly but forcefully forward, surrounded by an air of confidence the six shotguns provide. They look like they own the bank. They look like never in their lives have they been said no to. The police station is a five-minute walk from here, which means the clock is ticking. Jodie reaches out and I take her hand.
zh_text: 茱蒂看到我的表情，聽到其他人一起倒抽了一口氣。她轉過頭，看到背後的情况。有個女人尖叫了一聲。六個男人都戴著只露出雙眼跟鼻子的頭罩，身著黑色緊身衣和黑色牛仔褲，要說他們剛去了一場重金屬演唱會也不爲過。他們前進的姿態平靜且充滿力量，靠著那六支霰彈槍，散發出自信的氣息。他們的神情宛若他們是銀行的主人，彷彿在一生中從來沒碰到過敢拒絕他們的人。警察局離此步行只要五分鐘，所以他們的時間緊迫。茱蒂伸出手，和我緊緊相握。

en_text: “Next person to move gets their head taken off,” one of them yells, and most people come to a dead stop, a few more keep running, others are hiding behind anything that remotely covers their bodies. The security guard’s face turns about as white as his shirt. He’s absolutely motionless. He’s armed with a radio and the knowledge he’s not earning anything more than minimum wage to be here, and he’s trying to figure out what good either of those things are going to do against six men with shotguns. He doesn’t get far in his figuring, unless he was figuring on inaction, which he does down to perfection. He raises his hands in the air but doesn’t manage to do anything else, including duck, before one of the two men that went in his direction turns the stock of the shotgun and smashes it hard into his jaw. The guard’s head snaps back with a sick crack. He hits the floor, his body slumping in a heap, limbs twisted everywhere. All this and only fifteen seconds have passed. A silent alarm may have been tripped, or maybe the bank cut back on a few of those features so they could offer the competitive interest rates the posters are going on about. The bank staff have open mouths and wide eyes and any training they’ve been given is all shot to hell, a snapshot in a moment of time, like somebody pressed the pause button on life.
zh_text: 「誰敢動一下，我就轟掉他的頭。」其中一人大吼，大多數人嚇得動彈不得，少數跑走的幾個人仍沒停下腳步，还有一些人躲在根本藏不住身體的地方。銀行警衛的臉色煞白，跟他的襯衫顏色一樣，整個人動也不動。他只配備了無線電，而且他在這裡賺的錢不比基本薪資高多少，他還在想，自己到底有什麼本事來對付六個帶著霰彈槍的男人。應該想不到，除非他靜止不動的時候腦子也能轉，不過他倒是完全定住了。他高舉雙手，還來不及做下一個動作，比方說低下身子，兩個男人就向他走去，其中一個舉起槍托，對著他的下顎重擊。警衛的脖子往後折斷，斷裂的聲響令人心驚。他倒在地上，全身像坨爛泥，四肢扭曲散落在地。似乎發生了很多事，其實只過了十五秒。或许有人扳動了無聲警鈴，或許銀行縮減了幾項保全措施，好提供海報上那些能贏得客戶歡心的利率。行員個個瞠目結舌，受過的訓練全都丢到九霄雲外，這一刻，似乎有人按下了暫停鈕，一切都停下來了。

en_text: “It’s going to be okay,” I say, and I squeeze Jodie’s hand tight. She gives me a look that suggests she doesn’t think things are going to be okay. She’s pale and scared and I’m the same way and I wish we’d ordered something for lunch that would have taken longer to prepare.
zh_text: 「沒事，不會有事的。」我握緊茱蒂的手。她看了我一眼，表情似乎在說她覺得事情沒那麼簡單。她臉色蒼白，滿面驚恐，我也一樣，我眞希望午餐點了要花比較長時間準備的菜餚。

en_text: The same guy who yelled moves closer to the bank tellers. “Everybody on this side of the counter move over there,” he says, and he points to the far left of the line of counters. Nobody moves. “Now! And get down on the ground!”
zh_text: 大吼的男人朝著出納員走過去。「在櫃台這邊的人到那裡去。」他指著那排櫃台最左邊的地方。大家動也不動。「快點！然後坐在地上！」

en_text: We all move as one, footsteps shuffling on the floor, everybody hunched over and moving awkwardly, like old folks in a retirement home running from the Reaper. I don’t let go of Jodie’s hand. We sit on the ground, maybe twenty-five of us, all scared, all thinking the same thing—that we should have made more of Christmas last year.
zh_text: 我們的動作整齊劃一，拖著腳彎著腰，感覺很笨拙，就像老人院裡面的居民想要逃離在後追趕的開膛手。我一直抓著茱蒂的手。我們大概有二十五個人，一起坐到地上，都很惶恐，都有同樣的想法去年過聖誕節的時候應該更珍惜那段時光。

en_text: The six men, in three teams of two, spread further out to the sides. One of them turns and points his gun at the door, ready for more customers to wander on in, even though the whole front of the bank is made up of glass and everybody outside is staring at us. The man barking the instructions reaches the counter.
zh_text: 分成三組的六個男人繼續朝著銀行兩側走去。有一個人走回來，用槍指著門口，準備對付接下來晃進銀行的顧客，不過銀行正面是整片玻璃，所有站在外面的人都在瞪著我們看。發號施令的那個人走到櫃台前。

en_text: “You,” he yells, and he points his shotgun at a woman behind the counter. All the makeup in the world couldn’t hide the tightening of her features. “Take these back to the vault and fill them.” He throws some bags at her. They hit her counter and she doesn’t move. “Now!” he says.
zh_text: 「妳！」他用槍指著櫃台後的女人，對她吼叫。世界上所有的化妆品都無法讓她緊繃的五官變得更好看。「拿這些袋子去金庫，裝滿以後拿回來。」他把幾個袋子對著她丢過去。袋子掉到她的櫃台上，她呆住了。「快點！」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Fill them or die. The choice is yours.” She gets it. She picks up the bags.
zh_text: 「把錢裝滿袋子，不然妳就得死。看妳要怎麼辦。」她聽懂了，抓起袋子。

en_text: “Help her,” he says, pointing at another of the bank tellers. “You as well,” he says, glaring at a third. “And you too,” he adds, waving the gun at a fourth. “And if all four of you aren’t back here in two minutes we open fire on everybody else. Get that?”
zh_text: 「你幫她裝。」他指指另一個出納員。「還有你。」他對著第三個出納員瞪眼。「你也去。」又對著第四個人揮揮手上的槍。「要是你們四個沒有在兩分鐘內全部回到這裡，我們就對每一個人開槍。懂嗎？」

en_text:
As soon as the four disappear, an office door opens. We all turn toward it. A man with a pink tie and his shirtsleeves rolled up stands there with his hands raised in the air, and his head tilted and hunched down slightly, as if trying to avoid sniper fire.
“P . . . p . . . please, I’m the manager, please don’t hurt anybody and—” He doesn’t get to say any more. The shotgun barks and people cry out.
zh_text:
那四個人的身影才消失，一間辦公室的門打開了。所有人的目光都集中到那扇門上。一個男人高舉雙手走出來，他打了粉紅色的頜帶，襯衫袖子捲了起來，他歪著頭，又微微弓著身子，彷彿要避開狙擊。
「拜···拜···拜託，我是這家銀行的經理，拜託你們不要傷人···」

en_text: The manager isn’t thrown backward like in movies. He just stands where he was shot. His head hangs down so he seems to study the angry wound in his chest, seems to notice his shirt has blossomed red, and gravity pulls at the features on his face, making him appear sad. Then he folds at the waist, his ass going backwards, his feet staying in the same place, so when he hits the ground he’s folded in half, his legs out straight, his face against his knees, and he stays in that position with his arms by his side. The wall behind where he stood is streaked in blood, the window next to the door is shattered, other small pellets are buried into the wall. The manager looks like he’s stretching, warming up for yoga.
zh_text: 他沒有機會把話說完，霰彈槍響了，大家驚叫出聲。銀行經理不像電影裡中槍的人向後飛起來，他就站在原地不動。他垂下頭，似乎在研究胸前狂痛的傷口，似乎發現了自己的襯衫變成豔紅色，重力拉扯著他的五官，讓他的表情看起來很難過。然後他的腰一彎，臀部向後坐，雙腳留在原位，所以他撞到地上的時候，整個人對折了，雙腿伸直，臉孔靠向膝蓋，他就那嬮坐著，雙臂放在身體兩側。他背後的那面牆出現了好幾道血痕，門旁的窗戶震碎了，子彈的碎片卡進牆面。經理看起來像在拉筋，做瑜伽的暖身動作。

en_text: “Jesus,” I whisper, and I can see other people mouthing the same word but can’t hear it because my ears are still ringing. People are raising their hands to their faces. Others are crying. A man in his late sixties or early seventies has wet himself. A woman has passed out, her face pressing into the floor, looking far more relaxed than anybody else here.
zh_text: 「老天啊。」我低聲說，看到其他人也做出同樣的嘴型，但我聽不到聲音，因爲我的耳朵還在嗡嗡作響。有人用雙手掩臉，有人開始哭泣。一名貌似七旬的老翁尿濕了褲子。有個女人昏倒了，臉孔壓在地上，看起來比其他人都放鬆。

en_text: Jodie’s grip is almost breaking my fingers.
zh_text: 茱蒂抓緊我的手，幾乎捏碎我的指頭。

en_text: “Stay calm,” I say, “just stay calm.”
zh_text: 「保持鎭定，」我說，「一定要鎭定。」

en_text: “Everybody shut up!” one of the men yells, then he fires another shot, this one into the ceiling. Plaster dust rains down, it settles on his shoulders like dandruff.
zh_text: 「全部給我閉嘴！」一名搶匪大吼，又開了一槍，這次對著天花板。灰泥噗颼颼掉下來，跟頭皮屑一樣落在他的肩膀上。

en_text: The four people return from the vault. The bags are bulging with cash and obviously heavy. They manage to lift them up onto the counter.
zh_text: 前往金庫的四人回來了。裝滿現金的袋子鼓鼓脹脹，一定很重。他們很費力地把袋子抬到櫃台上。

en_text: “Too slow,” the man says, talking to the bank teller he first singled out. He pumps the shotgun and levels it at her chest. “You’re coming with us,” he says.
zh_text: 「太慢了。」搶匪對著第一個被他挑中的女出納員說。他搖了搖霰彈槍，對準她的胸口：「妳跟我們一起走。」

en_text: “No, no,” she says.
zh_text: 「不要，不要！」她嚷。

en_text: “Wait!”
zh_text: 「慢著！」

en_text: Everybody turns to the voice. It takes a moment to realize that they’ve all turned toward me, and a longer moment to figure out the reason for that —I’m the one who spoke. The man holding the shotgun on the bank teller turns his head toward me.
zh_text: 所有人都轉向聲音的來源。過了幾秒我才發覺大家都看著我，又過了幾秒我才明白他們爲什麼要看著我说话的人是我。拿霰彈槍抵著女出納員的搶匪轉向我。

en_text: “What?” he says.
zh_text: 「你說什麼？」他問。

en_text: “Eddie,” Jodie says, “what are you doing?”
zh_text: 「艾迪，」茱蒂說，「你在幹什麼？」

en_text: I have no idea. People are staring at me like I’m an anomaly, like they haven’t seen a twenty-nine-year-old white guy speaking in a bank before. I get onto my knees, then onto my feet, swaying slightly, with still no idea what I’m doing or why I called out. “I said wait,” I say, and my voice is firm. “We all heard what you said,” he says, “and I think we’re all curious now as to what you’re planning on doing next.”
zh_text: 我不知道。大家瞪著我，似乎我是個怪物，彷彿他們從沒看過一個二十九歲的西方白人在銀行裡開口說話。我跪起身子，然後站起來，搖搖晃晃，仍不知道我在幹什麼，爲什麼要開口大喊。「我說，慢著。」我的聲音很堅定。「我們都聽到了，」他說，「我想，大家都很好奇你接下來要發表什麼高見。」

en_text: “You’ve got what you came for,” I say, and the girl with the gun pointed at her takes the distraction to duck down behind the counter. Everybody back there does.
zh_text: 「你們的目的已經達到了。」我說，被霰彈槍指著的女人趁著搶匪不注意，往櫃台後一蹲。櫃台後的人也都趁機蹲下。

en_text: The man turns back to where she just was. “Hey, get back up here.” She doesn’t answer.
zh_text: 男人轉頭一看：「喂，給我回來。」她不吭聲。

en_text: “Please. You don’t have to hurt anybody else,” I say.
zh_text: 「求求你。你殺了一個人就夠了。」我說。

en_text: “I didn’t realize you were giving the orders here,” he says, looking over the counter for the woman. He can’t get an angle on her.
zh_text: 「我倒沒發現你才是老大。」他越過櫃台尋找女出納員的蹤跡，看不到她在哪裡。

en_text: “Eddie,” Jodie says.
zh_text: 「艾迪。」茱蒂說。

en_text: “It’s okay, Jodie.”
zh_text: 「茱蒂，沒事的。」

en_text: “We have to go,” another of them says, his finger pressed against his ear, listening to something small. “The police are only two minutes away.”
zh_text: 「該走了。」另一個搶匪說，他的手指壓著耳朵，聕聽裡面的小東西。「警察再過兩分鐘就到了。」

en_text: “Shit,” the first guy says, and he’s staring at me now. “Okay, buddy, you’re volunteering.”
zh_text: 「他媽的。」第一個搶匪說，然後轉眼瞪著我。「好吧，老兄，就當你自告奮勇。」

en_text: “I’ll do what you want as long as you don’t hurt anybody else,” I say.
zh_text: 「你們要怎樣，我都聽你們的，别再傷人了。」我說。

en_text: He offers a short, cold laugh. “No, you got it all wrong. You didn’t volunteer yourself, you went ahead and volunteered that pretty little thing next to you.”
zh_text: 他冷笑了一聲。「錯，大錯特錯。不是你自己站出來，你推的是你旁邊這位年輕可愛的美女。」

en_text: “Don’t,” I say, and I step toward the man coming toward me and put my hand out in a stopping gesture. He doesn’t even slow down. He comes in around my arm and hits me with the gun in the side of my face, hard enough to knock me down.
zh_text: 「不要。」我說，往前走了一步，搶匪朝我走來，我舉手比了停止的手勢。他並未放慢腳步。他走過來扭住我的手臂，用槍重擊我的側臉，力道足以把我打倒在地。

en_text: “Eddie . . .” Jodie is pulled to her feet.
zh_text: 「艾迪···」茱蒂被拉著站了起來。

en_text: Things are out of focus. I’ve fallen onto my side. I get my hands onto the ground and push up. There are two Jodies. Twelve gunmen. They pick up the bags of cash and head for the door. Nobody else is moving. Nobody else is helping. The twelve men turn back into six, they’re at the door and they have Jodie with them. I figure if the police are only two minutes away they’re probably driving and the Friday lunchtime traffic has brought them to a crawl.
zh_text: 眼前一片模糊，我側倒在地上。我雙手撲地撐起身子。有兩個茱蒂，十二個歹徒。他們抓起裝滿現金的袋子，朝著門口走去。其他人動也不動。沒有一個人出面幫忙。十二個男人變回六個，他們挾持茱蒂走到門口。我想，如果警察只在兩分鐘的路程外，他們應該會開車來，而星期五午餐時分的交通狀況會讓他們慢得像蜗牛在爬。

en_text: “Eddie,” Jodie screams, reaching toward me, and it takes two of them to drag her through the door. I get to my feet, wobbling left and right somewhat. I stumble over my feet and trip myself up, hitting the floor hard with my palms. They toss the bags of money inside a van and five of them climb in right alongside it. The sixth guy keeps holding my wife.
zh_text: 「艾迪！」茱蒂尖叫，雙臂朝我伸過來，要兩個男人合力才能把她拖出門外。我好不容易站起來，左搖右晃站不住身子。我跌跌撞撞，絆倒了自己，雙手重重打在地板上。他們把裝了錢的袋子丢到貨車裡，其中五個人跟著爬上去。第六個人則繼續抓著我的妻子。

en_text: I get outside. Nobody follows me. There are people on the street, but they’re all ducked down behind parked cars and huddling in shop doorways. Shopwindows painted over with Christmas scenes have faces pressed against the glass. The kids in the hoodies are popping their heads up from behind a row of motorbikes and pointing cell phones at us. I can’t hear any sirens or see any police. Cars have stopped about twenty meters away in both directions. The guy pushes Jodie toward me. She cries out and stumbles. She reaches out for balance and I can tell she’s going down, she’s going to hit the sidewalk.
zh_text: 我出了銀行，後面沒人跟過來。街上雖然有人，卻全都躲在路邊停著的車子後面，或擠在其店鋪門口。畫了耶誕節場景的商店櫥窗玻璃後也有人把臉貼在上面觀看。穿著連帽外套的青少年從一列摩托車後探出頭來，用手機對著我們。我聽不到警笛聲，看不到警察。兩邊的车子都停在二十公尺外。男人把茱蒂對著我推過來。她大叫，往地上摔倒。爲了平衡她伸出雙手，我知道她要跌倒了，她會撞到人行道。

en_text: He raises the shotgun. He points it right at her. He doesn’t even hesitate, just pulls the trigger. Shoot her in the back, Jack.
zh_text: 那人舉起霰彈槍對準茱蒂，一點也不遲疑地扣下扳機。傑克，對著她的背開槍。

en_text: “No,” I scream, but the word is lost over the explosion. My wife hits the road. The shooter jumps into the back of the van and closes the door. The driver accelerates hard, the engine revs loudly and smoke drifts up off the tires. I reach my wife as the van turns the corner, running a red light and leaving us alone.
zh_text: 「不要！」我尖叫，但爆炸聲蓋過了我的嘶喊。我的妻子倒在地上。開槍的男人跳上貨車車廂，把門關上。駕駛用力踩下油門，引擎大聲怒吼，輪胎冒出青燈。我跑到妻子身旁，貨車已經轉過街角，闖過紅燈，只留下我們兩人。

en_text: Keep her alive, Clive.
zh_text: 克里夫，别讓她死去。

en_text: I have no idea why I keep thinking of the song Jodie sang this morning, perhaps the last song she’ll ever get to sing, steam from the shower thick in the air, the penguin radio launching out classic songs from a classic hits station. The words are in my head but they don’t even feel like mine, as though somebody put them there, an English teacher or a bad comedian having reached out somehow and implanted them.
zh_text: 不知爲何，耳邊一直響起今早茱蒂唱的那首歌，或许是她唱的最後一首歌，空氣中滿是淋浴間散發出來的蒸氣，企鵝收音機從經典排行榜電台播放出經典歌曲。歌詞出現在我腦海中，但感覺不像我自己的思緒，彷彿有人把歌詞灌進去了，或许是英文老師，或许是很差勁的喜劇演員，不知道用什麼方法把歌詞移植到我的腦袋裡。

en_text: She’s dead, Fred—and don’t worry, you’ll be hearing from me soon.
zh_text: 她死了，佛瑞德——别擔心，你很快就會聽到我的消息。

en_text: I scream for help but the only thing people are brave enough to do is step out from whatever hole they hid in and point cell phone cameras at me while others make calls. I try to hold the blood inside her, but it keeps flowing.
zh_text: 我嘶喊求救，但旁邊的人沒有勇氣，只敢從躲藏的地方走出來，用手機上的鏡頭對著我，有些人則開始打電話。我想幫她止血，但血一直流個不停。

en_text: “Jodie, oh God, Jodie, it’s going to be okay,” I say, and I roll her onto her side so I can see her face while keeping pressure on her back. There is so much blood. Way too much blood. It’s seeping between my fingers. It’s like water. I need more hands. More help.
zh_text: 「茱蒂，噢天啊，茱蒂，你不會有事的。」我讓她側躺在地上，才看得見她的臉，同時壓住她背上的傷口。血好多，太多了，跟水一樣從我的指間流出來。我需要有更多隻手來止血，我需要更多人來幫忙。

en_text: I need a miracle.
zh_text: 我需要奇蹟。

en_text: Jodie’s eyes are open and she turns them toward me but focuses beyond me, somewhere a thousand miles away.
zh_text: 茱蒂眼睛睁得大大的，雖然對著我，卻聚焦在我背後幾千哩外的地方。

en_text: “It’s going to be okay,” I say. “I promise.”
zh_text: 「沒事，」我說，「我保證妳不會有事。」

en_text: “My shoes hurt,” she says, and she smiles, and she keeps staring past me and a moment later I realize she’s no longer seeing anything at all.
zh_text: 「我的鞋子好緊喔。」她說著微微一笑，仍瞪著我身後不知何處，過了幾秒我才明白她已經看不見了。

en_text: “Jodie . . .”

There are too many holes in her, I can’t stem them all. Her face is pale, except around her nose which has been broken and flattened when she fell. Blood is smeared there, there’s a deep cut in her upper lip where it’s been sliced by her teeth.
zh_text: 她身上的洞太多了，我沒辦法一一壓住。她的臉色蒼白，但剛才倒下時她摔斷了鼻梁，被壓扁的鼻子一片血污。牙齒也咬破了上唇，留下深深的傷口。

en_text: “Please, please, Jodie, don’t do this, don’t do this,” I say. “Don’t leave me alone.” But Jodie is doing this.
zh_text: 「求求妳，求求妳，茱蒂，不要這樣，不要這樣，」我說，「不要留下我。」但茱蒂偏偏要離開我。

en_text: “Jodie, please,” I say, but my words are only whispers now.
zh_text: 「茱蒂，求求妳···」連我自己都快聽不到自己的聲音了。

en_text: People move closer to get a better look, to get a better angle, a clearer photo. Nobody offers to help. Maybe they can see there is no point. Nobody has come out of the bank—either they’re in too much shock or maybe they’re trying to save the manager and the security guard. Sirens appear in the distance and get louder, and soon they appear, police cars and ambulances, all of them too late. The safety they bring with them allows more bystanders to come forward and watch and point and revel in the drama. Two paramedics rush over to Jodie, each of them carrying a case of lifesaving tools.
zh_text: 街上的人靠過來，想看得更仔細，找個更好的角度，拍到更清晰的照片。沒有人伸出援手。或許他們覺得沒有必要。沒有人從銀行裡出來一或許他們嚇到動彈不得，或許他們正忙著救活經理和警衛。遠方傳來警笛的聲音，愈來愈響，不久之後警車和救護車出現了，來得太遲了。他們的出現令人心安，更多人走過來看熱鬧，指指點點，十分入戲。兩名醫護人員衝到茱蒂身旁，手上都拿著一箱救命的工具。

en_text: “Out of the way,” one of them says.
zh_text: 「讓開。」其中一人說。

en_text: “She’s . . .” “Move,” he repeats.
zh_text: 「她···」「讓開。」他重複。

en_text: I move aside. The two men crouch down over her. One of them slides a pair of scissors up her shirt and exposes the wounds. His expression doesn’t change. He’s seen it all before.
zh_text: 我挪到旁邊。那兩人蹲到茱蒂身旁。其中一人用剪刀滑過她的襯衫，露出下面的傷口。他不動聲色，應該看多了。

en_text: “No pulse,” the other one says. “It doesn’t look . . .” “I know, I know,” the first one says.
zh_text: 「沒有脈搏，」另一個人說，「看來不···」「我知道，我知道。」第一個人說。

en_text: He pulls padding out from his case and jams it against the wound as if trying to pack the hole. They roll her onto her back and while one begins CPR, the other fires up a defibrillator. They hold off on using it, pursuing the CPR which—for the moment—couldn’t be any more useless.
zh_text: 他從急救箱裡拉出厚紗布堵在傷口上，似乎想把那個洞塞滿。他們讓茱蒂躺在地上，一人開始施行心肺復甦術，另一人啓動了電擊器。他們沒有立刻電擊，而是持續現在看起來一點用也沒有的心肺復甦術。

en_text: “Shock her,” the first one says.
zh_text: 「電擊吧。」第一個人說。

en_text: For a moment the two men stare at each other, the words unspoken, but I can see what they’re saying. They both know there’s no point. Both think it’s too late. One of them figures it’s best to at least put on a show because I’m watching.
zh_text: 他們兩人對看了一眼，一切盡在不言中，但是我懂。兩人都知道電擊無濟於事，都覺得太遲了。其中一人覺得最好要表演一下，起碼表演給我看。

en_text: They attach large pads to her chest, but they work slowly, methodically, their body language admitting defeat. Jodie’s body arches upward as the volts go through her, putting tension on her spine. The pool of blood on the ground beneath her grows as the holes in her back widen and close like small apertures.
zh_text: 他們把大大的電擊板貼到茱蒂胸口，動作很慢很有條理，身體語言透露出挫敗的訊息。電流過時，拉緊茱蒂的脊椎，讓她的身體向上拱起。背上的血洞開開闔闔，地上那灘血跡變大了。

en_text: “Again.”
zh_text: 「再來一次。」

en_text: They try it again. Then a third time. Then they go about packing everything away.
zh_text: 他們再試了一次，接著是第二次。然後他們開始收拾東西。

en_text: “I’m sorry,” one of them says.
zh_text: 「抱歉。」其中一人說。

en_text: “Do something else,” I say. “There is nothing else.” “There has to be.”
zh_text: 「再試試看。」我說。「沒有其他的辦法。」「應該有辦法的。」

en_text: “There’s too much damage. She’s too far gone. Even if we’d been here sooner there’s nothing we could have done. The gunshot—I’m sorry, mate,” he says, slowly shaking his head.
zh_text: 「傷勢太嚴重了。她早就走了。就算我們能早點到，也束手無策。槍傷——對不起，老兄。」他慢慢搖了搖頭。

en_text: “She can’t die like this.”
zh_text: 「她不能就這樣死了。」

en_text: “She’s already dead. She’s been dead from the moment she got hit.”
zh_text: 「她已經死了。她被打中的時候就死了。」

en_text: “No, no, you’re wrong. She’s supposed to die in another fifty years. We’re going to grow old together.”
zh_text: 「不對，不對，你說錯了。她要再過五十年才能死，我們要攜手到老。」

en_text: “Sorry, mate, I truly wish there was something we could do.”
zh_text: 「老兄，很抱歉，我真的很希望我們能想到其他的方法。」

en_text: I take a step toward him. He steps back. “You can do something,” I say. “You can save her.”
zh_text: 我對著他走了一步，他跟著後退。「你有辦法的，」我說，「你可以救她。」

en_text: His partner comes over. They’ve been in this situation before.
zh_text: 他的夥伴走過來，他們應該碰過類似的情况。

en_text: “I said help her.”
zh_text: 「我說了，快點救她。」

en_text: “I’m sorry, mate. We’ve done all we can.”
zh_text: 「老兄，很抱歉，我們已經盡力了。」

en_text: Armed police officers are filling the street. One of them heads toward us.
zh_text: 街上站滿了武装警察。其中一人走過來。

en_text: “Please,” I say. “There has to be something.”
zh_text: 「拜託，」我說，「一定有方法的。」

en_text: “I wish there was, I truly do,” he says, and then they walk away and head toward the bank, where two other paramedics are coming out, wheeling a gurney with the security guard on it who at the moment is still alive. The armed officer stops coming over and decides to give another officer a hand to string yellow police tape all over the place, making the street a lot more colorful, blending the crime scene into the Christmas atmosphere of town —tinsel, fake Santas, candy canes, fake snow, and real blood.
zh_text: 「我也希望有，眞的。」他說，然後他們朝著銀行走去，另外有兩名醫護人員從裡面出來，推著一具擔架，警衛躺在上面，他還活著。武裝警察停下了腳步，决定去幫另一名警察在周圍拉上黄色的警戒線，街道看起來顏色更繽紛了，犯罪現場融合了城裡的聖誕氛圍——金屬彩帶、假聖誕老人、枴杖糖、假雪和眞血。

en_text: I sit on the ground and hold my wife. I cradle her head in my lap and stroke her hair. I close her eyes but they keep opening up about halfway. The ground is blotted in blood and bandaging, there’s a bloody latex glove lying on her leg. A man in a suit comes up to me and crouches down. “I’m sorry for your loss,” he says, and I doubt he really understands the word “sorry” or the word “loss.” Nobody can. “The van, did you see a license plate? Did you see anything?”
zh_text: 我坐在地上，抱起妻子，把她的頭放在我的大腿上，輕撫她的頭髮。我想幫她闔上眼睛，但她的雙眼一直半開半闔。地上滿是血跡和繃帶，她腿上還丢了一只血跡斑斑的乳膠手套。一個穿西裝的男人走到我身邊蹲下來。「我很抱歉你失去了親人。」我想，他眞的懂得「抱歉」跟「失去」的意義嗎？沒有人能懂。「那部貨車，你看到車牌了嗎？可否把你看到的都告訴我。」

en_text: “They killed her.”
zh_text: 「他們殺了我的妻子。」

en_text: “Please, sir, this is important. If you . . .”
zh_text: 「对不起，先生，这件事情很重要。如果你···」

en_text: “They wanted a volunteer. Got to be twenty-five people in that bank. They could have taken anybody but they took Jodie. That’s a four percent chance. Calculate in that one person who was already dead, and that’s what? What?” I look up at him. “What the hell does that make it? Tell me!” I shout. “Tell me!”
zh_text: 「他們要一個人質。銀行裡起碼有二十五個人吧，選誰都可以卻偏偏選了茱蒂。被選上的機會只有百分之四。算出來的結果是這樣，但是有一個人已經死了，這是什麼意思？什麼意思？」我抬頭看他，「那到底算什麼？你能告訴我嗎？」我大吼，「告訴我！」

en_text: “The van. Did you see it?”
zh_text: 「搶匪的貨車，你看到了嗎？」

en_text: “All I could see was Jodie. I wish I saw more. I wish we’d never come here today. I wish . . .” I run out of words.
zh_text: 「我只看到茱蒂。我多麼希望我能多看她幾眼。我眞希望我們今天根本不要來銀行。我希望……」我說不下去了。

en_text: “Okay, okay, sir. You should step away from her now, you have to let us do our job.”
zh_text: 「好，好，先生。你可以站過去一點嗎？讓我們來處理。」

en_text: “Get away from me,” I say, and the words come out evenly and forcefully and he doesn’t argue. He steps away and I don’t watch where he goes. For a while nobody else approaches me. They see my dead wife and they know I didn’t shoot her so they leave me be. Somewhere else in the city they’re chasing the van, maybe they’ve caught it already. There’s been a shoot-out and all six bank robbers are dead. They’re all dying slowly from horrible, horrible gunshot wounds.
zh_text: 「走開。」我平静地吐出兩個字，勢不可當，他住口了。他轉身走開，我也不關心他往哪裡去。我獨自安靜了一會兒，沒有其他人靠過來。他們看到我死去的妻子，知道我不是兇手，就隨我去了。在城裡某處，警察正追著那台貨車跑，或許已經抓到搶匪了。經過一場槍戰，六個搶匪都死了。他們受了很嚴重很可怕的槍傷，死亡過程非常痛苦。

en_text: I want these people to be dead. I need them to be dead. Media vans speed into the street and brake heavily behind the barriers that have been set up. They jump out of their vans as if they’re on fire. Dozens of lenses and hundreds of eyes all staring at me, I’m sure some of them are making the connection, their synapses firing, thinking, we know that guy, we know that guy, their hunger for the story evident in the way their eyes almost bug out of their skulls as they stare in excitement, evident in the way they try to push past the officers forming a perimeter. I want to walk among them, wipe my wife’s blood on their faces, over their hands, I want to make them part of the story and ask them how it feels, ask how they can thrive on such suffering.
zh_text: 我要那六個人死掉。他們一定得死。新聞探訪車衝進這條街，在警方設好的路障後重重地緊急煞車。記者跳出車子，彷彿身上著了火。幾十個鏡頭對著我，幾百隻眼睛望著我，我想有些人已經想到了，他們的神經突觸火力全開，腦子轉個不停，我們認識這個人，我們看過這個人，們渴望挖出內幕，渴望到興奮盯著我的眼睛都快從腦殼中爆出來，渴望到他們想推開在外圍戒護的警察。我想走到他們中間，把我妻子的血抹在他們臉上和手上，我要他們也變成當事人，問他們有什麼感受，問他們在經歷這樣的痛苦後怎麼還能情緒高昂。

en_text: I don’t have the strength, and if I did, it would only add to their frenzy, offer up sound bites and make them more money. All I can do is cradle my wife and watch her become blurry as the anger and despair take their toll and the tears fall freely, dripping onto Jodie’s face.
zh_text: 我渾身無力，就算有力氣走過去，也只會讓他們更狂熱，拿到可以剪輯的關鍵字，賺更多的錢。我只能抱著我的妻子，看著她變得愈來愈模糊，任憤怒和絕望席捲全身，任眼淚毫不受控地落下來，滴在茱蒂的臉上。

en_text: Police push the barriers further back. They try clearing the street but the show is too good for these people to miss. Arguments turn into shouting matches. Some of the reporters yell questions at me. In the end the police are outnumbered. The police are always outnumbered. Reporters appear at the windows of neighboring buildings, filming us from the floors above.
zh_text: 警方擴大了警戒範圍。他們想把街上的人都趕走，但大家都不願意錯過這場精采的表演。有些記者對著我叫喊，問了好多問題。最後警察寡不敵衆，他們總是人手不夠。記者出現在隔壁幾棟大樓的窗口，從樓上對著我們拍攝。

en_text: A woman comes over and touches my shoulder and tells me it’s time to let Jodie go. I don’t want to, but I know I have to.
zh_text: 有個女人走過來，碰碰我的肩膀，說我該放開茱蒂了。我不肯，但我知道我必須放手。

en_text: “Get me something,” I say, “to put over her.” “Sir . . .”
zh_text: 「拿個東西來，」我說，「我要蓋在她身上。」「先生···」

en_text: “Please.”
zh_text: 「拜託妳。」

en_text: She comes back with a thick white sheet. I bunch up a corner of it into as good a pillow as I can make and prop it under Jodie’s head. I spread the rest over her. I step back and can’t pull myself away from the shape beneath it. I can still taste the lunch in my mouth, can still feel her hand in my hand as we walked to the bank.
zh_text: 她找了一塊厚厚的白布。我把一角摺起來弄成枕頭的樣子，好墊在茱蒂頭下，再把整塊布蓋在她身上。我後退了幾步，但我無法從白布下隆起的身子旁走開。我嘴巴裡還留著午餐的味道，掌心裡還有走向銀行時她手掌的觸感。

en_text: “We’ll take care of her,” the woman says, and she puts her hands on my arm. “Please, it’s time to come inside,” she says, and I let her lead me, my wife left outside, my wife an item now, a piece of evidence, and I crouch over and throw up before stepping back into the bank.
zh_text: 「我們會處理的。」女人說，然後把雙手放在我的手臂上。「請跟我到裡面去。」我讓她拉著我走，我的妻子留在外面，任人處理，是搶案的一項證據……還沒走進銀行，我就彎下身子吐了出來。

en_text: Where there is room, the cars pull over for him, his siren warning of the urgency. The problem is there isn’t always room and he gets caught up at intersections, boxed in by traffic that on Friday afternoons takes on a life of its own. Cars that try to pull over for him end up blocking the way, people panicking and almost causing accidents. Schroder’s already heard the bank robbers made a clean exit. Heard about the victims. There are plenty of armed officers on the scene but it’s all too late.
zh_text: 一有空間，其他的車子就閃開讓他先走，他的警笛狂閃，表示情況急迫。問題是別的車子沒有地方讓，在十字路口上寸步難行，被星期五下午難以控制的交通困住了。想讓他先過的車子反而堵住了車道，大家都很驚慌，幾乎要出車禍了。施羅德已經聽說搶匪乾淨俐落地逃走了。也聽說有人死傷。很多武装警察到了現場，可惜爲時已晚。

en_text: The entire block is cordoned off. Suction Cup Guy is out of Schroder’s mind as he parks outside the barriers, ducks under the police tape, and walks into the carnage. There’s a body in the middle of the street with a sheet over it. The woman. There are hundreds of onlookers and dozens of media and he figures, as bad as this is for the people who were in the bank, as bad as it is for the dead woman in the street, today is turning out to be a great day for the media and sightseers. A bad day for the cops is gold for the six o’clock news. A couple of street performers are hanging out behind everybody else, juggling bright-colored objects and trying to cash in on the gathering crowd.
zh_text: 整條街都被封鎖了。吸盤男早被施羅德抛到九雸雲外，他把車子停在警戒線外，彎身通過，進入殺戮現場。街道中央有一具覆了白布的屍體。那個女的。據他估算，看熱鬧的人有幾百個，媒體也有幾十家，銀行裡的人覺得今天倒楣透頂，路中間被殺的女人更是背到了極點，媒體和觀光客卻樂壞了。警察覺得傷腦筋，晚間六點鐘新聞卻挖到了寶藏。兩個街頭藝人在衆人身後徘徊不去，拿出閃亮的道具來抛擲，希望人潮能帶來生意。

en_text: Inside the bank people are pale, they’re lost and confused and there is streaked makeup from tears and swollen eyes. He’s the third detective on the scene, and he’s quickly given updates from the other two. There’s a body lying outside an office, this one exposed. He gives an instruction to cover it, hoping it will go some way to calming the witnesses.
zh_text: 銀行裡，每個人都臉色蒼白，他們很迷惘，有人的妆容上留下了淚痕，有人眼睛腫了。他是第三個到達現場的警探，前兩個很快把最新情況報告給他。辦公室外躺了一具屍體，沒蓋起來。他叫人也把這具屍體蓋上，希望能稍微安撫一下目擊者的情緒。

en_text: The husband of the woman killed is sitting in another office. “Edward Hunter,” one of the detectives says, pointing toward him. “Hunter?”
zh_text: 受害女性的丈夫坐在另一間辦公室裡。「艾德華·杭特。」一名警探指了指那名丈夫。「杭特？」

en_text: “Yeah. Why? You recognize him?”
zh_text: 「對，怎麼了？你認識他嗎？」

en_text: “I think so, but the name doesn’t line up. Anybody spoken to him yet?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「應該認識，但名字不太對。誰跟他談過了？」施羅德問。

en_text: “He only just came inside. We almost had to pull him away from his wife.”
zh_text: 「他才剛進來。我們差點得用拖的才能把他從太太身邊拉開。」

en_text: The office has new furniture and a rubber plant in the corner with leaves coated in dust. Schroder steps inside and closes the door and Edward Hunter looks up from the desk and watches him with eyes that are bloodshot.
zh_text: 辦公室裡的家具很新，角落放了一盆塑膠植物，葉面上都是灰塵。施羅德走進去，把門帶上，艾德華·杭特從桌前抬眼看著他，眼睛滿是血絲。

en_text: “It’s colder in here than before,” Edward says, then pulls his shirt away from his body. It’s covered in blood and sticking against him.
zh_text: 「這裡的溫度降低了。」艾德華說，把襯衫從身上拉開。他的襯衫沾滿血跡，已經黏在身上了。

en_text: Outside the office more people are arriving, other detectives to take statements. Men in white nylon suits are scouring the scene for evidence—the problem is the scene has been trampled over by too many people already.
zh_text: 辦公室外的人愈來愈多，幾名警探開始做筆錄。穿著白色尼龍袍的人開始搜查證據問題是現場人來人往，已經被破壤得差不多了。

en_text: “My name is Carl Schroder,” he says, sitting down opposite Edward and not offering to shake hands, “and I know this is difficult, I know answering questions is the last thing you want to do right now, but you . . .”
zh_text: 「我叫卡爾·施羅德。」說著，他坐到艾德華對面，免了握手的禮節。「我知道很難，我知道你現在壓根不想回答問題，但是你……」

en_text: “Not difficult,” Edward answers. “Impossible.”
zh_text: 「不難，」艾德華回答，「不可能。」

en_text: “You’re right. It is impossible.” He pauses, taking in the impossibility of the situation. He isn’t the one who woke up today and lost his wife. “Are you married?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「沒錯，不可能。」他停下來，確認不可能的程度。今天出門後失去愛妻的並不是他。「你結婚了嗎？」艾德華問。

en_text: “Please, we need to focus . . .”
zh_text: 「抱歉，我們得專心···」

en_text: “You imagine what it’d be like if that was your wife out there?” “I’d want the men who did this caught.”
zh_text: 「想想看，如果是你老婆躺在外面，你會怎麼辦？」「我會希望兇手被抓起來。」

en_text: “You mean you haven’t found them yet?”
zh_text: 「你的意思是說，你們還沒找到搶匪？」

en_text: “We’re working on it, Edward. It is Edward, right? Not Jack?” “I didn’t give you my name.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，我們正在努力。你的名字是艾德華，對吧？不是傑克？」「我還沒說我叫什麼名字。」

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “Jack’s my father’s name, not mine, not anymore. Which means you recognize me. Everybody recognizes me.”
zh_text: 「傑克是我爸爸的名字，我不叫傑克，我改名字了。所以，你認出我來了。大家都認得我。」

en_text: “Well, I don’t know about that.”
zh_text: 「那個嘛···我不知道。」

en_text:
“It’s true. You recognized me. You didn’t know whether to call me Jack or Edward, so you knew. Everybody knows.”
“I recognized you because I was there the day your dad was arrested.” “Yeah?”
zh_text:
「真的，你認得我。你不知道要叫我傑克還是艾德華，所以你知道我是誰。大家都知道。」「我認得出你，因爲你爸爸被逮捕那天我也在場。」
「眞的嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah,” he answers. It was his first year on the force. He hadn’t spoken to Jack Hunter Sr., or really been anywhere near him. He’d been one of the constables who’d come along for the ride. He got a real good look at Jack Hunter Junior, the young boy, full of tears and pain.
zh_text: 「眞的。」他答道。那是他當警察的第一年。他沒跟傑克·杭特一世說到話，也沒有機會靠近他。他只是隨行警察中的一員。他倒把傑克·杭特二世看了個清楚，那個小男孩，满臉眼淚和傷痛。

en_text: “I remember you,” Jack—now Edward—says. “But not from then. From the year after. You were the one who came when Mum died.”
zh_text: 「我看過你，」現在叫作艾德華的傑克說，「但不是那時候。再過一年。我媽死的時候你來了。」

en_text: “I know,” Schroder answers. That was his second year on the force. He and his partner had gone inside and found the woman in the bathtub. He can still recall exactly how she looked, how the bathroom felt, can picture the emptiness in her eyes. Edward and his sister were sitting on the bathroom floor, the sister with her arm around Edward, both of them leaning against the wall, Edward unable to take his eyes from the floor. Schroder and his partner had gone in and taken the children out before examining the body. The sister had told them what had happened. Edward never said a word.
zh_text: 「我知道。」施羅德回答。那是他進入警界的第二年。他跟夥伴進到屋子裡，發現那女人在浴缸裡。他仍能想起她確切的模樣和進入浴室後的感覺，還有她眼中的空洞。艾德華和姊姊坐在浴室地板上，姊姊摟著艾德華，兩人都靠在牆上，艾德華的眼晴緊緊盯著地板。施羅德和夥伴進去後，先把孩子帶出去，再回頭檢查屍體。姊姊告诉他們發生了什麼事。艾德華則一語不發。

en_text: “You’re always there when my family is hurting,” Edward says, and Schroder can see the little boy all those years ago in this man now. “And you’ve never made it any better. Am I a suspect in this, now that you know who I am?” his voice getting louder. Angrier.
zh_text: 「我家出事時總會看到你。」艾德華說，施羅德在眼前的男人身上看到多年前那個小男孩。「每次見你，一次比一次糟。現在你知道我是誰，那我是不是也變成嫌犯了？」他提高了聲量，語氣更加憤怒。

en_text: “Of course not. Why would you think that?”
zh_text: 「當然不是。你爲什麼會往那個方向想？」

en_text: “People always think weird shit like that. I’ve grown up with it.”
zh_text: 「每個人都會想到那種無聊愚蠢的東西。我這輩子已經受夠了。」

en_text: “What I need from you is to focus, Edward. I know this is hard,” he says, “but this is the time where you can help the most.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，我需要你專心想一想，我知道不容易，」他說，「但這個時候我們只能靠你了。」

en_text: “They just, they just came into the bank,” Edward says, shaking his head as he talks and turning his palms up, “you know? Just came in like they owned the place. The way they shot the manager, they didn’t care. They didn’t have to kill anybody. They were getting their money and . . . I mean, why do that? Why take the time to do that? Even when it was all done, they took Jodie with them. Why would they do that?”
zh_text: 「他們就……就這麼走進銀行，」艾德華說著搖了搖頭，兩手一攤，「你知道嗎？就這麼走進來，好像銀行是他們開的。他們就這麼殺了經理，一點也不在乎。他們不需要殺人。錢都拿到了……我是說，爲什麼？爲什麼要殺人拖延時間？最後拿到錢了，甚至還要把茱蒂帶走。爲什麼要費這麼大功夫？」

en_text: “We’ve heard from other witnesses the men said they wanted a volunteer.”
zh_text: 「聽其他的目擊者說，他們要一個志願者。」

en_text: “I tried to get them to take me.”
zh_text: 「我叫他們帶我走。」

en_text: “I know you did. They also said you saved one of the tellers from being taken, maybe even saving her life.”
zh_text: 「我知道。他們還說，你阻止他們帶走出納員，她的命應該算是你救的。」「什麼？」

en_text: “What?” “They say you called out. They say the men were going to take her, and you stopped them. That was a brave thing,” he says, trying to prompt Edward. “A brave thing, risking your life.”
zh_text: 「他們說你喊了一聲。他們說搶匪要把她帶走，你阻止他們。你很勇敢，」他想給艾德華一點鼓勵，「很勇敢，拿自己的生命冒險。」

en_text: “Yeah, it wasn’t my life I risked in the end, was it? They were going to take her and they took Jodie instead.”
zh_text: 「對，可是最後我不是拿自己的生命冒險，對不對？他們要把出納員帶走，最後抓走了茱蒂。」

en_text: “You couldn’t have known that.” “You think?”
zh_text: 「你也不可能想到最後會是這樣。」「你真這麼以爲？」

en_text: “It’s a fact. It’s a bad situation, Edward, a bad situation and people died, and you’re the only one in that bank who had the balls to try and do something about it, to try and save somebody’s life, and that woman is alive thanks to you.”
zh_text: 「這是事實。艾德華，當時的情況很嚴重，嚴重到有人死了，銀行裡只有你有膽量開口，想要救大家的性命，那出納員還活著，都是你的功勞。」

en_text: “It’s a shitty flip side, right? She’s alive because of me and my wife is dead for the same reason. It’s no different from me pulling the trigger myself.”
zh_text: 「另一方面結果卻很慘，對不對？因爲我，她還活著，也因爲我，我妻子卻死了。跟我自己開槍殺人沒什麼兩樣。」

en_text: “It’s very different,” he says.
zh_text: 「不一樣，真的不一樣。」施羅德說。

en_text: “All the people in here and they took her. They didn’t need to take anybody.”
zh_text: 「裡面有這麼多人，他們偏偏要挑她，他們根本不需要帶走人質。」

en_text: Schroder knows exactly why they took her. They wanted somebody dead out on the road. They wanted to use up more police resources. It creates confusion and panic and gives them more of a lead time. It shuts down traffic into the street, creates congestion, slows down the roads in and out of town, the cars that had stopped outside the bank are still out there, blocked in. He doesn’t tell Edward any of this. Doesn’t tell him that his wife was a tool, a device they used to help them escape.
zh_text: 施羅德確實知道搶匪爲什麼要把她帶走。他們要耗盡警方的資源。弄得一團亂，搞得人心惶惶，他們更有時間逃走。街上的交通因此大亂，停在銀行外的車子仍然動彈不得。他沒對艾德華明說。他不想告訴艾德華他妻子被利用了，搶匪利用他的妻子來逃脫。

en_text: “There was nothing you could have done,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「你也無能爲力。」施羅德說。

en_text: “You’re wrong on that. There was everything I could have done. I could have made the appointment for a different time. I could have kept my mouth shut and let that other woman get taken. Maybe they wouldn’t have killed her. I could have fought more, could have insisted they take me instead.”
zh_text: 「你錯了。我有很多方法。我應該約另一個時間來銀行。我應該閉嘴不要講話，讓另外那個女人被帶走。或许他們不會殺死她。我應該要更努力抗爭，應該堅持他們把我帶走。」

en_text: “It’s not your fault.”
zh_text: 「那不是你的錯。」

en_text: “Then why does it feel like it is?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼我覺得都是我的錯？」

en_text: “We have to focus, Edward, on finding the men who did this.” “I know. I know.”
zh_text: 「不要離題了，艾德華，我們要找到那些搶匪。」我懂，我知道。

en_text: “Then it’s time to tell me what happened. Start at the beginning,” he says.
zh_text: 「那你該詳細告诉我發生了什麼事，從頭開始。」

en_text: “Okay,” Edward says, tears slowly sliding down his face. Schroder takes out his notebook and writes it all down.
zh_text: 「好。」眼淚慢慢滑下艾德華的臉頰。施羅德掏出筆記本，記下所有的細節。

en_text: I’m given a lift home. The sun is past its peak and the city seems darker now. The shadows cast by the tired buildings are small but ominous, the people on the streets appear defeated, those caught in half shadows are dazed, the trees and plants and flowers that make up the garden city have all lost their vibrancy—the life is draining out of the world. We pass rundown fruit stalls on the side of the road, FOR SALE signs in front of houses that people want to leave. The blood on my clothes is drying, the color fading from bright red to deep maroon, my body itchy where the stains are stiff and scratchy. With every passing second the distance between me and Jodie stretches, and the hope of getting her back finally turns into the despair it was the moment I saw her gunned down. This is my city, my home, the place I loved but love no more. Now I don’t know what it is. Certainly not my home. Not now. Now it’s the place that killed my wife and took my daughter’s mother away. Now it’s a hellhole and I don’t see any future here.
zh_text: 我搭警察的便車回家。太陽已經開始下沉，整座城似乎更暗了。老舊的建築物在地上留下的影子雖短，卻宛如惡魔般可怕，街上的人兒拖著挫敗的腳步，在半明半暗間的臉龐一片茫然，基督城號稱花園城，但樹木花草都失去了活力——放眼望去只有死氣沉沉。在路邊看到了廢棄的水果攤，想離開的人在屋子前豎起「出售」的招牌。衣服上的血水慢慢乾了，從鮮紅色褪成暗棗紅色，僵硬的血漬刮著我的皮膚，讓我開始發癢。每過一秒，我和茱蒂之間的距離就更拉長了一些，期待她能起死回生的心情終究化成看到她被槍殺的絕望。我住在這座城裡，這是我的家，但我對基督城的熱愛已經消失了。我不知道這裡是哪裡，絕對不是我的家。現在我沒有家。這座城害死了我的妻子，奪走我女兒的母親，比地獄還不如，我在這裡看不到未來。

en_text: The officer driving doesn’t say anything. He’s never gotten around to preparing any rhetorical conversation for this exact situation. It’s a thirty-minute drive in busy traffic in which the world goes by and I wonder how I can change it. He’s relieved when he lets me out in my driveway. I’ve taken a car ride away from one reality to a new one. There aren’t any neighbors walking about or working in their gardens. The houses are all dirty, the plants and trees all too dry, the cars old and the sidewalks cracked, the colors everywhere seem so diluted. There are brief moments—less than a second—where I’m distracted and Jodie is still alive, small lifetime moments like putting my key in the door—bang! A distraction—and the world is okay. Then that split second passes and reality floods back in, crushing me.
zh_text: 開車的警官不發一語，他還沒來得及爲我的情況準備好冠冕堂皇的對話。在擁擠的車陣中走了三分鐘，世界依然在轉，我不知道我該如何改變一切。終於到了我家的車道，他讓我下車，也鬆了一口氣。搭了一趟便車，從一個實境轉到另一個實境。路上沒有鄰居，也沒有人在花園裡整理。所有的房子都很髒，植物和樹木都太乾枯了，路面裂開，眼前的顏色似乎都失去了飽和度。有幾刻——不超過一秒的時間內——我失了魂，而茱蒂還活著，就在生活中那一瞬間，譬如把鑰匙插進門鎖裡的時候，砰！我的心思渙散，一切都没事了。然後那一瞬間過去了，現實如潮水般湧入，把我壓垮。

en_text: It’s almost four o’clock and Sam has been picked up from school by Jodie’s parents. One of the detectives arranged it. One of them made the call so I didn’t have to, and I don’t know who broke the news to them first, the detective or the media. From a stranger they learned their daughter had the misfortune of getting herself gunned down this afternoon, had the misfortune of being married to a man who couldn’t keep his mouth shut, and they’d need to pick their granddaughter up from school.
zh_text: 快四點了，茱蒂的父母已經把小珊從學校接回他們家。是警方安排的，一位警員打電話告訴他們，免得我還得打過去，我不知道消息怎麼傳到他們耳中，是探長說的，還是媒體報導。他們從陌生人口中聽到他們的女兒今天下午不幸被槍殺，不幸嫁給一個不懂得該閉緊嘴巴的男人，所以得從學校把外孫女接回來。

en_text:
