“Please,” he says, and holds his hand up. “You were doing the right thing. Me, in that situation, I don’t know what I’d have done. Maybe nothing. I’d have been a coward and let that woman get shot, most probably. But you stood up. You didn’t know you were risking Jodie—all you knew was you were risking yourself. You did a good thing, but part of me is always going to hate you for that, Eddie, and I can’t help that.”
zh_text: 「拜託，」他舉手要我住口，「你一點也沒錯。我，要碰到那種情況，我不知道該怎麼辦。或许束手無策。很有可能我會當個懦夫，讓搶匪殺了那女人。但你站出來了。當時你並不知道你會用茱蒂的性命來冒險——你只知道你冒著生命危險講話了。你做得很好，但我心裡永遠會有一點恨你，艾迪，我克制不了。」

en_text: “I get it. A big part me—hell, all of me hates me too for doing it.”
zh_text: 「我懂。我覺得混帳，我恨死我自己了。」

en_text: “I know that. Weigh it all up, spread out the blame, and shit, Eddie, it wasn’t your fault. It was the men who came into that bank. They’re the ones responsible. Not you. And we want to let you know how much we’re relying on you now. It’s your job to take care of that little girl. You have to give up everything you can to make sure she’s raised right. And no matter what, we’re always going to be here for her. And for you. Remember that, Eddie. Remember that and you’ll do okay.”
zh_text: 「我明白。好好思量，把錯怪到別人頭上，媽的，艾迪，不是你的錯。犯錯的是那些搶匪，他們才該負責。不是你。我們要你知道，我們現在只能靠你了。你得負責照顧我們的外孫女。你必須放棄一切，確定你會把她好好養大。不論怎樣，我們一定會支持她，也支持你。艾迪，别忘了，别忘了我的話，你就不會有問題。」

en_text: He puts his hand on my shoulder. It’s warm and comforting. For the briefest second I believe him that everything is going to be okay. I take another drink of the beer.
zh_text: 他把手放在我的肩膀上，溫暖的手心帶來安慰。就在那一瞬間，我相信他的話，一切都會恢復正常。我又喝了一口啤酒。

en_text: It’s in your blood.
zh_text: 你天生就是那樣。

en_text: “Sorry?” I say.
zh_text: 「什麼？」我問。

en_text: “I said you’ll do okay.”
zh_text: 「我說，你不會有問題的。」

en_text: “No, after that. You said something after that.” “No, I’m pretty sure I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「然後呢？你又說了一句話。」

en_text: Suddenly I’m also sure he didn’t. It’s in your blood. It was the same voice I heard earlier, the one that told me I’d be hearing from it soon, and now I recognize it. It’s been almost twenty years, but it’s the voice from when I was a kid and the neighbor’s dog wouldn’t stop barking. It’s my dad’s monster—it found me twice when I was nine, and now it’s found me again.
zh_text: 「沒有，我就閉嘴了。」突然之間，我也確定他沒說話。你天生就是那樣。那是我之前聽到的聲音，那個聲音說它會回來，我認出來了。快二十年了，但那就是我小時候鄰居的狗叫個不停時我聽到的聲音。那是我爹的怪物一九歲的時候它來找我兩次，現在又回到我身邊了。

en_text: It’s dark by the time we get home. It’s a three-quarter moon. It throws white light over the house and reflects off the front windows and makes the house look very empty. I park the car in the driveway and can’t be bothered putting it in the garage. Jodie’s car is still parked in town near her work and can stay there a while longer yet. I grab the mail and take Sam inside. One of the things about the new house we were going to get was it had an adjoining garage. It was something we both wanted, because of the brutal Christchurch winters.
zh_text: 我們到家時天已經黑了。夜空上的月亮是檸檬的形狀，白色的月光灑在房子上，照亮了前方的窗戶，讓我們家看起來特別空蕩蕩。我把車停在車道上，懶得停進車庫裡。茱蒂的車子還在城裡靠近她辦公室的地方，可以再停幾天。我取出郵件，把小珊抱進家裡。我們要買的新房子很不錯，會有跟房子連在一起的車庫。我們兩個都想要這樣的車庫，因為基督城的冬天酷寒無比。

en_text: Jodie doesn’t have to worry about that anymore, now, does she . . .
zh_text: 茱蒂现在不用再擔心車庫的問題了，對吧···

en_text: “Shut up,” I whisper.
zh_text: 「閉嘴。」我輕聲說。

en_text: “What, Daddy?” Sam asks, her voice sleepy, her eyes half closed.
zh_text: 「爸爸，你說什麼？」小珊問，她的嗓音睡意濃濃，眼睛半開半闧。

en_text: “Nothing, honey,” I say, and I carry her inside.
zh_text: 「没事，小乖。」我把她抱到房子裡。

en_text: The house has gotten tidier over the last couple of days mainly because I found myself wandering through the rooms, never really sure what to do. Sometimes I’d spend hours in front of the TV, watching the news and staring at whatever else was on. Other times I’d surf the net, looking for updates on the case. Most of the time people would show up to spend time with us. Sam kept mostly to herself. Mogo would show up for food and nothing else. I’d clean the house sporadically, sometimes cleaning the same room only an hour after I’d last done it. I’d play with Sam. We’d watch TV together. We’d sit outside together. It was tough.
zh_text: 過去這兩天，家裡變得比較整潔了，主要是因爲我總從這個房間晃到那個房間，不知道要做什麼。有時候我會在電視機前面待好幾個小時看新聞，或盯著畫面看。有時候我會上網，尋找搶案是否有最新的進展。常有人來探訪我們。小珊總是悶悶不樂。魔菇現身只爲了進食。我偶爾會打掃，有時候過了一個小時又把同一個房間整理一次。我會陪小珊玩，一起看電視，一起到外面坐著。時間很難熬。

en_text: I carry Sam down to her bedroom. I keep searching for a glimpse of my wife, a shadow, a movement somewhere, something to let me know in some way she is still here. I lay Sam on her bed—Disney characters scattered in the pattern of the bedspread. She’s asleep again. I get her into her pajamas. She wakes a little but is too tired to help.
zh_text: 我把小珊送到她的臥房裡。雙眼尋找妻子的蹤跡，一道陰影，一個動作，能讓我知道她還在這裡就好了。我把小珊放在床上丨她的床罩圖案是迪士尼的卡通人物。她又睡著了。我幫她換上睡衣，她醒了一下子，但累到無法幫上忙。

en_text: I grab a beer from the fridge. I never bought any, but since Saturday friends have been showing up to share their sorrow with me, the women bringing wine, the men, beer, and in the beginning I thought I had enough to last me a lifetime, but now I’m not so sure. Now I think there might only be enough here for a few days. I settle in front of the TV and wait for the news to come on. The bank robbery, the funerals, they don’t even lead the news anymore. The lead story is about a seventy-five-year-old woman who, in the parking lot of a shopping mall, mistook her car for an identical-colored and almost identical-shaped vehicle parked next to it. The owner, seeing her putting her key into his lock, rushed over and shoved her so hard she fell over, hit her head on the sidewalk, and was pronounced dead at the scene. The second story is about a turned-over truck that allowed a few dozen sheep to escape on a notorious stretch of highway in the North Island. Nobody was killed. Then come the funerals, snippets from them both in a montage with slow classical music playing over the top of it, like it’s a movie preview. The coffins are different colors and styles, and everybody is dressed smartly. My daughter gets a lot of attention—it shows us following the coffin. Another daughter—three times Sam’s age—follows the other coffin. Then at the end of the story a brief report saying the men haven’t been captured, and that any member of the public with information is asked to call the hotline listed below.
zh_text: 我從冰箱拿了一瓶啤酒。我沒買酒，但從星期六以來，很多朋友到我們家致哀，女人送來葡萄酒，男人送來啤酒，一開始我還以爲這輩子都喝不完了，現在我可不確定。我想，可能夠喝幾天吧。我坐在電視機前，等新聞播報。銀行搶案跟葬禮已經不是頭條新聞了。最新的新聞是一名七十五歲的婦人在購物中心的停車場裡看錯了自己的車子，她旁邊正好停了一台同樣顏色、外型也很類似的車子。車主看到她把自己的鑰匙插進他的車子裡，急忙奔過來阻止，卻把她一把推倒，婦人的頭撞到地上，結果當場死亡。第二則新聞則是卡車翻覆，幾十隻綿羊跑到北島高速公頭，配上緩慢的古典音樂，很像電影預告片。兩具棺木的顏色和風格不太一樣，大家都穿得很正式。我女兒是新聞的焦點丨螢幕上播出我們跟在棺木後的樣子。另一個女兒年紀是小珊的三倍，跟在另一具棺木後面。播到最後，記者簡短報告搶匪尚未落網，民衆若有消息，可以撥打下面的專線。

en_text: I finish the beer and grab another. I open up the mail. There are two letters from the bank. The first one is brief.
zh_text: 我喝完啤酒，又拿了一瓶。翻了翻郵件，有兩封是銀行寄來的。第一封很簡短。

en_text: Dear Mr. Hunter,
zh_text: 杭特先生您好：

en_text: In what must be a very difficult time for you and your family, we at south pacific bank would like to offer our sincerest condolences for the loss of your wife.
zh_text: 此刻對您與家人來說想必非常艱辛。南太平洋銀行的全體人員爲尊夫人之不幸深感抱歉，謹此獻上最誠摯的慰問。

en_text: The tragic incident that happened outside the bank has touched the entire staff and, needless to say, you and your family remain in our thoughts and our prayers. Sincerely,
zh_text: 銀行外發生的悲慘事件讓本行人員痛心疾首，本行致上最高的歉意，並爲您與家人的平安喜樂禱告。

en_text: Dean Wellington
zh_text: 狄恩·威靈頓敬上

en_text: I read the letter a couple of times, looking at the words Dean Wellington used. He managed to sum the entire murder of my wife as an “incident” and convey his horror at it all in two paragraphs. I wonder if he used the words “outside the bank” specifically, hoping it will absolve any responsibility the branch has toward what happened.
zh_text: 我把這封信反覆讀了兩次，凝視狄恩·威靈頓的用詞。他用兩段文字，把我妻子被殺這整件事歸納成「事件」，也表達出他的震驚。不知道他是否特別強調「銀行外」這三個字，希望能免除他們分行在這件事上的責任。

en_text: The second letter isn’t as brief. It’s obviously a form letter with a brief scrawl of a signature at the bottom. It’s been overnighted down from Auckland, meaning they must have gotten to work on our loan application within hours of Jodie dying.
zh_text: 第二封信比較長，顯然是現成的內容在下面加一個潦草的簽名。從奥克蘭寄限時過來，表示一定在茱蒂過世後的幾小時內他們就處理了我們的貸款申請。

en_text: Mr. Edward Hunter,
zh_text: 艾德華·杭特先生：

en_text: Unfortunately, as you know, the property market at this current time is extremely volatile, which requires us to tighten the criteria on which we base our home loans.
zh_text: 時機不巧，您也知道，此刻的房地產市場極端反覆無常，因此我們必須縮緊房貸申請的標準。

en_text: Based on these criteria, we are unable to approve your application at this time.
zh_text: 根據這些標準，我們無法核准您的申請。

en_text: I read on. The letter goes on for another page, listing some of the criteria that I no longer fit. In the end I skim over the details and go right to the end.
zh_text: 我讀下去。下一頁列出我再也不符合的標準。最後我跳過細節，直接看信尾怎麼說。

en_text: As the market is in a constant state of change, we would be happy to review this decision at a later date. in the meantime, we hope that we can continue to assist you with all your banking needs. Yours sincerely,
zh_text: 由於市場變化不斷，我們很樂意之後再度審核這次的決定。而在下次審核之前，如果您需要任何服務，我們也希望能爲您效勞。

en_text: Katie Hughes I read the letter a second time, finishing off my second beer, the anger burning inside me, and yet I feel no disbelief at all. Katie Hughes must have typed this letter up pretty damn fast. I check the postmark and see it got posted on Saturday. I wonder if Hughes or Wellington spent an expensive Friday afternoon with lawyers to see where they stood on the whole “incident.” I finish a third beer while flicking through the phone book.
zh_text: 我重讀了一次，喝完第二瓶啤酒，一股怒火在胸口燃燒，但我一點也不懷疑自己的眼睛。凱蒂·休斯一定很快就把這封信打好了。我檢查郵戳，發現信在星期六寄出。我猜休斯或威靈頓星期五一定花了一大筆錢找律師商量他們對整個「事件」該探取什麼態度。我邊翻電話簿，邊喝第三瓶啤酒。凱蒂·休斯敬上

en_text: I’m not sure why I do it, but I look Dean Wellington up and write down his address before finishing off a third beer and deciding it might be about time to head off to bed.
zh_text: 我不知道爲什麼，但是我找到了狄恩·威靈頓的資訊，在喝完第三瓶啤酒前就把他的地址抄下來，然後決定我該上床睡覺了。

en_text: I wake up and everything is as it should be. My wife is alive. We’ve bought the new house. Sam is Sam and Mogo is being Mogo. Then those thoughts become blurred, my bedroom comes into focus, and Jodie isn’t in bed next to me. I reach over and her side is cold, untouched, and then it all comes racing back, as it did yesterday morning, and every morning since the . . . for some reason I think accident but that’s the wrong word. Since the what?
zh_text: 睁眼醒來，一切都很正常。我妻子還活著。我們買了新房子。小珊跟平常一樣，魔菇也跟平常一樣。然後這些念頭變得朦朧，房間變得清晰，而茱蒂不在床的另一邊。我伸手過去，她那半邊好冰冷，沒有人睡過，然後發生過的事情全部急速回到我眼前，就跟昨天早上一樣，還有···之後的每天早上，不知爲何我想到「意外」，可是不太恰當。自從什麼以後？

en_text: The execution the voice says, and I agree, though Dean Wellington would say “incident.”
zh_text: 那聲音說處決，我同意，雖然狄恩·威靈頓用了「事件」這個詞。

en_text: It’s after eight already. Normally Sam would be up watching cartoons and making a mess, but this morning she’s still asleep, the last few days . . .
zh_text: 已經過了八點。通常小珊早就起來看卡通把家裡弄得一團亂，不過今天早上她還在睡，過去幾天自從：

en_text: Since the execution . . .
zh_text: 自從處決以後···

en_text: The last few days since the execution she’s been sleeping later.
zh_text: 自從處決以後，這幾天她都睡得比較晚。

en_text: I sit on the porch and eat cereal directly out of the packet. The Tuesday-morning sun is slowly climbing into the sky. There’s a truck and a cherry picker out in the street about half a block away, motors and chainsaws making plenty of noise as they trim tops of trees away from the power lines. My head is slightly fuzzy and my mouth feels like I spent time last night licking the carpet. The cereal is dry and sticks to the roof of it. I think about work and the file I should be working on, and whether not going in today and no longer giving a damn about it means I no longer have a job. I wonder what kind of letter Dean Wellington would send if he knew I was dropping from one income down to none.
zh_text: 我坐在門廊上，直接從盒子裡把穀片倒出來吃掉。星期二早晨的太陽慢慢升入空中。離我家半條街的地方有台卡車和活動起重機，有人在修剪樹木，免得樹枝搭上電線，馬達和電鋸震天價響。我有點昏眩，嘴巴乾得像我一整晚都在舔地毯。穀片乾巴巴的，黏住了上顎。我想到工作，想到我該處理的檔案，我今天該去上班嗎？算了，反正我已經沒有工作了。如果狄恩·威靈頓知道我家從一份收入變成沒有收入，不知道會寫什麼樣的信給我。

en_text: The phone rings and I head inside for it, wanting to stop it from waking Sam.
zh_text: 電話響了，我走進屋裡接起電話，不想讓鈴聲吵醒小珊。

en_text: “Jack?”
zh_text: 「傑克？」

en_text: The voice is familiar in the way you can flick on the radio and hear a song you haven’t heard in twenty years and know how it goes. When you hear that song, your mind starts scrambling, taking you back to a time when you heard it last. Good memory or bad, you’re in that moment again, the smells, the sounds, the sights, they’re all there.
zh_text: 那聲音很熟悉，就像撥開了收音機的開關，聽到一首二十年前聽過的歌，知道要怎麼唱。聽到那首歌的時候，你覺得一團混亂，彷彿回到上一次聽到歌曲的時候。不論是不是美好的記憶，你又回到那個時刻，聞到同樣的味道，聽到同樣的聲音，看到同樣的景象。

en_text: “Who is this?” I ask, and I remember the handcuffs, the police, the smile on his face when he watched me from the back of the police car. I remember the dog, I remember the weight of the piece of steak in the plastic bag. I can feel the cold sunlight, my school uniform, my mother holding my hand and holding Belinda’s hand. I can remember the neighbors pouring out of their houses, the women with their hands over their mouths in shock, the men shaking their heads, the long line of police cars, dozens of cops, all showing up in force as if to arrest a small army. I remember the media vans, the photographers.
zh_text: 「你是誰？」我問，我想起手銬、警察、他從警車後座回頭看我時臉上帶的笑容。我想起了那條狗，想起了塑膠袋裡裝著牛排的沉重感覺。我能感覺到冰冷的陽光、學校的制服、母親一手拉著我一手拉著貝琳達。我想到鄰居在家對著我們指指點點，女人吃驚地用手掩住嘴巴、男人搖頭、一長列警車、幾十個警察，這麼大批的警力似乎要來逮捕一支軍隊。我想起新聞探訪車，想起了攝影師。

en_text: “Jack, it’s me. It’s your father.”
zh_text: 「傑克，是我，你爸爸。」

en_text: I don’t say anything. The kitchen disappears, the world disappears, all fading away as the front door of my childhood home appears, the policemen, the disgust on their faces. Of course that childhood home is gone now. About three months after Mum died, when I was living with Belinda at my grandparents’, somebody went along and set fire to that house. Nobody was ever caught. I always thought maybe Belinda did it, but it could have been anybody. Dad hurt a lot of people.
zh_text: 我不發一語。廚房消失了，世界消失了，一切都不見了，童年住所的前門出現了，警察來了，满臉僧惡。童年的家當然早就沒了。母親過世後三個月，我跟貝琳達住在祖父母家裡，有人把那棟房子燒了。警察沒抓到縱火犯。我一直以爲是貝琳達幹的，也有可能是別人。爹傷害了很多人。

en_text: “I’m calling to—”
zh_text: 「我打這通電話是要——」

en_text: “I don’t care why you’re calling,” I say, and I tighten my hand on the phone and for some reason, for some freaky-shit-get-the-hell-out-of-here kinda reason, I don’t hang up.
zh_text: 「我不在乎你爲什麼打來。」我抓緊了話筒，不知道爲什麼，不知道爲什麼他媽的狗屁倒灶的原因，我沒掛掉電話。

en_text: “I’m calling to tell you how sorry I am.”
zh_text: 「我打電話來，想告訴你我很抱歉。」

en_text: I let his sentence hang and he waits patiently. I guess my father is used to being patient.
zh_text: 我沒有立刻答腔，爹很有耐心地等待。我猜我父親一直都很有耐心

en_text: “You’ve had twenty years to apologize,” I say. “Anyway, you’re saying it to the wrong person, and you picked the worst damn time to do it.”
zh_text: 「二十年了，你終於說了一句道歉的話。」我說。「反正你找錯人了，你選的時機也糟透了」

en_text: “Not . . . not about the past, Jack. I’m ringing to tell you how sorry I am about Jodie. I wish things had been different. For her. For you. For everybody.”
zh_text: 「不……傑克，跟過去無關。我想打電話告訴你，我很抱歉茱蒂過世了。我眞希望這些事都不曾發生。對她好，對你好，對大家都好。」

en_text: “How the hell do you know about Jodie?” I ask. “How do you know a damn thing about me or Jodie?”
zh_text: 「你怎麼知道茱蒂的事？」我問，「你怎麼知道我跟茱蒂碰到什麼鬼事？」

en_text: “This isn’t the moon they’re keeping us locked away on, Jack.” “Don’t call me that.”
zh_text: 「我們又不是被關在月球上，傑克。」不要叫我那個名字。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Jack. Don’t call me Jack.”
zh_text: 「傑克，不要叫我傑克。」

en_text: “Oh? What am I supposed to call you?”
zh_text: 「噢？那我要叫你什麼？」

en_text: “Don’t call me anything. What the hell do you want? You ringing to tell me you know what it’s like to lose somebody? Like the way you lost Mum and Belinda?”
zh_text: 「不必管我叫什麼。你他媽的想幹囌？你打電話來，想告訴我你懂得失去親人的感受？就像你失去了媽媽和貝琳達？」

en_text: “I know you’re angry at me.”
zh_text: 「我知道你生我的氣。」

en_text: “No. How could I possibly be angry at you? You’ve really been there for me, a real role model.”
zh_text: 「不，我爲什麼要生你的氣？你一直都很支持我，眞是我的好榜樣。」

en_text: “Jack . . .”

“What do you want, Dad?” I ask, immediately nauseous at how comfortable the word “Dad” feels in my mouth. I’m nine years old all over again. The photo that told the world I was the son of a serial killer flashes into my mind. The memory turns as black and white as the picture. I’m holding on to my father, the police are taking him away, and my mum is trying to separate us, black-and-white tears spilling down my black-and-white face. The policemen weren’t friendly toward any of us. None of them wanted to touch me or push me away, as if they feared the killer gene they were so sure I would inherit could contaminate them, that it would jump from me and land on their hands and burrow under their skin. It would tell them bad things and make them suck on the end of a pistol at the end of a long tiring day. They looked at my mother and my sister and me with open hatred, so sure all of us had been in on the action, that Dad had brought the hookers home for the holidays, that we’d taken turns at draining the life out of them, raping them, a good-ol’-splasharoo in blood, the son and daughter committing the sins of the mother and father.
zh_text: 「爹，你到底想幹嘛？」我問，但爹這個字自然叫出口的感受立刻讓我感到厭惡。我又回到九歲的時候。腦海中閃過那張照片，告訴全世界的人我是連續殺人犯的兒子。記憶跟那張照片一樣只有黑色跟白色。我緊抓住父親，警察要把他帶走，母親想把我們分開，黑白的眼淚流下我黑白的面孔。警察對我們兇巴巴。他們都不肯碰我，不肯把我推開，彷彿還怕他們確信我一定會繼承的殺人犯基因會傳染給他們，會從我身上跳出來，落在他們手上，鑽進他們的皮膚裡。那基因會植入負面的思想，讓他們在漫長疲倦的一天結束時決定吞槍自殺。他們看著我媽媽我姊姊跟我的时候，毫不掩飾滿臉僧恨，確信我們都是共犯，放假時爹會帶妓女回來，我們便輪流榨乾她們的生命，強暴她們，讓她們唏哩嘩啦沾滿了鮮血，兒子和女兒犯下母親和父親的罪行。

en_text: “I want to see you,” my dad says, snapping me out of the memory, and my skin crawls, not at his request, but in the undeniable knowledge that yes indeed I’m going to go and see him.
zh_text: 「我想見你。」爹的話打斷了我的回憶，我渾身起了雞皮疙瘩，我不怕他開口請求，我怕我無法拒絕，沒錯，我會去監獄看他。

en_text: “I can’t.”
zh_text: 「不行。」

en_text: “You can.”
zh_text: 「可以。」

en_text: “I’m busy.”
zh_text: 「可以。」

en_text: “It’s important.”
zh_text: 「這件事很重要。」

en_text: “Being a father is important. Not killing eleven women is important. You staying locked up is important.” “I’m still your father. You can deny it as much as you want, but—” “I do deny it.”
zh_text: 「當個好爸爸比較重要。殺掉十一個女人就不重要。重要的是你不能出獄。」「我還是你的爸爸。你不承認就不承認吧，但是……」

en_text: “I’m sorry the way it worked out.”
zh_text: 「我很抱歉事情會變成這樣。」

en_text: “You make it sound like you had a different plan. How many more would have died, Dad? Another dozen?”
zh_text: 「聽起來不是這樣你還有哪樣？爹，你還要殺多少人？再殺十幾個？」

en_text: “We’ll talk about it when you get here.” “Go to hell,” I say.
zh_text: 「你來了，我們再談。」「下地獄吧。」我說。

en_text: “I’m already there,” he says. “Please, son, it’s important I see you,” he says, and he hangs up, and I’m angry at his arrogance as he leaves me holding the phone. I’m scared at the prospect of seeing him, yet curious too, and perhaps, yes, just a spark of this—perhaps a little excited.
zh_text: 「我已經在地獄裡了。」他說。「兒子，拜託，我一定要跟你見面。」他把電話掛了，他的自負令我大怒，居然先把電話掛了。想到要跟他見面，我不寒而慄，但我也很好奇，或許真激起了一點火花一或许我也有點興奮。

en_text: “Who was on the phone, Daddy?” Sam asks.
zh_text: 「爸爸，你在跟誰講電話？」小珊問。

en_text: I didn’t even know she was in the kitchen. I turn toward her. She’s still wearing her pajamas, the teddy bear clutched under her arm, and for the first time I realize that she’s hardly put that teddy bear down since her mother died. The bear’s name is Mr. Fluff ’n’ Stuff, and I bought him for Sam’s first birthday. The bear has fared rather well over the five and a half years since then, but he’s tattered around the edges and grubby in places, and if you asked the bear he’d probably tell you he was ready for retirement. “It was nobody,” I say.
zh_text: 我根本沒發覺她已經進廚房來了。我轉過身。她仍穿著睡衣，泰迪熊夾在手臂下，我突然發現，自從她媽媽去世後，她幾乎一直帶著泰迪熊。這隻熊叫毛飽先生，是我買給小珊的周歲生日禮物。過了五年半，這隻熊外表還行，但邊緣已經破損，有些地方也髒了，如果他能開口，應該會告訴你他準備好要退休了。「沒跟誰講電話。」我說。

en_text: “You called him Dad.”
zh_text: 「你叫他爹。」

en_text: “You must have misheard,” I say, and it’s a small lie but it hurts like a big one.
zh_text: 「妳一定聽錯了。」我撒了個小謊，但殺傷力遠超過漫天大謊。

en_text: “You did. I heard you.”
zh_text: 「真的，我聽到了。」

en_text: “I’m sorry, baby, you’re right. I did say Dad.” “Am I going to live with them?”
zh_text: 「乖寶，對不起，你說得對。我的確叫他爹。」「我要去跟他們一起住嗎？」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Daddy-Nat and Gramma,” she says, and she thinks that’s who I was talking to.
zh_text: 「納老爹和阿嬤。」她以爲我在跟茱蒂的爸媽講話。「爲什麼要跟他們一起住？」

en_text: “Why do you say that?” “I don’t know. Mummy’s gone and I thought you might want a new family now.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。媽媽走了，我以爲你想要一個新的家庭。」

en_text: “Is that what somebody told you?” I say, immediately . . .
zh_text: 「誰說的？」我問，然後立刻……

en_text: Make them suffer!
zh_text: 好好折磨他們！

en_text: . . . angry at my in-laws for poisoning her mind like that. I keep my voice low and calm and friendly, a singsong voice, like when the cat sits at the door and I’m trying to convince him to come in.
zh_text: ……怒火上升，岳父母居然講這種話來毒害小孩子的心靈。我放低了聲音，保持沉著溫柔，音調也拉平了，就像貓咪坐在門口，我想說服他進來一樣。

en_text: “No, nobody told me. But on TV sometimes that’s what happens. Is that why Mummy left? Because she didn’t want to be with me anymore?”
zh_text: 「沒有人說，但是我看到電視上這樣演。那就是媽媽爲什麼離開嗎？因爲她不想再陪我了。」

en_text: “Of course not, baby,” I say, and I crouch down in front of her. “Mummy loves you very much, I know that—”
zh_text: 「小寶貝，才不是呢，」我蹲到她面前，「媽媽很愛妳，我知道她——」

en_text: “You smell like the art teacher,” Sam says, interrupting me.
zh_text: 「你身上的味道好像美術老師喔。」小珊打斷我的話。

en_text: “Huh?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “After lunch sometimes when we have art. He has the same aftershave.” I smile. No more beer for Daddy. “Give Daddy a big hug, then eat some breakfast. I’m going to drop you off at Daddy-Nat’s and Grandma’s house for a bit. I have somebody I have to see, but I promise I won’t be long. I love you, sweetie.”
zh_text: 「有时候吃完午餐就上美術課。他的味道跟你一樣。」我微微一笑。爸爸不准再喝啤酒了。「來給爸爸抱一下，然後吃早餐吧。我要把妳送去納老爹和阿嬤家待一下。我要去找一個人，但是我很快就回來了。我最愛我的寶貝了。」

en_text: “I don’t want cereal,” she says.
zh_text: 「我不想吃穀片。」她說。

en_text: “You can have what you want,” I tell her, which is a mistake, because thirty minutes later we’re sitting in a McDonald’s, the day heating up, and all I can think about is my father and what it is he wants to tell me.
zh_text: 「妳想吃什麼都可以。」我告訴她，眞是禍從口出，因爲三十分鐘後我們就坐在麥當勞裡，天氣變熱了，我滿腦子想著我父親，還有他要告訴我的事情。

en_text: The media called my dad “Jack the Hunter.” They played the angle up and seemed real excited about the symmetry it suggested. He was a modern-day Jack the Ripper with almost a perfect name for it, the best, in fact, unless of course in the late nineteenth century the real killer’s name was Jack Ripper. Before he was caught, there was no name for him. There wasn’t really much of an interest. A prostitute would go missing and nobody would care. Another would go missing two or three or four years later and nobody searched for a connection. Then some of them showed up. Somebody somewhere figured out that prostitutes over a twenty-five-year period were dying in bad and similar ways. The media told the country about it, but they had no catchy title. They called him the “Prostitute Killer,” and the articles were small and easy to miss. Then came the arrest, then came the statistics, then came the connection to a name in history from the opposite side of the world and my dad became the worst kind of celebrity.
zh_text: 媒體稱我爹「獵殺手傑克」，因爲我們姓杭特，是獵人的意思。記者大做文章，似乎很興奮這個外號勾起的歷史回憶。他是現代的開膛手傑克，正好也叫這個名字，實在太好了，當然，除非那十九世紀末的殺手名字眞的叫作傑克·瑞普爾。爹被捕前沒有什麼外號。他犯的案子也沒人深入調查。有個妓女失蹤了，誰也不在乎。兩三年四年後，又有一個妓女不見了，無人細查是否有關聯。然後有幾件案子浮出水面。在某處，某人發覺過去二十五年來有不少風塵女子死得很慘，死法也很類似。媒體報導出來，卻找不到能引人注意的標題。他們稱兇手是「妓女殺手」，版面很小，一不注意就跳過了。然後父親被捕了，統計數字也出來，又跟世界另一段歷史上的名字起了共鳴，我爹的惡名眾人皆知。

en_text: I’ve never visited my dad. We may share the same name and DNA but that’s all. I spent nine years of my life being Jack Jr. before going by my middle name. Sometimes when I was in trouble at home, Mum would call me Jack-son. She would save that name for when she wanted my dad to deal with me. I was his son and his responsibility, like when I failed a subject at school or cut the hair off my sister’s favorite doll. Belinda would call me Jacky in the times before our lives changed, and kept telling me I looked like a girl.
zh_text: 我從來沒去過監獄探訪他。我們共有的，不過是同樣的基因。九歲前，我是傑克二世，然後我開始用中間名。有時候我該被處罰，媽會叫我傑克生，傑克生的兒子。如果要我爹來對付我，比方說我考試不及格，或把姊姊最心愛的洋娃娃剃了光頭，她才會叫我傑克生，我是他的兒子，他的責任。在我們的生活出現變化前，貝琳達叫我潔姬，她老說我看起來像個女孩。

en_text: My last memory of Dad is that shy, humble smile of his, flashed at me from the back of a police car, his head twisted toward us, not a hint of shame in his features, almost a look of relief in some ways, as if he didn’t have to hide his true self anymore.
zh_text: 我對爹最後的記憶是他臉上害羞謙卑的微笑，他坐在警車後座，扭過頭來看著我們，那微笑一閃而過，他毫無愧色，似乎還有點如釋重負，似乎不需要再掩藏眞實的自我。

en_text: I’ve seen him a few times since, but only on TV and in the papers. Nobody has taken a photo of him in about eighteen years, not since he got snapped dozens of times being led from the back of a van to the back steps of the courthouse. Only reason I knew he was still alive was because nobody has ever rung to tell me otherwise.
zh_text: 後來我又看過他幾次，但只有在電視和報紙上。他最後一次拍照應該是十八年前，從囚車後廂被領到法院後門台階上的時候，被拍了幾十張。我知道他還沒死，因爲從來沒人打電話來通知我他的死訊。

en_text: I don’t know whether you have to phone ahead or simply show up, but once I drop Sam off I use my cell phone and call directory and ask for the number. A minute later I’m on the phone to the visitation department. I ask for directions and compare them to a map that’s about ten years out of date but does the job.
zh_text: 我不知道要不要先打電話，還是直接去就好，放下小珊後，我用手機撥了查號台，問到監獄的電話號碼。一分鐘後，我已經跟探訪部通上話了。我問要怎麼開車去，在十年前的過時地圖上找路，還好找到了。

en_text: It’s a thirty-minute drive from my in-laws’ place. I take a shortcut out behind the airport where the roads are narrower but have a higher speed limit. There are cars parked up off the sides, the front windscreens facing the runways on the other side of the chain-link fences, people inside them watching for hours on end the planes come and go. I head down a highway enclosed by pastures, the road edged with fir trees and wildflowers. There are large transmission towers growing out of the fields and shrinking off into the distance. The road markings are all faded from the sun and worn from constant traffic. Mailboxes stand to attention every kilometer or so where gravel roads twist off from the highway between fields of gorse, winding their way toward large farmhouses built to capture the sun.
zh_text: 從岳父母家開車過去大概要三十分鐘。我走機場後面的捷徑，路比較窄，但是速限比較高。路邊停了車，前擋風玻璃對著鐵網圍欄另一邊的跑道，有人坐在車裡看飛機起落，一看就是幾小時。我開上一條被小牧場隔開的高速公路，兩旁有冷杉也有野花。田野上看得到高高聳起的高壓電塔，距離愈遠，看起來愈小。道路標線在日曬車輾下早就褪色。每隔大約一公里的路程就會看到醒目的路標，每個路標旁都有一條從高速公路迂迴穿過金雀花田的碎石子路，蜿蜒通往用來捕捉陽光的農莊。

en_text: The prison is hidden out of sight beyond fields of trees, well away from homes that escapees would visit within minutes of being on the run. The complex is a mixture of several buildings, several wings, all made up of concrete blocks and interconnected with more concrete blocks, the whole place with an industrial feel, as if inside are not the condemned, but men welding steel and creating the machinery that runs this city. Just concrete and steel everywhere, and wire too—plenty of razor-sharp wire tying the look together. A couple of guard towers up in the corners, unarmed men up in them staring down, ready to sound the alarm at the first sign of trouble. Behind it all the tall skeletons of cranes at work, dust in the air kicked up by heavy equipment, engine noise from the bulldozers and cement mixers carrying for miles. There’s a long wing with scaffolding erected near the end and workmen busy on extending it, big burly men covered in grease and sweat who all possibly live within the walls they’re creating.
zh_text: 過了一大片樹林，便看到藏身其後的監獄，遠離逃獄的人不到幾分鐘就會造訪的房屋。此處有好幾棟建築物，分成數翼，都用混凝土塊蓋成，再用更多混凝土塊互相連接，整個地方的工業感很重，彷彿不是囚禁著罪犯，而是有人在此鍛鐵製造機械，好讓這座城動起來。到處都是混凝土和鋼鐵，還有鐵絲——放眼望去好多鋭利的鐵絲，成就了整體的外觀。角落豎起兩座守衛塔，上面站的人沒帶武器，準備一看到有麻煩就立刻按警鈴。後面有許多高大的起重機，重型設備讓空氣中瀰漫著灰塵，推土機和水泥攪拌機的引擎噪音能傳到好幾哩外。長長側翼的末端搭起了鷹架，渾身油脂汗水的魁梧壯漢扮演工人的角色，正忙著擴建，或許他們就被關在自己蓋起的這道牆裡面。

en_text: The visitors’ entrance is far more modern, like the entrance to a three-star hotel. There are large glass doors that seem as though they could be opening into a well-furnished foyer. The entire thing has the fresh look of renovations, and I wonder about the reasoning behind it. I’m not sure how it looked in the past, but the last few years have seen plenty of add-ons and updates to accommodate the new and the aspiring criminals this city is producing. Already some of the large open grounds out here have been zoned for more buildings, more cells, more inmates, and the grounds immediately nearby are already being converted. There have been editorials in the papers lately suggesting they build the concrete walls around Christchurch City and save some time; some even think we should take the biblical route and fill those walls up with water. I never believed them. I never knew Christchurch was really this bad—but now I know it’s worse.
zh_text: 訪客入口就現代多了，有點像三星級飯店的門面。大片的玻璃門似乎一打開就能帶人進入巧妙佈置的門廳。有種剛翻新過的感覺，我很好奇爲什麼要重新裝潢。不知道以前是什麼樣子，但過去幾年添了不少東西，好容納這座城沒完沒了的罪犯。外面有些大面積的場地已經劃出來，要蓋更多建築物更多牢房，來容納更多囚犯，緊鄰的空地已經開始改建了。最近報上有些社論建議，不如在基督城外造一圈混凝土牆，说不定還更省時間；有些人甚至認爲我們應該走上聖經的道路，在圍牆裡灌滿水。我不相信，我從不認爲基督城已經這麼敗壞了但現在我知道，其實還要更糟。

en_text: There is a landscaped garden with a lush lawn heading toward the glass doors. I’m not sure what image they’re trying to sell here, but the whole thing seems very corporate. The doors open and it’s air-conditioned inside, which is a relief, because the parking lot with the asphalt has to be over forty degrees. A woman watches me from behind a reception counter with Plexiglas separating her from me. There are two men back there with her also. Three video surveillance cameras stare down at me from different angles within the room. “Can I help you, sir?”
zh_text: 玻璃門前的庭園顯然經過專人打理，草坪蒼翠繁茂。不知道他們想促銷什麼樣的形象，但整體的感覺很像一家公司。門開了，冷氣迎面而來，太好了，因爲鋪了柏油的停車場一定超過四十度。接待櫃台後有個女人看著我，我們中間隔了一片透明壓克力。她旁邊還有兩個男人。室內有三台監視攝影機從不同的角度瞪著我。「先生，請問貴幹？」

en_text: It’s like a bank in here, large potted plants, chairs everywhere, the counter with the smiling woman. If six armed men burst into this room I don’t think they’d get far. For the hundredth time today I wonder where those men are, and know they’re about as far away from this prison as you can get.
zh_text: 彷彿來到了銀行，大大的盆栽，到處都擺了椅子，櫃台後的女人臉上帶著微笑。如果六個持槍歹徒突然衝進來，應該無法爲所欲爲。今天我起碼又想了一百次他們到底是誰，而且他們一定跟你我一樣，離這座監獄離得遠遠的。

en_text: “Sir?”
zh_text: 「先生？」

en_text: The visitor’s entrance may be fresh and friendly, but the woman behind the desk is not. She’s in her forties with the kind of steely look that could scare half of the inmates straight. “Ah, yeah, I’m here to visit somebody.”
zh_text: 訪客入口的裝潢雖然新穎友善，但櫃台後的女人卻相反。她四十多歲，嚴峻的神色能讓一半囚犯正襟危坐。「啊，對了，我來探監。」「姓名？」

en_text: “Name?” “Mine or his?” “Both.”
zh_text: 「我的名字還是他的名字？」「兩個人都要。」

en_text: “Ah, I’m Jack Hunter,” I say, hating the sound of the name, and saying it because that’s the name my dad will have given them. “My dad is . . .”
zh_text: 「啊，我叫傑克·杭特。」聽到這個名字，令我覺得憤恨，更恨的是我得叫我自己傑克，因爲爹會把這個名字列在探訪名單內。「我父親是：」

en_text: “Jack the Hunter,” she says, and she flinches away from me, just a little, but enough to notice. “Hang on a moment,” she says, and she buzzes for one of the guards. “Take a seat.” I do as she says in case she stands up and throws me into one.
zh_text: 「獵殺手傑克。」她往後縮了一下，就那麼一點點，但我看到了。「等一下。」她按鈴叫警衞出來。「先坐一下。」我照做了，不然她可能會起身把我丢到椅子裡。

en_text: It takes a couple of minutes for the guard to appear. He’s older than me and a lot bigger and looks as if he can’t wait for me to say the wrong thing.
zh_text: 等了一兩分鐘警衛才出來。他年紀比我大，身材比我魁梧多了，看似非常期待我趕快說錯話好處罰我。

en_text: “This way,” he says, and I follow him.
zh_text: 「跟我來。」我跟在他後面。

en_text: “No touching,” he says. “No yelling. No passing any objects. That’s pretty much all you got to know, but you break any of those rules and you’re out of here. You get me?”
zh_text: 「不可以碰犯人，」他說，「不能大吼大叫，不可以拿東西給犯人。記住這些就差不多了，但如果你犯規，我們就會把你趕出去。懂吧？」

en_text: “No touching, no yelling, no handing over anything. I get it,” and I wonder if the rules are the same for everybody.
zh_text: 「不可以碰犯人，不能大吼大叫，不可以拿東西給犯人。我懂。」我忍不住想，不知道是否每個人的規則都一樣。

en_text: The corporate image disappears. We head down a concrete hallway to a heavy metal door, passing an office on the way full of video monitors showing images from the prison. There are a few guards there, and one of them comes out and pats me down and passes a metal detector over me. It beeps a few times and I have to leave my keys and wallet in a tray. The original guard leads me toward another door. It’s buzzed open, and then we’re in another corridor. Another metal door. Another buzzing sound. The guard opens the door and takes a step back. “In there,” he says, and then he follows me inside.
zh_text: 再往前走，就不覺得這裡是一家公司了。我們走過一條混凝土長廊，通過一間放滿螢幕的房間，看得到監獄各處的影像，來到一扇厚實的金屬門前。這裡有幾個警衛，其中一個出來幫我搜身，用金屬偵測器掃過我全身。偵測器響了幾次，我得把鑰匙和皮夾留在托盤裡。帶我進來的警衛領我走向另一扇門。門喞喞一響打開了，我們又進入另一條走廊。另一道金屬門，又一次喞喞作響。警衛開了門，往後退了一步。「進去吧。」他讓我先進去，然後跟了進來。

en_text: I was expecting a row of phones with a thick piece of Plexiglas between them, covered in palm prints and scratches. Failing that, it’d be an interrogation room, my dad handcuffed and shackled to a chair. Instead it’s a large room with about a dozen tables. There are plenty of other prisoners in their orange jumpsuits talking to family members. One of them I recognize, a man very much like my father. I’ve seen him scattered over the pages of the papers, his face always on TV. He’s sitting opposite a woman and a man in their midsixties—perhaps his parents, because the woman is an older, female version of him. The man is the Christchurch Carver, and the media made the connection quicker with him and hyped him up as the city’s most infamous serial killer—even though he has maintained his innocence. The Carver looks up at me. He’s got a scar running down the side of his face and an eyelid that’s all twisted and doesn’t seem to fit right. He smiles and his broken eyelid droops.
zh_text: 我以爲會看到一排電話，中間隔著厚厚的透明壓克力，上面布滿掌印和抓痕。不然就是審訊的房間，我爹被手銬腳鐐禁錮在椅子上。眼前卻是放了十來張桌子的大房間。已經有不少穿著橘色連身衣的犯人在和家屬談話。其中有一個人我認出來了，他很像我爹。我在好多份報紙上看過他，他的臉孔在電視上出現了一段時間。他對面坐了一男一女，大約六十多歲，可能是他爸媽，因爲那女人跟他長得一模一樣，只是比較老，又是女性。那人是「基督城屠夫」，媒體立刻愛上他，把他吹捧成本城最惡名昭彰的連環殺人犯丨不過他堅持他是無辜的。屠夫抬頭看看我。他臉上有條長長的疤痕，一邊的眼皮翻開了，似乎沒辦法好好闣上。他對我微笑，闔不住的眼皮垂了下來。

en_text: A door at the opposite end of the room opens, and my dad comes through, a guard right behind him. For a second I’m back in time, watching his smile, then I’m further back, Dad throwing a ball with me, hugging me at night, putting a Band-Aid on my knee or removing a splinter, and back then Dad was the best dad in the world. When I was eight years old I even bought him a coffee mug that said the same thing. The mug lied. The memories lied too. He walks over toward me, but before he can reach out the guard following him reminds us of the no-touching rule—which is perfectly fine with me.
zh_text: 房間另一頭的門打開了，我爹走進來，警衛緊緊跟著他。那一瞬間我似乎回到了過去，看見他的微笑，然後回到更早的時候，爹和我一起玩丢球，晚上過來抱抱我，在我的膝蓋上貼OK繃，幫我取出皮膚裡的木刺，那時候，他是全世界最好的爸爸。八歲的時候，我送他一個咖啡杯，上面就寫了「全世界最好的爸爸」。咖啡杯說謊，記憶也會說謊。他朝著我走過來，但他還沒伸出手，背後的警衛就提醒我們不可以有肢體接觸丨對我來說再好也不過了。

en_text: “Hello, son,” he says, and I wonder if he rehearsed what his first words would be to me. I don’t answer him. I don’t know how. “I can’t believe how much you’ve grown,” my dad says, and he sits down and I keep standing.
zh_text: 「哈囉，兒子。」他說，我想，他有沒有反覆練習要對我說的第一句話？我沒答腔，不知道該說什麼。「眞不敢相信你已經這麼大了。」爹說著坐了下來，我還是站著。

en_text:
“You thought I’d still be a kid?” I ask. “No. Not at all. Take a seat, Jack.” “It’s Edward these days.”
“Not to me.”
zh_text:
「你以爲我還是小孩子嗎？」我問。
「不，當然不是。傑克，坐吧。」
「我現在叫艾德華。」
「我不會叫你艾德華。」

en_text: The thing that strikes me the most is how much Dad has changed, but at the same time how much he is exactly the same. He has to be in his midsixties at least, though I’m not sure of his exact age. He could almost be seventy. He looks seventy, if that’s anything to go by. He was as large as life when I was kid—perhaps that’s because he was out there taking everybody else’s. He was a bigger man, certainly, but in jail the weight has slipped away from him, and my memories are old, and the combination of them means the man sitting ahead of me is not the man who raised me for the first third of my life. The time here has not only taken his weight, but also his hair. He’s bald on top with a ring of grey hair around the edges, and sideburns that don’t seem to match. He hasn’t stopped smiling since the moment he saw me, his lips peeled back, showing teeth that are slightly crooked that I don’t remember being crooked. His jaw is covered in stubble, his eyebrows longer now, hair sprouting from his ears and nose. But his eyes, his eyes are the same. Warm, friendly, smiling blue eyes that look at me with tenderness, and the wrinkles to the sides of them, the small wrinkles that appear when he smiles are the same, and Dad could be a hundred and ten years old and you’d still know him by his eyes. Is this me in the future? Is this the face I will one day have?
zh_text: 我不敢相信自己的眼睛，爹變了好多，但同時他跟以前又沒什麼差別。他應該至少六十五歲了，不過我不確定他的年齡。有可能快七十了。如果要估算，他看起來是七十歲。小時候總覺得他巨大逼人，或許正因爲他常出去逼死人。他以前當然比現在魁梧，不過入獄後他體重也掉了，我的記憶又來自童年，兩個理由結合起來，表示對面坐著的這個人不是那個在我生命的前三分之一把我養大的人。坐牢的時間不只帶走了他的體重，也削掉了他的頭髮。他的頭頂秃了，頭上剩下一圈白髮，和鬢角很不搭。一看到我他便笑容滿面，嘴唇翻開來，露出稍微歪扭的牙齒，但我記得他的牙齒這麼不整齊。他的下巴滿是鬍碴，眉毛也變長了，短毛從耳朵和鼻子裡冒出來。但他的眼睛，他的眼睛沒有變。溫暖友善、滿是笑意的眼睛親切地看著我，還有兩側的細紋，當他笑起來時出現的眼角細紋跟以前一模一樣，爹就算已經一百一十歲，一看到這雙眼睛你就能認出我爹。我以後也會變成這樣嗎？這是我未來的臉孔嗎？

en_text: “It’s been a while,” I say, finally coming up with something. I sit down and the guard takes a few steps back and tries to pretend he isn’t listening to what we’re saying while Dad’s guard wanders off to the other side of the room.
zh_text: 「好久不見。」我終於想到要說什麼了。我坐下，跟著我的警衛退後幾步，想假裝沒在偷聽，爹身後的警衛則晃到另外一邊去了。

en_text: “You got no argument from me,” Dad answers. “It’ll be twenty-one years next winter. That sure does count as a long time.”
zh_text: 「我也這麼想。」爹回答。「明年冬天就滿二十一年了，眞的好久。」

en_text: Fact is, it’s the longest time anybody has served in this prison. Your run-of-the-mill murders get you ten to twelve years with parole. Less if you find Jesus. But Dad strung himself together a collection of ladies that was too long not to go answered for, so the wheels of justice ground in a new direction for him and he became the first person ever to be given “life” where “life” actually meant he’d never step outside of these walls again.
zh_text: 事實上，爹坐牢的時間已經破紀錄了。一般的謀殺犯頂多判十到十二年，可以假釋。要早點上西天，就不用坐這麼久的時間。但爹牽扯到的女人太多了，多到無法一一負責，因此司法之輪爲他轉往新的方向，他也變成第一個服無期徒刑的囚犯，眞正永無踏出監獄之日。

en_text: “I have a granddaughter,” he says. “Did you bring a picture?”
zh_text: 「我有個孫女，」他說，「你身上有她的照片嗎？」

en_text: “No,” I answer, even though there is one in my wallet. I don’t want this man seeing her. I don’t want this man being part of her life, and by the time she ever has to learn of him he will hopefully be dead.
zh_text: 「沒有。」我回答，但我皮夾裡確實有小珊的照片。我不想讓這個人看到她的照片。我不要這個人走進她的生命，等她大到會問起自己的爺爺時，我希望他已經死了。

en_text: We stare at each other and I offer nothing else. I hardly know what to say. I always thought I would. I thought I’d scream at him, and suddenly I’m finding there’s something to be said about being with your dad again after all this time. Maybe I didn’t stop loving him at all way back then.
zh_text: 我們對看了一眼，我一語不發。我不知道該說什麼。我總以爲我知道。我想要對他大吼大叫，突然之間我發覺過了這麼多年再見到自己的父親，我有話要說。我以爲我再也不愛他了，實並非如此。

en_text: “I’m sorry how it turned out,” he says, and he spreads his hands magician style, as if he thinks his words carry more weight if he can prove he’s not hiding anything up his sleeves. “With your mum. And especially with Belinda. I loved that little girl. It almost killed me what happened to her.”
zh_text: 「對於以前的事，我很抱歉。」他用魔術師的手勢張開雙手，似乎覺得要是能證明袖子裡沒有藏著東西，他的話就更有分量。「你媽媽，還有你姊姊，尤其是貝琳達，我鍾愛的女兒。她死的时候我也難過死了。」

en_text: “You talk about her as if she was somebody you met,” I say. “She was your daughter. My sister. And you were out there taking away other parents’ little girls who were doing the same thing.”
zh_text: 「你說到她的時候，好像在講偶然碰到的某個人。」我說，「她是你的女兒。我的姊姊。你出去殺了別人的女兒，她們也做同樣的行業。」

en_text: “True,” he says. “Very true. But I still cry at night. I cry for the little girl I lost. I cry for the woman she never got to become.”
zh_text: 「對，」他說，「你說得很對。但我晚上還是會哭，我哭我女兒死了。我哭她沒有機會長大成人。」

en_text: “You never got to see who she did become. She gave up everything for me. She did your job and she did Mum’s job and in the end it killed her. She’s dead because of you. Mum’s dead because of you.”
zh_text: 「你沒有機會看到她變成什麼樣。她爲我放棄了一切。她要身兼父母的角色，所以才會死。她是你害死的，媽也是你害死的。」

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “You know? That’s it? When you cry, is it from remorse or from guilt?” “Always from both,” he says. “Always.”
zh_text: 「你知道？那又怎樣？你哭，你覺得懊悔嗎？有罪惡感嗎？」「都有，」他說，「都有。」

en_text: “I doubt that. I think you cry because you got caught. What do you want?”
zh_text: 「我不相信。我覺得你哭，是因爲你被警察抓到了。你叫我來想幹嘛？」

en_text: “I wanted to see you. I’ve always wanted to know how you are. I try to keep track as much as I can, which isn’t much. If it hadn’t been for Jodie, I’d never even know you were . . .”
zh_text: 「我想看看你。我一直想知道你好不好。我很關心你的消息，但我得到的消息很少。要不是茱蒂，我絕對不知道你已經……」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「怎樣？」

en_text: “Married,” he finishes.
zh_text: 「結婚了。」他結束了他的句子。

en_text: “What do you mean about Jodie?”
zh_text: 「你說要不是茱蒂，是什麼意思？」

en_text: “She told me she’d never tell you, but she came to visit me. Twice.” “Don’t you dare lie to me, Dad. You start lying and I’m out of here.”
zh_text: 「她告訴我，她絕對不會跟你說，但是她來看過我。來了兩次。」「爹，你別想騙我。你敢說謊，我馬上就走。」

en_text: “It was eight years ago—the year before you got married. I think twenty-two is pretty young to get married, to be honest, but she didn’t come to see me about marriage advice.”
zh_text: 「八年前的事了——你結婚前一年。老實說，我覺得二十二歲就結婚太早了，但她來找我，並不是把我當婚姻顧問。」

en_text: “And I don’t need marriage advice from you,” I say. Especially now, I think. “Why did she come to see you?” I ask, my stomach twisting into knots.
zh_text: 「我也不需要你對我的婚姻發表意見。」我心想，尤其是這個時候。「她來找你做什麼？」這個問題讓我的胃打結了。

en_text: “The first time was to meet me. To see what I was like, maybe to see how life could have gone for you if you hadn’t met somebody like her to keep you happy.”
zh_text: 「第一次是想認識我。看看我是什麼樣的人，或許想知道，如果你沒碰到像她能讓你如此幸福的另一半，你會變成什麼樣子。」

en_text: “What the hell is that supposed to mean? Mum couldn’t make you happy? You make it sound like it was her fault you killed those people, that if she’d been a better wife then . . .”
zh_text: 「你這話是什麼意思？媽不能讓你覺得幸福？你說這話好像你殺人都是她的錯，要是她能盡好做妻子的職責」

en_text: “That’s not what I mean at all,” he says, holding up his hand to stop me.
zh_text: 「我没有這個意思。」他舉起手，要我住嘴。

en_text: “Then what?”
zh_text: 「那是什麼意思？」

en_text: “It was a poor choice of words. Son, I never meant any of this to happen.”
zh_text: 「我的用詞不太恰當。兒子，我絕對不是故意的。」

en_text: “You didn’t? Thanks, Dad. That’s wonderful to hear. I wish I could repay you for those kind words. Maybe if you ever get out of here we can hang out together, maybe go bowling.”
zh_text: 「你不是故意的？爹，謝謝你喔。聽了眞開心。你說了這麼好聽的話，我眞希望我能報答你。要是你能出獄，或許我們可以約出去玩，打保齡球如何？」

en_text: “The second time,” he says, ignoring me, “she was pregnant.”
zh_text: 「第二次，」他不理我說了什麼，「她懷孕了。」

en_text: My stomach tightens. I hate the idea of her sitting out here, facing my father, exposing her deep-down fears, telling him she was scared that the things he did would run in the family. I hate the idea she exposed Sam to this kind of evil. I’m immediately angry at her for that. Angry at her for coming here, angry at her for dying.
zh_text: 我的胃抽緊了。想到她坐在這裡，面對我的父親，坦承内心深處的恐懼，告訴他她很害怕他的惡行會變成家族遺傳，我就覺得反感。我痛恨她讓小珊面對這樣的邪惡。我立刻氣起她來了。我很氣她來探監，很氣她死了。

en_text: “She was a real nice kid, and I didn’t hold it against her for hating me. I’m not kidding myself, I’ve got no friends in this world, and I’ve done nothing to deserve any, and anything she had to say to me I’d heard before.”
zh_text: 「她眞是一個好女孩，她恨我，我也不怪她。我不會騙自己，在這個世界上我沒有朋友，我沒做什麼好事來贏取友誼，她對我說的話，我早就聽過了。」

en_text: “What’s your point, Dad?”
zh_text: 「爹，你到底想說什麼？」

en_text: “Dad. I like the way that sounds.”
zh_text: 「爹。聽起來好好聽。」

en_text: “Enjoy it over the next two minutes. You’re never going to hear it again.”
zh_text: 「聽吧，再好好聽兩分鐘。以後就聽不到了。」

en_text: “I want to meet my granddaughter.”
zh_text: 「我想見見我的孫女。」

en_text: “Out of the question. Why did Jodie come to see you the second time?” “I have a right to see her. She’s blood.”
zh_text: 「沒轍。茱蒂第二次來看你是爲了什麼理由？」「我有權見她，我是她爺爺。」

en_text: “No. She’s nothing like you and she’s nothing to you. Why did Jodie come back?”
zh_text: 「不行，她完全不像你，她跟你沒有關係。爲什麼茱蒂又來了一次？」

en_text: “She came to tell me you were a good man and I didn’t deserve to have you as a son. She told me I would be a grandfather and would never meet my grandchildren. She told me I had ruined a lot of lives, but yours wasn’t one of them. She said she was fixing the damage inside of you that I’d done. She wanted me to know you were a good man and were going to make a great father. That was her gift to me, Jack. You were one lucky man meeting her, and you did the right thing by getting a ring on her finger as early as you did.” He leans forward. “But you are different. You’re my son, and she sensed it in you.”
zh_text: 「她來告訴我，你是個好男人，我不配有這麼好的兒子。她說我要當爺爺了，這輩子都見不到我的孫輩。她說我毀掉了很多人的生命，但你的不容我毀掉。她說她會修補我對你造成的心理傷害。她要我知道，你是個好男人，也會當個好爸爸。那就是她給我的禮物，傑克。你很幸運，認識了茱蒂，你也幹得好，儘早用婚姻套住她。」他的身子向前傾。「但你不一樣。你是我兒子，她也感覺到了。」

en_text: “Shut up.”
zh_text: 「閉嘴。」

en_text: “I really am sorry about what happened to her, son. A waste, such a waste. I have some idea what you’re going through, and it’s hard, son, it really is hard, and no matter how hollow it sounds, it’s true when people tell you that time does help. It doesn’t heal, but it helps. You will move on, and you have Sam, and if she’s anything like Jodie then you’ve got a beautiful little girl to look after.”
zh_text: 「對於她的結局，我很抱歉，兒子。可惜，眞可惜。我大概能了解你現在的感受，很難，兒子，真的很難，雖然聽起來很空洞，但如果別人告訴你時間會幫你淡忘一切，那倒是沒錯。沒辦法癒合你的傷口，但有一點點幫助。你會活下去，你還有小珊，如果她跟茱蒂是一個模子印出來的，那你就要有個可爱的小女兒要好好照顧。」

en_text: “I know, I know,” I say. “If it weren’t for her . . .”
zh_text: 「我知道，我知道，」我說，「要不是她···」

en_text: I trail off, and neither of us fills the silence for a few more seconds until Dad leans forward and looks me right in the eye. “Have you heard it yet?” he asks.
zh_text: 我的聲音不見了，兩人都沉默了幾秒鐘，然後爹又向前傾，直直盯著我的雙眼。「你聽到了嗎？」他問。

en_text: “What are you talking about?” I ask, leaning back.
zh_text: 「聽到什麼？」我往後靠。

en_text: My dad leans back too, imitating me, but then he crosses one leg over the other and taps his fingers on his knee.
zh_text: 爹學著我，也往後靠，但他把一條腿翹到另一條上面，手指在膝蓋上輕敲。

en_text:
“When you were a kid I used to take you and Belinda to the park. You remember? There was a fort there you’d always play on. Had a tire with chains on it that had been turned into a swing. There was a pole you could slide down. There was bark everywhere, and bars you could climb, ropes and chains you could hang from.”
“This going anywhere?”
zh_text:
「你跟貝琳達小時候，我常帶你們去公園玩。記得嗎？有座堡壘，你們老愛爬上去玩。還有個輪胎，加了鐵鏈改成鞦韆。也有可以爬上去滑下來的桿子。到處都是樹皮，可以爬鐵棒，可以掛在繩子和鏈條上。」
「你想說什麼？」

en_text: “There was a merry-go-round there too. You two used to play on that thing so fast that when you came to a stop and stood up, you’d fall over, dizzy as hell, clutching onto the ground as if it were moving, trying to keep it still.”
zh_text: 「那裡還有旋轉木馬。你們兩個總在上面轉得好快，快到停下來以後，你們想站起來卻會跌倒，暈得要命，只好抓著地面，好像地面在移動，你們卻要讓地面停止移動。」

en_text: “What is this? Some kind of father–son moment that you saw on TV and are trying to emulate?”
zh_text: 「你想說什麼？你在電視上看了什麼父子交心的時刻，想要模仿嗎？」

en_text: “One day, when you were eight,” he says, “when we were there, there was a man there too, walking his dog. It got off its leash and ran over to the fort where you and Belinda were riding the merry-go-round. You came to a stop and spilled off it, and the dog, it was all excited and tried sniffing Belinda. She got scared and she ran.”
zh_text: 「你八歲的時候，有一天，」他說，「我們在公園裡，有一個男人也在那裡遛狗。他的狗掙脫了皮帶，衝到堡壘那邊，你跟貝琳達正在玩旋轉木馬。你們停住了，從上面跌下來，那條狗興奮到不行，湊過去嗅貝琳達。她怕死了，拔腿就跑。」

en_text: “I don’t remember.”
zh_text: 「我不記得了。」

en_text: “It ran after her and tried to bite her, and she kept running and trying to watch the dog all at the same time, and she got off balance. She ran right into a tree and knocked herself out. Got her forehead grazed up. You remember what you said when we were carrying her back to the car?” “Not really.”
zh_text: 「那條狗追上去，想要咬她，她一直跑，又一直回頭看狗是不是追上來了，结果她跌倒了。她撞到一棵樹，把自己撞昏了。額頭上好大一塊擦傷。我們把她抱回車子裡，你記得你說了什麼？」「不太記得。」

en_text: My dad leans forward, and in a lower voice, he tells me. “You said you would kill it.”
zh_text: 爹往前傾，聲音也放低了，告訴我：「你說你要殺了那條狗。」

en_text: “No I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「沒有，我沒說。」

en_text:
“Six months after that, the dog a few houses down from us that always used to bark, you remember that dog . . . ?”
“Not really.”
zh_text:
「六個月後，那條很愛叫的狗，離我們家好幾戶那條，你記不記得？」
「我想不起來。」

en_text: “It was the same dog from the park. This big black dog with a lot of bark. That dog got itself killed.”
zh_text: 「就是公園裡那條狗。很愛叫，又大又黑。那條狗死了。」

en_text: “I don’t remember.”
zh_text: 「我不記得了。」

en_text: “That’s a long time to be angry at an animal,” Dad says.
zh_text: 「氣一條狗也可以氣那麼久。」爹說。

en_text: “What the hell are you talking about?”
zh_text: 「你到底在說什麼？」

en_text:
“You don’t think I noticed the steak was missing?” he asks, his voice low now, and I hadn’t noticed but I’ve leaned in close to him. “I told your mother I’d taken it. She never knew it was you who killed that dog. But I knew. Is that when you first heard it?”
“You’re delusional.”
zh_text:
「你以爲我沒發現牛排不見了嗎？」他低聲問，不知不覺中，我已經往前靠過去了。「我跟你媽說牛排是我拿走了。她一直不知道你害死了那條狗。可是我知道。那是你第一次聽見嗎？」
「你想像力太豐富了。」

en_text: “I think it probably was. You might have heard it earlier but didn’t know what it was. It would have taken a while to build up the courage. I first heard it when I was the same age,” he says. “This voice that was different from me, these thoughts that weren’t mine. They told me to do things that I didn’t want to do. I refused—in the beginning. Then I gave in, hoping it would shut the voice up. Soon the voice was the same as my own, and in the end I couldn’t even tell the difference.”
zh_text: 「我猜就是那個時候。或許之前已經聽到了，但不明白是什麼。要等一段時間才能累積足夠的勇氣。我第一次聽到的時候，也是這個歲數。」他說。「那個聲音不是我的，那些想法也不是我的。它們要我做我不想做的事情。一開始的時候，我不肯。然後我屈服了，希望那聲音就此住口。不久之後，那聲音就變成我自己的聲音，最後連我都分辨不出來。」

en_text: “You’re sick,” I say.
zh_text: 「你有病。」我說。

en_text: “I know. That’s what I said twenty years ago. Hell, I’m not so unreasonable that I know hearing a voice isn’t right. But right or wrong, I heard it. I don’t blame you for never coming to ask me about it, but . . .”
zh_text: 「我知道。二十年前我也說自己有病。見鬼了，我沒有那麼過分，我知道聽到聲音表示我不對勁。但不管對不對，我就是聽到了。你從不來問我，我也不怪你，但是···」

en_text: “I should never have come here.”
zh_text: 「我不该來的。」

en_text: “When you killed that dog, it was because you were hearing a voice of your own.”
zh_text: 「你殺死那條狗的時候，表示你聽到了你自己的聲音。」

en_text: “I didn’t kill any dog.”
zh_text: 「我從來沒害死過狗。」

en_text: “What happened after that?” he asks. “Did you keep hearing the voice, or did it disappear? Have you been giving in to it all these years? Are there graves out there waiting to be found?”
zh_text: 「後來呢？」他問。「你還一直聽到聲音嗎？還是就不見了？這麼多年來，你一直聽那聲音要你做什麼就做什麼？有沒有警察還沒找到的墳墓？」

en_text: “I’m nothing like you.” I begin to stand. He reaches across and grabs me, and before the guard can say anything he lets go. I sit back down.
zh_text: 「我跟你不一樣。」我想要站起來。他伸手過來抓住我，警衛還沒開口，他就放手了。我又坐回椅子上。

en_text: “The darkness. That’s what I called it,” he says. “I know you’re listening to it, but you also have to control it. If you can’t, it will take you to places before you’re ready. It doesn’t care if you get caught—it just wants to see blood. You have to rein that voice in, need to come to an understanding with it and, if you’re hearing it now, and I’m sure you are, then you have to find a way to stop it from overtaking you.”
zh_text: 「闍黑。我給它取的名字。」他說。「我知道你聽見了，但你也得學會控制。控制不了，你還沒準備好，它就會帶你走。不管你會不會被抓到丨它只要看到血。你得駕馭那個聲音，得跟它達成共識，如果你現在聽到了聲音，我很確定你聽得到，你必須找個方法，别讓聲音控制你。」

en_text: “I have no darkness.”
zh_text: 「我沒有闍黑這種東西。」

en_text: “It never goes away,” he says. “At night I can hear it whispering, but I have no outlet for it here. It’s faded some over the years, sure, but it’s still there, no denying that.”
zh_text: 「那聲音不會走。」他說。「晚上我會聽到它低聲呢喃，但我在牢裡找不到發洩的管道。當然，這幾年來我比較少聽到了，但那聲音還在，沒辦法否認。」

en_text: “Why are you telling me this?”
zh_text: 「你跟我說這些話有什麼用意？」

en_text: “To protect you,” he says, “from the same thing that happened to me. Please, son, let me help you.”
zh_text: 「保護你，」他說，「免得你跟我有同樣的遭遇。兒子，拜託，讓我幫你。」

en_text: “I call it the monster,” I say, the words out of my mouth before I can stop them, and Dad slowly nods, and for an awful moment I think my dad is going to smile, and say something sickening, perhaps a that’s my boy, but he doesn’t. The warmth goes out of his eyes and he stops nodding.
zh_text: 「我叫它怪獸。」我想閉嘴卻來不及了，這幾個字就這麼脫口而出，爹緩緩地點頭，那一刻我很害怕，我怕爹會微微一笑，說一些變態的話，比方說真是我的好兒子，不過他沒說什麼。眼中的善意消失了，點頭的動作也停下來。

en_text: “That’s a shame, son. It really is.”
zh_text: 「很遺憾，兒子，我真的很遺憾。」

en_text: “I never knew what else to call it. I figured you had a monster, and when you went to jail, it came to live with me. Came to live inside me.”
zh_text: 「我不知道該給它取什麼名字。我猜你也有個怪獸，當你入獄的時候，它就來跟我住在一起，住到我體內了。」

en_text: “Not my monster,” he says. “You proved that by killing the dog before I went to jail. You have your own darkness. I wish I could help you more, and I would, if I was out there with you. Son, word around here is that the cops have no idea who killed Jodie.”
zh_text: 「那不是我的怪獸。」他說。「在我入獄前，你就殺了那條狗，證明你有自己的怪獸。你有你自己的闍黑。我希望我能多幫你一點，要我跟你在一起，我就能幫你了。兒子，我聽到的傳聞是警方不知道誰害死了茱蒂。」

en_text: I stare at him blankly.
zh_text: 我瞪著他，脑海中一片空白。

en_text: “She didn’t like me much, but I could see she was a good person. She was a good wife, I bet, and certainly a great mother, and I owe her for what she did for you. What happened to her—that’s a shitty thing. A real shitty thing. Yet if you ask me, the fact the cops haven’t caught anybody, that’s a good thing.”
zh_text: 「她不怎麼喜歡我，但我看得出她人很好。我猜她是個好妻子，當然也是個好媽媽，她爲你做的一切，我都應該要報答她。她被槍殺丨很慘。眞的好慘。但如果你問我，警方還沒抓到搶匪，我倒覺得很好。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “It’s a good thing, son. Think about it.”
zh_text: 「很好啊，兒子，你想一想就明白了。」

en_text: “What are you on about? How the hell can you say that? What are you? What in the hell are you?”
zh_text: 「你想說什麼？你怎麼可以說很好？你是人還是禽獸？你到底怎麼了？」

en_text:
My dad leans forward in his chair then slowly pushes himself up. Both guards come over. “It was good talking to you, son.” He starts to walk away.
“Fuck you!”
zh_text:
爹往前靠，慢慢把自己撐起來。兩名警衛都走過來了。「兒子，很高興能跟你聊一聊。」然後他往裡面走去。
「去死吧！」

en_text:
“No yelling,” the guard says, and puts a hand on my shoulder and I shrug it off. The Christchurch Carver looks over and watches.
Dad turns back. “Go home and think about what happened to your wife,” he says. “And take some advice from your old man . . .”
“Save it,” I say.
zh_text:
「不准大吼大叫。」警衛說，把一隻手放在我肩膀上，我一聳肩把他的手甩掉了。基督城屠夫轉過頭來看著我們。爹轉頭對我說：「回去吧，好好想想發生在你老婆身上的事。也聽你老爹一句勸：」
「別說了。」

en_text: “It’s okay to listen to the voice,” he says, then he disappears through the doorway.
zh_text: 「聽那聲音的準沒錯。」然後他消失在門後。

en_text: Suction Cup Guy had a real name and Suction Cup Guy was murdered. His name was Arnold Langham and his friends called him Arnie. He was a husband and a dad and his forty-two years on this earth all ended when he was tossed from the apartment building. The suction cups were attached to him, he was stripped and dressed in a trench coat, one of his fingernails found buried in the roof as he tried to fight for survival, the reason for the staging still unknown. Langham no longer lived with his wife—hadn’t lived with her since he’d beaten her up badly enough to spend three years in jail for it. The wife wasn’t a suspect because she’d taken their son and moved north and west enough to hit the next country in line with New Zealand. Other than beating up his wife, Langham doesn’t have any other criminal record—no assaults, no rapes, no breaking and entering. A couple of speeding tickets but that’s all. He worked full time on an assembly line making control boards for motorized wheelchairs. It was an active case, but the urgency had dissipated—it’s the way it was when one case you were working dealt with a wife-beater, and there was another case dealing with a group of bank robbers who killed two people while stealing what turned out to be 2.8 million in cash. It was about priorities—and at the moment the bank robbery was everybody’s priority. Suction Cup Guy would have to wait. It was a shame that for the hundreds of man-hours invested so far, all they had were transcripts of pointless interviews and a burned-out van. They didn’t even have the dye-pack-damaged money. He’d have thought any ruined money would have been dumped with the van and set on fire, but forensics—at least so far—had found no traces of it. No currency—no red ink. All he has are a lot of unanswered questions, two bodies in the ground who deserve to be put to rest, and a wife who was cold to him most of the weekend. The job was interfering with his family life. The last weekend before Christmas and he should have been spending it with his wife and daughter and their new baby boy, and at the rate the investigation is going his son will be in school and his wife will have left him before it’s over. He’s been lucky so far in that he hasn’t missed any Christmases, but he’s certainly missed plenty of other occasions; each one his wife remembers and, in times of arguments, reminds him of. Sometimes she reminds him he’s the reason they’re having children so late, and that he’s the reason they’re going to be in their sixties before the kids are old enough to move out of home.
zh_text: 吸盤男有名字，吸盤男是被謀殺的。他叫作阿諾·朗漢，朋友叫他阿尼。他有妻有子，被人從公寓大樓丢下來，終止了他四十二年的生命。有人把吸盤綁在他手上，把他脫光了穿上風衣，掙扎著求生存的時候，他的一片指甲埋入了屋頂，警方仍未找出兇手爲何要編排這場戲。朗漢跟妻子分居了——自從他把妻子狠揍到得入獄三年，就沒跟妻子住在一起。妻子沒有嫌疑，因爲她帶著兒子跑到另一個在紐西蘭西北方的國家去了。除了痛打妻子，朗漢沒有其他前科——攻擊、強姦、闖人民宅，都沒有。曾經超速一兩次，僅此而已。他有全職的工作，在工廠當作業員，製造電動輪椅的控制板。案件尙未解決，但緊急程度已經消散了——當你有兩件案子，一件的死者毆打妻子，另一件則是一群搶匪搶了銀行、殺了兩個人、劫走兩百八十萬紐幣，自然前者會變得投入的幾百個工時都浪費掉了，他們只有無意義的筆錄和燒光光的貨車。連爆破後沾了墨水的鈔票都沒找到。他以爲鈔票被毀了，應該會被丢在貨車裡一起燒掉，但至少到目前爲止，鑑識人員還沒找到蹤跡。沒有紙鈔，沒有紅色墨水。他只有一堆沒有答案的問題，兩具已經下葬也需要安息的遺體，還有周末幾乎不跟他講話的妻子。他的工作已經妨礙到家庭生活。過完這個周末就是耶誕節了，他應該跟老婆、女兒和新生的兒子一起度過，而按著調查的速度，等到他兒子去上學，他老婆也離開他，案子應該還沒破。他還算幸運，到目前爲止每個耶誕節都能和家人共度，但他當然錯過了不少其他重要的節日；而他太太每個都記得，在吵架的時候就會拿出來提醒他。有時候她會提醒他，要不是因爲他，他們也不會這麼晚生小孩，也是因爲他，等孩子大到可以搬出去住的時候，他們都已經六十多歲了。

en_text: There are plenty of criminals on the street who occasionally do a favor for the cops in return for some minor charges being overlooked. But this time there’s nothing. The men responsible have involved nobody else. The cash, if not damaged, hasn’t been circulating anywhere. Whoever did this knew what they were doing. They got out of the bank almost two minutes before the police arrived. Reading criminal records has led to hundreds of possibilities, but linking enough names together to form the gang that robbed the bank has been impossible. They’ve conducted almost two hundred interviews already and he wonders if any of the men who actually stormed into the bank have been spoken to. Probably. Hard to know.
zh_text: 街上有不少罪犯，偶爾會幫警察一點忙，好讓警察對他們的小罪行睜一隻眼閉一隻眼。但這次一無所獲。負責人沒有讓其他人捲入。鈔票如果沒受損，也沒在市面上流通。犯案的人顯然精通此道。他們從銀行離開後，過了兩分鐘警察才到。瀏覽過犯罪紀錄後，嫌疑犯有好幾百個，但警方沒辦法找出關聯，沒有足夠的名字來組成那幫搶匪。他們已經進行了快兩百次訪談，不知道那些衝進銀行的人是否眞在訪談的範圍內。或许吧。找不到答案。

en_text: Schroder is sipping at a cup of cooling coffee and has just hung up from a phone call from the prison. Turns out Edward Hunter went to see his father today. He wonders what would prompt him to do that after all these years.
zh_text: 施羅德啜飲著快要冷掉的咖啡，剛接了一通監獄打來的電話。原來艾德華·杭特今天去探望他父親了。過了這嬮多年，不知道是什麼原因促使他現在才去監獄。

en_text: There’s a knock at his office door. “Somebody here to see you,” an officer says.
zh_text: 辦公室門上傳來一下敲門聲。警官說：「有人找你。」

en_text: “Who?”
“He says he has some information about the robbery.”
zh_text: 「他說他有搶案的線索。」

en_text:
“Another psychic?” Schroder asks. Whenever there is enough media coverage of a tragic event, the psychics come out of the woodwork. Jonas Jones, an ex-used-car dealer turned “renowned” psychic investigator who appears on TV giving “serious criminal insights” to cases the police have been unable to get a handle on, has already left over a dozen messages and has been banned from going any farther than the foyer in the police station.
“Worse. A shrink.” “Jesus.”
zh_text:
「又是靈媒嗎？」施羅德問。每當媒體大肆報導悲慘的事件，靈媒就會現身。強納斯·瓊斯本來是賣二手車的，搖身一變成爲「知名」的靈媒調查家，在電視上分享「重要的罪行洞察力」，解釋警方尚未掌控線索的案件，他已經留了十幾條訊息，也被禁止進入警察局大廳以外的地方。
「更糟，心理醫生。」

en_text:
“You want me to send him in?”
The thing about shrinks is that sometimes they can be worse than psychics. At least the psychics will put on a show. They’ll light a few candles and pretend they’re talking to the spirit world or tuning in to some kind of vision.
zh_text:
「天啊。」
「要讓他進來嗎？」
心理醫生，有時候可能比靈媒還糟糕。起碼靈媒會演一場好戲。他們會點幾根蠟燭，假裝在跟靈界對話，或似乎看到了什麼。

en_text: “Not really, but go ahead.”
zh_text: 「不太想，不過還是讓他進來吧。」

en_text: Benson Barlow is mostly bald with a serious comb-over, and Schroder wonders what other psychiatrists would say about it. In his midfifties and with a beard, the only thing missing from the shrink are elbow patches on his jacket and a pipe—but maybe that stuff he leaves in the office. After shaking hands, Schroder offers him a seat.
zh_text: 班森·巴羅幾乎全禿了，梳了一個條碼頭，施羅德不知道其他心理醫生看他這樣把頭髮梳過來會有什麼解析。巴羅五十多歲，留了一臉鬍子，但西裝袖子上缺了手肘的補丁，也沒有抽菸斗，不然就是典型的心理醫生了或许他把這些道具留在辦公室裡了。握過手後，施羅德請他坐下。

en_text: “The officer said you have some information about the robbery?” “Well, in a way.”
zh_text: 「剛才那位警官說你有搶案的消息？」「嗯，可以這麼說。」

en_text: “What exactly does ‘in a way’ mean?”
zh_text: 「可以這麼說，是什麼意思？」

en_text: “It means I don’t actually know anything about the robbery itself, not in those kind of terms.”
zh_text: 「意思是說，我對搶案內情一無所知，搶匪啊銀行啊，我都不知道。」

en_text: Schroder wonders if everybody who has a first and last name starting with the same letter is going to be a thorn in his side. Benson Barlow. Jonas Jones. Theodore Tate. “Then why are you here? To offer a profile?”
zh_text: 施羅德納悶，姓氏和名字用同樣的聲母開頭的人會不會都讓他坐立難安。班森·巴羅。強納斯·瓊斯。泰奧多·泰特。「請問有何貴幹？要提供搶匪的外型？」

en_text:
“Not exactly,” Barlow says, leaning forward. “Twenty years ago I was the psychiatrist who examined Jack Hunter.”
“Which one?”
“Well, both, actually.”
zh_text:
「不，不是。」巴羅往前靠。
「二十年前，我是負責檢查傑克·杭特的心理醫生。」
「老的還小的？」
「事實上，兩個都是我的病人。」

en_text: “And which one are you here to talk to me about? Jack Jr.?”
zh_text: 「你來找我，是想談哪一個？小傑克？」

en_text: “Mostly, though he’s Edward now. It was one of the first things he did when he was eighteen—legally change his name, though since the age of nine he wouldn’t answer to anything other than Edward. Jack Sr. suffered from paranoid schizophrenia. He heard voices and he believed he was being controlled by them. Or it. It was only the one voice, and he called it the darkness.”
zh_text: 「基本上是爲了他，他現在叫作艾德華了。他一到十八歲就改了名字正式改名，不過過了九歲，你不叫他艾德華，他也不會理你。老傑克得了妄想型精神分裂症。他會聽到聲音，他相信自己被聲音控制了。只有一個聲音，他叫那聲音闍黑。」

en_text: “Come on, that was a line of BS they tried feeding to the jury. Nobody bought it.”
zh_text: 「得了吧，他們想出這些胡說八道的東西來騙陪審團。沒有人信。」

en_text: “It wasn’t bullshit, Detective. It’s a real mental illness that people genuinely suffer from. It makes them think delusional thoughts. It can make you think you’re being followed, chosen by God for a quest, it can make you think you’re being watched by your neighbor or by the media. It can make you believe you’re being controlled by an external source.”
zh_text: 「探長，不是胡說八道。眞有這種病，也眞有人得病。患者會產生幻覺。會覺得自己被跟蹤、被上帝選擇要完成使命、覺得鄰居或媒體一直在窺探你。相信自己被外在的源頭控制。」

en_text: “And Jack Hunter thought he was on a quest for God?”
zh_text: 「傑克·杭特認爲他要完成上帝的使命嗎？」

en_text: “Well, no. He thought there was a real darkness living inside him that needed to see blood to stay happy.”
zh_text: 「嗯，不是。他認爲他體內住了眞正的闍黑，要看到血才會覺得快樂。」

en_text: “Then he thought right. I don’t see what this has to do with the robbery.”
zh_text: 「他想得沒錯。我不覺得你說的這些話和搶案有關係。」

en_text:
“Paranoid schizophrenia is a hereditary condition, Detective. What Jack Sr. has, there’s a chance that Edward might be struggling with the same illness—perhaps only to a minor degree, something that can be treated with medication. But considering the numerous traumas the boy went through at an early age, his current loss may compound the situation into something more serious. All those years ago when he was my patient, he told me things—things that make me worry about him. I fear for him, and for what he’s capable of.”
“What kind of things?”
zh_text:
「探長，妄想型精神分裂症會遺傳。老傑克得了，很有可能艾德華也爲同樣的疾病所苦或許沒那麼嚴重，用藥物就可以治療。但考慮到那孩子小時候就經歷了無數的創傷，喪妻之痛或許會讓情況變得更嚴重。多年前他還在接受治療的時候，他告訴我一些事情丨讓我覺得很擔心。我擔心他會出事，也很擔心他會做出不好的事。」
「他告訴你什麼？」

en_text: “I can’t tell you what he said. Those sessions were private.” “So you’ve come here to tell me you can’t tell me anything?”
zh_text:
「我不能告诉你他說了什麼。我們的療程都要保密。」
「所以，你來這裡告诉我，你什麼都不能說？」

en_text: “No. I’ve come here to tell you that Edward Hunter is potentially a danger to himself, possibly to others. Genetically, he’s like his dad. Emotionally, I think they’re the same. Edward stopped being my patient when he turned eighteen and I haven’t seen him since, but from what I’ve learned over the last few days it’s obvious he was living a very stable life in an environment he was comfortable with. But now things have changed. The death of his wife is a trigger, Detective. It’s a huge red flag and I’m telling you, there’s serious potential there for him to be a dangerous man, perhaps even as dangerous as his father.”
zh_text: 「不，我來是要告訴你，艾德華·杭特很有可能會傷害自己，或者害了其他人。他遺傳了他爸爸的基因。我覺得他們的情緒反應也一樣。艾德華十八歲的時候就停止治療，我再也沒見過他，但根據過去這幾天我聽到的消息，顯然他的生活很穩定，所處的環境也很舒適自在。但現在情況改變了。他妻子死去，或許會帶來刺激。探長，這個警訊不容忽視，我要告訴你，他很有可能變得很危險，或許會跟他父親一樣危險。」

en_text: Schroder picks up a pencil and rolls it between his fingers. “So what is it you want me to do? I can’t go and lock him up to satisfy your suspicion of him. Why don’t you get him in for some sessions?”
zh_text: 施羅德拿起一支鉛筆，在指間轉來轉去。「你要我怎麼辦？我不能把他關起來，滿足你的懷。你爲何不找他到你那邊去治療？」

en_text:
“I’ve tried. I’ve been leaving messages but he won’t return them.” Schroder doesn’t blame him. He wouldn’t return the messages either.
“So what do you want?”
zh_text:
「我試過了。我留了好幾次訊息，他都不回電。」
施羅德覺得錯不在巴羅，他留的訊息艾德華也不回。「那你要怎麼辦？」巴羅聳聳肩。

en_text: Barlow shrugs. “Ideally, I want Edward to get help. There are medications that can keep him under control.”
zh_text: 「最理想的情况就是艾德華接受協助，有些藥物可以控制他的情況。」

en_text: “You’re assuming he has what his dad has—and even that’s assuming his dad had anything other than a taste for blood.”
zh_text: 「你假設他跟他爸爸得了一樣的疾病即使那等於假設他父親除了嗜血外還有其他的毛病。」

en_text: “Even so,” Barlow says, dismissing him and standing up as Schroder’s office phone starts ringing. “I’ve done my professional duty. Ethically and legally I have to warn the police if I have a patient who I believe to be a danger to others or themselves, and that’s what this is—it’s a warning.”
zh_text: 「即便如此，」巴羅沒管他說了什麼，站起身來，這時施羅德辦公室裡的電話也響了，「我已經盡了我的義務。就道德和法律而言，如果我相信我的患者可能會傷害自己或別人，我必須通報警方，所以我來了，來警告你們。」

en_text: I listen to the lunchtime news on the way home. The guy who shoved and killed the woman in the parking lot is claiming he was on “P,” the fashionable drug with the fashionable defense for murder—meaning he’ll either get six months in jail or nine months in rehab since it really wasn’t his fault, but the drug’s fault, or the addiction’s fault, or everybody else’s fault for not reaching out and helping him sooner. Most of the sheep have been caught but four are still on the run. Maybe they’ll team up and make more sheep between them and go about robbing farms. There is more news: a security guard was killed last night and found naked in town, a primary school was burned down but nobody was hurt, then there’s sport and weather and nobody mentions the bank robbery anymore.
zh_text: 在開車回家的路上，我聽了午間新聞。在停車場把老婦人推倒並導致她死亡的男人宣稱他服了P，最流行的毒品，最流行的謀殺抗辯藉口表示他可能只要坐牢六個月或勒戒九個月，爲這其實不是他的錯，而是毒品或毒癮的錯，或許也是其他人的錯，他們沒有早點提供援助。羊隻幾乎都抓回來了，但還有四隻在外面亂跑。或許牠們會聯合起來，生出更多小羊，到處搶劫農場。還有其他新聞：有名警衛昨晚遭人殺害，裸體陳屍在市中心；小學校舍被燒毀，但無人受傷；接下來還有體育新聞和氣象報告，卻沒有搶案的消息。

en_text: I get caught behind a slow-moving truck, adding about twenty minutes to my drive, the amount of exhaust fumes coming from the back of it bringing global warming twenty minutes closer to a final conclusion. I’m still angry when I get home. Angry at the news, at the police, at the monster inside me, at the world for moving on when it should be pausing, when it should be taking a time-out to mourn my wife and to ask the big question, “Why?” over and over, why did this have to happen, why is society the way it is, why isn’t anybody doing anything about it?
zh_text: 我被一台慢吞吞的卡車擋住了，車程延長了二十分鐘，卡車後方排出的廢氣讓全球暖化的最終結局提早二十分鐘來臨。到家後我仍覺得很氣憤。生新聞的氣，生警察的氣，氣我身體裡的怪獸，氣這個該停下來卻仍繼續運轉的世界，時光早該暫停下來，悼念我的妻子，提出大哉問：「爲什麼？」問完再問，爲什麼一定要發生這種事？爲什麼社會變成這樣？爲什麼沒人站出來想想辦法？

en_text: I’m still angry at my dad. With twenty years between the last time I saw him and this time there should have been more to say. And why did he get me out there only to tell me it’s a good thing that the police haven’t caught the men who did this?
zh_text: 我還是很氣我爹。二十年了，距我上次看到他已經二十年了，應該有更多可以說的。他爲何把我叫到監獄去，只爲了告訴我，警方還沒抓到搶匪是件好事？

en_text: Don’t kid yourself, you know exactly why.
zh_text: 不要騙自己了，你真真確確知道爲什麼。

en_text: “No,” I say, and I grab a beer from the fridge.
zh_text: 「我不知道。」我從冰箱裡抓了罐啤酒。

en_text: Mostly I’m angry at myself. I didn’t go out there to share anything with him. I don’t really know why I went—certainly it wasn’t to tell him about the monster, but those words came out as if they had a life of their own. And in a way I guess that’s exactly what the monster is—a life of its own. I’ve kept hearing it over the last twenty years, small suggestions whispered to me that I’ve ignored, ideas on how to get rid of animals or people that I don’t like.
zh_text: 其實我最氣我自己。我去探監，並不是爲了告訴他什麼消息。我眞不知道我爲什麼要去監獄——當然不是爲了告訴他我體内有怪獸，但那些句子彷彿有自己的生命，就這麼脫口而出。我猜那怪獸也是這樣——有自己的生命。過去二十年來，我一直聽到它的聲音，低聲提醒我忽略了哪些小地方，建議我用什麼方法除掉我不喜歡的動物或人。

en_text: My wife has been dead four days and in the ground for less than twenty-four hours and I’m losing my mind. I sit outside and let the sun burn my face and eyes before turning away, the bright shadows and shapes moving across my vision. I go through my wallet for the business card I slid in there on Friday, and when I find it I can’t read the number on it and have to wait for a minute for my vision to settle.
zh_text: 我妻子死了四天，入土還不到二十四小時，我就要瘋了。我坐在門外，讓陽光曬痛了我的臉龐和眼睛，然後才轉過頭，明亮的陰影和形状橫過我的眼前。我從皮夾裡找出上星期五塞進去的名片，找出來後我根本看不到上面的號碼，等了一分鐘左右，視覺才恢復正常。

en_text: “Detective Schroder,” the detective says, answering his phone.
zh_text: 「施羅德。」探長接了電話。

en_text:
“Hi. It’s, ah, Edward Hunter. I’m, ah, ringing to see—” “I was just about to call you,” he says.
“Yeah? You have something?” I ask, walking outside with the phone.
zh_text:
「嗨，我是，呃——艾德華·杭特。我，嗯——打電話來想···」
「我正好也要打給你。」他說。

en_text: “You’ve caught the men who killed Jodie?”
zh_text: 「是嗎？有什麼發現？」我拿著電話走到門外。「你抓到了殺害茱蒂的兇手？」

en_text: “No. Not yet, but trust me, Edward, we’re following up some strong leads,” he says, but he doesn’t even sound like he could convince himself. “You have to be patient.”
zh_text: 「沒有，還沒，但是艾德華，你要相信我，我們查到了一些有力的線索。」話雖這麼說，他聽起來根本說服不了他自己。「你要有耐心。」

en_text: “I have been patient.”
zh_text: 「我已經很有耐心了。」

en_text: “I promise you, it’s still my top priority.”
zh_text: 「我向你保證，我最在意的就是這件案子。」

en_text: “In three days it will have been a week,” I point out.
zh_text: 「再過二天，就滿一星期了。」我挑明了講。

en_text: “I understand your frustration,” he says.
zh_text: 「你很難受，我明白。」他說。

en_text: “I’m not so sure you do. How much did they get?” “What?”
zh_text: 「我不覺得你懂。總共多少錢？」

en_text: “How much money did they take from the bank?” “I can’t discuss that with you.”
zh_text: 「什麼？」「他們從銀行搶了多少錢？」「我不能告诉你。」

en_text:
“Jodie was killed because of that money. Give me a break, Detective, I think I have more than a right to know how much my wife’s life was worth.”
“It doesn’t work that way.”
zh_text:
「那些錢害茱蒂被殺了。你也好心點，探長，我覺得我有權知道我妻子的命値多少錢。」
「不是這樣算的。」

en_text: “Yeah, yeah, I know, because two people died,” I say, and the accountant in me is doing the arithmetic, “so divide that number by two and that’s how much she was worth. I want to know if she died for more or less than the price of a new car, more or less than the price of a house? Of course it depends on the house, on the car, but—”
zh_text: 「好啦，好啦，我知道，因爲死了兩個人，」我心中的會計師開始算數了，「所以除以二，就知道她値多少錢。我想知道害死她的那筆數目跟一輛新車的價錢比起來是多還是少？跟一棟房子比呢？當然房子車子有貴也有便宜的，但是...」

en_text: “Look, Edward, I promise you we’re doing our best. We really are. We have everybody we can spare searching for those men.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽我說，我向你保證，我們絕對盡了全力。眞的。所有能騰出空的人都在搜查搶匪的下落。」

en_text: “Searching, not chasing,” I say. “Maybe I should do your job for you,” I say, and the words are out of my mouth before I can stop them, having come from nowhere, certainly not from me, and I realize they’re not my words at all, but somebody else’s. No, not somebody—something.
zh_text: 「搜查，不是追捕，」我說，「或许你的工作該由我來做。」這句話脫口而出，我來不及收回了，我不知道我怎麼會說這句話，絕不是我的本意，我也發覺那是別人說的，不是我。不，不是另一個人——某個東西。

en_text: “What does that mean?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你這話什麼意思？」施羅德問。

en_text: “It doesn’t mean anything,” I say. “I’m angry, that’s all.” “I hear you went to visit your father today.”
zh_text: 「沒什麼意思，」我說，「我很生氣，沒別的。」「聽說，你今天去探望你父親了。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “First time since he got put away. Why’d you do that?”
zh_text: 「自從他被捕後，你第一次去探望他。爲什麼？」

en_text: I slow down and think about his question, aware he’s talking to me now in a different capacity—he’s talking to me the way a cop talks to a suspect. He’s fishing for information. “He rang me. Told me he wanted to see me.”
zh_text: 我慢下步伐，思索他的問題，發覺這一刻，他的立場改變了——他把我當成嫌疑犯來詰問。他想探聽消息。「他打電話來，說他想見我。」

en_text: “And you dropped everything to go.”
zh_text: 「你就什麼都不管，立刻趕去了。」

en_text:
“He’s my father. He wanted to share his condolences. He wanted to know what the police were doing to get the men who killed my wife.”
“Is that all?”
zh_text:
「他是我父親。他想安慰我。他想知道警方探取了什麼行動來抓到殺死我妻子的歹徒。」
「就這樣？」

en_text: “Of course that’s all. My wife got murdered, Detective. What father wouldn’t want to try to console his son?”
zh_text: 「不然還有怎樣？探長，我妻子被殺了。做父親的當然想安慰兒子，對不對？」

en_text: “Have you been seeing anybody since the shooting? For help? A counselor, or a psychiatrist?”
zh_text: 「棺擊事件後，你找過人幫忙嗎？心理醫生或精神科醫生？」

en_text: “Why would I do that?” One of my neighbors starts up a lawn mower and I head back inside so I can hear Schroder clearly.
zh_text: 「爲什麼要找人幫忙？」鄰居開動了割草機，我退回屋裡，好聽清楚施羅德說的話。「幫你接納這件意外。」

en_text: “To help you come to terms with what happened.” “I can come to terms in my own way.”
zh_text: 「我可以用自己的方法來接納。」

en_text: “I hope that doesn’t involve doing anything stupid.” “Like what?”
zh_text: 「我希望你自己的方法不是做傻事。」「什麼樣的傻事？」

en_text: “Like trying to do my job.”
zh_text: 「比方說做我的工作。」

en_text: “One of us has to try,” I say, “because it seems to me nothing is getting done.”
zh_text: 「總得有人想辦法，」我說，「因爲我覺得，你們一點進度也沒有。」

en_text: “A word of caution, Edward. Leave everything to us. We know what we’re doing.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，我警告你，不要干涉我們的進度。我們才是專家。」

en_text: “Then prove it.”
zh_text: 「那就想辦法證明吧。」

en_text: I hang up, finish my beer, grab out another one, but don’t open it. I leave it on the kitchen counter and fire up the computer.
zh_text: 我掛上電話，喝乾啤酒，又拿了一瓶，卻沒立刻打開。我把啤酒丢在廚房的流理台上，開了電腦。

en_text: I go online and find all the newspaper reports from the last week that dealt with the robbery. There’s enough of them that by the time I print them out I have a stack of paper a centimeter thick. I take them outside and sit in the sun, reading through them. Surveillance from the bank puts the entry of the six men at 1:13 p.m. They were in the bank for less than four minutes, though it sure felt longer. The police were called by several witnesses outside who saw the men enter, as well as people who first heard the shotgun blast, but they were first alerted by a silent alarm. I close my eyes and try to remember as best I can. The men had been in the bank for almost a minute before the bank manager was killed. The newspaper says it took six minutes for the police to arrive at the scene. The men had been gone for two minutes by that point. The newspaper doesn’t say how much money was taken.
zh_text: 我上網找到上星期所有跟搶案有關的報導。挺多的，等我全部印出來，那疊紙大概有一公分厚。我把紙張拿到外面，坐在太陽下細讀。銀行的監視攝影機錄到六個人於下午一點十三分走進銀行。他們在銀行裡待的時間不到四分鐘，但實際上的感覺超過四分鐘。外面有幾名目擊者看到搶匪進去，便打電話報警，聽到第一聲槍響後，也有人報警，但早就有人按下無聲警鈴通知警方。我閉上眼睛，努力回想當時的情况。搶匪進入銀行快滿一分鐘，經理才被殺害。報紙說警方花了六分鐘的時間才到達現場。搶匪那時已經離開兩分鐘了。報紙沒提到被搶走了多少錢。

en_text: The accountant studies the figures. Four minutes. Six minutes. Six men. Two victims. Two fatal gunshots. An unnamed amount of money. The figures swirl around inside my head, I rest them against everything the newspapers say, try forcing them to fit against what I know, against my memories, but nothing sticks out, nothing shifts into such a focus as to tell me where to look next. The numbers mean nothing.
zh_text: 心中的會計師開始研究數字。四分鐘。六分鐘。六個人。兩個被害人。兩下致命的槍擊。不知道多少錢。數字在我腦中打轉，我對照報導的細節，強迫數字符合我知道的詳情，我腦海中的記憶，但沒什麼特別惹眼的地方，沒有數字變得特別清晰，告訴我下一步該怎麼走。這些數字沒有意義。

en_text: I pick up the sheaf of papers and throw them out into the yard. Most of them stay together, but the ones on the top and bottom slide away, the small breeze picking them up and pinning them into the corners of the yard. The answers are in the wind too, and though Schroder didn’t say it, I know that the bank robbery is already history, the death of my wife and the bank manager pushed aside as the Christchurch Crime Rate keeps rolling on, gathering momentum, leading to what, God only knows.
zh_text: 我拿起那疊紙，往院子裡一丢。一整疊紙大多還黏在一起，但最上面跟最下面的那幾張滑開了，輕柔的微風托起紙張，吹到院子的角落裡。跟被吹走的紙張一樣，答案飛走了，雖然施羅德沒有明講，我知道銀行搶案已經變成歷史，基督城的犯罪率沸沸揚，蓄勢待漲，只有老天才知道以後會變成什麼樣，眾人早已忘了我妻子跟銀行經理慘遭殺害的事情。

en_text: I end up drinking the beer and falling asleep, not heavily, but enough for about an hour to slip by mostly unnoticed, and when I wake up the lawn mower has stopped and my face is tight, and when I reach up to touch it, it’s tender from sunburn. When I stand up I realize that the few beers I’ve had, combined with the lack of food, have made me light-headed. I phone Nat and ask if they can take care of Sam tonight, and they tell me they can. In fact they sound more than happy to. I talk to Sam for a bit and she tells me she wants to come home and I tell her that she can’t, not today, that Daddy has some things he has to take care of.
zh_text: 我最後還是把啤酒喝了，倒頭就睡，睡得不熟，但也足以讓一個小時就這麼静悄悄溜走，醒來的時候，割草機已經停下來，我的臉很緊繃，伸手摸摸臉蛋，早被曬傷了，一碰就痛。起身時發覺，空腹喝了那幾罐啤酒後，我已經頭昏眼花了。我打電話給納森，問他們今晚不可以讓小珊留宿，他說可以。事實上他們聽起來非常樂意能讓小珊留下。我跟小珊講了幾句話，她吵著要回家，我說今天不行，爸爸有事情要忙。

en_text: “But you promised,” she says.
zh_text: 「我們早就說好了。」

en_text: “I know. I’m sorry.”
zh_text: 「我知道，對不起。」

en_text: She finally accepts things can’t be changed and hands the phone back to Nat, grumpy.
zh_text: 最後她不得不接受無法改變的情况，氣嘟嘟地把話筒交回給納森。

en_text: “She’ll be okay,” he says. “You know how kids can be.” “How’s she doing?”
zh_text: 「沒事啦，」他說，「你知道孩子就是這樣。」「她還好吧？」

en_text: “You know how it is,” he says, and he’s right. I do know. He means that Sam’s the same since the day we told her about her mum. Part shock and part disbelief and part simply not understanding. I’m the same way. We all are.
zh_text: 「你也知道是怎樣。」他說得沒錯。他的意思是，從我們告訴小珊她媽媽的壤消息後，她就一直這樣。有點驚嚇，有點不信，還有一點不明瞭。我也一樣。我們都一樣。

en_text: “Take care of yourself, Eddie,” he says, and something in the way he says that makes me think that he thinks he won’t be seeing me for a while. It’s the kind of thing you’d say to a friend leaving for jail or war.
zh_text: 「艾迪，好好照顧自己。」從他的口氣聽來，我覺得他認爲我會消失一段時間。有人要去坐牢或從軍時，你就會這麼叮嚀他。

en_text: I watch the sun peak in the sky. It disappears behind the tip of a giant fir tree next door for ten minutes before coming back into view, and then it slides back down. I drink another beer and then another, then head out front and grab the mail. There’s a letter from my insurance company. Both Jodie and myself have life insurance—but in a letter less than half a page long, our insurance company is holding back any decision to pay out because Jodie was killed in the commission of a crime. Life insurance is specifically there to cover accidents and illness—and does not cover murder, so the letter says, and they apologize for any inconvenience. I wonder why they got onto the case so quick—I hadn’t even contacted them—and I figure they wanted to rush through the bad news before Christmas.
zh_text: 我看著太陽升到天頂，然後消失在隔壁一棵參天冷杉的樹頂後，過了十分鐘又現身了，然後開始往下滑。我又喝了一瓶啤酒，再一瓶下肚後才去拿信。保險公司寄信來了。我跟茱蒂都買了人壽保險——但在不到半頁的篇幅裡，我們的保險公司無法決定是否要給付，因爲茱蒂死於犯罪事件。人壽保險主要適用於意外和疾病——信上說，謀殺不在保險範圍內，如果造成不便，他們深感抱歉。不知道他們怎麼會這麼快就處理我們的案子，我根本還沒跟他們聯絡，我猜他們想在耶誕節前迅速結案。

en_text: The sun gets lower and evening arrives. I play the “what-if” game, the one where what if we’d gone to the bank ten minutes later, or what if I’d kept my mouth shut, or what if I’d fought the men off. There are a lot of what-ifs. A thousand of them—of course it’s a pointless game to play and I could spend the rest of my life out here under the sun, drinking beer, thinking about the could-have-beens and should-have-beens, the entire time the reality never forgotten—I’m the reason Jodie got killed.
