zh_text: 太陽下降了，傍晚慢慢逼近。我開始玩「如果怎樣那就怎樣」的遊戲，如果我們晚十分鐘到銀行，如果我懂得閉上嘴巴，或如果我把那些人打倒。有很多「如果」，我可以想到上千個——但玩這個游戲毫無意義，我可以用下半輩子的時間曬太陽喝啤酒，思索那些「要是怎樣就好了」的情况，同時卻忘不了殘酷的事實——我害死了茱蒂。

en_text: More and more, the what-ifs begin to focus on the bank. I think about the security guard. I think about him a lot, and I imagine him acting. But he didn’t, did he. He just stood there and did nothing.
zh_text: 「如果」的思緒慢慢轉到銀行上。我想到了警衛。我一直想到他，我也想像他會探取行動。但他動也不動，對吧。他就呆呆站著，沒有行動。

en_text: Nothing! the monster says, and I guess the first part in the road to recovery, like being an alcoholic, is admitting you have a problem. So yeah, I admit, I have a monster.
zh_text: 沒有行動！怪獸說，我想，要恢復正常，比方說酒鬼要戒酒，不是要先承認你有問題嗎？好啦，我承認，我心裡有個怪獸。

en_text: And it’s nice to be here, it says, nice to be welcomed again after all this time.
zh_text: 真好，怪獸說，過了這麼久，又重新受到歡迎，真好。

en_text: The security guard, trained to help, there to defend, there to stop the innocent from being hurt, he did nothing. Not a goddamn thing.
zh_text: 警衛受過訓練，要幫助別人，要保衛銀行，要防止無辜的人受到傷害，他卻不採取行動。天殺的什麼也沒做。

en_text: I open up another beer.
zh_text: 我又開了一瓶啤酒。

en_text: Choosing to do nothing was the same as doing something. Doing nothing is what got everybody killed. You calling out—that didn’t get Jodie all shot up. The security guard—it’s his fault. He didn’t do his job.
zh_text: 不採取行動，等於站在壞人那一邊。不採取行動，才會害死大家。你大喊出聲，不是害死茱蒂的原因。是警衛的錯，他失職了。

en_text: “Damn straight,” I say.
zh_text: 「對，他媽的對。」我說。

en_text: I replay that moment over and over, and I’m not sure how it happens, but things shift a little and the truth appears, so obvious now, and it explains a lot. The first time I run things through, the security guard does nothing as the security tapes and history books state. But I slow down the action in my head, and then I notice something the cameras didn’t have the angle or the emotion to notice—this time the security guard smiles as the men come in, he smiles before he is smashed in the face with the butt of a shotgun. Then I slow it down even more, and there is more than a smile, but a wink and a nod of the head.
zh_text: 那一刻在我腦海中不斷重演，我不確定怎麼搞的，但情景稍有轉換，貞實的情況浮現了，現在顯而易見，也完全說開了。第一次回想時，警衛什麼也沒做，符合監視錄影帶和警方的紀錄。但我在腦海中放慢了動作，我注意到攝影機的角度拍攝不到、攝影機也不可能注意到的事情——搶匪進來的時候，警衛微微一笑，在搶匪用霰彈槍的槍托打扁他的臉孔前，他笑了。我把速度放得更慢，除了微笑外，還有別的！他點了個頭，眨了一下眼睛。

en_text: The security guard was in on it!
zh_text: 警衛跟歹徒是一夥的！

en_text: I slow it down again, the men rush in, the first one approaches the guard, and this time there’s the smile, the wink, the nod, and this time the guard puts his hand out and the bad guy takes it, they shake hands, there’s another nod, and bang, the guard is smashed in the head.
zh_text: 我再次放慢了速度，搶匪衝進來，第一個人走近警衛，這次我看到了微笑、眨眼、點頭，而且這一次，警衛伸出了手，歹徒跟他握手，又點了一下頭，砰！警衛的臉被打扁了。

en_text: Once more. The men come in. One approaches the guard. The wink. The nod. The grin. The handshake. They embrace. They part and then they share a small joke. The bad guy pushes his gun forward but this time the stock doesn’t connect with the guard’s jaw, but he falls anyway, he falls in a heap and when he lies on the ground the smile is still there.
zh_text: 再一次。搶匪進來。一個人走向警衛。眨眼。點頭。咧嘴而笑。握手。他們擁抱。他們分開，說了一個短短的笑話。歹徒把槍向前猛推，但這次槍托沒碰到警衛的下頜，他還是倒下去了，癱倒在地上，但臉上仍掛著微笑。

en_text: Another grin. Another wink. Another shared joke, and the men spill deeper into the bank and steal and kill; the entire time the guard watches them.
zh_text: 再一次咧嘴而笑。再一次眨眼。再一次說笑，搶匪四散到銀行各處，搶走錢後殺了人，警衛全都看在眼裡。

en_text: I go through one last time. This time when they take my wife, the security guard sits up and begins to clap.
zh_text: 我讓場景重播了最後一次。這次他們擴走我妻子時，警衛坐起來拍手。

en_text: I put down the empty beer bottle. There’s a row of them now, and thank God my friends, the ones with the platitude of “things will get better,” the ones who don’t know what to say, thank God they had the decency to bring lots of beer. Sure—they didn’t have the decency to be there to save my wife, and they can’t really help now, and since bringing beer is the best they can do then thank God for beer, thank God for people who think beer can heal the world.
zh_text: 我放下喝乾的啤酒瓶。已經有一整排了，感謝我的朋友，感謝那些滿口陳腔濫調「以後就沒事了」的朋友，感謝那些不知道該說什麼卻很得體地買來一堆啤酒的朋友。當然，他們也有失敗的地方——沒辦法救回我的妻子，現在也幫不上什麼忙，既然想不出比買啤酒更好的事情可以做，那就感謝天賜給我們啤酒吧，也感謝那些認爲啤酒可以克服一切難題的人。

en_text: I grab another one. It’s cold and doesn’t taste great but it goes down pretty quick. I head out into the backyard, stumbling—stupid yard—and go through the pages I threw out here earlier. I find some of the articles about the security guard. He was rushed to hospital with a serious concussion, which is a load of shit. The journalists—bless whatever it is they have that passes for hearts—have listed first and last names of everybody involved on the day—except, of course, for the six men who were more involved than anybody. I carry one of the stories about the guard back inside and fire up the computer. I search for the guard. Everybody in first-world countries these days is online somewhere, a member of some online community somewhere or whatever the hell is in fashion these days—people sharing their lives with strangers and credit-card thieves and . . .
zh_text: 我又拿了一瓶。很冰，不怎麼好喝，不過一下子就喝完了。我搖搖晃晃走到後院，他媽的院子，拾回我剛才亂丢的紙張。我找到幾篇跟警衛有關的報導。他被火速送往醫院，有嚴重的腦震盪才怪。記者如果他們有心肝，就請老天保佑吧列出了當天在場所有人的姓名，但是，當然沒有涉案最深的那六個人。我把一篇警衛的報導帶回屋裡，啓動電腦來搜尋他的名字。只要你住在已開發國家，一定能在網路上某個火紅的社群裡找到你的名字大家都會上網跟陌生人分享生活中的點滴，分享的對象也包括會盜用信用卡的人以及...

en_text: Monsters . . .
zh_text: 怪獸···

en_text: . . . identity stealers and serial killers. The computer takes too long to load, which annoys me, but I kill time by grabbing another beer. The beer is calming me, I’m so full of serenity right now I could write a fucking musical.
zh_text: ···冒用身分的人和連續殺人犯。電腦載入的速度很慢，搞得我煩躁不安，我只好又去拿了一瓶啤酒來殺時間。啤酒入喉後，我平静多了，我平静到可以寫出一部操他媽的音樂劇。

en_text: I get online and Google the bastard and it’s hard to type because the keyboard seems smaller. When I get his name entered plenty of stories from the last four days pop up. I don’t bother reading them. Instead I go straight to the White Pages and let my fingers do the walking. Within twenty seconds I have his address. Telecom is my friend.
zh_text: 打開網頁後，我用Google搜尋那個王八蛋，鍵盤似乎變小了，好難打字。終於輸入了他的名字，過去四天內的一大堆故事全部跳出來。我才不想花腦筋細讀。直接找到用戶名錄，用指頭在虛擬世界中行走。不到二十秒我就找到了他的住址。電信公司是我的好朋友。

en_text: Our accomplice.
zh_text: 我們的同夥。

en_text: “I think it’s time we go visit him,” I say.
zh_text: 「該去拜訪他了。」我說。

en_text: I can’t wait, the monster says.
zh_text: 迫不及待呢，怪獸說。

en_text: “One more beer for the road,” I suggest.
zh_text: 「再喝一瓶啤酒就上路。」我提議。

en_text: Hell, have two—you deserve it, the monster says, and I get changed and then we go for a drive.
zh_text: 管他的，喝兩瓶吧——你该多喝一點，怪獸說，等我換了衣服，我們就開車出門了。

en_text: My car is a four-door sedan family vehicle, but I guess I can get rid of two of the doors since I won’t be using them anymore. Maybe trade it in for a sports car—maybe let Sam choose the color. We walk out to it, my monster and me, stumbling down the driveway, almost—but thank-God-not-quite —dropping my beer. I can’t get the door open but then figure out it’s still locked, so I unlock it and things work out great. I get behind the wheel and at first I think somebody has shifted the ignition, so I have to play around with the key, but it gets there in the end, scraping over the edges in the beginning before slotting home.
zh_text: 我開一台四門的家庭房車，但我想以後兩門就夠了，反正也不會用到另外那兩扇門。或許拿這台車去換跑車好了——或許小珊可以選她愛的顏色。我們，我跟怪獸，走出門準備開車，踉蹌走下車道，啤酒瓶差點掉了，好險。我開不了車門，然後想到應該是鎖住了，用鑰匙打開之後，一切都很完美。坐到駕駛座上，一開始我以爲有人把開關弄不見了，用鑰匙東插西插，好不容易找到了開關，在鑰匙孔旁邊留下了不少刮痕，還好最後插進去了。

en_text: The mailbox almost becomes the first casualty of the evening, and then the neighbor’s cat, but things straighten out and the road points ahead and we follow it. Between us one of us reads the map while the other drives, the roads and intersections and other cars passing by in a blur of color and sound.
zh_text: 信箱差點就是今晚第一個被我輾過的東西，然後是鄰居的貓，然後沒事了，大路就在眼前，我們上路了。我們一個看地圖一個開車，眼前只有模糊的色彩和聲音，道路、交叉口和其他的車子皆然。

en_text: Christchurch is a better-looking city the later it gets in the day because the darkness helps hide the infection. I see it all around now—I was ignorant of it until four days ago. In the morning the sun will come up and tear that scab right off, the criminals will spew forth from their hovels, holes, and dens, merrily stealing and raping and killing their way through the twelve days of Christmas. The evening is still warm, and there are a few people out enjoying it, some of them walking hand in hand, or towing a dog on a leash, others on mountain bikes. It’s after nine o’clock, the sun has gone but it’s still light, the time of day approaching when it can go from light to dark in a matter of minutes. I drive past a park where a father and son are pointing up at a kite caught in a tall tree, stranded and pierced by branches. In the same park a group of teenagers are kicking a rugby ball back and forth, spiraling it high into the air before it gets too dark. There’s a fort and a merry-go-round and it reminds me of the story Dad told me earlier.
zh_text: 天色晚了，基督城也變美了，因爲黑暗掩蓋了黑暗。現在放眼望去盡是黑暗——四天前我渾然不覺。等到天亮，太陽升起，把黑暗留下的污斑撕走，罪犯從藏身的小屋和洞穴裡湧出，盡情享受十二天的耶誕假期，姦淫擄掠，無惡不作。傍晚依然溫暖，也有出來享受這天氣的人，他們或手拉著手散步，或用皮帶拖著狗，也有人在騎登山車。已經過了九點，太陽下山了，四周依然明亮，只要幾分鐘就到了那個光明與黑暗交界的時刻。我開過一個公園，有對父子正對著困在大樹上的風筝指指點點，卡在樹枝間的風筝早已破了好幾個洞。公園裡還有一群踢英式橄欖球的青少年，那顆球轉著圈飛向高空，等天色全黑他們的比賽就要結束了。也看到一座堡壘跟旋轉木馬，讓我想起爹說的故事。

en_text: The Security Guard—one Mr. “let me laugh my ass off while your wife is getting gunned down” Gerald Painter, lives in a quiet street with lots of trees and gardens and homes that all seem the same, and I figure Mr. Gerald Painter should have become a painter and not a guard and if he’d done that, taken that one little path his destiny and last name were trying to point him toward, then this Tuesday night three days from Christmas would be a very different Tuesday night than it will be for him now. It’s darker by the time I get there and I have my headlights burning. Painter’s white-trash car with the big-block million-decibel engine and fiery paint job he must surely own isn’t parked out on the street or up the driveway. Instead there’s a four-door sedan, a Toyota I think, a white one, with a FOR SALE sign in the window.
zh_text: 警衛名叫傑拉德·潘特，這個姓氏是畫家或油漆工的意思，我給他的外號則是——「因爲你老婆被人用槍打死了所以笑死我了」先生，他家那條街很安靜，種了很多樹，满街的花園，每棟房子看起來都一樣。我覺得傑拉德·潘特先生應該去當畫家，而不是警衛，如果他選擇了一個符合自家姓氏的職業，那麼，再過三天就是耶誕節的這個星期二就會有大不相同的遭遇。我到的時候天色更黑了，車前的大燈早已燒得火熱。潘特應該開那種下層階級白種人喜歡的车子，加裝了大體積的吵鬧喇叭，還有火紅色的塗裝，但街上沒有這台車，車道上也沒有。我只看到一台四門房車，應該是豐田，白色的，車窗上放了「出售」的牌子。

en_text: We drive past the house, head down to the end of the street, turn around, and drive back. We slow down, taking another look. Painter is in there, counting his money, wanting to spend it but having to wait. We drive past and pull over, the house on the same side of the road as us. I shut off the engine and turn off the lights and we sit in silence for a bit, thinking, thinking.
zh_text: 我們把車開過他家，到了街道盡頭又掉頭回來。我們放慢車速，再好好看了一眼。潘特在家，數他分到的錢，想好好揮霍一番，但得等風頭過去。我們把車開過他家，停在路邊，跟潘特家同一邊。我關掉引擎，把燈也關掉，靜靜地坐了一下，思考，再思考。

en_text: Everything is packed into Sam’s schoolbag. It was the only thing I could find. They fit in there easily enough, this bright red bag with a weird cartoon character of a dinosaur on it that is loved by children everywhere, but if it caught a flight into the country it wouldn’t get past customs. I wasn’t sure what I was going to need, but we figured it out in the end. Rope. A knife. Actually a couple of knives. Duct tape. Gloves. I don’t have any balaclavas, and the best I could come up with was a baseball cap. The beer I was carrying has fallen over during the drive and neither of us thought to bring a fresh one, which means there’s still much to learn.
zh_text: 我把東西都裝在小珊的書包裡。我找不到其他的袋子。東西一下子就裝進去了，書包是亮紅色，上面有個奇怪的恐龍卡通人物，深受世界各地的孩童喜愛，但它如果搭飛機來紐西蘭，應該進不了海關。我本來不確定要帶什麼，最後我們都想到了。繩子。一把刀，事實上我放了兩把。封箱膠帶。手套。我沒有頭罩，只找到一頂棒球帽來充數。我帶來的啤酒掉到車道上了，我跟怪獸都没想到要重新拿一瓶，表示我們還有得學呢。

en_text:
I turn off the interior dome light, then open the door. There are Christmas lights up on some of the houses, and in most of the windows you can see bright lights coming from make-believe trees. I lean against the car, then pull away from it when it sways behind me. I move around to the passenger door and open it and grab out Sam’s bag. I carry it by the strap, walk across the grass out the front of the neighboring house, then the strap on the bag unthreads because I’m holding the wrong one, the bag opens, and everything spills out onto the lawn, jangling and clanging against each other.
“Shit.”
Shit.
zh_text:
我關掉車頂的燈，打開車門。有幾棟房子裡裝了耶誕燈節，在大多數人家的窗戶上都能看到假樹上照射出來的明亮光線。我靠著車子站起來，然後推起身子，留下車子在我身後搖晃。我繞過去打開了副駕駛座的車門，抓起小珊的書包。我拎著書包的背帶，踩過旁邊那棟房子前方的草皮，書包的背帶突然鬆開了，因爲我抓錯了地方，袋口大開，裡面的東西全都滾到草坪上，發出撞擊的聲音。
「可惡。」
可惡。

en_text: I crouch down and pack everything into the bag, careful not to get cut. I keep looking around for anybody watching, but nobody is, at least not that I can see. Everything goes back in okay, even the hat, which for some reason I’ve forgotten to put on. I grab it out and prick my finger on the knife.
zh_text: 我蹲下去，把所有的東西裝回袋子裡，要很小心，免得割傷自己。我一直東張西望，怕被人發現，不過我沒看到窺探的眼睛。東西都順利裝回去了，帽子也放進去了，不知道爲什麼我忘了戴在頭上。我又把帽子拉出來，手指頭卻被刀尖戳破了。

en_text: “Aw, Jesus,” I say, shaking my hand, then sucking the cut on my thumb. It’s not much, but it hurts. I stand up and take a few more steps forward. I stare at the house, wondering why it’s different from when we drove past two minutes earlier, then realize I’m standing in front of the wrong one. I’ve led us the opposite way.
zh_text: 「噢，老天啊。」我搖搖手，把大拇指放進口中吸吮。傷口不大，但是很痛。我站起來走了幾步，瞪著眼前的房子，不知道爲什麼跟兩分鐘前開車經過時看起來不一樣，然後發現我找錯門牌了。我害我們走反了方向。

en_text: We turn around and head past my car toward the correct house. I don’t know what the next step is, I wait for my companion to fill in the blanks, and he does, because my monster is a real team player. He takes over and leads us up the path to the front door. I lean against the house while he puts his finger out and rings the bell.
zh_text: 我們回頭，走過我的車子，找到正確的房子。我不知道下一步該怎麼辦，只得等我的夥伴來塡空，因爲怪獸懂得合作的精義。他接下任務，帶著我們往前門走去。在他伸出手指按門鈴時，我的身體已經靠在那棟房子上。

en_text: Nice house. Nice street. A family street. Not a white-trash, let’s-rob-a-bank kind of street, but I guess those bastards can afford to live where they want. The house is a single-storey dwelling painted one of those Latin-sounding coffee-color names. The yard smells of freshly mown lawn, small different-colored flax bushes have been evenly spaced out around the house, so even I bet they were measured out, some with red leaves, others with green. They’re surrounded by yellowy white limestone instead of dirt or bark, a tidy low-maintenance garden planted on layers of weedmat I imagine, the kind of garden Jodie wanted and the kind of garden we were going to have until Gerald Painter took all that away from us. There’s a silver birch tree out front with the roots climbing out of the ground and cracking the sidewalk.
zh_text: 很不錯的房子。很不錯的街道。都是正常的家庭，不是住了「來搶個銀行吧」下層階級白人街道，但我想那些王八蛋愛住哪裡都住得起。房子只有一層，漆的顏色跟一種聽起來像拉丁文的咖啡一樣。前院的草皮散發出剛剪過的氣息，一叢叢不同顏色的紐西蘭麻均勻分布在房子四周，均勻到我打賭一定有量過距離，有些葉子是紅色的，有些則是綠色。周圍鋪了淡黃色的石灰石，而不是堆了土或樹皮，這個整潔的花園看似不需要花什麼功夫打理，我猜下面鋪了除草布，茱蒂原本也想要這種花園，我們也打算要弄一個，但是傑拉德·潘特奪走了一切。前面有一棵白樺樹，樹根已經爬到地面上，鑽破了走道。

en_text: It’s a brick home, a nice solid home, with a nice solid front door with thin pieces of glass striped down one third in from the left-hand side and one third in from the right-hand side, with a big matte-silver door handle on the right. The bell is a small black box with a white button that buzzes for as long as you hold it. I can hear it buzzing as the monster holds it down. He doesn’t let it go until we can see a shadowed image moving down the hallway toward the door, slowly and not quite in a straight line, all detail of the figure distorted in the strips of glass.
zh_text: 他的房子是磚造的，很堅固，前門看起來也很堅固，門左邊的三分之一也一樣，霧銀色的門把則在右側。門鈴是個黑色的小盒子，上面有個白色的按鈕，只要按著，門鈴就會一直響。怪獸按著門鈴，我聽到裡面的響聲。他一直不肯放手，直到一個人影穿過走廊朝著門走來，速度很慢，而且走得歪歪扭扭，人影很不清楚，細節都被玻璃片扭曲了。

en_text: The door opens. It opens my future and this man’s fate, this man with the bruises on his face and neck that resemble the bruises on mine. His nose has a small bandaged brace over it. He squints and presses his face forward to get a better look, and we want to shove the steak knife right into his head.
zh_text: 門開了。開啓了我的未來和這人的命運，他的臉跟脖子上都有瘀傷，和我身上的差不多。他的鼻子上有一小塊用繃帶固定住的托架。他瞇起眼睛，把臉靠過來想看得更清楚一點，我們則想現在就把牛排刀插到他的腦袋裡。

en_text: His eyes widen as he recognizes me—not us—just me—and for some reason he can’t see the monster, because a smile, not the your-wife-is-dead-and-it’s-my-fault-fuck-you smile, but a sad, sympathetic smile, stretches out beneath the bandaged brace.
zh_text: 他瞪大眼睛，他認出我來了不是我們，只有我不知道爲什麼，他看不見怪獸，因爲在那用繃帶固定的托架下出現了一抹微笑，流露出傷心與同情，而不是「你老婆死了，是我害的，你想怎樣」的微笑。

en_text: “Come in,” he says, before either of us say a word.
zh_text: 「進來吧。」我們還沒開口，他就說了這句話。

en_text: “Thank you,” we say, and he closes the door behind us.
zh_text: 「謝謝。」我們道謝，他在我們身後把門關上。

en_text: “I kind of thought you might show up,” he says. He walks ahead of us, he’s limping slightly, and he veers toward the left and has to keep correcting himself. As far as hallways go, it seems okay. Photos that seem fuzzy to me, a bookcase, a houseplant, all boring shit unless you lived here. He leads me into the dining room which is tidy and doesn’t have any beer bottles anywhere even though he seems drunker than me. “Take a seat,” he says, and there are seats at a breakfast bar of the kitchen, and we take one. It’s a few degrees warmer inside than out and a set of French doors are wide open, the dining room flowing out onto a deck where there’s outdoor lighting and a gas barbecue and a picnic table that’s turned silver in the sun. There’s a Christmas tree in the living room tall enough to touch the ceiling and thick enough to hold what must be about five hundred decorations.
zh_text: 「我曾經想過，或許你會出現。」他走到我們前面，有點一瘸一拐，一直往左邊倒，一直要把自己拉正。他家的門廳看起來還行。牆上的照片在我眼中只是一片模糊，有座書架，一盆植物，你要不住在這裡，這一切都無聊到爆。他領我走進餐廳，十分乾淨，也看不到啤酒瓶，不過他看起来比我還醉。「坐吧。」廚房的早餐吧台前有椅子，我們選了一張。裡面比外面暖和幾度，一對落地雙扇玻璃門全打開了，餐廳延伸到外面的平台上，那裡有戶外照明和瓦斯烤肉爐，以及一張被陽光曬成銀色的野餐桌。客廳裡的耶誕樹幾乎要碰到天花板，直徑寬到一定可以放上五百個掛飾。

en_text: “You . . . ah, you thought I might, might show up?” I ask, trying really hard not to slur my words.
zh_text: 「你……啊，你料到，我可能，可能會來找你？」我努力地把每個字清楚地吐出來。

en_text: “Can I get you something to drink? I don’t have anything alcoholic,” he says. “I did, until my wife poured it all down the sink. Doctor’s orders of course. Not that it stopped me from trying. I’ve got Coke or Sprite but it’s not the same. Want something?”
zh_text: 「你要來點喝的嗎？不過沒有酒，」他說，「本來有，但我老婆把酒都倒進水槽了。醫生當然說不能喝。不過我當然不想聽醫生的。我有可樂跟雪碧，當然跟酒不一樣。要來一點嗎？」

en_text: “Why’d, why’d you think, that, ah, that I was going to”—I suck in a deep breath and exhale loudly—“to, ah, show up?”
zh_text: 「你爲什麼，爲什麼，啊，想到我會，」我深吸了一口氣，然後大聲吐出來，「啊，來這裡找你？」

en_text: He shrugs. “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 他聳聳肩。「我不知道。」

en_text: Painter is taking on a slightly blurry complexion. It’s as though he’s standing with his identical ghost, his ghost living almost exactly in the same place but off by a few millimeters, so it looks like it’s trying to peel itself away. When I rub at my eyes the ghost disappears.
zh_text: 潘特的面孔稍稍變得模糊，似乎他的雙胞胎鬼魂也在這裡，那鬼魂站的地方跟他一模一樣，但差了幾公釐，感覺就像鬼魂想把自己從他身上剝開。揉揉眼睛後，鬼魂消失了。

en_text: “Yes you do. You wouldn’t”—I take another deep breath and can taste beer, and suddenly I really have to take a leak—“wouldn’t have said anything otherwise.”
zh_text: 「你知道，你知道爲什麼，」我又深呼吸了一次，聞得到啤酒味，突然之間我眞想衝進廁所撒尿，「不然，你不會那麼說。」

en_text: Painter is a man in his mid to late forties with a shaved head and dark eyes that don’t seem to focus well. He takes a seat at the kitchen bar, sitting slowly, exhaling heavily, and holding on to the bench at the same time. There’s a microwave in view behind him with a clock that doesn’t match my inner perception of time because it’s telling me I’ve already been here five minutes and I’m sure only one has passed.
zh_text: 潘特四十多快五十了，剃了個光頭，黑色的眼睛似乎無法聚焦。他也在吧台前坐下，慢慢地坐下來，重重地吐氣，同時抓住凳子。他身後有一台微波爐，上面的時鐘不符合我心中的時間知覺，時鐘說我已經進來五分鐘了，但我很確定只過了一分鐘。

en_text: “Since the . . . robbery, I’ve had problems,” he says. “Something in here,” he says, and he taps his head, and I realize the shaved head is fresh, “got broken. I mean, the doctors had bigger words for it, but if you ground those words up and put them in their simplest form, that’s what they’d say. I can’t walk straight. I reach for something and I miss. I take a piss and it goes all over the floor. I’ve got this ringing in my ears that won’t stop, and sometimes for no good reason I’ll just start to cry. It’s permanent too. They had big words for that also, but it didn’t matter how they tried to tie a goddamn bow on it, the gift was the same either way. Got this for life,” he says. “Can’t ever work again. Can’t drive. Can hardly ever go into public. Don’t know what I’ll do. I’ll lose my house, that’s for sure. I got insurance for what happened to me, but it doesn’t cover shit. But hey, look at me, bitching about what happened to me, what happened to me ain’t worth a damn considering what happened to you. To your wife and the bank manager.”
zh_text: 「自從……搶案發生後，我就有問題了，」他拍拍自己的腦袋，「這裡好像壞掉了。」我發現他的頭髮應該才剛剃掉。「意思是說，醫生用的字太難了我不會，但如果你把他們說的話磨碎了，重新組合成最簡單的樣子，應該就是壞掉了。我沒辦法走一直線。我伸手想拿東西，可是拿不到。去尿尿，尿得滿地都是。耳朵裡一直有聲音在響，停不下來，有時候不知道爲什麼就想哭。好不了。醫生還講了其他很難的字，但不管把東西包裝成他媽的什麼樣子，裡面的禮物都一樣。一輩子好不了，」他說，「以後不能去上班。不能開車。幾乎沒辦法出門。不知道該怎麼辦。我一定付不出房子的貸款。保險公司會賠錢，但也沒賠多少。唉，你看看我，一直發牢騷，抱怨自己倒楣，我再倒楣也沒有你倒楣。更不用說你太太跟銀行經理了。」

en_text: I put the bag up on the counter.
zh_text: 我把小珊的書包放在吧台上。

en_text: Open it, open it, open it.
zh_text: 打開，打開，快打開。

en_text: We open it. My bladder is going to explode.
zh_text: 我們把書包打開。我的膀胱快爆炸了。

en_text: “You gonna say anything?” he asks.
zh_text: 「你想說什麼？」他問。

en_text: “What do, do you . . . want to hear from us?” “Us?”
zh_text: 「你，呃，你想聽我們說什麼？」「我們？」

en_text: Us? Did I say us? No. I didn’t. “I said me.” “You said us.”
zh_text: 我們？我說了「我們」？沒有吧。「我說『我』。」「你說『我們』。」

en_text: “It was a, a mistake. Tell me. What do you want to hear?” “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「我，我搞錯了。你說吧，你想聽我說什麼？」「我不知道。」

en_text: “You said you were expecting me,” I say, focusing really hard on the words.
zh_text: 「你剛才說，你料到我會來。」我很努力地把話說清楚。

en_text: “Not really expecting. Hoping, I guess, is the word.” “Hoping? Why?”
zh_text: 「不是眞的預測。我覺得，應該說希望你會來吧。」「希望？爲什麼？」

en_text: “I don’t know why, not really.” “Tell me.”
zh_text: 「我不知道爲什麼，說不上來。」「告訴我。」

en_text: He spends a few seconds exhaling, grimacing at the same time. He can’t keep his hands still. “I can hardly sleep,” he says, “and when I do, there are always dreams. I didn’t see anybody die, but I know they did. I saw them after, you know, after they were shot. I saw your wife, I mean, I didn’t see her die, and I was still unconscious when they took me away, but I see her dying anyway. The reason I didn’t see it for real was I messed up and let them get me without a fight. I mean, they could have killed me instead, right? I’d rather have died trying than . . . than this. I dream about them, you know. About the men who did this. I dream about the ones who died. Your wife comes to me at night, in my dreams.”
zh_text: 他花了幾秒鐘吐氣，齜牙咧嘴的。他的雙手不斷顫抖。「我一直睡不著，」他說，「好不容易睡著了，也會做夢。我看不到誰死掉，但我知道有人死了。然後才看到死人，你知道，就是他們已經被打死了。我看到你老婆，我的意思是說，我沒看到她死掉，他們把我帶走的時候我已經昏迷了，但我還是看到她慢慢死去。我看不到實際的情况，因爲我搞砸了，我沒有抵抗，就被他們打倒。我的意思是，他們應該也可以殺了我，不是嗎？我寧可奮力抵抗，死掉也無所謂……因爲我討厭現在這樣。你知道，我也會夢到搶匪，就是那些壤人。我夢到死掉的人。你老婆晚上會來找我，跑到我夢裡。」

en_text: “What does she say?” I ask, genuinely curious. She hasn’t come to see me yet.
zh_text: 「她跟你說了什麼？」我眞的很好奇。茱蒂未曾到過我的夢裡。

en_text: “She tells me there was nothing I could have done.” “You believe her?”
zh_text: 「她說，那時候我什麼也不能做。」「你信嗎？」

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「不信。」

en_text: “You’re pathetic,” I say, but the words aren’t mine. “Fucking pathetic.” “I know,” he says, and tries to fight back tears.
zh_text: 「你有病，」我說，但這些話不是我說的，「病態到討厭。」「我知道。」他努力忍住眼中的涼水。

en_text: “Stop crying.”
zh_text: 「不要哭。」

en_text: “I’m not crying,” he says, choking on the words.
zh_text: 「我沒哭。」他的聲音都哽咽了。

en_text: “Jesus,” I say, slowly shaking my head, but I’m sober now, no longer in danger of throwing up. “You could have stopped them,” I say, my words forceful now, clear.
zh_text: 「天啊。」我慢慢搖搖頭，但我現在清醒了，不太可能嘔吐。「你應該要阻止他們才對。」我一字一字說得很清楚，很有力。

en_text: “You think I didn’t want to? Ah shit, it’s not fair, I mean, six of them, all with guns, and what the hell do I have?” he says, wiping at his eyes before the tears can fall. “Certainly no weapon of any sort. The bank gives me a uniform and that’s it. I mean, that’s not exactly a deterrent against professional bank robbers. Shit, I can’t even keep the damn skateboarders off the front sidewalk. I wanted to do more, I wish I could have done more, but . . . ah shit . . . ,” he says. “Are you . . . are you here to kill me?”
zh_text: 「你以爲我不想嗎？啊，去死啦，很不公平，我是說，他們有六個人，手上都有槍，我有個屁？」他在眼淚掉下來之前就把淚水擦乾了。「什麼屁武器也沒有。銀行給我一身制服，就沒有其他配備了。我的意思是，碰到專業的銀行搶匪，制服根本嚇不了他們。可惡，連那些死小孩在前面的人行道溜滑板，我都沒辦法把他們趕走。我本來可以……我眞希望我不是光站在那裡而已……啊，可惡……」他說。「你……你來我家，想把我殺掉嗎？」

en_text: “Is that what you want?”
zh_text: 「你希望我殺了你？」

en_text: “I . . . I think so.” His hands are clenched and shaking. Tears are running down his face. “I . . . I don’t have the courage to do it myself.”
zh_text: 「我···我希望你殺死我。」他握緊拳頭，雙手仍在顫抖，满臉淚水。「我···我沒有勇氣自殺。」

en_text: All those memories earlier today that weren’t memories, but more like reels of film of different scenarios that rolled through my head, they play out again, and in each one there is nothing this man could have done. One unarmed man against six men with shotguns. Each time he tried to protect us, one or more of the guns would put him in his place, his chest and head exploding into a ball of blood. “You could have saved my wife,” I hear myself saying, even though I know it isn’t true.
zh_text: 白天的回憶已經不是回憶，而像是不同場景的影片膠捲在我的腦海中播放，所有的鏡頭又重播了一次，在每一個場景中，眼前這個人都只能束手無策。一個人赤手空拳面對六個帶了霰彈槍的歹徒。他想要保護我們，就被打死了，鮮血從胸口和頭上噴出來。「你本來可以讓我老婆活下來。」我聽見自己說，即使我知道我在說謊。

en_text: I reach into the bag and pull out a serrated steak knife. He doesn’t seem as thrilled about dying as he did five seconds ago, but he doesn’t move or try to fight me.
zh_text: 我伸手到小珊的書包裡，拿出一把鋸齒狀的牛排刀。他似乎不像五秒鐘前那嬮嚮往死亡，但他動也不動，也不攔阻我。

en_text: He cries harder. “I’m so sorry,” he says. “It should’ve been me, it should’ve been me who died.” “You’re right. It should have been.”
zh_text: 他哭得更兇了。「對不起，」他說，「死的應該是我，我應該要死。」

en_text: “I . . . I wanted to do it myself,” he says, when we stand up and move closer to him. “But I couldn’t. I was too scared. I heard who you are and I wondered if you might come, if you were anything like your dad.”
zh_text: 「我……我本來要自殺的。」他說，我們站起來，對著他靠過去。「但我下不了手。我太害怕了。有人告訴我你是誰，我就猜你可能會來，如果你跟你爸爸一樣……」

en_text: “Edward the Hunter,” I say. I thought my hand would be shaking, but it isn’t, it’s firm and we hold the knife firmly and our nerves are steady. “I can’t fight my destiny,” I say.
zh_text: 「艾德華獵殺手。」我以爲我的手會抖，但是一點也不抖，很穩定，我們穩穩握著刀子，非常沉著。「我不能抗拒命運。」我說。

en_text: “Please, just make it quick.” “We will.”
zh_text: 「求求你，速戰速決。」

en_text: “Thank you,” he says, but I’m not so sure he means it.
zh_text: 「好。」「謝謝。」他說，但我不確定他眞的感激我們。

en_text: I head for outside, my hands shaking, the bag in one hand, the knife tucked away inside it. In the end I didn’t use any of the other supplies. Next time I’ll travel lighter.
zh_text: 我起身離開，雙手抖個不停，一隻手抓著小珊的書包，刀子塞在裡面。最後，其他的東西都沒用到。下次我要輕裝簡行。

en_text: I’m still in the doorway when a car pulls into the driveway. It’s similar to the one already parked there—same color, a bit smaller, equally as foreign. The passenger door opens and a little girl climbs out, and at first I can’t make sense of it. The headlights have blinded me, it’s dark out, so in that moment I think the little girl is Sam. No real reason for that—I’m at a stranger’s house, Sam is at her grandparents’, Sam will be in bed with Mr. Fluff ’n’ Stuff, curled up and asleep and dreaming of her mother. But the thought comes anyway, this little girl runs up to me and yells, “Daddy,” before she comes to a dead stop, staring up at me and then staring at the cartoon character bag in my hand.
zh_text: 我還沒走出門，就有一台車開上了車道停下來。很像已經停在那裡的第一台車一一顏色一樣，車身較小，一樣的外國廠牌。副駕駛座的門開了，一名小女孩下了車，一開始我有點茫然。外面很黑，在炫目的車燈下，我以爲是小珊來了。不可能呀——我在陌生人家裡，小珊在外公外婆家，應該已經跟毛飽先生躺在床上，蜷曲著身子睡著了，夢見她的媽媽。但我還眞以爲是小珊，小女孩向我跑來，口裡大喊「爸爸」，然後突然站定了，抬頭瞪著我，然後瞪著我手裡的卡通書包。

en_text: The headlights turn off and the engine dies and the driver’s door opens. A woman steps out—Painter’s wife—and has noticed I’m standing here, but hasn’t taken a good enough look to realize I’m not her husband.
zh_text: 車燈熄滅了，引擎也關了，駕駛座的車門打開。一個女人下了車——潘特的妻子——她看到我站在門口，卻沒注意到我不是她的丈夫。

en_text: “I thought maybe once we get her to bed, we might want to take a . . .,” she says, approaching me, and then, like her daughter, she comes to a complete stop.
zh_text: 「我想，等把她送上床，我們說不定可以···」她邊說邊走過來，然後，跟她女兒一樣，猛然停下了腳步。

en_text: “Who are you?” she asks, her eyes narrowing.
zh_text: 「你是誰？」她瞇起了眼睛。

en_text: “I was just leaving,” I say.
zh_text: 「我要走了。」

en_text: “Oh my God,” she says, and the recognition is there now. “Oh my God, is that blood on your shirt? What have you done to Gerald?”
zh_text: 「噢老天啊，」她認出我來了。「噢老天啊，你衣服上是血嗎？你把傑拉德怎麼了？」

en_text: I don’t answer her.
zh_text: 我沒答話。

en_text: She picks her daughter up and cradles her. I take a few steps toward the driveway and she backs toward the car.
zh_text: 她把女兒抱在懷裡。我朝著車道前進了幾步，她朝著車子後退了幾步。

en_text: “Gerald!” she yells.
zh_text: 「傑拉德！」她喊。

en_text: He doesn’t answer.
zh_text: 他沒回應。

en_text: “What have you done with my husband?” “Nothing,” I say.
zh_text: 「你把我老公怎麼了？」「沒怎樣。」我說。

en_text: “What did you do to him?” she repeats. Her body pushes against the car and she jumps as if she forgot it was there.
zh_text: 「你把他怎麼了？」她又問了一次。這時她已經靠到車上了，她驚跳起來，似乎忘了自己把車子停在那裡。

en_text: I circle around her and she turns, watching me the entire time. The night is cooling off and clouding over. “Nothing,” I repeat.
zh_text: 我從她身旁繞過去，她一直盯著我，跟著我轉身。晚上的溫度已經降低了，空中布滿雲層。「沒怎樣。」我重複了我的答案。

en_text: “It’s okay, honey,” Gerald says, coming to the door. “He didn’t do anything to me.”
zh_text: 「親愛的，沒事。」傑拉德走到門口來。「他沒對我怎麼樣。」

en_text: “Are you okay?” she asks.
zh_text: 「你沒事吧？」她問。

en_text: “Yeah. About as okay as I’ll ever be.”
zh_text: 「欸，沒事，我很好。」

en_text: “Are you crying?” she asks him, then she turns to me. “The blood on your clothes . . .,” she says, and trails off.
zh_text: 「你哭了嗎？」她對著他問，然後又轉向我。「你衣服上的血···」她的聲音愈來愈小。

en_text: “It’s my wife’s blood,” I say and slowly begin negotiating a path toward my car.
zh_text: 「我妻子的血。」我朝著我的車子走去，慢慢從她旁邊通過。

en_text: “I know who you are,” she says. “It wasn’t his fault!” “Honey, it’s okay,” Gerald says. “It’s really okay.”
zh_text: 「我知道你是誰，」她說，「不是他的錯！」「親愛的，沒事，」傑拉德說，「真的，沒事。」

en_text: “I know it wasn’t,” I say, and these words are mine now, clear and sober, they come from me, and when I get past the wife she puts her daughter on the ground, and the little girl runs over to her daddy and hugs him fiercely.
zh_text: 「我知道，不是他的錯。」這是我的眞心話，很清醒，很清楚，是我親口說的，我從傑拉德妻子旁邊走過去，她把女兒放下，小女孩立刻奔到她爸爸懷裡，狠狠抱緊他。

en_text: “Who’s that strange man?” she asks.
zh_text: 「那個人是誰？」小女孩問。

en_text: “It’s why I came here. To tell him I know it wasn’t his fault,” I say. I turn toward Gerald who’s holding his daughter tightly. “It wasn’t. I know that now.”
zh_text: 「這就是我來這裡的原因。我要告訴他，我知道不是他的錯。」我轉向把女兒緊抱在懷裡的傑拉德。「不是你的錯。我現在明白了。」

en_text: I turn back to the wife. Some of her anger drains away, but she says nothing. Gerald keeps crying. Sobbing heavily now, tearful, deep sobs that make me angry, remorseful, and a whole lot of wanting to leave. I tighten my grip on the bag and continue toward the street. I hold it tightly to make sure it isn’t going to spill open like before.
zh_text: 我又轉向他妻子。她不像剛才那麼怒氣沖沖，但也一語不發。傑拉德哭個不停。現在變成大聲啜泣，淚流滿面，用力嗚咽，我聽了好氣，好後悔，一心只想離開。我更用力抓緊了小珊的書包，往街上走去。我把小珊的書包抓得很緊，免得像剛才一樣把東西都撒在地上。

en_text: The woman stays against the car but keeps watching me. “It wasn’t his fault,” she says.
zh_text: 女人仍靠著車子，兩隻眼睛沒離開過我。「不是他的錯。」她說。

en_text: “I know.” “You know that now,” she says, “after being here,” she says, her eyes going to the bag for a quick second. “But what about before you got here? Did you know that then?”
zh_text: 「你現在知道了，」她說，「你來了才知道。」她的眼睛掃過我手裡的書包。「那你來之前想到了嗎？你那時候知道嗎？」

en_text: I don’t answer.
zh_text: 我没回答。

en_text: “We’re moving,” she says. “The house goes on the market next week, but I don’t think we can wait until it sells. My sister was murdered last year, she came home from the picture theater one night and this madman broke into her house and killed her. My sister spent her life in a goddamn wheelchair, and this city’s version of karma gets her raped and killed. A colleague from work disappeared a few months ago and got found a month later, cut up into a dozen pieces by a lawn mower. We have to leave. What happened to Gerald, I thank God it wasn’t worse. It was for you, I know that, but my husband, he’s ruined now. I still love him and will always be with him, but what those men did, he’s a victim too. They killed him and left him alive. My husband is a broken man.”
zh_text: 「我們要搬家了，」她說，「下禮拜就開始賣房子，不過我們不會等到房子賣掉。我妹妹去年被謀殺了，有天晚上，她看完電影回家，有個瘋子闖入她家，把她殺了。我妹妹這一生都要坐在該死的輪椅裡，這座城的業障害她被人姦殺。我同事失蹤了幾個月，一個月後終於被人發現，被割草機切成十幾塊。我們一定要離開。還好更糟糕的事沒有發生在傑拉德身上。我知道你的遭遇更可憐，但我老公現在已經完了。我依然很愛他，我這輩子都不會離開他，但是他也是搶案的受害者。他們毀了他，卻又留他一命。我老公完了。」

en_text: “It’s a broken city,” I say, and I turn my back on her and walk away.
zh_text: 「這座城也完了。」說著，我轉身離開。

en_text: You goddamn pussy!
zh_text: 没用的瞻小鬼！

en_text: “He had nothing to do with it.”
zh_text: 「他跟搶匪不是一夥的。」

en_text: He let your wife die.
zh_text: 他眼睜睜看著你老婆被殺。

en_text: “It wasn’t his fault.”
zh_text: 「不是他的錯。」

en_text: You know what—stop with the bullshit. You’re nothing like your father.
zh_text: 你懂個屁少——說廢話。你完全不像你老子

en_text: “I don’t want to be.”
zh_text: 「我不想像他。」

en_text: Well, you need to be if you want vengeance for Jodie. Or does that not matter anymore?
zh_text: 哼，如果你要幫茱蒂報仇，就得多跟你老子學學。還是你覺得，報仇一點也不重要？

en_text: “Of course it does.”
zh_text: 「當然很重要。」

en_text: Then the voice is gone.
zh_text: 然後那聲音消失了。

en_text: I walk straight in the beginning, my legs are solid, but then I stagger a little, then a little more, and by the time I get to the car I’m holding my stomach, the world swaying out of control. I drop to my knees and hold the ground in probably the same way my dad described when me and Belinda would finally climb off the merry-go-round. I don’t think I ever threw up back then, but this time my stomach tightens, my throat catches, then hot vomit gushes from my mouth, frothy beer and bile splashing into a puddle next to my car door. I get back to my feet, this horrid, burning taste in my mouth, and I wipe a hand across my mouth, and then I realize two things at the same time—first of all, I don’t know where my keys are, the second thing is I’ve dropped the bag again. The sobriety that the monster brought with him has just as quickly left with him too, abandoning me, and suddenly the world is spinning one way while my mind sways another, the mixture not good, and I feel very, very ill.
zh_text: 剛開始的時候我還能走一直線，雙腿挺牢靠，卻搖晃了一下，再一下，還沒找到我自己的車子，我就直不起腰來，完全無法掌控。我跪倒在地，扶著地面，或許就像我爹說我跟貝琳達終於從旋轉木馬上爬下來的樣子。我不記得那時候我會不會嘔吐，但現在我的胃好難受，喉頭卡住了，熱騰騰的嘔吐物從嘴裡噴出來，泡沫狀的啤酒，苦澀的膽汁，在車門旁積成一灘。我站起身子，口中有種可怕的灼燒感，我抹了一下嘴巴，同時發覺了兩件事——第一，車鑰匙不知道去哪裡了；第二，小珊的書包又掉了。怪獸在的時候讓我冷靜清醒，他丢下我走了，我又覺得茫茫然，周圍的世界突然開始朝著一個方向旋轉，我的腦子卻朝著另一個方向旋轉，很糟，我覺得非常非常不舒服。

en_text: The bag is a few meters away. I head back and snatch it up. I pat down my pockets but my keys haven’t appeared since I patted them down twenty seconds earlier. I reach the car and there’s a black and white cat sitting on the hood, staring at me. It watches me peer inside the car in case the keys are hanging from the ignition, but they’re not. I realize I’ve dropped the bag again. I move around the car and the keys are on the ground next to the puddle of vomit. I snatch them up, then fumble them then drop them right inside the bile-beer stew. Jesus. I pick them up and they drip, and when I try to wipe them on the grass I almost fall over and my hat falls off. I pick up the bag and the hat and spend too long unlocking the passenger door. The cat takes off and hides behind the closest bush it can find. I toss everything into the backseat.
zh_text: 書包在幾公尺外。我走回去，撈起書包。拍遍身上的口袋，鑰匙卻沒出現，跟二十秒前的結果一樣。我走到車旁，引擎蓋上坐了一隻黑白相間的貓，瞪著我看。在牠的注視下，我探頭看鑰匙是否插在打火開關裡，沒有。我發現書包又掉了。繞到車子的另一邊，發現鑰匙就在我吐的那灘東西旁。我抓起鑰匙，摸索間卻又把它們掉回嗯心的啤酒湯裡。老天啊。我撿起鑰匙，濕淋淋的，想在草坪上擦乾，卻差點摔個狗吃屎，帽子也掉下來了。拾起書包和鑰匙，費了一番功夫才把副駕駛座的車門打開。黑白貓從引擎蓋上跳下來，躲到最近的樹叢後面。我把手上的東西全丢到後座。

en_text: The night has darkened considerably since I arrived, making the Christmas lights on the surrounding houses appear brighter. They’re not bright enough to light me up as I stand against the side of my car finally relieving the pain from my bladder by emptying it on the lawn. It’s either that or piss myself in the car. A half dozen plastic Santas stare down at me, mounted on roofs, all thinking the same thing—that they’d rather be somewhere else.
zh_text: 天色比我剛到的時候更暗了，周圍房子上的耶誕燈飾因此感覺更明亮。但還沒亮到洩露我的行蹤，我站在車子旁邊往草坪上撒尿，终於釋放了緊張的膀胱。现在不解決，我肯定會尿在車上。旁邊房子的屋頂上擺了六七尊塑膠聖誕老公公，他們低頭看著我，心裡都在想同一件事——他們寧可到別的地方去。

en_text: When I’m done I slouch in the driver’s seat and discover there are two steering wheels ahead of me and two roads, but they merge into one when I put my left hand over my right eye. Small drops of rain appear on the windscreen. Gerald Painter is still inside his house with his family, and he’s probably still crying. I put a hand on my chest to check my heartbeat, thinking that it ought to be racing, but it’s not. I could have been a killer right now, and if the monster had his way, I would be. The question is, how long can I keep it quiet for? No, wait—the real question is, do I want it to be quiet?
zh_text: 完事後我沒精打采地坐進駕駛座，發現眼前有兩個方向盤和兩條路，用左手遮住右眼，又合而爲一。擋風玻璃上出現了細小的雨滴。傑拉德·潘特仍和家人留在屋裡，他或許還沒止住眼淚。我把手放到胸口檢查心跳，以爲心會跳得很快，事實上並沒有。我本來要變成殺人兇手了，要是怪獸能爲所欲爲，我就是殺人兇手。問題在於，我能讓怪獸閉嘴多久？不，等一下，我眞的要問的是，我希望怪獸閉嘴嗎？

en_text: I fold my arms onto the steering wheel and rest my head on them. I close my eyes for a few moments, and when I open them again it’s to the sound of tapping on the driver’s-side window and it’s pouring with rain outside.
zh_text: 我把交疊的雙臂放到方向盤上，再把頭靠上去。我閉上眼睛，過了一會兒，駕駛座旁的窗戶傳來叩叩的響聲，我睁開眼睛，發現外面下起了大雨。

en_text: “What the hell are you doing here, Edward?” he asks, and part of him, a small part, already knows. Or suspects. The warning Benson Barlow gave him has been stuck in his head all day, a warning that hasn’t been easy to dismiss—especially since Edward visited his father today and now he’s parked only two houses away from the security guard injured during the robbery.
zh_text: 「艾德華，你在這裡搞什麼鬼？」他問。其實他心裡已經有了模糊的答案，或已經起疑心了。一整天，班森·巴羅的警告總在他腦海中繠繞，很難拋諸腦後——尤其是艾德華今天去監獄探視他父親，现在車子停的地方再過去兩戶就是在搶案中受傷的那銀行警衛。

en_text: “Who . . . who’s that?” Edward asks, and he lifts his hand up to shield his eyes even though there’s no real light.
zh_text: 「你···你是誰？」雖然外面漆黑一片，艾德華仍舉起手遮住眼睛。

en_text: “Come on, I’m giving you a lift home.” “What?”
zh_text: 「來吧，我開車送你回去。」「什麼？」

en_text: “Get out and move into the passenger seat,” he says, and opens the door for him. “And hurry up. I’m getting drenched out here.”
zh_text: 「下車，坐到副駕駛座去。」他幫他拉開車門。「快點。我全身都淋濕了。」

en_text: Edward gets out. He gasps in a lungful of air which pains him, he doubles over, then he gets onto his hands and starts gagging. A puddle of vomit appears. The rain is coming down hard and from nowhere—certainly nobody in the weather forecasting world predicted it. The back of Edward’s shirt is already soaked through. He waits a bit while Edward coughs, and when it seems like the man is never going to get back up, he reaches down and grabs his shoulder. “Come on, we have to go.”
zh_text: 艾德華下了車。他用力倒抽了一口氣，表情痛苦地彎下腰，然後跪倒在地，用手撐住地面，開始嘔吐。地上出現了一灘嘔吐物。這場雨下得又快又急——沒有一個氣象預報員預測到今天會下雨。穿著襯衫的艾德華背上已經全濕了。艾德華開始咳嗽，他耐心等待，但艾德華似乎咳個沒完，他彎下腰抓住他的肩膀：「來吧，我們得離開了。」

en_text: He helps Edward to his feet, careful not to step in any vomit. Edward twists his body so he can see up the street. There is a patrol car parked about twenty meters away. Schroder leads him around to the passenger side where there are more rain-washed puddles of vomit.
zh_text: 他把艾德華扶起來，小心避開他吐出來的東西。艾德華扭過身子，把街上的情況看個清楚。一十公尺外停了一台巡邏車。施羅德領他走到車子另一邊，地上有更多雨水沖刷過的嘔吐物。

en_text: “What the hell are you doing here?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你到底在這裡搞什麼？」施羅德問。

en_text: “I was sleeping.”
zh_text: 「我睡著了。」

en_text: “Are they the same clothes you were wearing at the bank?” “Maybe.”
zh_text: 「你身上的衣服就是在银行穿的那一套吧？」「可能吧。」

en_text: “They’re covered in your wife’s blood.” “Are they?”
zh_text: 「上面沾了你太太的血。」「眞的嗎？」

en_text: “Get in,” Schroder says, unamused. Edward gets in the passenger side and Schroder races around and gets in behind the wheel. An hour ago all he had to do was move and he broke out in a sweat. Now he’s shivering. The inside of the car fogs up and he turns on the air-conditioning to clear the windscreen. The car that brought him here follows. He turns on the wipers. Already the rain is easing up, and by the time he’s driven a couple of blocks it’s almost completely stopped.
zh_text: 「上車。」施羅德的語氣嚴肅。艾德華坐進副駕駛座，施羅德匆匆繞過車子，坐上駕駛座。一小時前，他只要動一動就一身汗，現在卻冷得發抖。車子裡起霧了，他打開空調，吹掉擋風玻璃上的霧氣。送他過來的车子跟在後面。他打開雨刷的開關。雨勢開始減緩，才過了兩個街口，雨幾乎已經停了。

en_text: “Look, Edward,” he says, his tone softer now, “I know you want answers, but coming here isn’t the place where you’ll find them.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽我說，」他把口氣放得更溫和了，「我知道你想要答案，但來這裡找不到答案。」

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “Then why’d you come?” “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「那爲什麼要來？」「我不知道。」

en_text: “Uh-huh. Gerald Painter had nothing to do with the robbery. He’s a victim as much as anybody.”
zh_text: 「嗯哼，傑拉德·潘特跟搶案沒有關係。他跟其他人一樣，也是受害者。」

en_text: “Not as much as Jodie,” Edward answers, and Schroder knows it’s a good point.
zh_text: 「茱蒂比他慘多了。」艾德華答腔，施羅德找不出話來反駁這一點。

en_text: “Look, I know it’s hard, and the situation is shit, but you gotta man up. You’ve got a little girl that’s depending on you.”
zh_text: 「聽著，我知道你很辛苦，碰到這麼糟糕的事情，但你得振作起來。你還有一個小女兒要照顧。」

en_text: “I know that,” Edward says. “People don’t need to remind me. You think my wife getting killed makes me forget about Sam?”
zh_text: 「我知道，」艾德華說，「不用别人提醒我。你以爲我妻子死了，我就忘了小珊的存在？」

en_text: “Of course not. Problem is you do need reminding. If you didn’t, you wouldn’t be here right now. You wouldn’t be drunk and one step away from killing yourself in a car accident.”
zh_text: 「當然不是。問題是你確實需要別人提醒。如果不需要，你現在也不會在這裡了。你不會喝得這麼醉，也不會差點被別人撞死。」

en_text: “Why’d you come here?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「你來做什麼？」艾德華問。

en_text: “Gerald Painter’s wife called us. She said you came to visit him tonight, and according to her it wasn’t exactly a social call. Why’d you show up?”
zh_text: 「潘特的老婆打電話來。她說你今晚過來找他，她覺得你別有目的。你來這裡幹什麼？」

en_text: “Why don’t you ask her?”
zh_text: 「你爲什麼不問她？」

en_text: “She doesn’t know, and Gerald Painter isn’t saying much, but I have to tell you, Edward, I don’t like your being here. And you’re drunk and you’re wearing the clothes with your wife’s blood on them. Mrs. Painter isn’t the only one who called you in—another neighbor saw you stumbling to your car and pissing on the lawn. The constables in the patrol car back there, they came here to take you away. Me being here, this is a favor, Edward. I’m here to take you home and keep you out of jail for the night. I’m here to stop you from making any further mistakes.”
zh_text: 「她不知道，潘特也不說，但是我得告訴你，艾德華，你來找他，我覺得很不爽。你喝醉了，衣服上還沾了你妻子的血。報案的不只潘特的老婆——還有鄰居看到你搖搖晃晃走到車子旁邊，在草坪上小便。後面車子裡的警官本來要把你帶走。我過來這裡，是做給你人情，艾德華。我來帶你回家，今天晚上你就不用睡在監獄裡。我也要阻止你犯下更嚴重的錯誤。」

en_text: “You want my thanks now? How about you earn it by finding the men who killed Jodie?”
zh_text: 「你要我感激你嗎？如果你抓到殺了茱蒂的人，我當然會很感激你。」

en_text: “Why did you come here?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你來做什麼？」施羅德問。

en_text: “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」

en_text: “I think you know.” Edward shrugs.
zh_text: 「我覺得你知道。」艾德華聳聳肩。

en_text: “I think you blame Painter for not doing enough to save your wife. I think you wanted to make him hurt for what happened, and then you got here and found he already was hurting and that none of this was his fault. I think if you hadn’t made that realization then right now I wouldn’t be doing you any favors. We’d be having a very different conversation.”
zh_text: 「我覺得你怪潘特，怪他沒有盡力救你妻子。我覺得你要他爲發生的事情付出代價，然後你來這裡，發現他已經很痛苦了，而且他並沒有犯錯。我想，如果你還沒覺悟，現在我也沒辦法做人情給你。我們對話的内容也會完全不一樣。」

en_text: Edward says nothing, just stares out the window at the night. Schroder stays quiet for a bit, thinking about Benson Barlow and the shrink’s warning.
zh_text: 艾德華不發一語，直直盯著車窗外的夜色。施羅德也沉默了幾秒，又想到了班森·巴羅和他的警告。

en_text: “I have a friend,” Schroder says, “that you remind me of in a way. He looked into something he shouldn’t have, and it cost him. Same thing happened to him that’s happening to you. He thought drinking was the answer, but it screwed him up, screwed with his judgment. He went out one night in his car and ran into a woman, almost killed her. That shit will happen to you if you don’t get a grip on things. My friend, he was a cop once who knew better. You’ll end up falling into an abyss right alongside him, and his abyss now has him in jail. He’s locked away for six months for what he did. That what you want? To leave your little girl for six months?”
zh_text: 「我有個朋友，」施羅德說，「跟你有點像。他去調查不該調查的事，結果很慘。他碰到的事你也碰到了。他以爲喝醉了就好，但喝醉了就失去了判斷力，搞得他一敗塗地。有天晚上他開車出去，撞到一個女孩，差點把她撞死了。如果你不能冷静下來，會跟他一樣慘。我這個朋友以前也是警察，他早該明白。最後你會跟他一樣墮入萬丈深淵，他去坐牢了。被判要坐牢六個月。你想坐牢嗎？六個月都看不到你的小女兒？」

en_text: Edward doesn’t answer him.
zh_text: 艾德華默不作聲。

en_text: “Or it’ll be worse. You’ll head out driving and you’ll have your daughter with you. You’ll drag her into that abyss and get her killed.”
zh_text: 「還有可能更糟糕。你開車出去，還帶著你女兒。你會害她跟你一起落入萬丈深淵，害死她。」

en_text: Still nothing.
zh_text: 仍然沉默以對。

en_text: “Look, Edward, we’ll get the men who did this. These people, they always get caught. Always.”
zh_text: 「聽我說，艾德華，我們會抓到搶匪。這些人一定跑不了，一定會被逮到。」

en_text: “And you always let them go,” Edward says. “Isn’t that it? You’ll find these guys and you’ll find you’ve dealt with them before, locked them away before, and let them right out.”
zh_text: 「你們總會讓他們出獄，」艾德華說，「對不對？你們會抓到搶匪，發現他們都是熟面孔，以前就坐過牢，然後被你們放出來了。」

en_text: “It’s not like that,” he says.
zh_text: 「話不是這麼說。」他說。

en_text: “Isn’t it? How about you explain it to me.” “We kept your father locked away.”
zh_text: 「不是嗎？那你要怎麼說？」「我們沒把你爸爸放出來。」

en_text: “But he’s the only one, right? Everybody else gets tossed back out onto the street to do whatever it is they want to do.”
zh_text: 「就只有他一個，對不對？其他人都被丢回街上，爱怎樣就怎樣。」

en_text: “You think I don’t know that? You think it’s easy being a cop in this city? What would . . .,” he trails off. “Look, what’s the alternative? That we don’t try? You know how many cops we’re losing every year because nobody wants to try anymore? The last year, Edward, the last year has been damn hard. With all that’s happened—hell, even I have days where I want to give up. It’s what this city does. It produces these people. It catches them, takes them into its prisons, then churns them back out harder and rougher than they were going in. But we’re trying, Edward, and we’re making progress. Things will change. We’re doing the best we can with what we have, and I promise you, we’ll get the men who killed your wife. And I promise you they will pay.”
zh_text: 「你以爲我不知道嗎？你以爲在這裡當警察很容易？要是……」他沒把話說完。「告訴我，還有什麼辦法？你以爲我們放棄了嗎？你知不知道每年有多少警察離職，就是因爲沒有人願意堅持？去年，艾德華，去年我們過得很辛苦。發生了好多罪案——該死的，就連我也有想要放棄的時候。這座城就是這樣，製造出許多罪犯。罪犯被抓到，關到監獄裡，然後又回到城裡，比原來更難搞，更兇狠。但我們沒有放棄，艾德華，我們也看到進步了。情況會改變。我們盡力做好能做的，我向你保證，殺死你妻子的人不會逍遙法外。我一定會讓他們付出代價。」

en_text: “People think I’m the same as him,” I say.
zh_text: 「别人都以爲我跟他一樣。」我說。

en_text: “What?” “My father. They think I’m the same as him. People recognize me from the news and think I’m going to be the next big serial killer.”
zh_text: 「跟誰一樣？」「我父親。別人以爲我跟他一樣。他們看了新聞，認出我來，覺得我會變成下一個連續殺人魔。」

en_text: “No one recognizes you from the news, Edward,” he says, remembering what Barlow said. “That was twenty years ago. And you weren’t to blame for anything then.”
zh_text: 「沒有人看了新聞就能認出你，艾德華。」巴羅的話又在他耳邊響起。「都過了二十年，而且你爸爸的罪不用你來負責。」

en_text: “People are ready to convict me, they want to send me away for life. They’re frightened of me. But these men, why aren’t we frightened of them enough to keep them locked away forever? When you find them, Detective, and lock them away, what then? How long until you have to find them again for killing somebody else’s wife? Three years? Five?”
zh_text: 「大家都準備好要幫我定罪了，他們要判我無期徒刑。他們怕我。但是這些人，爲什麼我們還不夠怕他們，不判他們無期徒刑？探長，你抓到他們，把他們關起來，然後呢？要等多久你又會發現他們殺了別人的妻子？三年？五年？」

en_text: “I promise they’ll pay, Edward,” he says.
zh_text: 「我保證會讓他們付出代價，艾德華。」他說。

en_text: They reach the house and Schroder pulls into the driveway and they both climb out. The car following pulls up to the curb, its tires scraping against it. The wheels have splashed rain and dirt off the road onto the bottom half of the car.
zh_text: 他們到了艾德華家，施羅德把車子停在車道上，兩人都下了車。跟在後面的巡邏車停到馬路旁，輪胎刮到了人行道。四個輪子讓路上的雨水和泥土濺滿了下半的車身。

en_text:
They walk to the front door and Schroder unlocks it. “What happened to your friend?” Edward asks. “Huh?”
“The friend you were telling me about. He was looking into something.
zh_text:
他們走到前門，施羅德用鑰匙開了門。
「你朋友後來怎樣了？」艾德華問。
「誰？」

en_text: He ever sober up and find it?”
zh_text: 「你剛才提到的朋友。他去調查一件事。他後來清醒了嗎？找到答案了嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah. He found it, and people died because of it.” “He lose his family to bank robbers?”
zh_text: 「找到了，也害死了很多人。」「他的家人被銀行搶匪殺死了？」

en_text: “I’ll keep these tonight,” Schroder says, and he rattles the keys. “You can pick them up from the station in the morning. Where are the spares?”
zh_text: 「這些今晚先由我保管。」施羅德讓手裡的鑰匙發出叮叮噹噹的聲音。「明天早上你來警局，我就還給你。備用鑰匙在哪裡？」

en_text: “I don’t have any.” “Everybody has spare keys.”
zh_text: 「我沒有備用鑰匙。」「大家都有備用鑰匙。」

en_text: “Not me ’cause I never lose them.”
zh_text: 「我沒有，因爲我絕對不會把鑰匙弄不見。」

en_text: “Okay, Edward. Go and get some sleep,” he says. “Don’t do anything else stupid tonight. Don’t make me regret helping you out.” He closes the door and heads to the other car and drives away.
zh_text: 「好吧，艾德華，去睡吧，」他說，「今天晚上別再做傻事了。不要讓我後悔幫你做這個人情。」他關上門，上了警車，疾馳而去。

en_text: I take a leak, find the spare keys, take another leak, grab a beer, grab a jacket, and within ten minutes of being dropped off home I’m back on the road, which is better than jail, which is where I thought Schroder was going to take me for what the monster had wanted me to do tonight. The spare keys have Jodie’s car key too, and for a few seconds I can’t figure out which one to jam into the ignition.
zh_text: 我撒了一泡尿，找到備用鑰匙，又撒了一泡尿，抓了瓶啤酒，拿了外套，被送回家還不到十分鐘，我又上路了，比坐牢好，要是我聽了怪獸的話，施羅德肯定會把我丢進大牢。備用鑰匙上也掛了茱蒂的車鑰匙，我迷惘了幾秒鐘，才找到要插進打火開關的那支。

en_text: The car is harder to control than normal and there must be something wrong with it. I’m steering straight but the car keeps veering off to the left, and other times off to the right. It’s not the time to have a faulty car—the road ahead of me isn’t exactly laid out clearly because my vision is shot to hell. Everything is blurry, and when I squint I end up seeing double. I lose control of the car and hit the curb and come to a stop. I can see my house in the rear-vision mirror—I’ve only driven about thirty meters.
zh_text: 車子比平常更難操控，一定是哪裡壞了。我往前直開，車子卻老往左邊飄，有時候又往右邊滑。這時車子可不能出錯——我視線茫茫，眼前的路模糊不清。只看得到一片模糊，瞇起眼睛，卻看到重疊的影子。車子失控了，撞上人行道停了下來。我在後視鏡裡看到我家——我只開了三十公尺左右。

en_text: I give it another go, slower this time, more focused. There is even less traffic on the road now. A few people are out shopping since the malls are still open, Christmas extending the closing hours till midnight. Statistically, some of these people will go bankrupt over the Christmas season. Statistically, many of them will come home to find their homes have been burgled, or they’ll walk out of a mall to find their cars have been stolen. Statistically, one of these people will show up dead on some grass verge in the morning and Schroder’s caseload will become that much heavier for it.
zh_text: 我再試了一次，放慢了速度，更努力集中精神。路上的車子更少了。購物中心還開著，有些人去買東西，因爲耶誕節，購物中心要到半夜才停止營業。從統計數字來看，有些人會在耶誕假期破產。從統計數字來看，很多人回到家才發現被搶匪破門而入，或者走出購物中心卻發現車子被偷了。從統計數字來看，會有人一大早被發現死在路邊的草地上，施羅德要承辦的案子因此也多了一件。

en_text: I’m not familiar with the area and get lost on the way to the cemetery. I run a couple of red lights by accident, but I also end up sitting at a few green lights, which I figure balances the equation. I make it there safely and turn into the cemetery driveway. There is no detail in the church, only an absence of light, a dark shape somewhat darker than the night around it. I keep driving ahead and quickly become lost. I haven’t been out here since Jodie was buried, and then I was following everybody else. Now it’s a maze. The church disappears behind the line of trees, then it’s graves and grass everywhere, broken up by more trees. Maybe this is why it’s called the Garden City—the view is fucking fantastic when you’re dead.
zh_text: 我不熟通往墓地的路，開著開著就迷路了。不小心闖了兩個紅燈，也有幾次看到綠燈卻忘了起步，這樣應該就打平了。最後我平安到達，開上了墓地的車道。一點光線也沒有的教堂只剩下黑色的輪廓，比周圍的夜色還黑。我一直往前開，很快又迷路了。自從茱蒂下葬之後我還是第一次來，而那一次我跟在大家後面走。现在只覺得到一座迷宮。教堂消失在那一排樹後面，周圍都是墳墓跟草地，還有更多樹木散落其間。或许這就是爲什麼基督城號稱花園城翹辮子了，就可以看到美妙到該死的景色。

en_text: I drive around for about five minutes before deciding I can cover more ground on foot. I grab the beer and get out and lean against the car to open it, but slide right off the wet surface. I hit the ground and scrape my knees and drop the beer and it takes me a minute to find it. I walk among the plots searching for Jodie, even calling out to her after a few minutes. In the end I’m too tired to keep going. I sit down and lean against a grave that’s not as old as the others. The grass is very wet and the water leaches into my pants. There are gaps in the cloud cover letting moonlight through but I can’t see any moon. A light breeze pushes my wet clothes against my skin. I pop open the beer and it fizzes up from the earlier fall. What doesn’t froth out keeps me warm as the night continues to cool around me. I talk to Jodie even though the person beneath me isn’t Jodie, but someone who died a few months ago in his early twenties, according to the script on the stone, but it doesn’t say anything else about him—maybe nobody cared enough, or maybe people were glad he died.
zh_text: 我又開了五分鐘的車，然後決定用走的可能比較快。我拿起啤酒下了車，靠在車門上打開啤酒，但車身濕淋淋靠不住，讓我溜到地上。我倒在地上，擦傷了膝蓋，啤酒也掉了，找了一下子才找到。我在墓地裡亂走，尋找茱蒂，過了幾分鐘，甚至開始大喊她的名字。最後我太累了，走不動。我靠著一塊墓碑坐下來，這座墳墓不像其他的那嬮老舊。草地濡濕無比，雨水濾進了我的長褲。雲層間偶有空隙，射出少許月光，但我看不到月亮。輕柔的微風吹過來，把濕透的衣服吹得黏在我身上。我撬開剛才掉在地上的啤酒，冒出好多泡泡。泡沫流完了，剩下的啤酒讓我覺得好溫暖，因爲溫度一直降低。我對茱蒂講話，但我身下那個人不是茱蒂，墓碑上寫他才二十出頭，幾個月前去世了，沒提到其他的事情一或许大家都不在意，或許他死了大家都覺得很高興。

en_text: “I’m so sorry, Jodie,” I say. “For everything. I’m sorry you died. I’m sorry it was my fault. I’m sorry I smashed the plates against the kitchen wall.”
zh_text: 「對不起，茱蒂，」我說，「我很抱歉。我很傷心妳死了。我很抱歉，是我的錯。對不起，我對著廚房的牆把盤子都摔爛了。」

en_text: Jodie and the guy beneath me ignore me. The cemetery is deathly quiet but scenic. The sky is clearing, the veil of cloud is pulled back revealing thousands of stars. They light up the night, silhouetting the trees, shining down on the grounds where Death and a few of the friends he’s made over the years are buried all around me. The breeze becomes warm again and strong too, coming from the northwest over the Port Hills, which are lit up with street- and house lights, whipping across acres of tussock and grass and rock before sweeping down into the city. By the time it reaches the cemetery it’s picking up leaves and petals and throwing them about, it blows dirt into my eyes and I have to turn my back to it. Pretty soon the stars dim and I can no longer taste beer. I wake up what ought to be only a few minutes later, but must be several hours since the moon has been replaced by the sun. The bright light hits my eyes so hard it almost knocks a hole in the back of my head. I roll onto my side to bury my head into my pillow but there’s only grass and a cement marker. I rub my eyes and have no idea where I am for about two seconds, then it all rushes back to me. The breeze has died back down. I figure I’m one of many who have fallen asleep with a bottle of something out here with their loved ones cold in the ground. My clothes smell of sweat and vomit and Jodie’s blood.
zh_text: 茱蒂和下面那個人都不理我。墓地裡悄然無聲，但景色很美。雲層開始散去露出清澈的天空，千百顆星星在空中閃耀。星空照亮了黑夜，襯托出樹木的輪廓，照耀著地面上的死神和他這幾年來交的朋友，他們都埋在我周圍的地裡。微風又變暖了，風速也變強，從西北邊閃爍著街燈和民宅燈光的波特山吹下來，掃過一大片草叢丶草地和岩石，然後再吹到城裡。等風吹到墓地時，已經捲起了不少樹葉和花瓣，到處亂飄，塵土吹進了我的眼睛，我轉身背著風。不久，星輝變得黯淡，口中的啤酒味也消失了。我醒來，以爲自己睡了幾分鐘，但一定過了幾個小時，因爲月亮已經下沉，换成太陽高掛天空。明亮的陽光狠狠刺痛了我的眼睛，幾乎在我後腦勺上鑽出洞來。我翻過身，想躲到我的枕頭裡，卻找到草地和水泥墓碑。我揉揉眼睛，過了兩秒才想起來我在哪裡，立刻回到現實。風已經停了。我猜有很多人像我這樣，在外面喝了一瓶就睡著了，陪伴他們埋在地裡、冷冰冰的爱人。我的衣服有汗味，有嘔吐物的味道，也聞得到茱蒂的鮮血。

en_text: My body is aching as I stand up, the muscles stiff and sore. I’m not sure where my car is so I pick a direction and walk. Nothing is familiar as everything looks the same. I walk for twenty minutes in an expanding circle before finding it. The keys are still in the ignition. There are already a couple of mourners who throw me suspicious glances, probably because I look like I just crawled out of one of the graves here. The cemetery is in need of a caretaker—the lawns are too long and the gardens are being overrun by a crime wave of weeds. One side of the car is in bright sun, the other has wet leaves stuck to it.
zh_text: 站起來覺得全身發痛，肌肉又僵又痿。我不確定昨晚把車子停在哪裡，選定了方向之後就一直走。一切都很陌生，所有的東西看起來都一樣。我繞了一大圈，走了二十分鐘，才找到車子。鑰匙還插在開關裡。已經有兩三個掃墓的人面帶狐疑地瞥了我一眼，我應該看起來一副剛從墳墓裡爬出來的樣子。這塊墓地要有人來照顧——草坪該修了，雜草肆無忌憚地蓋滿了花園。車子一側沐浴在燦爛的陽光下，另一側則黏了濕葉子。

en_text: I take the backstreets home instead of the main ones, figuring they’ll be quicker, and figuring wrong. I pass a couple of people building fences, others mowing lawns, summertime activities that seem a world away from the world I live in now. When I finally make it, I race into the bathroom and take a leak doing my best to hit the bowl and not the floor and my feet. I’m pretty sure I’m draining off the only fluids I have in my body.
zh_text: 我放棄主要幹道，從小路開車回家，以爲會比較快，結果我錯了。路上看到兩個人在建造圍籬，還有人在修剪草地，這些夏日活動似乎跟我現在的世界兩不相干。終於回到家後，我飛奔到廁所裡小便，盡力對準馬桶，避開地板跟我的雙腳。我想，我應該把身體裡剩下的液體都尿完了。

en_text: I stagger through to the kitchen and open the fridge. The milk has expired but it seems to taste okay and I drink half a glass of it before deciding milk is the absolute last thing I want right now. I look at the beer. Strike that—milk ain’t that bad after all.
zh_text: 我蹣跚穿過廚房，打開冰箱。鮮奶過期了，但味道似乎還可以，我就喝了半杯，然後才覺得我現在最不想喝的東西就是鮮奶。再看看啤酒。算了鮮奶其實沒那麼糟糕。

en_text: I lean against the kitchen bench, disoriented and lost, like I don’t belong here, and that makes it harder for me to remember exactly what happened last night. Part of me doesn’t even feel like I’m back home: I’m stuck somewhere, maybe in some purgatory where the milk is always expired and my mouth is dry and my tongue sticks to the roof of it. Even my teeth are sore from grinding them in my sleep. I hang the bloody bank clothes back up before taking a long shower. It revives me a bit, at least physically, but mentally I’m exhausted as the memories of last night trickle back in.
zh_text: 我靠著廚房的流理台，覺得很迷惘很茫然，彷彿我不該在這裡，因此，我也更記不得昨晚發生了什麼事。我甚至有點覺得我還沒回到家：陷在某處，或許陷在煉獄裡，那裡的鮮奶一定都過期了，我的嘴巴一定很乾，舌頭也黏住了上顎。就連牙齒也覺得好痠痛，因爲我睡覺時一直磨牙。我把穿去銀行沾了血的衣服掛好，然後淋了一個長長的浴。我覺得恢復了一點活力，起碼身體有這種感覺，但心理上仍疲憊不堪，因爲昨晚的回憶慢慢浮現出來。

en_text: Mostly I’m ashamed by it all.
zh_text: 重點是，我覺得很羞愧。

en_text: My heart quickens as I recall pulling the knife up short of cutting Painter. I want to throw up again. I have no idea why in the hell I even went to Gerald Painter’s house. No idea what the plan was. If I’d killed Gerald Painter, would the monster have kept me sober, or abandoned me when that first splash of blood arced up onto the ceiling? What would have happened to his wife and daughter if they’d walked in on me?
zh_text: 想起我拉出刀子，卻沒有刺傷潘特，我的心跳就加速了。我又想嗌吐。我不知道我怎麼這麼该死，居然跑去潘特家。我不知道自己想做什麼。要是我殺了潘特，怪獸會讓我清醒過來嗎？還是當鮮血一噴上天花板，他就抛棄我？如果他的老婆女兒剛好目睹我行兇，她們會怎麼樣？

en_text: I tidy the kitchen, opening up and draining the remaining beer and wine down the sink. I remember what else Schroder said last night, then more importantly I remember what I said to him, and those memories seem to collide in a nice little way that jumbles everything up, and suddenly what my dad said to me as he walked away makes sense—It’s okay to listen to the voice.
zh_text: 我整理了廚房，把剩下的啤酒跟葡萄酒都開了，倒進水槽沖掉。我想起施羅德昨晚還說了一些事，最重要的是我記得我對他說了什麼，回憶似乎用很協調的方法碰撞在一起，把一切搞得雜亂無章，我突然懂了我爹進去前說的那句話「聽那聲音的準沒錯。」

en_text: I’m still a bit drunk, and I might be over the limit, but the world doesn’t sway around much as I drive through it. I find a park near the police station. My keys are waiting for me in the foyer behind the reception desk. They don’t ask me any questions about last night. All they do is ask for ID to make sure the keys belong to me. Schroder isn’t around. He’s probably at the beach somewhere or getting the last of his shopping done while Jodie lies cold in the ground. I realize I haven’t got Sam anything yet either for Christmas—me and Jodie always left that kind of thing till the last few days. There’s a guy out in front of the station with a sandwich board over his shoulders, he’s holding up a Bible and preaching his views in an abusive tone and I wonder if he knows Henry the homeless guy.
zh_text: 我還覺得有點醉，可能眞的喝太多了，但開車出門時倒不覺得眼前的景物搖動得那麼厲害。我進了警局，從接待處後面的門廳取回我的鑰匙。他們沒問昨晚發生了什麼事。只要我拿證件出來，確定鑰匙是我的就好了。施羅德不在。他可能去海灘度假了，或忙著買完耶誕節的禮物，留下茱蒂冷冰冰地長眠地底。我發覺我還沒買小珊的耶誕禮物——茱蒂跟我老喜歡把買禮物留到最後幾天。警局前有個肩膀上掛了廣告板的人，把聖經舉得高高，用一種罵街的口氣講道，不知道他認不認識遊民亨利。

en_text: I drive out to the prison, passing a couple of malls on the way where traffic is spilling out from the parking lot onto the road, Christmas shopping in full bloom now, people pushing carts full of groceries. There’s a billboard twice the size of a bus staked into the ground on the edge of the city advertising a brand-new subdivision, calling it the suburb of the future. I wonder what that means. I wonder if the billboard means Christchurch is stuck in the past, or that the new subdivision will resemble something out of The Jetsons. There is smoke drifting up from the fields, farmers burning off waste. Large irrigation units are watering crops under the hot sun.
zh_text: 我開車往監獄去，路上經過了兩座購物中心，車潮從停車場湧出，現在是耶誕節購物的最高峰，大家都推著裝滿貨品的購物車。到了城緣，有一塊公車兩倍大的廣告牌聳立在地，廣告全新的重劃區，稱之爲未來的郊區。我不知道那是什麼意思。我猜，廣告板的意思是基督城脫離不了過去，抑或重劃區就像卡通《摩登家庭》裡的樣子。田野中冒出了白煙，應該是農人在燒廢物。龐大的灌漑系統在烈陽下幫農作物澆水。

en_text: Sam’s bag is still packed in the backseat, full of goodies of death that I have to return to their rightful place. If Curious Schroder had taken a peek, things might have turned out very different.
zh_text: 小珊的書包仍放在後座，裝滿了死亡玩具，我得把它們放回原處。如果好奇寶寶施羅德看了一眼，後果或许會完全不一樣。

en_text: I don’t phone ahead this time. I park the car in the same spot and the same woman I spoke to yesterday is here today, the same smile—a smile that could make beached whales roll back into the water—falters when she recognizes me.
zh_text: 這次我沒先打電話。我把車子停在同一個地方，昨天那個女人今天也在，臉上掛著同樣的笑容她的笑能讓擱淺的鯨魚滾回海洋裡認出我是誰後，她的笑容僵住了。

en_text: “I’m here to see my father,” I say, as if there could be any one of a hundred reasons.
zh_text: 「我來見我父親。」我說，這個理由彷彿很充足。

en_text: “He’s been waiting for you,” she says.
zh_text: 「他正在等你。」她說。

en_text: “But . . . I didn’t phone ahead.”
zh_text: 「但是···我没通知他我要来。」

en_text: “Must be a miracle,” she says, but she’s wrong. I don’t know what to think about my dad figuring that I’d show back up. Mostly it pisses me off that he’s arrogant enough to think it, and I suspect perhaps arrogance is the wrong word since he was right.
zh_text: 「一定是奇蹟。」她錯了。爹知道我會再來，讓我心中百感交集。最主要的是我很氣，氣他居然如此傲慢，料到我會回來，我猜說他傲慢也不對，因爲他眞的料到了。

en_text: “You listened to the voice,” he says, once the guard has escorted me down to the visitors’ room. It was the same guard from yesterday and he gave me the same rules as yesterday, reinforcing the no-yelling one twice. There are fewer people in the visitors’ room, which should make it seem bigger, but somehow it has the opposite effect. Fewer people makes it colder, stagnant, far more depressing, it makes it seem the walls are closing in and I can only imagine what the cells must be like. The Carver isn’t anywhere to be seen. Nobody pays me any interest.
zh_text: 「你聽從了那個聲音。」警衛一把我送進訪客室，爹就對我說。警衛跟昨天是同一個人，他重複了跟昨天一樣的規則，重複了兩次不可以大吼大叫。訪客室裡的人沒有昨天那麼多，空間應該會有放大的感覺，不知怎地卻相反。人變少了，感覺更冰冷，更蕭條，更令人沮喪，似乎四面牆都對著我壓過來，我忍不住想像牢房是什麼樣子。基督城屠夫不在，其他人對我也沒有興趣。

en_text: I sit opposite him. He’s different from yesterday. Younger, if that’s possible—as though all this is rejuvenating him.
zh_text: 我在爹對面坐下。他看起來變了，更年輕了。居然能變年輕——彷佛這一切讓他回春了。

en_text: “Let me ask you something,” he says. “You think being an accountant gives you the credentials to know what the entire sum of a man is?”
zh_text: 「我問你，」他說，「你覺得當會計師讓你有能力計算出一個人的總和嗎？」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “See, twenty years in here, I have them. A man is made up of many parts,” he says. “There are things within his core. They are shaped by his family, his friends, shaped by the blood that runs through him. Of course the events shape a man too. Those in the past, and those unfolding in front of him. I am the sum of many things,” he says. “You, your sister, your mother, they were part of me, as well as my own family, growing up. But it wasn’t enough to make me complete. I thought it might be, I mean, when I first met your mother and when our family began, I thought it might be enough. But it wasn’t. You and me, we’re made up from the same components.”
zh_text: 「瞧，坐牢二十年，我就學到了。一個人有很多組成部分，」他說，「最重要的核心取決於他的家人、朋友、身體裡流的血液。經歷，當然也會改變一個人。過去的事件，未來要發生的事件。我是很多東西的總和。你，你姊姊，你媽媽，都影響了我，還有從小養育我的家人。但我還不夠完整。我本來以爲可以，遇到你母親後，我們成立了自己的家庭，我以爲那樣就夠了，但是不夠。你跟我，我們都由同樣的東西組成。」

en_text: “You’re full of shit,” I say.
zh_text: 「你全是大便吧。」我說。

en_text: “You’re my son,” he says. “You can’t deny much of what is inside me is inside you too.”
zh_text: 「你是我兒子，」他說，「你不能否認，我有的你也有。」

en_text: “You’re wrong. I can deny that because it isn’t true. You, me, we’re nothing alike.”
zh_text: 「你錯了。我可以否認，因爲你錯了。你跟我，完全不一樣。」

en_text: “Why’d you become an accountant?” he asks.
zh_text: 「你爲什麼要當會計師？」他問。

en_text: I lean back, unsure of his point. “I don’t know,” I say, shrugging.
zh_text: 我靠向椅背，不知道他想說什麼。「我不知道。」我聳聳肩。

en_text: “Want to know what I think?” “No.”
zh_text: 「想知道我的看法嗎？」「不想。」

en_text: “Well, you’re going to hear—after all, it’s why you came out here.” “Then why ask,” I say, shaking my head. “Just spit it out.”
zh_text: 「嗯，我還是要說——畢竟，你來就爲了聽我講話。」「那幹嘛還問，」我搖搖頭，「有屁快放。」

en_text: “It was to make me proud. You wanted to be an accountant like your dad.”
zh_text: 「你希望我以你爲傲。你要跟你爹一樣，當個會計師。」

en_text: “Wait . . .”
“What for? So you can deny it.” “Wait . . . you were an accountant?”
zh_text: 「慢什麼？給你否認的機會嗎？」「慢著···你以前也是會計師？」

en_text: “You were nine years old when I was taken away. Don’t try pretending you have no idea what I used to do for a living. You’re just like your old man,” he says.
zh_text: 「我被帶走的時候你都九歲了。別假裝你不知道我做哪一行。你跟你老子一樣。」

en_text: I don’t answer him. I don’t even want to think about it.
zh_text: 我沒回答。我連想都不願意想。

en_text: “And the voice confirms it. My darkness and your monster—they’re as similar as we are.”
zh_text: 「那聲音，就是確證。我的闈黑跟你的怪獸他們很像，我們也很像。」

en_text: “This is crazy,” I say. “You’re crazy. I don’t know why I came along. I hate myself for showing up yesterday. I’m going to go,” I say, but don’t make any motion.
zh_text: 「別再發瘋了。」我說。「你瘋了。我不知道我爲什麼要來。昨天來這裡，我已經很氣我自己。我要走了。」但我卻沒站起身來。

en_text: “You came here to learn,” he says, “not to dismiss everything I say.” “No. I came here because . . . ,” I trail off, suddenly unsure.
zh_text: 「你來這裡，因爲你想向我學習，」他說，「不要對我講的話嗤之以鼻」「錯，我來是因爲···」我的聲音不見了，突然不知道怎麼接下去。

en_text: “Because you want answers. Everything that’s happened over the last week . . . You’re hearing the voice, aren’t you, Jack? It’s come back.”
zh_text: 「因爲你想要答案。過去一個禮拜發生了很多事···你聽到了聲音，對不對，傑克？那聲音回來了。」

en_text: My dad smiles. It’s the same smile I remember when I was a kid, and part of me, one small part of what makes up the whole of who I am—at least according to my dad—wants to hug him, wants to cry against his chest and ask him to make everything better.
zh_text: 爹微微一笑。我記得小時候曾看過同樣的微笑，我心裡有個念頭，想要讓自己變成完整的我一就我爹的話來說是這樣一想要擁抱他，想要靠在他懷裡哭泣，想要慿他的力量來改變一切。

en_text: “You’re here to ask for my help,” he adds.
zh_text: 「你來這裡，要我幫你忙。」他補充說。

en_text: I lean forward and the guard seems about to say something, but stops when he sees I’m not leaning forward for a hug or punch. I lower my voice. “You said it was a good thing the cops had no idea who killed Jodie. What did you mean by that?”
zh_text: 我的身體往前傾，警衛欲言又止，因爲我並沒有靠過去擁抱我爹或揍他一拳。我放低了聲言：「你說，警察不知道誰殺了茱蒂，其實是好事。你是什麼意思？」

en_text: My dad glances up at the guard, who is openly staring at us, then my dad leans in too, and suddenly we’re pals, we’re whispering secrets—let the good times roll.
zh_text: 爹向警衛看了一眼，他正瞪大眼睛看著我們，然後我爹也靠過來，突然之間我們變成死黨了，我們在講悄悄話且珍惜美好的時光吧

en_text: “It means what you think it means.”
zh_text: 「意思是，你覺得是什麼意思，就是什麼意思。」

en_text: “I think it means that you’re insane. That you couldn’t care less about what happened to my family. Or even to your family.”
zh_text: 「我覺得意思是，你瘋了。你對我家人的不幸一點也不在乎。對你家人的不幸你也不在乎。」

en_text: “No you don’t,” he says. “It means what it means.” “Which is?”
zh_text: 「不，你才不是這麼想。」他說。「意思是，就是那個意思。」

en_text: “It means those men are still out there, awaiting justice, and there isn’t any reason it has to be police justice.” “Except for the law,” I say.
zh_text: 「意思是那些人還逍遙法外，等待正義的判決，而且絕對不可能有警方來執行正義。」「除非是司法正義。」我說。

en_text: “Did the law step in to save your wife?” he asks. “Does the law warm up the other side of your bed at night? Does it give your daughter somebody to look up to? Make her school lunches and tuck her in at night and tell her to have sweet dreams? Is the law there to hold your life together, is it there to hold your daughter’s hand and tell her everything is going to be all right? Was it there to stop the blood dripping out of Jodie’s body when she hit the road?”
zh_text: 「司法站出來救了你老婆的命嗎？」他問。「法律會把幫你暖床嗎？法律給你女兒一個可以依靠的人？幫她做午餐帶去學校，晚上幫她蓋好被子，祝她好夢連連？法律會讓你的生活上軌道？會握著你女兒的手，告訴她一切都沒問題？茱蒂倒在路上時，法律會站出來，停止鮮血從她的身體流出？」

en_text: “Shut up,” I say. “I don’t want you talking about her like that.”
zh_text: 「不要再說了，」我說，「我不喜歡聽到你講到她的事情。」

en_text: “Twenty years ago, son, you weren’t ready to kill that dog, but the darkness, your monster, made you do it. You killed that dog and the police came sniffing around with their questions. The darkness tries to make you impulsive, son, and twenty years ago your darkness got me arrested.”
zh_text: 「二十年前，兒子，你還沒準備好宰掉那條狗，但闍黑，你的怪獸，逼你下手了。你殺了那條狗，警察來明查暗訪，問了好多問題。闍黑想激發你的衝動，兒子，二十年前，你的闍黑害我被捕了。」

en_text: “Huh? What are you talking about?”
zh_text: 「什麼？你這話什麼意思？」

en_text: “It was that damn dog. You killed it, and you invited the police into our neighborhood. Do you remember you wrapped the steak in a plastic bag? You did, and when you gave the steak to the dog you dropped the plastic bag. The bag was from home, son, and it had my fingerprints on it. They matched the prints found with the prostitutes. The police got warrants to search houses in the street because they knew a killer lived there. They came with their questions and then they came back with more. They searched the garage, son. They looked for the mix of sharp things you put into that steak, and they found them. But they found other things too. Other . . . mementos.”
zh_text: 「那該死的狗。你殺了狗，把條子引來了我們這一區。你記得嗎？你把牛排包在塑膠袋裡。眞的，然後你把牛排給狗吃了，塑膠袋掉在路上。兒子，那塑膠袋從我們家來的，上面有我的指紋。他們發現指紋跟妓女身上的吻合。警察申請了搜查令，因爲他們知道殺人犯就住在我們這條街上。他們來問了問題，然後又來問了更多的問題。他們搜了我們家的車庫，兒子。他們要找你放到牛排裡的銳利物品，找到了。但他們也找到其他的東西。其他的……紀念品。」

en_text: “You kept things from the victims?”
zh_text: 「你留下了被害人的東西？」

en_text: “Small things. Earrings, mostly. Sometimes a necklace. I couldn’t help myself. They came looking for fishhooks and nails and they found souvenirs of my women.”
zh_text: 「小東西。大部分是耳環。也有幾條項鍊。我忍不住。他們來找魚鉤，卻找到了我留下的紀念品。」

en_text: “You were . . . wait, you were caught because of me?” I ask.
zh_text: 「你……等等，因爲我，你才被逮捕？」我問。

en_text: “It wasn’t your fault,” he says.
zh_text: 「不是你的錯。」他說。

en_text: “Honestly, I don’t know if I care whether it was my fault or not,” I say. And it’s true. Am I glad my father was caught and could no longer kill? Yes. Am I upset he was taken away? Absolutely. I think about what it means. On one hand I’m a hero. I saved future victims. On the other hand I betrayed my family. If I hadn’t listened to the voice, if I hadn’t killed that dog, my sister, my mother, they’d still be alive. I killed them as surely as I killed that dog. Last week I sacrificed Jodie to save a bank teller. Twenty years ago I sacrificed my family to save other prostitutes. What does that make me? Does it make me a trader in death?
zh_text: 「老實說，我不知道，是不是我的錯，我也不在乎。」我說。眞的。我高不高興我爹被抓了，再也不能殺人？高興。他被逮捕了，我傷不傷心？當然很傷心。我想了一想其中的意義。一方面來說，我是英雄，以後再也不會有人受害。另一方面我背叛了我的家人。要是我不聽那個聲音，我不殺那條狗，我媽媽跟我姊姊，现在應該還活著。她們等於是我害死的，就跟我害死那條狗一樣。上禮拜我犧牲了茱蒂，救了銀行出納員。二十年前我犧牲了家人，保護其他的妓女。那我算什麼？死亡的交易員？

en_text: “Son, I’m not blaming you. You couldn’t know, and you were too young to control the darkness. Since that dog you killed, how many times have you heard it?”
zh_text: 「兒子，我不怪你。你不知情，你也太小了，沒辦法控制闍黑。自從你殺了那條狗，你聽到那聲音幾次了？」

en_text: “Why are you telling me any of this?”
zh_text: 「你告訴我這些，有什麼意義？」

en_text: “The men who did this, they have something inside them too, not a voice like we have, but something that makes them different. Each of them must have some criminal history,” he says. “Think about it, it’s obvious.”
zh_text: 「那些涉案的人，他們也有自己的魔怪，不一定像我們會聽到聲音，但也有那種東西讓他們異於凡人。他們一定都有前科，」他說，「想一想，很明顯。」

en_text: I think about it. I think about what Schroder said last night, our nice friendly chat about people getting locked away and let right back out, our nice friendly chat about what a huge revolving door prison is these days.
zh_text: 我想了想。我想到施羅德昨晚說的話，我們親切和諧地聊到有人入獄後又立刻被放出去，我們融洽地討論現代的監獄就像巨大的旋轉門。

en_text: “They’ve all spent time in jail,” he carries on. “Had to have. I’m betting some of them, if not all of them, probably met in jail. That’s what jail is, right? For me, it’s my home. I’ll never see outside of these walls again, but for these men it’s a place to learn new skills, make new friends.”
zh_text: 「他們都坐過牢，」他接下去，「一定坐過牢。我猜其中幾個應該是坐牢的時候認識的，或許不是所有人都一起坐過牢。那不就是監獄的功能嗎？我覺得這裡跟我家一樣。我再也看不到外面的世界，但這些人卻在牢裡學到了新的技能，認識新的朋友。」

en_text: I stay silent, but continue to listen.
zh_text: 我沉默不語，繼續聽他說。

en_text: “Jail takes people in, it educates them in very, very dangerous ways, then it spits them back out into society. Most if not all of Jodie’s killers have walked in and out of these doors for various crimes.”
zh_text: 「監獄把他們收進來，用非常非常危險的方法教育他們，然後再把他們送回社會裡。害死茱帝的人一定會犯下罪案，進出過這裡的大門。」

en_text: “And you know who these people are, right? It’s why you’re telling me.
zh_text: 「你知道他們是誰，是嗎？所以你才要告訴我。你要我把他們揪出來，满足你的闍黑。」

en_text: You want me to find these people to satisfy your darkness.” “I think we can help each other out,” he says.
zh_text: 「我想，我可以幫你，你也可以幫我。」他說。

en_text: “No way. This is bullshit,” I say. “I’m not helping you out.”
zh_text: 「不可能。都是胡說八道，」我說，「我才不幫你。」

en_text: “Would that be such a bad thing, son? Or would you rather let them go free? The voice can be a bad thing, son, but it can be a good thing too. You can use it to make the men who did this pay for what happened.”
zh_text: 「兒子，幫我有那麼糟嗎？還是你寧可讓這些人逍遙法外？那聲音或許無益，兒子，但也有可能幫到你。你可以聽從那聲音，讓那些壞人付出代價。」

en_text: “To satisfy your darkness?”
zh_text: 「來滿足你的闇黑？」

en_text: “No. To keep you sane. If you can’t control it the way I could, you’re going to hurt good people.”
zh_text: 「不。讓你不要發瘋。你如果不能像我一樣懂得控制那聲音，你會害到好人。」

en_text: “Hang on a second. Are you saying you controlled it all those years?” “Of course. I gave in to it as well, in a way, but I controlled it. That’s why I never killed anybody who mattered.”
zh_text: 「等一等。你是說，這些年來，你都懂得怎麼控制？」「當然。我也會屈服於那聲音之下，但我懂得控制。所以我殺的人都無關緊要。」

en_text:
“You killed eleven prostitutes,” I say. “How can you say they don’t matter?”
“They don’t.”
“They do.”
zh_text:
「你殺了十一個妓女。」我說。「怎麼能說她們都無關緊要？」
「没有人在乎。」
「一定有。」

en_text: “Compared to what? Compared to my own family? My friends? Our neighbors? They didn’t matter compared to anybody else I knew. Once you can control it, it’ll keep you from hurting good people. It’ll keep you from going off the rails and losing your daughter. The monster won’t go away now, not if it’s taking the steering wheel and making you do things. If you can’t control it, you’re going to be more like your old man than you ever thought possible. We’re blood men,” he says.
zh_text: 「怎麼比？跟我的家人比嗎？我的鄰居？跟我認識的人比起來，她們眞的無關緊要。一旦你能控制那聲音，你就不會傷害好人。聽那聲音的，你不會偏離軌道，失去你的女兒。怪獸現在不會走了，除非他能搶走方向盤，讓你表現一下。如果你控制不了怪獸，結果絕對超乎你的想像，你會變得跟你老子一樣。我們都是嗜血之人。」他說。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Other people, they’re attracted to looks, or money, nice jobs, all the hollow things in this world. Other men are attracted to tits or ass, women are attracted to smiles and eyes. Your monster, my darkness, they’re attracted to blood. It makes us blood men.” He stands up, and suddenly I realize that this meeting, if that’s the word for it, is over. I stand up too. Dad reaches over and grabs my hands.
zh_text: 「有些人醉心美貌，或喜歡金錢和好工作，這世界上一切膚淺的東西。有些人喜歡胸部或屁股，女人則深受微笑或眼睛吸引。你的怪獸，我的闇黑，則喜歡血。所以我們都是嗜血之人。」他站起來，我突然發現這場會面如果可以稱爲會面的話結束了。我也站起來。爹靠過來，抓住我的雙手。

en_text: “No touching,” the guard says, and when Dad doesn’t let go, the guard comes over and separates us. “That’s enough for today,” the guard says, stamping his authority on us.
zh_text: 「不可以有肢體接觸。」警衛說，但爹不放手，他只得過來把我們分開。「夠了。」警衛說，表明他的權威。

en_text: Dad walks away. “I love you, son,” he says, but he doesn’t turn back to say it. “No matter what happens now, remember that.”
zh_text: 爹退後了。「兒子，我愛你，」他說，但沒轉過身來，「不論發生什麼事，都不要忘了我愛你。」

en_text: I don’t know how to answer him, so I don’t. I walk away too. And it’s not until I’m in the parking lot that I look down at the folded piece of paper in my hand.
zh_text: 我不知道怎麼回答，所以不發一語。我也離開了訪客室。走到停車場，我才敢鬆開手掌，露出手心裡摺起來的紙條。

en_text: I haven’t seen my father’s handwriting in twenty years. He used to help me with my homework. We’d lie down on the floor in the living room with the TV going but the volume mostly down, discussing why bees collected honey or how seven wouldn’t divide into twelve. He’d write things down for me, he’d read over my assignments and jot down ideas in the margins, other times he’d take notes out of whatever books I was searching through for answers. He has this elegant printing style, where the letters don’t bleed into each other, each one separate, easy to read, easy to recognize even after all this time. He always wanted me to be the best that I could at school. Those days come back to me, the smells of my mum baking something, or cooking dinner, the TV going, laughter, warm weather, a dog barking, school uniforms, life.
zh_text: 我已經二十年沒看到父親的字跡了。以前他常幫我做作業。我們會躺在客廳的地板上，開了電視，但把音量放到最低，討論爲什麼蜜蜂會收集蜂蜜，或七爲何沒辦法整除十二。他會幫我記筆記，看過我的作業，在空白的地方草草寫下想法，有時候我在書裡找答案，他也幫忙寫筆記。他的字跡是高雅的印刷體，字母不會連在一起，各有各的位置，讀起來很輕鬆，就算過了這麼久，仍然一看就能認出來。他總希望我在學校能考第一名。我想起了從前的日子，媽媽在廚房烤東西或煮晚餐，香味撲鼻，電視開著，笑聲不斷，氣候溫暖，外面傳來狗叫聲，我的學校制服，

en_text: Another car pulls into the parking lot. It’s a rundown Mercedes, the type that isn’t old enough to be classic, but nowhere new enough to be cool. There’s a long scratch running along the bottom of the passenger side. A guy, maybe around twenty, steps out of it, his dreadlocks bouncing.
zh_text: 另一台車開進了停車場。陳舊的賓士，款式還沒老到能成爲經典，但絕對稱不上拉風的新款。副駕駛座那側的車門下方有道長長的刮痕。一名二十歲左右的男子下車，他留了雷鬼頭，滿頭的辮子跳上跳下。

en_text: “Hey, bro, what up?” he asks, tilting his head upward as he does so. I immediately hate him. His T-shirt is full of holes and has I ATE AT THE BLEEDING BUDGIE all in capital letters across the front of it. No picture, no further explanation, maybe there’s a punch line on the back, but I don’t look. He realizes his mistake in speaking to me because I ignore him. He shrugs and heads in through the glass doors.
zh_text: 「嘿，老兄，還行嗎？」他問，把頭往上揚了揚。我立刻心生厭惡。他的T恤上用大寫字母寫了「我在該死的長尾鸚鵡那邊吃過了」。沒有圖片，沒有其他解釋，或許背面還有笑點的關鍵，但我不想看。他發現他不該跟我講話，因爲我默然以對。他聳聳肩，往玻璃門走去。

en_text: The air in the car is so hot it almost curls the paper my dad gave me. I wind the windows down but it doesn’t help. I read it over a couple of times and think about what it means.
zh_text: 車裡的空氣燠熱，爹的紙條都熱到要捲起來了。我搖下車窗，溫度卻沒跟著下降。我反覆讀了兩遍，思索爹想跟我說什麼。

en_text: Listen to the voice. Shane Kingsly. 23 Stoneview Road.
zh_text: 聽那聲音的話。夏恩·金斯理。石景街二十三號。

en_text: I drive home, but the only voice speaking comes from the radio. The news comes on but the announcer ignores the bank robbery and doesn’t mention anything about the men being caught. I end up pulling in behind another slow-moving truck so I take a different way home, getting caught instead at a set of roadworks where the street has been ripped up and there’s dust and dirt in the air. There are exposed pipes and wiring and machinery but nobody around, the workers off for the Christmas break, the roadworks now in limbo until sometime next month. Tiny bits of gravel shoot out from beneath the tires of the car ahead of me, hitting the windscreen but not chipping it. My cell phone rings. I recognize the number.
zh_text: 我開車回家，一路上只聽到收音機的聲音。開始播新聞了，但節目主持人沒有播報跟銀行搶案相關的報導，也沒提到警方是否逮捕了搶匪。最後我跟在一台慢呑呑的卡車後，所以我換了一條路回家，結果卻碰上好幾處道路施工，路面都被翻開了，空氣中滿是塵土。水管、電線和機械都暴露在外，卻沒有人管，工人都回家過耶誕節了，要棄置到下個月才會有人回來施工。前面那台車的輪胎下不斷彈出細小的砂礫，打在我的擋風玻璃上，幸好沒留下缺口。我的手機響了，螢幕上出現熟悉的號碼。
