en_text: “You went to visit your dad again,” Schroder says. “Want to tell me why?”
zh_text: 「你又去探望你父親了，」施羅德說。「爲什麼？可以告訴我嗎？」

en_text:
“He’s my dad. I don’t need a reason other than that. And I certainly don’t need to give a reason to you.”
“You sound different, Edward.” “Yeah?”
zh_text:
「他是我爹，這理由就夠了吧。而且我當然不需要告訴你爲什麼。」
「是嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah. You sound like you’ve been thinking about things, and I’m pretty sure I wouldn’t like the kind of things you’ve been thinking.”
zh_text: 「是，聽起來你似乎想了很多事情，我想，我應該不喜歡你腦袋裡的想法。」

en_text: Somehow I think Schroder is the kind of guy who might like what I was thinking—problem is I can’t share with him. “Are you ringing to tell me you’ve caught the men who killed my wife?”
zh_text: 不知爲何，我覺得施羅德應該是那種人，或許他會很喜歡我的想法一問題是我不能告訴他我在想什麼。「你打電話來，是爲了告訴我你們已經抓到殺死我妻子的兇手？」

en_text: “We’re working on it.”
zh_text: 「我們正在努力。」

en_text: “I thought so. So why are you calling, other than to bust my balls for visiting my dad?”
zh_text: 「我猜也是這樣。那除了叨唸我去探監，打來有何指教？」

en_text: “To remind you not to get any bad ideas.” “I don’t even know what that means.”
zh_text: 「我要提醒你，不要起壤念頭。」「我有什麼壤念頭？連我自己都不知道。」

en_text: “I think you do. I think you’re so lost right now you’re turning to your father for advice, and trust me, he’s the last person you want to be turning to.”
zh_text: 「我覺得你知道。我覺得你很迷惘，才會找你爹給你建議，相信我，找誰都可以，千萬不要找他。」

en_text: “I keep thinking if you spent less time worrying about my life, you’d spend more time on catching the people who ruined it.”
zh_text: 「我一直覺得，如果你少花一點時間擔心我怎麼過活，就能多花一點時間抓到那些毀了這一切的人。」

en_text: “Don’t do anything stupid, Edward.”
zh_text: 「别做傻事，艾德華。」

en_text: “To who? Nobody knows who I could do anything stupid to anyway!” I say, and I hang up. He doesn’t call back.
zh_text: 「會害到誰？沒有人知道萬一我做了傻事，我會害了哪些人！」我掛上電話，他也沒再打來。

en_text: Back home I sit at the dinner table and smooth the piece of paper out, pressing it flat against the wood, pushing my fingertips and palms onto it as if ironing out the wrinkles. My house is still empty. No shadows, no presence, my wife even less here today than she was yesterday. I have a name and an address and I don’t know what I’m supposed to do with it. Not once did I even think of giving that information to Schroder when I was on the phone, and weighing it up now I’m glad I didn’t. It wasn’t Schroder’s wife who got killed. Does that mean I’m listening to the voice? I listen for it now. There’s nothing.
zh_text: 回到家後，我坐到餐桌旁，把紙條攤開，對著木板壓平，用指尖和手掌用力推，想把皺褶熨掉。我家仍然很空蕩。沒有陰影，沒有幽魂，我的妻子離家愈來愈遠。紙張上寫了一個名字，一個地址，该怎麼辦？剛才講電話的時候，好幾次蹦出要告訴施羅德這件事的念頭，現在坐下來好好考慮了一下，倒慶幸我沒說。死的又不是施羅德的妻子。難道這表示我已經聽了那聲音的話？我側耳傾聽。安靜無聲。

en_text: I can’t go through what I went through last night. Can’t drive to this man’s house and . . . and what?
zh_text: 我沒辦法重蹈昨晚的覆轍。難道我又要開車去找這個人···然後呢？

en_text: Let me help you.
zh_text: 讓我來幫你吧。

en_text: And there it is.
zh_text: 来了。

en_text: “No,” I say, and the word sounds empty in my empty home.
zh_text: 「不要。」在空空蕩蕩的家裡，我的聲音也很空洞。

en_text: We can do this.
zh_text: 我们可以合作。

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「不要。」

en_text: Then let me do this for you.
zh_text: 那讓我幫你吧。

en_text: I go online and search for Shane Kingsly. He shows up pretty quick, he’s made the news on and off his entire life. Nothing big—not in the taking-a-life way of being big. He’s done plenty of shitty things. Plenty of theft convictions. He has some assault charges, and a couple of drug possession charges. Not all the statistics are here to tell me how many years he’s spent in jail on and off. His last sentence was for two years after he held up a service station with a shotgun. It doesn’t say when he was released from jail, but it must have been early for being a model prisoner—which I guess is easy to do when there aren’t any service stations or shotguns in prison. This man was one of the six, but he wasn’t the one who planned it. Is this the man that killed Jodie? He may well be.
zh_text: 我上網搜尋夏恩·金斯理的名字。一下子冒出了很多結果，他這一生上過好多次報。都不嚴重丨沒有到殺人那麼嚴重。他做過不少鳥事。多次因竊盗罪而被判刑。數次因攻擊他人而遭到指控，還有兩次則是持有毒品。這裡的統計數字無法告訴我他斷斷續續坐了多少年的牢。最近一次他持霰彈槍挾持加油站，遭判刑兩年。我找不到他何時出獄，但應該很早，因爲他是模範犯人丨我想要當模範也不難，因爲監獄裡沒有加油站也沒有霰彈槍。這人是其中一名搶匪，但他不是主謀。茱蒂是他殺的嗎？有可能。

en_text: When the phone rings it’s my father-in-law.
zh_text: 電話響起，我岳父打來的。

en_text: “When are you coming to pick Sam up?” he asks. “She misses you.”
zh_text: 「你什麼時候要來接小珊？」他問。「她很想你。」

en_text: “I know. I’m sorry,” I hear myself saying. I’m on automatic now. “I’ve been busy. I’ve been at the police station all morning.”
zh_text: 「我知道，我很抱歉。」我聽見自己的回答，無意識的句子。「我很忙，一整個早上都在警察局。」

en_text: “Do they have . . . any news?” “Not yet.”
zh_text: 「喔，他們有……消息了嗎？」「没有。」

en_text: “Are you okay, Edward? You sound weird.” “I’m fine. Can I talk to Sam?”
zh_text: 「艾德華？你沒事吧？你講話聽起來怪怪的。」「我沒事。讓我跟小珊講話好嗎？」

en_text: “Sure. Hang on a second.” “Daddy?”
zh_text: 「當然好，等等。」「爸爸？」

en_text: “Hello, honey. Daddy-Nat and Gramma taking good care of you?” “We’ve been putting up a Christmas tree,” she says. “They let me help. It was so cool. Will Santa bring something for Mummy this year?”
zh_text: 「哈囉，小寶貝。納老爹跟阿嬤對妳好不好呀？」「我們把耶誕樹搭起來了，」她說，「他們也讓我幫忙。好酷唷。耶誕老公公今年會送什麼禮物給媽咪？」

en_text: I sit down, my legs weak. I suddenly realize that I have no idea where our cat is. I can’t even remember the last time I saw him, and I’m not even sure if I’ve been feeding him or if he’s even still alive. Jesus—the monster didn’t get him when I was drunk, did it?
zh_text: 我雙腿一軟，坐了下來。突然發覺，我們家的貓不知道去哪裡了。連上次看到他是什麼時候都想不起來，也不確定我有沒有餵他，說不定他已經死了。老天啊，難道我爛醉如泥的時候怪獸拿他下手了嗎？

en_text: “Daddy?”
zh_text: 「爸爸？」

en_text: “Not this year, honey. I’m going to come and see you, okay? Tell Daddy-Nat and Gramma that I’m on my way.”
zh_text: 「小寶貝，今年沒有禮物。我過去看妳好不好？告訴納老爹跟阿嬤爸爸會去。」

en_text: “Okay, Daddy,” she says, and hangs up without another word.
zh_text: 「好。」她掛上電話，沒說其他的。

en_text: I pack some of her clothes. Jodie bought a bag for this a couple of years ago as occasionally Sam spends the night at her grandparents’. I find a couple of toys, and I figure it ought to be enough. Everything else—pajamas, toothbrush, et cetera—are at Nat’s house.
zh_text: 我把她的一些衣服裝到袋子裡。兩年前茱蒂特別買了一個提包，因爲小珊偶爾會去外公外婆家過夜。我又找了一兩個玩具裝進去，應該夠了吧。睡衣、牙刷等必備用品都在納森家。

en_text:
The sun is still blazing bright, the day isn’t as hot as it was a few hours ago but I still drive with the window down. Christchurch weather has the ability to turn on a dime. There are bus stops full of people all waiting to go somewhere, tourists with backpacks half the size of them visiting the Garden City, mums with baby carriages and bags full of shopping. Every mailbox outside every house is jammed full of supermarket and store brochures. Kids on front lawns are running through and sitting on top of sprinklers. I pass hedgehogs flattened by cars and dogs walking freely along sidewalks, sniffing at fast-food bags dropped in the gutters. I’m in control the entire drive, and I’m in control when I pull up in the driveway and step out. Sam comes and hugs me, and leads me inside to show off the Christmas tree. It’s the same tree they have every year. I smile at the tree and say how good it looks, but the truth is I’ll probably never enjoy Christmas again.
“You look like hell,” Nat says, and I guess he’s right—I haven’t really checked.
zh_text:
太陽依舊熾烈耀眼，比起幾個小時以前，溫度已經下降了，但上路後我仍搖下了車窗。基督城的天氣說變就變。路上的公車站旁滿滿都是等著要去某處的人，也有來這座花園城參觀的遊客，身後負著半個人大的背包，還有推著嬰兒車滿手購物袋的媽媽們。房屋外的信箱都塞滿了超級市場跟商店的廣告傳單。孩子们在前院的草地上嬉戲，或坐在灑水器上面。路上也看到被車子壓扁的刺蝟，自己沿著人行道散步的狗，對著丢在排水溝裡速食店的袋子嗅嗅聞聞。一路上我都沒有失控，把車子停到車道上，然後下車，我還是把自己控制得很好。小珊跑過來擁抱我，帶我到屋子裡，得意洋洋地展示耶誕樹。他們每年都用同一棵樹。我微微一笑，告訴她很好看，但事實上，或许我再也無法享受耶誕節的氣氛了。
「你看起來跟死人一樣。」納森說，或許吧我根本沒檢查儀容「要不要吃點東西？」小珊的阿嬤問。

en_text: “Can I fix you something to eat?” Diana asks.
“Sure, thanks,” I say. I don’t think I’ve eaten anything since the boxed cereal yesterday.
zh_text: 「好，謝謝。」昨天吃過盒裝穀片後，就沒其他東西下肚了。

en_text: I spend a couple hours at the house. I fit in well enough, but it’s like I’m an outsider the entire time, and even though my in-laws try hard, I think this may be the last time I visit them—other than to drop Sam off or pick her up. I can’t be here with them, and I don’t know why. They don’t blame me for what happened, but their pain and loss are written all over their faces. I don’t need to see that, not now, perhaps never again. After dinner we sit out on the porch, me and Nat, him drinking a beer and wondering why I don’t want one too.
zh_text: 我在他們家待了快兩個小時。努力跟大家融洽相處，但我一直覺得自己是個外人，雖然岳父母也盡力了，我想著或許這是最後一次來拜訪以後就只送小珊過來，然後接她回家。我不能跟他們處在同一座屋簷下，我不知道爲什麼。他們不會把茱蒂的死怪在我頭上，但他們痛失愛女的哀傷都寫在臉上。我不需要看到他們的傷痛，現在不要，或許以後也不要。晚餐後我跟納森坐在門廊上，他拿了一瓶啤酒，不解爲什麼我說我不喝了。

en_text: “Listen, Nat, can you watch Sam again tonight? There’s something I have to do.”
zh_text: 「納森，聽我說，你們再照顧小珊一晚好嗎？我要去辦點事情。」

en_text: He takes a long swallow of beer before answering. “You know, Eddie, I’m not kidding when I say you look like hell.”
zh_text: 他喝了很大一口啤酒，然後才答話。「艾迪，你知道嗎？我說你看起來跟死人一樣，我可不是開玩笑。」

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “The only thing you ought to be doing right now is taking care of what family you have left.”
zh_text: 「你現在只有一件事要做，就是好好照顧你僅存的家人。」「我就是要把她照顧好。」

en_text: “That is what I’m doing.”
zh_text: 「嗯，嗯，那你到底要怎麼做？」

en_text: “Uh-huh. And how exactly are you doing that?” “Can you take care of Sam or not?”
zh_text: 「你們能不能讓小珊再留一晚？」

en_text: “Of course we can, Eddie, you know that. I’m just worried you’re thinking of doing something stupid.” “Like what?”
zh_text: 「當然可以，艾迪，你知道當然可以。我只是很擔心你想要做傻事。」「什麼傻事？」

en_text: “I don’t know. Something. Stupid.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。反正一定是傻事。」

en_text: “I’m only helping the police with a few things.”
zh_text: 「我只是想幫警方一點忙。」

en_text: “You’ve got a daughter who needs you. I’m not telling you to let go of what happened, but you have to let the police do their job. A man needs to know what his priorities are.”
zh_text: 「你還有女兒要照顧。我不是要你放下一切往前看，但你要讓警方好好辦案。男人，要知道该把心思放在哪裡。」

en_text: “I know. You’re right. It’s only for tonight,” I say, “I promise.”
zh_text: 「我知道，你說得沒錯。就今天一個晚上，」我說，「就一個晚上。」

en_text: “Okay, Edward. And don’t worry, I won’t hold you to your promise,” he says, and finishes off his beer.
zh_text: 「OK，艾德華。別擔心，你不一定要遵守諾言。」他一口氣把啤酒喝完了。

en_text: I sit in my living room with the curtains closed and the stereo off and the TV off and the phones off. I’m sick of the world. Sick of my phone—sick of messages left by reporters and the psychiatrist I used to see years ago and by people wanting to check up on me. I stare at the TV as if it were on. In the beginning I can see my reflection, but the later the day becomes the harder it gets to see. I have nothing to do but wait for it to become dark. I stare at the Christmas tree and once again I think about taking it down, but once again I decide to leave it up for Sam. The sun comes in through one of the living room windows, it climbs up the walls as it sinks toward the horizon, reflecting off the shiny balls and bells on the tree. It moves over a photo of Sam, over a wedding photo of me and Jodie, it reflects across the room, orange light, weakening, and then it’s gone.
zh_text: 我坐在客廳裡，拉起窗簾，音響關掉，電視關掉，電話也關掉。這個世界令我作嘔。我討厭我的答錄機，記者留了訊息，多年前看過的心理醫生留了訊息，想知道我好不好的人也留了訊息。電視沒開，我依然瞪著空白的畫面。一開始還看到自己的倒影，但隨著時間過去，就看不見了。我無事可做，只能等待黑夜來臨。我瞪著耶誕樹，又開始思索要不要把樹收起來，最後決定爲了小珊還是留著。陽光從客廳的一扇窗戶射進來，太陽朝著地平線下沉時，牆上的光線愈爬愈高，把樹上閃亮的圓球和鈴鐺照得更加亮晶晶。陽光移過小珊的照片，再移過我跟茱蒂的結婚照，橘色的光線橫過了整個客廳，愈來愈弱，然後消失了。

en_text: I keep waiting.
zh_text: 我繼續等。

en_text: Darkness settles in. An hour goes by. I switch on the TV and there’s a New Zealand–made show about psychics on. They’re trying to solve the crimes the police haven’t been able to. A short time ago this kind of thing disgusted me. People were making money off the misery of victims—from the psychics themselves to anybody who had anything to do with the shooting of the show. Women were raped and murdered only to have their story re-enacted and retold by psychics trying to make a quick buck, and the TV-viewing public loved it—or at least enough of them did to keep making the show. But now I think of it differently. If the police can’t do their job, maybe the psychics can. Before I can change channels, the front of the bank appears, then two side-by-side photos, one of my wife, one of the bank manager. Jonas Jones, the main psychic on the show, sits down at an office table that may or may not be inside the bank, closes his eyes, and, surrounded by burning candles, tells the public that the stolen money is still in Christchurch, hidden, somewhere near water, which is a great feat considering Christchurch is on the edge of an ocean. No wonder psychics aren’t winning the lottery every week.
zh_text: 黑暗來臨。一個小時過去了。我打開電視，正在播映紐西蘭製作的節目，討論靈媒。他們想解決警方無能爲力的案件。不久以前，我最討厭這種主題了。這些人的收入來自受害者的不幸遭遇包括那些靈媒跟所有參與節目製作的人。被姦殺的女性又得讓想輕鬆賺錢的靈媒把她們的故事重述一遍，觀衆可愛看了至少愛看的人也多到能讓節目回本。但現在我的看法改變了。如果警察無法破案，或許可以靠靈媒。正想換台，銀行出現在螢幕上，然後是兩張並列的照片，一張上面是我妻子，另一張則是銀行經理。固定上這節目的靈媒強納斯·瓊斯坐在不知道是否在銀行內的辦公桌後，周圍放滿了點燃的蠟燭，他閉上眼睛，告訴觀衆贓款仍在基督城裡，被藏起來了，藏在水邊，哼哼，夠厲害，基督城不就在海邊嗎？難怪靈媒贏不了每個星期都開奬的樂透。

en_text: Midnight comes and goes.
zh_text: 午夜来了，又走了。

en_text: I get changed at one o’clock. The shirt has dried out from last night and is stiff and scratches at me and smells the same as it did this morning. I drive through the early-Thursday-morning streets, most of them deserted until I get toward town, where there are sparks of life from the drunk and disorderly. In suburbia Christmas lights flash at me from windows and roofs and trees, the dark air illuminated by the reds and yellows as well as the pale light from the moon. If Jodie were alive it would all look fantastic. Instead it’s gaudy and cheap, the decorations coming from sweatshop factories in third-world countries. It makes the people in these houses seem desperate to cling to happiness.
zh_text: 凌晨一點鐘，我換了衣服。前一晚弄濕的襯衫乾透了，變得硬梆梆，刮擦著我的身體，味道聞起來跟早上一樣。我開車穿過星期四凌晨的街道，街上幾乎空無一人，到了靠近市區的地方，醉鬼跟鬧事的人才帶來了一些生氣。進入郊區，窗戶、屋頂和樹上的耶誕燈節閃閃爍爍，夜晚的空氣中有紅光黃光，还有蒼白的月光。如果茱蒂還在世，這景色會讓我覺得很美。但她走了，來自第三世界國家血汗工廠的裝飾品看起來既俗氣又廉價。住在這些房子裡的人似乎想靠著耶誕裝飾抓住一點點幸福。

en_text: If map reading was one of Darwin’s tests for survival of the fittest, I’d have been screwed long ago. It takes me a while, but I manage to find the address. Draw a straight line on a map and plot the neighborhoods on it, and they go steadily downhill, nice homes near town, okay homes further away, homes that can only be improved with the introduction of a Molotov cocktail further out again. This is where the map takes me, into a neighborhood you’d normally see on the news where the insurgents are fighting off an invading army. I keep a steady pace, not wanting to risk slowing down. I pass beaten-up cars, old washing machines parked on the sidewalk, random pieces of timber, split-open rubbish bags with waste spilling out. The street I want isn’t any better. Every yard is covered in brown grass and dog crap. Half of the streetlights don’t work. Only a few of the homes have fences, and those that do have about a quarter of a fence at most, every third or fourth paling stolen or used as firewood. A few years ago a neighborhood like this wouldn’t have existed. There were bad areas but not to this extent. Study the line I plotted on the map, and you’d see this neighborhood is spreading, it’s like a virus, touching other suburbs, infecting them, finally consuming them before moving further on. Gerald Painter’s wife is right to move her family away. They live maybe five kilometers from here in a nice street with nice cars and nice trees, but it’s only a matter of time before the virus parks up outside their house and moves in.
zh_text: 如果達爾文適者生存的條件也包含看地圖，那我早該滅絕了。看了半天才找到正確的地址。在地圖上畫一條直線，把鄰近的地區標在上面，感覺愈來愈差，靠近市區的房子很不錯，再走遠些就還好，更遠一點的房子乾脆丢個可以攻擊戰車的莫洛托夫汽油瓶毀掉算了。跟著地圖走，就到了一般會在新聞上看到反動分子在這裡擊退入侵軍隊的區域。我保持平穩的車速，不想冒險放慢速度。我看到破爛的车子、人行道上丢了老舊的洗衣機、這裡一塊那裡一塊的木頭、撕開的垃圾袋，裡面的東西散得到處都是。我要去的那條街也沒好到哪裡去。到處都是褐黃的草地和狗屎。一半的街燈不亮。只有幾戶人家有圍籬，但他們的圍籠只剩下了四分之一，其餘的被偷走了，或拿去當柴燒了。幾年前這樣的區域還不存在。有些鄰里比較差，也沒差到這種程度。看了看我畫在地圖上的那條線，這個區域看來還擴大了，跟病毒一樣，接觸到別的郊區，傳染毒素，最後吃下來，再往其他地方擴張。傑拉德·潘特的妻子做了正確的决定，要搬到別的地方去。他們離這裡大概五公里吧，那條街不錯，大家都開好車，還種了漂亮的樹木，但再過不久，病毒就會蔓延到他們家。

en_text: I drive past the house I want, my heart racing, my palms sweaty, but all I’ve come to do is see the house, maybe catch a glimpse of Shane Kingsly, then drive home and . . .
zh_text: 我開過了我要去的那個地址，我的心跳加速，手心冒汗，但我只爲了過來看看他家長什麼樣，或许會瞥見夏恩·金斯理一眼，然後我就回家：

en_text: Well, drive home and do something. I don’t know what. Maybe phone the police. Maybe go to bed. Maybe write his name down next to Dean Wellington and the life insurance guy.
zh_text: 嗯，回家要幹什麼，我不知道。或許打電話給警察。或許睡覺。或許把他的名字寫在狄恩。威靈頓和那個人壽保險公司的傢伙旁邊。

en_text: Then why is Sam’s bag still in the backseat?
zh_text: 那麼，爲什麼小珊的書包還在後座？

en_text: “I forgot to take it out,” I say. The killing kit is still stuffed inside.
zh_text: 「我忘記拿回家了。」殺人工具仍塞在裡面。

en_text: Then why’d you get changed?
zh_text: 那麼，爲什麼你換了衣服？

en_text: “How about shutting up?”
zh_text: 「閉上嘴，可以嗎？」

en_text: I park a few houses down under a busted light, this time on the opposite side of the road, this time with the house ahead of me so I can keep watch. That’s the plan. Sit for a while. Watch for a while. Then leave.
zh_text: 我停在隔了幾戶、街燈已經被打爛的地方，這次我停在街對面，這次房子在我前面，我可以仔細觀察。計畫就是這樣，在這裡坐一會兒，看一會兒，然後回家。

en_text: Yeah right.
zh_text: 是啊，對呀。

en_text: Immediately I realize the problem. This isn’t the kind of place I can sit for a while. I stand out here. Soon one of the neighbors will come to mug me, or kill me. I’ve seen all that I can safely see, and now it’s time to leave.
zh_text: 我馬上發現問題在哪裡。這裡不適合坐一會兒。我太顯眼了。很快，住在這區的人就會過來搶我的錢，或把我殺了。我已經看到在安全範圍內能看到的東西，該走了。

en_text: Like hell it is. Let me help you.
zh_text: 真他媽的該走啦？讓我幫你。

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「不要。」

en_text: Fine. Have it your way. Let the men who did this to Jodie go free. Go back to your life and move on. It’s not long until you hear that from everybody you know. Move on.
zh_text: 好。你自己想辦法。讓害死茱蒂的人逍遥法外。你好好活下去。不久之後你認識的所有人都會告诉你，好好活下去。

en_text: “What do you need me to do?” I ask.
zh_text: 「你要我怎麼辦？」我問。

en_text: We climb out of the car. I turn a three-sixty looking for somebody, anybody, but there is nobody. I grab Sam’s bag and carry it tightly.
zh_text: 我們下了車。我轉了一圈看看有沒有人，一個人也沒有。我拉出小珊的書包，緊緊抓在手裡。

en_text: We move onto the edge of the property. The dry grass crunches underfoot. I hunker down and pull on the hat and the gardening gloves and take a knife out, then move closer to the house. There are no lights on inside. None of the houses in the street have any Christmas lights. Santa doesn’t even know this place exists. Kingsly’s house is government subsidized, maybe sixty years old, made from wood siding that hasn’t seen fresh paint in all that time. The guttering is covered in dark mould and sags in places where it’s all cracked and busted. There are clumps of grass growing out of it. There is a run-down car parked up the driveway, another one on the lawn, and if you combined all the bits that worked you’d have a car that probably wouldn’t get you anywhere. I slowly approach the house and try to peer in through the windows. I can’t see a damn thing.
zh_text: 我們移動到金斯理家外面。乾燥的草地在腳下發出嘎吱聲。我蹲下，戴上帽子跟園藝手套，拿了一把刀，慢慢靠近房子。裡面沒有燈光。這條街上的房子都沒有耶誕燈飾。耶誕老人甚至遺忘了這個地方。金斯理的家是棟尖頂小房子，可能有六十年了，擋雨板從未重新粉刷過。屋頂的排水管蓋滿了黑色黴菌，有些地方斷開了往下垂。車道上停了一台破車，草坪上還有另一台，把兩台車上可用的零件組合在一起，或許能組成一台跑不動的车子。我慢慢靠近房子，想偷看窗戶裡有什麼動靜。什麼鬼都看不到。

en_text: I head easily around the side of the house, walking slowly, careful in case there are dogs here, but so far nothing has barked at me. I thought a neighborhood like this would have a thousand dogs. Maybe the virus got them.
zh_text: 我往房子旁邊走去，輕而易舉，我腳步很慢，小心翼翼，怕他養了狗，不過到目前爲止都還沒聽到吠叫聲。我本來以爲這種區域肯定有上千條狗，或许早被病毒弄死了。

en_text: I look through the back windows and get the same result. The back door is locked. I don’t know how to get inside. I guess knocking on the door is the way to go.
zh_text: 從後面的窗戶往屋裡看，仍舊什麼也看不見。後門鎖住了，我不知道怎麼進屋裡去。我猜我應該敲門吧。

en_text: No it’s not. We don’t know how many people are inside. We don’t know who will answer. It’s easier than that. Just follow my lead.
zh_text: 不，不要敲門。我們不知道裡面有幾個人。我們不知道誰會來應門。我有更簡單的方法。聽我的就對了。

en_text: There aren’t many places in the backyard to hide, but I find a gap in a mangle of hedge that’s overgrown in the corner. We move toward it, searching the ground for something to throw. I take aim and fire a stone hard up onto the roof. It thumps heavily, and I duck in behind the hedge, the branches scratching at me and snagging my clothes. I stay absolutely still. Nothing happens. I throw a second stone twenty seconds later.
zh_text: 後院能藏身的地方不多，但我在角落胡亂叢生的樹籬裡找到了一個縫隙。我們朝著樹叢前進，在地上摸索可以投擲的東西。瞄準了，我把一塊石頭用力丢到屋頂上。石頭重重敲響了屋頂，我往樹叢後一縮，樹枝刮傷了我，勾住了我的衣服。我動也不敢動，屋裡仍沒有回應。過了二十秒，我又投了一塊石頭。

en_text: A light comes on inside the house. Just one light in a bedroom. Could mean the other bedrooms are empty. Could mean the others are better sleepers. A few moments later I can hear the front door open. Twenty seconds after that it closes, and not long after that the back door opens. A man, silhouetted by the hallway light, steps into the backyard. He’s wearing pajama bottoms and nothing on top. Tattoos that probably have violent stories behind them climb up his body from under the waistband. He’s skinny and tall and looks like he’s spent too many years in jail and the rest of them on drugs. He takes a customary glance over the backyard, shrugs for his own benefit, then goes back inside. I wait until the lights go off, then I wait another few minutes, then I throw a third stone, same speed, same place, same kind of sound.
zh_text: 房子裡的燈亮了。臥房裡的一盞燈。難道其他房間都是空的？難道其他人睡得比較沉？過了一會兒，我聽到前門打開了。二十秒後又關起來了，不久之後後門打開了。一個男人走到後院，走廊上的燈光照出了他的輪廓。他穿著睡褲，赤裸著上半身。刺青從腰下爬遍他的身體，或許隱含著暴力的故事。他身形瘦長，看起來在牢裡待了很多年，出獄後就一直嗑藥。他的目光合情合理地對著後院繞了一圈，聳聳肩向自己表示沒事，然後又進到屋裡去。等到燈光熄滅，我又等了幾分鐘，然後丢了第三塊石頭，同樣的速度，同樣的目標，同樣的響聲。

en_text: The light comes on much quicker this time. Still just the one light. Front door. Nothing. Then back door. He walks out into the yard.
zh_text: 這次燈亮的速度變快了。也只有那盞燈。前門。沒事。後門。他走進院子。

en_text: “Fuck is out there?” he asks, and he probably asked the same thing out the front and got the same answer, but he’s probably thinking he’s talking to a cat or a possum.
zh_text: 「他媽的誰在外面？」他問，或許他在前門也問了同樣的問題，得到同樣的答案，但或許他以爲他在跟貓咪或負鼠對話。

en_text: We don’t answer him. He doesn’t walk far, stays near the door, wondering if the sound was an animal, or a pinecone falling from somewhere. Only difference between this time and the last time is this time he’s carrying a flashlight. He’s not using it as a flashlight, though, he’s using it as a weapon. It’s not even switched on. It’s black and steel and about the length of his forearm and I figure if he had a better weapon he would have brought it out here. Nobody brings a flashlight to a gunfight. He heads back inside. The light goes off. Silence.
zh_text: 我們不回答。他沒走幾步，就站在門外，思索那聲音是不是動物弄出來的，还是不知從何而來的松果。跟幾分鐘前有個不一樣的地方，他拿了手電筒出來。不過，他並沒有拿來照亮院子，而是當作武器。連開關也沒開的手電筒是黑色的，搭配不鏽鋼材質，跟他的前臂一樣長，我想他應該匆促之間沒找到更好的工具。沒有人會帶手電筒去槍戰。他走回房子裡。燈關了。恢復寧靜。

en_text: We give it ten minutes this time. Long enough for him to think the sound isn’t coming back. Long enough that he might be falling asleep again.
zh_text: 這次我們等了十分鐘。夠久了，他會以爲那響聲不會再出現。也夠他重新入睡。

en_text: This time the lights don’t come on. The front door doesn’t open. Only the back door, and it’s fired open quickly and he storms outside, the meat of the flashlight slapping into the palm of his hand. He’s dressed this time, black jeans, black top, black everything.
zh_text: 這次燈沒開。前門沒開。只開了後門，而且後門嗖一下就開了，他猛衝出來，手電筒繫繫抓在手裡。這次他穿好了衣服，黑牛仔褲，黑上衣，一身黑。

en_text: “Who’s out there?” he yells. “That you, Reece? This ain’t funny.”
zh_text: 「誰在那裡？」他大吼。「雷斯，是你嗎？別再給我搞鬼了。」

en_text: He moves deeper into the yard. He switches on the flashlight and spotlights random areas. He passes it over the hedge but he doesn’t squat down or move branches aside or come any closer. He doesn’t circle behind it. He thinks whatever is being thrown on his roof is either some random event or it’s being thrown from outside his yard. He walks one way, then the other way, and he comes back to the doorway and he stares out toward us awhile without seeing us, then he closes the door. His bedroom light turns on and off, but he’s not in there, he’s waiting inside the doorway, waiting for the next sound, ready to burst out at a second’s notice.
zh_text: 他又在後院裡走了幾步，打開手電筒的開關，隨處亂照。光線掃過樹叢，但他沒蹲下來或移開樹枝或更靠近我們。他沒有繞到樹叢後面來。他沒想到有人故意往他的屋頂丢東西，也沒想到那人已經跑到他的院子裡了。他朝著這邊走走，又朝著那邊走走，然後回到後門，對著我們瞪了一會兒，卻看不見我們，然後他把門關上了。臥房的燈亮了又暗，但他不在臥房裡，他在門後等著，等下一次發出聲響，準備好不到一秒就可以衝出來。

en_text: I move away from the hedge, slowly, confident slow movement will be less likely to draw his attention in case he’s watching from the window. I put more distance between the house and us, backing into the neighboring property, a similar house in similar disrepair, same warped wood siding, same dirt-packed yard, probably the same kind of person living inside. I keep the hedge between me and Kingsly. I head slowly down the side of the next-door house and make it back out to the road. My car is still where I left it. All the wheels are still on it. I figure it’s like winning the lottery out here. I move to the front of Kingsly’s house and walk up the pathway, staying low, moving slow. I stick the bag on the path halfway between the house and the road. I reach the front door and squat down and take a few moments to calm down, drawing strength from the monster.
zh_text: 我慢慢在樹叢後移動，萬一他在窗口看著，我相信只要夠慢，就不會引起注意。我離房子更遠了，慢慢移近隔壁的房子，跟金斯理家很像，也一樣破爛，擋雨板也變形了，院子裡也只有土，或許住的人也跟金斯理是同樣的類型。我用樹叢擋住金斯理的視線，慢慢移動到鄰家的邊界，然後回到路上。我的車子還在原來的地方，四個輪胎也都在。在這一區能安然無恙，簡直跟赢了樂透一樣。我走到金斯理家前面，蹲低了身子走上人行道，動作緩慢。我把書包放在房子和道路間那條通道的中央。我移到前門，蹲下，先安撫自己的情緒，從怪獸那邊吸取力量。

en_text: I knock. Twice. Two loud, heavy knocks. Footsteps pound down the hallway. I run, staying low, back to the side of the house before he gets the door open. I can hear him saying something but I’m not sure what, something that sounds like “what the fuck.” I reach the back of the house and put my hand on the door handle and trust in Kingsly’s desperation to get outside as fast as he could. Sure enough, the handle turns and the door opens. I can’t see a thing inside. The hallway has a bend in it, so I can’t see Kingsly either. He’s outside. I can hear him walking around out there, asking who’s out there, when he should be asking an entirely different question. He should be asking who’s in here. I close the door. I head into the bedroom where the light was turning on and off before, using my hands to lead the way, almost tripping on rope lining the floor. Kingsly stays outside for another minute before returning to the hallway. The front door closes.
zh_text: 我敲了兩下門。很大聲，很沉重。重重的腳步聲從走廊另一頭傳來。我蹲低了身子跑走，在他開門前就跑到房子旁邊。我聽到他說話，但聽不清楚，很像是「媽的在搞什麼鬼」。我跑到房子後面，把手放在門把上，我相信金斯理爲了盡快跑到前門，一定來不及鎖後門。果然，門把轉動，門開了。我看不到裡面的情況。走廊轉了一個彎，所以我看不到金斯理。他在外面。我可以聽見他在外面走來走去，怒問是誰敲門，但他錯了，應該問一個完全不一樣的問題。他應該問誰在裡面。我關上門，用手在黑暗中摸索，走到之前看到燈亮燈滅的臥房，差點被地上鋪的繩子絆倒。又過了一分鐘，金斯理才進來。前門關上了。

en_text: We wait in the dark for him to come into the bedroom.
zh_text: 我們在黑暗中等他回臥房來。

en_text: Kingsly heads out to the backyard. He moves around out there for a minute, swearing loudly, unsure of what he’s looking for. He knows he’s not dealing with pinecones anymore. He finally comes back in. He walks up and down the hallway a few times with the lights off. I’m not sure why, but as he does, it comes to me that I’ve already made my first mistake. The knife won’t make him talk. He isn’t going to come in here and see the steak knife in my hand, then start talking.
zh_text: 金斯理走到後院。他在那裡繞了一分鐘，大聲怒罵，不知道自己在找什麼。他知道不光是松果那麼簡單了。最後他終於回到屋子裡。他在走廊上來回走了幾趟，也沒把燈打開。我不懂他爲什麼不開燈，但在他來回踱步時，我突然發覺我已經犯了一個錯。用刀子沒辦法讓他開口。就算他回到臥房，看到我手中的牛排刀，也不會立刻告解。

en_text: I can’t see anything, but I can hear him. All I can see are the numbers from the clock radio and a small glow coming from the power button of a stereo. Kingsly knows the layout of his own house, knows where to walk without banging into anything. He has the flashlight on which helps him, I guess, but helps me too.
zh_text: 我什麼也看不見，但我聽得到。我只能看見收音機時鐘上的數字跟音響電源按鈕的細微光亮。金斯理知道他家裡有什麼擺設，知道怎麼走才不會撞上東西。他有手電筒可以幫忙，但我想他開了手電筒，也等於幫我忙。

en_text: The flashlight beam comes into the room from the hallway, lighting up part of the bed from the angle he’s on. The light grows in size the closer he gets. I squat down and wait for him, the knife out ahead of me. As he comes into the room, he twists the flashlight toward the light switch and reaches for it.
zh_text: 手電筒的光線從走廊照進臥房，從他那個角度照亮了一小半的床。他愈靠近，光線照亮的範圍就愈大。我蹲下來等他，刀子舉在身前。他一進房間，就把手電筒轉向電源開關的方向，伸手過去開燈。

en_text: He switches it on at the exact time I move forward. I can’t kill him. I need him. I need names and addresses and information that he can’t provide if I stick the knife into his throat. So I aim for his shoulder. He hears me coming and turns and lifts his arm. It throws off my aim. The knife bites into his hand and pushes it back to the wall, but the knife goes into the wall too, right through the drywall, the blade burying down to the hilt, extending all the way into the wall and ripping into the wiring behind the light switch.
zh_text: 就在他打開電源的同時，我也向前移動了。我不能殺他。我需要他。我需要姓名住址跟其他資訊，要是我把刀插到他喉嚨裡，就什麼也聽不到。所以我對準了他的肩膀。他聽見我移動的聲音，轉過身來舉起手臂。我沒刺中目標。刀子咬進他的手掌，把他的手推回牆上，但刀子也插入了牆面，刀鋒沒入了石膏板，只留下刀柄露在外面，插過了整堵牆，撕裂了電源開關後的電線。

en_text: Every single muscle in my body tightens, my head crashes up into his chin, my right arm numb and in pain. I can’t let go of the knife. Every muscle in Kingsly goes tight too, his arm with the flashlight swings up randomly, the metal casing hits me hard in the shoulder and pushes me back. My hand comes off the knife and I fall down and quickly back away, hitting the bed and pushing the mattress askew.
zh_text: 我全身的肌肉緊繃，頭一頂用力撞上了他的下巴，右臂麻木疼痛。我沒辦法放開刀子。金斯理全身的肌肉也僵直了，他拿著手電筒的手臂東晃西甩，金屬外殼重重打中了我的肩膀，把我向後撞開。我的手離開了刀子，我往地上一倒，很快地倒在床上，把床墊撞歪了。

en_text: Then nothing.
zh_text: 然後一片死寂。

en_text: Kingsly stands almost still. There are veins standing out in his neck and forehead. He’s still holding the flashlight, his arm straight up in the air like he’s asking a question. He isn’t screaming. Isn’t trying to pull the knife away. I can hear a low hum, and a couple of sparks fly from the wall from behind his hand, but nothing else. No crackle of electricity. Almost perfect silence—except for the low hum.
zh_text: 金斯理直挺挺站著。脖子和額頭上的青筋冒了出來。他仍拿著手電筒，手臂舉在空中，像個要問問題的學生。他沒有尖叫，沒有想辦法把刀子拉開。我聽見細微的嗡嗡聲，然後在他頭後面，有兩星火花從牆上飛出來，就這樣。沒有電氣的爆裂聲。幾乎全然寂靜，除了那細微的嗡嗡聲以外。

en_text: Then I realize he actually is moving. Small, shallow movements, almost every part of him swaying minutely back and forth, convulsing almost, as if he’s having an epileptic fit but doesn’t have the energy to give it his all. He can’t break the contact, all he can do is this death dance as the power flows through him. His feet seem bolted to the floor. The lights in the bedroom fade, then come on real bright, then fade again. One of them blows, the other one brightens, dims, brightens.
zh_text: 然後我發現他其實不是站著不動。他的動作很微弱，不著痕跡，全身上下都在輕輕地來回搖動，幾乎像在抽搐，彷彿他突然癲癇發作，卻沒有力氣完全發出來。他放不開刀子，只能跳著死亡之舞，讓電力穿透全身。他的雙腳好像釘在地上。臥房裡的燈暗下來，然後突然大放光明，接著又暗下來。一盞燈爆掉了，另一盞則一下子亮一下子暗。

en_text: Kingsly’s face is in a tight grimace, his lips are pulled back and his teeth have clenched tight on his protruded tongue. The tip of it, a slug-sized piece, sticks out between them. His body keeps shaking, harder now, spasms rolling up and down his tall frame, blood splashing up onto his nose and face and down his chin. The tip of his tongue comes away, the bloody side of it hits the wall and grips a little, sliding down the wall like a pickle on a window at McDonald’s. It hits the floor. The front of his pants darken. I can smell shit. I can smell barbecue. His eyes bulge from his face. No smoke anywhere.
zh_text: 金斯理扮起了繄繃的鬼臉，他的嘴唇向後翻，牙齒咬緊了伸出來的舌頭。蛞蝓大小的舌尖從兩排牙齒之間突出來。他的身體繼續搖晃，现在搖得更厲害了，高瘦的身軀由上而下不斷痙攣，血噴到他的鼻子和面孔上，向下流到了下巴。他終於咬斷了舌頭，血淋淋的一塊肉飛到牆上，黏住了一秒鐘，又開始往下滑，就像在麥當勞窗口會看到的小黃瓜。那塊舌頭掉到地上。他的褲襠顏色變深了。我聞到屎味。我也聞得到烤肉味。他的眼睛暴突出來。我看不到煙霧。

en_text: A small flame jets out from the wall and equally as fast goes out. The humming comes to a stop. The light goes out. The flashlight hits the ground and stays going. Slowly, Kingsly slides down the wall, following his tongue. He slides as far as his pinned hand will allow, which is enough for his knees to bend and his face to press up against the doorjamb, his upper lip snagging on the latch and stretching out before tearing on the way. His head lolls over his shoulder, his eyes staring at me, no smoke coming from them. Other than the torn lip and bloody stump of a tongue, he’s not in too bad a shape. Of course one look into his now-empty eyes is an immediate giveaway that things aren’t good for the guy.
zh_text: 牆上冒出了一小簇火燄，又以同樣的速度消失了。嗡嗡聲停止了。燈滅了。手電筒掉到地上，繼續往前滾。金斯理跟著他的舌頭，慢慢從牆上往地上滑。最後，被釘住的手掌讓他無法繼續往下滑，但足以讓他雙膝跪地，臉壓在門把上，上唇卡到了門門，然後被拉長扯開。他的頭倒然，如果你看著他現在已經空洞洞的眼睛，立刻就知道他大事不妙了。

en_text: Something in his hand gives. I’m not sure what, exactly, but his hand forks open in a V as his body weight pulls it down past the blade, and then the rest of him slides down the wall and he tips onto the floor, covering the flashlight and blanketing me in darkness.
zh_text: 他手上有什麼東西鬆了。我沒看清楚是什麼，但他的體重把手往下拉，他的手掌通過刀鋒，裂出V字形的開口，然後他的身體繼續靠著牆往下滑，他一頭倒在地上，蓋住了手電筒，我陷入了一片黑暗。

en_text: I can hear my own breathing. Ragged-sounding. Painful-sounding. Panicked.
zh_text: 我聽得到自己的呼吸聲。很粗重。很痛苦。很驚恐。

en_text: I can’t hear Kingsly. Can’t see him. My arm hurts and so does my chest. There’s a sharp pain right down in the base of my throat. My heart is thumping. I count off the seconds. One. Two. My entire body has broken out in a sweat. Three. I push myself further away from him, backing into the corner of the bed. Four. I can’t figure out why the fuses didn’t pop and cut the power. Five.
zh_text: 我聽不見金斯理的聲音，看不到他。我的手臂很痛，胸口也很痛。喉嚨底部劇痛，心跳劇烈。我開始數秒，一、二。我全身冒汗。三。我用力把自己從金斯理身邊推開，向後退到床邊。四。我不知道爲什麼保險絲沒燒掉，把電力切斷。五。

en_text: I take my cell phone out of my pocket and learn another lesson. Bringing a cell phone is a mistake unless it’s turned off. If somebody had called while I was hiding behind the hedge, or in the bedroom, things would have gone very differently. I point the display away from me and it lights up the meter or so ahead. I can’t see much except my own feet and the floor. I get to my knees and move closer to Kingsly. The power is out but I don’t touch him. I kick him to roll him off the flashlight so I can see better.
zh_text: 我從口袋裡取出手機，又學到了一課。除非關掉電源，不然帶手機就犯了大錯。我躲在樹叢裡或臥室裡的時候，要是有人打電話給我，現在的局面可就大大不同了。我把螢幕朝著前面，照亮了一公尺左右的距離。除了我在地上的雙腳，其他什麼也看不到。我跪起來，朝著金斯理移過去。沒電了，但我不會碰到他。我把他從手電筒上踢開，好看得清楚一點。

en_text: I’ve killed a man.
zh_text: 我殺了一個人。

en_text: And you liked it.
zh_text: 你很喜歡吧。

en_text: There’s a long cut in the palm of my right hand; it’s not too deep but it’s very ragged. The knife has ripped right through the glove when I slid forward after stabbing him. It’s also why I got electrocuted. If he hadn’t hit me with the flashlight I could be lying right beside him now. I touch the side of his face and poke him. His head lolls to the side and doesn’t loll back. His face is puffy and his lips pulled back and pieces of flesh from the bloody stump of his tongue are threaded through the small gaps in his teeth. The fuses should have popped. A circuit breaker should have kicked in somehow. The voltage shouldn’t have done this to him.
zh_text: 我右手的手掌上有一條長長的傷口；不深，但歪七扭八的。我刺傷他後往前滑，那時刀子刺破了手套。如果他沒用手電筒打我，現在我就跟他躺在一起了。我碰碰他的臉頰，戳戳他。他的頭滾向一邊，沒滾回來。他的面孔浮腫，嘴唇翻開，齒縫間卡了細碎的舌頭肉。保險絲應該燒壤了，我想是斷路器啓動了。光憑電壓應該不會讓他死成這樣。

en_text: I grab the flashlight. There is blood on the wall, on the floor, all over the knife and his arm, and some of his blood has mixed with the wound in my hand. I scoot myself back against the bed, roll onto my side, gag, open my mouth, and . . .
zh_text: 我拿起手電筒。牆上、地板上、刀子上、他的手臂上都有血，我手上的傷口也混合了他的血。我急急退回床邊，滾倒了身子，張開嘴巴……

en_text: And nothing. Nothing happens. I stop gagging. I can taste vomit but none appears. I move off the floor and onto the bed, trailing blood with me. I put my own hands on the bed, bleeding into it, and I realize there is no way I can ever get away with any of this.
zh_text: 什麼也沒有。什麼也沒出來。我不再作嘔。覺得有東西要吐，但吐不出來。我起身坐到床上，留下了一行血跡。我把我的雙手放在床上，看著血流出來，我發覺，我不可能逃得掉。

en_text: “You did this to me,” I say.
zh_text: 「都是你害的。」我說。

en_text: You? I am you!
zh_text: 你？我跟你早就是一體！

en_text: I keep staring at him, waiting for him to do something. He doesn’t. I wait for somebody to appear. Nobody does. And nobody will.
zh_text: 我繼續瞪著他，等他探取行動。他不動。我等人出現，没有人來。也不會有人來。

en_text: I head into the hallway and find the fuse box almost immediately—the ropes I was stepping on earlier turn out to be power cables coming out of it and snaking across the floor. They’re pinned up to the fuse box with alligator clips. The fuse box is one of those old ones that requires wire to be wound between the terminals, except in this case there is no wire between any of them, instead there are five-centimeter nails, wedged in where the fuses would slot. One of them has melted in the middle. A wire fuse would have broken in a tenth of a second. The nail took thirty seconds. I try the hallway lights and they come on. The only fuse to have blown is the one for the bedroom.
zh_text: 我走到走廊，立刻找到了保險絲盒一剛才我踩到的繩子原來是從盒子裡延伸出來、隨意散落地上的電纜。電纜用鱷魚夾固定在保險絲盒上。保險絲盒很舊了，要把電線纏在電極上，只是這裡的兩個電極沒有電線，只有五公分長的釘子，插在保險絲該插進去的地方。中間有根釘子熔了。用電線當保險絲，十分之一秒就燒掉了，不過釘子要三十秒。我試了走廊的燈，沒問題，只有臥室的保險絲燒掉了。

en_text: I follow the cables along the floor into another bedroom. The door is heavy to open and warm to touch. When it opens a thick piece of foam attached to the base of the door slides across the floor, and immediately orange light comes out, warming my face. The bedroom has been converted into a marijuana greenhouse. There are tables running from one wall to the other, full of beds of plants. There are heat lamps hanging from the ceiling over each of them. The room is more humid than it is bright. All the curtains are drawn, and in front of the curtains are large pieces of plywood, blocking any view from the outside world. I take a step inside; the air gets thicker. There are watering cans, bags of fertilizer, all the little knickknacks that old ladies with green fingers have. All of the plants stand about thirty centimeters high. I wonder how long they take to grow, how much money is invested here. I wonder what will happen to them now Kingsly is dead. I push some of them off the tables, they hit the floor and fall out of their trays, the roots exposed, the dirt exploding outward in every direction. I stomp on them, crushing the spines and leaves, destroying the drugs, hoping that I’m creating a reason for Kingsly to have been killed. The police aren’t going to look beyond a drug connection.
zh_text: 我跟著地上的電線走進另一間臥房。門很重，摸起來很溫暖。打開後，門底釘著的厚厚泡棉條滑過地板，橘色的光線立刻射出來，照在我的臉上。原來這間臥房被改裝成大麻溫室。長長的桌子從這面牆延伸到那面牆，放滿了植栽床。每個植栽床上都有掛在天花板上的加熱燈。這間房不怎麼明亮，非常潮濕。所有的窗簾都拉起來了，窗簾前還放了大片的三夾板，從外面看進來絕對什麼也看不到。我往前走了一步，空氣更加凝重。我看到澆水罐，一包包的肥料，愛好園藝的老太太一定會準備的小玩意應有盡有。所有的植物都大概三十公分高。不知道要花多久時間才能長成，也不知道他們投資了多少錢在這裡。現在金斯理死了，更不知道這些植物會怎麼樣。我把幾棵大麻從桌子上推下去，植物落到地上，跟托盤分離了，根暴露在外，塵土朝著四面八方飛揚。我亂踩一通，踩爛了莖葉，毀掉了大麻，希望這樣能製造出金斯理被殺的理由。警方應該會朝著毒品的方向去追查。

en_text: I step back out of the room and close the door.
zh_text: 我退出房間，把門關上。

en_text: There’s enough hallway light to see into the bedroom, and I use the flashlight for the rest. A brick of money is poking out from beneath the edge of the mattress I knocked out of place when I fell down and pushed myself back earlier. I tip it up the rest of the way. Bricks of cash, fresh, virgin money, all of the bricks made up from hundred dollar notes. Could be between a quarter and half a million dollars here. I reach out to touch it, wanting a tactile experience as to how that money feels, but pull my hand back. This is the reason my wife died. Or at least one-sixth of the reason. In some ways I’m owed this money. But in a much bigger way I can’t even touch it, let alone take it. This is blood money. I drop the mattress back onto it.
zh_text: 我藉著走廊上的燈跟手電筒看第一間臥房裡的情況。我剛才倒下去又爬起來的時候，把床墊一邊撞開了，一疊鈔票露了出來。我把床墊整個翻開。一疊疊鈔票，全新的紙鈔，全都是百元大鈔。這裡應該有二十五到五十萬紐幣吧。我伸手出去碰碰鈔票，想知道紙幣的觸感如何，但又把手縮了回來。這就是害死我妻子的贓款。或至少是其中六分之一。就某個理由來說，這些錢是我手的。但因著更強烈的因素，我連碰都不能碰，更不用說把錢帶走了。這些錢沾滿了鮮血。我把床墊蓋回去。

en_text: A pile of porn magazines are stacked on an old wooden chair by the bed. The clock radio sits on top of them, it’s big and ugly and could be worth a lot of money since it’s probably the first one ever built. The bed is a double with sheets balled up, white and grey and covered in hair, the mattress sagging in the middle. I get the idea that if I pulled the top sheet away and exposed the surface of that mattress, I wouldn’t eat for two weeks. The stereo that added to the glow of the room is brand new, the cardboard box right next to it, big brand letters stamped across it. It’s the only thing in this room built in the last decade.
zh_text: 床邊的老舊木椅上有一堆色情雜誌。收音機時鐘放在上面，又大又醜，或許值很多錢，因爲有可能是收音機時鐘的始祖。床是雙人床，灰白色的床單捲成一團，蓋滿了毛髮，床墊中間都陷下去了。我想，如果我把上面的床單拉開，露出床墊的表面，大概兩個星期都没胃口吃飯了。剛才發出微光的音響是全新的，紙箱就放在旁邊，上面印著大大的品牌名稱。房裡唯一不超過十年的東西應該只有這台音響。

en_text: There’s an old school desk with a shaving mirror on top of it, it has thin sprinkles of white powder and a razor blade on it. A supermarket cart next to the window is full of plastic bags packed with dried-out marijuana. A shelf hammered into the wall on a slight angle has tobacco papers, tobacco, scissors, and tinfoil all looking ready to slide onto the floor. Posters of muscle cars and naked women hang on the walls, along with a mirror with writing stenciled over it, telling me what alcohol Kingsly loves to drink.
zh_text: 臥房裡有張很舊的書桌，上面放了刮鬍子用的鏡子，桌上薄薄浮了一層白粉，还有一支刮鬍刀。窗邊停著超市的推車，放滿了塑膠袋，裡面裝著乾掉的大麻。釘在牆上的架子有點歪，上面放的捲菸紙、菸草、剪刀和錫箔紙似乎都準備要滑到地面上了。牆上掛了大馬力跑車和裸女的海報，一面鏡子上面用蠟筆寫了字，告訴我金斯理最愛喝什麼酒。

en_text: Tying it all together is a dead man on the floor with his eyes wide open and his teeth clenched tightly on a bloody stump of tongue. The carpet is threadbare and has what might be grease stains on it, as if somebody rolled a hundred-piece KFC meal back and forth picking up the dust instead of a vacuum cleaner.
zh_text: 這一切配上地上那死人再完美也不過了，他眼睛瞪得老大，牙齒緊緊咬著鮮血淋漓的斷舌頭。地毯很破爛，似乎沾滿了油漬，彷彿有人用上百塊肯德基的炸雞取代吸塵器，來回滾來滾去，沾起上面的灰塵。

en_text: I find the bathroom and take off the ruined glove and run my hand under the tap and try to wash my blood away and Kingsly’s blood away but more blood keeps appearing. I pull the glove back on and wrap a pillowcase from the bedroom around it, knowing the infection from this house, this neighborhood, is inside me now.
zh_text: 我找到浴室，翻開撕破的手套，開了水龍頭洗手，想洗掉我的血和金斯理的血，但愈洗血愈多。我拉上手套，從臥房拿了一個枕頭套包住我的手，這棟房子和這個區域的細菌現在已經跑到我身體裡面了。

en_text: In the kitchen I go through the cupboards, finding bleach in the laundry. I twist off the top and head through the house, splashing bleach over all the places where I’ve dripped blood, ruining the DNA—at least that’s what I hope is happening. It smells awful, a sharp acrid smell that burns my nostrils. I tug the knife out of the wall. It no longer has a serrated edge near the top, the metal has blackened and melted there. A gargling air bubble appears on Kingsly’s lips. I watch it, waiting for it to pop, but it doesn’t, it slowly deflates, as if he’s sucking the air back in. I pour bleach over the knife and carry it into the kitchen, then wrap it in a dish towel. My daughter’s bag is by the front door. It’s been turned upside down and the contents spilled out. Did Kingsly know he was looking at a killing kit?
zh_text: 我翻遍廚房的櫃子，最後在洗衣間裡找到了漂白水。我轉開瓶蓋，在房子裡四處走動，把滴到我血跡的地方都灑了漂白水，毀掉DNA證據丨起碼我希望能把證據毀掉。聞起來很可怕，濃烈刺激的味道刺痛了我的鼻孔。我把牆壁上的刀子拔出來，靠近頂端的地方已經沒有鋸齒了，金屬變成黑色，熔在牆裡。金斯理的嘴唇上出現了一個氣泡。我盯著泡泡看，等它爆開，但泡泡沒有爆，慢慢消回去了，彷彿他把氣吸回肚子裡。我把漂白水倒在刀子上，然後拿回廚房裡，用抹布包起來。小珊的書包放在前門，已經翻倒了，裡面的東西散落在地上。金斯理知不知道他看到了一包殺人工具？

en_text: The smell of bleach makes me nauseous and I breathe into the crook of my elbow to try and cope. I make a more detailed search of the house, hunting for anything that might give me the other names but come up short. Jesus, I don’t even know if Kingsly was involved. He may have been. I spend little time questioning how bad I feel about the accident, because that’s what it was—him getting killed—it was an accident. I decide that I’m still undecided. That is until I think about his past, the drug convictions, the armed robberies, and the more I think about them the less I care about what happened.
zh_text: 漂白水的味道讓我想吐，我把鼻子塞到彎起的手肘裡，希望能覺得好受點。我更仔細地搜了一次房子，想找出其他搶匪的名字，但一無所獲。我甚至不知道金斯理是不是搶匪。或许是吧。我問自己，這次意外對我有什麼影響，因爲就是這樣，他被殺了，是一場意外。我決定我還不知道有什麼影響。等我想到他的過去、持有毒品而被判刑、持械搶劫，愈想，我愈不在意剛才發生的事。

en_text: They all going to be accidents?
zh_text: 全都是意外嗎？

en_text: Maybe. I don’t know.
zh_text: 或许吧。我不知道。

en_text: There is no computer. No address book. I go through every scrap of paper I can find, sure there has to be more names here, and the longer I can’t find anything, the more despondent I become. And angry. This was my link to these men. And I’ve killed it. I also don’t find a balaclava, but if he was one of the six men in the bank, he would have thrown it away by now.
zh_text: 沒有電腦。沒有通訊錄。所有的紙張我都看過了，一定哪裡寫了其他的名字，但我什麼也沒找到，也覺得愈來愈沮喪。還有憤怒。就這麼一個可以找到搶匪的線索。我破壞了唯一的機會。我也找不到搶匪戴的帽子，但如果他是銀行裡六個搶匪的其中一個，應該早把帽子丢掉了。

en_text: You’re new at this, but you’re doing great. Think. Think. How would these men communicate with him?
zh_text: 你是新手，但你做得很好。想想看。这些人會用什麼方法找他？

en_text: “A cell phone,” I say.
zh_text: 「手機。」

en_text: Taking care not to step in the blood, I crouch over Kingsly and pat down the sides of his jeans. There’s a lump in his right pocket. I reach inside and find a cell phone and a set of car keys. I splash more bleach over him before heading out the back door, wiping down the handles on the way, my daughter’s bag slung over my shoulder.
zh_text: 我小心翼翼地避開血跡，彎身去拍了拍金斯理的兩條腿。右邊的口袋有個東西鼓起來。我伸手到裡面取出他的手機和一串車鑰匙。我在他身上灑了更多漂白水，然後才揹著小珊的書包從後門離開，一路上碰過的門把都擦乾淨了。

en_text: I check Kingsly’s car. It’s an old Holden that’s almost twice as big as any modern sedan. I’m careful not to get blood or fingerprints over the door. There’s a metal strip on the passenger seat, about the same size as a crowbar, but much thinner. It’s one of those tools a thief uses to pop the lock in a car. I go through the glove box but it’s as useful as going through the house. I check the trunk: there are some tools in there but nothing else. I get back to my car and I’m all full of surprises—surprised my car is still there, surprised that it’s almost four a.m., surprised that the monster inside me for the moment hasn’t anything else to say. I swing by the cemetery on the way home and have the same amount of luck finding my wife’s grave as I did the night before.
zh_text: 我看了看金斯理的車子。很舊的澳洲產Holden，是現代轎車的兩倍大。我很謹愼，不在車門上留下血跡或指紋。副駕駛座上有一片金屬，差不多是扳手的大小，但細多了。偷車賊會用這種金屬片來撬開車鎖。我搜過了前座的置物盒，跟在屋子裡一樣找不到線索。行李廂我也看過了：有些工具在裡面，沒有其他東西。我回到自己的車子裡，覺得驚奇連連丨很驚訝我的車子還在，驚訝幾乎要凌晨四點了，更驚訝的是我體內的怪獸現在沒什麼可說了。在回家的路上，我到墓地晃了一下，跟前一晚一樣，還是找不到我妻子的墳墓。

en_text: It’s their first serious lead.
zh_text: 終於出現了重大的線索。

en_text: Fifteen one-hundred-dollar notes are hanging from a line strung across the back of the laundry. A tray of water and bleach next to them. Most of the notes are stained in red ink, the bleach doing nothing to clean them up, but a few are okay, the serial numbers matching the notes taken from the bank. Others are damaged from the small explosion, perhaps too badly in some cases. These are from the blocks of cash that had the ink packs inserted next to them.
zh_text: 橫過洗衣間後方的細繩上晾了十五張百元大鈔。旁邊的托盤上放了清水跟漂白水。鈔票幾乎都沾了紅墨水，用漂白水也無法清理，但有幾張還好，上面的序號符合從銀行被搶走的鈔票。其他的則在染色包爆破後毀了，有幾張特別慘重。這些鈔票原本跟染色包放在同一疊。

en_text: Shane Kingsly has a rap sheet going back almost twenty years. It began with shoplifting and ended with armed robbery, the years in between littered with burglary charges. In fact the few times Kingsly hasn’t been in trouble were the times he’s spent in jail.
zh_text: 夏恩·金斯理前科累累，犯罪紀錄幾乎將滿二十年。從順手牽羊開始，進步到武裝搶劫，中間則有不少次破門盗竊的紀錄。事實上，如果金斯理有一段時間沒惹上麻煩，他應該正好在監獄裡。

en_text: Schroder already knows none of the neighbors have seen anything. He already knew before any of them were questioned. This isn’t what he’d call a police-friendly neighborhood. Nobody here is opening their doors and offering information and coffee and kind helpful words.
zh_text: 施羅德早就知道鄰居一定什麼都沒看到。早在警方訊問前他就想到結果了。這條街絕非他口中會友善對待警察的區域。沒有一家人敵開大門提供消息，還幫他們泡咖啡，說些和善鼓勵的話。

en_text: The house is a death trap, and according to the ME, Kingsly would have survived the attack if not for the overload of electricity. Schroder imagines living in a place like this but doesn’t imagine it for too long—the mere thought of it is enough to make him want to go and take a bath. Cables are running from the fuse box to the marijuana room where they were powering heat and light. The house smells of dirt and in one room the air is so dry he’s worried it’s going to ignite. In another room it’s cold and damp even though it’s over thirty degrees outside. Nearly every wall in the house has mold growing on it, and every light fitting is covered in cobwebs.
zh_text: 金斯理的家非常危險，根據法醫的說法，如果電力沒有超載，他應該能逃過攻擊。施羅德想像了一下住在這種地方是什麼感覺，也只想了一下而已光想像就夠了，他迫不及待想去洗個澡。電纜從保險絲盒連到種大麻的房間，提供熱力和光源。房子裡有股土味，有個房間裡的空氣乾燥到讓他擔心要起火了。另一間房則又冷又濕，但外面卻已經超過三十度。房子裡幾乎所有的牆面都長黴了，每盞燈上都蓋著蜘蛛網。

en_text: “What do you think?” Landry asks. “A drug thing?”
zh_text: 「你覺得怎麼樣？」藍德里問，「跟毒品有關嗎？」

en_text: Landry looks tired, with dark bags beneath his eyes. He looks in need of this Christmas break more than anybody.
zh_text: 藍德里神色疲倦，臉上掛著大大的黑眼圈。他看起來比任何人都需要耶誕假期

en_text: “Unlikely. They’d have taken the drugs. If Kingsly was part of the robbery, then whoever killed him took his share of the cash, assuming it was here to begin with. So either it’s one of his own crew, or somebody else.”
zh_text: 「不太可能。他們應該會把毒品帶走。如果金斯理涉嫌搶案，殺死他的人會把他分到的贓款拿走，而且一開始就想到錢在這裡。所以不是他的同黨，就是另有其人。」

en_text: “You think Hunter?”
zh_text: 「你覺得是杭特嗎？」

en_text: “I don’t want it to be him, but there’s something else.” He leads Landry down the hall to the back door. Outside, next to the step, is a solid-aluminium box with walls an inch thick, big enough to fit a soccer ball.
zh_text: 「我希望不是，但還有一個東西。」他頜著藍德里穿過走廊走到後門。門外的台階旁邊有個堅固的鋁盒，盒壁有兩三公分厚，裡面裝得下一個足球。

en_text: “What is it?” Landry asks. “Some kind of safe?”
zh_text: 「這是什麼？」藍德里問，「保險箱嗎？」

en_text: “There’s no lock on it. Doesn’t even have a door. Just a lid. Open it up.” Landry lifts the top. “Jesus, is that blood?” he asks.
zh_text: 「沒有鎖。甚至沒有門，只有一個蓋子。打開來看看。」藍德里掀開蓋子。「天啊，是血嗎？」他問。

en_text: “Dye.”
zh_text: 「染料。」

en_text: “Dye? From the exploding dye pack?” “Yep.”
zh_text: 「染料？自動爆破染色包裡的？」「答對了。」

en_text: “So the bank robbers isolated the bundles with the dye packs to protect the rest of the cash,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「所以搶匪把放了染色包的鈔票隔開，來保護其餘的現鈔。」藍德里說。

en_text: “They came prepared. They must have had the box inside the van, and they knew they had only a couple of minutes to transfer the dangerous cash into it.”
zh_text: 「他們有備而來。他們一定把盒子放在貨車裡，也知道只有一兩分鐘的時間能把夾了染色包的鈔票放進盒子。」

en_text: “They really knew their stuff,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「真的是内行人。」藍德里說。

en_text: “Only it doesn’t make sense,” Schroder says. “Why not throw the cash out the window? Why go to the effort to keep it, and even then, why not leave the metal box with the van? Why bring it here?”
zh_text: 「但是沒道理呀，」施羅德說，「爲什麼不把錢從窗戶裡扔出去？爲什麼辛辛苦苦要留著這些錢？還有，爲什麼不把金屬盒留在貨車裡一起燒了？爲什麼要帶過來？」

en_text: “Maybe they’re planning on using it again?”
zh_text: 「或許，他們計畫要再用一次？」

en_text: “Maybe, but I don’t think that’s it,” Schroder answers. “There were hundreds of bricks of cash thrown into those bags, how do you think they knew which ones had the dye unit in it?”
zh_text: 「或许，但我不認爲。」施羅德回答。「他們丢了上百疊鈔票到袋子裡，你以爲他們怎麼知道哪些夾了染色包？」

en_text:
“Maybe they used some kind of metal detector?” “Yeah, and if they did, why hide it?”
“I’m not following . . .”
“I think they had inside help.” “What?”
zh_text:
「或許他們用了金屬偵測器？」
「是呀，如果用了，幹嘛要藏起來？」
「我聽不懂···」
「我覺得他們有内應。」
「什麼？」

en_text: “Think about it. When the four people went back to the vault, they all knew the dye packs had to be inserted. If somebody forgot, they’d look suspicious. But what if somebody loaded them into a specific place? Laid them on top, maybe marked them somehow? The bank crew get the bags back into the car and take out the marked notes and contain them immediately in the metal box. They can’t throw them out the window because then we’d wonder how they found the dye packs among all that other cash. They couldn’t leave the box with the van because we’d think the same thing.”
zh_text: 「你想。那四個人去金庫的時候，他們都知道必須要塞染色包。要是忘了，就很可疑。但如果有人把染色包放在特定的地方呢？比方說放在最上面，或者做個記號？搶匪把錢放到貨車上，就立刻把做了記號的錢拿出來，放到金屬盒裡。他們不能把錢丢出窗外，不然我們就會納悶他們怎麼知道染色包放在哪裡。他們不能把金屬盒留在貨車裡，不然我們也會有相同的結論。」

en_text: “Jesus, you think somebody from the bank was in on it?” “It makes sense,” Schroder answers.
zh_text: 「老天啊，你認爲銀行裡有人吃裡扒外？」「很有道理啊。」施羅德回答。

en_text: “You think this is the person who killed Kingsly?” “They’d have taken the box.”
zh_text: 「你覺得是這個人殺了金斯理？」「如果是，他會把盒子拿走。」

en_text: “Maybe they didn’t see it,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「或許沒看到吧。」藍德里說。

en_text: “Maybe. Other possibility is this person, whoever they are, might be after the others. Next step is to run down Kingsly’s known accomplices. See if we can find a link between somebody and the bank.”
zh_text: 「或许。還有一個可能，這個人，不管是誰，他要追捕所有的搶匪。如果知道金斯理還有哪些同黨，下一步就是幹掉他們。我們可以查查跟搶案有關的人。」

en_text: “So you think Hunter is capable of this?” Landry asks, nodding toward Shane Kingsly as he’s carried from the house in a body bag on a stretcher.
zh_text: 「你覺得杭特能幹出這種事來？」藍德里對著夏恩·金斯理的屍體點點頭，他已經被裝入屍袋，放在擔架上抬出了房子。

en_text: “I don’t know.” Schroder thinks about Benson Barlow and his warning. “I hope not,” he says, “but let’s go find out.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」施羅德想起了班森·巴羅的警告。「希望不是他，我們去看看吧。」

en_text: The knocking wakes me. I unplugged the alarm clock last night since time doesn’t really matter much these days. I get to my feet and pull back the curtain and the Christmas Eve sun is high enough to suggest it’s sometime around noon. I knew the knocking would come today, I just didn’t know when. The clothes I wore last night are gone. As is the murder weapon—or accident weapon, to be accurate. I’ve cleaned my hand up, put a fresh bandage on it, it hurts but that’s the price you have to pay, I guess. First thing the monster made me do when I got home last night was drop a glass on the kitchen floor when I was trying to take painkillers.
zh_text: 敲門聲把我吵醒了。昨晚我把鬧鐘的插頭拔掉，因爲現在時間對我來說也沒什麼意義。我站起身來，拉開窗簾，明天就是耶誕節，今天的太陽高掛天空，看來已經中午了。我知道今天會有人來敲門，只是不知道幾點。我昨晚穿的衣服不見了。殺人武器，或者該說製造意外的武器，也不見了。我清理過手上的傷口，换了繃帶，很痛，不過我想那也是該付出的代價。昨天晚上回到家後，想要吃止痛藥，怪獸就讓我把玻璃杯掉在廚房地板上。

en_text: I pull on some jeans and a shirt. My shoulder hurts and I rub at it. My body is stiff and sore. The knocking comes again.
zh_text: 我穿上牛仔褲和襯衫。肩膀很痛，我揉了揉肩膀。全身又僵又痿。敲門聲又來了。

en_text: I reach the door in bare feet. The house is closed up and the air is warm and stale. I open the front door and bright light floods in, the windscreen of the car parked out front reflecting a load of it into my eyes. I hold my hand up to shield them, squinting, exposing the bandage to the men standing outside.
zh_text: 我赤腳走到門口。屋裡密不通風，很熱很悶。我打開前門，明亮的陽光竄進來，我把車子停在家門前，擋風玻璃反射了大量的陽光到我的眼睛裡。我抬起手來蓋在額前，瞇起眼睛，手上的緝帶正好對著外面的人。

en_text: “We have some developments,” Detective Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我們有進展了。」施羅德警探說。

en_text: “What kind of developments?” I ask, and I realize that I haven’t actually spoken out loud since leaving Sam last night at her grandparents.” My voice catches and my mouth is dry and the words are croaky, and I have to repeat the sentence.
zh_text: 「什麼進展？」我問，這時我才發現，昨晚把小珊留在外公外婆家後，我就沒有真正大聲開口講話。我的聲音卡住了，嘴巴很乾，發出粗啞的字句，必須再重複一次。

en_text: “Mind if we come in? This is Detective Landry,” he says, and Detective Landry looks too small for his clothes and a little too tired to be working. I lead them inside and we sit in the living room. At least I do, and Landry does, but Schroder stays standing near the Christmas tree, which pisses me off. I don’t offer them a drink. It’s not a social call.
zh_text: 「我們可以進去嗎？這位是藍德里警探。」藍德里警探的衣服似乎太大，皺到讓人覺得他該下班了。我領著他們走到客廳坐下。起碼我坐下了，藍德里也坐了，但施羅德卻站在耶誕樹旁邊，讓我覺得有點不快。我沒問他們要喝什麼，他們又不是來拜訪朋友。

en_text: “You’ve found the men who murdered my wife?” I ask.
zh_text: 「你們找到了殺死我妻子的人？」我問。

en_text: “We recovered some of the money at a homicide this morning,” Landry says. “Drug dealer went and got himself murdered.”
zh_text: 「今天早上，在一處命案現場，我們找到了一些贓款，」藍德里說，「毒販被殺了。」

en_text: “So somebody bought drugs from him with the stolen cash?” “That’s quick thinking,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「所以，有人用贓款跟他買毒品？」「你的腦筋轉得很快。」施羅德說。

en_text: “I like that,” Landry adds. “A quick thinker.”
zh_text: 「我喜歡，」藍德里接著說，「聰明人。」

en_text: “But no. That’s not what we’re saying,” Schroder says. “The cash we found was from the bank. It was stained with dye and damaged.”
zh_text: 「可惜不是。情況不像你說的那樣。」施羅德說。「我們找到從銀行來的鈔票。都沾了墨水，不能用了。」

en_text: “I don’t follow,” I say.
zh_text: 「我不懂。」我說。

en_text: Schroder explains to me what a dye pack is and it makes enough sense. The whole time I keep thinking there’s something he’s not telling me. Maybe they found something of mine at the scene. Could be a neighbor saw me—it doesn’t seem likely, it was too dark. And why isn’t he mentioning the rest of the money? The bricks of cash under the mattress weren’t ruined with dye.
zh_text: 施羅德向我解釋染色包是什麼，很有道理。他說話的時候，我一直在想，他有件事情瞞著我。或许他們在現場找到了屬於我的東西。難道有鄰居看到我不可能，天色夠黑了。那爲什麼他不提剩下的錢怎麼了？床墊下的一疊疊鈔票可沒染上顏色。

en_text: “How much of the money did you find?” I ask.
zh_text: 「你們找到了多少錢？」我問。

en_text: “Can’t tell you that,” Schroder says. “Was this the man that killed Jodie?” “No,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「不能告诉你。」施羅德說。「就是這個男人殺了茱蒂嗎？」「不是。」藍德里說。

en_text: “He was one of the six?” I ask. “One of the seven,” Schroder says. “What?”
zh_text: 「他是六人當中的一個？」我問。「七人當中的一個。」施羅德說。「什麼？」

en_text: “Six men came into the bank,” Schroder says, “but another man sat out in the car.”
zh_text: 「進銀行的有六個人，」施羅德說，「但有另一個人留在車子裡。」

en_text: “A getaway driver?”
zh_text: 「負責駕車逃跑？」

en_text: “A wheelman,” Landry says. “So one of them killed him?” “Maybe.”
zh_text: 「我們叫他馬夫。」藍德里說。「所以，那六個人當中有一個殺了他？」「或许吧。」

en_text: “Who found him?” I ask.
zh_text: 「誰發現他死了？」我問。

en_text: “Now, why would you ask that?” he asks.
zh_text: 「喂，你爲什麼要問這個問題？」他問。

en_text: “If this is somebody who was in the gang that killed my wife, maybe whoever found him is part of it.”
zh_text: 「如果殺死我妻子的是六人當中的一個，或许找到屍體的人也有嫌疑。」

en_text: “They wouldn’t have phoned it in,” Schroder says. “It was his probation officer. The victim didn’t show up this morning, and his probation officer came looking for him.”
zh_text: 「他們不會打電話來報告。」施羅德說，「他的觀護人發現的。被害人今天早上未如預期般出現，他的觀護人打電話來警局找他。」

en_text: “So what are you saying? Who killed him?”
zh_text: 「所以，你的結論是什麼？他是誰殺的？」

en_text: “We don’t know,” Landry says. “Doesn’t make sense that somebody would kill him, and leave all those drugs behind.” And the money.
zh_text: 「我們不知道。」藍德里說，「如果有人殺了他，應該會把毒品跟錢都拿走，可是東西都仕。」

en_text: “Unless he was killed for a different reason,” Schroder says. “Something more personal,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「除非他被殺還有不同的理由。」施羅德說。「更私人的理由。」藍德里說。

en_text: “Like revenge,” Schroder says, the two cops bouncing off each other now.
zh_text: 「比方說報仇。」施羅德說，這兩個條子唱起雙簀來了。

en_text: “But you must know his accomplices, right?” I ask. “He would have worked with these men before?”
zh_text: 「但你們一定知道他的共犯是誰，對不對？」我問，「他跟這些人以前也犯過案吧？」

en_text: “We’re looking into it,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我們正在調查。」施羅德說。

en_text: “I don’t understand, why have you come here to tell me this?”
zh_text: 「我不懂，你們來告訴我這些事情幹什麼？」

en_text: “We thought it was important to keep you updated,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我們覺得應該要告訴你第一手的消息。」施羅德說。

en_text: I don’t think that’s it at all. And he knows I don’t believe him.
zh_text: 我心想，才怪吧。他也知道我不信他的话。

en_text: “You haven’t exactly told me anything, except somebody who could have been part of the robbery got killed. How do you know he was the wheelman and not one of the six in the bank?”
zh_text: 「你們什麼也沒告訴我，除了某個可能是搶匪一夥的人被殺了。你怎麼知道他是馬夫，不是銀行裡那六人其中的一個？」

en_text: “Height.”
zh_text: 「身高。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “He was a tall man. None of the six in the bank were as tall as him. The bank crew were all average, this guy was over six foot.”
zh_text: 「他個子很高。銀行裡那六個人都不像他這麼高。銀行裡的搶匪都是普通身高，這個人超過一百八十三公分。」

en_text: “Still doesn’t mean he drove the van,” I say.
zh_text: 「那也不代表他負責開車。」我說。

en_text: “He drove the van,” Schroder says. “And he was part of the robbery.” “So now what? It means you’ll have the others soon, right?”
zh_text: 「貨車是他開的，」施羅德說，「他跟搶匪是一夥的。」「那又怎樣？表示你們很快也會抓到其他人嗎？」

en_text: “We have some leads,” Schroder says, and the way he says it makes me think that they have some leads on who killed Kingsly, not who robbed the bank. “What happened to your hand?”
zh_text: 「我們找到一些線索了。」施羅德說，他說話的樣子讓我覺得他們找到的線索跟誰殺了金斯理有關，跟搶銀行無關。「你的手怎麼了？」

en_text: “I dropped a glass last night,” I say, glancing over at the kitchen where I dropped the glass last night ready for this question. “I cut myself picking up the pieces. I should have gotten stitches.”
zh_text: 「昨天晚上我打破了一個杯子。」我轉頭看看廚房昨晚打破杯子的地方，早準備好答案了。「收拾碎片的时候割到了，我應該去醫院縫幾針。」

en_text: “Uh-huh. And your daughter? Where’s Sam?” “At her grandparents’.”
zh_text: 「嗯，這樣啊，你女兒呢？小珊在哪裡？」「在外公外婆家。」

en_text: “So you were here alone last night?”
zh_text: 「所以你昨晚一個人在家？」

en_text: “Sounds like you have something to ask me.” I say.
zh_text: 「看來你有話要問我？」我說。

en_text: Schroder’s cell phone goes off. He flips it open and walks off a few meters, keeping his voice low.
zh_text: 施羅德的手機響了。他翻開手機，走到幾公尺外的地方接聽，聲音放得很低。

en_text: “Yeah. We want to know how you can be in two places at once,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「對。我們想知道你怎麼可能同時出現在兩個地方。」藍德里說。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “You’re going to tell us you were at home alone last night, right?” “I was.”
zh_text: 「你要告訴我們，昨晚你一個人在家，對吧？」「我真的一個人在家。」

en_text: “We got a description of you and your car seen outside our vic’s house last night. In fact we’re planning on having a lineup later on which you’ll be coming along to.”
zh_text: 「根據目擊者描述，你的人跟你的車子昨晚出現在死者家門外。事實上，我們正打算等一下要讓目擊者指認嫌犯，你也要過來。」

en_text: “I wasn’t there,” I say, doing my best not to break out in a sweat.
zh_text: 「我沒去別的地方。」我盡力不讓自己冒出一頭大汗。

en_text: “We can prove you were.”
zh_text: 「我們可以證明你去了。」

en_text: “No. You can’t. Because I wasn’t. My wife is killed, and you come here and treat me this way? Screw you, Detective,” I say, my heart racing. “But you know what? I’m glad he’s dead. Maybe you can find whoever’s responsible and ask him to get the other six.”
zh_text: 「不，你們沒辦法證明，因爲我沒出門。我妻子被殺了，你們上門來這樣對待我？幹你媽的臭警察，」我說著心跳也加快了，「但你知道嗎？我很高興他死了。或許你們可以找到眞正的殺人犯，要他供出其餘六個人是誰。」

en_text: “Interesting you’d put it that way,” Landry says. “See, when you say other six and not other five, that suggests you don’t think the killer was one of the gang.”
zh_text: 「你居然會這麼說，很有趣，」藍德里說，「瞧，你說其他六個人，而不是五個人，表示你認爲兇手不是搶匪一夥的。」

en_text: I don’t answer him. Before he can start back at me, Schroder snaps his phone closed. “There’s been a development,” he says, looking uncomfortable. “I mean, an incident.”
zh_text: 我沒答腔。在他繼續指控我之前，施羅德啪的一聲關上了手機。「有進展了，」他的表情不太自然，「我是說，出事了。」

en_text: “What kind of incident?”
zh_text: 「出了什麼事？」

en_text: “It’s your father,” he says, and he stares at the ground for a few seconds before looking back up at me, and without him telling me, I already know what’s happened. “You’re going to need to come with us.”
zh_text: 「跟你父親有關。」他盯著地板，過了幾秒才抬頭看著我，他不用說，我也知道發生了什麼事。「你得跟我們走一趟。」

en_text: The back of the car is hot even with the air-conditioning going. The only other sound is the tires traveling over the road, neither detective seemingly in a talkative mood—not like twenty minutes ago. They probably don’t know what to say. It’s an unmarked sedan, so it doesn’t look like I’ve been arrested, but it feels that way, sitting in the backseat, only the handcuffs are missing. I watch the landscape change as we head through different neighborhoods into the city, the sun beating down hard on all of it, nice areas, not-so-nice areas, other areas you’d kill yourself to avoid. We’re delayed in the beginning, a minor car accident outside the Hagley Park golf course in town bringing cars to a crawl, a golf ball sliced out of bounds and into the windscreen of a car, sending the driver into a spiral. Other people are jogging the park circuit, cherry blossom trees lining the route. I think about the cell phone I took from Kingsly last night. It was blank. No records of any incoming or outgoing calls. No text messages. It was a new phone. A disposable phone.
zh_text: 雖然開了冷氣，車子後座還是很熱。耳朵只聽得到輪胎在地上轉動的聲音，兩名警探似乎都不想講話丨跟二十分鐘前截然不同。或許他們不知道該說什麼。這台車沒有警徽，所以我不像被逮捕的犯人，但坐在後座的感覺還眞像我被逮捕了，只差沒戴手銬而已。我們穿過不同的區域進入市中心，風景不斷變化，太陽熱辣辣地照在整座城上，高級的區域，不怎嬮高級的區域，你寧可自殺也不願住在那裡的區域。上路後我們耽擱了一下子，海格利公園高爾夫球場外的小車禍讓車速慢得跟用爬的一樣，有顆高爾夫球飛出圍籬，砸到一台車的擋風玻璃上，害那台車開始打轉。我也看到有人在公園的環道上慢跑，跑道兩邊都是櫻花樹。我想到我從金斯理身上拿來的手機。裡面空無一物，沒有來電或去電的紀錄，也沒有簡訊。全新的手機，用完就可以丢掉了。

en_text: We park around the back of the building next to a patrol car, audience to a family of ducklings on a nearby grass shoulder who seem to have lost their mother. We take a rear entrance and enter a cold corridor with linoleum flooring and plaster walls, a few Christmas decorations hurriedly stuck up on the walls with bits of tape. None of us say anything. We walk in single file, one cop ahead of me, one behind.
zh_text: 警探把車停在建築物後面，旁邊就是一輛警車，附近的草地邊上有一群小鴨子在呱呱叫，似乎找不到媽媽。我們從後門進去，穿過一條冰冷的走廊，鋪了塑膠地板，牆上只有灰泥，幾個耶誕裝飾用膠帶胡亂貼在牆壁上。我們三個都没講話。三人走成一列，我前面有一個警察，後面也有一個。

en_text: A nurse with bright blue eyes greets us and frowns at me before talking to Schroder. She gives him directions to the ward and I tune out the conversation. I can’t stop looking at the patients scattered about the ground floor, people hooked up to IV drips on bags going for walks, some of them heading outside to puff on a cigarette, and I can’t see a single person in this hospital that doesn’t seem bored, this day stretching out into many others. If the hospital has air-conditioning, it must be buried somewhere, maybe in the nurses’ lounge, because it’s about forty degrees in here.
zh_text: 過來迎接我們的護士有雙閃亮的藍眼睛，她對我皺皺眉，然後才跟施羅德講話。她告訴施羅德病房要怎麼走，我沒注意聽。一樓的病人吸引了我的注意力，有人插了點滴也能出外散步，有人到外面解解菸癮，醫院裡的人似乎都不會無聊，一天要當好幾天用。如果醫院裡裝了空調，肯定已經被埋起來了，或許在護士的休息室裡，感覺起來裡面大概有四十度吧。

en_text: We go up a few flights, taking the elevator. The doors open into a corridor branching into different wards. Two police officers are standing outside one of the rooms. The larger of the two comes over and he must know Schroder because he nods at him and doesn’t ask who any of us are. Landry holds back and makes a phone call. I’m left to stare at my feet.
zh_text: 我們搭電梯上了幾層樓。門開後，我看到一條分支到好幾間病房的走廊。兩名警官站在一間房外。個子較高的那個向我們走來，他一定認識施羅德，因爲他對他點了點頭，沒有詢問我們的身分。藍德里刻意落後，拿出手機來講電話。我只好低頭盯著我的腳看。

en_text: “In the corner with the curtain drawn around him,” the officer says.
zh_text: 「在角落，布簾都拉起來那張床。」警官說。

en_text: There are six beds in the room, all spaced an equal distance apart, three on each side of the room. Christchurch Hospital isn’t exactly the hub for medical advancement, but it makes do with what it has, even if most of what it has looks like it got ordered from a 1980s “Good Guide to Living” brochure. All the beds are full, but only one of them has a curtain pulled around it. There’s a gap big enough between the curtain and floor to see the feet of a doctor, and as we approach, he pulls the curtain away—ta-da!—revealing my dad. For the briefest second I’m sure he’s not going to be there, but of course he is, held down in his bed by tubes and a set of handcuffs connecting his right arm to the right rail.
zh_text: 房間裡有六張病床，一邊三張，每張中間都留了同樣的距離。基督城醫院絕非高科技醫療技術的集散地，但現有的設備也夠了，不過大多數的設備看起來都像從一九八〇年代的《生活好指南》小冊訂購。所有的床位都有病人，只有一張床周圍的布簾拉上了。布簾和地板之間的空隙夠大，可以看到醫生的雙腳，我們朝著那張床走去，同時醫生拉開了布簘一出現了一露出我老爹的身影。在那一瞬間，我確信他不在裡面，不過他當然在，被許多管子壓倒在床上，一副手銬把他的右臂銬在右邊的床欄上。

en_text: Dad’s eyes are closed, all warmth and color gone from his face. His features have sunken, as if the near-death experience triggered an internal collapse in which his body began falling in on itself. This man is a cold-blooded killer, but he’s also my dad, and seeing him this way—well, I don’t know what I feel. He’s in jail because I killed a dog twenty years ago.
zh_text: 爹閉著雙眼，臉色冰冷蒼白。五官都陷下去了，彷彿瀕死的經驗引發了內在的塌陷，他的身體跟著垮了下來。這男人雖是冷血殺手，但也是我爹，看著他這樣丨嗯，我也不知道我有什麼感覺。因爲二十年前我殺了一條狗，害他去坐牢了。

en_text: “It’s not as bad as it seems at first,” the doctor says, after Schroder tells him who we are. “One wound with a sharp object into the chest from the side. Not real close to puncturing the left lung, but if the weapon had been longer, who knows? Sounds bad—and believe me, it is bad—but it could have been a whole lot worse. The operation went about as well as it could. He’s heavily sedated still, won’t be waking up till this evening.”
zh_text: 「不像一開始那麼糟糕了。」施羅德表明身分後，醫生對我們說。「有個傷口是利器從胸口側邊刺進去造成的。不太可能刺穿左邊的肺部，但如果兇器再長一點，那就難說了。聽起來很糟糕，相信我，真的很糟，但也有可能更糟。手術還算順利。鎭定劑的藥效還沒退，他要到今天傍晚才會醒過來。」

en_text: “He’ll be okay?” I ask. “He’ll make a full recovery?”
zh_text: 「他不會有事吧？」我問。「會完全康復嗎？」

en_text: “Should do,” the doctor says, nodding toward my dad. “We’ll keep him for a couple of days, and we’ll check him every few days or so after that, but yes, your dad still has the rest of his life to look forward to. Of course we’ll know more this evening once he’s woken up. The only thing to worry about at this point is infection. We’ll keep you updated,” he says, then walks off to the next patient.
zh_text: 「應該會，」醫生對我爹點點頭。「我們會讓他住院兩天，之後就每隔幾天幫他檢查一下，不過沒問題，你父親沒有生命危險了。當然，傍晚他醒來後，我們會更清楚他的情況。現在只有一件事要擔心，就是感染的問題。我們會隨時告訴你最新的情況。」說完，他走到下一個病人床邊去。

en_text: “Who did this?” I ask, turning to Schroder.
zh_text: 「誰幹的？」我轉頭問施羅德。

en_text: “Nobody knows. A fight broke out during lunch. Inmates swarmed each other, and when they were pulled apart the guards found him,” Schroder says. “He was stabbed with a toothbrush, easy to file down, effective to use,” he says, and he sounds like he’s rattling off a sales pitch, like he makes a dollar for every filed-down toothbrush jammed into a convict. “Question is, why would somebody want him dead?”
zh_text: 「沒人知道。吃午餐的時候他們打起來了。囚犯擠來擠去，警衛把他們分開後，發現你父親受傷了，」施羅德說，「他被牙刷刺傷了，牙刷很容易磨尖，效果很不錯。」他喋喋不休的詞句宛若推銷的宣傳用語，似乎每一支磨尖後拿來刺傷罪犯的牙刷都能讓他賺進一塊紐幣。「問題是，爲什麼有人要他死？」

en_text: “He killed a lot of women,” I say.
zh_text: 「他殺了很多女人。」我說。

en_text:
“And people have had twenty years to try and kill him in jail. Why now? Why the day after you visit him for the second time?”
I shrug.
zh_text:
「要在監獄裡害死他，這二十年來都有機會。爲什麼剛好是現在？就在你第二次探監後的第二天？」
我聳聳肩。

en_text:
“See, the timing is pretty suggestive, Edward. Your dad knows as much as anybody that prisons are good places for bad people to meet. I think your dad figured he could do some detective work of his own. We checked criminal records and came up with names and we’re still working that angle, and the ball’s rolling now and we’ve got some real good leads, but your dad worked it quicker from the inside. Who was he working for? Does he want those names to give to you? Or to us?”
“I have no—”
zh_text:
「艾德華，你看，時機似乎太巧了。你父親跟別人一樣，知道監獄正好是壤人彼此認識的地方。我想，你父親覺得他可以自己調查一些事情。我們查過了罪案紀錄，找到了一些人名，我們仍在調查，已經投入人力了，也有一些不錯的線索，但你父親從裡面似乎能更快得到消息。他在幫誰？他要把這些名字給你嗎？還是給我們？」
「我不知——」

en_text: “See, Edward, it gets me thinking. It makes me think he gave you a name. And our victim last night had a stab wound in his hand, a big dirty wound similar to the one that’s on yours.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，所以我就忍不住開始想。我覺得他給了你一個人名。昨晚的被害者手上被戳了一個傷口，又大又難看，就跟你手上的一樣。」

en_text: “The only person who knows what my father was doing is my father,” I say. “And he stopped being my father twenty years ago.”
zh_text: 「我爹想幹什麼，只有他自己知道。」我說。「而且，二十年前，我就不認他是我爹了。」

en_text: “For you, maybe. Not for him.”
zh_text: 「或许你不認他，他可不這麼想。」

en_text: “Well, maybe you can ask him when he wakes up.” “Don’t worry, we will. First we’ll go through his cell.”
zh_text: 「或许吧，等他醒來你們就可以問他了。」「別緊張，我們會問他。首先我們會去搜他的牢房。」

en_text: “Well, until then, if you don’t mind, I’d like to spend a minute with him. Alone.”
zh_text: 「嗯，等你們有消息再說吧，如果你們不介意，我想單獨在他床邊坐一會兒。」

en_text: The detectives step away. I draw the curtain behind me for some privacy and then face my dad. It’s the third time in three days. My wife murdered last week, my father almost killed this week—what will happen next week? People say that things happen in threes. The accountant in me has always known that’s bullshit—but what if it’s true?
zh_text: 警探走開了。我拉上背後的布簾，不讓別人看見，然後才跟我爹面對面。三天來的第三次。上星期我妻子被殺了，這星期我爹差點被殺丨下星期會發生什麼事呢？俗話說，事無三不成。我的會計師身分總知道那是胡說八道丨但要眞有第三次呢？

en_text: I try to imagine how I’d be feeling if the knife had gone in differently, ten millimeters deeper or to the left, hitting whatever it is that it missed—whether I’d be happy or sad or indifferent. I reach for my father’s hand but don’t quite make it there. I don’t want to touch him. This man isn’t even my father. He used to be, once. Then he became something else. I may have called him “Dad” over the last few days, but he wasn’t really that, not anymore. I don’t really know what he is. All those years—add up the sum of a man, and his total, a serial killer. A demon. There isn’t a single one of us who doesn’t think he got what he deserved. Including me.
zh_text: 我開始想像，要是刀子進去的方法不一樣，多了十公分，或偏左邊一點，刺到這次沒刺到的地方，我會有什麼感覺丨或許我會開心，或許我漠然無感。我想握住爹的手，卻只伸到一半就停住了。我不想碰他。這人甚至不算我父親。他當過我幾年的父親，然後就變了。或許過去這幾天我還是叫他爹，但他其實不是我爹，再也不是了。我眞的不知道他算什麼。這些年來丨算出一個人的總數，他的結果是連續殺人魔。魔鬼。大家都覺得他罪有應得。包括我在內。

en_text: There are two things separating my dad from the morgue. The first is two hospital floors of concrete and steel. The second is ten millimeters of good luck. Schroder and Landry take me down into the basement of the hospital and I don’t question it. I go along for the ride—which is a straight drop in an elevator that opens up into a corridor about a quarter of the temperature of the ones upstairs. We walk in the same order as before, with me in the middle. The corridor reminds me of the prison, concrete block with no Christmas fanfare, a painted line on the floor to follow. There’s an office door and then there’s a large set of double doors. We go through the double doors and the air gets even colder.
zh_text: 我爹跟太平間中間隔了兩樣東西。一是兩層混凝土和鋼鐵構成的醫院樓層。二是十公分的好運氣。施羅德和藍德里把我帶到醫院的地下室去，我沒有異議，就跟著他們去了——搭電梯直接下樓，門開了，走廊的溫度只有樓上的四分之一。我們前進的順序跟剛才一樣，我走在中間。這條走廊讓我想起監獄，沒有耶誕飾品的混凝土塊，地上漆了一條線來指引方向。有一扇門通往辦公室，還有一對巨大的雙扇門。我們穿過了雙扇門，空氣甚至更冷了。

en_text: I’ve never been to the morgue before. Never seen for real what I’ve seen in dozens of variations of crime shows and movies over the years, the stark white tiles and dull-bladed instruments, saws with archaic designs even though they’re modern, sharp edges with only one purpose in mind. Then you have to factor in the morgue guys—people sympathetic, people who seem to take each death personally, people making jokes while munching through sandwiches and pointing out the “this and that” of anatomy.
zh_text: 這還是我第一次踏入太平間。過去這些年來，我在許許多多犯罪節目和電影上看過太平間，雪白的地磚和需要磨利的設備，鑲了古老標誌的鋸子其實很新很利，而且只有一個用途。然後還有看守太平間的人很有同情心的人，把每具屍體都當成自己的親友，或者邊嚼三明治，邊討論「這個和那個」解剖結構和講笑話的人。

en_text: A man in his early to mid fifties walks over, his hands thrust deep in his pockets. He sighs deeply. “Been a long day,” he says, and I can’t help but glance at my watch and note that it’s not even two o’clock yet. “You here to see our newest entry?”
zh_text: 一名五十出頭的男人走過來，雙手深深插入口袋裡。他用力嘆了一口氣。「今天還沒過完呀。」他說，我忍不住瞄了手錶一眼，發覺連兩點都不到。「你們來看最新那具嗎？」

en_text: “That him over there?” Schroder asks, and he nods toward a body on a gurney, naked and grey and looking nothing like I remember him looking last night.
zh_text: 「那邊那個嗎？」施羅德問，對著擔架上的屍體點點頭，屍體光溜溜的一片灰色，跟我昨晚看到的男人完全不一樣。

en_text: “That’s him. Haven’t got to him yet. I’m running behind, what with all the Christmas suicides beginning earlier every year. I swear as soon as malls put up their trees and tinsel, people start jumping from bridges.”
zh_text: 「就是他了。我還沒處理到呢。進度落後了，每年的耶誕自殺潮都會往前提早。我說啊，購物中心一擺出耶誕樹和金蔥，就有人從橋上跳下來。」

en_text: “’Tis the season,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「季節到了。」藍德里說。

en_text: “We’ll only be a few minutes,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我們只會待幾分鐘。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Take your time,” he answers, then wanders off to an office, slowly shaking his head.
zh_text: 「你們慢慢來。」他答腔，然後晃回辦公室去，慢慢地搖頭。

en_text: We walk over to the body. For a few moments it’s hard to believe it’s the same man. The tattoos seem diluted against his skin. His eyes are closed and the wound in his hand is open. It’s ugly and raw and runs from the center of his palm right out the side. It would have hurt a hell of a lot if he’d lived. The edges of it have blackened.
zh_text: 我們走到屍體旁。一開始時很難相信是同一個人。刺青似乎在他的皮膚上褪色了。他的雙眼緊閉，手上的傷口很難看，還是原來的樣子，從手掌中心向右延伸到外側。要是他沒翹辮子，肯定痛死了。傷口的邊緣已經燒黑了。

en_text: “Is this the man you think I killed?” I ask.
zh_text: 「這就是你們認爲被我害死的人？」我問。

en_text: “Nobody said we think you killed him,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「沒有人說我們認爲你殺了他。」藍德里說。

en_text: “You can cut the bullshit,” I say. “So why are we here?”
zh_text: 「你們不用再拐彎抹角了，」我說，「不然我們來這裡幹什麼？」

en_text: “We were in the neighborhood,” Schroder answers. “And I thought it would be good for you.”
zh_text: 「我們就在附近，」施羅德回答。「我覺得對你也有好處。」

en_text: “In what way?”
zh_text: 「有什麼好處？」

en_text: “This could as easily have been you,” he says.
zh_text: 「你不小心點，也可能跟他下場一樣。」他說。

en_text: “No. It couldn’t have been. I didn’t do this to him.”
zh_text: 「不。不可能的。害他變成這樣的又不是我。」

en_text: “I thought we were cutting the bullshit,” he says. “Look, Eddie, you have to know you’re messing with the wrong people here. I don’t mean the cops, I mean these people,” he says, and he points down at Kingsly. “This man is lying here today, but tomorrow or the next day, this is going to be you. Is that what you want?”
zh_text: 「我以爲我們已經停止拐彎抹角了，」他說，「艾迪，你得明白，你惹上了一些不好惹的人。我不是說警察，我是說這些人。」他指指金斯理。「這人今天躺在這裡，但明天或後天可能就是你了。你想要死得這麼慘嗎？」

en_text: “Of course not.”
zh_text: 「當然不想。」

en_text: “Then it’s time you were straight and tell us what happened.” “I didn’t kill him,” I say.
zh_text: 「那你就該老老實實，告訴我們發生了什麼事。」「我沒殺他。」我說。

en_text: “You sure of that?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你確定嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: They lead me back upstairs and out into the sun. We drive about two hundred meters until they turn in the opposite direction to my house. After a few more minutes it becomes pretty evident where we’re heading. I don’t complain. It’s like we’re taking a day trip, just driving around the city. The car ride to the prison is about the same as the ride to the hospital. Same amount of silent conversation, same amount of heat being thrown about by the air-conditioning. About the only thing different is the scenery. Farms with burned-off grass. Large fields full of dull animals burning in the sun, each of them with bad futures, slaughterhouses and dinner tables the only thing on their horizon. I can’t imagine driving a tractor around, plowing fields, milking cows, getting up early and going to bed early, working the land, the soil under your nails, backbreaking work—but maybe if I could have imagined it five years ago I would have lived on a farm with Jodie, away from the city, away from banks and bank robbers.
zh_text: 他們帶我走回樓上，走回陽光裡。車子走了大約兩百公尺，他們朝著跟我家相反的方向轉彎。過了幾分鐘後，我就知道我們要去哪裡了。我沒有抗議。很像出門郊遊，只是在城裡開車繞一圈。到監獄的路程跟到醫院的路程差不多。大家都沉默不語，冷氣依舊軟弱無力。只是景色不一樣了。路邊農地上的草都燒光了。大塊牧地上擠滿了有氣無力的動物，在陽光下快烤焦了，牠們的未來不甚光明，先去屠宰場，然後變成人類的晚餐。我無法想像農人的生活，開著拖拉機到處跑、幫乳牛擠奶、早睡早起、耕地、指甲裡塞滿泥土、工作到腰痠背痛——但或许五年前我會做這種白日夢，跟茱蒂住在遠離城市的農場上，遠離銀行和搶匪。

en_text: These are the same sights convicts see if they manage to run free—but people don’t really have to escape from jail when they’re getting released so soon anyway, the big revolving-door policy kicking prisoners back into the public because there’s no room for them, or no real desire to buck the system and say enough is enough.
zh_text: 如果囚犯能逃得出來，他們也會看到同樣的景色但囚犯其實不用逃獄，反正他們坐一下牢就被放出來了，那偉大的旋轉門條款把他們踢回社會大衆之間，因爲監獄人滿爲患，沒有人想反抗這個體系，站出來說我們受夠了。

en_text: We pull up further past the visitors’ entrance and walk across the hot asphalt to a back door. The pavement between us and the work crews and cranes shimmers—it looks like a layer of water has pooled across it.
zh_text: 警探開過了訪客入口後才把車停下來，我們走過發燙的柏油地面到了後門。我們跟工人和起重機之間的人行道閃閃發光一看起來像上面積了一灘水。

en_text: “Hope you don’t mind,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「希望你不介意。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Why? You think coming out here is good for me too?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼？你覺得來這裡對我也有好處嗎？」

en_text: We’re given an escort through the maze of concrete corridors that have to be almost ten degrees cooler than the outside world. We make our way to general population where the temperature heats back up to hospital temperatures. I can smell the sweat and the hate and the blood and the evil of the inmates as we walk past their cells. The cells mostly have concrete-block fronts with heavy metal doors in the middle, all of them ovens in this heat. There are narrow gaps at head height to look through, and at the moment many of those gaps are full of eyes staring out at me.
zh_text: 我們跟著警衛穿過迷宮般的混凝土走廊，比外面至少涼快十度。我們來到大衆聚集的地方，氣溫又回升到醫院的溫度了。通過牢房時，我聞得到囚犯的汗味、恨意、脾氣和邪惡。牢房前面大多是混凝土塊，中間有道沉重的金屬門，在這樣的熱力下跟烤箱一樣。跟頭差不多高的地方有窄窄的隙縫可以向外看，這時隙縫裡都塞滿了盯著我看的眼睛。

en_text: From behind the doors prisoners yell at us, some ignore us, others ask for cigarettes; the lucky ones have probably passed out from the heat. We reach my father’s cell. It’s the same as any of the others we’ve passed. It’s kind of surreal to see what my dad has called his home for the last twenty years.
