A concrete bunker with a metal door, a single metal bed bolted to the floor with an old mattress on top, a couple of posters taped up on the wall to add color, some books piled on the floor, everything neat and tidy, a stainless-steel toilet in the corner. I stand outside with four prison guards as Schroder and Landry begin tossing it over, turning everything upside down and pulling it apart. They take their time about it even though there aren’t many places to search, letting me wait in the corridor, the inmates in my local proximity all talking to me. One of them calls me Eddie, then he tells the others who I am and they all start saying the same thing. They’re all telling me they’re going to be seeing me soon. One of them eventually gets around to wolf-whistling at me, and the others laugh. All I can see are their eyes staring out at me, and occasionally some fingers come out from the gaps too. This is why Schroder brought me here—to give me the other preview of my future. He’s telling me I’m either going to end up in the morgue or in prison. I imagine spending twenty minutes inside one of those cells and the idea isn’t pleasant. I wonder how my dad survived. I wonder what kept him alive, what kept him from tying his bedsheet into a noose.
zh_text: 有的囚犯從門後對著我們吼叫，有的不理我們，還有人跟我們要香菸；最幸運的應該是已經熱昏的人。我們到了我父親的牢房。跟剛才經過的一樣。感覺很不眞實，看到我爹過去這二十年來稱爲家的地方。一座裝了金屬門的混凝土碉堡，一張固定在地上的金屬單人床，上面放了陳舊的床墊，牆上貼了兩張增添色彩的海報，地上堆了幾本書，所有的東西都很整潔，角落有座不鏽馬桶。我跟四名監獄警衛站在外面，施羅德和藍德里開始亂翻，把所有東西都倒過來和撕開來。他們很悠閒地搜索，不過能搜的地方也不多，我站在走廊上等，靠近我的囚犯都開始跟我講話。有一個人叫我艾迪，他告訴其他人我是誰，他們全都開始講一樣的話。他們異口同聲地說，他們很快就會見到我了。有一個人最後對我吹口哨，其他人都笑了。我只能看見他們的眼睛盯著我，偶爾會有人把手指頭從縫隙裡伸出來。这就是爲什麼施羅德要帶我來這裡——他要我看看我，未來會是什麼樣子。他要告訴我，我不是去太平間，就是到監牢裡。我想了想在牢房裡待二十分鐘會是什麼感覺，感覺似乎不太好。不知道我爹怎麼活下來的，不知道他有什麼指望，不知道是什麼讓他沒把床單綁成一個結來上吊。

en_text: The warden shows up. He’s in a suit that probably cost all of a hundred bucks, and he has a neutral sick-of-the-same-shit look about him—like my dad almost getting murdered can’t muster up a single ounce of excitement in him. He’s in his midfifties and uses the facial expressions he’s learned over all those years to look at me with complete contempt. Without saying a word to me, he heads into the cell and directs his wrath at Schroder.
zh_text: 典獄長來了。他穿的西裝應該是便宜貨，隱隱約約有種厭煩了無聊亂搞的表情我爹差點被殺了，似乎無法激起他一絲絲的興奮。他五十五歲上下，累積了多年的經驗，用非常輕視的眼光看著我。他沒對我說話，直接走到牢房裡對著施羅德大發脾氣。

en_text: “Who the hell said you could bring a civilian in here?” he asks, loud enough for most of the prisoners in the wing to hear. “Are you insane? This is an absolute breach of policy and will cost you your badge.”
zh_text: 「誰他媽的讓你把老百姓帶到這裡來？」他問，聲音大到這一翼的囚犯應該都可以聽到。「你瘋了嗎？居然敢這麼違反規定，小心你的位子不保。」

en_text: I don’t hear Schroder’s response—his voice is low and forceful, and when the warden responds his voice is low and forceful too. I try my best to listen in to what they’re saying, but can’t pick up much except a couple of names, one of which I’ve heard before. Their quiet argument goes on for a few minutes, and when the warden reemerges from the cell, he’s no happier as he storms past me, followed by the two prison guards he brought with him, cheered along the way by some of the prisoners.
zh_text: 我沒聽到施羅德回了什麼——他的聲音很低，但很有力，典獄長回話時也放低了聲音，但威脅度不減。我側耳傾聽，還是聽不到他們說了什麼，除了兩個名字，其中一個我之前聽過。他們又低聲爭吵了幾分鐘，典獄長才從牢房裡出來，跟剛才一樣怒氣冲沖地擦過我身旁，後面跟著他剛才帶來的兩個監獄警衛，一路上有幾個囚犯幫他們拍手叫好。

en_text: The two detectives keep searching my father’s cell as if there could be a dozen hidden compartments, and after thirty minutes they come up with nothing. In the end they walk out dejected, like they were hoping for a reason to arrest my dad all over again. We’re escorted back out the same way we came in.
zh_text: 兩名警探在我父親的牢房裡搜個不停，彷彿裡面有十幾個密室，過了三分鐘後，他們空著手出來。最後他們垂頭喪氣地走出去，彷彿希望能找到再度逮捕我爹的理由。跟進來的時候一樣，我們又被警衛護送出去。

en_text: In the car Schroder lays out the facts. There are no suspects in my father’s case—except for the fifty men who piled on top of him. It seems unlikely that figure will be narrowed down, and even more unlikely they’ll try to narrow it down. When my dad wakes up he may be able to help—but until then there’s not much they can do.
zh_text: 上了車以後，施羅德告訴我他們查到了什麼。我爹這件案子裡沒有嫌疑犯除了那五十個壓在他身上的人。很難抽絲剝繭縮小範圍，他們想查也無從查起。等我爹醒來或許能提供一些資訊但在我爹醒過來前他們也無能爲力。

en_text: I remember what my dad said yesterday when he gave me that name. He knew he was putting himself in danger. I think after twenty years he’d had enough of this place, he’d seen his son again, he’d seen an opportunity to be a father, and that was the best he was ever going to get.
zh_text: 我記得昨天他給我那個名字時說了什麼。他知道他惹麻煩上身了。我想，在這裡過了二十年也受夠了，他又看到自己的兒子，他發現有機會能再度扮演父親的角色，所以他再怎麼努力也會落得這個下場。

en_text: We pass a couple of media vans going the other way, racing out toward the prison; news of my dad has already hit the city. It’ll be on the news tonight, the prison as a backdrop, and I’ll be on the news tonight and in the papers tomorrow too. They’ll probably accuse me again of killing my wife. Of course that’s just journalists being journalists, not caring if they turn my life upside down for the chance of a story. Each year the competition gets edgier and edgier, compelling them to give up their ethics —and tonight they’ll be speculating on how far the apple really fell from the serial-killer family tree.
zh_text: 路上看到兩台新聞探訪車，跟我們的方向相反，朝著監獄疾馳而去，我父親的新聞已經傳到城裡了。今晚會上新聞，背景是監獄，我也會上今晚的新聞和明天的報紙。他們或許又會指控我害死了我的妻子。當然，那只是爲了炒新聞，爲了有料可以報導，完全不在乎是否把我的生活搞得天翻地覆。年復一年，競爭愈來愈激烈，迫使他們放下道德——今晚他們會猜測，連續殺人魔的基因能流传到第幾代。

en_text: We reach my street and there are no media vans parked anywhere. They’ll arrive though, with their cameras and lights and makeup kits. Landry is driving. He pulls up outside of the house and I climb out.
zh_text: 到了我住的那條街，还沒看到新聞探訪車。不過他們等一下就會來了，帶著攝影機燈光和化妝箱。負責駕駛的藍德里把車停在我家門外，我下了車。

en_text: “Hang on a sec, Bill,” Schroder says to Landry, then follows me out. “You can make our lives a lot easier, Edward, if you tell me what you and your father discussed. You probably don’t see it, but it could go a long way toward catching the people who killed your wife.”
zh_text: 「比爾，等一下。」施羅德對藍德里說，然後跟著我下了車。「艾德華，你可以幫我們很大的忙，只要你告訴我你跟你父親說了什麼。或许你沒發現說實話說不定很有用，可以讓我們抓到殺了你妻子的人。」

en_text: “What makes you think that’s what we were talking about?”
zh_text: 「你爲什麼覺得我們在討論跟搶案有關的事情？」

en_text: “Far as I can figure, there’s plenty for you two to talk about—but with the timing the way it is, it’s pretty obvious he was putting together a list of names. Look, Edward, you better think long and hard about what you want to do next,” he says. “See, it doesn’t look good for you. You go and see your father yesterday, and today one of the men who robbed that bank is dead. Then today your father gets a hit put out on him.”
zh_text: 「根據我的猜測，你們兩個有很多話可以講一但就這個時機來說，顯然他在收集名單。艾德華，聽我說，你最好能好好想一想，接下來你要怎麼辦，」他說，「你瞧，情勢對你很不利。昨天你去監獄探你父親，搶銀行的人就死了一個。然後今天你父親又被刺傷了。」

en_text: “I can’t help that.”
zh_text: 「我也沒辦法。」

en_text:
“I know you can’t, Edward. But you’re not seeing the big picture,” he says.
“And what’s that?”
zh_text:
艾德華，我知道你沒辦法，但你看不到整體的局勢。
「什麼叫整體的局勢？」

en_text: “I’m not saying you killed our victim last night. We’ll know soon—there was enough blood at the scene that somebody thought they could clean up with bleach, but they didn’t get it all. We’ll run it against your father’s, check for DNA markers—that way we don’t need a warrant for your DNA. So we’ll know about you for sure, soon enough. The problem you’ve got is that I’m not the only one who thinks you were there. They tried to shut your dad up before he got more names. That means they’re going to want to shut you up too. You’re going to drown in the mess, Edward, unless you start helping us.”
zh_text: 「我不是指控你昨天晚上殺了那個人。我們很快就會知道了——現場有很多血，兇手以爲用漂白水就可以清掉，但沒有完全清掉。我們會跟你父親的血液核對，檢查DNA標記——那我們就不用申請授權令來取得你的DNA。所以，不要多久時間，我們就會知道是不是你了，很快。問題是，除了我以外，還有其他人認爲那人是你殺的。他們想叫你父親住嘴，怕他找到其他人名。那表示他們也會想辦法叫你住嘴。艾德華，你已經深陷泥沼了，除非你幫我們。」

en_text: “You’re wrong,” I say, thinking about the small concrete cells, the other men inside them, and spending the next ten years there. “There’s another alternative.”
zh_text: 「你錯了。」我想到小小的混凝土牢房、裡面的人、在裡面住起碼十年的感覺。「還有另外個解釋。」

en_text: “Oh?”

“These people killed their own man for whatever reasons. Drugs, money, some weird gang-loyalty thing, whatever. They killed him, and that means they have no reason to come after me. They know I’m innocent.”
zh_text: 「這些人不知道爲什麼就把自己的同黨殺了。毒品、金錢、什麼奇怪的幫派忠誠啦。他們殺了他，表示他們沒有理由來追殺我。他們知道我是無辜的。」

en_text: “I certainly hope for your sake that’s what happened,” he says.
zh_text: 「爲了你，我眞的希望情况就是這樣。」他說。

en_text: I open my mouth to answer, but am not sure how. I think about Sam and I think about the cells, and I think the best solution for everybody is if I take my daughter and leave. Today. Get the hell out of this city. Out of this country.
zh_text: 我張開嘴巴，卻不知道該怎麼回答。我想到小珊，我想到牢房，我想對大家來說，最好的解決方法就是我帶著女兒離開。離開這座可怕的城市。遠離這個國家。

en_text: “The blood will tell us if you were there last night. You can save yourself a lot of pain by telling me the truth. You sure you want to play it this way?”
zh_text: 「血液會告訴我們你昨晚是不是在那裡。告訴我眞相，你可以讓自己不要那麼痛苦。你確定你要堅持下去嗎？」

en_text: I don’t answer him.
zh_text: 我没回答。

en_text: “Then you better watch your back,” he says, then turns and heads to the car.
zh_text: 「那你最好小心一點。」說完，他轉身回到車上。

en_text: I head inside. It’s a beautiful day but I close the door on it. Nat and Diana were going to take Sam to the park today, so right now they’re probably pushing her on a swing or making sure she doesn’t fall off a slide. They don’t have a cell phone. Well, they do, but they use it differently from the rest of the world—they only switch it on when they need to make a call, the rest of the time saving power, a habit I think most people in the retirement generation have. I try the cell phone now but it’s switched off.
zh_text: 我走進家門。天氣很好，但我關上門把好天氣關在外頭。納森和黛安娜今天會帶小珊去公園，現在說不定小珊正坐在鞦韆上，他們兩個在後面推，或看著小珊，不讓她從滑梯上摔下來。他們沒有手機。嗯，其實有，但是他們用手機的方法跟其他人不一樣——需要打電話的時候才會開機，不然就關著節省電力，我想退休世代大多數人都有這個習慣吧。我撥了手機，眞的沒開。

en_text: I try their home number on the chance they’re home, but nobody answers and they don’t have a machine. They’re at the park or the pool or the mall. When she comes home, what do I do then? Tell Schroder the truth and live the next ten years of my life the way Dad has lived the last twenty? I can’t do that, but I also can’t take the chance of Sam becoming a target. I hate the idea of leaving my wife behind, but she’ll understand. She’ll want what’s best for Sam—and what’s best for Sam is somewhere like Australia or Europe. Last night was an accident, but Schroder will never believe that. There will be no more accidents, though. The police have a name, they have a starting place now, and they’ll find the rest of the men who killed Jodie. Those men will be put away for eight or ten years and that’s the best I can hope for. There will be future robberies, future victims, but there’s nothing I can do about that.
zh_text: 說不定他們在家，所以我又試了家裡的號碼，沒人接電話，他們也沒有答錄機。他們在公園，或在游泳池，或在購物中心。等她回到家，我該怎麼辦？向施羅德坦白發生了什麼事，然後接下來的十年內過著我爹這二十年來的生活？我辦不到，但我也不能冒險，讓小珊變成箭靶。我不想丢下我的妻子，但茱蒂應該會懂。她總希望要給小珊最好的最好能帶她去澳洲或歐洲生活。昨晚是個意外，但施羅德不會相信那是意外。不能再出意外了。警察有了個名字，他們可以開始調查，然後找到其他害死茱蒂的同黨。這些人會被關八到十年，我想也不會再多了。以後仍會有搶案，還是會有人被殺，但我也無能爲力。

en_text: Making the decision to leave is hard in some ways, easy in others—but once it’s made there’s no reason to delay. I know how guilty that’s going to make me look. Damn it, I should’ve taken the money from Kingsly’s house, to make this move a whole lot easier. I move around the living room but don’t dwell on the fact that soon I’ll never see this house again, my in-laws, this festering city that took my wife. With this in mind, my neighborhood is different—darker, everything gritty, it’s now the kind of place where only one bad day separates it between suburbia and a war zone. I walk to the sidewalk and search up and down the road for the sedan I figure will be there. It’s about fifty meters away, dark grey, two shapes behind the window, too far away to see their faces. They’re going to babysit me, they’re going to report every move I make to Schroder—which means I might make it to the airport but not on board a plane.
zh_text: 下定決心離開這裡，說難不難，說容易也不容易但決定要走了，就不要再留戀。我知道，別人一定會覺得我畏罪潛逃。可惡，我應該把金斯理家的錢帶走，現在事情就好辦了。我在客廳裡來回踱步，不久之後我就再也看不到這棟房子、我的岳父岳母、這座害死我妻子的罪惡城市，但這些我都不去想。想到這裡，這一區也變得不一樣了更加邪惡，所有東西都蒙上了一層沙，只要一天的時間，這裡就能從郊區變成戰場。我走到外面的步道，查看有沒有一台我估計會停在街上的轎車。有了，離我家大概五十公尺，深灰色，坐了兩個人，看不到臉孔，只看到陰影。他們要照顧我，他們會把我的一舉一動都報告給施羅德知道所以，我或許能到機場，但上飛機前就會被攔下來。

en_text: I drive up the street, watching the sedan in my mirror. It doesn’t move, not until I reach the intersection, then it pulls out from the curb. I go around the corner. Twenty seconds later the car comes around the corner too. I’ve never been tailed before, and I don’t know whether the driver is doing a good job or a bad one. Then I realize it all comes down to whether or not he cares about being seen. Schroder probably figures if I know the tail is there I’ll be less of a problem for them. Fewer people will die.
zh_text: 我把車開到街上，從後視鏡裡看著那台轎車。沒動，等我到了十字路口，他們才把車子開到路上。我轉彎，過了二十秒那台車也彎過來了。我從來沒被跟蹤過，也不知道那司機幹得算不算好。然後我明白了，他只在乎會不會被我發現。施羅德或許認爲，如果我知道有人在監視我，或許就不會惹那麼多麻煩。死的人也會少一點。

en_text: I drive past an old miniature golf course that was brand new when my dad took me for the first and only time, when I was a kid. All the shine and color has drained from the signs over the years, the Wild West theme now just looks wild, as weeds and moss gradually pull the signs down into the earth. There are a couple of cars in front, but I can’t see anybody playing through the wire-mesh fence. I still remember vividly Dad and me walking from one hole to the next, miniature water hazards and ramps all encompassed by a miniature ghost town, writing down our scores with miniature pencils. It was a simpler time back then, I guess. Smaller in a way.
zh_text: 路上我經過一座老舊的迷你高爾夫球場，小時候爹帶我去過那一百零一次，那時候可是全新的。過了這麼多年，閃耀的光芒和顏色早已消失殆盡，荒野西部風只留下了荒涼，野草和青苔慢慢地把招牌往地上拉。前面停了兩台車，但透過鐵絲網我看不到有人在玩。我還記得很清楚，爹跟我從這一洞走到那一洞，迷你的鬼鎭包圍著迷你的障礙水潭和小丘，我們用迷你鉛筆記下分數。我想，那時候的日子比較簡單吧。什麼都比較小。

en_text: I wonder what my dad would do if he were still free and knew he was being followed. This must have happened to him too, near the end, when the noose tightened. He probably wouldn’t even have felt the pressure.
zh_text: 要是爹有自由，也知道有人在跟蹤他，不知道他會怎麼辦。他一定碰過同樣的情况，就在他快要被捕之前，警方快要探取行動。也有可能，他根本感受不到壓力。

en_text: It takes fifteen minutes to get to my in-laws.’ I pull up in the driveway and the sedan drives past. I get out and knock on the front door but nobody answers. I get my cell phone out and try calling again but still no answer. I walk around the house, through the side gate and into the backyard. I look through the windows for turned-over furniture and blood on the carpet, holding my breath as I move from one window to another, Schroder’s warning coming to life in my imagination—but there’s nothing out of place. I try the door. It’s locked. I head to the garage and put my face against the window, and when I pull back I can see the reflection of the grey sedan pulling up. It sits there with the engine running. I turn toward it. The windows are up and the sun reflects off them so I can’t see inside, not until the passenger-side window is wound down. A pale face with a sunburned nose looks at me from behind a pair of dark sunglasses.
zh_text: 開車到我岳父家要十五分鐘。我把車停到車道上，那台轎車開過去了。我下車，敲敲前門，沒有人來應門。我拿出手機重撥了一次，仍無人回應。我走到房子旁邊，穿過側邊的小門，走到後院了。從窗戶往裡面看，屛息尋找被翻倒的家具和地毯上的血跡，看完一扇就移到下一扇，施羅德的警告在我腦海中大聲重播，但一切看起來都很正常。我試著打開門，鎖住了。我走到車庫前，把臉貼在窗戶上，往後拉回的時候，看到灰色轎車的倒影，他們也把車子停下了，但是沒把引擎關掉。我轉身朝著車子走過去。窗戶都關上了，在太陽的反射下我看不到裡面，等副駕駛座的窗戶搖下來，我才看到裡面的樣子。一張鼻子曬傷的蒼白面孔藏在深色的太陽眼鏡後，一雙眼睛盯著我。

en_text: “Eddie Hunter?” he says, and the way he asks it makes me nervous. If these were cops, they’d know who I was. They’d know where I’ve just led them. Reporters would know too.
zh_text: 「艾迪·杭特？」他問話的口氣讓我緊張起來了。如果是條子，他們早就認識我了。他們知道我現在在我岳父母家。記者也應該知道。

en_text: “What do you want?” I ask.
zh_text: 「你要幹嘛？」我問。

en_text: “We know who killed your wife,” he says, and my body instantly freezes. “For the right price we can tell you.” “What?”
zh_text: 「我們知道誰殺了你妻子。」他說，我的身體立刻僵住了。「只要價錢對，我們就告訴你。」「你說什麼？」

en_text: “Nothing in this world is free,” he says. “I got something here to show you, it’ll prove what I’m saying,” he says.
zh_text: 「天下沒有白吃的午餐，」他說。「我要給你看一個東西，你就知道我說得沒錯。」

en_text: I take another step forward, a voice in my head yelling at me that this is a mistake, that I’m being lured closer. I take a step sideways, away from the car, and the barrel of a shotgun appears in the open window and fires.
zh_text: 我又向前踏了一步，似乎有個聲音在對我大吼，你錯了，不要再靠近了。我往旁邊走了步，拉開我跟車子之間的距離，打開的窗戶裡出現了霰彈槍的槍管，有人開槍了。

en_text: It’s a matter of priorities. If one of the bank tellers was an inside man, they’ll know soon enough. Schroder is confident a series of interviews will get them some answers before the day is out. Hell, maybe the whole thing will be over before Christmas Day even begins.
zh_text: 凡事都有優先順序。如果銀行出納員裡應外合，他們很快就會查出來。施羅德心想，在今天下班前如果能問到一些答案就好了。该死的，说不定在耶誕節來臨前就能結案。

en_text: He drives back to Kingsly’s house with Landry and drops him off. The plan is for Landry to get started on the interviews while Schroder goes back out to the prison. The trip there earlier didn’t net them much. They found medication in Hunter’s cell. The warden said he was given two pills to take every day. Adding up the pills they found suggests he stopped taking his meds the day of the robbery. Instead of flushing them, he was saving them. Maybe, Schroder thinks, Hunter was planning on building a stockpile to take the whole lot at once.
zh_text: 他把車子開回金斯理家，讓藍德里下車。他們計畫讓藍德里開始找人問問題，施羅德則回監獄去。上一趟去監獄的時候沒找到什麼線索。他們在杭特的牢房裡找到了藥物。典獄長說他每天都要吃兩顆藥丸。算了算藥丸的數目，他們發現在搶案發生那天，杭特就停止吃藥。他沒把藥沖下馬桶，反而留起來。施羅德心想，或许杭特想多存一點藥，然後一口吞下。

en_text: When he gets back to the prison, Theodore Tate is already waiting for him. Tate used to be a cop until a few years ago, when he turned private investigator, and after both those things he became a criminal. The visiting room is empty except for Schroder and Tate and one prison guard against the far wall, hardly paying any attention. It’s been a few months since he last saw Tate. He hasn’t changed much, except his hair is shorter and he’s lost a bit of weight.
zh_text: 到了監獄後，泰奧多·泰特已經在等他了。泰特以前也是警察，幾年前改當私家偵探，最後則入獄服刑。訪客室空空如也，只有施羅德和泰特，監獄警衛站得遠遠的，幾乎不管他們在幹什麼。距他上次來找泰特的時候已經過了好幾個月。他沒什麼改變，只是頭髮短了，體重也減輕了。

en_text: “Thanks for doing this, Tate,” he says, sitting down opposite him.
zh_text: 「謝謝你答應見我，泰特。」他在泰特對面坐下來。

en_text: “I was surprised you called,” Tate says. “I mean, in the beginning I was. I thought you were calling to check up on me, to see how I was doing. It was a surprise, a nice one even. Then it turns out you wanted something.”
zh_text: 「你打電話來倒嚇了我一跳，」泰特說。「我是說，一開始我很驚訝。我以爲你打電話來問我的情況，看我過得怎麼樣。應該說驚喜吧。結果你只是要打探消息。」

en_text: “Look, Tate, I’ve been meaning to come and see you for some time now,” he says, and even though he means it, he knows he would never actually have done it. There’s nothing worse than seeing a fellow cop in jail —even if he isn’t a fellow cop anymore. “I just, you know, didn’t get around to it. You know how it is.”
zh_text: 「聽我說，泰特，我一直想來看你，」這雖然是肺腑之言，但他知道自己永遠不會來探望他。在監獄裡看到曾經共事的警察感覺實在大糟糕了——雖然他現在已經離開警隊了。「我只是，你知道的，一直没时间。你知道我们的工作就是這樣。」

en_text: “Actually I don’t. You could educate me. We could swap places and see how it goes.”
zh_text: 「事實上我不知道。你要是好心，可以講給我聽。不如我們換個位子，感覺一下。」

en_text: “I understand why you’re bitter, but it’s not my fault you’re in here.”
zh_text: 「我知道你爲什麼覺得不爽，但你進來也不是我的錯。」

en_text: “I realize that. Only sometimes it’s easier if I can blame somebody else except myself. Hell, maybe it’s even therapeutic,” he says, smiling at that last bit. “So—what’s new? How’s Christchurch? Is it still broken?”
zh_text: 「我懂。只是有時候能怪別人，不要怪自己，會讓我覺得好過點。去死吧，還有治療效果呢。」他對自己的最後一句話莞爾一笑。「所以——有什麼消息嗎？基督城還好嗎？仍然殘破不堪？」

en_text: “It’s not broken,” Schroder says, and he really believes that. Really, absolutely, almost believes that. “Yeah, well, I think it’s broken no matter what side of the bars you’re on.
zh_text: 「並沒有殘破不堪。」施羅德說，也眞相信自己說的。眞的，一點沒錯，幾乎能說服他自己。

en_text: “Your help. You heard about Hunter, right?” “Everybody heard,” Tate says.
zh_text: 「我要你幫忙。你聽說杭特的事情了嗎？」「大家都聽說了。」泰特說。

en_text: “You heard anything more than that? Like who stabbed him?” “Nothing. Why?”
zh_text: 「你有沒有聽到其他的消息？比方說他被誰刺傷？」「沒有。爲什麼要問？」

en_text: “I think he was stabbed because he got hold of some names.” “What names?”
zh_text: 「我猜他被刺，因爲他拿到了幾個人名。」「什麼人名？」

en_text: “I think he was putting together a list of the men who robbed the bank last week.”
zh_text: 「我覺得他在收集名單，上星期銀行搶匪的名單。」

en_text: “And that got him stabbed?”
zh_text: 「所以他受傷了？」

en_text: “Giving those names to his son got him stabbed,” Schroder answers.
zh_text: 「他把名字給了他兒子，所以有人想幹掉他。」施羅德回答

en_text: “And you think the son is going to go after these people?”
zh_text: 「你覺得他兒子會去追殺這些人？」

en_text: “I’m pretty sure he already has. One of the robbers was found dead this morning. The victim drove the van. Timing fits perfectly. Dad gives son a name, that guy shows up dead, the next day Dad gets stabbed. The scene this morning was pretty messy. He got killed by somebody who had no idea what they were doing. Whole thing could have been an accident, or a fluke, the way it played out.”
zh_text: 「我相信他已經開始行動了。今天早上已經有一名搶匪被殺。負責開車的。時機配合得剛好。老子給兒子人名，那人就死了，第二天老子被刺了。今天早上那現場挺亂的。兇手根本狀況外。整件事情可以說是意外，照過程看起來，也是僥倖得手。」

en_text: “You think the son is capable of it?”
zh_text: 「你覺得他兒子幹得出這種事？」

en_text: “You tell me,” Schroder says. “You think it’s possible for a man to kill in revenge for his family?”
zh_text: 「你說呢？」施羅德說。「你覺得一個人如果要爲家人復仇，他做得到嗎？」

en_text: “Depends on the man,” Tate says.
zh_text: 「要看他是什麼樣的人。」泰特說。

en_text: “Well, this man has a father who’s a serial killer. His shrink came to see me yesterday. He thinks Jack Hunter suffers from an illness that could be passed to the son. Paranoid schizophrenia—he says it can be hereditary. Says it’s a medical thing. He told me Edward Hunter has the potential to be a real bad guy. I wasn’t so sure, not then—but now I think so.”
zh_text: 「嗯，這人的老子可是連續殺人魔。他的心理醫生昨天來找我。他認爲傑克·杭特有種病，可能會傳給兒子。妄想型精神分裂症——他說可能會遺傳。是一種病症。他告訴我，艾德華·杭特很有可能變成超級大壞蛋。我那時候還不確定——現在我相信他的話了。」

en_text: “So arrest him.”
zh_text: 「那就去把他抓起來啊。」

en_text: “We will, once we have more evidence. Landry tried to bluff him out saying we had a witness, but he didn’t go for it. We have blood, though. That’ll tell us.”
zh_text: 「等我們有多一點證據，就可以去逮捕他。藍德里嚇唬他，說我們有目擊證人，但是他沒上鉤。不過我們找到了血跡。驗出來就知道了。」

en_text: “So where do I fit into this equation of yours?”
zh_text: 「那我跟你這件事有什麼關係？」

en_text: “Two different ways. You can find out who stabbed Hunter. That might lead us back to the bank crew. Or maybe you can get some names for us. Hunter managed it, so maybe you can manage it too.”
zh_text: 「兩個問題。你幫我們問出來，是誰刺傷了杭特。或许我們就能找出搶匪是誰。或许你可以幫我們列一些人名。杭特都做到了，你應該也沒問題。」

en_text: “Nobody’s going to talk to me.”
zh_text: 「以後沒有人會理我。」

en_text: “There’s more of a chance they’ll talk to you than to me.”
zh_text: 「跟我比起來，他們比較願意跟你講話吧。」

en_text: “So why am I doing this for you? Why stick my neck out like that?” “Because it’s the right thing to do.”
zh_text: 「那我爲什麼要幫你？幹嘛把我脖子伸出去等人砍？」「帮我，才是你應該做的。」

en_text: “For you, maybe. Not for me. My best chance of survival in here is to keep a low profile, which is damn hard to do when there are others in here I arrested back in the day.”
zh_text: 「或许對你來說是吧，但對我可不是。我要在裡面活下去，最好保持低調，很難，裡面有些人還是我抓進去的。」

en_text: “There’s a girl in the equation. Edward Hunter has a daughter.”
zh_text: 「這件事情裡還有一個小女孩。艾德華·杭特有個女兒。」

en_text: Tate slowly nods. “And you were waiting to lay that on me, figuring it would work.”
zh_text: 泰特慢慢點點頭。「你終於把王牌拿出來了，就知道我會被打敗。」

en_text: “Did it?”
zh_text: 「有效嗎？」

en_text: Tate stands up and Schroder follows suit. “I’ll see what I can find.”
zh_text: 泰特站起來，施羅德跟著起身。「我看看吧，我會盡力而爲。」

en_text: I drop down, the shotgun exploding, and I’m back at the bank all over again, the air-conditioning replaced by real air, the houseplants replaced by bushes and trees, the six men replaced by two men in a car. A hole appears in the garage door about the same time my knees crash into the concrete.
zh_text: 我往下一蹲，槍響了，我又回到了銀行，從頭再來一次，真正的空氣取代了空調，樹叢和樹木取代了盆栽，車裡的兩個人取代了那六個搶匪。車庫門上出現了一個洞，同時我的膝蓋也撞到了水泥地。

en_text: The car door starts to open. I have nowhere to run, I have no idea what to do. But then I realize I’m not alone, I have my monster with me and he knows what to do. We’re already in action. I get up and run forward, the monster leading the way, the monster in full control and now I’m the one along for the ride. We get closer to the car. To me this seems the wrong way to be going, but I’m in no position to argue. A leg comes out of the car and touches the sidewalk: jeans and a black steel-capped boot. I drop down and ram the entire weight of my body into the door, leading with my shoulder, slamming it hard on the leg. The guy inside yells out and the shotgun drops somewhere inside the car, buying me a couple of seconds. I don’t wait around. I run up the street, crossing behind the car, making it difficult for them to fire on me.
zh_text: 車門開了。我無處可逃，不知道該怎麼辦。但我發現我不是一個人，怪獸跟我在一起，他知道該怎麼辦。我們已經展開行動。我站起來往前跑，怪獸負責領路，一切都在怪獸的控制之下，我跟著跑就對了。我們朝車子跑去。我覺得似乎選錯了方向，但我無權爭論。一條腿從車子裡伸出來，踏在人行道上：牛仔褲，黑色的鋼頭靴。我低下身子，把全身的重量壓下車門，我的肩膀先撞上去，車門重重地壓在那條腿上。裡面的男人怒吼，霰彈槍掉在車子裡，給了我幾秒鐘的餘裕。我一點時間也沒浪費。我跑下街道，在車子後面穿過馬路，讓他們沒辦法打中我。

en_text: The car hits reverse. The transmission whines loudly as the gap closes. Words of anger spill out the window as the two men swear at each other, a miscommunication passing between them. Maybe the passenger wanted to get out and take another shot, or the driver wanted to hit me with the car in the beginning. I weave across to the opposite sidewalk. The car screeches to a halt. It fishtails so the front turns toward me. The doors fly open and the two men jump out, but the driver has forgotten he’s still wearing his seat belt and he’s pulled back in, his eyes wide in confusion.
zh_text: 車子進了倒退檔。變速箱嘎嘎亂響，我跟車子之間的距離拉近了。怒吼聲從窗戶裡傳出來，兩個男人對著彼此咒罵，看來他們有點溝通不良。有可能乘客想要下車對我再開一槍，有可能駕駛一開始就打算用車子撞我。我穿越馬路跑到對面的人行道上。在刺耳的煞車聲後，車子停了下來。車尾一擺，車頭對著我。車門嗖地一聲打開了，兩人跳出來，但駕駛忘了他還繫著安全帶，又被拉回車裡，他瞪大眼睛，不知發生了什麼事。

en_text: The passenger runs around the side of the car and lines up another shot as I dive forward, getting behind a parked car and bang, metal is ripped out of the bodywork as I hit the ground. I get up and run, weaving between silver birch trees lining the street, waiting for the next shot, but there isn’t one, only footsteps as they pound the ground behind me.
zh_text: 乘客從車子旁邊跑過來，對著我又開了一槍，我往前一躍，跳到一台停在路邊的车子後面，砰！我倒在地上，掩護我的車子車身開花了。我跳起來繼續跑，利用街旁的白樺樹掩護我，等待下一聲槍響，但子彈沒有發射，只聽到後面那兩人重重踏在地上的腳步聲。

en_text: The houses in the street are all similar, around ten years old, in great condition but a little tired, none of them—thankfully—with any front fences. I race over the front yard and down the side of a house, hitting the side gate with my shoulder, busting the latch holding it closed. I get through and the gate swings back and the top section explodes in a cloud of splinters from the next gunshot. I go left, cutting across the backyard, over the deck and past the french doors and a small sandpit that has bright yellow toy trucks in it. I reach the corner of the house and go left again, back toward the road. This time there’s a fence across, but no gate. I duck into the alcove by the back door. It’s a glass laundry door that I ram my fist through, the bandage around my hand protecting me from any cuts. The glass shatters into a thousand tiny pieces. I reach inside and unlock the door and spill into the house, my feet slipping on the glass. I go left into a hallway as the men come into the house behind me. Nobody’s home. I turn into a bedroom and shut the door behind me. I tip a chest of drawers across the doorway and a moment later it rattles as the men push against the door. The door wobbles in its frame as it’s kicked. I try opening the windows, but they have security latches and only open far enough to fit my arm through. I grab the nearest thing, which is a clock radio, and yank it from the power socket and thrash it against the window. It cracks on the third hit, then smashes on the fourth. A shot roars from the hallway and a large hole appears in the door, then the entire thing folds in on itself with one more kick. I don’t wait around to see the rest. I take a running jump where the window was and do my best to clear the glass, but end up dragging my right thigh along a shark tooth of glass jutting out from the frame.
zh_text: 這條街上的房子長得都很像，屋齡大約十年，狀況還不錯，只是略微破舊，還好，沒有一棟房子前面裝了圍籬。我衝過一棟房子的前院，跑到屋側，用肩膀撞開側門，原本扣在門上的門門被我撞斷了。我穿過去，門往後一擺，槍聲又響了，門頂的木屑如雪花般爆開。我往左跑，橫過後院，穿過露天平台和落地雙扇玻璃門，還跳過一個小小的沙坑，裡面放了亮黃色的玩具卡車。我從下一個角落再往左轉，想回到街上。這次有一道圍籬，但沒有門。我鑽回庭院，穿過後門。用拳頭砸開洗衣間的玻璃門，手上的繃帶正好保護我不被割傷。玻璃碎裂，掉得滿地都是。我伸手進去把門打開，衝進房子裡，一腳踩在滑溜溜的玻璃上。我向左轉進入走廊，那兩人也跑進屋子裡來了。還好這家的人都不在。我衝進一間臥室，把門關上。再用一座五斗櫃堵住門口，幾秒鐘後那兩人把門用力推得咯咯響。在他們猛踢下，那扇門在門框裡抖個不停。我想打開窗戶，但上面有安全栓，只能開一點點讓我的手臂伸出去。我隨手一抓，抓到一個收音機時鐘，把它從插頭裡拉了出來，然後用力砸在窗戶上。敲到第三下，玻璃裂開了，第四下，碎了。走廊上傳來一聲槍響，門上出現了一個大洞，然後再一踢，門跟五斗櫃都倒了下來。我沒有回頭看發生了什麼事。我往打破的窗戶跑了幾步，然後一跳，盡力避開還在上面的玻璃，但我右大腿卻從一塊窗框上突出來的碎玻璃片上拖了過去。

en_text: I get straight to my feet and run toward the road, my shoe filling with blood. I hear tinkling glass as the man behind me breaks more of the glass out of the framework with the gun to make his jump easier. The front door of the house opens as I pass, and the man without the gun comes out, running hard at me. I put my head down and pump my arms and go as hard as I can, my feet pounding into the sidewalk, my foot splashing inside the shoe, creating a suction effect that squelches blood over the edge onto the ground. The only advantage I have is that these guys are wearing big heavy shoes and I’m not, and I figure my desire to survive is stronger than their desire to gun me down—though on that last part I’m not so sure. My legs are burning, my chest even more, every breath is like swallowing smoke.
zh_text: 我站直身子，往街道跑去，鞋子裡盛滿了血水。我聽到玻璃的叮噹聲，後面那人用槍射擊玻璃把洞弄大，好讓他們能更輕鬆地跳出來。我還沒跑到街上，房子的前門就開了，没拿槍的人蹦出來，對著我猛衝。我低下頭，用力揮動手臂，使盡力氣快跑，雙腳打在人行道上，右腳從鞋子裡踩出了不少血水，製造出吸盤效應，把血從鞋緣壓到地上。我只佔了一個優勢，他們兩個穿的鞋子又大又重，我的鞋子比輕輕，而且我認爲我求生存的欲望遠超過他們想把我打死的欲望不過這一點我就沒那麼確定了。我的雙腿發熱，胸口快要爆炸，每吸一口氣就像吞一口煙。

en_text: I reach their car. Both doors are still open, the keys in the ignition, the motor running. I jump in and jam my foot on the clutch and accelerator and pop it into gear at the same time as he reaches me, pulling at my shoulder. I peel rubber, and as the car lurches forward the door slams hard on his fingers. He yelps, and as the car powers ahead, he falls forward too, dragged along beside the car. The window is still up but I can hear him screaming, can hear his knees scraping along the asphalt, his feet bouncing and kicking at it. I swerve left and right to shake him loose, the bones in his fingers breaking like gunfire. I take the car up to fifty. Then sixty. Still swerving, still trying to shake him loose.
zh_text: 我跑到他們的车子旁邊。兩扇門仍開著，鑰匙插在開關裡，引擎還在轉。我跳上車子，重重踩下離合器和油門，同時換了檔，其中一人這時也跑到車旁，用力拉我的肩膀。我加大油門，車子向前一跳，車門也猛然打在他的手指上。他痛得大喊，車子向前衝的時候，他也向前一倒，被車子拖著走。車窗已經搖起，但我聽得到他的尖叫聲，聽得到他的膝蓋在柏油路上摩擦，他的雙腳亂踢亂彈。我忽而向左，忽而向右，想把他甩掉，他手指上的骨頭斷裂了，發出槍響般的聲音。我把時速加到八十公里，然後快到一百公里，不停轉向，想把他甩掉。

en_text: No you’re not. If you wanted him gone you’d pop the door open and watch him fall away. You’re the one in control now.
zh_text: 不，你不想把他甩掉。如果你要甩掉他，你會把車門彈開，看著他落在車後。现在你才是老大。

en_text: I jam my foot hard on the brake and the car swerves. My passenger slingshots forward at the speed the car was doing two seconds before I jumped on the brakes. His hand bends all the way back on itself, the tops of his fingers against the back of his hand, then—schrip—a wet sound as the fingers come free—only they’re not free at all, they’re still in the door. Flesh tears from the base of his fingers and runs halfway up his forearm like an apple being peeled, muscle and tendons exposed, and then he’s free, flying and then rolling past the car out on the street, his hand reduced to a piece of meat with only a pinkie and a thumb. He hits the ground hard, rolls a few times, and comes to a stop with his bloody hand cradled against his chest. He doesn’t get up, just lies there, trying to figure out how things have gone so badly and why he’s in so much pain.
zh_text: 我一腳踩下煞車，車子猛地轉彎。我的乘客用我踩煞車前兩秒的車速往前彈了出去。他的手轉了一百八十度，指尖靠到了手背，然後——啪嗒——手指斷開了，有種液體會發出的聲音——只是他的手指還沒得到自由，還卡在車門裡。肉從他的手指根部撕裂，一路撕到前臂的一半，就像削了皮的蘋果，肌肉和肌腱露了出來，然後他被放開了，飛到半空中，滾過車子，掉在街上，他的手只剩下帶了小指和大拇指的一塊肉。他咚地一聲掉在地上，滾了幾圈，然後停下來，血淋淋的手攏在胸口。他沒起來，只是躺在地上，不知道爲什麼情況會變得這麼糟，他爲什麼會痛到無法言喻。

en_text: The car comes to a complete stop sideways on the road. The guy with the shotgun is running toward me, getting bigger in the view from the passenger window. He’s about two hundred meters away and could probably cover the distance in about nineteen seconds if he were an Olympic athlete and wearing running shoes, but he isn’t, he’s wearing jeans and heavy boots and carrying a shotgun and he’s built big, and none of that is helping him right now. I figure I have thirty seconds until he reaches me, but he doesn’t need to cover all that distance to put me back into range.
zh_text: 車子完全停下來，最後停在路邊。拿著霰彈槍的那傢伙朝著我跑過來，在後視鏡裡變得愈來愈大。他大概還有兩百公尺遠，如果他是奧運選手，穿著跑步鞋，或許只要十九秒就可以跑完這段距離，但他不是奧運選手，而且穿著牛仔褲和沉重的靴子，還提著霰彈槍，加上體格粗壯，看來一點優勢也沒有。我想等他跑過來應該還要三十秒，不過他不用跑到車子旁邊，就可以開槍打中我。

en_text: I gun the engine and the wheels spin up as I turn toward him, but I lose control; the car keeps turning and I end up facing away from him again. The engine stalls. The back windscreen explodes, a hailstorm of glass peppering the back of my seat and the dashboard as I hunker down. My hand finds the key and I twist it. A follow-up gunshot hits the rear wheel as the car comes back to life. I take off and the back of the car drops down as the tire shreds away. The ground vibrates through the rim and the chassis as I drive, pumping the blood out harder from my torn leg. There’s a high-pitched squeal from the back of the car, making me wince. The steering wheel fights with me, but I keep forward and then the car jumps up—boom dud—and the front wheel goes over the legs of the guy with the missing fingers, and then—schlock—as the rim with no tire goes over him.
zh_text: 我踩下油門，車輪快速轉動，我把車子轉向對著他，但我沒有好好控制，車子一直轉，又轉回原來的位置。引擎抛錨了。後面的擋風玻璃炸開，玻璃如雹暴般撒在我的椅背上，我低下身子，讓玻璃飛到儀表板上。我摸索找到車鑰匙，扭了一下。又一聲槍響，車子引擎打著了，後輪卻被子彈打中。我開動車子，輪胎從輪圈上脫了下來，車尾往地面沉了下去。我繼續往前開，輪圈和底盤摩擦地面，傳來的震動讓我割裂的大腿噴出了更多血。車後傳來尖鋭的聲音，我感到臉部肌肉抽搐了一下。方向盤愈來愈難控制，但我繼續往前，然後車子跳了起來砰噠前輪壓過了掉了手指那人的腿，然後嚨噹少了輪胎的輪圈也壓過了他。

en_text: I can hear his screams over the sound of the car. In the mirror, I see him roll to one side, but his left leg doesn’t move at all, it’s still on the ground, severed. His right leg goes with him, blood jutting toward the sky like a fountain. He drags himself, and gets about half a meter between him and his severed leg before giving up.
zh_text: 他的尖叫聲蓋過了車子的聲音。我從後視鏡裡看到他滾了半圈，但他的左腿卻沒跟著動，仍留在地上，被切斷了。他的右腿還連著，鮮血如噴泉般湧出。他想拖動自己的身體，從斷腿處拖了半公尺，他就放棄了。

en_text: His partner runs right past him and takes another shot, but it doesn’t do any damage as I gun the engine, turn the wheel, and in a flurry of sparks, round the corner and leave them behind. I take the car up to sixty, race through a couple of intersections, take a hard right, and pull over.
zh_text: 他的夥伴從他身邊跑過，又開了一槍，但等於白開了，我用力踩著油門，轉動車輪，拉出一陣火花後轉過街角，把他們抛在後面。我把時速加到一百公里，衝過了兩個十字路口，往右急轉後把車停了下來。

en_text: I try calling Nat’s cell phone again. I’ve got blood on my hands somehow and it smears the buttons on the phone. I keep hitting the wrong ones and have to lean back and take a couple of deep breaths before trying again. My hands are shaking so badly I have to hold the phone in both of them to get it to work. There’s still no answer. Surely they’re okay. If something happened to them it would have happened at the house, not in public.
zh_text: 我又試了一次納森的手機。我的手上也沾了血，在按鍵上塗得到處都是。我一直按錯鈕，得靠著椅背深呼吸兩次，然後再嘗試。我的手抖得很厲害，不用雙手握住手機，根本沒辦法撥號。仍然沒人接。他們當然沒事。如果有事的話，應該是在家裡，不是在大庭廣衆之下。

en_text: Jodie was killed in public.
zh_text: 茱蒂就在大庭廣眾之下被殺害。

en_text: So where does that leave me?
zh_text: 那跟我有什麼關係？

en_text: It leaves you and anybody close to you in danger.
zh_text: 那表示你跟周圍的人都有危险了。

en_text: The media coverage was extensive, so the men who killed Jodie certainly know all about me and think I’m coming after them. These people, they know I killed their friend. They know my dad gave me a name, and they suspect he gave me more than one.
zh_text: 媒體的報導無孔不入，所以殺了茱蒂的人應該知道我是誰，也知道我會追查他們的行蹤。這些人知道我殺了他們的同夥。他們知道我爹給了我一個名字，他們會懷疑他給了我不止一個名字。

en_text: I pull away from the curb. I find myself heading toward home, then decide it’s not the best place to go if I don’t want to be found. Could be the guy with the shotgun has made one phone call and another pair of men are descending on my house right now.
zh_text: 我再度發動車子，發現自己走上了回家的路，我覺得如果不要被人找到，最好不要回家。拿著霰彈槍的人可能已經打了電話，召喚另外兩個人朝我家前進。

en_text: I change direction. The way the car is handling, with the wheel rim squealing on the road and my forearms burning from trying to control it, I probably wouldn’t have made it there anyway. Other cars slow down and people stare at me.
zh_text: 我掉了頭。這台車開起來很不順，輪圈在地上吱吱嘎嘎，我抓方向盤抓到兩隻手臂都痛了起來，想開回家應該也開不到。其其他的車子都慢下來了，好多人盯著我看。

en_text: I pull over. I’ve put about two minutes between me and the shooter. When I open the door the three fingers that were jammed there are dislodged, all three connected by the back of the guy’s hand and a long piece of skin resembling torn wallpaper. They hit the ground, the middle finger tapping louder than the other two because of a silver ring on it. The ring has been flattened and has a skull on it; maybe that’s what kept his fingers from slipping out of the door. I climb out. My leg is covered in blood, my shoe so full of it now that it’s leaking through the material. I feel woozy and grab on to the side of the car to stay balanced. I try calling Nat again but there’s still no answer.
zh_text: 我把車停下。槍手應該要再過兩分鐘才能找到我。打開車門後，卡在裡面的三根手指掉出來了，都還連在那人的手背和一大片皮膚上，那片皮膚看起來像撕下來的壁紙。手指頭掉在地上，中指的聲音比另外兩根更響，因爲上面戴了一個銀戒。戒指已經壓扁了，上面有個骷髏頭；或許就是戒指卡住了，他的手才會黏在車門上。我下了車。整條右腿沾滿了血，鞋子裡的血多到從鞋面上滲了出來。我覺得頭昏眼花，抓住車身來保持平衡。我又撥了納森的電話，依然沒有人接。

en_text: I get back into the car. There are dance-step footprints made up of blood on the ground where I was just standing. I start to feel dizzy, and then tired. I open the glove box and rummage through it. Tissues, a road map, a woman’s sunglasses. There’s a gym bag in the backseat covered in broken glass. It’s open, and I can see a woman’s clothes in there. Whoever this car belongs to, it sure as hell isn’t either of the men who showed up in it.
zh_text: 我回到車裡。剛才站過的地面上有很多血腳印，看起來就像有人在那裡跳過舞。我覺得好暈又好累。我打開置物盒，翻弄了一下。面紙、地圖、女人的太陽眼鏡。後座有個運動包，上面蓋滿了碎玻璃。袋口開著，我看到裡面有女人的衣服。不管這台車是誰的，絕對不是剛才那兩個男人的。

en_text: I rest my head back. Even with my eyes closed the world keeps swaying. I hold my hands on my leg and the blood is warm, the world fades and it takes me with it.
zh_text: 我把頭靠著椅背。雖然閉上了眼睛，還是覺得一切都在搖晃。我用手按住腿，血感覺溫溫的，世界消失了，我也跟著失去意識。

en_text: New tax regulations were being standardized, Inland Revenue was desperate to take more money from those who were poor, rich, and everybody in between. There were seminars being run by enthusiastic men in suits, the kind of men you see on TV late at night selling home gyms and futuristic kitchen equipment. The fun part about the seminars was we all had to pay to go along and learn new skills so we could stay in line with the new tax laws—and of course the seminars were run by Inland Revenue staff —which was another way of them making money.
zh_text: 新的稅務條例已經標準化，不論賃富還是不貧不富，稅務局都急著要從你身上榨出更多錢來。身穿西裝的男人滿腔熱情，舉辦了專題討論，他們很像半夜看電視會看到的那些人，在購物台推銷家庭運動器材和充滿未來風的廚房設備。好笑的是我們都得付錢才能參加專題討論，學習新技能，好跟得上新的税法——專題討論當然也由稅務局的人舉辦，這也是一種賺錢的方法。

en_text: I was in a room of around a hundred people—you could look down the row you were sitting in and see that each person had about the same amount of boredom pinned to their faces, like we were all watching a twelve-hour mime show. I looked down the row and at the same time a woman was looking back. I offered one of those “weird, huh?” kind of smiles, and she offered a “this is bullshit but what are you going to do?” response. There was that awkward social mingling afterward, where we all stood around drinking orange juice and not touching the half-cooked sausage rolls. I think the food was deliberately inedible so it could be offered at the next seminar and the one after that—all cost-cutting measures. I introduced myself to the woman I’d made eye contact with. Her name was Jodie.
zh_text: 房間裡大概有一百個人從你坐的這排看過去，可以看到大家臉上幾乎都有同樣無聊的表情，彷彿我們已經看了十二個小時的默劇。我轉頭看看，正好有名女性也對著我看過來。我做了個「很怪吧？」的微笑，她則回我「狗屁不通但你還能怎嬮辦？」的表情。後來有段很尷尬的交際時間，大家都站著，啜飲手上的柳橙汁，不敢去碰看似沒熟的熱狗捲。我覺得他們故意不把食物煮熟，好等到下一場跟再下來那一場還可以用都是降低成本的手段。我向那位跟我四目交接的小姐自我介紹。她叫茱蒂。

en_text: I was shy around women. I hadn’t really had much experience of them. I was afraid every woman I ever met was probably figuring I would try and cut them in half. Jodie didn’t seem to know anybody else—and I thought perhaps in her own way she was a little socially awkward too. All I knew was she was supercute and alone and her earlier smile had made me feel good about myself in some weird way. Before I knew it, I’d asked her out for dinner.
zh_text: 我在女性面前一向很害羞。我很少跟女性往來。我怕不管我碰到誰，她都會認爲我想把她切成好幾塊。茱蒂似乎沒碰到認識的人——我想，或许以她的習慣來說，她也有點社交障礙。我只知道她美呆了，一個人來，而且剛才她對我一笑，不知爲了什麼古怪的理由，讓我覺得自己其實很不錯。結果，我就糊裡糊塗地開口約她吃晚餐。

en_text: Our first date I spent in some nervous daze where I could hardly look her in the eye. Our second date we caught a movie and then sat in a café for hours—and again I have no idea what we talked about. All I knew was there was something about this woman that made me look forward to having a future.
zh_text: 第一次約會的時候，我緊張到恍惚茫然，幾乎不敢直視她的眼睛。第二次約會我們去看電影，然後在咖啡店坐了好幾個小時我還是不記得我們聊了什麼。我只知道她很特別，特別到我對未來充滿了期望。

en_text: Part of me thinks it’s happening right now—that first time I saw her, that first date, the first time we were in bed together. It’s a memory and a dream and at the same time it’s unwinding in front of me for the first time, all of it new and fresh and wonderful. Jodie is alive and in my world again and I want her to stay.
zh_text: 我有點覺得彷彿就是現在第一次看到她，第一次約會，第一次上床。是回憶，也是夢想，同時第一次在我眼前開展，一切都是新的，很新鮮，很美好。茱蒂還活著，又來到我的世界中，我要她留下來。

en_text: On our third date she’s different, but I can’t figure out how. Like when somebody wears glasses for the first time or gets their hair cut; it’s something subtle until they tell you, and then it becomes obvious.
zh_text: 第三次約會時她變了，但我說不上來哪裡變了。就像有人初次戴眼鏡，或剪了頭髮；很細微，等他們告訴你，你才恍然大悟。

en_text: Our fourth date—this one a lunch date—and again there’s a difference but I can’t get a read on it. She seems lighter, somehow. Not in the sense that she’s lost weight—but in another, hard-to-register kind of sense.
zh_text: 第四次約會，我們去吃午餐，又有一點不一樣，但我還是說不上來。不知道爲什麼，她感覺變得更輕盈了。並不是說她體重減輕了而是另一種輕法，很難表達的感覺。

en_text: I’m reliving the fifth date when I realize what it is: she’s paler, almost translucent around the edges. On our sixth date the skin is grey under her eyes and the tips of her fingers have turned blue. By the next date her hair is messed up and her clothes wrinkled, and the skin on the back of her hands is baggy, it’s slipping, like she’s had her hands in hot water for ages. There are dark shapes beneath the surface of her face, bruise shapes that aren’t bruises, but something else. When we walk I put my hand on her back and it’s damp with blood. Her strides are awkward, her muscles are cramped, it’s as though she’s walking on heels for the first time. Her arms move stiffly.
zh_text: 重溫第五次約會的經過時，我發現問題所在：她更蒼白了，整個人的輪廓幾乎是透明的。第六次約會時，她眼下的皮膚灰灰的，指尖發藍。到了下一次約會，她的頭髮亂得要命，衣服發皺，手背上的皮膚垂下來，要鬆脫了，就像她已經把雙手在熱水中浸了好幾個小時。她的臉上一層黑氣，看似有瘀傷，卻不是瘀血，而是其他的東西。走在路上，我輕碰她的背部，她的背上沾滿了鮮血。她的步伐笨拙，肌肉痙攣，就像第一次踩高跟鞋走路。雙臂僵硬地擺動。

en_text: Then, on a dinner date, she struggles to get the food into her mouth, and when she does she finds it impossible to chew. When she takes a sip of wine, it runs out of her mouth and down her chin, it pools onto the tablecloth and blossoms outward. Her skin is even greyer, and in some areas it’s coming away, revealing a darkness beneath. Dark spaghetti lines form in her features. We don’t go out much anymore after that one. We hardly even look at each other. And every time I touch her she is colder than before.
zh_text: 然後，我約她吃晚餐，她費盡千辛萬苦，才把食物放進嘴裡，好不容易放進去了，卻無法咀嚼。她喝了一口葡萄酒，卻從嘴裡往外流，流下了她的下巴，在桌布上滴成一灘，然後向外蔓延。她的膚色更灰了，有些地方暴露出下面的黑色。黑色的細線構成她的五官。之後我們很少出門。我們甚至很少彼此互望。每次碰到她，都覺得她比上一次更冷了。

en_text: Then on our last date, a lunch date on a hot Friday afternoon ahead of a bank appointment, I realize the woman I’m with is dead. The skin has pulled back around her face, making her eyeballs bigger, drying out and cracking her lips, her nose a loose blister, and she smells of earth and worms and rot.
zh_text: 然後到了最後一次約會，炎熱的星期五中午，我們要去吃午餐，然後要去銀行辦事，我才發現眼前的女人已經死了。她的皮膚往後扯，讓她的眼球看起來更大，肌膚愈來愈乾燥，她的嘴唇也裂開了，鼻子是個鬆垮垮的氣泡，她身上有股土味，是蟲子和腐臭的氣息。

en_text: “You need to be careful, Eddie,” she says, and her mouth hardly moves when she speaks, her voice sounding like gravel has stuck in her throat. I can see her vocal cords moving behind the thin skin of her neck.
zh_text: 「艾迪，你要小心點。」說話的時候她的嘴唇幾乎動也不動，聲音聽起來像是喉嚨裡塞了砂磼。在頸部細薄的皮膚後，我看得到她的聲帶上下移動。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “You have to choose what’s best for you.” “I know.”
zh_text: 「爲了你自己，你得做出最好的選擇。」「我知道。」

en_text: “And Sam.”
zh_text: 「還有爲了小珊。」

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “Don’t let the monster choose for you.” “What monster?”
zh_text: 「不要讓怪獸幫你做決定。」「什麼怪獸？」

en_text: She reaches across the table. I’m certain she’s trying to reach across from her world to my world, to come and get me. Her hand closes on mine, it’s cold and clammy, a loose glove of skin slipping back and forth. Her smile slips too, it drags her face down, widening her eyes, and there is something moving beneath the surface of them, something wormlike. When her lips part to carry on the conversation another hand tightens on my shoulder, another voice enters the mix, and the restaurant disappears, the menus fade to nothing. My wife clings to the moment for a few more seconds, the strain obvious in her decaying features. She is silhouetted against a perfect white background, like a glowing movie theater screen. Then she too disappears, fading into the light in a second.
zh_text: 她伸手橫過桌子。我相信，她想從她的世界進入我的世界，她要過來接我。她的手蓋在我手上，濕濕冷冷，鬆脫的皮膚來回晃蕩。她的笑容也鬆脫了，把她的整張臉往下拉，她的兩隻眼睛瞪大了，皮膚下面有個東西在移動，像蟲子一樣蠕動。她的雙唇分開，想繼續跟我對話，另一隻手抓住了我的肩膀，另一個聲音插進來了，餐廳消失了，菜單化爲虛無。我妻子掙扎著多留了幾秒，她敗壞的五官掩蓋不住拉扯。她背後一片雪白，如同發亮的電影院銀幕，襯出她的輪廓。然後她也消失了，過了一秒鐘，她消失在光線裡。

en_text: I open my eyes. I’m still sitting in the car. A woman with grey hair pulled into a tight ponytail and a crisp white shirt with sharp edges is kneeling next to me applying pressure to my leg. A man has his hands on my shoulders, then he hooks me beneath my armpits, his fingers digging into me. The world shifts strangely as I’m lifted onto a gurney. I can see the man’s face and wonder if it’s the same paramedic who tried to save Jodie. More pressure is applied to my leg, and when I try to look down at my body I find I can’t. I can’t even lift my head without the urge to be sick. I stare up at the sky. Blue sky, no clouds, a perfect day to . . . to what? To kill somebody? The two men who came after me certainly thought so.
zh_text: 我睜開眼睛。我仍坐在車裡。一名白髮在腦後繄繄繫成馬尾的女士跪在我旁邊壓著我的腿，她身上穿著俐落的白襯衫，仍有明顯的熨斗痕跡。一個男人雙手抓著我的肩膀，然後他把手從我的腋下穿出來，手指頭陷入我的身體。世界很奇怪地轉了一下，我被抬上了擔架。我看到那男人的臉孔，納悶他是不是在槍案當天救治茱蒂的人。我的腿被壓得更用力了，我想看看我怎麼了，卻看不到自己。想把頭抬起來，卻忍不住想吐。我抬頭看著天空。一片藍天，萬里無雲，很適合……的天氣？適合什麼呢？殺人嗎？剛才跟蹤我的那兩個人肯定抱著這樣的念頭。

en_text: I can feel the gurney moving but there’s no reference point in the sky so I can’t tell how fast we’re going, and the sensation is like dropping through the air on a roller coaster. The ambulance comes into view and I’m hoisted inside. An IV is punctured into my arm and more pressure is applied to the wound and people go to work. I close my eyes. The ambulance doors close and the sirens don’t come on.
zh_text: 我感覺到擔架動了，但空中沒有基準點，我不知道速度有多快，感覺很像坐雲雸飛車從空中掉下來。救護車進入我的視線，我被抬進去了。手臂上插了點滴，腿上的壓力更重，幾個人在我身邊忙成一團。我閉上眼睛。救護車的門關上了，警笛卻沒響。

en_text: Next time I open my eyes I’m in the hospital with the hallway lights whizzing by. There are two new faces above me. I’m wheeled into ER and stabbed a few times with needles and then my leg goes completely numb. My shoes are removed and my pants cut away. The blood is wiped off, revealing a deep gash, but the fact blood isn’t spraying out hopefully means no major arteries have been cut.
zh_text: 再度睁開眼睛，我已經到了醫院，走廊上的燈從我眼前快速掠過。我看到兩張新面孔。我被露出深長的傷口，但是血沒有噴出來，表示很有希望，我的主要動脈都沒有損傷。推進急診室，扎了好幾針，右腿完全麻木了。有人脫掉我的鞋子，剪開我的長褲。血被擦掉了，

en_text:
“Not as bad as it looks,” a doctor says, filling up a syringe. “We’ll have you up and about in no time. You’re not going to feel a thing,” he says, but he’s wrong. I mean, I can’t feel the needle and sutures pushing through my flesh, but I feel anger and fear and . . . and something else.
Excitement.
zh_text:
「看起来很糟，其實還好，」醫生邊說邊在針筒裡裝滿液體。「我們馬上就會把你治好。你不會有什麼感覺的。」他錯了，我是說，我感覺不到穿過血肉的針跟縫線，但我覺得憤怒，覺得害怕，還有……還有一種感覺。
興奮。

en_text: No. I don’t think it’s that.
zh_text: 不，我不覺得興奮。

en_text: Yes it is. Stop lying to yourself. You’re excited because you took down one more man. Only five to go now. Put your hand up and be proud.
zh_text: 不，你很興奮。不要騙自己了。你很興奮，你又打倒了一個人。现在只剩五個了。舉起手來，爲自己感到驕傲。

en_text: “Proud of what?” I mutter. “What?” the doctor asks. “Nothing.”
zh_text: 「有什麼好驕傲的？」我喃喃自語。「什麼？」醫生問。「沒什麼。」

en_text: There’s no time to be proud.
zh_text: 我才沒時間驕傲。

en_text: “What the hell do you think you’re doing?” the doctor asks, when I try to get up.
zh_text: 「你在做什麼傻事？」醫生怒問，我正把自己從床上弄起來。

en_text: “I have to get out of here.”
zh_text: 「我得走了。」

en_text: “The hell you do,” he says. “Mate, I haven’t even begun sewing you back together here.”
zh_text: 「走，走個屁。」他說。「老兄，我還沒把你縫好呢。」

en_text: “I need to . . .”
“Lay back down or you’re going to keep bleeding, and if you don’t bleed out you’ll get infected, and then you’ll lose your leg. That what you want?”
zh_text: 「躺回去，不然你會一直流血，你要血沒流乾，也會感染，然後你就要少條腿了。你想要丢掉一條腿嗎？」

en_text: It isn’t what I want. He goes back to work, and is about halfway done when Schroder walks into the room.
zh_text: 我不想。他又埋首縫線，縫到一半時施羅德走進了病房。

en_text: “You don’t remember who loaded the dye pack?”
zh_text: 「你不記得染色包是誰裝進去的？」

en_text: Because they weren’t officially treating any of the bank staff as suspects, Landry and two other detectives were interviewing the other three people who went back to the vault, while Schroder dealt with the fourth—William Steiner. They were doing the interviews at the suspects’ houses—this gave the detectives a better chance to get a sense of who they were talking to; whether or not they looked like they could use a few extra hundred grand. Maybe they’d spot a bag full of money somewhere too.
zh_text: 他們並未正式宣布銀行職員也可能是嫌犯，藍德里和另外兩名警探正在和進入金庫的三個職員談話，而施羅德負責第四個威廉·史坦納。他們在嫌犯家中和他們對談警探也更有機會觀察談話對象是什麼樣的人；是否給人手頭很緊的感覺。或许在他們家裡也有可能找到裝滿鈔票的袋子。

en_text: Steiner was a man in his midthirties with a pale complexion that helped highlight the acne scars around his neck. He didn’t seem nervous, and before he could answer only the third question Schroder had time to ask—the one about who loaded the dye pack—Schroder’s cell phone started ringing.
zh_text: 史坦納大約三十五六歲，面色蒼白，因此靠近脖子的痘疤更顯突出。他似乎不怎麼緊張，但才問到第三個問題染色包是誰放的他還沒有回答，施羅德的手機就響了。

en_text: “Excuse me a moment,” he said. He stood up from the living-room couch, stepped into the hallway, and opened the phone. He barely managed to get out two words before the information came racing in. Edward Hunter. A shoot-out. A dead man.
zh_text: 「不好意思，等我一下。」他從客廳沙發上站起身來，走到玄關，翻開手機。他還沒講到第二個字，消息便來勢洶洶。艾德華·杭特。槍戰。一人死亡。

en_text: That had been ten minutes ago. The drive into town was quicker than the last few days, most people having finished their shopping by now.
zh_text: 那是十分鐘前的事了。開車進城的速度比過去幾天快了不少，大多數人都買好過節的東西了。

en_text: “Quite some mess, Edward,” he says, stepping around the doctor and looking down at the leg.
zh_text: 「艾德華，一團亂呢。」他繞過醫生，看著艾德華的腿。

en_text: “It’ll heal.”
zh_text: 「會復原的。」

en_text: “I’m not talking about the leg. I’m talking about the scene you left behind.”
zh_text: 「不是你的腿。我是说你留下的案發現場。」

en_text: Hunter is nervous. His hands are shaking and his eyes are big and he looks like he’s wired on amphetamines. “I had to leave it behind,” he answers. “If I hadn’t got out of there I’d be dead right now.”
zh_text: 杭特神色緊張。他雙手顫抖，瞪大了眼睛，似乎剛吸飽了安非他命。「我必須脫身。」他回答。「我要是没逃跑，现在早就死了。」

en_text: Schroder nods. It’s what he’d heard, and it’s what the evidence supports. His next trip from here will be to the scene. “A lot of people watched you running for your life,” he says. “A lot of witnesses.”
zh_text: 施羅德點點頭。他聽說的情況也是這樣，還有支持他的證據。等下離開這裡，下一站就是案發現場。「很多人看到你逃命了，」他說。「目擊證人很多。」

en_text: “Any of them feel the urge to help?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「有人想跳出來幫忙嗎？」艾德華問。

en_text: “What do you think?”
zh_text: 「你覺得呢？」

en_text: “I think you’re here when you should be out there, looking for Jodie’s killers.”
zh_text: 「我覺得，你應該正在搜查誰殺了茱蒂，可是你卻在這裡。」

en_text: Schroder ignores the remark. “I think you’re lucky you’re still alive,” he says, “and that luck will run out if you don’t tell me the truth.”
zh_text: 施羅德沒理他的話。「我覺得你運氣好，居然沒死，」他說，「你要不說老實話，運氣也救不了你。」

en_text: “I want to see my daughter.”
zh_text: 「我想看我女兒。」

en_text: “Sure, Edward, no problem. As soon as you’re done telling me what happened.”
zh_text: 當然，艾德華，沒問題。你告訴我發生了什麼事，我就讓你見女兒。

en_text: “I want to see her now.” “Where is she?”
zh_text: 「我現在就要看到她。」「她在哪裡？」

en_text: “She’s with her grandparents. I don’t know where they are.”
zh_text: 「她跟她外公外婆在一起。我不知道他們在哪裡。」

en_text: “Where are they supposed to be?” Schroder asks. Is there a chance the men who went after Edward would also go after his daughter? No . . . surely not . . .
zh_text: 「他們會在哪裡？」施羅德問。追殺艾德華的人會不會也找他女兒下手呢？不會吧……當然不可能……

en_text: “I don’t know. At their house.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。在他們家吧。」

en_text:
Schroder’s stomach sinks. He tightens his features and tries to hide his concern. “And you haven’t heard from them?”
“That’s what I’m telling you.”
zh_text:
施羅德心頭一涼。他繃緊五官，不敢流露出一絲擔憂。
「你一直沒找到他們？」「我就是這個意思。」

en_text: He takes his cell phone out and heads a few meters away. While it rings, he watches the doctor, who so far has said nothing since he arrived, just kept on stitching. He’s probably heard similar stories a hundred times already. Schroder passes the information about Sam on to the detectives at the scene then goes back to Edward.
zh_text: 他取出手機，走了幾步。鈴聲響起，他看著自他進來後一句話也沒說的醫生，只是專心縫線。或许類似的故事他早就聽過幾百次了。施羅德把小珊的事情告诉在現場的警探，然後走回艾德華身邊。

en_text: “Okay, we’re going to send somebody to bring her in here,” he says, trying not to sound concerned. “In the meantime, tell me what happened.” Edward tells him what happened from the moment Schroder dropped him off to fleeing the scene in the stolen car, running over one of his attackers on the way.
zh_text: 「好，我們會派人把她帶過來，」說著，他極力掩飾聲音中的不安。「在等的時候，告訴我發生了什麼事。」艾德華從施羅德送他回家後說起，一直說到他開著偷來的車逃離槍戰現場，路上輾過了其中一個攻擊他的人。

en_text: “Okay, okay, that’s good, Edward. What I really need you to do now is tell me what happened last night. Don’t make me wait for the blood results. We don’t have the luxury of time anymore, especially now that these people are coming for you.”
zh_text: 「OK，OK，很好，艾德華。其實我比較希望你現在能告訴我昨晚發生了什麼事。不要讓我等到血液測試的結果出來。我們沒時間慢慢繞了，尤其現在這些人已經找到你頭上來了。」

en_text: “I don’t know anything, except two men were trying to kill me. With all the people that called the cops, and the gunfire, and the blood and chaos, nobody got there in time to arrest the second guy, am I right?”
zh_text: 「我什麼都不知道，只知道有兩個人想殺我。報警的人那麼多，槍戰目擊者那麼多，到處都是血，搞得亂七八糟，就是沒人能及時把另一個人抓起來，對不對？」

en_text: “Look, Edward, the car is going to show up all sorts of prints. The dead man wasn’t wearing gloves, so the shooter probably wasn’t either. Their plan would have been to wipe the car down or burn it. We’ll find him, and that will lead to the others. All of them. What’s the verdict?” he asks, turning toward the doctor.
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽我說，我們在車上會找到很多指紋。那個死掉的人沒戴手套，開槍的人應該也來。一個也不會放過。醫生，怎麼樣？」他轉頭問醫生。

en_text: “Nothing major. It’s a deep laceration and he’s lost some blood,” the doctor says. “We’ll bandage it up and keep him on a drip for a few more hours—but no reason we can’t release him tonight. However, he’ll have to stay off his feet for a couple of days.”
zh_text: 「不嚴重。很深的撕裂傷，他也流了一點血，」醫生說。「我們會綁上繃帶，讓他再打幾個小時點滴——不過他今晚就可以出院了。要小心，最好這兩天都不要走路。」

en_text: “Come on, Edward,” Schroder says as the doctor leaves them, “you’re in some deep shit here. You absolutely have to tell me what happened last night with Greensly.”
zh_text: 「承認吧，艾德華，」施羅德等醫生走後再開口，「你惹上大麻煩了。你一定得告訴我昨天晚上在格林斯理家發生了什麼事。」

en_text: “You mean Kingsly,” Edward finishes, and the look of horror at his mistake appears immediately.
zh_text: 「你是說金斯理。」艾德華接嘴後立刻滿臉驚恐，發現自己犯了大錯。

en_text: Schroder slowly shakes his head back and forth a couple of times. In some weird way he feels betrayed. He really wanted to believe Hunter was innocent.
zh_text: 施羅德慢慢地把頭前後來回搖了幾下。很奇怪，他居然覺得杭特背叛了自己。他眞的希望自己能相信他是無辜的。

en_text: “Kingsly,” Schroder says, and he hangs on the word for a few seconds. “That’s right, Edward. Not Greensly, but Kingsly. I never told you his name and the media don’t know it yet. There’s only one way you could have known that name, Edward, and that’s if your father gave it to you.”
zh_text: 「金斯理，」施羅德慢慢地說，「沒錯，艾德華。不是格林斯理，是金斯理。我從沒提過他的名字，媒體也還不知道。你知道這個人是誰，只有一個方法，艾德華，應該是你父親告訴你的。」

en_text: “He gave me the name, but I never went there.”
zh_text: 「他給了我名字，但我沒去他家。」

en_text: Schroder knows he did. He knows he went there and maybe he didn’t intend to kill him, or maybe he did—either way the result was the same, and no matter how you look at it it’s completely unfair. Right now Edward Hunter should be celebrating Christmas Eve with his wife and daughter. Easiest thing to do now is to get Hunter to confess, then take him into custody.
zh_text: 施羅德知道他一定去了。他知道他去了，或許他不想殺他，或許他想——不論如何，結果都一樣，不管你怎麼看，就是很不公平。現在艾德華·杭特應該跟他的老婆女兒共度耶誕夜。最簡單的做法就是讓杭特認罪，然後拘留他。

en_text: “Look, Edward,” he says, keeping his voice low, “here’s the thing—the last two years have been hell. Too many goddamn psychopaths running around. Two long years, and I’m tired, real tired of this shit. I look at this city and I want to believe it’s a good city, and it is, it really is, there’s still a lot of good here, Edward, a lot worth defending. So many people, they think this city has turned to shit, but it hasn’t. It’s my city, I love this city —but, like I keep telling you, it’s on a precipice. Thing is, it doesn’t have to fall. We can save this city, it can be returned to the way it was. Looking back, there are things I wish I’d done differently. Things that could have—expedited investigations. Things that could have saved lives. If I could do it all over, there are rules I would’ve broken. Sometimes the ends can justify the means, you know? Sometimes you have to do bad things for the greater good. Bad things to save the city.
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽著，」他低聲說，「我告訴你，這兩年來眞的很糟糕。太多該死的心理變態到處犯案。兩年，漫長的兩年，我很累，眞的累到不想再管這些狗屁倒灶的事情。看著這座城，我想要相信，這是個好地方，沒錯，眞的是，這裡還有很多美好的人事物，艾德華，很多值得我們去保護的東西。有好多人覺得基督城沒救了，我不同意。這是我的家，我愛基督城，但就像我跟你說的，已經岌岌可危了。重點是，基督城不需要倒下。我們可以拯救這座城，可以讓它回歸原來的風貌。想想從前，有些事我希望我用了不同的方法來處理。或許能加快調查的速度。或許能挽救更多人的性命。要是能重來，我一定會打破規則。有時候，爲了正當的目的，可以不擇手段，你知道嗎？有時候，爲了大衆的利益，只好做壤事。能拯救這座城的壤事。」

en_text: “Killing Kingsly, that was a bad thing, but you helped defend the city by doing it. What you have to do is say he attacked you and you defended yourself. A jury isn’t going to convict you on that, not when they know this son of a bitch helped kill your wife. Some scriptwriter will come along and ask to make a movie about it. And me—if it’d been my family that was hurt, I’d have done the same thing. You can’t keep denying you were there, Edward, the blood will prove it. And these people after you, they’ll keep coming. Let me take you into custody. Let me help you.”
zh_text: 「殺了金斯理，就是壞事，但你殺了他，反而保護了基督城。你只要說，他攻擊你，你不得不自我防衛。陪審團不會判決你有罪，如果他們知道那個王八蛋幫同黨害死你的妻子。說不定會有編劇來找你，要把你的故事寫成劇本。至於我——要是我家人被害，我也會跟你一樣。你不能一直否認你沒去他家，艾德華，血液報告出來就能證實你在現場。還有那些追殺你的人，他們不會放過你。讓我帶你去拘留所。讓我幫你。」

en_text: Edward turns his gaze from Schroder to the ceiling and stares at it for a long moment.
zh_text: 艾德華移開了凝視施羅德的双眼，抬眼看著天花板，沉默了好一陣子。

en_text: “Bring me my daughter first. I want to see her,” Edward answers, “then we’ll talk.”
zh_text: 「先把我女兒帶來。我想看到她，」艾德華回答，「然後我們再談。」

en_text: The curtain opens up and a nurse pushes forward a cart full of bandages and gauze pads. She smiles at Edward. “Looks nasty,” she says, “but we’ll get you up and about in no time. This won’t take long,” she adds.
zh_text: 布簾拉開了，護士把裝滿繃帶和消毒紗布墊的推車推過來。她對艾德華微微笑。「看起來很嚴重，」她說，「但你馬上就會好了。一下就好。」她又補了一句。

en_text: “I’ll leave you to it,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「妳幫他處理吧。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Bring me Sam.”
zh_text: 「把小珊帶來。」

en_text: “I will. I promise,” he answers, hoping it isn’t already too late.
zh_text: 「我會帶她來，我答應你。」他暗自想，希望還來得及。

en_text: It’s another messy crime scene, the kind of scene where the killers had no real idea what they were doing. The house most of the action took place in belongs to a family with a couple of kids, who were lucky enough to be at the beach instead of at home. Schroder knows it easily could have been a whole lot different—knows the medical examiner could just as easily have been sending more than one station wagon. There’s broken glass out the front and broken glass around the back and a busted-up door inside and blood in various places on the driveway and the sidewalk. There are holes in fences and in the side of a parked car from the shots fired.
zh_text: 一團亂的命案現場又一個，看得出兇手根本沒有經驗，不知道自己在幹嘛。涉案人闖入的屋子屬於四口之家，还好兩個小孩都在海邊，不在家裡。施羅德知道，要是他們在家，情況就大不相同——他知道法醫會告訴局裡，一台旅行車裝不下所有的屍體。屋子前面有破掉的玻璃，後面也有，裡面有扇門被撞爛了，車道和人行道上都找到血跡。圍籬上有洞，發生槍戰的地方停了一台車，車身也被打了好幾個洞。

en_text: The street has been closed off, limiting the view to only the neighbors. Even the reporters are being held back, their cameras in range but not much for them to see. The victim has been covered up, and the shape of the body shielded by patrol cars. It makes for a nice backdrop for the cameras, but nothing more. The car the two men stole and that Hunter escaped in has already been loaded onto the back of a flatbed truck and is on its way to the police station to be examined.
zh_text: 整條街都被封鎖了，只有居民看得到現場。就連記者也被擋在外面，他們的攝影機拍得到現場，但他們看不到什麼。被害人已經蓋上白布，巡邏車擋住了屍體的形狀。或許拍攝的背景還不錯，但沒什麼好看的。那兩人偷來又被杭特開走的車子已經搬到平板車上，準備送回警察局受檢。

en_text: “So the shooter killed his partner,” Schroder says, and Sheldon, the medical examiner, nods slowly, as if scared any quick movement will tear a muscle.
zh_text: 「所以槍手殺了他的夥伴。」施羅德說，法醫謝爾登慢慢地點點頭，似乎怕急速的動作會撕裂肌肉。

en_text: “One shot in the face,” he says. “One shot in each hand.” “Confirms what witnesses said.”
zh_text: 「臉上一槍，」他說，「雙手各一槍。」「證實了目擊者的說法。」

en_text: “Hell of a way to go,” Sheldon says.
zh_text: 「真他媽的幹得好。」謝爾登說。

en_text: “We’ve seen much worse. Would he have survived the injuries from being run over?”
zh_text: 「更糟的我們也看過。他要沒死，有可能撐得過被車子輾過造成的傷害嗎？」

en_text: “Left leg completely severed, right leg half severed, half crushed. I’d have rated his chances as somewhere between extremely slim and none.”
zh_text: 「左腿整條切下來了，右腿切斷了一半，一半壓爛了。我想他能存活的希望微乎其微。」

en_text: Unable to take his partner with him, and worried they could be identified, the shooter had taken steps to try and hide the identity of the dying man by blasting away his face and fingerprints. It didn’t work: the forensics team have already emptied the victim’s pockets, turning up some coins, a cigarette lighter, and a packet of smokes—all of which have clear fingerprints on them. They’ll have a name within the next two hours. Plus they’ve got the car with another whole set of prints to narrow down. He looks over at the bump in the canvas sheet over the body where the severed leg is. The very bottom of it, with a shoe still attached, is sticking out from underneath, the canvas not big enough to hide the blood on the street. It looks like the guy was attacked by a bear. “Jesus,” Landry says, coming over as Sheldon leaves. “The Hunter family must really be cursed.” “Where are we on the interviews?”
zh_text: 沒辦法把夥伴帶走，又怕他被認出來，槍手決定開幾槍把快死的夥伴臉孔打爛，指紋也打掉。沒用：鑑識小組已經掏空了死者的口袋，找到一些零錢、一個打火機和一包香菸——上面都有他的指紋。不到兩個小時，就能找出他的姓名。而且他們還有那台車跟其他一組指紋可以縮小尋人範圍。他轉頭看看帆布下隆起的那團肉，也就是斷腿的位置。腳上還穿著鞋子，從下面伸出來，帆布太小了，蓋不住街上所有的血跡。感覺這人剛被隻大熊攻擊了。「老天啊，」謝爾登走開，藍德里就走過來了。「杭特一家肯定受了詛咒。」

en_text: “Still working on it. Surveillance from the vault doesn’t suggest anything one way or the other. Just shows four panicked people stuffing money into bags,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「還沒處理完。金庫的監視器看不出所以然。只看到四個驚慌的傢伙把錢裝到袋子裡。」藍德里說。

en_text: “Yeah, well, combined with the names we’re going to get from this, I think by the end of the day we’re going to know who all the players are. No sign of the in-laws and daughter?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「好吧，那等到查出跟這個現場有關的名字，我想今天下班前吧，就能知道涉案的有誰了。還沒找到他岳父母跟女兒嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: “None. You really think these men have her?”
zh_text: 「還沒。你真覺得這些人把她抓走了？」

en_text: “Doubtful. I think they’re somewhere completely unaware of the danger they could be in. Anyway, I don’t see any real reason for the robbers to go after Hunter’s daughter. It gets them nothing—all it does is put them at risk.”
zh_text: 「值得懷疑。我覺得他們還不知道自己的處境有多危險。不論如何，我眞不知道爲什麼搶匪要綁架杭特的女兒。他們勒索不到什麼，只會暴露自己的行蹤。」

en_text: “And Hunter?”
zh_text: 「杭特呢？」

en_text: “He’s freaked out, but he’s doing okay.” “He give anything up about Kingsly?” “Nothing,” Schroder answers.
zh_text: 「他嚇壞了，不過還好。」「他透露了跟金斯理有關的線索嗎？」「沒有。」施羅德回答。

en_text: “You think he did it?”
zh_text: 「你認爲是他做的？」

en_text: “The bank robbers sure as hell think so. Both Hunters in one day. We have to find his daughter. Hunter said he’d talk once we got her safe.”
zh_text: 「搶匪已經認定是他做的。一天兩個姓杭特的都入院了。我們得找到他女兒。杭特說只要他女兒安全，他就會說清楚講明白。」

en_text: “Every patrol car in the city has a description of them. We’ll have her soon.”
zh_text: 「我們已經把消息傳給城裡的每一部巡邏車，很快就會找到她。」

en_text: “I hope so,” Schroder says, “for everybody’s sake.”
zh_text: 「但願如此，」施羅德說，「不然就有大麻煩了。」

en_text: They wheel me into another room when the stitches are done. Each stitch as it went in made me stronger. There are three other men in here in different states of pain and misery. One has both legs in casts, suspended above him. A man in his seventies is snoring, a bald patch with stitches on the side of his head. The third man is reading a magazine and coughing every fifteen seconds. There are two cops outside the door, either there to protect me or to stop me from fleeing. I think about my dad—he’s in a different ward with cops of his own.
zh_text: 縫完針後，他們把我推到另一個房間去。每刺進去一針，我就變得更堅強一點。病房裡已經有三個人，各有自己的病痛和慘狀。其中一個人兩條腿都打了石膏，高高掛在空中。一個七十幾歲的老人在打鼾，頭上秃了一塊，上面有縫線。第三個人在看雜誌，每隔十五秒就咳一下。門外有兩個警察，說是保護也好，是要防止我逃跑也好。我想到我爹——他在另一間病房裡，也有警察看著他。

en_text: My leg hurts a lot. After an hour, a nurse comes in and holds up a chart with five “happy faces” on it. The first face is yellow and smiling. The last one is purple and has a large frown and an upside-down smile. The three faces between range in color from yellow to purple, their expressions from somewhat happy to pretty much unhappy.
zh_text: 我的腿很痛。過了一個小時，護士拿著上面畫了五個「表情」的圖卡進來。第一張臉是黃色的，笑瞇瞇。最後一張臉則是紫色，皺著眉頭撇著嘴。另外三張臉則介於黃色跟紫色之間，表情從還算開心到有點不開心。

en_text: “Point to the one that represents how you feel,” she says.
zh_text: 「選一張你覺得最符合你感覺的臉。」她說。

en_text: I look for the happy face of the guy who had his wife murdered last week but he isn’t on there. “Just give me some painkillers,” I say, “and I’ll be fine.”
zh_text: 那個妻子上禮拜被謀害的男人不在上面，我找不到他的臉。「給我一些止痛藥就好，」我說，「就沒事了。」

en_text: The nurse, who is overweight with breasts the size of bowling balls, gives me one more chance to get it right. “Point,” she repeats.
zh_text: 那名護士身形肥胖，胸前宛若揣著兩顆保齡球，她給了我第二次選擇的機會。「選一張臉。」她重複。

en_text: I point to the smiley face. “Can I go now?”
zh_text: 我指了指笑臉。「我可以出院了嗎？」

en_text: “Soon,” she says. “Now take these,” and she hands me a small plastic cup with pills in it. I shake the two pills into my palm and she gives me a cup of water. “Drink,” she says, as if I couldn’t figure out the next step by myself. Then she takes my blood pressure and seems neither pleased nor concerned by the result. I don’t understand the numbers.
zh_text: 「你很快就可以出院了，把這些藥吃了。」說著，她遞給我一個裝了藥丸的小塑膠杯。我搖搖杯子，把裡面的兩顆藥丸倒進手心，護士同時給了我一杯水。「喝吧。」她說話的口氣彷彿我不懂吃藥的方法。然後她量了我的血壓，對結果似乎不滿意也不在乎。我不懂那些數字代表的意思。

en_text: “We’ve found your daughter,” Schroder says, coming into the ward, and for the briefest of seconds I’m terrified, absolutely shit-scared because I don’t know how he’s going to finish that sentence. They found her at the park and she was playing on a swing with Mr. Fluff ’n’ Stuff, or they found her covered in blood with her throat cut? Schroder’s pause is so brief, so hardly noticeable, but for me it lasts a lifetime. “They’d gone to the movies. They’re at home now.”
zh_text: 「我們找到你女兒了，」施羅德聲隨人到，走進病房來，就在那一剎那間，我滿心恐懼，簡直要屁滾尿流，因爲我不知道接下來他會說什麼。他們在公園找到她，她正跟毛飽先生在玩盪鞦？還是發現她滿身是血，喉嚨被割開了？施羅德只停了一下下，短到幾乎無法察覺，我卻煎熬到坐立難安。「他們剛去看電影，現在回到家了。」

en_text: “So . . . so they’re okay?”
zh_text: 「那···那他們沒事吧？」

en_text: “They’re okay. But they thought it might scare her too much to bring her down here to the hospital. We’ve got a man at their house to keep an eye on them until we get there.”
zh_text: 「沒事，但他們覺得把小珊帶來醫院可能會把她嚇壞了。我們留了一個人在那裡看守，等我們過去再說。」

en_text: “Just the one?”
zh_text: 「只有一個人？」

en_text: “It’s Christmas Eve,” he says. “One’s all we can spare, but it will be enough. You’re the target, not them.”
zh_text: 「今天是耶誕夜，」他說，「我們只挪得出一個人，應該夠了。搶匪的目標是你，不是他們。」

en_text: He tosses me a pair of pants that are old but are at least in better shape than mine. He also has a pair of sneakers that aren’t full of blood, so I don’t complain. The nurse with the bowling-ball breasts comes back and unhooks the IV from my arm.
zh_text: 他丢給我一條長褲，雖然舊，總比我身上那條好。他也帶來一雙運動鞋，裡面沒裝滿鮮血，我也没什麼好抱怨。巨乳護士又來了，拔掉我手臂上的點滴。

en_text: “Ten minutes,” Schroder says. “That’s the deal. I give you ten minutes with your daughter, and then you’re coming to the station to tell me everything.”
zh_text: 「十分鐘，」施羅德說，「就這麼辦，我給你十分鐘跟你女兒在一起，然後你來警察局，把事情一五一十說清楚。」

en_text: The pain is instant when I stand; my leg throbs and I almost collapse. All the blood drains in one direction and I get light-headed. The nurse pushes me back toward the bed but I regain myself and straighten up. “See?” I say, pointing at my face. “A happy smile. I’m fine.”
zh_text: 我一站起來就痛得不得了；雙腿抽動，差點倒了回去。全身所有的血液都往同一個方向流乾了，我覺得暈頭轉向。護士把我推回床上，但一回復後我就站直了身子。「瞧？」我指著自己的臉。「笑臉。我很好。」

en_text: “You don’t look fine.” “I will be.”
zh_text: 「你看起來不很好。」

en_text: It takes me longer than usual to get dressed, and instead of walking out of the hospital they push me out in a wheelchair. All the people that seemed to be around this afternoon have gone home for Christmas. We pass only two nurses on the way out and an orderly and nobody else, not even any visitors. Everything that was in my pockets is handed to me in a white paper bag. I don’t bother opening it. At the hospital doors I leave the wheelchair behind. My leg is tight with all the new stitching.
zh_text: 「等一下就好了。」我穿衣服穿鞋的速度比往常慢了许多，他們不讓我自己走，反而用輪椅把我推出醫院。今天下午還在醫院的人似乎都回家過耶誕節了。一路上只看到兩個護士和一個總務人員，沒看到其他人，連探病的人也沒有。我口袋裡的東西都被裝到一個白色紙袋裡。拿到紙袋後我根本無心打開。到了醫院門口，我從輪椅上站起來。剛縫過的右腿感覺非常緊繃。

en_text: Schroder is parked in one of the handicapped spots close to the door. The parking lot is empty except for two other cars. I think he’s about to put me in the back of the car, but he lets me ride up front. He knows I’ve killed two people within the last twenty-four hours, and I’m sure he’ll try to prove it once he gets me into an interrogation room. I have no idea how, but the day has stretched into night. I’m no longer wearing my watch—I don’t even know if it’s in the paper bag, or if I lost it in the excitement of the day, or maybe one of the paramedics stole it. It must be around 9:30.
zh_text: 施羅德把車停在靠近入口的殘障車位裡。整座停車場空空蕩蕩，只停了兩部車。我本來以爲他要讓我坐在後座，但他讓我坐他旁邊。他知道過去二十四小時以來我已經殺了兩個人，我確信他只要一把我關進偵訊室，就會證明我殺了人。不知道時間怎麼過得這麼快，白天已經變成晚上。我沒戴手錶——我甚至不知道手錶在不在紙袋裡，有可能在今天的混亂中我的錶掉了，或被急救人員偷走了。應該已經過了九點半。

en_text: There’s a warm breeze. Clear sky. Perfect weather conditions for Santa, and if I were home with Sam, if I still had a family life, we’d watch TV together and watch Santa’s approach to New Zealand, her excitement building at the presents to come. I still haven’t got anything for her, but Nat and Diana took care of that, picking up and wrapping some gifts. The malls are closed and I’d like to have got her something myself. Jesus, I’m a bad father. How can I have not made an effort to pick her something up? Some toys, a doll, something to make her feel better. I’m focusing on revenge and not on the things that matter.
zh_text: 溫暖的微風吹來。天空非常清澈。很適合耶誕老公公送禮物的天氣，如果我跟小珊在家，如果我還有正常的家庭生活，我們會一起看電視，看著耶誕老公公來到紐西蘭，小珊想到即將送來的禮物，就愈來愈興奮。我什麼也沒買，但納森跟黛安娜準備了，買了禮物也包好了。購物中心已經關門了，不然我眞想自己去買禮物給她。天啊，我不是好爸爸。我怎麼連禮物都没準備？玩具也好，洋娃娃也好，能讓她比較好過的東西。我一心只想報仇，没想到其他重要的事情。

en_text: Revenge matters.
zh_text: 報仇很重要。

en_text: “You talk about defending the city like this is a war,” I say, staring out the windows as we drive through town where drunk teenagers are roaming the streets.
zh_text: 「你說過，要保衛這座城市，好像要打仗一樣。」我看著窗外的景觀，醉醺醺的青少年正在街上漫步。

en_text: “I could rant on about this city for the next five hours and it wouldn’t be anything you didn’t already know,” he says. “There are thousands and thousands who live here, ignorant of the violence that is seething in the soul of this city, until one day it reaches out and pulls them down. You probably knew about it because of your dad. But it wasn’t until last week that you really cared.”
zh_text: 「談到基督城，我可以花五個小時大叫大嚷，但内容你一定都聽過了，」他說。「這裡住了幾十萬人，渾然不覺暴力已經深入了城裡的土地，總有一天暴力會冒出頭來，把大家全部帶進地獄。或许因爲你父親的緣故，你早就知道了。但一直到了上星期，你才開始關心。」

en_text: “I always cared. No matter what you think, I hate my father for what he did. I hate him for this inheritance he left me.” We reach my in-laws’ street and approach the patch of ground where the man I ran over was shot and killed. There isn’t any crime scene tape up anywhere. They probably had to roll it up as quick as they could and use it somewhere else. There would have been media and cops all over the place, but now they’re gone, and there’s nothing here to suggest what happened this afternoon. It’s too dark to tell, but I’m sure the blood has been hosed away. I wonder if they picked the dead man up first, or his leg. I wonder how much a leg weighs.
zh_text: 「我一直都很關心。不管你怎麼想，我眞的很恨我爹做了那些事。我恨他把這些東西留給我。」車子開到我岳父母住的街道上，靠近今天的案發現場，我輾過的那人被槍殺了。黃色警戒線已經撤掉。警方或許得趕快把警戒線收起來，好拿到另一個犯罪現場去用。應該有很多媒體跟警察，但他們都走光了，下午發生的慘案早已抹得一乾二淨。天色太黑了看不到什麼，但我想血跡早就用水沖掉了吧。不知道他們先把死人抬起來，還是先撿他的腿。不知道一條腿有多重。

en_text: From the paper bag, a cell phone rings.
zh_text: 紙袋裡傳來手機的鈴聲。

en_text: Not my cell phone because I don’t recognize the ringtone.
zh_text: 不是我的手機，不是我熟悉的鋡聲。

en_text: “You gonna get that?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你要接嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: I unfold the top of the bag and reach inside. The phone I took from Kingsly is lit up.
zh_text: 我翻開紙袋的封口，把手伸進去。我從金斯理家拿來的手機亮起來了

en_text: “Hello?” I say, my heart thumping.
zh_text: 「喂？」我突然心跳如雷，轟然作響。

en_text:
“Listen carefully. You say one more word and I’m going to kill your little girl.”
“Who . . .”
zh_text:
「給我聽好了。你再說一個字，我就殺了你女兒。」
「你···」

en_text: “Shut up,” he says. “One more word and she’s dead. I’m not kidding around. Now, tell me yes if you understand.”
zh_text: 「閉嘴，」他說，「再一個字她就得死。我從不開玩笑。好，你聽懂的話就說『是』。」

en_text: My mind goes completely blank, then everything rushes at me from the darkness, the bank robbery, the bodies, my daughter . . . my daughter what? “Yes,” I say, the word hard to form through my dry mouth and I have to catch my breath. My hand is shaking and Schroder is too focused on driving to notice. He pulls in behind the cop car.
zh_text: 我的腦筋一片空白，然後一切又從黑暗中奔出來攤在我眼前，銀行搶案、屍體、我女兒……我女兒怎麼了？「是。」我費盡全力從乾燥的口中吐出這個字，然後屛息凝氣。我的手開始發抖，但施羅德開車開得很專心，沒有注意到。他把車子停在警車後面。

en_text: “Your girl, she’s ours now. We own her. And unless you do exactly as I say, you’ll never see her again. You get what I mean?”
zh_text: 「你女兒，在我們手上。她由我們擺布。除非我說什麼，你就做什麼，不然你再也看不到她了。懂我的意思嗎？」

en_text: “Yes,” I say. I break out in a sweat.
zh_text: 「是。」我已經出了一身冷汗。

en_text: “Good. Let me know when Schroder gets out of the car.”
zh_text: 「很好。施羅德下車後告訴我。」

en_text: “Wait here while I have a quick word with the officer,” Schroder says, mostly to himself because I’m not really listening to him. I nod.
zh_text: 「你先等一下，我跟警官講幾句話。」施羅德似乎在喃喃自語，因爲我也沒認眞聽。我點點頭。

en_text: “He’s gone,” I say.
zh_text: 「他下車了。」我說。

en_text: “In a moment he’s about to run into the house. I want you to go with him. When he reaches for his cell phone I want you to take it off him.”
zh_text: 「等一下他會跑進房子裡。我要你跟著他。等他拿手機出來，我要你把他的手機搶過來。」

en_text: “You understand I’m in police custody.”
zh_text: 「你知道我已經被警察拘留了。」

en_text: “Of course we know, we’ve been watching you all afternoon,” the voice says. “All the more incentive for you not to miss the right moment, Eddie. Don’t mess it up. You’ll get more instructions once you’re inside. Now go!” He hangs up as Schroder runs back toward me.
zh_text: 「我們當然知道，一整個下午我們都看著你，」那聲音說。「艾迪，你最好把握時機，别搞砸了。等你進屋後，我們會給你進一步的指示。去吧！」他掛了電話，這時施羅德回頭朝著我跑過來。

en_text: Jesus, it’s bad. Real bad. A dead officer out here and who knows how many dead people inside. Blood all over the inside of the patrol car. There should have been two cops watching tonight, hell, should have been four of them, but the budget didn’t allow for the man-hours required, and nobody wanted to pull that shift on Christmas Eve, and damn it, goddamn it, he should have done more because this officer’s blood is on his hands and so is the blood of anybody dead inside. His training tells him to wait for backup, but his instinct is to go inside, into the unknown. Either way, now he knows he has to as he sees Edward limping toward the front door.
zh_text: 天啊，糟糕，太糟糕了。外面死了一個警察，天曉得裡面死了幾個人。巡邏車裡滿是血跡。應該派兩個人來的，可惡，應該派四個人來，但預算無法支付他們需要的人力，也沒人願意在耶誕夜當班，可惡，太可惡了，他應該探取更多預防措施，現在這名警官算是他害死的，屋子裡若死了人也算在他頭上。受過的訓練要他等人來支援，但本能要他進屋裡去，面對未知的情况。不管怎樣，現在他知道他得進去了，因爲艾德華正朝著前面一跛一跛走來。

en_text: “Get back in the car,” Schroder yells, but Edward is ignoring him. He breaks into a run and grabs Edward at the front door.
zh_text: 「你給我回車裡去。」施羅德大吼，但艾德華不理他。他快步衝過去，在門前抓住了艾德華。

en_text: “Get back in the car!” Schroder orders again. He tries to lift his cell phone to his ear while keeping Edward under control. He gets the phone about halfway up when Edward spins around and grabs it out of his hand.
zh_text: 「上車！」施羅德再度下令。他一手制住艾德華，一手想把耳機舉到耳朵旁。手才舉到半，艾德華就轉身把他的手機搶走了。

en_text: “What the hell?” he says, but doesn’t say anything else before the phone is snapped in half and tossed onto the ground. “Jesus, Eddie, what the hell?” he asks, and he shoves him against the side of the house.
zh_text: 「幹！你在搞什麼？」他還沒來得及說下去，他的手機就被折成兩段摔在地上。「天啊，艾迪，你搞什麼屁？」他把艾德華往牆上一推，制住了他。

en_text: “Sam isn’t in there,” Edward says.
zh_text: 「小珊不在這裡。」艾德華說。

en_text: “How do you know that? We haven’t searched the house yet,” Schroder asks as he presses Edward against the front door. “How would you know that?”
zh_text: 「你怎麼知道？我們還沒進去搜呢。」施羅德邊問邊把艾德華壓在前門上。「你怎麼知道小珊不在？」

en_text: “They called me and told me. And they sounded impatient!”
zh_text: 「他們打電話來告訴我，而且口氣很不耐煩。」

en_text: “We need all the help we can get,” Schroder says. Something isn’t right, but he can see the fear in Edward’s eyes and knows he’s telling the truth.
zh_text: 「我們得先找所有人來支援。」施羅德說。有點不對勁，但他看得到艾德華眼中的恐懼，也知道他說的是實話。

en_text: He lets Edward go and opens the front door. All the lights are off. He goes inside and turns toward the living room. Edward follows him but there’s nobody else here. He keeps flicking light switches and nothing appears out of place.
zh_text: 他放開艾德華，打開前門。屋裡一片黑。他走進去，轉進客廳。艾德華跟在後面，但屋裡空無一人。他把燈一個個打開，到處看起來都很正常。

en_text: “The cop outside,” Edward asks. “Where is he?”
zh_text: 「外面那個警察，」艾德華問，「他怎麼了？」

en_text: “Dead,” Schroder says. “Why’d you break the cell phone? Who called you?” he asks.
zh_text: 「死了，」施羅德說。「你爲什麼要折斷我的手機？誰打電話給你？」

en_text: Edward doesn’t answer. Schroder opens the hallway door. The only light on down there is coming from the bathroom. “Stay behind me,” he says.
zh_text: 艾德華沒回答。施羅德開了走廊的門。唯一的燈光來自浴室。「跟在我後面。」

en_text: The bathtub is full of water. On the surface is a plastic tray, floating there, one corner nudged up against the side of the tub. On top of the tray is a brick of cash. Schroder steps into the bathroom and looks down at it, and he knows, he immediately knows he’s made a mistake, a very costly one, and before he can try to rectify it he hears a shotgun being primed.
zh_text: 浴缸裝滿了水。水面上有個塑膠托盤，浮在上面，一角靠著浴缸旁邊。上面擺了一疊厚厚的鈔票。施羅德走進浴室，低頭看著托盤，然後他明白了，他立即發現自己犯錯了，代價高昂的錯，根本沒時間修正，就聽到霰彈槍上膛的聲音。

en_text: Schroder doesn’t move. He keeps facing the bath and his face scrunches up, waiting for the gunshot. He wonders if he’ll outlive that blast by a few seconds and will get to see the front of his chest spraying across the tile wall. When nothing happens, he slowly raises his hands and turns around. A solid man with tattoos on his hands and a thick black jersey covering the ones that probably continue up his arms is pointing a shotgun that covers both him and Edward.
zh_text: 施羅德動也不動。他仍低頭看著浴缸，他的整張臉都皺起來了，等待開槍的聲音。不知道中槍後他還能活幾秒，能不能看到自己的血肉從胸口噴出來，灑在磁磚上。但一點動靜也沒有，他慢慢舉起雙手轉過身子。一名結實的男人用霰彈槍對著他跟艾德華，他雙手都有刺青，應該手臂上也有，但被他身上厚實的黑色緊身衣蓋住了。
