en_text: “What do you want?” Schroder asks. “Where’s my daughter?” Edward asks. “Where’s the money?” the gunman asks. “What?” Edward replies.
zh_text: 「你想要怎樣？」施羅德問。「我女兒呢？」艾德華問。「錢呢？」槍手問。「什麼？」艾德華回他。

en_text: “The money you stole last night.”
zh_text: 「你昨晚偷走的錢。」

en_text: “What are you talking about?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「你說什麼？」艾德華問。

en_text: “I’m talking about the cash you took from Kingsly.” “What?” Edward asks, and he sounds genuinely confused.
zh_text: 「我說你從金斯理家偷走的錢。」「什麼？」艾德華又問，口氣眞的很迷惑。

en_text: “Don’t bullshit me, boy. You answered the phone. Only way you could have got the phone was if you took it from Kingsly. So you took the money too. You return it, and we return your daughter.”
zh_text: 「喂，不要再給我裝傻。手機是你接的。你能拿到那支手機，一定是從金斯理家拿來的。所錢也是你拿的。把錢還來，我們就把女兒還你。」

en_text: “Wait, wait a moment,” Schroder says. “The money, we took the money into evidence this morning. Edward didn’t take it.”
zh_text: 「等等，等一下，」施羅德說。「錢？錢被我們帶到局裡當證物了，艾德華沒拿。」

en_text: “No. What you took was a couple of thousand dollars. I’m talking about the four hundred thousand.”
zh_text: 「不，你們只拿了兩千紐幣。我說的是四十萬。」

en_text: “Edward . . . ,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「艾德華···」施羅德說。

en_text: “I didn’t take it,” Edward says.
zh_text: 「我沒拿。」艾德華說。

en_text: “Turn around and get on your knees.” “Why?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「轉過去，跪下。」「爲什麼？」艾德華問。

en_text: “Not you. You, cop, get on your fucking knees and put your hands behind your head.”
zh_text: 「不是你。你，條子，給我他媽的跪下，雙手抱頭。」

en_text: “Look, we can . . .” “Now, asshole!”
zh_text: 「聽著，我們可以」「馬上給我跪下，王八蛋！」

en_text: It’s the last thing Schroder wants to do, but he can’t see an alternative. There’s no way he can jump forward and battle for the shotgun. That’s certain death. Turning around and putting his hands on his head suggests death, but at the moment it’s all he has. He turns around and kneels down.
zh_text: 施羅德滿心不情願，但別無他法。他不可能跳上前去搶那支霰彈槍。跳上去一定死。轉身，然後雙手抱頭，或许也會死，但當下只有這個選擇。他轉過身，跪了下去。

en_text: “Take his cuffs and use them on him.”
zh_text: 「把他的手鋳拿來，鋳住他。」

en_text: Edward reaches into Schroder’s pockets and finds the cuffs and latches them around Schroder’s wrists.
zh_text: 艾德華把手伸到施羅德的口袋裡，找到手銬，扣在施羅德的手腕上。

en_text: “Drown him.”
zh_text: 「淹死他。」

en_text: “What?” Edward says, and Schroder is thinking the same thing.
zh_text: 「什麼？」艾德華說，施羅德也想問同樣的問題。

en_text: “Put his head in the bath and drown him.” “Wait,” both Schroder and Edward say in unison.
zh_text: 「把他的頭壓到浴缸裡，淹死他。」「慢著，」施羅德和艾德華異口同聲地說。

en_text: “You heard me. Drown him or your daughter doesn’t see tomorrow.”
zh_text: 「你聽清楚了。淹死他，不然你女兒活不到明天。」

en_text: Schroder tries to get up but doesn’t get far before his chest hits the edge of the bathtub. All of Edward’s weight goes on top of him, pushing his face right down to the water.
zh_text: 施羅德想站起來，但胸口才超過浴缸邊緣就失敗了。艾德華把全身的重量壓在他身上，把他的臉按到水裡。

en_text: “I can’t,” Edward says.
zh_text: 「我辦不到。」艾德華說。

en_text: “Now. Do it. Do it now!” Tattoo Man says.
zh_text: 「现在，淹死他，立刻淹死他！」刺青男吼。

en_text: “I can’t.”
zh_text: 「我辦不到。」

en_text: “You can if you want to save your daughter.”
zh_text: 「你想救你女兒，你就辦得到。」

en_text: “Edward . . . ,” Schroder says, but he doesn’t know how to follow it up. There’s nothing. He knows what’s coming and he takes a deep breath.
zh_text: 「艾德華···」施羅德說，但他不知道自己要說什麼。沒什麼好說了。他想像得到接下來的情况，深吸了一口氣。

en_text: “I’m sorry,” Edward whispers before pushing his head into the water.
zh_text: 「我很抱歉。」艾德華輕聲說，然後把他的頭壓到水裡。

en_text: Schroder’s cuffed arms make it impossible for him to fight his way out, though he seems to think differently. If I were any lighter he’d probably make it too. His head bangs against the bottom of the tub and the water turns a very pale shade of red. I pull more of his body from outside the tub and stuff it under the water. I hold him by the back of his neck, pushing hard, his muscles tightening—it’s like holding down a mechanical bull. His feet thrash against the floor, the tips of his shoes draw black lines across the tiles. Water is splashing all up the walls and I’m already half soaked. The bandage on my hand is waterlogged and starts slipping off. I try to imagine that I’m drowning a dog, not a person—that mangy mutt from twenty years back—and imagining that actually helps, not much, but enough to stop me from letting him up. Schroder slows down. His feet stop hitting the floor. More of him slides into the tub.
zh_text: 雙手被銬住後，施羅德絕不可能掙扎得開，不過他仍掙扎個不停。如果我體重再輕一點，或許他就能成功了。他的頭重重敲在浴缸底部，水變成淺淺的紅色。我把他的身體往水裡推，想把他整個人塞到水裡。我抓住他的頸背，使盡力氣壓他，他的肌肉繃緊了就像玩馴服機械牛的遊戲。他的雙腳一直拍打地板，鞋尖在磁磚上畫下黑色的線條。水花噴在四面牆上，我已經半身濕透了。手上的繃帶吸飽了水，開始滑下來。我想像我要淹死一條狗，不是人二十年前那條討厭的雜種狗胡思亂想雖然沒什麼幫助，也足以讓我繼續用力壓著他。施羅德慢下來了。他的雙腳不再拍打地板，往浴缸裡滑得更深。

en_text: “Keep holding him.”
zh_text: 「不要放開他。」

en_text: I keep holding him. A couple of bubbles break the surface. Schroder’s legs stop moving but he’s still moving his head, still fighting, still desperate to survive. The seconds keep ticking away. Five more. Another five. The bubbles stop. There is one final shudder and then Schroder no longer struggles. I let go of him and he stays in the water, makes no effort to get up. I turn around. My hands are shaking and I drop to my knees and start to dry-retch.
zh_text: 我繼續壓著他。水面上浮出兩個泡泡。施羅德的兩條腿不動了，但頭還動來動去，繼續掙扎，繼續求生。時間一秒一秒過去。五秒，再五秒。泡泡消失了。施羅德抖了一下，然後停止掙扎。我放開他，他留在水裡，沒有想要起來的意思。我轉過身，雙手抖個不停，我跪了下來，開始乾嘔。

en_text: “No time for this shit,” the man says. “Get me the money.”
zh_text: 「別演了，」男人說，「把錢給我。」

en_text: I cough like I’m the one with lungs full of water. “Where, where are they? My, my daughter and in-laws?”
zh_text: 我咳得像我才是那個肺裡裝滿水的人。「他們，他們在哪裡？我丨我女兒跟我岳父岳母？」

en_text: “The money,” he says. “Then we talk.” “The money is here.”
zh_text: 「先給我錢，」他說，「再說別的。」「錢在這裡。」

en_text: “Where?”
zh_text: 「哪裡？」

en_text: One more cough and I’m done. I slowly get to my feet, holding on to the side of the bath, careful not to touch Schroder. The guy with the gun isn’t wearing a balaclava. He looks like he did this afternoon. He probably hasn’t changed his clothes, or his gun. I doubt he’s used it tonight because it’s too noisy. I bet the policeman outside was killed a different way. I wonder how badly he wants to avoid using it.
zh_text: 再咳一聲，我也咳完了。我慢慢扶著浴缸邊緣站起來，小心避開施羅德的身體。刺青男並沒有戴著頭罩。他跟今天下午看起來一模一樣。他應該沒有換衣服，帶的也是同一支槍。我不知道他晚上開了槍沒，因爲槍聲很響。我猜外面那個警察應該被他用其他的方法弄死。我心裡納悶，爲了避免發出槍聲，他一定很小心吧。

en_text: “You’ll kill me once you have it.”
zh_text: 「你拿到錢，就會殺了我。」

en_text: “You got this all wrong, boy. I am going to kill you. What you’re doing now is you’re buying your daughter’s life.”
zh_text: 「小子，你搞錯了。我會殺你。你現在只是拿錢買你女兒的命。」

en_text: “How do I know you’ll let her go?”
zh_text: 「我怎麼知道你會放了她？」

en_text: “She doesn’t know who we are. We got no reason to keep her. Now where’s the goddamn money?”
zh_text: 「她不知道我們是誰。我們沒有理由留著她。幹他媽的錢到底在哪裡？」

en_text: “Living room,” I say.
zh_text: 「起居室。」我說。

en_text: “Lead the way,” he says, and he backs out of the bathroom.
zh_text: 「你先走。」他說著，慢慢退出浴室。

en_text: I lead him down the hallway. We reach the living room. “At the end of the couch,” I say, “against the wall.”
zh_text: 我帶頭走下走廊，走到起居室外。「在沙發那一頭，」我說，「靠牆那邊。」

en_text: “Grab it.”
zh_text: 「拿出來。」

en_text: I reach down and grab the bag, trying to keep my injured leg as straight as I can. The bag is full of crayons and coloring pencils and some drawing books for Sam and is nowhere near big enough to hold all the money I saw last night. As usual it’s open. I zip it closed, pick it up, and toss it at his feet.
zh_text: 我伸手過去抓住袋子，盡量把受傷的腿伸直。袋子裡裝滿了蠟筆和色鉛筆，跟小珊的畫圖本，根本不夠裝我昨天看到的那些錢。袋口跟平常一樣拉開了。我拉上拉鍊，拿起袋子，丢在男人腳邊。

en_text: “What the . . . ?” he says, and he looks down at it and . . .
zh_text: 「什麼···？」他一低下頭···

en_text: Now. Now! Now!
zh_text: 現在。趁現在！就是現在！

en_text: We step forward, my monster and me, only this time I don’t even need him, I’m so mad. I swing my arm upwards, entering Tattoo Man’s line of sight from below, the pencil pointing straight up. He must see it coming, but he can’t avoid it, can’t even scream. He snaps his head upward as the pencil drives deep through his eye and, like a sneeze, thick, clear residue splashes all over my hand. He stands up as straight as a board. One hand releases the shotgun, which hangs by his other side for a moment before hitting the floor. He stays standing, staring at me, one eye bright and wide, the other a liquid mess with half a pencil behind it and half of that same pencil out in front. He doesn’t fall while I wipe the eye juice and blood off my hand; he saves it until I crouch down and grab the shotgun. He falls the way a dead man falls, without a care in the world, without any conviction or fear, his face hitting the armrest of the couch and driving the pencil home before snapping it off. He ends up on his side, a jagged finger of wood in his eye, looking at me but not watching as I race toward the bathroom.
zh_text: 我跟怪獸，我們往前衝，但這次我不需要他幫忙，我氣炸了。我手臂向上一揮，進入刺青男往下的視線，鉛筆筆直指向天花板。他一定看到了，但他避不開，連叫都沒叫。鉛筆深深刺入他的眼睛，他把頭向上一甩，感覺像他打了個噴嚏，濃稠無色的液體灑得我滿手都是。他的身子挺直，跟塊板子一樣。一隻手放開了霰彈槍，槍在他身體另一側掛了一下，然後才掉到地上。他仍站著，瞪著我，一隻眼睛瞪得大大的，另一隻則是亂糊糊的液體，外面有半支鉛筆，裡面也有半支鉛筆。我把他眼睛流出來的液體和血從手上擦掉，他仍然沒倒；等我蹲下去抓住霰彈槍，他才倒下去。他倒下的方法就跟死人一樣，不在乎外面的世界，沒有顧忌，沒有恐懼，他的臉撞到沙發的扶手，把鉛筆推得更深，然後露在外面的地方折斷了。他最後側躺在地上，眼中插了一條鋸歯狀的木頭，對著我，但看不到我，這時我立刻往浴室跑去。

en_text: What are you doing?
zh_text: 你在幹嘛？

en_text: I’m trying to save him.
zh_text: 我想救他。

en_text: Why?
zh_text: 爲什麼？

en_text: I need him alive.
zh_text: 我需要他幫我。

en_text: Why?
zh_text: 爲什麼？

en_text: Shut up.
zh_text: 閉嘴。

en_text: Only thing you should be doing right now is to enjoying the rush. God, that was a thing of beauty! Come on, Eddie, the way you drove that pencil home—sweet Jesus, that’s a real winner of a memory—a real keeper—much better than Fido. Bet you a hundred to one that’s the way your father felt when he took his knife and . . .
zh_text: 現在，你應該只要做一件事，就是好好享受興奮的感覺。天啊，多美啊！艾迪，你看看，你把鉛筆一口氣插進去的樣子我的上帝啊，那真是值得記憶的一刻——眞的很值得紀念，比那條笨狗有意思多了。我跟你賭，你老子拿刀殺人的時候百分之百也有同樣的感覺……

en_text: “I said shut up,” I say, then breathe more air into Schroder. His chest rises when I breathe in and drops when I take my mouth away. There is no pulse. His body is limp and heavy. I figure he’s been in the water three minutes tops.
zh_text: 「給我閉嘴。」我說，然後繼續對著施羅德吹氣。吹氣時他的胸口鼓起，移開嘴巴他的胸口就陷下。沒有脈搏，他軟綿綿的身体非常沉重。我猜他最多在水裡待了三分鐘。

en_text: I push at his chest. I’m not exactly sure what I’m doing. The last first-aid course I took was ten years ago and Schroder sure as hell feels a lot different from a dummy made of rubber and steel. I could be saving him, or I could be cracking his ribs and driving them into his lungs.
zh_text: 我壓壓他的胸口，其實我也不知道我在幹嘛。最近一次上急救課已經是十年前的事了，施羅德當然他媽的跟橡皮鋼筋做成的娃娃不一樣。我說不定能救他，說不定會把他的肋骨壓斷，插到他的肺裡。

en_text: I breathe into him. Compress his chest ten times. Should it be ten? Twelve? Breathe into him again. How long do I give this? He’s been dead close to four minutes. What’s the cutoff before there’s a serious risk of brain damage? Isn’t it around four minutes? Only thing I can remember about the first-aid course was the instructor. She kept looking at me as though I were the reason the dummy wasn’t breathing anymore.
zh_text: 我對著他吹氣，把他的胸口壓了十次。十次嗎？還是十二次呢？我又對著他吹氣。我該急救多久？他已經死了快四分鐘了。要過多久就會對腦部造成嚴重損傷？似乎就是四分鐘？我只記得急救課的講師，她一直往我這邊看，彷彿我就是娃娃停止呼吸的元兇。

en_text: Schroder convulses under me and a low roaring comes from his lungs. He begins coughing, his body almost doubling up. I roll him onto his side and he coughs out mouthful after mouthful of bathwater. Then he collapses onto his front, his forehead on his arm, breathing heavily into the floor, his body rising and falling seemingly more than need be as though he’s putting on a show. Other than the show, he doesn’t do anything else. Doesn’t jump up to see if he’s still in danger. Nothing. I’ve removed the handcuffs from one wrist, but they’re still dangling from the other.
zh_text: 躺著的施羅德開始抽搐，肺部發出低沉的吼聲。他開始咳嗽，身體幾乎折成兩半。我讓他側躺，他咳出一口又一口的洗澡水。然後他癱了下來，額頭壓在手臂上，對著地板重重地呼吸，身體一起伏的幅度有點誇張，似乎在作戲。除了作戲外，他什麼也沒做。沒有跳起來查看是否還有危險。没有。我已經把手銬從他一邊的手腕上除下來，但還掛在另一邊的手腕上。

en_text: “Hessus,” he mutters, but can’t add anything else.
zh_text: 「惱天啊，」他咕噥著說了三個字。

en_text: “Hessus woo . . . ,” he says, and raises a hand up to his face and cups his eyes. He coughs again, then tries to sit himself up and lean against the bath but can’t make it.
zh_text: 「惱天啊···」說著他舉起一隻手蒙住眼睛。他又開始咳，然後他想坐起來靠著浴缸，卻坐不起來。

en_text: “Come on,” I say, and help him. He pulls his knees up against his chest and rests his head on them. The bandage on my hand is loose. I pull it off and dump it on the floor.
zh_text: 「來吧。」我把他拉起來。他把膝蓋靠在胸口，把頭放上去。手上的繃帶鬆了，我乾脆扯下來丢在地上。

en_text: “Wash,” he says, and doesn’t elaborate for a few seconds, until “Wash hash,” and then he begins coughing again.
zh_text: 「啥麼，」他說，但也沒解釋什麼意思，然後他說了「啥麼哈麼」，又咳起來了。

en_text: “Wait here,” I say, and I leave him.
zh_text: 「等等。」我說，然後走出了浴室。

en_text: I check the bedrooms. It’s a three-bedroom house, built in the peak of the townhouse era and painted in showroom colors that are as boring as hell but managed to stay in style longer because of it. The first bedroom, the smallest of the three, has been set up for Sam. There’s a single bed and kit-set furniture and toys and posters and nobody fought for their life in there. The next bedroom has been turned into an office, with a desk and computer against one wall and a treadmill adjacent to the other.
zh_text: 我到臥房看了看。這間房子有三間臥室，建造在聯排住宅最流行的時候，内裝用了展示間無聊到爆的顏色，但正因無聊，所以能夠持久。第一間臥房最小，專門給小珊用。裡面有張單人床、組合家具、玩具和海報，沒有人在這裡爲生死而搏鬥。第二間房改成書房，書桌和電腦靠著一面牆，另一面牆邊則放了跑步機。

en_text: It leaves one room unchecked, and I walk into it praying that it’ll be empty. I open the door. The air is warm and stale and feels like the room has been unearthed from the back of a very deep cave. Nat and Diana are both lying on the floor, their eyes wide open, staring right at me. I move over to them and crouch down and Nat lifts his head but can’t do much more because he’s been hog-tied, and so has Diana. I rush back down to the kitchen and grab a knife and a moment later they’re free and rubbing their wrists.
zh_text: 只剩一間房了，走過去的時候我希望裡面也是空的。開了門，房間裡的空氣溫暖沉悶，彷彿這個房間剛從很深的洞裡挖出來。納森和黛安娜都躺在地上，他們雙目圓睜，一起瞪著我。我蹲下身子，納森抬起頭來，但他的身體卻動彈不得，因爲雙手雙腳都被綁在一起，黛安娜也一樣。我衝到廚房拿了一把刀，馬上把他們放開，他們不住搓揉手腕。

en_text: “Jesus, Eddie, what’s going on?” Nat asks. “Where’s Sam?” “I don’t know. I think they have her.”
zh_text: 「天啊，艾迪，發生了什麼事？」納森問。「小珊呢？」「我不知道。他們把她帶走了。」

en_text: “They have her? Who? Who has her?”
zh_text: 「他們把她帶走了？誰？誰把她帶走了？」

en_text: “I don’t know. The men from the bank, I think.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。我猜是搶銀行的那些人。」

en_text: “The ones who killed Jodie? Why the hell would they take Sam?” “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「害死茱蒂的人？他們在搞什麼？爲什麼要帶走小珊？」

en_text: “You don’t know?” he repeats, getting louder now. “You don’t know? What the hell does that mean? You must know! You have to know!” “I’m going to get her back.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」「你不知道？」他重複我的話，聲音也提高了。「你不知道？那是什麼意思？你應該要知道！你一定要知道！」「我會把她找回來。」

en_text: “Oh, I know you will. For your sake. I’m pretty convinced you brought these men into our house. What have you done, Eddie?”
zh_text: 「噢，我知道你會把她找回來。爲你自己。我覺得一定是你把這些人帶來我們家。艾迪，你做了什麼蠢事？」

en_text: “I haven’t done a goddamn thing,” I say.
zh_text: 「我什麼他媽的也没做。」我說。

en_text: “They think you did,” Diana is sobbing now. “And now they’ve taken our little Sam.”
zh_text: 「他們認爲是你，」黛安娜開始啜泣。「現在他們把我們的小珊抓走了。」

en_text: “If you’ve caused this, Eddie, if something happens to her,” Nat says, “I swear I’ll kill you. I will goddamn kill you.”
zh_text: 「艾迪，如果貞是你，如果她出了什麼事，」納森說。「我發誓我會把你殺了。我絕對要宰了你。」

en_text: I go back into the bathroom. Schroder doesn’t have the strength to be angry or thankful. “You drowned me,” he says.
zh_text: 我回到浴室。虛弱的施羅德不生氣，也不感激我。「你想把我淹死。」他說。

en_text: “I saved you.”
zh_text: 「我救了你一命。」

en_text: “You drowned me.”
zh_text: 「你想把我淹死。」

en_text: “I had no choice. If I hadn’t, he’d have shot you. We’d both be dead. Now, listen, you—”
zh_text: 「我別無選擇。要是我不淹死你，他會用槍射死你。我們兩個都會死。好，聽著，你···」

en_text: “You drowned me,” he repeats.
zh_text: 「你想把我淹死。」他說來說去只有那一句。

en_text: With Nat’s help, we get him to his feet, lead him into the dining room, and sit him down. My leg is bleeding and I try taking the weight off it as we walk. “You need to focus here,” I say on the way. “This isn’t about you. It’s about my daughter.”
zh_text: 在納森的協助下，我們讓他站起來，把他扶到餐廳裡坐下。我的腿開始流血，走路時只好把重心放在左腿上。「你得好好想一想。」我邊走邊說。「這跟你無關。要緊的是我女兒。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “You owe me, okay? You owe me your goddamn life. Tell me you understand that. Don’t make me throw you back in the water. You owe me because if you’d done your job and caught the people responsible none of this would have happened. If you’d put more than one goddamn man on duty my daughter would still be here.”
zh_text: 「你欠我一個情，對不對？你的命是我救回來的。告訴我你聽懂了。不然我就把你丢回水裡。你欠我，因爲你有失職守，沒抓到搶匪，不然這一切就不會發生了。如果你他媽的多派一個人來保護我女兒，我女兒就不會不見了。」

en_text: “Where is he? The man with the gun?” “I took care of him.”
zh_text: 「他呢？那個拿槍的人？」「我把他處理掉了。」

en_text: “Same way you’ve been taking care of everybody else?”
zh_text: 「用你處理其他人的方法嗎？」

en_text: “Not quite,” I say. “The guy I ran over, that was an accident.”
zh_text: 「不一樣，」我說。「那個被我輾過的人，那是意外。」

en_text: “Jesus, Eddie, what’s going on?” Nat asks. “Do you know where Sam is?” “And Kingsly?” Schroder asks. “Was he an accident too?”
zh_text: 「天啊，艾迪，發生了什麼事？」納森問。「你知道小珊在哪裡嗎？」「金斯理呢？」施羅德問。「也是意外嗎？」

en_text: “I was never there.”
zh_text: 「我沒去過他家。」

en_text: “He said you had Kingsly’s cell phone. Plus you knew his name.”
zh_text: 「他說你拿了金斯理的手機。而且你也知道金斯理的名字。」

en_text: “There was a cell phone in the stolen car,” I say, feeling nothing at how seamless the lies are coming now. “One of the paramedics must have thought it was mine and put it with my stuff. I didn’t even know it was there.”
zh_text: 「他們偷來的車子裡有一支手機。」我說，謊言似乎變得天衣無縫，但我毫無愧意。「急救人員一定以爲是我的，就跟我的東西放在一起。我原本不知道紙袋裡有手機。」

en_text: He nods. “Okay, Edward, fine, we’ll go with that for now.”
zh_text: 他點點頭。「好，艾德華，很好，就這麼說吧。」

en_text: “Maybe the man who tried killing us is the one who killed Kingsly.” “I’m not following any of this,” Nat says. “Where’s Sam?”
zh_text: 「或許那個想殺我們的男人殺了金斯理。」「我一個字也聽不懂，」納森說。「小珊在哪裡？」

en_text: “Yeah, maybe. But he’d have taken the money with him, right?” Schroder answers.
zh_text: 「對，或许吧。但他應該會把錢拿走，不是嗎？」施羅德答道。

en_text: “I don’t have any money. If I did I’d have given it to him to get my daughter back.”
zh_text: 「我沒拿錢。如果我拿了，我會還給他，換回我女兒。」

en_text: “Now that I really do believe.”
zh_text: 「這我倒毫無異議。」

en_text: Nat helps me check through the rest of the house in case Sam’s hidden here somewhere, in a cupboard or under a bed. He takes one look at the dead guy on the floor and doesn’t say a word. I check the playhouse outside —it’s empty. It’s what the men have been telling me—they have her, and I have to pay to get her back. In the living room Diana is taking care of Schroder. She’s brought him some dry clothes and probably offered to make him coffee in the way that anybody over sixty always has to offer something, no matter what the situation. Schroder’s taken the other cuff off his wrist.
zh_text: 納森幫我在屋裡搜了一遍，確定小珊沒藏在櫥櫃裡或床底下。他看了那死人一眼，沒說什麼。我搜了外面的遊戲屋——空的。眞跟那些人說的一樣——他們把小珊帶走了，我得付錢把她換回來。黛安娜在餐廳裡照顧施羅德。她拿了一些乾衣服給他，或許也提議要給他一杯咖啡，六十歲以上的人不論碰到什麼情況，總會發揮無比的善意。施羅德把手銬拿了下來。

en_text: “We have to go,” I say.
zh_text: 「我們該走了。」我說。

en_text: “We need to call for backup.”
zh_text: 「我們得請求支援。」

en_text: “We have to get the hell out of here first.” I grab him by the collar and help him to his feet. “They have Sam. We have to do what it takes to get her back. Come on, you’ve got to help me.”
zh_text: 「我們得先滾出這棟房子。」我抓住他的衣頜，把他拉起來。「他們把小珊抓走了。我們得盡全力把她救回來。來吧，你得幫我。」

en_text: “You all need to get out of here,” Schroder says to my in-laws.
zh_text: 「你們最好不要住在這裡。」施羅德對我的岳父岳母說。

en_text: “To hell with what you want,” Nat says, “we’re helping you find Sam.” “No, no you’re not,” I say. “You’ll only get in the way.”
zh_text: 「你講的屁話我都不聽，」納森說，「我們要幫你們找到小珊。」

en_text: “Settle down,” Schroder says. “Nobody is doing anything here except me. I’m calling for backup, and you’re going to let the police take care of it.”
zh_text: 「不用，你們不用來，」我說。「你們只會礙手礙腳。」「都給我坐下，」施羅德說。「除了我以外，你們都不用動手。我會找人來支援，你們讓警方處理就好。」

en_text: “The same way you’ve taken care of finding the men who killed my daughter?” Diana asks.
zh_text: 「我女兒被殺了，也是由你們處理，同樣的方法嗎？」黛安娜問。

en_text: “Look, we’re doing—”
zh_text: 「聽著，我們一定會···」

en_text: “What you can,” Nat finishes. “To hell with that.”
zh_text: 「盡力而爲，」納森接嘴說。「去死吧。」

en_text: “So what, you and your wife are going to come along, is that what you think?”
zh_text: 「那要怎樣？你跟你老婆也要來，你們是這個意思？」

en_text: “I’d like to,” Nat says, “but I know my limitations. That’s important in a man; and one thing we’ve learned since Jodie got shot is your limitations, Detective. This is why you’re taking Eddie. He got us into this mess, and he knows what it takes to get us out of it. Like it or not, Detective, he’s certainly done more to find these men than you ever have, and if he’s responsible for what happened here, then I’ll deal with him when this is over. But right now I have more faith in him finding my granddaughter than you. Call for backup. We’ll deal with whoever you send here and help in any way we can, but right now you and Eddie need to get your asses out there and find Sam.”
zh_text: 「我想幫忙，」納森說，「但我知道我老了。一定要知道你的極限在哪裡，自從茱蒂被殺，我們也知道你們的極限在哪裡。所以你要把艾迪帶走。他害我們陷入這一團糟，而他也知道怎麼幫我們脫身。探長，他能找到這些人，付出的努力絕對超過你們，要是他得負責今天在我家發生的事情，事後我會親自教訓他。但現在要找到我的外孫女，我對他比對你們更有信心。找人來支援。人來了，我們會應付，能幫什麼就幫什麼，但現在，你跟艾迪快滾吧，快出去找小珊。」

en_text: “You know he’s right,” I say, looking away from Nat to Schroder.
zh_text: 「你知道他說得對。」我的視線從納森轉到施羅德身上。

en_text: “Okay, okay, fine. Where’s the man who did this?”
zh_text: 「OK，OK，好吧。那個男人呢？」

en_text: I lead him into the living room. A pool of blood has formed around the guy’s head. He’s ended up lying on top of the bag of pencils and crayons.
zh_text: 我帶他到起居室裡。那個人頭旁邊已經有一灘血了，最後他倒在裝了鉛筆和蠟筆的袋子上。

en_text: Nat and Diana stand in the doorway. “That’s one of them,” Nat says.
zh_text: 納森和黛安娜站在走廊上。「那是其中一個人。」納森說。

en_text: “And the other?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「另一個呢？」施羅德問。

en_text: “The other one took Sam,” Nat says. “Not much more I can tell you. I mean, he looked kind of like this one. Shaved head, tattoos—we can try to describe him. I’m pretty sure, if things had gone differently, he was going to kill us. I don’t know why he hadn’t already.”
zh_text: 「另一個人把小珊帶走了。」納森說。「我沒什麼好說的。我的意思是，他看起來跟另一個人很像。頭剃光了，有刺青——我們可以指認他。我想，要是情況有變，他會把我們殺了。我不知道爲什麼他要留我們活口。」

en_text: “We’ll get some mug shots for you to go through,” Schroder says. He steps closer to the body and I roll it so he can see it better. For a moment I wonder how many dead bodies this man has seen. Plenty, I guess. Certainly many more than my father ever saw.
zh_text: 「我們會拿一些嫌犯照片給你們看。」施羅德說。他走近屍體，我把那人翻過來，好讓他看得更清楚。有一刻我突然在想，這人不知道看過多少具屍體。一定很多吧，我猜。起碼比我爹看過的還多。

en_text: “Oh my God,” Diana says, when she sees the stub of the pencil. “Eddie . . . I didn’t think you could, that you were . . . capable . . . ,” her voice tails off.
zh_text: 「噢，我的老天啊，」黛安娜看到那截鉛筆時開口了，「艾迪……我從來沒想過你能，你……可以……」她的聲音愈來愈小。

en_text: “These bastards took my daughter!” I say, glaring at her. “You’d rather I let him shoot me? You’d rather have let him drown Schroder, then come down and shoot you and Nat? Let Sam die too?”
zh_text: 「那些狗養的抓走了我女兒！」我對她怒目而視。「妳寧可讓他殺了我嗎？妳寧可讓他淹死施羅德，然後再用槍打死妳跟納森？也讓小珊死掉？」

en_text: Nobody answers. Nat nods once, understanding, maybe for the first time seeing I’m doing what I can to get us through this alive. All of us.
zh_text: 沒有人答腔。納森點了一下頭，似乎懂了，或許他終於明白我正竭盡全力讓大家都能度過這個難關。我們所有人。

en_text: “You recognize him?” I ask Schroder.
zh_text: 「你認得他嗎？」我問施羅德。

en_text:
“No, I . . . wait.” He crouches down over the body, then reaches for my hand when he wobbles. He coughs again, trace amounts of bathwater spattering on the dead guy. “He doesn’t look familiar,” he says when he’s composed himself.
“He has to.”
zh_text:
「不認得……等等。」他蹲到屍體旁邊，站起來時搖搖晃晃，必須扶著我的手。他又咳了幾聲，少許洗澡水濺在死人身上。「我似乎沒看過他。」他很快又恢復沉著。
「應該認得吧。」

en_text: “He doesn’t. I’ll call it in. The fingerprints, we’ll have a hit on them by now.”
zh_text: 「沒見過這個人。我會報告給局裡。指紋的話，現在應該找到資料了。」

en_text: “Then what? You compile a list of names and spend a week making a case? We need to act tonight.”
zh_text: 「然後呢？你又列出一堆名字，花一個星期成立案件？我們馬上就得行動。」

en_text: “I know, I know,” he says. “Look, let me think, just give me a minute.” “We don’t have time.”
zh_text: 「我知道，我知道，」他說。「聽我說，讓我想一想，給我一分鐘就夠了。」「沒時間了。」

en_text: “Who phoned you?” he asks, “when we were outside?” “They did.”
zh_text: 「剛才我們在外面的時候，」他問，「誰打電話給你？」「他們打的。」

en_text: “And they told you to take my phone off me.” “They said they’d hurt Sam if I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「然後他們告訴你要把我的手機搶走。」「他們說我要不照做，小珊就完蛋了。」

en_text: He looks down at the dead man.
zh_text: 他低頭看看死人。

en_text: “Call them back. Tell them you’ll give it to them in exchange for Sam.” “What?”
zh_text: 「回撥給他們。告诉他們，你會用錢換回小珊。」

en_text: “He was asking you for money you don’t have. The rest of the crew are waiting for him to show up with it. But he’s not going to. What value does your daughter have then?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」「他要你給他錢，而你沒有錢。其他人在等他把錢帶回去。但他不會拿到錢。那你女兒到時候對他們來講也沒有用了，對不對？」

en_text: “And tell them what?” “Tell them you have it.”
zh_text: 「要跟他們說什麼？」「說錢在你手上。」

en_text: It doesn’t seem the best of ideas, but it’s the only one. I go through the cell phone menu and find the recent calls. My fingers are shaking as I select the number then press CALL. It rings a couple of times, and then someone picks up.
zh_text: 似乎不是最完美的構想，但也沒有其他辦法了。我打開手機的功能表，找到最近的來話。選定電話號碼，按下撥號，我的手指抖個不停。響了兩聲後，接通了。

en_text: “I have the money,” I say, my grip tight on the phone.
zh_text: 「我願意給你錢。」我緊緊抓著手機。

en_text: “Where’s my man?” “He had an accident.”
zh_text: 「我的手下呢？」

en_text: “So you think now you can buy your daughter back by dealing directly with me?”
zh_text: 「他出了一點意外。」「所以你覺得你可以直接跟我談，把你女兒買回去？」

en_text: “Yes.”
“It’s too late,” he says. “Your daughter is about to have an accident too.”
zh_text: 「太遲了，」他說。「你女兒也會馬上碰到意外。」

en_text: He hangs up. Nat is standing with his arm around Diana. They’re both looking lost, like they don’t recognize me, don’t recognize the house. Schroder is changing his shirt. “What happened?” he asks.
zh_text: 他把電話掛了。納森站在黛安娜旁邊，用手臂環著她。兩人的表情都很迷惘，彷佛認不得我是誰，認不出自己在誰家裡。施羅德正準備換上乾衣服。「怎麼了？」他問。

en_text: I don’t answer him. I stare at the phone as the rage inside me builds. I don’t even know what I just heard.
zh_text: 我沒回答。我瞪著那支手機，内心的怒火愈燃愈烈。剛才那個人說的似乎是外星話，我聽不懂。

en_text: “Eddie? What the hell did he say?” Nat asks.
zh_text: 「艾迪？他到底說了什麼？」納森問。

en_text: “He . . . he said it was, was too late,” I say.
zh_text: 「他……他說，他說太遲了。」我回答。

en_text: Diana gasps and Nat tightens his grip on her. Without even being aware I’m about to do it, I kick the dead guy on the floor, over and over.
zh_text: 黛安娜倒抽了一口氣，納森抓緊了她的肩膀。我開始對著地上的死人亂踢，渾然不覺我把怒氣都發洩在他身上。

en_text: “Edward, calm down, just calm down a moment,” Schroder says, putting his arms out in a consoling gesture, one arm threaded through a sleeve, the other one bare. “These men are professionals. They know what they’re doing. They know if they kill her there’s no money in it for them. Give them a minute. They’ll call back.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，冷静點，先冷静一下，」施羅德展開雙臂，想要表達安撫的意味，他的一隻手臂穿進了袖子，另一隻還露在外面。「他們是職業罪犯，懂得怎麼犯罪。他們知道，要是殺了小珊，就拿不到錢了。先等一分鐘。他們會打回來。」

en_text: “And if you’re wrong?” “Give it a minute,” he says.
zh_text: 「要是你錯了呢？」「等一分鐘。」他說。

en_text: “A minute, maybe two,” Nat says. “They’ll call back. They always call back,” he says, but Nat has no point of reference other than what he’s seen on TV; he’s trying to convince himself as much as the rest of us.
zh_text: 「一分鐘，或许兩分鐘，」納森說，「他們會再打來。」但納森知道的，也都是從電視上看來的；他只想說服自己，同時說服我們。

en_text: I kick the dead guy once more. His head rolls left and right, the pencil wedged in so tight it doesn’t even wobble.
zh_text: 我又踼了死人一腳。他的頭左右滾動，鉛筆卡得很緊，一點也沒晃動。

en_text: “I’m going to be sick,” Diana says and rushes off to the bathroom. Nat stays in the living room for about five seconds before following her. A minute goes by. Then another.
zh_text: 「我要吐了。」黛安娜往浴室衝去。納森在起居室等了五秒鐘，然後跟著她過去。過了一分鐘。然後再一分鐘。

en_text: “You were wrong,” I say.
zh_text: 「你錯了。」我說。

en_text: “Give it time.”
zh_text: 「再等一下。」

en_text: “I’m going to kill these people,” I say, and that’s true too. Schroder doesn’t respond. He’s probably thinking it’s time to try and get some handcuffs on me. But he’s also thinking that these guys tried to kill him, and he knows he owes me one.
zh_text: 「我要把這些人都宰了。」我不是在開玩笑。施羅德沒答話。或許他想，是時候了，該幫我上手銬。但他也想到，那些人想殺了他，而我救了他一命。

en_text: “Look, Edward, you have to stop kidding yourself here. This isn’t something you can deal with.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽我說，不要再自欺欺人了。你沒辦法處理現在的局面。」

en_text: “I’m doing okay so far.”
zh_text: 「到目前爲止，我都還能應付。」

en_text: “Yeah? Tell that to your in-laws. Tell that to the dead officer outside. After everything you’ve said about being nothing like your father, you’ve got blood on your hands now.”
zh_text: 「是嗎？你把這句話告訴你的岳父岳母。告訴外面那個死掉的警察。你一直說你跟你的父親完全不一樣，而你手上也已經沾滿了鮮血。」

en_text: We’re blood men—that’s what Dad said.
zh_text: 我們是嗜血之人——爹說的。

en_text: “I didn’t do a damn thing,” I say, but he’s right. I got my wife killed by speaking out. The police officer outside is dead because of me. All this blood on my hands, some of it innocent, and I know I’m still not done.
zh_text: 「我他媽的什麼也沒做。」但他說對了。我想要主持正義，卻害我妻子被殺。外面那個警察也因我而死。我雙手沾滿了鮮血，包括無辜之人的血，而我明白，我仍覺得不滿足。

en_text: The cell phone rings. My in-laws appear as if they’d been waiting around the corner. I answer it.
zh_text: 手機響了。岳父岳母立刻出現，彷佛已在外面等候多時。我接起電話。

en_text: “I killed a cop for you,” I say, before the caller has a chance to say a word. “I’ve killed two of your men already. This can all end. I’ll bring you the money and you give me back my daughter.”
zh_text: 「我幫你殺了一個條子。」我搶在那人之前先開口了。「我殺了兩個你的手下。就這麼扯平吧。我把錢帶給你，你把女兒還我。」

en_text: There’s a pause on the line. “She’s still alive. For now,” the man says. “An even trade. One hour. Come alone. If we see anybody else we’ll kill her.”
zh_text: 電話那頭沉寂了幾秒。「她還沒死，現在還活著，」他說。「公平交易。一個小時。你一個人來。如果看到別人，我們就殺了她。」

en_text: “Where?”
zh_text: 「去哪裡？」

en_text: “I’ll call you at the time. Don’t want you having a chance to set something up.”
zh_text: 「時間到了我會打給你，免得你有機可乘。」

en_text: He hangs up and I explain it to Schroder, who is about as happy as Nat and Diana—who look like the world has fallen apart around them.
zh_text: 他掛了電話，我說給施羅德聽，他高興的程度跟納森和黛安娜不相上下——似乎周遭的世界已經垮了。

en_text: “You can’t do this alone, Edward. We need backup,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「你不能一個人去，艾德華。我們需要支援。」施羅德說。

en_text: “They’ll kill her if you make that call. I’m playing this safe, and that means paying for her. You owe me.”
zh_text: 「如果你通知警察局，小珊就死定了。我必须很小心，而且要付錢給對方。你欠我一個人情。」

en_text: “He’s right,” Nat says to Schroder. “Give them the money and we get Sam back. It’s like Eddie said, it’s that simple.”
zh_text: 「他說得沒錯，」納森對施羅德說。「給他們錢，换回小珊。就像艾迪說的，很簡單。」

en_text: “Except it’s not that simple,” I say, “because there is no money.”
zh_text: 「其實不簡單，」我說，「因爲沒有錢。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “This money they’re asking about, I don’t have it. If I was there, if I had the money, I’d be using it to get my daughter back. Can the police department raise the cash?” I ask Schroder.
zh_text: 「他們在問的那筆錢，不在我這裡。如果我去過那裡，如果我把錢拿走，我會用錢把我女兒換回來。警察局可以幫忙籌錢嗎？」我問施羅德。

en_text: “The department wouldn’t go for it,” he says.
zh_text: 「局裡不會同意。」他說。

en_text: “Even if it meant saving Sam’s life?”
zh_text: 「連爲了救小珊的命也不行？」

en_text: “It doesn’t work that way. If it did, people would be getting kidnapped all the time. We’d be throwing cash at every criminal in the city.”
zh_text: 「沒那麼簡單。要能讓警察局出錢，綁架事件就會層出不窮。我們不能拿錢砸城裡的所有罪犯。」

en_text: “What about the damn bank?” Nat asks. “This is all happening because of what happened there. Surely they’d give us the money. They have to! They owe us—they bloody well owe us!”
zh_text: 「那天殺的銀行呢？」納森問。「現在演變到這種局面，都是因爲銀行被搶了。他們應該要給我們錢。應該的！他們欠我們那群王八蛋欠我們欠大了！」

en_text: “I’ll make a couple of calls and see what I can do.”
zh_text: 「我先打幾個電話，看看能怎麼辦。」

en_text: “If Eddie doesn’t have the money, then who does?” Nat asks.
zh_text: 「錢不在艾迪這裡，那在誰那裡？」納森問。

en_text: “Maybe there wasn’t any money,” Schroder says, and I think of the bricks of cash lying on Kingsly’s bed.
zh_text: 「說不定根本沒有錢。」施羅德說，而我想起金斯理床下的大疊鈔票。

en_text: “There has to be,” I say. “It’s too much effort for them to go to if there wasn’t.”
zh_text: 「一定有，」我說。「他們大費周章，怎麼可能沒錢。」

en_text: “So who took it?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「那誰拿走了？」施羅德問。

en_text: “What about the probation officer? You said he found the body, right?” I say.
zh_text: 「觀護人呢？你說他發現了屍體，對不對？」我說。

en_text: “Yeah, he found the body, but you’re making a dangerous assumption here. He’s not a suspect in the killing. He has no motive to kill his client.”
zh_text: 「對，他發現了屍體，但你的假設很危險。他不是殺人嫌疑犯。他沒有動機要殺死自己的客戶。」

en_text: “That’s my point. He wasn’t a suspect, but he could have taken the money.”
zh_text: 「我的意思是，他不是嫌犯，但他可能把錢拿走了。」

en_text: “No, the killer would have taken the money.”
zh_text: 「不對，殺人兇手把錢拿走了。」

en_text: “Maybe Kingsly was killed for an entirely different reason. Maybe the killer didn’t see the money.”
zh_text: 「或许金斯理被殺，並不是因爲錢在他那裡。或许殺手沒看到那些錢。」

en_text: “Something you want to share, Edward?”
zh_text: 「艾德華，你有秘密要告訴我嗎？」

en_text: “We can spend the next hour here making guesses,” I say, “but at the moment the probation officer is the only thing we have.” I reach down and pick up the dead man’s shotgun. “Let’s take a drive.”
zh_text: 「我們可以花一個小時玩猜謎遊戲，」我說，「但現在唯一的線索指向他的觀護人。」我彎下身子，撿起死人的霰彈槍。「出門兜個風吧。」

en_text: Schroder’s chest is burning and it’s tight and he swears there’s still water in there. Still, all things considered, he’s much better off now than he was twenty minutes ago. When he gets more time he’ll think about those moments between when he stopped breathing and when he started up again. He’s never been a religious person, but that hasn’t stopped him from hoping there’s something when all of this is over, maybe not a heaven in the traditional sense, but something close to it. If there is, he didn’t get to see it, or even glimpse it. For him there was nothing. No memory—not even a memory of darkness. Or a memory of nothing. That’s all there was. Drowning, and then not drowning anymore. Whoever said drowning was a peaceful death had no idea what they were talking about.
zh_text: 施羅德的胸口又緊又痛，他認爲裡面還有水沒吐出來。不過，整體來說，比二十分鐘前好多。等到有空間，他會回想從停止呼吸後到恢復呼吸的這段時間。他向來不信鬼神，但他仍希望當一切結束時，會看到某樣東西，或許不是一般人心目中的天堂，只是類似的地方。要眞有的話，他什麼也沒看到，瞄都沒瞄到。啥也沒有。沒有回憶——甚至不記得自己是否看到了一片黑暗。也不記得是否什麼也沒有。就那樣了。溺死在水裡，然後失去了溺水的感覺。有人說過溺水這種死法很平靜，他一定不知道自己在說什麼廢話。

en_text: He follows Edward to the car. He can’t stop coughing. He walks slightly off balance like a man with an inner-ear infection—or like a man who has been brought back from the dead.
zh_text: 他跟著艾德華走向車子。還是咳個沒完，走路的姿勢歪歪斜斜，就像內耳感染了細菌一也像個剛剛死裡逃生的人。

en_text: Edward’s car is still parked outside, and they take it since it doesn’t resemble an unmarked police cruiser. But first Edward grabs the paper bag out of Schroder’s car. Inside it are two sets of car keys and a wallet and another cell phone. They go past the patrol car with the dead officer inside. Partly it’s his fault what happened; Edward was right about that—if he’d pressed those in charge to get more people watching Edward’s daughter, maybe this could have been avoided. His notebook is wet but he’s able to get the probation officer’s name out of it, along with an address.
zh_text: 艾德華的车子仍停在外面，他們決定開他的車，因爲這台車不像沒有標示的警車。但艾德華先到施羅德的車裡把紙袋拿出來。裡面有兩組車鑰匙，一個皮夾，另一支手機。他們走過警察死在裡面的巡邏車。他的確該負責任；艾德華說得沒錯如果他強迫上面的人多撥一些人力來看著艾德華的女兒，或許就不會發生這些事情了。他的筆記本濕了，但他仍能找到觀護人的名字和地址。

en_text: Edward drives because Schroder isn’t up to it. The only thing he really wants to do is curl up in the backseat and fall asleep. Nat gave him his cell phone, and he uses it to call Landry. He explains as much of the situation as he feels like explaining—not telling him where they’re heading—and listens as Landry updates him.
zh_text: 艾德華開車，因爲施羅德不想開，他只想窩在後座好好睡一覺。納森把手機借給他，他撥了藍德里的電話。该說的他都說了，不過他沒說他們要去哪裡一然後換藍德里向他報告最新的狀況。

en_text: “Theodore Tate has been trying to get hold of you,” Landry says. “Where’s your cell?”
zh_text: 「泰奧多·泰特找你好幾次了。」藍德里說。「你的手機呢？」

en_text: “Lost it. He leave a number?”
zh_text: 「不見了。他有沒有留電話號碼？」

en_text: “He said he’d keep calling back every twenty minutes. Warden gave him permission to use the phone. He can reach you on the number you’re calling from?”
zh_text: 「他說他會每隔二十分鐘就再打一次。典獄長准許他打電話。他打這個號碼就能找到你嗎？」

en_text: “Okay. Text me the number for the warden’s office and I’ll call.” He hangs up.
zh_text: 「OK。用簡訊把典獄長辦公室的電話傳給我，我打過去。」他掛上手機。

en_text: “You going to call the bank manager?” Edward asks.
zh_text: 「你要打電話給銀行經理嗎？」艾德華問。

en_text: “No.”
“You said before that—”
zh_text: 「你剛剛說···」

en_text: “I know what I said, and that was only to keep your in-laws happy. There’s no point in calling the bank. They won’t play ball. If I thought there was any chance at all that they’d help—no matter how small—I’d call them. Shit, this is a goddamn mess,” he says, more to himself than to Edward. “And I’m doing the wrong thing right now.”
zh_text: 「我知道我剛才說了什麼，我只是想讓你岳父母不要擔心。打電話給銀行沒用。他們不會配合。要我認爲有一絲絲希望他們肯幫忙——不論希望多麼渺茫——我都會打去。操！實在亂透了！」他不理艾德華，對著自己咒罵。「現在我要跟你去做蠢事了。」

en_text: “You’re doing the right thing,” Edward says. “Anything else and my daughter is dead. We’re doing what it takes to get her back.” “Within reason,” he says.
zh_text: 「你做了正確的決定，」艾德華說。「一念之差，我女兒就沒命了。我們要盡全力救她回來。」「也不能做不合理的事。」他說。

en_text: Edward doesn’t answer.
zh_text: 艾德華沒回答。

en_text: “They matched the prints from the car,” Schroder says. “We got two names—and I’m pretty sure they’ll match the two dead men you’ve left behind.”
zh_text: 「他們比對了車上的指紋，」施羅德說。「比出了兩個名字——我確定跟那兩個被你宰掉的人吻合。」

en_text: “You know who they work with?”
zh_text: 「你知道他們跟誰一夥的？」

en_text: “They’ve worked with lots of people. We’re making progress. It’s only a matter of time until we have more names.”
zh_text: 「他們跟很多人一夥。我們有進展了。假以時日，一定能調查出更多嫌犯。」

en_text: “A matter of time. How much time? Five minutes? Five hours? Five days?”
zh_text: 「假以時日。要等多久？五分鐘？五小時？五天？」

en_text: The cell phone beeps. Landry’s text has come through with the number for the warden’s office. “Look, Edward, if I didn’t get your point I wouldn’t be here right now.”
zh_text: 手機嗶了一聲。藍德里傳來典獄長辦公室的電話號碼。「聽我說，艾德華，如果我不明白你的想法，我現在就不會坐在你的車子裡了。」

en_text: He dials the number and it rings a couple of times before it’s answered by the warden. The warden doesn’t seem thrilled by the fact he’s still at the prison when he should be at home, but he doesn’t give Schroder too much grief about it.
zh_text: 他撥了電話，響了兩聲後，典獄長接起來了。應該在家的時候卻還在監獄裡，他聽起來意興闌珊，倒沒有因爲這個緣故就給施羅德罪受。

en_text: “He’s here,” the warden says, and Schroder can hear the phone being put down on the desk and then picked back up.
zh_text: 「他在這裡。」典獄長說，施羅德聽到話筒放在桌上的聲音，然後又被拿起來了。

en_text: “Roger Harwick,” Tate says, getting right to the point.
zh_text: 「羅傑·哈威克。」泰特一點也不拖泥帶水。

en_text: “Roger . . . Hardwick?”
zh_text: 「羅傑···哈德威克？」

en_text: “Harwick. No ‘d.’ ”
zh_text: 「哈威克，沒有德。」

en_text: “How do I know that name?”
zh_text: 「我認識他嗎？」

en_text: “Everybody knows that name. You couldn’t have missed it. He was all over the news this year. He was a small-time newspaper columnist convicted of molesting teenage boys.”
zh_text: 「他很出名。你不可能沒聽過。今年他常上頭版。他在報上寫些不成氣候的專欄，因爲猥藝青少年被判罪。」

en_text: “Oh yeah,” he says, remembering how much joy it gave the media, ripping one of their own apart.
zh_text: 「哦，是他。」他想起媒體如何不遺餘力地圍剿他們的圈內人。

en_text: “He’s served three months of a ten-year stretch. He’s been nothing but a sperm bank for everybody around him since he got his teeth knocked out his first night in the joint. I think he got offered protection to kill Hunter.”
zh_text: 「他被判十年徒刑，才入獄三個月。進了這個狗洞的第一天，他的牙齒就被打掉了，他周圍的人如果想打炮，就拿他當精子銀行。我猜他寧可殺了杭特，來換取保護。」「是誰下令要殺他？」

en_text: “Any ideas who ordered the attempt?” “I can keep asking around.”
zh_text: 「我再問問看。」

en_text: “Yeah. I appreciate it,” he says, and hangs up.
zh_text: 「好，感谢你的帮忙。」他把電話掛了。

en_text: “That was the prison you just rang, right?” Edward asks. “That about my father?”
zh_text: 「你剛打去監獄？」艾德華問。「跟我父親有關係？」「對，有一個嫌疑犯。」

en_text: “Yeah. We got a name.” “That Harwick guy?” “Yeah.”
zh_text: 「那個哈威克？」

en_text: “So you can spare resources to spend time at the jail, but you couldn’t spare them to look after my daughter? Is that what you’re telling me?”
zh_text: 「對。」「所以，你能派人在監獄裡調查，卻不能派人保護好我女兒？你敢否認嗎？」

en_text: “We’re going to find her,” Schroder says. “And no, we’ve got somebody on the inside working the angles.”
zh_text: 「我們會把她找回來，」施羅德說，「你猜錯了。我們找了個犯人來幫忙。」

en_text: “What, you mean your friend you were telling me about who got arrested for drinking and driving? The ex-cop?”
zh_text: 「什麼？你跟我說過那個酒醉駕車的朋友？以前是警察那個？」

en_text: “He’s reliable.”
zh_text: 「他很可靠。」

en_text: “Who is he?”
zh_text: 「他是誰？」

en_text: “It doesn’t matter who he is,” Schroder says, “what’s important is what he learned.”
zh_text: 「他是誰沒有關係，」施羅德說，「重點是他學到了教訓。」

en_text: “I heard you talking with the warden this afternoon. I heard you mention a name. Tate. I recognized it. And the detective you spoke to a few minutes ago, I heard him mention it. He’s the guy you’ve been telling me about, right? Your buddy? Theodore Tate? The guy who got drunk and hurt somebody? Got people killed? He was in the news a lot last year. This the guy?”
zh_text: 「今天下午，我聽到你跟典獄長講話。你說了一個名字。泰特。我聽過這個名字。幾分鐘前跟你通電話的警探，我聽到他提了這個名字。他就是你拿來警告我的例子，對不對？你的好朋友？泰奧多·泰特？那個酒醉駕車出了意外的人？他害死了好幾個人？去年他常上報。就是這個人？」

en_text: “It doesn’t matter who it is,” Schroder says, dismissing the line of questioning.
zh_text: 「他是誰沒關係。」施羅德不理他一連串的質疑。

en_text: “So why’d Harwick do it?”
zh_text: 「哈威克爲什麼要殺我爹？」

en_text: “He was offered protection to do it. A murder like that this early on, Harwick would only get time served concurrently, maybe an extra year, but it increased his chances of living.”
zh_text: 「殺了你爹，就有人保護他。他才剛入獄就殺人，頂多多個罪名，或許多一年刑期，但他的日子就不會過得太慘。」

en_text: The probation officer’s name is Austin Bracken. When they reach his house Schroder tells Edward to park up the driveway, but instead Edward pulls up two houses past.
zh_text: 觀護人名叫奧斯汀·布萊肯。到了他家，施羅德要艾德華把車停在車道上，但艾德華卻停到隔了兩棟房子遠的地方。

en_text: “What the hell?”
zh_text: 「搞什麼鬼？」

en_text: “Just being cautious,” Edward answers, grabbing the shotgun.
zh_text: 「小心點總沒錯。」艾德華邊回答邊抓起霰彈槍。

en_text:
“You won’t need that,” Schroder says, thinking that Edward looks more hopeful than cautious.
“You don’t know that.”
zh_text:
「你不需要拿槍。」施羅德覺得艾德華似乎滿心期待，跟小心扯不上關係。
「你怎麼知道不需要。」

en_text: “We don’t know if he stole the money, and even if he did, this isn’t somebody looking for you. We question him, see what he knows, and if he has the money we take it. Then we do things both your way and my way—you get to deliver the money, but we call it in and get backup first—it’s safer for both you and your daughter.”
zh_text: 「我們不知道錢是不是他偷的，就算他偷了，他也不是追殺你的人。我們先問他，看他知道什麼，如果錢被他偷了，我們把錢拿走。然後照你的方法進行，但也要照我的方法你把錢拿去給綁匪，但我們先通知局裡，請求支援你跟你女兒的安全才更有保障。」

en_text: “He isn’t going to give up the money if he has it. What the hell are you expecting? Knock on the door and he’ll hand it over to you?”
zh_text: 「如果他偷了錢，他才不會給我們。你想得太美了吧？敲敲門，他就把錢給你？」

en_text: “Something like that,” Schroder says fully aware that he doesn’t sound convincing. They’ll talk to Bracken, and if he gets a bad vibe he’ll call for backup. He’s not taking any more chances tonight.
zh_text: 「就是那樣。」施羅德當然知道自己的話很沒說服力。他們要質問布萊肯，如果他覺得不對勁，就找人過來支援。今晚他可不要再冒險了。

en_text: “He deals with scumbags every day of his life,” Edward says. “You think you can break a person like that just by talking to him on his doorstep?”
zh_text: 「他每天都接觸作奸犯科的人，」艾德華說，「你以爲跟他在門口聊幾句，他就會聽你的？」

en_text: “And you think pulling a shotgun on an innocent man will help? Let’s get a read on him first and take it from there.”
zh_text: 「你以爲拿霰彈槍對著一個無辜的人就有幫助嗎？先看看他怎麼說，再臨機應變。」

en_text: When they walk up to the front door, Schroder is still out of it, like he’s walking through a world slightly out of sync. He knocks on the door and there’s movement and voices and Schroder knocks again to hurry them up. A few seconds later a man answers the door, his shirt open and the large belt buckle on his pants hanging loose. He’s around Schroder’s age, but bigger. He has that slab look about him, the not-quite-fat-and-not-quite- muscle look. He has a handlebar mustache that’s about a hundred years out of date.
zh_text: 他們走向布萊肯的家門，施羅德還是覺得怪怪的，彷彿他正穿過一個略微脫了節拍的世界。他敲敲門，聽到裡面有人走過來，也聽到說話聲，施羅德又敲了幾下，催促他快來開門。幾秒後一個男人把門打開了，他的襯衫敵開，褲子上的大皮帶釦也鬆開來了。他年紀跟施羅德差不多，只是個子更高。看起來不怎麼乾淨俐落，不肥胖，但也沒有肌肉，留了一撮很老派的八字鬍。

en_text: “What the hell?” he asks, as soon as he sees them.
zh_text: 「你們搞屁啊？」看到兩人，他劈頭就問。

en_text: Schroder holds up his ID. The badge has dried out but the wallet is still wet. Bracken doesn’t look at it, just stares at Schroder, and then at Edward, and Schroder is pretty sure he knows who each of them is.
zh_text: 施羅德舉起警徽。識別證乾了，但皮套還濕漉漉的。布萊肯對他的警徽沒興趣，瞪著施羅德看了幾秒，又瞪著艾德華，施羅德心想，他一定知道誰是誰。

en_text: “We have a couple of questions,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我們有事要問你。」施羅德說。

en_text: “At this time of night?”
zh_text: 「這麼晚有什麼好問？」

en_text: “You’re lucky we didn’t show up at two in the morning.” “Questions about what?”
zh_text: 「算你好運，現在還不是凌晨兩點。」「要問什麼？」

en_text: “Some routine stuff about Shane Kingsly.” “Like what?”
zh_text: 「跟夏恩·金斯理有關，稀鬆平常的問題。」「比方說什麼問題？」

en_text: “Background.”
zh_text: 「基本資料。」

en_text: “And you had to come to my house at this time of the night?” “We’re chasing some leads.”
zh_text: 「得在這麼晚的時候跑到我家來問？」「我們正在追查一些線索。」

en_text: “With him?” he asks, and nods at Edward.
zh_text: 「跟他一起？」他對著艾德華點點頭。

en_text: “Can we come in?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「我們可以進去嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: “I’m busy.”
zh_text: 「我沒空。」

en_text: “It’s important.”
zh_text: 「這件事很重要。」

en_text: “It’s Christmas Eve,” he says. “I don’t care if it’s important or not.” “Actually . . . ,” Schroder begins, but Edward interrupts him.
zh_text: 「今天是耶誕夜，」他說，「重不重要我都不管。」「事實上——」施羅德才開口，就被艾德華打斷了。

en_text: “Shit,” Edward says. Both men look at him. “My phone,” he says, patting down his pockets. “It’s in the car. I know how to solve this.”
zh_text: 「靠！」艾德華說，另外兩人都看著他。「手機，」他拍拍口袋，「在車子裡。我知道該怎麼辦了。」

en_text: “What?” Bracken says. “Edward . . . ,” Schroder says. “Just a second,” Edward says. “Edward, wait,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「什麼？」布萊肯說。「艾德華···」施羅德說。「等一下，」艾德華說。「艾德華，等等，」施羅德說。

en_text: “It’s important,” Edward answers, and Schroder watches him walk away for a few seconds before turning back to Bracken. His head is muggy and his thoughts are muddled, and he knows he’s probably making a mistake right now but he can’t seem to focus exactly on what that is. Edward saved his life before; and that aside, Schroder knows if he’d been better at his job, then Edward’s daughter never would have been taken tonight. Whatever happens to her will be on his conscience. So yeah, maybe he does owe Hunter some slack. He knows he does—it’s why he’s here. It’s why he hasn’t turned on Edward and tried to handcuff him.
zh_text: 「很重要，」艾德華回答，施羅德看著他走掉，幾秒後又轉頭對著布萊肯。他的頭很悶，腦子一團糊塗，他知道自己可能犯了大錯，卻無法確切指出是什麼樣的錯誤。艾德華救了他的命，此外，施羅德也知道，要是他更盡責一點，艾德華的女兒就不會被綁架了。不管她發生什麼事，他的良心都會受到譴責。對，沒錯，或許他眞的欠杭特一個人情。他知道，所以他才會來。這就是爲什麼他還沒回頭制伏艾德華，幫他戴上手銬。

en_text: Question is, how much slack is he prepared to give him?
zh_text: 問題在於，他要容許他亂搞到什麼程度？

en_text: Austin Bracken lives in a neighborhood the virus hasn’t hit yet. The houses are modern and well looked after and don’t have front yards made up from rusting mechanical parts. The dashboard clock on the car says we’re closing in on 10:30; it seems like the day has been about forty hours long. Most of the houses still have lights on inside them, people probably closing in on bedtime, watching the tail end of prime-time TV, waiting for the kids to have been asleep long enough so they can play Santa’s role and put the presents under the tree. It’s what I should be doing with Jodie. It’s such a magical moment and I don’t know if there’ll ever be any more.
zh_text: 奧斯汀·布萊肯住在還沒被病毒入侵的區域。現代化的屋舍都得到良好照料，前院也沒堆满生鏽的機械零件。車子儀表板上的時鐘告訴我，快十點半了；今天感覺似乎有四十個小時那麼長。大多數屋子裡的燈還亮著，裡面的人應該都準備好要睡覺了吧，黃金時段的電視節目就要結束，他們等孩子睡熟了，便可以扮演耶誕老人的角色，把禮物放在樹下。我應該跟茱蒂在家等小珊睡熟，然後去放禮物。這個時刻對我而言有無比的魔力，而我不知道是否還有機會體驗同樣的感覺。

en_text: I could tell in two seconds Bracken had the money. I didn’t even need the monster to help me out on that one. But Schroder couldn’t even get his foot in the door. I grab the shotgun because we don’t have time to play nice. We’re meeting the people who have my daughter in about forty minutes and I have nothing to exchange for her. I carry the gun behind my back, nice and easy, the same way I’d hide a bouquet of flowers. I bring it into view and Bracken’s eyes widen and Schroder sees his reaction and turns to face me, but he doesn’t turn quick enough to avoid what happens. I crash the butt of the shotgun into Schroder’s head, not as hard as the security guard got hit, but hard enough to make it count. His head rocks to the side and his eyes roll back and he drops real fast.
zh_text: 一看到布萊肯，我就知道他把錢拿走了。甚至不需要怪獸來幫我找出答案。但施羅德連他家的門檻都無法越過。我抓起霰彈槍，沒時間好聲好氣求他了。再過大約四十分鐘，就要跟把我女兒綁走的壞人碰面，我不能連贖款也沒有。我把槍藏在身後，藏得好好的，就像把要給茱蒂驚喜的花束藏起來。我秀出霰彈槍時，布萊肯瞪大了眼睛，他的表情讓施羅德回頭看我怎麼了，但他轉身的速度不夠快，無法阻止我。我用槍托對著施羅德的頭狠狠一敲，不像銀行警衛下巴那記那麼重，但也夠他受了。他的頭往旁邊一歪，翻起白眼，咚一聲倒在地上。

en_text: Bracken takes a few steps back as I take a few steps forward. Schroder stays slumped on the ground, doing what Schroder seems to be doing best lately.
zh_text: 布萊肯向後退了幾步，我則步步進逼。施羅德像團爛泥般倒在地上，這似乎是他最新的招牌動作。

en_text: “What do you want?” Bracken asks.
zh_text: 「你想怎樣？」布萊肯問。

en_text: “The money.”
zh_text: 「把錢給我。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “The money you stole. I’m here for it.” “What the hell are you talking about?”
zh_text: 「你偷走的錢。我要那些錢。」「你到底在說什麼？」

en_text: We get into the hallway and I kick back and close the door. It’s a pretty nice house with a wide hall and modern furniture, and the outside looks nice, nice plants, nice paint job, garden gnomes in the garden and a policeman planted on the doorstep, not a Christmas decoration in sight. Bracken keeps moving down the hallway. I keep following.
zh_text: 我們進了他家，我向後一踢，把門關上。他家挺漂亮，門廳很寬敵，配上現代的家具，外面也很不錯，種了漂亮的植物，油漆刷得很好，花園裡放了地精，門口還倒了個警察，不過放眼望去看不到任何耶誕擺飾。布萊肯一直後退，我則一直前進。

en_text: “You stole money from Kingsly,” I say. “Probably around four hundred thousand dollars,” I say. “Maybe more, maybe less.”
zh_text: 「你偷走了金斯理的錢，」我說。「大概四十萬紐幣吧。或許超過四十萬，或許不到四十萬。」

en_text: “No I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「我沒偷。」

en_text: “Yes. You did.”
zh_text: 「有，你偷走了。」

en_text: “What are you on about? If he had money, why’d you think I’d take it? And how’d you even know what he had unless . . .” His expression changes, as if he’s figuring it out, but it changes too much, as if it’s an act. Something here isn’t quite right but I don’t know what.
zh_text: 「你想怎樣？要是他有錢，爲什麼你認爲被我偷走了？你怎麼知道他有錢？除非···」他的臉色大變，彷彿猜到了答案，但變得太快了，看起來反而很假。這裡有點不對勁，但我說不上來是什麼。

en_text: “You killed him,” he says, and something in the way he says it makes me think he already knew that. Not just thought it, or suspected it, but actually knew it, like he was there.
zh_text: 「你殺了他。」他說話的方式讓我覺得他早就知道了。不光是想到，不光是心裡懷疑，而是早就知道了，彷彿他也在現場。

en_text: “The money,” I say. “Take me to it.” “I don’t have any money.”
zh_text: 「錢，」我說，「帶我去拿。」「我沒有錢。」

en_text: “The people that money belongs to have my daughter. They’re going to kill her unless I get it back for them.”
zh_text: 「搶走那些錢的人把我女兒抓走了。除非我幫他們把錢拿回去，不然他們會殺了我女兒。」

en_text: “Like I said, I don’t have any money.”
zh_text: 「我說了，我沒拿錢。」

en_text: Listen to him—he’s lying. If he was truly sorry he’d tell you where that money is. He’d act more sympathetic. He’d tell you that if he could help, he would.
zh_text: 聽他這什麼口氣——他騙你。他要是眞覺得愧疚，就會告訴你錢在哪裡。他也會表現得更有同情心。他會告訴你，如果可以幫得上忙，他很樂意伸出援手。

en_text: “I think it’s time you left,” Bracken says.
zh_text: 「我想你該走了。」布萊肯說。

en_text: “They’re going to kill her.”
zh_text: 「他們會殺了我女兒。」

en_text: “And I’m sorry about that, I truly am.”
zh_text: 「我很抱歉，真的很遗憾。」

en_text: He truly isn’t.
zh_text: 他真的無感。

en_text: “Somebody else must have taken it,” he carries on. “Somebody either before or after, I don’t know, all I know is I don’t have it.”
zh_text: 「一定是別人拿走了，」他接著說下去。「可能在我之前，或在我之後到了他家，我不知道。我只知道錢不在我這裡。」

en_text: He’s lying. “You’re lying.” “It’s the truth.” He’s lying.
zh_text: 他騙你。「你騙我。」「我說的是實話。」他還在說謊。

en_text: “Okay, then,” I say. “Any ideas who?” “What?”
zh_text: 「好吧，」我說，「那你知道有可能是誰嗎？」「什麼？」

en_text: “You were his probation officer. Who else did he work with?” “I don’t know. I’d have to check.”
zh_text: 「你是他的觀護人。他還跟誰往來？」「我不知道。我得查一下。」

en_text: “The police didn’t ask you this already?”
zh_text: 「警察還沒問過你嗎？」

en_text: “I don’t know. Yeah, I guess so.” “And?”
zh_text: 「我不知道。可能問過了。」

en_text: “And what? I gave them a bunch of names they already knew and it was a waste of time.”
zh_text: 「那是誰？」「有什麼人？我給了一些名字，他們早就知道了，根本是浪費時間。」

en_text: “Okay. Okay. Who else is here?” “What?”
zh_text: 「OK，OK。還有誰在這裡？」「什麼？」

en_text: “In this house. Who else is here?” “I don’t know. Just some woman.” “Show me.”
zh_text: 「這屋子裡。還有誰在這裡？」「我哪知道，就有個女人吧。」「給我看看。」

en_text: He leads me to a bedroom where a woman with large breasts and very big hair is finishing off getting dressed.
zh_text: 他頜我走進一間臥房，裡面有個大胸部蓬頭髮的女人，剛把衣服穿上。

en_text: “I promise you this is the last goddamn time, you son of a bitch,” she says, straightening up her skirt which is torn up the side. When Bracken doesn’t answer, she looks up and sees first me and then the shotgun, and the anger washes out of her face, just like that, in about half a second, and gets replaced with a big amount of fear. Her eyes are puffy and mascara has run down her face, making her look like a Goth.
zh_text: 「我告訴你，王八蛋，這絕對是他媽的最後一次了。」她低著頭，拉平了被撕裂的裙子。沒聽到布萊肯答話，她抬頭一看，才看到我，然後看到霰彈槍，臉上的怒氣一掃而空，眞的不到半秒鐘表情就變了，變得驚恐無比。她的眼睛浮腫，睫毛膏流到臉上，有股哥德風。

en_text: “What the . . . ,” she says, but she runs out of words.
zh_text: 「什麼···」她說了兩個字就接不下去了。

en_text: “Shut up,” Bracken says to her, and then I make him do exactly that by banging him on the head with the gun as hard as I hit Schroder. He goes down about as hard and looks like he’ll be staying down for about as long.
zh_text: 「閉嘴。」布萊肯命令她，但我先讓他閉嘴了，霰彈槍敲下去，就跟剛才對付施羅德的方法一樣。他跟施羅德一樣重重倒下，看來也會昏迷同樣久的時間。

en_text: “Please, don’t hurt me,” the woman begs. “I didn’t even want to be here.”
zh_text: 「拜託，別打我，」女人對著我哀求，「我根本不想來這裡。」

en_text: She’s wearing a really short skirt and high-heel shoes and must keep her yearly calorie intake at under a thousand. “You wanna earn some cash?” I ask.
zh_text: 她的裙子短得要命，鞋跟高得驚人，一年吃下肚的熱量應該不超過一千卡。「妳想賺點錢嗎？」我問她。

en_text: She doesn’t even think about it. “Does it involve hurting him?” she asks, and nods down at Bracken.
zh_text: 她不假思索地問：「要對付他嗎？」同時對著地上的布萊肯抬抬下巴。「行嗎？」

en_text: “That a problem for you?” “You can save your cash, sugar,” she says, the fear gone now. “This I’ll do for free.”
zh_text: 「不用給我錢，帥哥，」她的恐懼消失了，「老娘願意免費服務。」

en_text: “Then we better get started,” I say.
zh_text: 「那就立刻上工吧。」我說。

en_text: Torture is all about balance, and more often than not, proves to be an extremely ineffective way of getting information. It comes down to pain thresholds: inflict too much pain and the victim will end up saying anything to make it stop. Problem with that is it makes the information unreliable. Don’t inflict enough pain and they’ll continue to resist. Inflict way too much and the body shuts down. I think it comes down more to fear than pain. I have under thirty minutes to create as much fear in Bracken as I can before it’s too late.
zh_text: 拷問的藝術在於精準拿捏，想要從別人身上拷問出什麼，屢見不鮮的結果是什麼也沒有。重點在於對方的耐痛程度：太痛，他爲了怕痛，什麼鬼話都說得出來，但是這種情況下得到的資訊很不可靠。不夠痛，他就一直頑強抵抗。痛翻了，他就暈過去了。我認爲，關鍵在於恐懼，而不是疼痛。我只有不到三十分鐘的時間，要用盡方法撩起布萊肯的恐懼，讓他愈怕愈好。

en_text: I don’t know why I suddenly seem to know so much about torture. It’s as if a section of my mind has been unlocked, a hidden vault of knowledge opening its contents up to me. The monster has something to do with it. I think to myself, this entire ordeal could be more Disney-oriented if I gave the monster a name—Mickey. Mickey is telling me how to torture a man. Mickey is begging me to kill him. But Mickey isn’t in control here—not yet anyway.
zh_text: 不知道爲什麼，我突然變成拷問專家。彷彿我的腦子裡有些東西被禁錮已久，藏滿了資訊的寶庫終於開啓，對我展現其中的寶藏。一定跟怪獸有關。我心想，如果我給怪獸取名叫作米奇，這場嚴刑拷打就開始走迪士尼風了。米奇告訴我該怎麼拷問這個人。米奇求我殺了他。但現在不由米奇作主還不到時候。

en_text: Bracken is starting to come to, and he’s noticing that his entire world has changed in the last few minutes. He’s resuming transmission and finding himself naked and tied to a chair. He’s shaking and he’s cold and scared. On the dining table there are two tools: a steak tenderizer from his kitchen drawer that looks like a wooden mallet, and a very large chef’s knife. The knife has a stained handle and is worn, the blade is chipped near the end but still very sharp.
zh_text: 布萊肯快醒了，他也注意到才過了幾分鐘，他的世界就變了。他的傳動系統恢復，發現自己赤裸裸地被綁在椅子上。他抖個不停，因爲他很冷很害怕。餐桌上有兩項工具：從他廚房裡拿來的牛排錘，看起來像根木槌，一把巨大的主廚刀。刀子已經磨損了，把手也很髒，靠近刀尖的地方也有缺口，但依然很鋒利。

en_text: I feel nothing.
zh_text: 我非常冷静。

en_text: Good. You’re coming along nicely.
zh_text: 很好。你進步很快。

en_text: Detective Inspector Schroder hasn’t resumed transmission yet, so maybe he took a harder knock—or it’s an accumulative thing for him, having been drowned an hour ago. When he wakes up he’ll find he’s been dragged inside and propped up against the living-room wall with a clear view of the show, his hands cuffed behind him and his feet bound in front of him. There’s a gag in his mouth because, truth is, I’m sick of hearing him talk.
zh_text: 施羅德探長的傳動系統尚未恢復，所以，或许他頭上那記比較重一或许一個小時前浸在水裡那段時間所造成的損害讓他受到的一擊雪上加霜。等他醒來，他會發現自己被拖進屋子裡，靠布，因爲，說老實話，他一直教訓我，讓我很厭煩。

en_text: The woman, who may or may not be a prostitute but who probably is, is also in the living room. Bracken blinks a few times, bringing his new world into focus. He sees the steak tenderizer and the knife and his imagination is conjuring up his future.
zh_text: 那說像妓女又不像妓女、或許眞是妓女的女人也在客廳裡。布萊肯眨了幾下眼睛，看清楚眼前的新世界。他看到牛排錘，看到刀子，腦海中立刻浮現出自己的未來。

en_text: “Where’s the money?”
zh_text: 「錢在哪裡？」

en_text: His first impulse is anger. “Go to hell,” he says, and I jam a dish towel in his mouth and swing the tenderizer as hard as I can into his knee. Something in there gives, and he lurches forward with so much force the chair jumps off the ground and nearly tips over. His leg can’t kick forward because it’s bound to the chair. His face turns red and then almost purple as tears stream from his eyes. He bites down so hard the dish towel is the only thing stopping his teeth from snapping off against each other. I give him two minutes to thrash around uselessly on the chair until he gets himself back under control.
zh_text: 他出現了第一個反應——懫怒。「去死吧。」他說，我把一條擦碗布塞到他嘴裡，用盡力氣把牛排錘對著他的膝蓋甩過去。有個東西塌陷了，他向前一顛，力量大到椅子從地上跳了起來，差點翻倒。他的腿被綁在椅子上，所以踢不起來。他滿臉通紅，紅色又幾乎轉成紫色，眼中淌下了淚水。他用力一咬，要是嘴裡沒塞擦碗布，牙齒可能都要咬斷了。我給他兩分鐘的時間在椅子上徒勞無功地翻騰，最後他停止了扭動。

en_text: The woman says nothing, just keeps on watching, all quiet now, maybe not so sure now about helping me out.
zh_text: 女人不發一語，只是盯著我們看，非常安靜，或許有點後悔答應了要幫我。

en_text: I pull the gag out.
zh_text: 我把擦碗布扯出來。

en_text: “I’ve never figured out why they start with this kind of bullshit in the movies,” I say. “All this torture foreplay. I’ve always thought I could do better. Thing is, I’ve always been a simple man with simple pleasures. That’s all. I had the most beautiful woman in the world as my wife, we have an amazing daughter together . . . and the things that made my dad who he was never touched me. But in those movies where guys like me torture guys like you, they never cross the line. They break bones and cut skin, and the guys they’re torturing always seem to stand up to it. I figure there are two ways to make a man talk. You either go through his eyes or you go through his dick.” I pick up the knife. “I’m gonna start with the latter, so you can still watch.”
zh_text: 「以前看電影的時候，都不懂爲什麼有人要折磨別人，好無趣，」我說，「用拷打鋪陳情節。我一直以爲我能表現得更好。注意了，我本來很單純，我的樂趣也很單純。就這樣。我有世上最漂亮的女人當我妻子，我們生了一個最最最可愛的女兒……我爹幹了什麼，跟我毫不相干。但在電影裡，像我這樣的好人折磨你這樣的壤人時，他們絕不會越線，被折磨的壤人總能挺得住。我想，要讓你開口，只有兩個方法。挖眼睛，或切老二。」我拿起刀子。「我先把你的老二切掉好了，你還可以好好觀賞。」

en_text: “Wait,” he says.
zh_text: 「慢著。」他說。

en_text: “Too late,” I say.
zh_text: 「來不及了。」我說。

en_text: I move the knife to his groin. His red face suddenly goes pale. “My bedroom. In the closet,” he says, the knife above his dick. “Under the manhole in the floor in the wardrobe. The money is in there. Take it. It’s yours.”
zh_text: 我把刀子對著他兩腿之間移過去。他漲紅的臉突然變得慘白。「在我房間，衣櫃裡，」他說，刀子在他的陽具上方停下了。「衣櫃底部有個蓋子。錢在裡面。拿去吧，都是你的了。」

en_text: I put the gag back into his mouth before handing the knife and tenderizer to the woman, who looks at them as if they contain the Ebola virus. Then she takes them. She hefts them in her hands and gets a feel for the weight. “What am I supposed to do with these?”
zh_text: 我把擦碗布塞回他嘴裡，把刀子跟牛排錘交給女人，她瞪著這兩樣工具，彷彿上面有伊波拉病毒。然後她接過去了，在手上掂掂有多重。「拿著要幹嘛？」

en_text: “If he moves, then do what makes you happy.” “No problem,” she says.
zh_text: 「他要敢亂動，就隨妳處置。」

en_text: I head into Bracken’s bedroom and open the wardrobe door. There aren’t many clothes hanging in there, and most of what is there are all dark pieces, a size too big for me. I push them to one side, the hangers grating across the iron bar. There are shoes on the floor and a couple of cardboard boxes. I kick them out, exposing the floor. I get down on my knees. The stitches pull at the wound in my leg; I feel a couple of them pull through. I drag back the piece of carpet. There’s a manhole cover with a hole drilled into it for me to hook my finger through. It leaves a gap one man could fit through, but not two.
zh_text: 「沒問題。」她說。我走進布萊肯的臥房，拉開了衣櫃門。裡面沒掛幾件衣服，大多是深色，比我穿的大了一碼。我把衣服推到一邊，衣架摩擦鐵桿，發出刺耳的聲音。下方放了鞋子和兩個紙盒。我把所有東西踢出來，露出衣櫃底面。我跪到地上，腿上的縫線拉扯著傷口；似乎有一兩針爆開了。我再拉開鋪在底部的地毯。下面露出了一個蓋子，上面鑽了可以讓手指穿過去的洞。蓋子可以讓一個人通過，兩個人就太擠了。

en_text: I reach in and find a strap. I pull the bag up just as a muffled but unmistakable scream comes from the living room. I race out there. The woman has taken a few steps away from Bracken. She turns toward me and there’s a line of blood, not very wide, arcing up her body from her midriff, across her chest and neck and over her face. Bracken’s eyes are wide open and he’s staring down at his body, which is exactly how it ought to be—except for about ten centimeters of steel coming out the bottom of his stomach. The other ten centimeters of the blade is nowhere to be seen, but it’s obvious where it is.
zh_text: 我伸手進去，抓到一條帶子，拉起一個提包。這時客廳裡傳來模糊不清的聲音，但絕對是尖叫聲。我衝回客廳，女人已經離開布萊肯好幾步。她跑到我身旁，我看到一道細細的血跡，從她的上腹部劃了個弧形，橫過她的胸口和脖子，也劃過她的臉頰。布萊肯瞪大了雙眼，瞪著自己的肚子看，他的肚子跟本來沒什麼兩樣——只是小腹上突出了大約十公分長的刀子。另外十公分的刀刃不見了，不過顯然就插在他的肚子裡。

en_text: “Shit,” I whisper.
zh_text: 「靠，」我低聲說。

en_text: “He moved,” she says.
zh_text: 「他亂動。」她說。

en_text: “You didn’t have to—”
zh_text: 「你也不用···」

en_text: “Didn’t have to what?” she asks. “You said if he moves, then—” “I know what I—”
zh_text: 「不用怎樣？」她問。「你說如果他亂動，我就···」

en_text:
“So that’s what I did.” “Shit.”
She reaches forward and grabs the handle.
“Wait,” I say, dropping the bag, but it’s too late. She pulls the knife out. She gives it a distasteful glance before offering it to me. Blood is overlapping the edges of the wound. Lots of blood.
zh_text:
「我知道，我說過···」
「所以我就用了刀子。」
「幹。」
她伸手過去抓住刀把。
「等等，」我丢下袋子，但來不及了。她已經把刀子拔出來，满臉嫌惡地看了一眼，然後才遞給我。傷口兩側出現了血跡。好多血。

en_text: She drops the knife on the carpet and moves against the wall. She has that look about her that people get when they think they had a really great idea but it hasn’t turned out how they pictured; the thing she thought would make her happy is making her sick.
zh_text: 她把刀子丢在地毯上，靠到牆上。臉上的表情就像得意洋洋的人突然洩了氣，發現計畫未如預期般進行；本來以爲自己會很開心，現在卻快要吐了。

en_text: “He deserved it,” she says. “He was a piece of—”
zh_text: 「他活該，」她說，「這個爛」

en_text: “I don’t care,” I say. I hunt around for something but I don’t know what, then settle for the dish towel in his mouth.
zh_text: 「我不想聽。」我東張西望，不知道要找什麼，最後把他嘴巴裡的擦碗布拉了出來。

en_text: “Oh God, oh God, oh Jesus,” he says. “Oh Jesus.”
zh_text: 「噢，天啊，噢，老天啊，噢，上帝呀，」他說，「噢，上帝呀。」

en_text: I wad the dish towel up and push it against his stomach and he flinches back. I apply as much pressure as I can without jamming the dish towel right through his spine.
zh_text: 我把擦碗布揉成一團，壓在他的肚子上，他痛得往後一縮。我用力壓住，但不敢用力到把擦碗布塞進他的傷口裡。

en_text: “Ah, ah fuck, ahhh!”
zh_text: 「啊——啊，操你的，啊——！」

en_text: The blood keeps pouring out. He’s scared and tired all at the same time, and a whole lot paler than when he answered his door earlier.
zh_text: 鮮血從傷口湧出來。他又怕又累，臉色比剛才應門時蒼白了幾百倍。

en_text:
“I’m . . . I’m sorry I took it,” Bracken says.
“I bet you are.”
zh_text:
「對不起……對不起，我把錢拿走了。」布萊肯說。
「你應該覺得抱歉。」

en_text: “The guy, the guy was . . . was. Dead. I figured . . . it wouldn’t . . . Ah Jesus, hurt any . . . anybody.”
zh_text: 「他，他……他。死了。我猜……沒……沒關係。啊，老天啊。應該……沒關係。」

en_text: “It hurt me. It got my daughter kidnapped. It got people killed. Almost got Detective Schroder here killed too. And it got you stuck with a knife.”
zh_text: 「對我來說有關係。我女兒被綁架了。有人死了。連施羅德探長都差點死了。也害你被人捅了一刀。」

en_text: “Oh Jesus, please, please, you have to help me.” “I’m trying.”
zh_text: 「噢，上帝啊，求你，求你，求你，求你救我。」「我正在想辦法。」

en_text: “Call an ambulance.”
zh_text: 「叫救護車來。」

en_text: “I want my money,” the woman says, looking down at the bag.
zh_text: 「給我錢。」女人對著地上的袋子張望。「妳說沒錢也願意幫我。」

en_text: “You said you were doing this for free.” “That was before all this . . . blood.”
zh_text: 「那是剛才···剛才沒這麼多血。」

en_text: “Please, please, call an ambulance,” Bracken says, quieter now.
zh_text: 「拜託，拜託，叫救護車。」布萊肯的氣息漸弱。

en_text: “Five thousand,” she says.
zh_text: 「五千紐幣。」她說。

en_text: “You know who I am?” I ask her.
zh_text: 「妳知道我是誰嗎？」我問她。

en_text: “What? Yeah, I guess. From the news.”
zh_text: 「什麼？知道啊。我應該在新聞上看過。」

en_text: “You know what my father did, then, right?” She nods.
zh_text: 「那妳也知道我爹幹的好事了，對不對？」她點頭。

en_text: “People think that kind of thing is in the blood. You want to test if they’re right?”
zh_text: 「大家都認爲會遺傳。妳說呢？會不會遺傳？」

en_text: “Maybe I did say I’d do this for free.”
zh_text: 「我剛才說我幫你不用拿錢。」

en_text: “Maybe you did.” “Can I go now?” “Make it quick.”
zh_text: 「妳是這麼說的。」「我可以走了嗎？」

en_text: Before she can get out of the room, Schroder makes a low moan. He’s still casually leaning against the wall. He’s had a long day. His eyes half open, nothing fixed in his view yet, and then there I am, holding a dish towel on a dying man. He tries to say something but can’t.
zh_text: 「快滾。」她還沒走出客廳，施羅德低聲呻吟了一下。他仍歪七扭八地靠在牆上。今天他可辛苦了。他眼睛睁開了一半，似乎還看不清楚，然後他看到我了，把條擦碗布壓在一個快死的人身上。他想開口說話，卻說不出字句。

en_text: “He did it,” the woman says, pointing at me. “He did it,” she repeats, and then she is gone.
zh_text: 「他幹的，」女人指著我，「他幹的。」她又說了一次，然後就跑掉了。

en_text: The dish towel has soaked through with blood and I find another. It soaks through immediately too. I look at my watch. The hour is nearly up and I haven’t heard back about the meeting.
zh_text: 擦碗布浸滿了鮮血，我又找來一條，也馬上浸滿了鮮血。我看看手錶，快過一個小時了，我還沒接到電話告訴我到哪裡會面。

en_text: “An ambulance,” Bracken says, and his eyes are only half open now.
zh_text: 「救護車。」布萊肯說，他的眼睛快張不開了。

en_text: I take out the cell phone and start to call for help and then end the call. Instead I dial the number of the man who has my daughter. Bracken is suffering but it’s his own fault and my daughter comes first. It begins to ring.
zh_text: 我拿出手機，撥了緊急號碼，又把電話掛了。第二次撥號，我打給綁匪。布萊肯快死了，是他罪有應得，我女兒比較重要。電話響了。

en_text: Only it sounds weird, like it’s ringing in both ears, a continuous ringing.
zh_text: 只是聽起來很奇怪，鈴聲似乎遠在天邊，近在眼前。

en_text: It takes me another second to figure out why. I look at Bracken and he’s got his eyes locked on all the blood. He’s wishing he’d turned his cell phone off. Instead it’s ringing from his pants pocket. I hang up and Bracken’s phone stops. I dial it again and it starts back up. I hang up. Bracken’s phone stops ringing, and I put the phone away, and any chance of calling an ambulance goes with it.
zh_text: 我停了一秒，才明白爲什麼。我瞪著布萊肯，他只看著自己流的血。他很希望他先關機了。但是，他的手機在褲袋裡響個不停。我掛掉電話，布萊肯的手機也不響了。我重撥一次，他的手機又響起來。我掛掉，布萊肯的手機就不響，我把手機收起來，幹他媽的救護車，去死吧。

en_text: Bracken doesn’t say a thing. Everything that seemed odd the moment I got here doesn’t seem odd anymore. He watches as I take the cell phone out of his pants. There are a thousand things all fighting to be said, but in this moment not one of them can be heard. This man took my daughter and he has her somewhere. His eyes are open all the way again. Blood is still draining out of the wound.
zh_text: 布萊肯保持緘默。剛進來時那股不對勁的感覺終於消失了。他看著我從他的褲子口袋裡拿出手機。千言萬語在口腔間竇動，卻什麼也說不出口。這人綁走了我女兒，把她藏起來。他的眼睛完全睁開，血快從肚子上的傷口流乾了。

en_text: “Please, please,” he says, his words slurring slightly, “call am-ambulance.”
zh_text: 「求求你，求求你，」他已經連話都說不清楚了，「叫救——救護車。」

en_text: “Where’s my daughter?” “Please . . .” “Is she here?”
zh_text: 「我女兒呢？」「求求你···」「我女兒在哪裡？」

en_text: “Help me and I’ll tell you where she is.”
zh_text: 「救我，我就告诉你在哪裡。」

en_text: I slap him across his face. Hard. “That’s not how it works. You tell me where she is, then I help you.”
zh_text: 我打了他一巴掌，重重的一巴掌。「聽你的還是聽我的？你告訴我她在哪裡，我再叫救護車。」

en_text: He clenches his eyes shut, his mouth in an open grimace, his teeth tight against each other, revealing an overbite that I’ll take the steak tenderizer to if he doesn’t talk. His entire face has caved in somewhat, as if he’s lost ten kilos in the last two minutes. Blood and now a mixture of urine too is pooling on the floor beneath him. It smells bad.
zh_text: 他緊緊閉上眼睛，嘴巴咧開，牙齒用力咬在一起，上面的門牙跟犬齒蓋住了下面的門牙，他要是不講話，我就拿牛排錘敲爛他的牙齒。他整張臉似乎凹了下去，彷彿才過了兩分鐘他就掉了十公斤。除了血一直流，他也尿濕了褲子，跟血一起流在地上，味道很難聞。

en_text: “Where is she?”
zh_text: 「她在哪裡？」

en_text: He doesn’t answer, just keeps the grimace and the tight facial features of a man going through something very intense. It’s pain and fear and maybe something spiritual too.
zh_text: 他沒回答，只是齜牙咧嘴，五官緊繃，完全是正在經歷生死關頭的表情。痛楚、恐懼，或許還有些心靈上的東西。

en_text: “Hey,” I say, and I slap his face again.
zh_text: 「喂，」我又打了他一巴掌。

en_text: He shakes his head and a moment later he doesn’t seem to know where he is.
zh_text: 他搖搖頭，似乎忘了自己身在何處。

en_text: “Tell me where she is and I stop the bleeding. Schroder calls for an ambulance and you get fixed up. Quicker you talk, quicker I help you.”
zh_text: 「快說我女兒在哪裡，我就幫你止血。施羅德會打電話叫救護車，你就得救了。快說，我就快點救你。」

en_text: “He won’t want to . . . but he has to.” His face turns into a grimace again as he rides another wave of pain.
zh_text: 「他不肯……也得保護我。」他又開始齜牙咧嘴，忍受另一波疼痛。

en_text: “Are you the son of a bitch who shot my wife?” “No.”
zh_text: 「我妻子就是你這個王八蛋殺的？」「不是。」

en_text: “Who, then? Give me a name. Is this the person who has my daughter?”
zh_text: 「那兇手是誰？告訴我是誰？是那個綁走我女兒的人？」

en_text: He doesn’t answer. The pool of blood is still spreading, but not as quickly now.
zh_text: 他沒回答。地上那灘血愈來愈大，但擴張的速度變慢了。

en_text: “Answer me, damn it. How do I get her back?”
zh_text: 「回答我，操你媽的。我要去哪裡找她？」

en_text: “Help me,” he says, his voice low. His eyes focus on something above me before rolling into the back of his head. I slap his face and they roll back down and stare right at me.
zh_text: 「救我。」他的聲音變得很小。他的眼睛看著我頭上的某個東西，然後往後一翻。我摑了他一巴掌，他的眼睛又翻回來，直勾勾看著我。

en_text: “My daughter,” I say.
zh_text: 「我女兒。」我說。

en_text: “My daughter,” he repeats, almost whispering now.
zh_text: 「我女兒。」他重複我的話，聲音低不可聞。

en_text: “Where’s Sam?”
zh_text: 「小珊在哪裡？」

en_text: “Sam,” he says, then he closes his eyes. I slap him but they don’t open back up. I check him for a pulse but there’s nothing.
zh_text: 「小珊，」說著，他閉上了眼睛。我重重摑他，他的眼睛卻不睁開。我摸摸他的脈搏，停了。

en_text: “Wake up!” I slap him harder. “Please,” I say, grabbing his shoulders, “tell me where she is.”
zh_text: 「你給我醒醒！」我更用力打了他一巴掌。「拜託，」我抓住了他的肩膀，「告訴我她在哪裡。」

en_text: The dead man doesn’t answer. I look over at Schroder before sitting on the floor and resting my head in my hands with no idea at all what to do next. I think about what Dad said, about having to learn to control the monster otherwise it would make me do things I didn’t want to do. Did the monster do this?
zh_text: 死人不答腔。我轉頭看看施羅德，然後一屁股坐到地板上，雙手抱頭，不知道接下來該怎麼辦。我想到爹說的，要學會控制怪獸，不然它會讓我倒行逆施。難道這是怪獸的傑作？

en_text: No. Of course not.
zh_text: 不。當然不是。

en_text: You knew she wanted to hurt him. Why leave her alone with him and a large knife? You knew it’d play out this way. No. I didn’t.
zh_text: 你知道她想拿刀捅他。爲何叫她拿刀看著他？你早就知道結果會這樣。不。我不知道。

en_text: Yeah? How else you think it was going to go?
zh_text: 是嗎？你以爲會有不一樣的结果？

en_text: I lean forward and remove Schroder’s gag.
zh_text: 我彎下身，拿出塞在施羅德嘴裡的布。

en_text: “Listen to me, Edward,” he says. “I know how it must have gone down. You snapped, and you certainly didn’t mean to kill him. You were trying to get information, and you were right about Bracken, he knew where your daughter was. Let me help you.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，聽我說，」他說，「我知道爲什麼會這樣。你崩潰了，你當然不想殺他。你只是問出你女兒在哪裡，你說對了，布萊肯知道你女兒被綁到哪裡去。讓我幫你吧。」

en_text: “I didn’t do it. It wasn’t me that cut him.” “Then who? Who was that woman?”
zh_text: 「不是我。刀子不是我插進去的。」「那是誰？剛才那女人是誰？」

en_text: “She was nobody.”
zh_text: 「她誰也不是。」

en_text: “Come on, Edward, it’s time to stop all of this. Too many people are getting hurt.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，别鬧了，别再任性了。已經死了好幾個人。」

en_text: I put the gag back into his mouth. He doesn’t struggle—he’s resigned to the fact there’s nothing he can do except wait things out. I get up and pace the living room, covering a few hundred meters over the same piece of carpet while I try and work it all out.
zh_text: 我把布塞回他嘴裡。他沒有掙扎他認命了，除了耐心等待，别無他法。我站起來，在客廳裡來回踱步，在同一塊地毯上走了幾百公尺，想找出答案。

en_text: Bracken has two cell phones, it turns out. He has a normal one, with what appear to be work and family contacts. Then he has the second one, the one that rang earlier. There are only two numbers in the memory, with no name attached to either of them. One is for the phone I’ve been using. I scroll down to the other number and press CALL. It rings three times and then it’s picked up.
zh_text: 原來，布萊肯有兩支手機。一支平常用，用來聯絡同事和家人。一支則剛才響過了。記憶體內只有兩個號碼，都沒有相關的姓名。一個號碼是我身上的手機。我選了另一個號碼，按下撥號鍵。響了三聲後，有人接起來了。

en_text: “I’m still waiting,” a man says. “I have the money.” “Money?”
zh_text: 「我還在等。」一個男聲說。「錢在我這裡。」「錢？」

en_text: “Please, I can . . .”
zh_text: 「求求你，我可以···」

en_text: The line goes dead. I call the number again but he’s switched off the phone.
zh_text: 對方掛斷了。我按下重撥，但他已經關機了。

en_text: I keep pacing. Thinking about it.
zh_text: 我繼續踱步，繼續思考。

en_text: “I know how it happened,” I say to Schroder. “Bracken planned the whole thing, and when they split the money up they gave Kingsly his share. When Bracken found him this morning he took the money. Instead of breaking it evenly among his partners, he told them whoever killed Kingsly must have taken it. That way he could keep it all. There never was any plan to pay to get my daughter back. It was a charade. He stashed Sam somewhere with no intention of me paying to get her back, but as an act so the others would think I had the money. Bracken only guessed I’d killed Kingsly because the media kept speculating that I was capable of it. I don’t even know if Sam’s alive anymore. I have all this but nobody to trade it with,” I say, and I open up the bag I found under the floor. It’s full of identical bricks of cash that I found but didn’t take last night. I don’t even know the exact amount. It’s all blood money that I don’t want, but it may still be my only chance of finding Sam. Schroder doesn’t nod or shake his head or offer anything useful. He’s watching a man falling apart. “I bet Bracken was going to kill the guy who has Sam. It would tie up a loose end and give him more money. They were going to kill me too.”
zh_text: 「我知道來龍去脈了，」我對施羅德說。「布萊肯是主謀，然後他們把錢分了，金斯理也有份。今天早上布萊肯發現他的時候，把他的錢拿走。他沒有平均分給其他人，反而說一定是殺了金斯理的人把錢拿走了。這麼一來他就可以獨吞。他根本不想讓我用錢贖回女兒，只是在演戲。他把小珊藏起來，根本不想從我這邊拿到贖金，只是要誤導其他人相信我把錢拿走了。布萊肯猜到我殺了金斯理，只是因爲媒體推斷我遺傳了殺人魔的基因。我甚至連小珊是死是活都不知道。錢拿到了，卻沒有人可以贖。」我拉開在密洞裡找到的袋子。裡面裝滿了我昨晚看到卻沒拿的一疊疊現鈔。我連確切的數目都不知道。這些錢沾滿了鮮血，我不想要，但我只有這個機會可以換回小珊。施羅德不點頭也不搖頭，一點忙也不幫，只看著眼前這個男人心碎到四分五裂。「我打賭，布萊肯也想殺了綁走小珊的人。這樣就可以收拾爛攤子，他分到的錢也更多。他們也打算殺了我。」

en_text: I go through the house. There’s a bedroom that’s been converted into an office, and I switch on the computer. While waiting for it to boot up, I go through the rest of the house. I check under the floor in the wardrobe where the money was hidden but there’s nothing else down there. I check other wardrobes but find nothing. Every time I walk past Bracken’s body I resist the urge to grab him by the shoulders and shake him.
zh_text: 我開始搜他的房子。有間被改裝成書房的臥室，我打開了桌上的電腦。等電腦開機時，我又找到。每次經過布萊肯的屍體，我都想抓住他的肩膀搖醒他，但我克制住了。去搜其他的地方。我查了剛才藏錢的密洞，裡面沒有其他的東西。我查了其他的衣櫃，什麼也沒

en_text: I sit down in front of Bracken’s computer and navigate around the desktop. It’s a clean desktop with only a few icons, and I click one open to find a folder full of porn, maybe a hundred or so video clips. I don’t watch any of them. I close the folder and go into his documents folder. Turns out Bracken is—or was—an aspiring novelist. There are a couple of manuscripts here that he’s working on. I don’t read any of them. There is a games folder, and a music folder, and then I go through the folders on the hard drive, looking for something, for anything related either to work or to robbing a bank. I go through his emails—and it turns out that Bracken doesn’t have many friends. Even his address book is barren except for a half dozen people, half of whom share the same last name as him. I scan through the emails; mostly they’re all bad jokes that have been circulated around the world millions of times already. There are no emails at all relating to work or to robbing a bank. There aren’t any emails to or from Shane Kingsly. I spend fifteen minutes going through his computer—which is a long time when there’s a corpse leaking blood all over the living-room floor—and in the end the only thing I’ve accomplished is to waste precious time.
zh_text: 我坐在布萊肯的電腦前，先看看桌面。他的桌面很乾淨，只有幾個圖示，我點開一個資料夾，裡面全是A片，或許有上百齣。我跳過不看，把資料夾關上，打開他的文件夾。原來，布萊肯立志要當小說家，裡面有兩本原稿。我沒打開看。還有一個遊戲資料夾，一個音樂資料夾，然後我查看硬碟上的資料夾，看看有什麼東西，有沒有東西和搶銀行有關。我看了他的電子郵件——看似布萊肯沒什麼朋友。通訊錄空空如也，只有五六個人，其中一半的人跟他同姓。我快速讀了一下郵件的内容；大多是無聊的笑話，已經在網路上傳了幾百萬次。沒有和工作或搶銀行有關的郵件，也沒有跟金斯理往來的郵件。我花了十五分鐘查他的電腦——如果客廳裡有具血流满地的屍體，十五分鐘算久了——最後一無所獲，我浪費了寶貴的十五分鐘。

en_text: Out in the living room, Schroder has disappeared. He’s rolled himself out or got to his feet. I check the front door and it’s open. I step outside but there’s no sign of him. He could have jumped out fifteen minutes ago or only two, but either way the result is the same for me—the police are on their way.
zh_text: 走回客廳，施羅德不見了。他有可能滾了出去，有可能站了起來。前門打開了。我走到外面，仍沒看見施羅德。或許他十五分鐘前就跳出去了，也有可能才離開兩分鐘，不論如何，結果都一樣警察馬上就要來了。

en_text: I grab Bracken’s pants and find his wallet, then head out to my car. I wonder what the statistics are now for Schroder—what percentage chance he has of bouncing along to a neighbor who will help him, or one that will try to cannibalize him.
zh_text: 我拉開布萊肯的褲袋，拿走他的皮夾，走向我的車子。不知道現在施羅德的統計數字是什麼——他跳著找鄰居求救，找到人幫他的機率有多高？找到人想吃掉他的機率有多高？

en_text: I don’t have the time to care.
zh_text: 沒時間管他了。

en_text: It’s no longer Christmas Eve—Christmas kicked in about two minutes ago and town is full of people celebrating. The homeless and the party animals mingle and mix and I can’t help but hate all of them as they move through this world, ignorant to what some of us are going through to save our families.
zh_text: 平安夜悄悄結束了耶誕節約莫在兩分鐘前開始，城裡到處都有人在狂歡。遊民和夜店咖混在一起不分彼此，我恨他們，恨他們無憂無慮，根本不知道有些人得付出什麼才能救回家人。

en_text: The center of Christchurch is mapped around a bull’s-eye of tourist markets and street performers and of course the Cathedral, a giant church over a hundred years old that’s popular with tourists and God and graffiti artists—although these days the popular consensus is that God moved out of Christchurch, meaning that God is everywhere except here. It’s all crammed into a location known as Cathedral Square. The Cathedral is packed with people celebrating Christmas Mass. The markets are gone, and the drunk, the homeless, and the glue sniffers have to share the Square with churchgoers as they sit on steps and huddle on park benches, living in perfect harmony.
zh_text: 基督城以觀光市場和街頭藝人爲中心，當然也有一座教堂，超過百年的大教堂，很受遊客和上帝歡迎，也是塗鴉藝術家最喜歡的地方只是到了最近大家都認爲，上帝已經搬離基督城了，所以祂無所不在，就是不在這裡。教堂廣場則是中心的中心，全城的人都跑來了。大教堂裡擠滿了人，慶祝耶誕彌撒。市場收起來了，醉鬼、遊民和吸強力膠的人得和上教堂的群衆共享廣場，他們坐在台階上，或擠在公園的長凳上，氣氛一團和諧。

en_text: The probation offices are only a few blocks away, in a part of town where the only clubs are strip joints, where the bouncers are bigger and the tattoos take up more real estate on their arms and necks than their counterparts at regular clubs. The building is six storeys, and probably houses other things too, maybe some law or accountancy firms. I got the address from a business card inside Bracken’s wallet. The only windows on the ground floor are the automatic doors, which at this time of night are automatically impossible to open, unless I drive right into them. The rest of the building is tile and brick and has graffiti scrawled across it, showing off the creative talents of the city’s youth.
zh_text: 觀護人辦公室過幾個街口就到了，這裡要上夜店，只能去脫衣舞酒吧，酒吧門口的保鑣個子更大，手臂和脖子上的刺青也比一般夜店的同行佔了更大的地盤。辦公室所在的建築物有六層樓，或许也有其他機構，比方說律師或會計師事務所。我從布萊肯皮夾裡找到一張名片，得知辦公室的地址。一樓沒有窗戶，只有自動門供人進出，到了現在這個時候，當然不會自動打開，除非我開車撞過去。很普通的磚瓦建築，上面有大大的塗鴉，展現出基督城年輕人的創作天分。

en_text: There’s an alleyway heading up the side of the building, and I pull the car in and swing around the back. My headlights wash over a guy leaning against a Dumpster with a woman kneeling in front of him. They both look at me.
