The guy has vomit down the front of his shirt and the woman doesn’t look any better. They wave at my car as if trying to swat away a fly, before straightening their clothes and leaving.
zh_text: 旁邊有條巷子，我把車開進去，到巷尾轉了個彎。車頭燈打在一個男人身上，他靠著垃圾箱，前方蹲了一個女人。兩人都看著我。男人的襯衫上有嘔吐物，女人看起來也好不到哪裡去。他們對著我的車揮手，做出打蒼蠅的手勢，然後才整理衣物，離開了我的視線。

en_text: At the back of the building, there are two doors about ten meters apart from each other. The accountant inside me works the numbers. The police are busy. It’s been a long day for them, and even now they’re at Bracken’s house and at my in-laws’ house and they’re dealing with dead bodies, and Schroder is trying to round up the rest of the men who robbed the bank and find my daughter while the rest of the force are at home, taking the night off. That means if an alarm goes off I probably have a minute or two longer than usual. A place like this, it’s more likely a patrol car will show up than a security firm. And in a city like this, maybe nobody will show up for an hour. Of course there’s only one statistic that matters—my daughter. I will do whatever it takes to get her back.
zh_text: 到了建築物後面，我看到兩扇門，之間的距離大約十公尺。我心中的會計師開始計算了。警方很忙。他們忙了一整天，現在還要到布萊肯家和我岳父家處理屍體，施羅德要追捕其餘的搶匪和找回我女兒，而其他警察都回家休假了。那表示如果警鋡響了，或许警察到達的時間會比平常晚一兩分鐘。在這樣的區域裡，比較可能出現警車，而不是保全公司。在這樣的城市裡，或許過了一個小時也不會有人來。當然，重要的統計數字只有一個——我女兒。不論如何，我都要把她找回來。

en_text: Bracken’s keys have a keycard hanging from them. One of the doors is the good old-fashioned lock and key, but the other door has a pad on the side of it. I swipe the card and there’s a click; I try the door and it opens. I step inside and a fluorescent light blinks on overhead, blinding at first. There’s a second door; this one with a numeric keypad. I lean back and kick near the handle. It takes five strong kicks because I have to use my left leg, and even then it jars through to my right, the door breaking at the same time as some of the stitches in my leg. An alarm beeps somewhere.
zh_text: 布萊肯的鑰匙圈上掛了一張磁卡。一扇門是傳統的門鎖，另一扇旁邊則有感應器。我刷了卡，聽到卡嗒一聲；試試門鎖，開了。我走進去，頭上有盞日光燈，照得我頭暈目眩。裡面還有一扇門；需要輸入密碼。我向後退了一步，用力踢門把旁邊的地方。右腿施不上力，只好用左腿猛踢，踢了五下後右腿也隱隱刺痛，門終於被我踢開，右腿上的縫線也繃開了。某處的警鈴開始嗶嗶作響。

en_text: I’m in a corridor that has every fourth light going, which is enough to see by. It winds around to the front entrance where there’s a foyer and two elevators and a flight of stairs. There’s a directory by the lift: it turns out the probation offices are on the ground floor. I’ve left bloody footprints between the door I kicked down and the elevators. I press the elevator button and wait for the doors to open and step inside. I take off my shirt and wrap it over my foot while the elevator goes nowhere. Then I open the doors and step out. I press the button and send the elevator, empty, to the top floor.
zh_text: 我進了一條走廊，只開了四分之一的燈，但光線也夠了。走廊曲曲折通往前門，有個門廳，兩座電梯，和樓梯入口。電梯旁有樓層指南：原來觀護人辦公室就在一樓。在我踢壞的那扇門和電梯之間，我留下了血腳印。我按下電梯鈕，等門打開後走進去。我脫下襯衫，裹在腳上，電梯仍留在一樓。然後我從電梯出來，按下樓層按鈕，把空空的電梯送到最上面去。

en_text: I head to the probation office, no blood trail behind me, and use Bracken’s swipe card to gain entry. The alarm keeps beeping, but still hasn’t gone off. I enter a large waiting room with a series of offices scattered around the sides and back. None of the office doors have names on them. There’s a giant reception desk in the middle of the room. I have no idea which office belongs to Bracken. The layout of the floor reminds me of my own office, which makes me think of a simple solution: I go into each office and look for family photos and drawings done by children, with the idea of eliminating the offices that do have them since Bracken doesn’t; but the idea is a bust because there aren’t any pictures anywhere. I guess probation offices aren’t the kind of place where employees want to share their personal lives with the public. It’s the type of place where one day they have a photo of their nine-year-old daughter up on the wall, and the next day they’re taking that photo to Missing Persons. I try to think about what else could make Bracken’s office stand out from any other.
zh_text: 我朝著觀護人辦公室走去，身後不再出現血跡，我用布萊肯的通行證開了門。警鈴繼續嗶嗶，但仍未放聲大響。我走進一間寬敒的候客室，兩側和最後面都有連在一起的數間辦公室。辦公室門上都沒有姓名。房間中央有張巨大的接待桌。到底哪間辦公室屬於布萊肯？樓層的配置讓我想起我自己的辦公室，也想到了一個簡單的推理方法：我走進辦公室，尋找家人的照片和孩子的繪畫，只要有照片或圖畫，就不是布萊肯的辦公室；但是這個方法不可靠，因爲辦公室裡都沒有照片。我猜在觀護人辦公室工作的人應該不想跟其他人分享私人生活的點滴。在這種工作環境裡，如果今天把九歲女兒的照片貼在牆上，明天就要用這張照片來通報失蹤人口。我又開始想有沒有其他的方法能辨別出布萊肯的辦公室。

en_text: Sixty seconds have passed since I entered the offices. A moment later a high-pitched scream shrieks from every corner of the building. I grab some Blu-Tack from the reception desk and ball it into my ears.
zh_text: 自從我開始搜查辦公室，又過了六十秒。接著，尖銳的警鋡聲從建築物的所有角落響起來。我從接待處抓了一些寶貼黏土揉成球，塞到耳朵裡。

en_text: I take out Bracken’s business card and the cell phone. There are three numbers on the card, an office line, his direct line, and his cell phone number. I dial the direct line but can’t hear anything over the alarm. I head from office to office and barely manage to hear a phone ringing in the fourth one I try. There is a narrow angle of sight from the desk, past the reception area to a window leading outside. I glance at the view every few seconds, waiting for when it changes from parking meters and bike stands to patrol cars.
zh_text: 我拿出布萊肯的名片和手機。上面有三個號碼，辦公室的、他的專線和他的手機。我撥了專線，但警鈴聲蓋過了所有的聲音。我換了一間又一間，到了第四間才勉強聽到微弱的鈴聲。從辦公桌看出去的視角非常狹窄，可以看到接待處和通到外面的窗戶。我每隔幾秒就抬頭看一眼，等一下除了停車收費器和腳踏車架，也會出現巡邏車。

en_text: I switch on the computer which offers more light, then I go through the drawers. There are too many files to go through so I pile them onto the desk. The computer loads up and by the time a desktop appears I’m too nervous to hang around. I consider tearing the computer apart and taking the hard drive, but the files are probably on a server somewhere. The alarm is still shrieking and the Blu-Tack in my ears doesn’t seem to be helping.
zh_text: 我打開電腦，增加了一點光源，然後我開始翻他的抽屜。要看的檔案太多了，所以我把它們都堆到桌上。電腦啓動了，等到桌面出現時，我已經緊張到想奪門而出。說不定我該把電腦拆開，拿走硬碟，但檔案可能都在伺服器上。警鈴聲依然尖銳，耳朵裡的黏土完全擋不住。

en_text: There’s a gym bag behind the desk. I unzip it and dump the clothes on the floor. I’m packing everything I pulled out of the drawers into the bag when a patrol car pulls up outside.
zh_text: 桌子後有個運動包。我拉開拉鍊，把裡面的衣服都倒在地板上。再把從抽屜裡拿出來的東西都裝到袋子裡，這時，外面有台巡邏車停下來了。

en_text: As I reach the door to the foyer and elevators, the alarm goes quiet. The rest of the lights come on and I duck behind a desk. There are footsteps in the foyer, and voices. I can’t quite hear what they’re saying, but the words I’m looking for stick out from the rest—“blood,” “elevator,” and “top floor.” The police out there know they have a lot of ground to cover, but they’ve noticed that the elevator with blood leading up to it has been sent to the top. A radio squawks, and one of them speaks into it. “Backup.” The word is clear.
zh_text: 快走到門廳和電梯時，警鈴停了。所有的燈都亮了，我找了張桌子躲在後面。門廳裡傳來了腳步聲和說話聲。聽不太清楚，但我想聽的字眼都出現了血、電梯、頂樓。外面的警察知道要搜完六層樓不容易，但他們已經注意到沾了血跡的電梯曾爬到頂樓去。對講機嘎嘎作響，有人說話了。請求支援。我聽得很清楚。

en_text: Another door opens, and then there are footsteps in the stairwell. Thirty seconds later the elevator doors open and close. The accountant and the monster think things through. We figure there are two cops here already and more coming soon, so I need to act now. We figure one of them is probably at the third or fourth floor now. He’s laboring his way to the top floor while his partner rides up in comfort.
zh_text: 另一扇門打開了，腳步聲進了樓梯間。三十秒後，電梯門開了，又關了。會計師和怪獸細細思索。我們知道來了兩個警察，等一下還會有更多警察，我得立刻行動。我們猜其中一個或許到了三樓或四樓。他氣喘吁吁地往上爬，而他的夥伴則一派輕鬆地搭電梯。

en_text: Another patrol car pulls up outside.
zh_text: 外面又來了一台巡邏車。

en_text: I untie the shirt from my foot and pull it back on. I open the door and run into the foyer, the gym bag in one hand, a stapler in the other, ready to hurl it hard in case somebody is still down here—but there’s no one. I turn toward the main door. There are two police constables walking toward it, a man and a woman. They stop dead and stare at me and I do the same, me on one side of the door, them on the other, then they race forward and one of them grabs the door.
zh_text: 我解開腳上的襯衫，穿回身上。開了門，我跑進了門廳，一手提著運動包，一手拿著釘書機，要有人還在一樓，我已經準備好把釘書機對著他丢過去——不過一個人也沒有。我轉向正門。兩名警官正走過來，一男一女。他們猛然停下腳步瞪著我，我也停下來瞪著他們，我在門這一邊，他們在門另一邊，然後他們朝著我衝過來，拉開了大門。

en_text: His head has cleared in the hour or so since he died, and he likes to think that the fuckups in that time were brought about by that experience, likes to think they’re not the kind of mistakes he’d make on any other day.
zh_text: 死裡逃生後過了一個小時吧，他的腦袋終於恢復正常，他想，在這一小時內發生的蠢事都是因爲他快死了，絕不是他平日會犯的錯誤。

en_text: Getting out of the house was easy. All Schroder had to do was caterpillar his way to the front door, get to his feet, twist his body so he could reach the door handle, and run like hell—or in this case bounce. It took him a couple of tiring minutes to reach a house that had lights on. He used his nose to ring the doorbell. It was a young couple whose kids had gone to bed; they were wrapping presents and had shared half a bottle of wine and seemed to look at Schroder with as much suspicion as anything, but he was thankful they took him in and cut the ties that held his feet. Nat’s cell phone was still in his pocket, and he used it to phone the station, and then he phoned his wife. He told her he was running late, told her it was going to be a long night, told her he was sorry, and didn’t tell her that a short time ago she was technically a widow. She told him she was disappointed but she understood, and he should get home when he could. It was the best-case scenario—and her first Christmas present to him.
zh_text: 從房子裡逃出來很簡單。施羅德只需要像毛毛蟲般爬到門口，跳起來轉過身，抓住門把打開門，然後衝出去就行了——不過現在他只能用跳的。他跳了兩分鐘，快累死了，才找到屋裡還亮著燈的房子。他用鼻子按下門鈴。裡面住了一對年輕夫婦，已經把小孩送上床；他們正在包禮物，共享了半瓶葡萄酒，看到施羅德的時候，兩人都一臉懷疑，不過他很感恩，他們救了他，幫他剪開了腿上的束縛。納森的手機仍在他口袋裡，他打回警局，然後又打給他的妻子。他說，事情還沒辦完，可能要熬一整夜了，他很抱歉，不過他沒說，其實在一小時前，嚴格來說她已經當了幾分鐘的寡婦。她說，她有點失望，但她能諒解，他可以回家的時候，就應該要回家。整體來說已經好到不能再好了——她的諒解也是給他的第一份耶誕禮物。

en_text: By the time the first patrol car arrived, Edward was long gone. The responding officers removed Schroder’s handcuffs.
zh_text: 第一台巡邏車到了，但艾德華早就不見了。回應支援的警官幫施羅德解開了手銬。

en_text: “So where’s he gone now?” Landry asks. They’re standing in Bracken’s living room, a photographer and a couple of other officers hanging out in the corner. Others are out canvassing the neighborhood, hoping to narrow down Hunter’s destination.
zh_text: 「他跑到哪去了？」藍德里問。他們站在布萊肯的客廳裡，有人在拍照，另外兩名警官站在牆角。也有幾名警官在附近詢問，希望能追蹤到杭特的去向。

en_text: “I don’t know. But Jesus, Bill, everything that’s happened—everything that Hunter did to Bracken, he was right in the end. Bracken was part of the robbery. He had somebody take Hunter’s daughter, and now we’ve got nothing.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。但老天啊，比爾，剛才一剛才杭特狠狠折磨了布萊肯，最後居然被他說對了。布萊肯也是涉案人。他讓人綁走了杭特的女兒，现在我們什麼線索也没有。」

en_text: “Not nothing,” Landry says. “We’ve got a couple of names. That gives us a bunch of known accomplices.”
zh_text: 「不是什麼也沒有，」藍德里說，「我們得到兩個人名，就能再查出他們的同夥。」

en_text: “Yeah, but in time to save Hunter’s daughter?”
zh_text: 「對，但來得及救杭特的女兒嗎？」

en_text: “He shouldn’t have killed Bracken. He could have helped us.”
zh_text: 「他不该殺了布萊肯，說不定他能幫我們。」

en_text: “He says he didn’t do it. Says the woman did it.” “You believe him?”
zh_text: 「他說不是他殺的，是妓女殺的。」「你信嗎？」

en_text: “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」

en_text: “That’s not much of an answer, Carl. Sounds more like you want to believe him but don’t.”
zh_text: 「卡爾，答了等於沒答。感覺你想相信他，可是你不信。」

en_text: “Whether he did it or not, he’s gone somewhere. Something here must have tipped him off.”
zh_text: 「不管是不是他幹的，他已經走了。肯定找到了其他的線索。」

en_text: “Maybe he found a name or an address.” “Yeah, and took it with him.”
zh_text: 「或許他找到了人名，或地址。」「對，也把線索带走了。」

en_text: “Well, if we’re lucky, maybe he’ll succeed. Maybe he’ll get his daughter back and take another couple of bad guys off the street.”
zh_text: 「好吧，要是我們走運，或許他能辦到。或許他能把女兒找回來，讓幾個壤人從世界上消失。」

en_text: “I don’t see it working out that way,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「我不覺得會那麼順利。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Sure. Would be good, though, right?”
zh_text: 「當然。不過聽起來很不錯，不是嗎？」

en_text: A few more detectives arrive on the scene and join them in searching the house.
zh_text: 又來了幾名警探，大家開始在布萊肯家裡四處搜索

en_text: “It’s official,” Landry says, finishing up a phone call. “Our two victims today are also Bracken’s cons.”
zh_text: 「證實了，」藍德里把電話掛掉。「今天那兩名死者也是布萊肯的同黨。」

en_text: “Like Kingsly.”
zh_text: 「跟金斯理一樣。」

en_text: “Yeah. That’s three for three.”
zh_text: 「對，三個都中了。」

en_text: “So Bracken put the crew together,” Schroder says. “I’ll go to his office. Check his files. Maybe it’s even where Hunter is heading.”
zh_text: 「所以布萊肯召集了一群人，」施羅德說，「我去他辦公室瞧瞧。看看檔案裡有沒有線索。說不定杭特就往那裡去了。」

en_text: “Maybe,” Landry answers, and ten minutes later it turns out he’s right.
zh_text: 「有可能。」藍德里說，十分鐘後消息傳來，眞被施羅德猜對了。

en_text: “Shit,” the officer says, because the automatic doors are locked and don’t open for him. He fumbles with the keys but I don’t hang around to watch. I limp past the elevators, past the busted door and the footprints of blood toward the back entrance. I burst out behind the building into the alleyway. I reach my car, the shotgun still on the passenger seat. The woman cop is running down the alleyway toward me. I turn the shotgun toward her and she comes to a complete stop. She raises her hands the same way the bank manager did.
zh_text: 「可惡。」警官說，自動門鎖起來了，並沒有打開來迎接他們。他摸找鑰匙，我可不想等他開門。我一跛一跛經過電梯、穿過被我踼開的門、踩過血跡淋漓的腳印，朝著後門走去。我衝出建築物，跑到巷子裡。上了我的車，霰彈槍仍擺在副駕駛座上。女警穿過巷子跑過來。我舉起霰彈槍對著她，她停住了腳步，舉高雙手，就跟銀行經理一樣。

en_text: Kill her.
zh_text: 殺了她。

en_text: There’s no need.
zh_text: 不需要吧。

en_text: There’s always a need. There always has been.
zh_text: 有需要，一直都有需要。

en_text: “Please,” she says. She’s a few years younger than me, and about as scared as I probably looked when six men came bursting through the bank doors. She takes a couple of steps away.
zh_text: 「別殺我。」她比我年輕幾歲，臉上恐懼的表情或許就跟六個男人衝進銀行大門時我的表情一模一樣。她退後了兩步。

en_text:
I prime the shotgun. She takes another step backward. Jodie was killed as a distraction and it worked. It commanded a huge police force and effort at the bank while they sped away. A shotgun blast here would do the same thing. It would give me more time to find my daughter.
Do it.
zh_text:
我把子彈上膛。她又向後退了一步。搶匪殺了茱蒂，來分散警方的注意力，非常有效。他們加速逃離時，警方必須在銀行投注更多的人力。在這裡轟一槍，效果也一樣。我就更有餘裕去找我女兒。
殺了她。

en_text: “Please, I have a family,” she says.
zh_text: 「求求你，我有家人要照顧。」她說。

en_text: “Move over there,” I say, and I point the shotgun toward the door I just came out of. She reaches it and I move around to the driver’s side of the car and climb in. I put the gun standing up from the footwell onto the passenger seat and the cop stays still. I reverse quickly back toward the road. A third patrol car shows up and covers the exit. I push hard on the accelerator and the back of my car hits the side of the patrol car right in the middle of the front wheel. The crash jolts me back and forward and the Blu-Tack falls out of my ears. The patrol car is pushed away from the side of the road. My car stalls and I restart it and jam my foot on the accelerator again and swerve out onto the road. The back of the car produces a rattling sound that gets louder the further I drive. The patrol car comes after me but manages all of five meters before taking a sharp right-hand turn, the axle probably broken. I slow down at the intersection, and when I push my foot back down the engine revs but doesn’t grip and the car rolls without any acceleration. I try changing gears but it doesn’t make a difference.
zh_text: 「過去那邊。」我用霰彈槍指著我剛衝出來的門。她走到門邊，我移到駕駛座的車門邊，上了車。我把槍立在副駕駛座的座椅前面，女警動也不動。我嗖一聲把車子倒回路上。第三輛巡灉車出現了，擋住了出口。我用力踩下油門，車尾撞上了巡邏車的車身，正好撞到前輪的中央。撞擊的力量讓我來回搖動，寶貼黏土從我的耳朵裡震了出來。巡邏車從路邊被推開。我的車子熄火了我再度啟動，再度狠狠踩下油門，旋回到大路上。車尾開始嘎嘎作響，而且愈來愈響。巡灉車追過來，但只開了五公尺，就突然向右甩尾，車軸可能斷了。到了十字路口，車速變慢了，我踩下油門，引擎加速後卻開始空轉，車子的速度沒有變快。我試著換檔，卻仍然無法加速。

en_text: One of the other patrol cars comes away from the curb. I pull over and jump out, slinging bags over my shoulders, the money much heavier than the files. The patrol car is about a hundred and fifty meters away when I point the shotgun at the tattoo-covered bouncer at the strip club door and make my way inside.
zh_text: 一輛停在路邊的巡邏車開過來了。我把車停到路邊，跳下車，兩個袋子甩到肩膀上，鈔票比檔案還重。巡邏車大概還有一百五十公尺遠，我用霰彈槍指著滿身刺青的保鑣，輕鬆地進了脫衣酒吧。

en_text: The club is dark and there’s cigarette smoke hanging in the air; it’s like a fog rolled in, bringing with it the dregs of modern man. Girls in nothing but underwear, with breasts of all different sizes, are walking between the tables, some carrying drinks, others leading a patron by the hand toward a three-minute lap dance. The music is loud and aimed at the generation most of these girls seem to be in—one that’s about ten years younger than mine. There are maybe fifteen or twenty patrons in the club, mostly men sitting by themselves, a group of six in front of the stage. I keep the shotgun by my side, pointing down, and nobody seems to notice it. Most of the lighting is aimed at the stage, where a girl in a nurse outfit who looks nothing like the nurse who showed me the happy face chart earlier today is spinning around a pole. The look on her face reminds me of the waitress on the day Jodie died, the look of the damned—it was a lifetime ago now.
zh_text: 裡面烏漆麻黑，空氣中滿是菸味；彷彿煙霧捲了進來，連帶送入了現代社會的渣滓。除內衣外身無寸縷的女郎在桌間遊走，胸部大小各有千秋，有的端著飲料，有的牽著顧客的手，準備來場三分鐘豔舞。音樂震耳欲聾，似乎正適合此處大多數女郎的世代——她們都起碼比我小十歲。酒吧裡大概有十五到二十個顧客，多半是獨坐的男人，舞台前則有六個人坐在一起，應該是一夥的我。把霰彈槍貼在身旁，槍口對著地板，似乎沒被人發現。最亮的地方在舞台上，一名穿著護士服的女郎正繞著鋼管旋轉，完全不像稍早拿笑臉圖給我看的護士。她臉上的表情讓我想起茱蒂過世那天那名女服務生，一臉要死不活的表情——感覺是上輩子的事了。

en_text: I take a corridor that leads past the toilets to a fire-exit door. The police haven’t hit the club yet. The toilets smell of disinfectant and the floor outside is wet. I hit the fire-exit door hard but the damn thing opens only about thirty centimeters, then bounces back, a chain flexing against the handles with a padlock securing it in place. I point the shotgun at the lock and people in the club scream when they hear it go off. The music keeps going and people are no longer watching the stage. The chain falls away and I take it with me outside. I jam the doors closed behind me and wrap the chain around the handles.
zh_text: 我穿過通往廁所的走廊，找到逃生門。警察還沒到。廁所有股消毒水的味道，外面的地板濕濕的。我用力撞開逃生門，但這扇爛門只開了大約三十公分就彈回來，門把上沒繞緊的鐵鏈用掛鎖扣住了，沒辦法打開。我舉起槍對著門鎖，槍響時酒吧裡的人也尖叫起來。音樂仍放個沒完，大家卻不能像剛才一樣聚精會神盯著舞台。鐵鏈落下來了，我一把抓起。從外面把門關上後，我用鐵鏈繞住門把。

en_text: The alleyway is similar to the last one I was in, except this one runs at a different angle, along the back of clubs and shops instead of up between them. I turn right, passing more back entrances; from some come loud music, from others nothing. I stick with the direction and run for about sixty seconds, taking most of the weight on my left leg, hobbling more than running. I can hear sirens patrolling the streets. I climb a fence and drop into an open parking lot with bad lighting and about two cars. On the opposite side I take thirty seconds to catch my breath and begin to transfer the files out of the gym bag and stuff them in with the money. I tuck my arms through it and strap it onto my back and leave the empty bag behind and carry on moving.
zh_text: 眼前的巷子很像剛才那條，但看出去的角度不太一樣，通往夜店和商店的後門，而不是夾在營業場所中間。我向右轉，經過更多後門；有些門傳出吵鬧的音樂聲，有些則安安靜靜。我朝著同一個方向跑了快六十秒，盡量把體重放在左腿上，與其說跑，應該說半跑半跳。我聽到街上傳來警笛聲。我爬過栅欄，跳入一座露天停車場，裡面沒什麼燈光，只停了兩台車。跑到另一端後，我花了三十秒喘息，開始把檔案從運動包移到放錢的提袋裡。我用雙臂穿過提把，揹起了袋子，丢下掏空的運動包，繼續前進。

en_text: The parking lot comes out a driveway on Manchester Street. There are cars that don’t have sirens on them driving past, hookers standing on corners, run-of-the-mill people staggering down the street, some wearing Santa hats. I run across Manchester and head further from the central city, down Gloucester Street toward a one-way system where there is less lighting. A patrol car comes into the street and I duck in behind a row of bushes lining a tile shop and the car drives past. I move again, getting further away, the hookers becoming less frequent and harder-looking, like they’ll do far more for far less. I cross Madras Street and keep heading east. The sirens aren’t as loud now. I get another block before turning north, back toward home, slowing down as more blood runs out of my leg. I need somewhere I can read the files. Somewhere I can bandage myself back up.
zh_text: 出了停車場，前面的路通往曼徹斯特街。沒有警笛的车子呼嘯而過，街角站了流鶯，很平凡的人在街上搖搖晃晃快跌倒了，有些頭上還戴了耶誕老人的帽子。我用跑的穿過曼徹斯特街，逐漸遠離市中心，先走到格勞斯特街，朝著照明不足的單行道走去。街上出現了巡邏車，我往磁磚店前的一排樹叢後一縮，等車子開過去。我又繼續走，更加遠離市中心，流鶯變少了，姿色也更差了，應該用更低的價格就能買到更多的服務。我穿過馬德拉斯街，繼續朝東走。警笛聲愈來愈弱。我又走了一條街後才轉向北，朝著我家的方向走去，速度愈來愈慢，因爲腿上流的血愈來愈多。我得找個地方翻查檔案。我得找個地方幫自己綁上繃帶。

en_text: I’m a good six or seven blocks away when the cell phone I took from Kingsly rings. I flip it open.
zh_text: 又走了六、七個街口，從金斯理家拿來的手機響了。我翻開手機。

en_text: “Hello?”
“What the hell, Edward? You’re making this a whole lot worse than it needs to be,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「艾德華，你在搞什麼？本來沒這麼糟，也被你搞砸了。」施羅德說。

en_text: “I’m finding my daughter.”
zh_text: 「我要把我女兒找回來。」

en_text: “No you’re not. You’re killing her. Look, we have some names, we’re banging on some doors right now. We’re going to find her.”
zh_text: 「不，你搞砸了，你會害死她。聽我說，我們查到了幾個人名，也要去他們家突襲。我們會把你女兒找回來。」

en_text: “You can guarantee that?”
zh_text: 「你保證能把她找回來？」

en_text: “I can guarantee we’re doing our best.”
zh_text: 「我保證我們會盡全力。」

en_text: “What about the person who visited Roger Harwick in jail?” “Who?”
zh_text: 「那個去監獄探羅傑·哈威克的人呢？」「誰？」

en_text: “Somebody had to visit Harwick before my dad got stabbed, right? Somebody from the outside.”
zh_text: 「我爹被刺殺前，一定有人去探訪哈威克，對不對？外面的人？」

en_text: “It’s a good thought,” he says, “except nobody came to see Harwick today, or yesterday. In fact nobody has been to see him since the bank robbery.”
zh_text: 「你腦筋動得很快，」他說，「只是今天沒有人來看他，昨天也沒有。事實上，自從銀行被搶後，他根本沒有訪客。」

en_text: “That doesn’t make any sense,” I say. “Somebody had to talk to him.” “And somebody did. It means another inmate was visited and got told to pass the message along.” “Who?”
zh_text: 「那就不合理了，」我說，「一定有人去找他談事情。」「的確。表示有人去探訪另一名囚犯，然後那名囚犯把消息告訴他。」「會是誰？」

en_text: “We’re looking into it. Problem is there are so many opportunities for Harwick to interact with another inmate. Could be there were other links in the chain. Somebody comes to see Inmate A, who speaks to Inmate B, who talks to Inmate C. Or maybe one of the guards organized it.”
zh_text: 「我們正在調查。問題是，哈威克跟其他囚犯接觸的機會也不少。有可能當中還有其他的環節。有人去探訪犯人甲，犯人甲告訴犯人乙，犯人乙又告訴犯人丙。或许聯繫人是警衛也說不定。」

en_text: “So it’s a dead end,” I say. “I’m doing what I can, Eddie.” “It’s just never enough.” “Where are you?”
zh_text: 「那就沒有線索了。」我說。「我已經盡力了，艾迪。」「你還不夠努力。」「你在哪裡？」

en_text: “I have to go.”
zh_text: 「我得掛了。」

en_text: “What did you find? Another name? An address? Edward, listen to me, if you know where your daughter is, you have to let me help you.”
zh_text: 「你又有其他線索了嗎？人名？還是地址？艾德華，拜託你，如果你知道你女兒在哪裡，你要讓我幫你。」

en_text: “I don’t know where she is. Not yet.”
zh_text: 「我不知道她在哪裡，还没找到。」

en_text: “You’re armed and running around the city, Edward. The word has come in—you’re a threat. A SWAT team unit is coming for you. They see you with that shotgun, they’re going to open fire. There won’t be any dialogue. You hear what I’m saying?”
zh_text: 「艾德華，你帶著武器在城裡亂跑。已經有人通報了你很危險。已經有一隊武装警察在追捕你了。他們看到你拿著霰彈槍，會對你開火。你沒有機會辩解。你懂我在說什麼嗎？」

en_text: “I hear it,” I say, and hang up, then I try calling Nat but the phone just rings and rings.
zh_text: 「我聽到了。」我把電話掛掉，然後打給納森，鈴聲響個不停，卻無人接起。

en_text: What I need is transport and somewhere to read over the files. I find somewhere secure to hide the shotgun before heading back onto the road to flag down a taxi. The first three go by, passengers already inside them; the fourth pulls over, the driver sees the blood on my leg, shakes his head, and drives off. Another taxi pulls up a few minutes later, and this time I keep the gym bag covering my leg. The blood on my shirt from where I wore it over my foot is all on the back, so the driver doesn’t notice it. He just seems to be happy that I’m not carrying a shotgun, but struggles to express his gratitude in clear English. I tell him to take me back toward town, which doesn’t please him because he was hoping for a bigger fare. There are a dozen patrol cars circling the streets, but their search patterns don’t extend to taxis. They’re out there dressed in black, carrying assault weapons and itching to take down Eddie the Hunter, the man they always knew would turn into a killer.
zh_text: 我需要交通工具，我也需要找到地方翻閱檔案。我找到一個安全的地方把槍藏好，然後回到路邊招計程車。前三台都已經載到乘客了；第四台靠過來，駕駛看到我腿上的血，搖搖頭又把車開走了。幾分鐘後又來了一台，我用運動包蓋住我的腿。剛才把襯衫裏住腳沾到的血都在背上，所以駕駛沒看到。我身上沒有武器，應該就讓他很高興了，他費盡力氣，想用清楚的英語表達感謝之意。我叫他把我載回城裡，他似乎很失望，因爲車資太少了。路上有十來輛巡邏車來回穿梭，但他們搜查的對象不包含計程車。警察一身黑色，準備了攻擊武器，恨不得立刻把獵殺手艾迪追捕到案，他們早知道他會變成殺人犯。

en_text: There is blood leading from the kicked-in door to the elevators. It’s how Hunter fooled the first two cops on the scene into thinking he’d gone upstairs. With all the mistakes Hunter has been making, Schroder knows there’s at least something in that mind of his that’s working. He wonders if he’d be doing the same thing if it was his daughter who’d been taken, and decides that he would. He’d do what it takes—which makes it hard to know the SWAT team is out there gunning for Hunter, ready to take him down.
zh_text: 被踢爛的門口出現了血跡，一直滴到電梯裡。杭特就這麼騙過最早到場的兩名警察，以爲他搭電梯上樓了。杭特犯了這麼多錯，但施羅德知道他的腦袋瓜其實還滿管用。他想，要是他自己的女兒被抓走了，他應該也會跟杭特一樣孤注一擲吧。他一定會奮不顧身去把女兒救回來想到武裝警察已經開始搜捕杭特，準備把他捉拿歸案，實在覺得痛心。

en_text: Schroder has never had any reason to come down to the probation offices before, and he knows there’s every chance after tonight he’ll never come here again. The building is fairly nondescript and the offices inside about as impersonal as you can get, with rubber plants either side of the reception desk and a sunset picture hanging on the wall the only signs of excitement. He imagines it’d be hard to work in a place like this, getting to know people on a return basis as they’re released every few years for the same crimes, addictions to drugs, taking other people’s money, taking other people’s lives, all in endless circles. At least, being a cop, your job is to put criminals away; these guys have to reintroduce criminals into the outside world, over and over and over again.
zh_text: 施羅德今天還是第一次到觀護人辦公室，他以後應該也不會有機會再來了。建築物很單調，裡面的辦公室也平淡無奇到了極點，接待處兩側都放了塑膠植物，牆上掛了一幅日落的圖片，算是室內有點吸引人目光的裝飾。根據他的想像，在這裡工作一定很無趣，跟你接觸的人來了又來，每隔幾年就犯下同樣的罪行、吸毒、搶奪他人財物、殺人，惡性循環無窮無盡。當警察的話，起碼可以打擊犯罪；觀護人讓罪犯重回外面的世界，一而再再而三，永無止境。

en_text: It’s too early to tell if Edward had time to find anything here. After talking to him he got the impression Hunter was still winging it with no idea where to go next. That made him dangerous.
zh_text: 他還無法判斷艾德華是否來得及在這裡找出什麼線索。通過電話後，他覺得杭特依然搖擺不定，不知道接下來要去哪裡。這表示他變成危險人物了。

en_text: The IT woman, Geri Shepard, is currently going through Bracken’s computer. Shepard—in her late twenties and with a body other women would kill for—is about as put out by being here as she is attractive.
zh_text: 資訊部的潔芮·雪帕正在檢查布萊肯的電腦。快三十歲的雪帕有著女人夢寐以求的好身材，意興闌珊的程度可媲美她迷人的外表。

en_text: “This couldn’t wait?” she asks for the third time already. “You’re real sure on that?”
zh_text: 「一定要現在查嗎？」她第三次提出同樣的問題。「你確定嗎？」

en_text: “You found anything yet?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「有什麼異常的地方嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: “Possibly. See here? We’ve got a list of files he accessed going back as far as you want. I still don’t see why you can’t tell me what you think Austin has done—it might make me be able to speed things up.”
zh_text: 「似乎有。看到了嗎？我已經按照你的要求列出來他看過的檔案。但是，我不懂爲什麼你不肯講你懷疑布萊肯幹了什麼好事——你要告诉我，說不定我能更快找到答案。」

en_text: “Search for Shane Kingsly,” he says, ignoring her. “When did Bracken access that file?”
zh_text: 「查查看夏恩·金斯理這個名字，」施羅德不理她的要求。「布萊肯上次看他的檔案是什麼時候？」

en_text: She clicks away at the keyboard. “Today. The twenty-fourth. Though I guess it’s the twenty-fifth now, right?”
zh_text: 她在鍵盤上按了幾下。「今天，二十四號。但應該說二十五了，對吧？」

en_text: Today would fall in line with what Bracken told them this morning. His client didn’t show up, so he went to his house looking for him. Makes sense he’d have pulled the file.
zh_text: 今天，那就符合布萊肯早上的說法。他服務的對象沒出現，所以他去他家找他。他看過檔案，也是理所當然。

en_text: “Is it standard practice for probation officers to immediately go to somebody’s house if they’ve missed an appointment?”
zh_text: 「如果受保護管束人在約定的時間沒到，觀護人立刻去他家探訪，符合標準的程序嗎？」

en_text: “It depends on the probation officer, and it depends on the person who missed their appointment. It’s not common, no, but it’s not unheard of. Seems he accessed the guy’s records yesterday too.”
zh_text: 「要看觀護人，還要看錯過約定的人是誰。一般不會立刻過去探訪，但也有人這麼做。看來他昨天也查過這個人的檔案。」

en_text: “Was there an appointment scheduled?”
zh_text: 「他們約定的時間呢？」

en_text: “Hmm . . . that’s weird. According to his planner, he wasn’t due to see Kingsly for another week.”
zh_text: 「唔···怪了。根據他的時間表，他要再過一個禮拜才會跟金斯理見面。」

en_text: “What about Adam Sinclair?” Schroder asks. Sinclair is the man Edward hit with his car.
zh_text: 「那亞當·辛克萊呢？」施羅德問。被艾德華輾過去的那個人就是辛克萊。

en_text: “Let me check. Um, November first.” “How often was he seeing Sinclair?” “Ah . . . according to this, he wasn’t.” “He wasn’t?”
zh_text: 「我看看。嗯，十一月一號。」「他跟辛克萊多久見一次？」「啊……你看，他們沒有約好時間。」「沒有？」

en_text: “No. Not according to this.”
zh_text: 「沒有。紀錄上找不到。」

en_text: “Then why’d he pull his file?” he asks.
zh_text: 「那他爲什麼要調辛克萊的檔案？」

en_text: “I’m not sure. Maybe it was in relation to somebody else he was dealing with.”
zh_text: 「我不確定。或許跟他負責的某個人有關。」

en_text: “Ryan Hann?” he says, Hann being the man Edward stabbed with a pencil.
zh_text: 「萊恩·漢恩？」漢恩被艾德華用鉿筆插死了。

en_text: “Um . . . same. November first. This is weird—Hann is also no longer under probation.”
zh_text: 「嗯……一樣，也是十一月一號。奇怪，汉恩早就脱離保護管束了。」

en_text: “Okay. Good. This is good. Can you find any other files he’d have no need to pull up that he accessed around that time period?”
zh_text: 「OK，很好。非常好。你可不可以找出十一月一號前後他看過哪些不需要他處理的檔案？」

en_text: “Hang on,” she says, and works at the keyboard for another minute. “Here, we got five more names of people no longer under probation. Wait —make that four—one of these men just died,” she says, and she twists the monitor so Schroder can take another look.
zh_text: 「等我一下，」她在鍵盤上又敲了一分鐘。「好了，另外有五個已經脫離保護管束的人。等，四個才對，有一個人才死不久。」她把螢幕轉過來給施羅德看。

en_text: He scrolls down the list. It’s a short list and it only takes a second for Arnold Langham’s name to show up. Suction Cup Guy. “Jesus,” he whispers. “He was part of it.”
zh_text: 他把名單往下拉。既然只有五個人，不到一秒鐘他就看到了阿諾·朗漢的名字。吸盤男。「天啊，」他悄聲說。「他也有份。」

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: Arnold Langham only had a criminal record for beating up his wife—but that in no way meant beating up his wife was the only criminal thing he had done. There were two possibilities he could see. Langham was involved with these other men, meaning there must be other things he was good at. He was recruited into the gang, then, leading up to the robbery, there must have been something about him the others didn’t like or couldn’t trust, and he became a liability. Shooting him or stabbing him could have brought the investigation closer to the bank robbers, but dressing him up like a pervert and throwing him off the top of a building, that pushed the investigation into a completely different direction.
zh_text: 阿諾·朗漢唯一的犯罪紀錄就是打老婆但那並不表示他犯下的罪行僅限於家暴。他還想到另外兩個可能性。朗漢跟這些人是一夥的，表示他除了打老婆，肯定還有其他的技能。他被吸收入夥，然後在搶銀行前，這傢伙一定惹到了其他人或失去了同黨的信任，變成累贅。用槍或用刀把他殺了，可能會讓警方調查到自己頭上，但把他打扮得像個變態，再從屋頂上丢下來，調查方向就會轉個一百八十度。

en_text: The second possibility was Langham wasn’t involved, but learned of the robbery and became a liability. Schroder is more inclined to go with the first possibility—it would suggest the gang was suddenly one man short, which would explain why Bracken chose Kingsly.
zh_text: 第二個猜測是朗漢沒加入這幫人，但聽到了搶劫的风聲，也對大家不利。施羅德覺得第一個猜測比較有可能，那就說明了爲什麼他們突然短少一個人，所以布萊肯才會選金斯理當車夫。

en_text: Either way, it still left Schroder with a list of four names, each belonging to a man whom Bracken recruited to steal $2.8 million in cash.
zh_text: 不論如何，施羅德還有四個名字，這四個人都被布萊肯招納入夥，搶走了兩百八十萬紐幣現鈔。

en_text: When the taxi driver drops me off he smiles with relief, as he probably does every time he drops somebody off without getting stabbed. His English is perfect when he tells me how much the fare is, but not so good when figuring out the change. Gas price increases have pushed taxi fares up astronomically over the last few years—it’s no wonder more and more people are drinking and driving. I tell him to keep the change.
zh_text: 計程車司機把我放下時，臉上現出鬆了一口氣的微笑，或許每次乘客下車，他發現自己毫髮無傷，就有這種表情。告訴我車資時，他的英語一字不差，零錢卻算錯了。過去幾年來油價高漲，計程車資也跟著狂飆一難怪愈來愈多人寧可酒後駕駛。我告訴他，不用找錢了。

en_text: I’m right next to the parking building where Jodie’s car has been for the last week. My keys are still hanging in my car, but the spare keys have been in my pocket all day. I make my way upstairs. Jodie’s car is a four-door Toyota about six years old. It starts on the first turn of the key and I let it warm up for thirty seconds. There’s a modern stereo in the center console and a GPS on top of the dashboard that both seem to be defying the law of gravity, since they haven’t fallen in some passerby’s possession. I find Jodie’s swipe card in the glove box and use it to exit the building.
zh_text: 我在立體停車場旁邊下車，過去一星期以來，茱蒂的車一直停在這裡。我的車鑰匙還掛在我車上，但備用鑰匙在口袋裡放了一整天。我上樓找到茱蒂的車，一台四門的豐田，車齡約莫六年。我一轉鑰匙，就把車子發動了，我等了三十秒，讓引擎熱起來。中央控制台上新穎的音響和儀表板上方的導航系統似乎都成功反抗了重力定律，因爲到現在都還沒被人偷走。我在置物盒裡找到茱蒂的磁卡，順利開出了停車場。

en_text: I drive back the way I came and find the shotgun exactly where I’d left it. I try calling Nat and Diana again and get the same result. I drive a few minutes out of the city and pull over.
zh_text: 我回頭走剛才走過的路，找到霰彈槍，還在原來的地方，未動分文。我又撥電話給納森和黛安娜，仍然沒人接。出城後我再開了幾分鐘，然後把車停在路邊。

en_text: I stack up the files and go through them. The names and faces stare out at me, but none of them stand out. Twenty files, all of random people who have nothing to do with the case. After ten minutes it seems it’s all been for nothing—whatever contact Bracken had with the men who killed my wife isn’t to be found in these pages. There’s no way I can make it back into the offices to check for more. I pack the files away and get moving.
zh_text: 我把檔案疊起來，開始翻閱。看到不同的名字和臉孔，沒有特別吸引我目光的檔案。二十份檔案，分屬跟搶案沒有關係的人。過了十分鐘，我覺得這一趟無功而返——在檔案裡我找不到布萊肯跟殺我妻子的人有什麼關係。我不可能再回觀護人辦公室調查。我把檔案裝進袋子裡，又上路了。

en_text: There are even fewer cars in the hospital parking lot when I get there than there were earlier tonight—mine doubles the number; the other is a van with a bunch of guys a few years younger than me leaning against it drinking. I wrap the weapon in a jacket Jodie left in the back of her car.
zh_text: 醫院停車場裡的車子比之前更少了我停進去後，車子的數量就加倍了，因爲原本只有台貨車，數名比我年輕很多的男人靠在車上喝酒。我從後座拿了茱蒂留下的外套，把霰彈槍包在裡面。

en_text: Visiting hours are over and have been for probably six or seven hours. I walk in looking like somebody who knows where they’re going and nobody says anything because there’s nobody around. Not a single person in this part of the ground floor—everybody is either at home for Christmas or working in the emergency room. I make my way down the corridor to the elevators, not leaving any bloody footprints behind because my shoe has dried up. I go up to the fifth floor and step past a nurses’ station that doesn’t have any nurses. Only about half the lights are on that were on this afternoon and it’s only about half the temperature. I reach the ward where my father is and there aren’t any police officers outside like there were this afternoon—which the accountant in me puts down to simple supply and demand. Tonight the city is demanding the most from its guardians, and the police are supplying every man who’s prepared to work overtime and ignore their family—which isn’t many, it seems.
zh_text: 探訪時間結束了，而且應該早在六七個小時前就結束了。我泰然自若，看似知道自己的去向，沒有人懷疑我，因爲連個人影都看不到。一樓這一區一個人也沒有大家都回家過耶誕節了，或者都在急診室裡。我穿過走廊來到電梯前，沒留下血腳印，因爲我的鞋底已經乾了。我到了五樓，通過裡面沒有護士的護理站。點亮的燈光比下午少了一半，溫度也降低了一半。我找到我父親的病房，外面不像今天下午停駐了警察我心中的會計師認爲這只是供應跟需求的緣故。今天晚上，基督城最需要有人守護，警方全面動員，肯丢下家人加班的人都派出去了看來肯丢下家人加班的不多。

en_text: Still, this isn’t going to be a walk in the park. There aren’t any officers here, but there is a security guard sitting in a chair reading a magazine, doing what he can to stay awake. I help him out there by showing him the shotgun. He’s in a similar situation to the one Gerald Painter was in last week—he’s sitting here earning a minimum wage, armed with nothing useful. He doesn’t even make it out of his chair. He wants to—he gets about halfway up before realizing there’s no point in moving any further. He doesn’t sit back down either—just stays suspended between the two actions.
zh_text: 但現在可不能抱著到公園散步的心態。少了警察，椅子上卻坐了個警衛在看雜誌，他正努力讓自己保持清醒。我當然要幫忙了，秀出霰彈槍，他馬上清醒得不得了。他跟上禮拜的傑拉德·潘特處境很像——坐在這裡賺最低的工資，身上一項有用的武器也沒有。他甚至不能從椅子上起來。他原本想站起來——身子起了一半，才發覺起來也沒用。他也沒坐回去——就這麼停在半空中，要站不站要坐不坐。

en_text: “Don’t say a word,” I say.
zh_text: 「給我安静。」我說。

en_text: “I won’t.” “Stand up.” “Okay.”
zh_text: 「好，我閉嘴。」「站起來。」「OK。」

en_text: “Is there anybody else here?” “Like who?”
zh_text: 「這裡還有什麼人？」「誰？」

en_text: “Police. Other security guards.” He shakes his head.
zh_text: 「警察，其他的警衛。」他搖搖頭。

en_text: “Any nurses in there?” I ask, nodding toward the ward.
zh_text: 「護士在裡面嗎？」我用下巴指指病房。

en_text: “There’s one somewhere but I haven’t seen her in about half an hour.” “Okay. You know who I am?”
zh_text: 「有個護士在外面，不過我大概半小時沒看到她了。」「OK。你知道我是誰嗎？」

en_text: He shrugs. “Am I supposed to?”
zh_text: 他聳聳肩。「我應該認識你嗎？」

en_text: “That’s my father in there you’re looking after.” “Oh shit,” he says. “Please, please, don’t kill me.” “Then pay close attention.”
zh_text: 「我老子在裡面，你在照看他。」「噢，糟了，」他說，「拜託，我求求你，饒了我吧。」

en_text: I direct him into the ward. There are six men all sleeping in the room, a combination of snoring and farting coming from every corner: if somebody lit a match the air would ignite. The curtain is no longer pulled around my father’s bed. He turns his head toward us.
zh_text: 「那你給我注意點。」我指揮他進入病房。裡面六個人都睡著了，打鼾聲和放屁聲從各個角落傳來：要有人點根柴，空氣應該會燒起來。我爹床邊的布簾沒完全拉上。他轉過頭，看到我們。

en_text: “The curtain,” he says, and nods toward it.
zh_text: 「布簾。」他對著簾子點點頭。

en_text: I reach up and pull the curtain around us. The security guard stands on the opposite side of the bed. My dad has his left arm free, but his right is still cuffed to the bed railing.
zh_text: 我伸手把布簾拉上。警衛站在病床的另一頭。我爹的左手可以亂動，右手仍銬在病床欄杆上。

en_text: “I hear you’ve had a busy day, son,” he says.
zh_text: 「兒子，聽說你今天很忙啊。」他說。

en_text: “They have Sam.”
zh_text: 「他們把小珊抓走了。」

en_text: “What?” he asks, and his face looks pained.
zh_text: 「什麼？」他滿臉驚恐。

en_text: “The men who killed Jodie. They took Sam tonight. They’re going to kill her, Dad, they’re going to kill her unless I can get her back.”
zh_text: 「殺了茱蒂的那些人。他們今天晚上把小珊抓走了。爹，他們會殺了小珊，除非我去救她，然小珊死定了。」

en_text: The security guard doesn’t seem sure what to do. He takes a small step back and ends up sitting down, most likely thinking he doesn’t get paid enough for this.
zh_text: 警衛似乎手腳不知道該往哪裡放。他向後退了一小步，結果坐到椅子上了，很有可能他心裡在想，這麼一點點薪水根本不值得。

en_text: “I had no idea,” Dad says.
zh_text: 「我沒想到會發生這種事。」爹說。

en_text: “I need names.”
zh_text: 「我要知道是誰。」

en_text: “I’ve given you a name.”
zh_text: 「我給你一個名字了。」

en_text: “It didn’t pan out. Dad, I wouldn’t be here if there were any other choices. You must have something else.”
zh_text: 「爹，結果不成功。我要有其他選擇，就不會來找你了。你一定還有事情沒告訴我。」

en_text: “Hand me that water, son.”
zh_text: 「把那杯水拿給我，兒子。」

en_text: There’s a glass of water on the stand next to the bed. I grab it for him. He takes a long slow sip before handing it back.
zh_text: 床旁的架子上有杯水，我一把抓起遞給他。他喝了好大一口，才把杯子還給我。

en_text: “Water tastes better here,” he says. “In prison, by the time the water makes it to us about half a dozen guards have already spat in it. Or worse.” “Dad . . .”
zh_text: 「外面的水比較好喝。」他說。「牢裡的水等我們喝到口，早就被五六個警衛吐過口水了。有時候還更多呢。」

en_text: “Kingsly was the driver, right?” “Yes.”
zh_text: 「金斯理是車手，對嗎？」「對。」

en_text: “So, minus the man you ran over, there are five more.” “Three more.”
zh_text: 「所以，扣掉你輾過的那個人，還有五個人。」「還有三個。」

en_text: “Three?”
zh_text: 「三個？」

en_text: I give him the details. “The monster got them,” I add. “Okay, son. Well, I have another name that can help.” “Who?”
zh_text: 我告訴他事情的始末。「怪獸把他們處理掉了。」我補了一句。「好，兒子，呃，我還知道一個人，或许也有關聯。」「誰？」「別急。」

en_text: “Not so fast.” “What?”
zh_text: 「你說什麼？」

en_text: “Twenty years is a long time,” he says. “The air inside, it tastes different. It tastes stale, it tastes of desperation. At night, tough men who try to kill you during the day cry. In winter it’s always so damn cold and in the summer it’s so damn hot and . . . twenty years, son, twenty years is a long time.” “It’s still better than what the women you killed got.” “Is it? Is it really?”
zh_text: 「二十年，好漫長呀，」他說，「裡面的空氣感覺也不一樣。感覺臭掉了，有股絕望的味道。到了晚上，白天想砍死你的硬漢也會掉淚。冬天他媽的冷，夏天他媽的熱……二十年呀，兒子，二十年好久啊。」「跟那些被你幹掉的女人比起來，坐牢沒那麼差勁吧。」「是嗎？真的嗎？」

en_text: “I think if you could ask them, they’d agree.” “I’m not so sure,” he says.
zh_text: 「你問她們啊，問得到的話，她們一定會點頭。」「我倒是不確定。」他說。

en_text: “The name?”
zh_text: 「到底是誰？」

en_text: “I’m coming with you.” “What?”
zh_text: 「我跟你一起去。」「什麼？」

en_text: “You want that name, you have to take me with you.” “They have Sam, Dad. Give me the goddamn name.” “I know they have Sam.”
zh_text: 「你要人名，就带我跟你走。」「他們把小珊抓走了，爹。告訴我那個王八蛋是誰。」「我知道他們把小珊抓走了。」

en_text: I point the shotgun at my father’s chest. He flinches. “I’m not messing around, Dad.”
zh_text: 我舉起霰彈槍，對準他的胸口。他嚇了一跳。「爹，我不會跟你開玩笑。」

en_text: “You going to shoot me?” “If I have to.”
zh_text: 「你敢開槍打死我嗎？」「有必要的話。」

en_text: “How’s that going to help you?” “It’ll make me feel better.”
zh_text: 「那對你又有什麼好處？」「起碼讓我心裡好過點。」

en_text: “That’s my boy,” he says, and then smiles. “But you’re not going to pull that trigger.”
zh_text: 「乖兒子，」他說著微微一笑。「但你不會扣下扳機。」

en_text: “Oh?”
zh_text: 「怎麼說？」

en_text: “Too noisy. You won’t make it out of here.” “Don’t be so sure about that.”
zh_text: 「會驚醒很多人。你逃不出去的。」

en_text: “And you’d be leaving without a name. You could look around, maybe try to find some drugs or tools to torture me, but the quickest and easiest option,” he says, then rattles the handcuff against the frame, “is to take me with you.”
zh_text: 「話不要說得太早。」「而且你也不會聽到那個王八蛋的名字。你可以到處看看，找些藥逼我吃，拿工具來折磨我，但最快最簡單的方法，」他的手銬敲著欄杆啷啷作響，「就是帶我一起去。」

en_text: “I can’t.”
zh_text: 「沒辦法。」

en_text: “You can if you want to get your daughter back.”
zh_text: 「你要把女兒找回來，就要讓我一起去。」

en_text: Take him with us. Things will go a lot quicker.
zh_text: 带他走吧。那就簡單多了。

en_text: “Keys?” I ask, pointing the gun at the guard.
zh_text: 「鑰匙呢？」我拿槍指著警衛。

en_text: “I, ah . . . don’t have them.”
zh_text: 「我，啊……不在我身上。」

en_text: “Yeah you do,” Dad says. “They have to in case they need to rush me back into surgery.”
zh_text: 「你一定有鑰匙，」爹說，「一定有，萬一我要動緊急手術怎麼辦？」

en_text: The guard stands up slowly and digs into his pocket.
zh_text: 警衛慢慢站起身來，開始掏口袋。

en_text: “There was a time when there’d be more people guarding me,” Dad says. “Back when I was younger, when I was somebody to be feared. Now, nobody knows who I am.”
zh_text: 「曾有一度，他們會派更多人看著我，」爹說，「那時候我還年輕，那時候大家都怕我。現在，沒有人知道我是誰。」

en_text: “That’s funny,” I say, “because everybody knows who I am.”
zh_text: 「好好笑，」我說，「因爲大家都知道我是誰。」

en_text: The security guard leans in and unlocks the cuff, then pulls away fast, expecting my dad to try dragging a scalpel across his throat. Nothing happens. My dad lies in the same position and massages his wrist.
zh_text: 警衛靠過來，把手銬解開，又快速向後退，深怕我爹拿把手術刀拖過他的喉嚨。沒事。我爹仍用同樣的姿勢躺著，摩挲著自己的手腕。

en_text: “I’m going to need a wheelchair,” he says.
zh_text: 「我需要輪椅。」他說。

en_text: “You can’t walk?”
zh_text: 「你不能走路嗎？」

en_text: “I got stabbed today, son, so no, I can’t walk. At least not that well.”
zh_text: 「兒子，我今天被刺傷了，所以不能，我沒辦法走路。能走也走不快。」

en_text: I point the shotgun at the guard again and give him a fresh set of instructions, and a few seconds later he’s lying on the floor naked with one hand wrapped through the base of the bed frame and cuffed to his ankle. I take his phone and keys and step back to the other side of the curtain. The other five men still appear to be asleep. A nurse walks past the open doorway to the corridor but doesn’t look in. She’s probably so used to never seeing a security guard sitting outside the room that she doesn’t notice him missing. I give her a few seconds’ head start, then follow her out. She goes one way and I go the other, heading toward a row of wheelchairs I spotted earlier.
zh_text: 我又拿槍指著警衛，下了新的命令，幾秒後他赤裸裸躺在地上，一隻手繞過床架底部，跟他的腳踝銬在一起。我拿走了他的手機和鑰匙，走到布簾外面。另外五個人仍然睡得很甜。門口閃過了一名護士，但她沒有往裡面看。或許病房外沒有警衛才是她習慣的樣子，所以她沒注意到少了一個人。我讓她走過去，過了幾秒就跟到她身後。她繼續走，我卻轉了個彎，朝著一列我剛才看到的輪椅走過去。

en_text: I get back to my father and half of me expects him to be gone and the other half expects him to have killed the guard, but nothing has changed—he’s still lying on the bed. I slip the IV needle out of his wrist and help him into the security guard’s clothes, which are a bit big but better than the hospital gown. He winces and breathes heavily, and does more of the same when I get him into the wheelchair. He holds his hands over the area where half a day ago surgeons were busy at work, and he keeps them snug against the wound as if trying to hold parts of himself inside.
zh_text: 回到病房後，我暗自期許父親已經走了，卻又希望他已經把警衛殺了，但一切都跟剛才一樣——他還躺在床上。我把他手腕上的點滴拔出來，幫他換上警衛的衣服，有點大，但比醫院的袍子好看多了。他皺皺眉，開始喘氣，我扶他坐到輪椅上，他喘得更厲害了。他用雙手捧著半天前被外科醫生處理過的地方，用力搗著傷口，彷彿怕內臟掉出來。

en_text: “Stay quiet,” I say to the guard. “Let us get out of here without having to shoot any nurses.”
zh_text: 「不要發出聲音，」我對警衛說，「讓我們安安靜靜地出去，不需要開槍送掉護士的小命。」

en_text: “Okay.”
zh_text: 「OK。」

en_text: I have to put the gun in my father’s lap so I can push the wheelchair. We reach the corridor. Dad’s hands don’t ever extend beyond the wound. We reach the elevators. I hide the shotgun behind my body when the doors open on the ground floor, then put it back in my father’s lap when nobody shows up. I wheel him out of the hospital and out into the parking lot and past the same group of teenagers leaning against the van, who show interest in the shotgun by all becoming immensely quiet. I help Dad into the car and can’t figure out how to fold the wheelchair into the boot, so leave it behind. I figure this entire thing should have been more difficult. I figure getting in to see my dad should have been hard enough, let alone getting him out. I figure a few years ago it would have been. A few years ago there were enough people left to care enough about paying one or two cops overtime or shifting some resources to have them sit beside him. If they can’t pay them enough to protect my daughter, they sure won’t pay them enough to guard an old man.
zh_text: 我得把槍放在爹腿上，才能好好推輪椅。我們到了走廊上，爹的雙手仍繄緊摀住傷口。到了電梯裡，我把槍藏在身後，到了一樓後，沒看到别人，我又把槍放回爹腿上。我把他推出醫院，到了停車場，又經過那群靠在貨車上的青少年，他們看到那把槍，全都安靜下來了。我把爹扶到車上，但不知道怎麼把輪椅折起來放到後車廂裡，只好丢在一旁。我想，也太順利了吧。我本來以爲要見到我爹就很難了，更不用說還能把他弄出醫院。我猜，幾年前就不會這麼順利。幾年前還有人願意撥出足夠的資金來付一兩名警察的加班費，或想辦法輪調一些人來看著他。如果他們沒辦法給警察更好的薪水來保護我女兒，當然也不會付錢讓他們來看守一個老頭子。

en_text: “Where to?” I ask.
zh_text: 「去哪裡？」我問。

en_text: “First I need some food.” “Dad . . .”
zh_text: 「我想先吃點東西。」「爹...」

en_text: “I haven’t had a real meal in twenty years, son.” “We don’t have time.”
zh_text: 「我已經二十年沒吃過眞正的食物了，兒子。」「沒時間了。」

en_text: “We’ll make the time. I’m sure there’ll be a McDonald’s on the way.” “On the way to where?”
zh_text: 「一定有時間。路上一定會碰到麥當勞。」「去哪裡的路上？」

en_text: “On the way to the next name on the list,” he says, and I pull away from the curb and follow my father’s directions.
zh_text: 「去找名單上的下一個人。」我發動車子，讓我父親指路。

en_text: Turns out the Serial Killer choice of food isn’t a Happy Meal, but a Big Mac. Dad complains how it falls apart in his hands but still eats it as I drive, probably faster than any Big Mac has ever been eaten.
zh_text: 我還以爲連續殺人魔會選快樂兒童餐，不過他點了大麥克。爹抱怨他的漢堡拿在手裡會一直散開，但我邊開車，他邊把漢堡吃下肚，或許創下了迅速吃完大麥克的世界紀錄。

en_text: “I don’t think your doctor would approve,” I say.
zh_text: 「你吃麥當勞，會讓醫生皺眉頭吧。」我說。

en_text: “Probably not,” he answers, following it with a Coke, “but he probably wouldn’t have approved of me being stabbed either.”
zh_text: 「或許吧，」他又開始喝可樂，「但我被刺傷了，應該也會讓他皺眉頭。」

en_text: “Want to tell me about it?”
zh_text: 「要告訴我你被刺傷的經過嗎？」

en_text: “Not much to tell,” he says, then takes another bite.
zh_text: 「沒什麼好說的。」他繼續吃剩下的東西。

en_text: I keep driving. Dad works away at the fries. When he’s done, he balls up the wrappers and tosses everything out the window.
zh_text: 我把車往前開。爹把薯條吃下肚。食物一掃而空後，他把包裝紙揉成一團，把所有的東西丢到車窗外。

en_text: “What?” he says. “People don’t throw things out the window these days?”
zh_text: 「怎樣？」他說。「現在不流行往窗外丢垃圾了嗎？」

en_text: “Where are we heading?”
zh_text: 「我們要去哪裡？」

en_text: “It all looks the same,” he says. “Newer, maybe, but not much. A couple of apartment complexes, some new homes, other than that it’s like I was here yesterday.”
zh_text: 「都沒變，」他說，「或許變新了一點，但變化不大。幾棟公寓大樓，幾棟新房子，其餘的看起来就跟我坐牢前一模一樣。」

en_text: “Fascinating, Dad, it really is. Now, where are we heading?” “You’ve killed four men starting with Shane Kingsly, is that right?” “Something like that.”
zh_text: 「唷，爹，很好，真的很好。好，我們該往哪裡去？」「你已經殺了四個人，第一個是夏恩·金斯理，對不對？」「好像吧。」

en_text: “So you’ve been listening to the monster, as you call it.” “Something like that.”
zh_text: 「所以你也聽那東西的話了，你說它叫怪獸。」「或许吧。」

en_text: “And now the rest of them have Sam and you’re going to do what it takes to get her back.”
zh_text: 「現在，還沒死的人把小珊抓走了，你會不計一切代價，只想把她救回來。」

en_text: “What’s your point?”
zh_text: 「你想說什麼？」

en_text: “My point is that we’re certainly alike.” “We’re nothing alike.”
zh_text: 「我想說，有其父必有其子。」

en_text: “Whatever you say, Jack.” “Where to?”
zh_text: 「我不認爲。」「傑克，隨便你愛怎麼說。」「去哪裡？」

en_text: “You know what, son, suddenly I don’t feel so good,” he says, and he grips his stomach.
zh_text: 「兒子，我告訴你，我突然覺得不對勁。」他抱住肚子。

en_text: I slow down. “I’ll take you back to the hospital.”
zh_text: 我放慢了車速。「我送你回醫院去。」

en_text: “No, no, it’s not that. My stomach’s bloated. Oh shit, I need to find a bathroom. This food, I haven’t eaten food like this in twenty years, oh shit, oh shit, this is going to be bad.”
zh_text: 「不，不是，跟傷口沒有關係。我肚子好脹。噢，糟糕了，我要找廁所。剛吃的那些東西，我二十年沒吃過麥當勞了，噢，不行了，噢，完蛋了，眞的要糟糕了。」

en_text: “Just hold on,” I say.
zh_text: 「忍一忍。」我說。

en_text: “That’s great advice, son,” he says, doubling over and holding an arm across his stomach.
zh_text: 「兒子，你說得倒輕鬆。」他彎下腰，抱緊自己的肚子。

en_text: I make a left and drive to a nearby service station, pulling up around the side where there’s a bathroom door and Dad, hunched over, makes his way inside. I wait inside the car and five minutes later he comes back out, his skin even paler than when he went in.
zh_text: 等，過了五分鐘，他出來了，臉色比進去前還要蒼白。我向左轉，開進一座加油站，把車停到廁所門前，爹彎著腰蹣跚走進去。我坐在車子裡面等，過了五分鐘，他出來了，臉色比進去前還要蒼白。

en_text: “It’s going to take a while getting used to the outside world,” he says. “Don’t get too used to it. Once I get Sam back I’m taking you in.” “You don’t mean that.”
zh_text: 「要過一陣子才會習慣外面的世界。」他說「不需要習慣。等小珊回來，我就送你回去。」「你不是認真的吧。」

en_text: “Get in the car, Dad.”
zh_text: 「爹，快上車。」

en_text: He gets in the car and we’re back on the road. His skin is clammy and he doesn’t look too good: I’m not sure whether it’s the food or the stabbing he took earlier in the day. The roads are empty except for an occasional taxi taking the drunk home, or other killers out there looking for their daughters.
zh_text: 他上了車，我們又上路了。他的皮膚濕冷，面容慘澹：不知道是麥當勞，還是他稍早受的那一刺。路上偶爾有一台把醉漢載回家的計程車，除此之外空空如也，只有在外尋找女兒的殺人犯。

en_text: Dad gives me the address and I punch it into the GPS unit and it gives us the directions. Dad stares out the window watching the city, remembering it as best as he can. Occasionally we come across a new intersection that confuses him, but for the most part he knows his way around. I wonder if I’d be doing as good a job as him if I’d been inside for twenty years. I suspect there are plenty of other things my dad is still good at, other things that instinct and muscle memory would help him complete.
zh_text: 爹給了我地址，我輸入導航系統，計算出路線。爹看著窗外的城市風光，盡力想起他曾有的回憶。穿過他沒走過的新路口，他會有些迷惘，但一路上他大概都指出方向。要是我也坐了二十年牢，或許認路的能力跟他根本沒法比。我猜，爹會的東西眞不少，本能和肌肉記憶依然保持在很好的狀態。

en_text: The neighborhood the GPS directs us into is another of the areas hit heavy by the virus—only this one has been hit by a rust epidemic too: the cars parked out front are all beaten up and gardens as dry as a bone. It’s all out of date, as if the GPS has brought us to 1982 instead. Dad’s still wobbly when I get him out of the car, but nowhere near as clammy as he was ten minutes ago.
zh_text: 導航系統帶我們來到另一個染滿病毒的區域，不過這區還有一個毛病到處都生鐤了：房子前停的车子都又破又舊，花園乾枯如沙漠。所有的東西都過時了，彷彿導航系統把我們帶回一九八二。我把爹從車子裡扶出來，他仍走不穩，但不像十分鐘前那麼軟弱無力。

en_text: “Tyler Layton,” Dad says. “He one of the guys?” “He’s why we’re here.”
zh_text: 「泰勒·雷頓。」爹說。「他也是搶匪？」

en_text: I look at the street and the houses and the cars and I think, I’ve been here before, maybe not this exact location but certainly one just like it, certainly in a similar frame of mind to the one I’m in now, except instead of the monster in the passenger seat it’s my father—a different type of monster but a monster nonetheless. Maybe we’re all here, Dad’s darkness and my monster riding in the backseat, chatting to each other, comparing stories and wagering on the outcome of the night. Schroder was wrong when he said the city is on a precipice. He’s wrong in thinking it can still be saved. Just ask Jodie.
zh_text: 「我們要先找他。」我看看街道，看看周遭的房子跟車子，有種似曾相識的感覺，或許地點不太一樣，但真的很像，當時的心情也跟現在差不多，而副駕駛座上不是怪獸，換成我爹了——不同類型的怪獸，但他絕對也是怪獸。或许我們一起來了，爹的闍黑跟我的怪獸都坐在後座，聊得很愉快，分享自己經歷，拿當晚的成果來打賭。施羅德說這座城岌岌可危，他錯了。他認爲這座城還有機會得救，也錯了。不信的話，他應該問茱蒂的意見。

en_text: “Tell me about him,” I say. “There isn’t much to tell.” “There has to be something.”
zh_text: 「這人怎麼樣？」我問。「沒什麼好說的。」「一定有東西可以講吧。」

en_text: “What do you want to hear, son? That he’s a bad person who has whatever is coming to him coming to him?”
zh_text: 「兒子，你想聽到什麼樣的答案？他是壞人，能夠爲所欲爲？」

en_text: “Something like that.” “Let’s go inside.”
zh_text: 「類似吧。」「我們進去吧。」

en_text: I follow Dad up to the front doorstep. We’re only a couple of hours away until the dawn lights up this part of the world. It’s becoming routine to me now. I knock on the door a couple of times and wait a minute before knocking again, and when the guy comes to the door I jam the shotgun into his face—and the rest is so familiar now I don’t even need the monster.
zh_text: 我跟著爹走上前門的台階。再過兩個小時，黎明就會降臨在這個時區。我熟練地敲了兩下門，等了一分鐘，又繼續敲門，那人開了門，我用霰彈槍堵住他的臉一接下來的步驟我也駕輕就熟，甚至不需要怪獸幫忙。

en_text: Tyler Layton is exactly like the kind of person you’d expect to hold up a service station or a bank with a shotgun—except maybe a bit older than I’d expected. A shaved head with tattoos adorning his scalp, prison tear tattoos raining down his face, he’s around ten years shy of Dad’s age. He doesn’t say a single word from the moment he sees the shotgun to the moment my dad finishes tying him up with cord he cuts from the venetian blinds. We don’t get into any semantics about right and wrong and the ends justifying the means.
zh_text: 泰勒·雷頓有張會持槍搶劫加油站或銀行的臉——不過他的年齡似乎比我預期的更老。頭髮剃光了，頭皮上有刺青，臉上則有在監獄裡留下的一串淚珠刺青，他大概比爹小十歲。看到霰彈槍後，他一語不發，等爹用百葉簾上割下來的繩子把他綁起來，他仍保持緘默。不需要爭執誰對誰錯，也不需要爭論我們是否不擇手段。

en_text: “Start talking,” I say.
zh_text: 「說話啊。」我說。

en_text: “About what?”
zh_text: 「說什麼？」

en_text: “About my daughter. Where is she?”
zh_text: 「我女兒，她在哪裡？」

en_text: “This your son, Jack?” Tyler asks, watching my father.
zh_text: 「傑克，這你兒子？」雷頓問我父親。

en_text: “Answer the damn question,” I say to Tyler.
zh_text: 「快回答我，王八蛋。」我對雷頓說。

en_text: “I don’t know anything about your daughter,” he says, keeping his eyes on Dad. “Been a long time, Jack. The security guard uniform doesn’t suit you.”
zh_text: 「我不知道你女兒怎樣了，」他仍盯著我爹。「傑克，好久不見了。這身警衛的制服不適合你。」

en_text: “Not that long,” my dad says. “Not for me. Seems like it was only yesterday.”
zh_text: 「也不算很久，」爹說，「對我來說，就像昨天的記憶。」

en_text: “It’s been four years,” Tyler says.
zh_text: 「四年了。」雷頓說。

en_text: “Where’s my daughter?” I ask.
zh_text: 「我女兒呢？」我問。

en_text: “What’s he talking about, Jack?” he asks my father.
zh_text: 「傑克，他在嚷什麼？」他問我父親。

en_text: “What the hell is going on here?” I ask.
zh_text: 「這到底是怎麼一回事？」我問。

en_text: “I knew your father real well,” Tyler says, “if you catch my drift. Quite a few times if I remember correctly—though after the first few times I stopped remembering. Was it the same for you, Jack?”
zh_text: 「我跟你爸爸是老朋友嘍，」泰勒說，「你聽清楚了吧。如果我沒記錯，應該有好幾次只是剛開始那幾次過了以後，我就沒記了。傑克，你呢？也一樣嗎？」

en_text: “Tyler here was kind enough to introduce me to one of the darker elements of prison,” my father says, but there is nothing kind-sounding about his voice at all. “He was there when I first got thrown in jail. My first night there and he broke four of my fingers and cracked two molars and shredded my asshole so hard I couldn’t sit down for a month. I was barely fixed up before he went at it again. He was in and out of jail over the years, but he always came looking for me.”
zh_text: 「雷頓啊，人很好，他讓我看到監獄裡更黑暗的一面，」爹說，但從他聲音裡聽不出來這個人有什麼好。「我剛進去的時候，就碰到他了。第一天晚上，他打斷我四根手指頭，打裂我兩顆臼齒，還把老子的屁眼整個磨爛了，我一整個月都沒辦法好好坐下來。傷口還沒好，他又插進去了。這些年來，他進進出出好幾次，每次都來找我麻煩。」

en_text: “And now you’ve come looking for me,” he says.
zh_text: 「現在換你找我麻煩了。」他說。

en_text: “What the hell, Dad? Does he have anything to do with Jodie or Sam?” “No,” Dad says.
zh_text: 「爹，搞什麼鬼？他跟茱蒂和小珊都没有關係吧？」「没有。」爹說。

en_text: “Then why are we here?”
zh_text: 「那我們來這幹囌？」

en_text: “If we had more time,” Dad says, talking to Tyler, “I’d cut you apart piece by piece.”
zh_text: 「如果我們不趕時間的話，」爹對雷頓說，「我會把你切成一塊一塊。」

en_text: Tyler doesn’t answer him. For all his attempts to act as if he doesn’t care, like this is just one more day in the life of one really tough bastard, there is a fear in his eyes identical to the look in that dog’s eyes twenty years ago when it was chomping on a steak full of nails. He tightens the muscles in his arms.
zh_text: 雷頓沒答腔。雖然他極力裝得不在乎，彷彿像他這樣頑強的惡棍被人綁起來用槍指著根本是家常便飯，但他的眼神卻讓我想起二十年前那條狗，大嚼扎滿釘子的牛排時，牠的眼神就像雷頓一樣充滿恐懼。他手臂上的肌肉繃緊了。

en_text: “I always knew prison was going to be tough,” Dad says. “I always knew it was going to be one of those places that turns out exactly as awful as you figured it would be before you ever set foot in the place. Thing is—” he says, and then I interrupt him.
zh_text: 「我早就知道坐牢不好過，」爹說，「不需要眞正去坐牢，我就知道了，這種地方就是那麼可怕。重點是——」他還要說下去，卻被我打斷了。

en_text: “Dad, we don’t have time for this. Sam is out there, we have to find her.”
zh_text: 「爹，没時間了。小珊不知道在哪裡，我們得先去找她。」

en_text: He looks at me, his eyes sharp, cutting into me. After a few seconds, he nods.
zh_text: 他瞪著我，凌厲的眼神切入我的身體。過了幾秒鐘，他點點頭。

en_text:
“You’re right, son,” he says. He puts his hands out. “The shotgun?” “No,” I say. “I didn’t free you so you could kill people.”
“Yes you did.”
zh_text:
「兒子，你說得沒錯。」他伸出手來。「槍呢？」
「不行，」我說，「我把你帶出來，並不是爲了讓你胡亂殺人。」
「你带我出來，不就是要我殺人。」

en_text: “Not people who have nothing to do with what happened.” “Give me the gun, son.”
zh_text: 「兒子，把槍給我。」

en_text: “Don’t give it to him,” Tyler says.
zh_text: 「不要給他。」雷頓說。

en_text: Give it to him. Let him take control for a bit. We’ll get over this speed bump and find Sam.
zh_text: 把槍給他，讓他當一下老大。過了這個關卡，就能找到小珊。

en_text: “He’s a bad man, son. If we turn our back on him other people will suffer for it.”
zh_text: 「他是個大壞蛋。要是我們不把他處理掉，其他人就慘了。」

en_text: Give him the shotgun.
zh_text: 把槍給他。

en_text: “Do you want to know how many people he’s hurt? How many women he’s raped? Women like Jodie? Teenagers like the kind of girl Sam will become?”
zh_text: 「你知道他害了多少人嗎？你知道他強姦了多少女人嗎？像茱蒂那樣的女人？像小珊未來會長成的少女？」

en_text: I hand him the shotgun.
zh_text: 我把霰彈槍送到他手上。

en_text: It’s all happening so fast. The night is becoming absolute chaos. Jack Hunter has escaped—helped by Edward—and Schroder has to push that fact to the back of his mind right at this moment and deal with it soon. At this rate he’s doubting he’ll make it home on Christmas Day for even five minutes. His wife will hate him, his daughter might too. Thankfully his son is only a few months old so at least somebody won’t be pissed at him.
zh_text: 一波未平，一波又起。一整晚混亂不斷。在艾德華的協助下，傑克·杭特逃出了醫院施羅德不得不放下他對艾德華的看法，先處理最急迫的問題。他想，再這樣下去，耶誕節可能連回家五分鐘都回不去。他老婆會大怒，他女兒可能也會生氣。還好他兒子才幾個月大，起碼有一個人不會氣他。

en_text: The SWAT team is running at about 50 percent, the other half having already left for the holidays or drunk already and not returning Schroder’s calls, giving him a team short on manpower but a team nonetheless, still extremely capable. Schroder has already died once tonight and doesn’t want that to be the start of a pattern. He has a better use for the team than he did half an hour ago, with them driving around looking for Hunter.
zh_text: 武装防禦小組來了大概一半，另一半已經去度假了，或者已經醉倒，沒回覆施羅德的召集，雖然人力不足，仍是一支精英隊伍。施羅德今晚已經死過一次，不想再嘗嘗看死亡的滋味。跟半小時前比起來，他已經爲防禦小組定了更好的目標，要他們開車到處尋找杭特。

en_text: When his cell phone rings again, it’s Anthony Watts, a detective who is currently with Edward Hunter’s in-laws.
zh_text: 手機又響了，警探安東尼·瓦茲打來的，他正在艾德華的岳父岳母家。

en_text: “They don’t recognize any of the photos from the files,” Watts says. “I mean, the only one they recognize is the victim lying dead on their living-room floor.”
zh_text: 「檔案上的照片他們都不認得，」瓦茲說，「我是說，他們只認得死在他們家起居室那個被害人。」

en_text: “Okay. Get back down to the probation offices. If Bracken scrambled to put all this together since finding Kingsly’s body, then maybe this other person has a file he accessed today. It could give you a fresh set of mug shots.”
zh_text: 「OK，你先回觀護人辦公室。如果布萊肯一找到金斯理的屍體就把這些檔案都打開來看，或許這人的檔案他今天也看過。你就可以再弄一組嫌犯照片出來。」

en_text: Kelvin Johnson is on the top of the list of six names he printed out, predominantly because three of the other people are dead—including Ryan Hann, who died by pencil. Bracken wasn’t on the list, giving Johnson a one-in-three chance of being the first. Incarcerated nine years ago for the robbery of a jewelry store in which a sales assistant permanently lost the use of one arm after he shot her, Johnson was released four years ago and upon his release had contact with his parole officer once a week for two years, then once a month for the following year. As of a year ago the justice system was satisfied that Kelvin Johnson was a model Christchurch citizen, having undergone the exact amount necessary of jail time and a probation period afterward.
zh_text: 他印出來六個名字，第一個要找的是凱爾文·強森，因爲其他三個人已經死了包括被鉛筆插死的萊恩·漢恩。布萊肯不在名單上，所以強森名列第一的機率高達三分之一。強森九年前因爲搶劫珠寶店而入獄，射傷了店員，害她一隻手臂殘廢，四年前出獄，出獄後每個星期都要跟觀護人聯絡，持續兩年，第三年每個月聯絡一次即可。一年前，司法機構很滿意強森表現得就像個模範基督城市民，坐牢坐得夠久，後來接受觀護的時間也夠長。

en_text: Johnson lives in a government-subsidized house in an area of town that seems to attract violence the same way rotten food attracts flies. At the moment they’re all parked four blocks away, a miniature command post set up.
zh_text: 強森住在一棟尖頂小房子裡，附近暴力事件频傳，就像腐爛的食物總會招惹蒼蠅。他們把車子全都停在四個街口外，成立了迷你指揮所。

en_text: “Two things,” Schroder says, and the team of men listen intently. “First, we don’t know for a fact Johnson was part of the robbery. Second thing is, even if he was, we don’t know that he has anything to do with Sam Hunter being kidnapped, or if she is here. That means we need to be careful; we need to make sure there are no slipups, and that we get him in one piece. Any questions?”
zh_text: 「有兩點要注意，」施羅德說，其他人都凝神聽著。「首先，我們不確定強森是不是搶犯。第二點，就算他搶了銀行，我們不確定他是否涉及小珊的綁架案，也不知道小珊在不在這裡。所以我們要很謹愼；我們得注意，一點差錯也不能出，我們得活捉他。有問題嗎？」

en_text: There are always questions. They spend another ten minutes going over it. When they’re ready, two vans pull in to the street where Johnson lives, one from each side. A drive-by three minutes earlier had confirmed there were no lights on inside the house, and no signs of life. A team of two people are parked on the street behind the house in case Johnson climbs the back fence in an attempt to get away.
zh_text: 總有人有問題。他們又花了十分鐘討論問題。準備好了之後，兩台貨車開到強森家那條街上，一邊停了一台。三分鐘前探路時，已經確認他家裡沒開燈，也沒有人走動。兩個人把車開到後面的街上，免得強森爬過他家後面的圍籬逃走。

en_text: The SWAT team members move quickly. They’re all dressed in black and they hit the house hard and fast, busting in the door, and then there’s thirty seconds of shouting and no gunfire. Schroder and Landry wait out on the street, and a minute later Johnson is led out in a pair of pajama bottoms and handcuffs.
zh_text: 武装防禦小組的動作很快。他們一身黑，迅捷有力地踹開了大門，叫嚷了三十秒，沒聽到槍來。響。施羅德和藍德里在街上等待，過了一分鐘，強森被帶出來了，下身穿著睡褲，雙手被銬起

en_text: “There’s nobody else,” Officer Liam Marshall, the man leading the unit, says. “No sign of any girl. The house is secure.”
zh_text: 「只有他一個人，」負責指揮的警官連恩·馬歇爾說，「沒看到小女孩。屋裡沒問題。」

en_text: “Get him in the van,” Landry says. “I’ll try to convince him to talk while you check out the house.”
zh_text: 「讓他進貨車，」藍德里說，「你們去搜房子，我來勸他說實話。」

en_text: “Maybe he doesn’t know where she is.” “Maybe,” Landry says, “but we’ll know soon.”
zh_text: 「或许他不知道小女孩在哪裡。」「或许吧，」藍德里說，「等一下就知道了。」

en_text: It takes Schroder three minutes to find the money. It’s hidden above the manhole in the ceiling. Things are always hidden up there; he figures there isn’t a burglar yet who hasn’t considered hiding something in the roof.
zh_text: 施羅德只花三分鐘就找到錢在哪裡。強森把錢藏在天花板的通道裡。大家總愛把錢藏在天花板上；想要破門搶劫的人一定都會先去查屋頂。

en_text: He calls Landry and updates him. “He’s definitely one of them, but there’s nothing else in the house to suggest he had the girl here. If he’d taken her, he’d be with her now.”
zh_text: 他打電話給藍德里，通知他最新的狀況。「他一定是搶匪，但屋裡找不到小女孩的蹤跡。要是他綁了小珊，她應該在這裡。」

en_text: “Not if he’s already killed her,” Landry says.
zh_text: 「如果他殺了小珊，你們當然找不到她。」藍德里說。

en_text: “I know. I know,” Schroder answers, and hangs up.
zh_text: 「我知道，我明白。」施羅德邊回答邊掛上了電話。

en_text: “One down and two to go,” Marshall says, “and we’re set for the next location.”
zh_text: 「結束了，還有兩個，」馬歇爾說，「我們準備好進攻下一個地點了。」

en_text: “Let’s go,” Schroder says, and he gets in his car. He’s about two minutes away from the second name on the list when the call comes in of a gunshot. The address doesn’t match either of the other two addresses he still has to visit, and he wonders if the gunshot is random, or whether it means Hunter has found his daughter, or brought himself one step closer.
zh_text: 「走吧。」施羅德回到自己的車裡。再過兩分鐘，就要到達名單上第二個人的住所，卻有人打電話來報告槍擊案。地址跟他要去的另外兩個地方都不相符，他納悶槍擊是否跟本案無關，还是杭特找到了女兒，抑或他快找到女兒了。

en_text: Tyler’s screams stop around the same time we reach the car. The gunshot tore through him and the seat of the chair and made it collapse into a splintery heap. His genitals and lower intestines are splashed out all over the floor. The arteries in his thighs are all torn up and coating the room in squirts of blood.
zh_text: 我們走到車子旁邊的時候，雷蟦的尖叫聲也停止了。子彈撕裂了他的身體，穿過座椅，把椅子打爛成一堆木屑。他的生殖器和腸子噴得滿地都是。大腿上的動脈全都裂開了，屋裡濺滿了血。

en_text: Could be this is the kind of neighborhood where nobody would even call the police, but we’re not hanging about to take a poll. We reach the car and pick a direction and stick with it.
zh_text: 在這一區聽到槍響，應該沒有人會叫警察，不過我們也不想留下來看結果。我們上了車，選定了方向，開動了車子。

en_text: “Holy shit, Dad, you just killed an innocent man.” “No I didn’t.”
zh_text: 「真的很糟糕，爹，你剛殺了一個無辜的人。」「沒，我沒有。」

en_text: “What? You just—”
zh_text: 「什麼？你剛才···」

en_text: “You said innocent, Jack. Tyler was far from innocent. You could see that right off, right? It’s why you gave me the gun.”
zh_text: 「傑克，你說無辜的人。雷頓無辜？才怪！你一看到他就知道了，對不對？所以你才把槍給我。」

en_text: “I gave you the gun to speed things along, that’s all,” I say. “Sam is out there somewhere, and you’re turning all of this into you. You won’t help me until I get you out of hospital. Then we go and see somebody who has nothing to do with what we’re trying to do. All you’re doing is proving we are absolutely nothing alike.”
zh_text: 「我把槍給你，只是想快點上路而已，」我說，「小珊不知道在哪裡，你卻只想到自己。我不幫你逃出醫院，你就不幫我。然後我們來找的這個人跟小珊的綁票案一點關係也沒有。你的所作所爲，只證明了我們一點也不像。」

en_text: “He had it coming,” Dad says. “And the darkness—it needed to be fed.” “To be fed? He said he hadn’t seen you in four years. How’d you know where to go? No way you would have been keeping tabs on where he lived, not unless you were planning on making a visit. How’d you know you’d be getting the chance?”
zh_text: 「他活該，」爹說，「還有闍黑——闍黑需要得到满足。」「得到滿足？他說他跟你四年沒見了。你怎麼知道該去哪裡找他？你怎麼可能知道他住在哪裡？除非你一心想要找到他。你怎麼知道會碰上這個機會？」

en_text: “I didn’t know,” he says. “But before you showed up at the hospital, I was able to find out.”
zh_text: 「我不知道，」他說，「但你還沒來醫院前，我就找到了。」

en_text: “How?”
zh_text: 「怎麼發現？」

en_text: “It doesn’t matter.”
zh_text: 「不關你的事。」

en_text: “Why though? Why’d you want to find out?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼呢？你爲什麼要找他的住址？」

en_text: “You just sermonized about me making all of this about myself,” he says, “now you’re the one doing it. I thought you only cared about finding Sam.”
zh_text: 「你才剛對我說教，說我只想到自己，」他說，「現在換你了。我覺得你只想去找小珊。」

en_text: “And it’s obvious that’s not your priority at all,” I answer. “Because it all doesn’t fit properly.”
zh_text: 「顯然你不在乎能不能找到小珊，」我回答，「因爲你只顧自己想幹什麼。」

en_text: “You want my help or not?”
zh_text: 「你到底要不要我幫你？」

en_text: “That depends on whether you’re going to actually start helping me, and I’m thinking you have no idea who to speak to next.”
zh_text: 「那就看你肯不肯幫我了，我覺得你也不知道接下來要找誰。」

en_text: “Okay, okay,” he says. “Bracken was the parole officer, right?”
zh_text: 「好啦，好啦，」他說，「布萊肯是觀護人，對不對？」

en_text:
“Right. But he took the money from Kingsly and didn’t tell the others.
Everybody thinks I have it.” “You do have it.”
zh_text:
「對。但他拿了金斯理的錢，沒告訴其他人。大家都以爲我拿了。」
「你真的拿了。」

en_text: “Yeah, I have it now, but I didn’t have it earlier, and now I don’t know how to get hold of any of them.”
zh_text: 「對，現在在我手上，但之前我沒拿，現在也不知道該怎麼找到那些人。」

en_text: “Maybe they know how to get hold of you? You took his phone, right?” “Yeah—but nobody’s called.”
zh_text: 「或许他們知道怎麼找到你？你拿了他的手機，不是嗎？」「對可是没人打來。」

en_text: “He give you anything, anything at all?” Dad asks.
zh_text: 「他還給了你什麼？有什麼線索嗎？」爹問。

en_text: “Bracken? No. Nothing.” “You search his house?”
zh_text: 「布萊肯？沒，什麼也沒有。」「你搜過他家了嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah. And his office. There was a cell number in his phone but it doesn’t connect.”
zh_text: 「搜過了，辦公室我也搜了。他的通訊錄裡有個手機號碼，但沒人接。」

en_text: “You went to his office?”
zh_text: 「你去過他的辦公室？」

en_text: “I didn’t find much. Just some files that didn’t lead anywhere.” “Where are they?”
zh_text: 「没找到什麼。只拿了一些看起来没用的檔案。」「檔案在哪裡？」

en_text: I nod toward the backseat. Dad reaches over for the bag and grunts when he tries to lift it.
zh_text: 我比比後座。爹伸手過去拿運動包，邊咕噥著邊費力地把包包舉起來。

en_text: “They’re on top,” I say, and a moment later he has them in his hands.
zh_text: 「在最上面。」我說，他接著就把檔案拿在手裡了。

en_text: “Who the hell are these people?” he asks, opening the first couple of folders.
zh_text: 「這幾個王八蛋是誰啊？」他邊問邊翻開前兩份檔案。

en_text: “Nobody,” I say. “Just files the probation officer had in his drawer.”
zh_text: 「不知道，」我說，「就是布萊肯放在抽屜裡的檔案。」

en_text: “So they’re clients he has. You went to his office and found his current work and nothing else.”
zh_text: 「所以他負責監護這些人。你去他的辦公室，找到他目前要處理的檔案，就這樣。」

en_text: “I didn’t have time to keep looking.”
zh_text: 「我沒時間一直找。」

en_text: “You should have made the time. These are useless,” he says. “Some of these people don’t even have a record for armed robbery. What have we got here,” he says, thumbing through them, “we’ve got half a dozen armed holdups, an arson, a couple of rapists, a couple of drug traffickers, a kidnapper, a compulsive shoplifter—any of them could be part of this thing.”
zh_text: 「你應該要繼續找。這些檔案沒用，」他說，「有些人連持械搶劫的前科也沒有。這裡呢，我看看，」他開始翻閱檔案，「五六個持槍搶劫、兩個強暴犯、兩個毒品走私、一個綁匪、一個盗竊狂——他們都有可能把小珊綁走。」

en_text: “I know, Dad, I already know. Two men took Sam tonight, one of them I killed, the other one has her. Nat and Diana, they saw the other guy.”
zh_text: 「我知道，爹，我早就知道了。今晚有兩個綁匪，一個被我殺了，一個抓走小珊。納森跟黛安娜看到了那個把小珊抓走的人。」

en_text: “Have you showed the folders to them?”
zh_text: 「你給他們看過檔案了嗎？」

en_text: “I can’t. The police are with them. Schroder was going to get them to check out some mug shots.”
zh_text: 「不行，他們家有警察。施羅德要他們辨認嫌疑犯的照片。」

en_text: “So maybe they have a name already. Maybe the police have already found Sam.”
zh_text: 「那，或许他們已經知道是誰了。或许警察已經找到小珊了。」

en_text: “And maybe they haven’t.” “Call them.”
zh_text: 「或许他們還沒找到。」「打電話過去。」

en_text: “The police?”
zh_text: 「給警察？」

en_text: “No, your in-laws. Maybe they’ve made an ID and can give us a name.” “I’ve been trying.”
zh_text: 「不是，打給你的岳父岳母。或許他們已經認完人了，可以跟我們說那人叫什麼名字。」

en_text: “Well, try again.”
zh_text: 「嗯，再打一次吧。」

en_text: I pull over. After ten rings I’m about to hang up when suddenly it’s picked up.
zh_text: 我把車停到路邊。電話響了十聲，我正要掛斷，突然有人接起來了。

en_text: “Hello?”
“Nat?”
zh_text: 「納森？」

en_text: “Jesus, Eddie, where the hell are you?”
zh_text: 「天啊，艾迪，你他媽的跑哪裡去了？」

en_text: “I’m looking for Sam. Where the hell else would I be?” “With your father? The police say you broke him out.” “He’s helping.”
zh_text: 「我在找小珊。我還能去他媽的哪裡？」「跟你爸爸一起？警察說你幫他逃獄了。」「他會幫我忙。」

en_text: “He’s a monster.”
zh_text: 「他是魔鬼。」

en_text: “So is the man who took Sam. Were you able to make an ID?”
zh_text: 「把小珊帶走的人也是魔鬼。你們認出是誰了嗎？」

en_text: “Not at first. The cops know who the bank robbers are but none of them took Sam. The detective who showed them to us brought back a new batch of photos. We picked him out right away, Edward. The police know who took Sam.”
zh_text: 「一開始沒認出來。條子知道搶匪有哪些人，但他們都不是綁匪。後來給我們看照片的警探又送了一批新照片來。我們立刻就認出來了，艾德華。警察知道誰把小珊綁走了。」「他們知道是誰，但還沒把小珊找回來，不一樣吧？」

en_text: “They have the name, but that’s not the same as having Sam, is it?” “Well, no.”
zh_text: 「你說得對，是不一樣。」

en_text: “Then give me the name of the man who took her.”
zh_text: 「告诉我是誰把小珊抓走了。」

en_text: “I don’t know, Eddie. I think the police are better equipped.”
zh_text: 「艾迪，我不该說吧。我覺得警察的裝備比較齊全。」

en_text: “The police, if they find her, will put the man who took her in jail for five or ten years and then let him go. That what you want? Remember when you said you wished you could have time alone with the people who killed Jodie?”
zh_text: 「如果警察找到她，只會把綁匪關五到十年，然後又放他出來。你願意嗎？你記不記得你曾經說過，希望能跟殺死茱蒂的人單挑？」

en_text: “We only want Sam back safely.”
zh_text: 「我們只要小珊平安回來。」

en_text: “Give me the name. I swear to you, Nat, I’m not going to do anything that puts her at risk.”
zh_text: 「告訴我是誰。納森，我發誓，我不會讓她遇到危險。」

en_text: “I don’t know . . .”
zh_text: 「我不知道···」

en_text: “I deserve to know the name of the man who kidnapped my daughter, Nat. Jesus—she’s my daughter. My daughter!”
zh_text: 「我有權利知道誰綁走了我女兒，納森。天啊——她是我女兒。我的女兒！」

en_text: “Oliver Church,” he says, and I recognize the name. “That’s all I know. I don’t know any addresses or anything else.”
zh_text: 「奧利佛·丘奇，」我看過這個名字。「我只知道他叫奧利佛·丘奇，地址跟其他的資料我都不知道。」

en_text: “Thank you,” I say, and I hang up.
zh_text: 「謝謝。」我掛上了電話。

en_text: “See, I knew they’d answer the phone,” Dad says. “I’m your good-luck charm.”
zh_text: 「你看，我就知道他們會接電話，」爹說，「我是你的幸運星。」

en_text: “Give me the folders.”
zh_text: 「把檔案給我。」

en_text: He hands them over. The fourth one in belongs to Oliver Church. Out of the list of crimes in the files, Oliver Church is the only one who has kidnapping and manslaughter next to his name, but there are no details of the crimes.
zh_text: 他把檔案遞過來。第四份就是奧利佛·丘奇。在檔案上列出的罪案裡，只有奧利佛·丘奇的名字旁邊列了綁票跟殺人，但罪案的細節不在上面。

en_text: “Address won’t be current,” Dad says, “so no point in going to his house, and even if it is current he sure as hell won’t have taken Sam there.”
zh_text: 「地址可能改了，」爹說，「去他家也没有用，就算他還住在那裡，也不會把小珊帶過去。」

en_text: “You ever hear of him?”
zh_text: 「你聽過這個人的名字嗎？」

en_text:
“Never. Can’t your in-laws go online and find out about him?” “They barely know what online means.”
“Well, there has to somebody you can ask.”
zh_text:
「沒聽過。你岳父能不能上網搜尋一下？」
「他們連上網是什麼意思都不知道。」
「總有人可以問吧。」

en_text: “Not really. What we need is a computer,” I say, looking out the windows, knowing that nine out of every ten houses out there has one. I think about all my conversations with Schroder, about my dad in jail, about the stabbing, about the ex-cop working for Schroder trying to solve part of the case.
zh_text: 「沒人可以問。我需要電腦。」我看向窗外，十棟房子裡應該有九棟裡面有電腦。我想起我跟施羅德的對話，關於我爹在牢裡，關於他被刺傷的事情，關於幫施羅德調查刺傷案的前任警察。

en_text: The ex-cop.
zh_text: 前任警察。

en_text: Because Christchurch is clinging to the past, it’s still possible to pass an occasional phone booth, and I drive back toward town to find one. The Yellow Pages have been torn out, and so has the phone receiver, but the White Pages are still there and I use them to look up a name and address.
zh_text: 因爲基督城割捨不下過去，路上偶爾仍能看到電話亭，我開車回城裡找到一座。黃頁的工商電話簿被撕爛了，話筒也被拔掉了，但用戶電話簿還在，我在裡面找到了姓名和地址。

en_text: All the lights are off inside the house, as they are in every other house in the street. The difference between this house and the others is the others all have a Christmasy look about them, lights and decorations in the window, oozing joy and peace to the world. This house is cold and certainly empty, and when I break a window and make my way inside it feels like my house, like something has been lost from this home the same way something was lost from mine.
zh_text: 屋裡的燈都關了，街上其他的房子也是漆黑一片。但這棟房子不像其他房子都帶有耶誕風味，窗戶上裝了燈泡和飾品，對著世界散發喜樂與和平。看起來冷清清，裡面一定沒有人，我打破窗戶進了屋子，覺得很像我家，似乎我跟屋主一樣，都失去了很珍貴的東西。

en_text: I use the cell phone to create some light, then decide that it’s so late in the night I’d have to be really unlucky if somebody saw the lights burning, so I flick them on. I open up the back door for Dad and he comes inside.
zh_text: 我拿手機出來照路，然後想反正這麼晚了，我一定很倒楣才會被別人看到燈開了，所以我打開了電燈開關。我幫爹開了後門，他也進來了。

en_text: It’s a three-bedroom home with one bedroom set up for a young girl, perhaps one similar to Sam’s age. The room hasn’t been slept in for a long time, and it’s far tidier than any young girl would ever leave it. There’s an office with not much in it, but it has a computer, and the remaining bedroom has a big bed with folded clothes lying on top.
zh_text: 這間房子有三個房間，一間看起來是小女孩的臥室，說不定跟小珊差不多年紀。看起來已經很久沒有人睡在裡面了，也比一般小女孩的臥室整潔得多。書房裡家具不多，不過有電腦，剩下那間房裡面則有一張大床，上面放了摺好的衣服。

en_text: “Who lives here?” Dad asks, looking at some of the photos. “You know this guy?”
zh_text: 「這是誰家？」爹看看牆上的照片。「你認識這個人嗎？」

en_text: “Not really,” I say.
zh_text: 「不怎麼熟。」我說。

en_text: “He seems familiar.”
zh_text: 「覺得他很面熟。」

en_text: “Maybe you’ve seen him around.”
zh_text: 「或许你看過他。」

en_text:
“Only place I’ve been around lately is jail,” Dad says.
“And there’s your answer.”
zh_text:
「我最近能看到人的地方只有監獄。」爹說。
「那就對了。」

en_text: The house belongs to Theodore Tate—the ex–police officer Schroder told me about a few times, the man in jail for drunk driving, the guy who figured out who stabbed my dad. There are other photos on the wall—a pretty woman and a young girl around Sam’s age. I wonder what happened to Tate’s family, and have a real bad feeling that somehow the virus got them the same way it got mine. Maybe Tate lost his wife and went seeking revenge in an attempt to save his daughter. Maybe when he gets out of jail he’ll keep on searching.
zh_text: 這是泰奥多·泰特的家那名酒駕入獄的前警察，施羅德提過他的名字幾次，刺傷我爹的兇手也由他查出來。牆上還有其他的照片照片中的女人很漂亮，小女孩跟小珊差不多大。不知道泰特家發生了什麼事，眞覺得很難過，病毒用蔓延到我家的方式也蔓延到他家了。或許泰特妻子死了，他爲了救回女兒而踏上復仇之路。或许等他出獄，他仍會繼續尋找兇手。

en_text: I go online and quickly scan the latest news reports. The name of the man I ran over this afternoon has been released—Adam Sinclair. There are already many details: a year or so ago there wouldn’t be any names released for at least a day, let alone facts, but these days you can see a dead body on the front page of the newspaper.
zh_text: 我上線後快速掃了一下最新的新聞報導。下午被我開車壓過那個人的名字公布了亞當·辛克萊。已經有不少的細節：一年前起碼要等一天媒體才會公布姓名，但現在你在報紙頭條上就能看到死屍的照片。

en_text: The reports spell out the events and are unusually accurate. They say two men tried to kill me; one of them was hit by a car when I fled the scene, and the second man then executed the first. The reports are unclear on why the men were after me—but hint at my involvement in the killing of Shane Kingsly. The phrase “revenge killing” shows up about five times—as my hypothetical reason for killing Shane Kingsly, and as their reason for trying to kill me. It’s the first time in twenty years that the media has guessed correctly what I might be capable of.
zh_text: 事發經過的報導鉅細靡遺，居然滿符合事實。他們說有兩個男人想殺我，在我逃走時一個人被車撞倒，另一個人則把他處決了。記者不知道他們爲什麼要追殺我——卻暗示我跟夏恩·金斯理脫離不了關係。「報仇殺人」出現了五次——他們假設我爲了報仇而殺死夏恩·金斯理，那兩個男人爲了報仇而想殺我。二十年了，媒體終於猜對我能做出什麼好事。

en_text: Tonight’s deaths are still too soon for there to be any details, plus it’s Christmas, so most of the reporters are doing society a favor and taking the night off. There’s only a vague outline with no names, stating that one of the two victims is a police officer. Bracken’s death is still too early to even get a mention.
zh_text: 他們還來不及爲今晚死掉的人寫出詳細的報導，而且正逢耶誕節，大多數記者都去放假了，不啻爲社會造福。只有模糊的大綱，沒有姓名，指出兩名死者中有一名是警察。布萊肯之死更趕不上報導。

en_text: I type Oliver Church’s name into the computer and a minute later we have his story.
zh_text: 我在電腦上輸入奧利佛·丘奇的名字，一分鐘後我們看到了他的人生。

en_text: Nine years ago Church kidnapped a six-year-old boy and tried to ransom him back to his parents, but he got busted when he went to pick up the money. Church took the child to an abandoned slaughterhouse north of the city. When he got caught, he wouldn’t give up the location of the child. He tried to make a deal to cut back jail time for the safety of the child. Lawyers came to the party, but by the time they struck a deal the child had died—combination of cold and hunger and everything else that happens when you tie a kid up and leave them in a place like that. Poor kid probably died of fright. That’s why it was manslaughter and not murder. Because of the deal he made, he only got six years. Didn’t matter that the boy had died: the deal was for the boy’s location, and since nothing specific was put in writing saying the boy had to be alive, nothing could be done to reverse the deal.
