zh_text: 九年前，丘奇綁架了一名六歲男童，想跟他父母親勒索贖金，但去取款的時候，被警方逮捕了。丘奇把那孩子帶到城北一處廢棄的屠宰場。被捕的時候，他不肯透露男孩的所在。他想跟警方討價還價，縮短服刑期限來換回小孩的安全。律師也插了一腳，但等他們談妥了，男孩也死了他又冷又餓，又被人綁起來丢在屠宰場裡，有很多可能的因素。可憐的孩子或許被嚇死了。那就是爲什麼他只被判過失殺人，而不是謀殺。根據討價還價的結果，他只坐了六年牢。小男孩死了，沒差：交換條件是男孩的所在，沒有特別寫下條款說小男孩得要活著，因此不能推翻交易。

en_text: “You think he could kill a child deliberately?” I ask Dad.
zh_text: 「你覺得他會蓄意謀殺小孩嗎？」我問爹。

en_text: “Make no mistake, son. That is what he did. He was in custody for three days without giving up the location. He knew that kid was going to die and he did nothing to stop it. That means he can do it again. It should only be about the money, but this guy—shit, look at these stories. The men who robbed the bank, maybe they’re all killers, maybe just one or two of them, but if Bracken hired this guy it means none of that crew are capable of killing a child. Church is.”
zh_text: 「別出差錯，兒子。他殺了一個孩子。他被拘留了三天，還不肯透露地點。他知道那孩子會死，也不願意救他。那表示他還會有下一次。原本只是爲了錢，但這個人幹，你看這些報導。銀行搶匪或許都殺過人，或許其中一兩個人有殺人前科而已，但如果布萊肯也找了這個人，表示其他人都沒辦法下手殺小孩子。只有丘奇狠得下心。」

en_text: “Oh Jesus, Dad, what do we do? What the hell do we do?”
zh_text: 「噢，天啊，爹，我們要怎麼辦？我們他媽的該怎麼辦？」

en_text: “He’s not going to take Sam somewhere she can figure out how to lead the police back to. He’ll have somewhere else. For now, it’s about the money.”
zh_text: 「他不會把小珊帶去認得路的地方，不然她就能幫警察指路。他得找另外一個藏身點。現在，問題在錢上面。」

en_text: “But there is no money, don’t you get that? There never was! Bracken knew I never had it, he was just playing the game so the others would believe.”
zh_text: 「但是沒有錢，你還不明白嗎？我沒把錢拿走！布萊肯知道我沒拿，他只是假裝我拿了，騙其他人相信。」

en_text: “Then maybe Oliver Church believes it too,” Dad says. “You better hope like hell that he does.”
zh_text: 「那麼，或許奧利佛·丘奇也信了，」爹說，「你最好用力祈禱，希望他也相信。」

en_text: “It still doesn’t tell us where she is.”
zh_text: 「那我們還是不知道小珊在哪裡。」

en_text: “Criminals return to what they know best,” Dad says. “That I know for a fact. The slaughterhouse has been abandoned a long time,” he says. “Way back when I was a teenager. We used to call it the Laughterhouse.”
zh_text: 「罪犯都喜歡回到熟悉的地方，」爹說，「我知道，屠宰場廢棄好久了。在我十幾歲的時候，我們都叫它笑宰場。」

en_text: “You think she’s there?”
zh_text: 「你覺得她會在那裡？」

en_text: “At this stage we have nothing else.”
zh_text: 「我們現在也沒有其他的線索。」

en_text: It’s a twenty-five minute drive which I cover in about twelve, at times hitting speeds that Santa would be impressed by. Christmas decorations pass us in a blur, turning into streaks of light. We don’t see a single car on the road. I slow down at red lights before blowing right through them. Suburbia ends and the pastures start again like they do in every direction in this city—except for the east; only way you can keep going east in this city is if your car can float. I try the cell phone number from Bracken’s phone again but there’s no joy, which isn’t fair because Christmas is supposed to be a time of joy.
zh_text: 原本要二十五分鐘的路程我十二分鐘就開到了，有時候速度高到可能連聖誕老人都要嘖嘖稱奇。路邊的耶誕裝飾變得一團模糊，化身爲長長的光條。路上一部車也沒碰到。碰到紅燈時我會稍微放慢速度，然後一口氣衝過去。出了郊區，到處都是小牧場，這座城不管往什麼方向走，都會碰到牧場除了東方以外；如果要一直往東走，你的车子要能浮在水上。我又撥了從布萊肯手機上找到的號碼，没人接，不公平，耶誕節不就是能讓人心想事成的節日嗎？

en_text: When we reach the slaughterhouse we pull up short of the road leading up to it. I leave all three cell phones—my one, Kingsly’s, and Bracken’s—in the car, and we get out. The ground is cool and damp, as if the ghosts of thousands of animals have drained into the soil. I stash the bag of money in the boot and grab a flashlight from the emergency breakdown kit.
zh_text: 到了屠宰場，我把車子停在通往屠宰場入口的車道末端。我把三支手機我的、金斯理的、布萊肯的都留在車子裡，跟爹一起下了車。地面冷冷濕濕，彷彿數千頭動物的冤魂都流入了土壤。我把裝了錢的袋子塞進後車廂，然後從緊急抛錨工具箱裡拿出手電筒。

en_text: “This prostitute at the probation officer’s house, you get a name?” Dad asks.
zh_text: 「剛在觀護人家那個妓女，你知道她叫什嬮名字嗎？」爹問。

en_text: “What? Why?” “Just curious.” “No. No name.”
zh_text: 「什麼？爲什麼要問？」「好奇而已。」不知道，不知道她的名字。

en_text: The road is ankle-breaking material, cracked and busted from the weight of trucks that once upon a time used to go up and down it, so we walk off to the side where the dirt is hard packed. We have to walk slower because of our wounds, Dad’s and mine. I figure it’s been a long day for him too.
zh_text: 這條路走起來會扭傷腳踝，路面被一度在上面往來的大卡車壓得體無完膚，我們只好走到旁邊的硬土地上。我跟爹都有傷，只好放慢了速度。我想，他今天也夠受的了。

en_text: Christmas doesn’t quite reach out here. No tinsel or lights, just a bleak setting with shadows cast only by the moonlight and stars.
zh_text: 這裡沒有耶誕節的氣氛。看不到金蔥或燈節，只有月亮和星星的光芒留下了陰影，氣氛非常凄凉。

en_text: “What’d she look like, then?” “What?”
zh_text: 「那她長什麼樣？」「什麼？」

en_text: “The prostitute. What’d she look like?” “I don’t know. The way they all look.”
zh_text: 「那個妓女。她長什麼樣？」「我不知道。就一副妓女樣。」

en_text: “They all look different, son. Trust me. It’s only on the inside they look the same.”
zh_text: 「她們看起來都不一樣，兒子。聽我的準沒錯。只有裡面都一樣。」

en_text: I don’t ask him what he means by that and thankfully he doesn’t elaborate. We keep walking.
zh_text: 我沒問他「裡面」是什麼意思，還好他也沒解釋。我們不停向前走。

en_text: “You’re not really going to take me back after all this, are you, son?” he asks.
zh_text: 「一切都結束後，兒子，你不會真的要把我送回去吧？」他問。

en_text: I don’t answer him. The slaughterhouse comes into view. It seems to grow out of the earth the closer we get, looming out of the darkness and bearing down on us. The words NORTH CITY SLAUGHTERHOUSE have been stenciled in letters a meter high, big enough to make out in the dark. The smell is still here, even decades after the place has shut down, hanging in the still air. Or maybe the smell is only in my imagination. There’s certainly something here. I wonder how bad it smelled back then. The slaughterhouse was only up and running for two years or so before it was closed down, a victim of expanding suburbia that never did expand. The building was shut down before the road leading up to it could be repaved in thicker cement, the land sold, and then nothing, until somebody came along with a couple of tins of spray paint and blacked out the “S” on the word Slaughterhouse.
zh_text: 屠宰場就在眼前。愈靠近愈覺得這棟建築物是從地裡長出來的，陰森森聳立著，似乎要對著我們壓下來。印在牆上的「北城屠宰場」幾個大字有一公尺高，在黑暗中也清晰可見。味道還沒散去，即使關閉了幾十年，沉悶的空氣中仍有味道。或許那味道只是我的想像。一定有什麼東西在裡面。不知道以前聞起來有多臭。屠宰場建好後只營運兩年就關閉了，因爲郊區原本要擴展到這裡，卻又放棄擴展。關閉前還沒來得及用更厚的水泥重鋪前面的車道，地賣了，卻什麼變化也沒有，直到有人帶了兩罐噴漆來，把「屠宰場」改成「笑宰場」。

en_text: Fifteen years ago this building was the scene of a double homicide, and nine years ago it was used to hide a boy who died from fear while a man tried to shave some years off his sentence. Tonight it possibly holds my daughter.
zh_text: 十五年前，這裡出了件雙屍命案，九年前被藏在這裡的小男孩害怕到失去性命，只是因爲綁架他的人想少蹲幾年苦牢。今晚，我女兒很有可能就在裡面。

en_text: A dark four-door sedan is parked in front of the building. We split up; Dad heads toward the back and I head toward the car. We work well together, not having to talk, only a minimum of hand gestures, as if we’ve done this before. I can tell my dad is enjoying it and I hate him for that. I reach the car and take a look inside before moving on.
zh_text: 屠宰場前停了一台深色的四門轎車。我跟爹兵分兩路；他往後面走，我朝著車子走去。我們合作無間，不需要說話，一點點手勢就夠了，彷彿我們早就習以爲常。我覺得爹非常樂在其中，我很氣他居然以此爲傲。我靠近車子看了看裡面，然後繼續查探。

en_text: The slaughterhouse walls are mostly made up of concrete blocks, with some sections of corrugated iron. The base of it is lined in mold that grows up the walls, darker near the bottom where it grows the thickest, and there are plenty of weeds growing up through the cracks in the sidewalk. I reach a window but can’t see a damn thing inside. The side door leading into an office area is lying on the ground, the top hinge busted, the bottom hinge still attached but twisted ninety degrees. The temperature drops when I step through. I stand still and listen before turning on the flashlight. There’s no furniture anywhere, nothing hanging on the walls, nothing on the concrete floor. The room has been completely stripped. The door to the corridor has been removed. I head through, and another empty doorway later and I’m in the slaughterhouse, a huge, cavernous room that smells of rot. The air is graveyard cold, and the darkness seems to suck at the back of my eyeballs. The flashlight doesn’t even break the dark, just lights up a thin beam of it and is lost. I can sense large hooks hanging from the ceiling ahead of me somewhere, but can’t see them. There’s machinery left here to rust—the tools of the trade that started the animals down the path from living, breathing entities to supermarket specials and hamburgers. No wonder a young boy, tied up and left alone out here, died.
zh_text: 屠宰場的四面牆幾乎都是混凝土，有些地方則是波浪狀鐵皮。牆底生滿了鰴菌，都爬到牆上了，在靠近牆腳的地方最厚，顏色也比较深，步道有縫隙的地方也長出了不少雜草。我靠近窗戶，卻看不到裡面有什麼。通往辦公區的側門倒在地上，最上面的鉸鏈斷裂了，下面的鉸鏈還連著，但扭轉了九十度。一走進去，溫度就明顯下降。我站著不動，側耳聆聽了一下子，才把手電筒打開。裡面沒有家具，牆上沒有東西，水泥地上空無一物。完全搬空了。通往走廊的門被拆掉了我穿過大門，再經過走廊，就進了屠宰場，大而空洞，聞起來有腐臭的味道。空氣如墓地一樣冷，黑暗似乎吞噬了我的眼球。手電筒在黑暗中也不管用，只射出細弱的光線，然後消失在黑暗中。我可以感覺到再往前走的話，天花板上似乎掛了巨大的鉤子，但什麼也看不見。還有留在這邊生鏽的機器——屠宰機器，把活生生有呼吸的動物變成超市的特價品和漢堡肉。難怪被綁起來孤單留在這裡的小男孩活活嚇死了。

en_text: I turn back into the corridor. There’s a bend in it, and once around it I can see a light coming from beneath a door not too far ahead—one of the few doors remaining. It’s a heavy wooden door, the bottom of it lined with vertical scratches, probably from rats. I reach it and put my face against it and listen but can’t hear a thing.
zh_text: 我回到走廊上。繞過一個彎後，我看到前面有扇門下透出了光線這裡只留下了幾扇門。厚重的木頭門，門底都是垂直的抓痕，或许是老鼠抓的。我伸手過去，把臉貼到門上傾聽，卻聽不到聲音。

en_text: I suck in a couple of deep breaths, tighten my grip on the shotgun, and swing the door open.
zh_text: 我深吸了兩口氣，抓緊霰彈槍，把門推開了。

en_text: The second name on the list, Zach Everest, is a bust. The SWAT team ended up breaking into a house that Everest hadn’t set foot in for about two years, and the new residents weren’t thrilled at the intrusion—let alone the kids who, having heard the commotion, were horribly disappointed to see six men in black storming into their home instead of one man dressed in red. There are no other known addresses for Everest, but Schroder knows it’s only a matter of time now—probably less than a day, he guesses—before they have him in custody.
zh_text: 名單上的第二個人查克·艾弗瑞斯特讓他們撲了個空。艾弗瑞斯特早在兩年前就搬離武装防禦小組攻進的房子，該處的居民一點也不興奮有人闖入更不用說他們家的孩子了，聽到騷動後，他們看到六個黑衣男人衝進來，而不是一個紅衣老公公，失望到了極點。艾弗瑞斯特名下沒登記其他的住址，但施羅德知道早晚他們會抓到這個人他猜應該不用一天的時間吧。

en_text: Reports have already come in about the gunshot victim half an hour ago. Tyler Layton was tied to a chair and executed. Witnesses woken by the noise reported two men fleeing the scene in a four-door sedan that certainly doesn’t belong to Edward Hunter, because Hunter’s car got busted up in town, but which might have been his wife’s. At this point there’s nothing to connect Hunter and his dad to the killing, and nothing to connect Tyler Layton to any of the men responsible for the bank robbery or the abduction of Sam Hunter—but Schroder is confident there will be a link somewhere. Layton has a criminal record long enough to pretty much guarantee some interaction with Jack Hunter or the bank robbers—and the way the night is going, Jack Sr. seems to be the catalyst for all the violence around here.
zh_text: 半小時前，槍擊被害人的報告就進來了。泰勒·雷頓被綁在椅子上處決。被槍聲吵醒的目擊證人說，有兩個男人開著一輛四門轎車離開，車子應該不是艾德華·杭特的，因爲他的車在城裡拋錨了，但有可能是他老婆的。此刻還找不到杭特父子跟槍擊案的牽連，泰勒·雷頓跟銀行搶匪或小珊的綁票案也沒有關聯——但施羅德相信他能找到其中的環節。雷頓前科累累，肯定跟傑克·杭特或綁匪有所牽扯——按著今晚的走勢，似乎所有的暴力事件都由杭特催化。

en_text: At the moment Oliver Church is the far more urgent target. Church kidnapped and killed a boy, for which he only served six years. Schroder knows Church’s involvement ups the danger factor for Sam Hunter. Bracken didn’t choose somebody who would just stash the kid away for a few hours and free her somewhere, but somebody capable of ending the life of someone so young.
zh_text: 這時，奥利佛·丘奇是更要緊的目標。丘奇曾綁票殺害一個男童，而且只因此坐了六年的牢。施羅德知道，一旦丘奇涉案，小珊就更危險了。布萊肯不會選一個只能把小孩藏起來幾個小時然後把她放走的人，他會選一個能辣手殺害小孩的壞人。

en_text: He redirects the assault team to Church’s address, and twenty minutes later it’s all for nothing. The address is current—there’s mail inside addressed to Church, there’s fresh food in the fridge and a half-empty packet of cigarettes on the table, but no sign of Church.
zh_text: 他指揮突襲小組前往丘奇家，二十分鐘後證實是又一場徒勞無功。他確實住在那裡一他們找到寫給他的信件、冰箱裡有新鮮的食物、桌上還有半包菸，可是丘奇不在家。

en_text: More detectives arrive, among them Detective Watts, who has Church’s criminal record with him.
zh_text: 更多警探遇来了，瓦兹也到了，帮来了丘奇的犯罪紀錄。

en_text: “A model prisoner,” Watts says. “According to the file he made every meeting with his probation officer.”
zh_text: 「模範犯人，」瓦茲說，「根據紀錄，他從未錯過跟觀護人約好的會面。」

en_text: “There has to be another address.”
zh_text: 「一定有其他的住址。」

en_text: “Only other thing listed here is his parents,” Watts says.
zh_text: 「檔案上只有他父母的地址。」瓦兹說。

en_text: “And we’ve already sent people there. He’s probably somewhere with the girl, somewhere he’s stashed her away with nobody else around.”
zh_text: 「我們已經派人過去了。或许他帶著小女孩躲起來了，把她藏到空無一人的地方。」

en_text: “That could be any one of a thousand places,” Watts says.
zh_text: 「空無一人的地方有成千上百個。」瓦茲說。

en_text: “That’s not real helpful,” Schroder snaps at him. “Look, there can’t be too many possibilities. It’s probably somewhere he knows, right?” He looks back down at the file. “Last time he took the kid to the North City Slaughterhouse.”
zh_text: 「廢話，」施羅德怒氣沖沖地回答。「你看，不可能有成千上百個。一定是他熟悉的地方，是不是？」他低頭看看檔案。「上次他把小孩帶去北城屠宰場。」

en_text: “You think he’s taken her there?”
zh_text: 「你覺得他把小珊帶過去了？」

en_text: “Only one way to find out,” Schroder says. He needs coffee and he needs a break and he needs this all to be over and for Sam to be returned safely. “It’s as good a place as any.”
zh_text: 「只有一個方法能找出答案，」施羅德說。他很想喝咖啡，他需要休息一下，他想結束這切，讓小珊安全回來。「這個地方似乎很有可能。」

en_text: He calls Landry for an update. “Johnson knows nothing,” Landry says. “He certainly robbed the bank, but he’s not giving anything up. I think he knew Sam Hunter was going to be taken, but I don’t think he knew who by, or where she’s being held.”
zh_text: 他打電話給藍德里詢問狀況。「強森什麼也不知道，」藍德里說，「搶銀行他參了一腳，但他什麼都不肯說。我覺得他料到小珊會被綁架，但我不覺得他知道綁匪是誰，也不知道她被送到哪裡去了。」

en_text: Liam Marshall comes over. “We’re all ready to hit the next house.” “Let’s go,” Schroder says. On the way he makes a call to the station and asks for a patrol car to head out urgently to the North City Slaughterhouse to take a look around.
zh_text: 連恩·馬歇爾走過來。「我們準備好要突襲下一個地址了。」「走吧。」施羅德說。上路後他打電話回警局，要求他們立刻派一台巡邏車去北城屠宰場看看情況。

en_text: Everything looks normal. Take away the fact that the man sitting down playing on a handheld games unit isn’t anybody I’ve seen before. Take away the fact the floor is concrete and the windows are boarded up and the walls have graffiti on them. Ignore the damp air, ignore the smell that’s etched into the walls like a stubborn stain, ignore the fact the mattress my daughter is lying on is a hundred years old, and it’s all normal, just a night in at home.
zh_text: 一切看起來都很正常。除了我從來沒見過那個坐著玩手持式遊戲機的男人。除了地板是混凝土，窗戶上都釘了木板，牆壁上還有塗鴉。且不管潮濕的空氣，且不管宛若頑垢般刻入牆面的氣味，且不管我女兒躺的床墊有多麼老舊，感覺就很正常，就像晚上我們在家裡一樣。

en_text: The light coming from a battery lantern is pale blue and doesn’t make the room any prettier. There’s a couple of relics in here—an old rusted filing cabinet, a laminated table that must weigh close to fifty kilos, cables and wires hanging freely from the ceiling like spiderwebs. Church lowers the game unit. It keeps making animal fighting sounds. There’s a cell phone on the table next to him and I wonder what he’s waiting for.
zh_text: 電燈籠射出淡藍色的光線，只增添了房間裡慘澹的氛圍。這裡有幾樣紀念屠宰場的舊物老舊生鏽的檔案櫃，重量肯定接近五十公斤的塑膠桌，如蜘蛛網般懸吊在天花板上的電纜和電線。丘奇放下遊戲機。動物打架的聲音仍不斷傳出來。旁邊的桌上有支手機，不知道他在等誰打電話來。

en_text: “Oh Jesus, please don’t kill me,” he says, and it’s taking all my willpower not to. He’s as thin and as creepy-looking as he was in the photos in his file.
zh_text: 「噢，天啊，拜託，别殺我。」他說，我用盡所有的意志力，才壓下殺他的衝動。他跟檔案上的照片一樣瘦，一樣令人不寒而慄。

en_text: “You took my daughter.”
zh_text: 「你綁走我女兒。」

en_text: “I know, I know, but it was just business.” “And so is this,” I say, and I pump the shotgun.
zh_text: 「我知道，我知道，但我是聽命行事。」「這也是聽命行事。」我把霰彈槍上了膛。

en_text: “Wait, wait,” he says, putting his hands up. “We can deal,” he says.
zh_text: 「等等，等一下，」他舉高雙手。「不如我們談筆交易。」

en_text: “Deal?”
zh_text: 「交易？」

en_text: “I can give you a name.”
zh_text: 「我告诉你是誰下的命令。」

en_text: “Yeah? What name? Austin Bracken?” “Shit.”
zh_text: 「喔？誰？奥斯汀·布萊肯？」「可惡。」

en_text: “Exactly.”
zh_text: 「沒錯。」

en_text: “Wait, wait, there has to be something I can offer.”
zh_text: 「等等，聽我的，總有你想跟我交换的東西。」

en_text: I move toward Sam, keeping the gun trained on Church. When I reach the mattress I squat down but decide not to wake her. My little princess is dreaming of much happier times, her little mouth wide open.
zh_text: 我朝著小珊移動，一直用槍指著丘奇。走到床墊旁邊，我蹲下身子，卻決定不要叫醒她。我的小公主正夢見更加快樂的時光，她的小嘴巴張得大大的。

en_text:
My father walks into the room. He’s found a piece of rebar about half a meter long with a small chunk of concrete attached to the end. He looks at
Church, then at me, then down at Sam, and he smiles at her, comes across, and crouches down. It’s the first time he’s ever seen her and the emotion gets to him. I’ve never seen it before—but my father starts to cry.
zh_text:
父親也走進來了。他找到了一條大約半公尺長的鋼筋，末端黏了一小球水泥。他看看丘奇，又看看我，然後低頭看著小珊，他對小珊微微一笑，走過來蹲在床墊旁邊。這是他第一次見到小珊，情緒非常激動。我從來沒看過他哭但爹哭起來了。
「這就是我的孫女，」他說。「她好可爱。」

en_text: “So this is my granddaughter,” he says. “She’s beautiful.” “She’s exactly like her mother,” I say.
zh_text: 「她跟她媽媽一模一樣。」我說。

en_text: Mummy’s a ghost.
zh_text: 媽媽變成鬼了。

en_text: I stroke her hair back. “He doesn’t know anything useful,” I say, nodding toward Church. “You sure?” he asks, wiping at the tears.
zh_text: 我把她的頭髮往後撥開。「他什麼也不知道。」我對著丘奇抬抬下巴。「你確定嗎？」他擦擦眼淚。

en_text: “Please, guys, I can help you.”
zh_text: 「拜託，老兄，我可以幫你們。」

en_text: “I’m taking Sam out to the car,” I say.
zh_text: 「我把小珊帶到車上去。」我說。

en_text: “I think that’s best, son.” “You’ll be okay here?”
zh_text: 「兒子，很好，你帶她上車吧。」

en_text: “It’s been twenty years, son. I have certain needs. Best you hurry up and get your little girl out of here. If he knows anything more, I’ll find out. I promise.”
zh_text: 「你留在這裡沒關係吧？」「兒子，已經二十年了。我得想辦法滿足我的需要。你最好快點把你的小寶貝帶出去。如果他還知道其他的內幕，我會問出來。相信我。」

en_text: I scoop Sam up. She tightens her arms around my neck without waking. “I’m done,” I say to Dad, keeping my voice low, not wanting to wake Sam. “Whether you learn anything or not, I’m done now. The police can do the rest. Whatever this bastard has to say, we’ll hand the information over.”
zh_text: 我把小珊抱起來。用她的雙臂勾緊我的脖子，但她沒醒過來。「沒我的事了，」我對爹說，聲音放得很低，不想吵醒小珊。「不管他還知道什麼，沒我的事了。剩下的都交給警方。這個王八蛋還有什麼好說的話，我們都告訴警方。」

en_text: “Okay, son. I understand. Leave me the shotgun, would you?”
zh_text: 「OK，兒子，我懂。把槍留下，好嗎？」

en_text: “Come on, let me help you out here,” Church says, “All I know is my old probation officer called me up and told me I had to help him out. He said if I didn’t he’d make life hard for me. I don’t know anything else. There’s no need to do this, any of this. It was business, I swear, just business.”
zh_text: 「拜託，求求你們聽我說。我只知道，以前的觀護人打電話來要我幫他。他說萬一我不肯，我就會死得很難看。我只知道這些。不需要殺我，不需要流血。我就是按他說的照做，我發誓，我只是聽命行事。」

en_text: “Shut up,” Dad says, then turns toward me. “The shotgun, son.”
zh_text: 「閉嘴，」爹對他說完後轉向我，「兒子，槍給我。」

en_text: I think about Jodie and her parents, then I think about the cop parked outside their house and the bank manager and then I think about Gerald Painter. I hand Dad the shotgun and carry Sam outside.
zh_text: 我想到茱蒂和她的父母親，我想到他們家外面那個警察，我想到銀行的經理，最後想到傑拉德·潘特。我把槍遞給爹，然後抱著小珊出去。

en_text: The dark sky is breaking on the horizon, a purple-colored light bruising the edge of the world. I carry Sam over my shoulder and she’s chilly; I wonder if her blanket is still in Jodie’s car. I walk quietly. I keep waiting for the gunshot that will send hundreds of birds into the sky and Sam jumping out of her skin. I buckle her into the backseat, tucking the blanket in around her and under her chin. I sit in the driver’s seat and wonder what Dad is doing right now, but I don’t go and check. I look at the cell phones, killing time while my father kills time in a different way. I’ve missed a couple of calls from Schroder but I don’t phone him back. I turn them off. I don’t care about anything else now except Sam.
zh_text: 地平線上，黑色的天空出現了隙縫，紫色的光線擦傷了世界的邊緣。我把小珊扛在肩上，她渾身冰冷。不知道她的毯子是不是還在茱蒂的車裡。我不讓自己的腳步發出一點聲音，等待槍聲響起，一響就有會好幾百隻鳥飛向天空，也會把小珊嚇一大跳。我幫她繋好後座的安全帶，用毯子把她好好裏起來。我坐上駕駛座，不知道爹在幹嘛，可是我不想進去看了。我看看手機，消磨時間，而我爹正用很不一樣的方法消磨他的時間。有兩通未接來電，是施羅德打來的，我不想回電。我把手機的電源關掉。现在我什麼都不想管，只要照顧小珊。

en_text: After a couple of minutes an engine revs loudly, then headlights appear as a car races toward us, slightly out of control, as if driven by someone who hasn’t driven a car in twenty years. It swerves past us, then it’s gone, a dust cloud following it.
zh_text: 兩分鐘後，我聽到怒吼的引擎聲，車頭燈出現了，朝著我們衝過來，有點失控，似乎開車的人二十年沒上路了。那台車繞過我們，消失了，留下一大團沙塵。

en_text: I turn the key but nothing happens. I try a couple more times but the result is the same. I pop the hood. Dad hasn’t done any damage. All he’s done is tug the leads off the spark plugs. It only takes me a minute to secure them back into place, but it’s all the head start he needs. I pop the boot. The bag of money is gone. The taillights of Dad’s new car have disappeared; he’s getting further away, with a shotgun and a bag full of cash and his desires of the last twenty years no longer suppressed.
zh_text: 我轉動鑰匙，車子卻沒動靜。我又試了兩次，結果還是一樣。我把引擎蓋抬起來。爹沒弄壞我的車子。他只把火星塞上的導線拔掉了。我用了不到一分鐘的時間就把線接回去，但他已經搶得先機。我打開後行李廂，錢不見了。爹的新車消失了；他已經遠遠逃走，手上有槍，还有一整袋的錢，過去二十年累積下來的欲望再也不用受到壓抑。

en_text: I don’t bother chasing him because I’d never catch him, not unless I drove at speeds that would put my daughter’s life at risk. What I said to Dad earlier still stands now—I’m done with it. The police can catch the rest of the men—they surely know by now who they’re looking for. On the chance they haven’t been caught, I can’t go back home and can’t go to my in-laws’. Driving into the police station is an unknown—too many reasons for them to arrest me. By now they want to put me away, if for nothing else than for freeing my father. They’re out there searching for him too. Before I end up in jail I want to at least spend Christmas Day with my daughter.
zh_text: 我不想追上去，反正我也追不上，不然我開車的速度會讓我女兒的生命受到威脅。我剛才對爹說的話仍有效——沒我的事了。警察會把剩下的人都抓起來——他們現在一定知道該去追捕誰。要是搶匪尚未束手就擒，我不能回家，也不能去岳父岳母家。要把車子開去警察局嗎？我不知道一警方要逮捕我，已經有充分的理由。现在他們會把我關起來，不爲別的，光爲放走我爹就夠了。他們也會去搜尋我爹的行蹤。在入獄前，我至少可以跟女兒一起度過耶誕節。

en_text: My head is jumbled up with anger and hate and fear, and I’m so tired that, in the end, the easiest decision is to head to a motel. I find a place modern enough to have been built this year, with a sign out front saying VACANCY. I park outside the office and ring the bell and a couple of minutes later a sleepy man in his fifties appears and helps me out. I pay with cash.
zh_text: 我滿腦子憤怒、憎恨、恐懼，而且我好累，最後我決定最簡單的方法就是去汽車旅館。我找到一個地方，很新，應該是今年才開的，前面的板子上寫著有空房。我把車停在辧公室外面，按了鈴，過了兩分鐘，一名五十多歲的男人睡眼惺忪地走出來，幫我找了一間房。我付了現金。

en_text: The room is as modern as the surroundings would suggest, but I don’t really take the time to check them out. I carry Sam and put her gently into bed, taking off only her shoes, then I collapse on top of my bed and fall asleep.
zh_text: 房間很新，跟周遭的環境很配，但我也無心細看所有的設施。我輕輕地把小珊放在床上，只幫她脫了鞋子，然後也倒下去睡著了。

en_text: They’re shooting one in four. They found Kelvin Johnson, but the other two bank robbers are in the wind, along with Oliver Church—though news of another body means Church may have been found. Dawn has come and gone and Schroder is dead on his feet. They all are. They all feel like zombies and look like zombies and it’s nights like these that keep divorce lawyers rolling in cash.
zh_text: 機率是四分之一。他們找到了凱爾文·強森，但正在追查另外兩個搶匪，仍有奧利佛·丘奇不過又出現了一具屍體，表示找到了丘奇。黎明降臨，又離開了，施羅德覺得自己跟殭屍一樣。大家都變成殭屍了，看起來也像殭屍，就是這樣加班的夜晚，讓離婚律師的荷包滿滿。

en_text: The SWAT team is long gone now, having packed away its guns and headed for home, all of them still on standby if needed—all of them probably tempted to switch off their phones. Schroder knows that he is. They’ve busted into four houses and for all their efforts they’ve come away with one suspect.
zh_text: 武裝防禦小組早就離開了，收起槍枝打道回府，有些人仍會待命，以備不時之需——他們應該都很想把手機關掉。施羅德自己也想把手機關掉。他們已經闖入了四間民宅，費了這麼多力氣只找到一個嫌犯。

en_text: The patrol officers sent to check the slaughterhouse have reported a body, the head of a male so badly damaged that identification was impossible. No sign of anybody else, but a couple of magazines, a small games unit, and a battery-powered lantern suggest whoever was out there had been there most of the night.
zh_text: 去屠宰場探看的巡警回報他們發現了一具屍體，頭被打爛到根本無法辨認。沒看到其他人，只發現了兩本雜誌、掌上游戲機和電池燈籠，應該有人在那裡待了一晚上。

en_text: It’s a twenty-five-minute drive to the slaughterhouse from his last location. He’s too tired to drive fast, and has the window down so the air can whistle around his face to keep him awake. He makes a couple of calls to get the ball rolling, organizes the forensics techies to come out; long nights for everybody now turning into long mornings too.
zh_text: 從他所在的地點到屠宰場，大概要開二十五分鐘的車。他累到沒辦法開太快，还得把車窗搖下來，讓拂過臉上的氣流幫他保持清醒。他又打了兩通電話叫其他人做事，要鑑識專家跟他會合；大家忙了一整晚，接下來還要忙一整天。

en_text: The slaughterhouse is an imposing building in the early-morning light. It’s mostly made up of concrete that could probably survive an atomic bomb. There’s a police car parked outside with two officers sitting in it. The air is full of birdsong and the loudest sound is Schroder’s feet across the ground. The officers lead him inside and he keeps yawning on the way. Assuming he ever makes it home, he’s going to sleep for about twenty-four hours, he thinks; but at this stage it’s an assumption he wouldn’t bet his life on.
zh_text: 在清晨的光線中，屠宰場十分宏偉。幾乎全用混凝土蓋成，或許連原子彈都無法炸毀。外面停了一台警車，裡面坐了兩名警官。空氣中全是鳥兒啁啾鳴囀的聲音，施羅德的腳步聲最吵。警官領他進了屠宰場，他一路一直打呵欠。要是能回到家，他應該會睡上二十四個小時；但此刻也只能想罷了，他不確定自己能不能回家。

en_text: Oliver Church is surrounded in blood. He thinks it’s Oliver Church. The clothes certainly suggest it’s not Edward Hunter or his father, and he doesn’t see too many other possibilities at this point. Church’s head is twisted to the side with a large indentation in the side of it which has elongated the front of it, so the distance between his left eye and the left side of his mouth is far greater than the right. He looks like he’s fallen from a great height, so much so that for a moment Schroder is reminded of Suction Cup Guy. A piece of rebar with a bloody lump of cement on the end lies next to him. No way of knowing at this point if Church was tortured to give up more information, or tortured for taking Sam Hunter.
zh_text: 奥利佛·丘奇躺在血泊中。應該是奥利佛·丘奇吧。那身衣服顯然不是艾德華·杭特，也不是他父親，還會有其他人嗎？丘奇的頭扭向一旁，旁邊凹下去一大塊，把他的頭拉長了，所以他左眼和左邊嘴角之間的距離比右邊長很多。感覺他從很高的地方掉下來，眞的很像，施羅德不禁想起了吸盤男。他旁邊丢了一條鋼筋，連著一塊血淋淋的水泥。現在還不知道丘奇是否曾經遭人折磨，還是因爲綁走小珊而遭到拷打。

en_text: “No other cars out there?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「沒看到其他的車子嗎？」施羅德問。

en_text: “None.”

Probably Jack Hunter took Church’s car, which means father and son have separated. There’s an old mattress lying on the floor. Jammed between it and the wall, barely in sight, is a small teddy bear. The bear isn’t that old but seems to have had a hard life. He bets Sam Hunter cuddled that bear every night of her life, and wonders what she called it. His own daughter has a bear that she sleeps with. For a second he imagines it was her out here and not Sam, and the image is so strong it makes him want to cry. Jesus—he’s so tired.
zh_text: 或许傑克·杭特把丘奇的車開走了，表示他們父子已經分道揚鑣。地上有塊很舊的床墊。床墊和牆間塞了一隻小小的泰迪熊，不仔細看還看不到。泰迪熊看起來還很新，卻磨損得很厲害。他猜小珊一定每天都抱著泰迪熊睡覺，不知道她給這隻熊取了什麼名字。他女兒睡覺時也會抱著泰迪熊。在那一剎那間他想像被困在這裡的是他女兒，不是小珊，光想到他就承受不了，眼淚幾乎奪眶而出。天啊——他眞的累壞了。

en_text: “You think he found her?” Landry asks on the phone.
zh_text: 「你覺得他找到女兒了嗎？」藍德里在電話上問。

en_text: “I think so. I think Oliver Church paid the price for taking her.” “He deserved what he got,” Landry says. “Deserved it years ago.”
zh_text: 「應該找到了。我覺得奧利佛·丘奇已經付出綁架她的代價。」「他早該碎屍萬段，」藍德里說，「早在幾年前就該死了。」

en_text: “I know. But now I have to lock Edward Hunter up for it. Wasn’t his job to find Church, wasn’t his job to get his daughter back.”
zh_text: 「我知道。但現在我得因爲他死了而把艾德華·杭特關起來。他不該負責去找丘奇，不該負責去把他女兒找回來。」

en_text: “Wasn’t it?” Landry asks.
zh_text: 「爲什麼不應該？」藍德里問。

en_text: Even if it was Jack Hunter who pounded in Church’s skull, it still comes back on Edward for freeing the old man. Edward has to go to jail now, and that leaves Sam where? Maybe, if he’s lucky, he could get a suspended sentence—if he can prove he didn’t kill any of the others. Maybe.
zh_text: 就算把丘奇的頭打爛的兇手是傑克·杭特，還是要怪罪艾德華放走了他爸爸。艾德華得去坐牢了，那小珊怎麼辦呢？或許，夠幸運的話，他可以被判緩刑如果他能證明自己沒殺其他人的话。或许吧。

en_text: Schroder bends down and picks up the teddy bear. Jack Hunter is on the loose and there’s already a task force looking for him—but that’s not his job, his job is to find the men who robbed the bank, and that job is almost over.
zh_text: 施羅德彎下腰，撿起泰迪熊。傑克·杭特逃走了，已經有人出去搜索但他不負責追捕老杭特，他要負責抓到搶匪，而這件工作已經快要結束了。

en_text: “There’s nothing more we can do tonight,” Landry is saying. “The girl was there, and she’s not there anymore. Edward Hunter got her, has to be him. He’ll have taken her somewhere safe, and he’ll keep her safe until all this is over. We’ll get the rest of the bank crew today, you know we will.
zh_text: 「今天晚上就這樣了，」藍德里說，「小女孩被綁架，現在不見了。艾德華·杭特一定把她帶回去了，不是他還有誰？肯定把她帶去安全的地方了，也會好好保護她到風聲平息爲止。我們今天就會抓到所有的搶匪，你知道我們辦得到。不然就明天了。」

en_text: Tomorrow at the latest.” He hangs up and walks past the two officers. “Call me if anything changes,” he tells them. And with that he gets into his car and heads home, hoping for at least a couple of hours’ sleep and some time with his family before he has to start up again, right where he’s left off.
zh_text: 他掛上電話，走到兩名警官旁邊。「情況有變的話就通知我。」他對兩人說。然後他把車子開回家，希望至少能睡兩個小時，跟家人相處一段時光，然後再從此刻中斷的地方繼續辦案。

en_text: I wake up in the early afternoon with Sam cuddled up next to me. I let her carry on sleeping while I make some coffee and go about waking up some more. I switch on the TV and can’t find any news anywhere, as if this city is sick of the news now. There are holiday movies on, a fantasy on one channel, action on another, drama everywhere else, and I wonder what Hollywood would think if one day a Christchurch story showed up on its doorstep—whether it’d think the tale was too dark or too real to turn into a Christmas blockbuster. I prop Sam up in front of one of the movies and she watches it quietly, not laughing or smiling or even saying a word. She misses her mum and she misses Mr. Fluff ’n’ Stuff and she doesn’t understand why we’re spending Christmas Day in a motel room instead of our home, or with her grandparents.
zh_text: 過了中午我才醒來，小珊貼在我懷裡。我沒吵醒她，我泡了杯咖啡，讓自己更清醒一點。開了電視，卻沒有一台在播報新聞，彷佛這座城已經看膩了新聞。很多節日電影，一台在播奇幻片，一台在播動作片，還有好多台在播劇情片，基督城的故事會不會也有一天變成好萊塢的題材？——要拍成耶誕節賣座鉅片，故事會不會太黑暗？還是太眞實？我撐起小珊的身子，讓她看電視，她靜靜看著，不哭，不笑，不發一語。她想念媽媽，她想念毛飽先生，她不知道爲什麼我們要在汽車旅館過耶誕節，不是在家裡，也不是在外公外婆家。

en_text: I take Sam to the cemetery so she can spend some time with her mother. With all that’s happened, I figure it’ll be the last time the three of us are together for a while. I carry Sam out of the car and sit her down by her mother’s grave and we hold hands and I tell her over and over that everything is going to be okay. There are plenty of other people out at the cemetery, all of them like me, spending time with the dead; Christmas Day is a day for celebration no matter what world you’re in. When I head back to the car with Sam, people keep watching us, and though I’m used to it, this morning it bothers me more than ever. I shield Sam from their stares and drive her back to the motel. She’s asleep again before we get there, and I lay her back on the bed and check on her every five or ten minutes, sometimes holding her hand, not sure what I should do next. I leave the TV on and flick channels but nothing of any interest comes up. Outside, Christmas afternoon is looking like a hot one; only a couple of clouds in the sky, the sun beating down on the city. Mine’s the only car in the parking lot out front. I figure everybody else has family or a better place to be than this motel.
zh_text: 我帶小珊到墓地去，讓她跟媽媽在一起。發生了這麼多事，我想這是最後一次我們三個人相聚的時光。我把小珊抱出車子，讓她坐在媽媽的墳墓旁邊，我們握著手，我一次又一次地告诉她，會沒事的。來掃墓的人不少，他們都跟我一樣，和逝者一起共度佳節；不論你在活人還是死人的世界裡，都該好好慶祝耶誕節。和小珊一起回到車上時，大家都在看我們，雖然我已經習慣了旁人的目光，這天早上我郤覺得特別不自在。我用身體擋住小珊，不讓他們瞪著她，然後開車回汽車旅館。回到汽車旅館前她又睡著了，我把她送回床上，每隔五到十分鐘就看看她怎麼樣，有時候我會握住她的手，不知道接下來該怎麼辦。我開著電視不停換台，看不到吸引目光的節目。外面的耶誕節下午看起來很熱；空中只有兩朵雲，太陽熱辣辣地照著基督城。前面的停車場裡只停了我的車。我想，其他人都有更好的去處吧，不需要留在這間汽車旅館裡。

en_text: I sit at the window watching the Christmas day, thinking about what today could have meant, about the presents we didn’t get to give, the family time we never got to have, the Christmas lunch and barbecue dinner and the excitement of Santa. I think about my dad, wondering where he is now, what or who he’s looking for. I think about the darkness he’s trying to satisfy. My own monster is quiet now, and maybe that’s the way it’ll stay.
zh_text: 我坐在窗邊看著窗外的耶誕節，思索今天有什麼意義，想到那些我們沒機會送的禮物、那段我們永遠無法擁有的家庭時光、耶誕節午餐和烤肉晚餐，還有小珊欣喜欲狂的樣子。我想到我爹，不知道去哪裡了，不知道他想去找誰，或找什嬮東西。我想到他想要滿足的閽黑。我自己的怪獸安靜下來了，或许它再也不會開口說一句話。

en_text:
My thoughts turn to Schroder when his car pulls in to the motel parking lot. Two patrol cars pull up alongside him, but Schroder is the only one who gets out. A fourth car, a dark station wagon, also pulls in. I watch Schroder go to the office; he disappears inside for about sixty seconds, then comes back out. It’s Christmas Day and I figure he’d rather be anywhere else but here, and I’m the same—except there are still a few places worse than this, for me. Jail is one of them. The slaughterhouse is another.
He walks past my window and glances in and sees me but doesn’t stop.
zh_text:
念頭才轉到施羅德身上，他的車就開進了汽車旅館的停車場。旁邊跟來了兩台巡邏車，但只有施羅德下車了。第四台車跟著進來，深色的旅行車。我看著施羅德走進旅館的辦公室；他進去了大約六十秒，然後又出來。今天是耶誕節，我想他一定很不希望來這裡找我，我也不想待在這裡——只是有幾個地方對我來說比這間汽車旅館還討厭。比方說監獄。比方說屠宰場。
他走過窗前，往內瞥了一眼，看到我卻沒停下腳步。他直接走到門口敲了敲門。

en_text: He heads right to the door and knocks on it.
zh_text: 他走過窗前，往內瞥了一眼，看到我郤沒停下腳步。他直接走到門口敲了敲門。

en_text: “Come on, Eddie,” he says, going with Eddie instead of Edward, and I figure he thinks it makes him sound friendly. “Open up.”
zh_text: 「嘿，艾迪，」他說，叫我艾迪，而不是艾德華，我猜他想要聽起來友善點。「開門。」

en_text: “Leave us alone,” I say.
zh_text: 「不要管我們。」我說。

en_text: “Eddie . . .”
“It’s Christmas.”
zh_text: 「今天是耶誕節。」

en_text: “You can’t keep her here.” “What?”
zh_text: 「你不能把她留在這裡。」「什麼？」

en_text: “You can’t keep your daughter here. It isn’t right.” “There are plenty of things that aren’t right.”
zh_text: 「你不能把女兒留在這裡。這樣不好。」「我們已經碰到很多不好的事情了。」

en_text: “I know that, Eddie.” “You were wrong.” “About what?”
zh_text: 「艾迪，我知道。」「你說錯了。」「我什麼說錯了？」

en_text: “About a lot of things,” I say. “Mostly about this city being on a precipice. It’s already fallen, don’t you see that?”
zh_text: 「你錯了，大錯特錯，」我說，「尤其是你說，這座城岌岌可危。基督城早就完蛋了，你還看不出來嗎？」

en_text: “Open the door, Eddie.”
zh_text: 「艾迪，開門。」

en_text: I get up and open the door. There’s nowhere to run, and no need to. It’s all over. I have my daughter back and the police can deal with the rest, they can find my dad, they can find the men who killed my wife. Schroder doesn’t look as if he’s slept. He steps inside, carrying a brown paper bag.
zh_text: 我站起來開了門。無處可逃，也不需要逃。結束了。女兒回到我身邊，剩下的就交給警方了，他們會找到我爹，他們會找到殺了我妻子的人。施羅德看起來沒闔過眼。他走進來，手上拿著牛皮紙袋。

en_text: “Don’t take her yet,” I say.
zh_text: 「等一會兒再帶她走。」我說。

en_text: “Eddie . . .”
“Please, it’s Christmas.”
zh_text: 「拜託，今天是耶誕節。」

en_text: “I know. It’s not fair. It’s . . . it’s just the way it is.”
zh_text: 「我知道。很不公平。但……但我要公事公辦。」

en_text: I take a step back. Schroder looks over at the other cars and the station wagon turns around and backs toward the room. Schroder comes in and looks down at Sam, who isn’t even aware of his presence.
zh_text: 我退後一步。施羅德回頭看看其他的車子，旅行車掉了個頭，對著我們的房間倒車。施羅德走到床邊看著我女兒，小珊根本沒發覺有人來了。

en_text: “Such a beautiful little girl,” he says.
zh_text: 「好可爱的小女孩。」他說。

en_text: “I know.”
zh_text: 「我知道。」

en_text: “I have a daughter of my own,” he says. “And a son.” “And?”
zh_text: 「我也有一個女兒，」他說，「和一個兒子。」「那又怎樣？」

en_text: “And I don’t know, I guess I wanted you to know. Maybe what you said about this city, maybe I should take your advice and get out of here.”
zh_text: 「我不知道，我只想讓你明白。或許你對基督城的看法沒錯，或許我該聽你的，遠走高飛。」

en_text: “Then who will protect it?”
zh_text: 「那誰來保護這裡的人？」

en_text: Two men step out of the station wagon and open the back of it. They lift out a gurney and a sheet.
zh_text: 旅行車上下來了兩個人，打開了車尾的門。他們抬出一座擔架和一張床單。

en_text: “Let me take her,” I say. “It’s not how it’s done.” “Please . . .”
zh_text: 「我來抱她吧。」我說。「程序不是這樣。」

en_text: “I’m sorry, Eddie, I’m really, really sorry.”
zh_text: 「拜託···」「我很抱歉，艾迪，我真的真的很抱歉。」

en_text: At first I stand back as the two men come inside, and then Schroder has to hold me back as they lay Sam on the stretcher. They unfold a sheet and drape it over her, then carry her away. Schroder opens the paper bag in his hand and pulls out Mr. Fluff ’n’ Stuff. He lifts the sheet and tucks it between Sam’s arm and her body.
zh_text: 那兩個男人進來時，我還能承受，退到一旁，然後，當他們把小珊抬上擔架時，施羅德必須把我制住。他們攤開床單，蓋住小珊，然後把她抬走了。施羅德打開手中的紙袋，拉出毛飽先生。他翻開床單，把毛飽先生塞在小珊的手臂和身體中間。

en_text: “We’ll take good care of her,” he says.
zh_text: 「我們會好好照顧她。」他說。

en_text: I try to say something but can’t. It feels like Schroder has extended his fist right down my throat. I cry, and right then Schroder embraces me and I let it all out, crying on his shoulder as the two men take my dead daughter out of the motel room and out of my life.
zh_text: 我想開口說話，卻哽住了。感覺就像施羅德的拳頭一把塞進了我的喉嚨。我放聲大哭，就在施羅德抱住我的時候，我把持不住了，靠在他肩膀上悲泣，兩個男人把我早已死去的女兒帶走，帶出我的生命。

en_text: Edward sits in the passenger seat saying nothing on the way to the police station. When they arrive, Schroder leads him into an interrogation room and heads back out to grab a couple of coffees and to let Hunter compose himself. The police station is busier than it’s ever been on a Christmas day; the task force to find Jack Hunter is operating at full speed, as are the people searching for the final two bank robbers. It’s only a matter of time now—but of course everything is always just a matter of time.
zh_text: 在前往警局的路上，艾德華坐在施羅德旁邊，默不作聲。到了警局後，施羅德領他走進偵訊室，又出去拿了兩杯咖啡，给杭特一點時間鎭定下來。耶誕節的警察局從來沒像今天這麼熱鬧；搜尋傑克·杭特的工作已經全速進行，搜捕最後兩名銀行搶匪的警探也卯足全力。只是早晚的問題了——但不論如何，什麼都只是早晚的問題。

en_text: Seeing the little dead girl was hard. Once again he imagined it was his own daughter, and once again it brought him close to tears, and when he hugged Edward and held him he had no idea he was about to do it before it happened, and no idea of the impact it would have on him. Hunter sobbed into his shoulder, his entire body convulsing, and they stayed that way for what seemed like ages before Hunter pulled himself away.
zh_text: 看到死去的小女孩眞令人難過。他又在腦海中想像如果那是他的女兒，眼淚又差點奪眶而出，抱住艾德華的時候，他事前不知道自己會如此眞情流露，也不知道自己會飽受衝擊。杭特靠在他的肩膀上哭泣，全身不斷抽搐，他們抱在一起的時間感覺好漫長，然後杭特把自己拉開了。

en_text: It was almost seven o’clock in the morning by the time Schroder got home. His family was awake. They hadn’t waited up for him—his daughter had woken early because that’s what Christmas was all about, at least for the kids. His wife had let her open just one present; she was waiting for him to get home before opening the rest. He managed to stay awake for another hour before going to bed, and had got almost four hours’ sleep before his wife came in to wake him. She handed him his cell phone. He didn’t want to answer it but he had to. Witnesses had spotted Edward Hunter that morning at the cemetery where his wife was buried. They’d phoned the police because Edward was carrying his daughter around and his daughter obviously wasn’t just sleeping. Before the phone call was over, there was more news—another body had been found.
zh_text: 施羅德回到家的時候，快要早上七點了。家人都起床了。他們沒熬夜等他——他女兒特別早起，因爲孩子們在耶誕節總會特別早醒過來。他妻子只讓女兒拆了一個禮物；她要等他回家，然後再打開剩餘的禮物。他勉強撐了一個小時才上床睡覺，睡了差不多四個小時吧，他妻子進來把他叫醒，把他的手機遞過來。他不想接電話，但不得不接。那天早上，目擊證人在艾德華·杭特妻子的墓地看到他。艾德華抱著女兒走來走去，但小珊顯然不是睡著了，所以他們報警了。電話還沒掛上，又有新聞了——發現了另一具屍體。

en_text: A week ago Hunter had everything—a wife, a child, a job, he had dreams, the family had Christmas, they all had a future. It makes Schroder sick to know that on any given day your entire future can change.
zh_text: 一星期前，杭特什麼都有妻子、孩子、工作，他有梦想，他們一家人等著過耶誕節，期望美好的未來。想到就在某一天，你的未來可能會天翻地覆，施羅德就覺得難受。

en_text: He makes his way back toward the interrogation room and has his hand on the door handle, the two cups of coffee balanced in his other hand, when his cell phone rings. He steps back from the door and almost drops both coffees while fumbling for the phone.
zh_text: 回到偵訊室，他一手托著兩杯咖啡，一手剛放上門把，他的手機就響了。他後退幾步，從口袋裡摸出電話時差點把兩杯咖啡都打翻了。

en_text: “Schroder,” he says.
zh_text: 「我是施羅德。」他說。

en_text: “Hey, Carl. I hear it’s been a long night,” Tate says.
zh_text: 「嘿，卡爾，聽說你忙了一晚上。」泰特說。

en_text: “You got something for me?”
zh_text: 「你有消息要告诉我嗎？」

en_text: “Yeah. I know who put Roger Harwick up to stabbing Jack Hunter.” “Who?”
zh_text: 「對呀。我知道是誰指使羅傑·哈威克刺傷傑克·杭特。」「誰？」

en_text: “You’re not going to believe it,” Tate says, but he’s wrong, because Schroder does. After all—the last twenty-four hours have been nothing but believable.
zh_text: 「你聽了也不會信。」泰特錯了，因爲施羅德相信他的話。畢竟，過去二十四個小時內的事件都不由得人不信。

en_text: I knew Sam was dead from the moment I saw her in the slaughter-house. I knew it before I had even stepped fully into the room. Felt it, even, if that makes sense. Knew it, felt it, saw it—and then ignored it. Just pushed it out of my mind for as long as I could until somebody—and it took Schroder to do it—came along and shoved the reality back into my face.
zh_text: 在屠宰場一看到小珊，我就知道她已經死了。還沒走進那個房間，我就知道了。應該說我感覺到了。知道了、感覺到了、看到了——然後我不理會。我故意不去想，直到有人要我面對事實，這個人就是施羅德。

en_text: Dad’s tears weren’t tears of joy when he saw her, they were tears of pain. Sam was more like her mother than ever because Mummy’s a ghost, and so is Sam now. It was Christmas morning and I took my dead little girl out to the cemetery to see her dead mother while those around me stared and watched, not understanding, wondering what was happening.
zh_text: 爹看到小珊便流下了眼淚，並非欣喜若狂，而是傷痛難當。小珊看起来更像她媽媽了，因爲媽媽變成鬼了，小珊也變成鬼了。耶誕節到了，我帶我死掉的小公主去墓地看她死掉的媽媽，周圍的人驚訝瞪視，他們不明白，不知道發生了什麼事。

en_text: Schroder doesn’t make me wait long in the interrogation room—maybe five minutes in total, which I figure is pretty good of him. He comes in with a folder tucked under his arm and a couple of coffees in his hand, supported by a small cardboard tray. He sits down opposite me and slides one of the coffees over.
zh_text: 施羅德沒讓我在偵訊室等很久一只等了五分鐘吧，他一直對我還不錯。他進來的時候，手臂夾了檔案，手上的紙板托盤放了兩杯咖啡。他坐在我對面，把一杯咖啡推過來。

en_text: “You need it,” he says.
zh_text: 「喝吧。」他說。

en_text: “What I need is to be with Sam.”
zh_text: 「我想看小珊。」

en_text: “Look, Eddie, this is tough—God knows you’ve gone through more than anybody deserves, but . . .”
zh_text: 「聽我說，艾迪，我們心裡都不好過——你承受的痛苦比誰都多，但是……」

en_text: He runs out of words. Just like that, like somebody wound him up ten minutes ago and the spring keeping him going has come to a stop.
zh_text: 他說不下去了。就停住了，彷彿有人十分鐘前幫他上了發條，現在發條已經鬆開了。

en_text: “I want to be with Sam.” “I know. I know you do.” “Please.”
zh_text: 「我想跟小珊在一起。」「我知道。我知道你想見小珊。」「求求你。」

en_text: “Soon. Okay? Just—we just need to go over a few things first. Then I can take you to her. Okay?” I nod.
zh_text: 「等一下，好嗎？我們先處理一些事情。然後我就帶你過去。OK？」我點頭。

en_text: “Tell me what happened. Do you know where your father is?”
zh_text: 「告訴我發生了什麼事。你知道你父親在哪裡嗎？」

en_text: “No idea at all,” I say, and then I fill him in on the details. I tell him about the slaughterhouse and how he can find Oliver Church out there, how Dad killed him, how I have no idea where Dad is now.
zh_text: 「不知道。」然後我告訴他事情的經過。我告訴他地點是屠宰場、要怎麼找到奧利佛·丘奇、我爹怎麼殺了他、我爲什麼不知爹的去向。

en_text: “Look, Eddie, we already know about the slaughterhouse. You got out there not long before we got there. Truth is you could be facing some serious jail time. We’ve got bodies stacking up and you’re at the center of it all.”
zh_text: 「聽著，艾迪，我們已經查到屠宰場了。你們才剛離開，我們就過去了。事實上，你可能要坐牢坐很久。我們找到了好幾具屍體，都繞著你打轉。」

en_text: “I didn’t kill anybody,” I say, “except for the guy who made me drown you, and the guy I ran over—but that was an accident. I didn’t even kill Bracken. It was the woman.”
zh_text: 「我沒殺人，」我說，「除了那個逼我淹死你的人，跟那個被我輾過去的人——可是那算意外吧。我沒殺布萊肯。兇手是那個女人。」

en_text: “We know. We checked the prints on the knife. There was blood on them. Location of the prints beneath the blood showed she was the one holding them when it got used. You’re sitting okay as far as that one goes, and maybe for Church too, if you can prove self-defense,” he says, “if you hear what I’m saying. You or your dad had to defend against him. But Jesus, Eddie, you helped a serial killer escape. We can’t write that one off.”
zh_text: 「我們查出來了。我們檢查過刀子上的指紋，上面有血。血跡下的指紋位置表示刀子插進布萊肯身體時，握刀的人是她。所以，這件殺人案跟你撇清了關係，或許丘奇的也一樣，如果你能證明是爲了自衛，」他說，「但你懂我的意思吧。你或你父親爲了自衛而抵抗他。但天啊，艾迪，你幫連續殺人犯逃獄。這可沒辦法一筆勾銷。」

en_text: “When she killed Bracken she took away our chance of finding Sam alive.”
zh_text: 「她殺了布萊肯，害我們沒機會救回小珊。」

en_text: “Then we need to find her before your father does,” Schroder says. “There’s another thing, Eddie. Your father. It turns out he’s the one who put Harwick up to stabbing him.”
zh_text: 「我們得搶在你父親前面先找到她，」施羅德說，「還有一件事，艾迪。跟你父親有關。原來，是他指使哈威克來刺傷他。」

en_text: “What? What are you saying?”
zh_text: 「什麼？你是什麼意思？」

en_text: “It was all a setup. He got Harwick to stab him, to hurt him enough to require hospital treatment but not enough so he’d need a morgue. He knew you’d come and get him. He played everybody. He completely played you.”
zh_text: 「是他布的局。他要哈威克刺傷他，要傷得夠重，必須送到醫院诊治，但不能太重，不然他就要進太平間了。他知道你會來找他。大家都被騙了。他從頭到尾都在騙你。」

en_text: I wonder at what point Dad decided to use his daughter-in-law’s death to his advantage; whether the man knew immediately he could use the tragedy to escape. I wonder if he even cared about what happened to Jodie. I’d like to think it at least took him a few days to think it through, but for some reason I don’t think it did. For some reason I think the moment the news was broken to him about the bank robbery he knew in an instant he was going to manipulate me; that he would tell me about the darkness and the monster and would get me to become like him; that the only thing standing between him and freedom was an innocent stabbing of the kind where every major organ was missed, where he could spend the night in a hospital so understaffed that only a single nurse was seen.
zh_text: 我心想，不知道爹何時決定該好好利用兒媳婦的死；他是不是立刻想到能用茱蒂的悲劇來逃獄。不知道他到底在不在乎茱蒂死了。我寧可想，他起碼花了幾天的時間好好思索，但不知爲何，我覺得他根本連想都没想。不知爲何，我認爲他一聽到搶案的消息，他就知道他可以玩弄我；他要告诉我闍黑跟怪獸的事，讓我變得跟他一樣；只要無害的一刺，避開重要的器官，他就能被送進人手不足到只看到一個護士的醫院過一晚上，就能重獲自由。

en_text: “I’m sorry, Eddie.”
zh_text: 「艾迪，我很抱歉。」

en_text: “You got the rest of the bank robbers?”
zh_text: 「其餘的搶匪都抓到了嗎？」

en_text: “We got the names. One of them we have in custody, one of them we’re still looking for.”
zh_text: 「我們知道是誰了。一個已經被拘留，另一個我們還在找。」

en_text: “And the third?”
zh_text: 「還有一個呢？」

en_text: “The third was found a few hours ago. He was cut up so badly we were lucky to identify him. We found your father’s prints at the scene.”
zh_text: 「還有一個幾小時前被發現了。他被切得亂七八糟，能認出來算我們好運。我們在現場找到你父親的指紋。」

en_text: I stare at him without saying a word. My dad got one of the men who killed Jodie. I don’t know how I feel about this. I don’t know how I feel about anything. I’m numb, too numb, all I have now is all this hurt from Sam not being here.
zh_text: 我閉著嘴，瞪著他。我爹殺了一個害死茱蒂的人。我不知道該作何感想。我不知道我還有沒有感覺。我麻木了，整個麻木了，我只因爲小珊不在而覺得難受。

en_text: “Did you tell your dad to kill these men?” “No.”
zh_text: 「你叫你爹去殺了這些人嗎？」「沒。」

en_text: “But you’re glad he’s made a start, right?” “Yes.”
zh_text: 「但你很高興他下手了，對不對？」「對。」

en_text: “How’d he get the name?”
zh_text: 「他怎麼知道有誰？」

en_text: “I . . . I don’t know. Maybe from Church. Maybe he had it all along.” “Maybe.”
zh_text: 「我……我不知道。可能是丘奇說的。可能他早就知道搶匪是誰了。」

en_text: “What’s going to happen to me?”
zh_text: 「或许吧。」「你們要怎麼處置我？」

en_text:
“For now? Nothing. We can’t link you to any premeditated killings. The blood results came in and have cleared you with Kingsly. I’m sorry I didn’t believe you earlier—it’s just that, well, I was certain you’d killed him.”
“The blood cleared me?”
zh_text:
「現在？我們要放了你。我們找不到你蓄意殺人的證據。驗血報告出來了，洗刷了你謀殺金斯理的嫌疑。對不起，我不该懷疑你——只是，怎麼說，我一直以爲你殺了他。」
「驗血報告還我清白？」

en_text: “We ran it against your father’s and none of the markers matched, it’s a completely different blood type, so whoever killed Kingsly isn’t related to your father.”
zh_text: 「我們比對了你父親的血液，標記都不符合，完全不一樣的血型，所以殺了金斯理的人跟你爸爸沒有血緣關係。」

en_text: “It didn’t match,” I say.
zh_text: 「不符合。」我說。

en_text: “You sound surprised.”
zh_text: 「你似乎很驚訝。」

en_text: “What? No. No, of course not,” I say, my mind racing. What does this mean? What does this mean?
zh_text: 「什麼？沒有，沒有，怎麼會覺得驚訝。」我的心跳得好快。爲什麼？爲什麼？

en_text: “You set your father free, and for that we should be keeping you in custody, Edward, but things having gone the way they have, those who make these kinds of decisions have agreed that you can go home instead. For now anyway. You’ll have to answer for it—and not to me, but to a judge. If your dad doesn’t hurt anybody innocent and we get him back real soon, I’ll do what I can to help you. Of course there are other factors to consider, like . . .”
zh_text: 「你放走了你父親，我們可以用這個理由拘留你，艾德華，但事情就這麼發生了，負責做決定的人同意你可以回家。反正你先回去吧。你得負責，不是對我，而是對法官。如果你父親沒害了無辜的人，我們不久之後就把他抓回來，我會盡力保你。當然，還有其他的因素要考量，比方說……」

en_text: He keeps talking but I’m no longer listening. All I can think about is the blood type. My blood type doesn’t match my father’s blood type. If Schroder took blood from me now and compared it to the blood found at Kingsly’s house, it would match, only he’s got no reason to do that. He’s got no reason because he doesn’t suspect me anymore. He’s got no reason to run the blood found at Bracken’s office because he knows it’s mine. If he took blood from me now and compared it to my father . . .
zh_text: 他說個不停，我卻充耳不聞。我一直在想血型的事情。我的血型跟我爹的不一樣。如果施羅德抽了我的血，跟在金斯理家的血跡比對，一定相符，只是他沒有理由要取我的血液樣本。他沒有理由，因爲他不懷疑我了。他沒有理由拿布萊肯家的血跡來比對，他知道那是我的血。如果他現在拿我的血液跟我爹的比對……

en_text: It wouldn’t match, the monster says, so maybe it hasn’t gone quiet at all.
zh_text: 不相符，怪獸說，所以怪獸還沒眞的閉嘴。

en_text: How is that possible?
zh_text: 怎麼可能？

en_text: Come on, Eddie. You can figure it out. And Jack—he has no idea. Poor, poor Jack. You and your father are nothing alike and that makes me your very own creation.
zh_text: 拜託，艾迪。你想想就知道了。傑克——他可沒想到。可憐，好可憐的傑克。你完全不像你爹，所以我是你獨力創造出來的。

en_text: “Edward? Hey, Edward? You listening to me?” “Huh?” I focus back on Schroder. “What?”
zh_text: 「艾德華？喂，艾德華？你聽到我說什麼了嗎？」「嗯？」我把注意力放回施羅德身上。「什麼？」

en_text: “I’m telling you there are other things to consider here. Nat and Diana know the full story. They know you didn’t start this . . . war. But . . . Edward, this is hard, but they don’t want you to see them again. Other than the . . . funeral, they want you out of their lives. Forever.”
zh_text: 「我說，還有其他的事情要考慮。納森跟黛安娜已經知道發生了什麼事。他們知道不是你挑起這場……戰爭。但……艾德華，我不知道該怎麼說，他們不想再看到你了。等到……葬禮過後，他們要跟你斷絕往來。」

en_text: “Am I free to go now?” “I guess.”
zh_text: 「我可以走了嗎？」「可以。」

en_text: “Then I want to see Sam,” I say, and Schroder drives me to the morgue.
zh_text: 「那我想看看小珊。」施羅德開車送我去停屍間。

en_text: “This is all very unusual,” he says.
zh_text: 「有點奇怪吧。」他說。

en_text: “It’s an unusual situation.”
zh_text: 「這情況原本就不尋常。」

en_text: “Well, yes, I suppose it is, but it’s Christmas Day, Detective, and on Christmas Day I don’t want to see patients. I want to spend it with my children. My ex-wife had them last Christmas, and this year it’s my turn.”
zh_text: 「對，是啊，我猜你說得沒錯，但今天是耶誕節，探長，而且耶誕節我不收病人。我想陪孩子過節。去年前妻陪他們，今年輪到我了。」

en_text: “This won’t take long,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「一下子就好。」施羅德說。

en_text: Benson Barlow sighs. “Then you’d better come in,” he says.
zh_text: 班森·巴羅嘆了口氣。「那你進來吧。」

en_text: The house suggests that psychiatry pays well. There have to be four or five bedrooms in the place, it’s two years old at the most, and if Barlow lives here alone except for when he’s allowed the children, then it must be a very lonely place to live in. Barlow leads him through to a study where there are books arranged by size and color, and there’s a view of a gated swimming pool beyond the bay window that people with emotional hang-ups paid for. The sun is shining down hard on it. He can hear a couple of children laughing from somewhere in the house, and a TV going. Barlow looks different from the other day, he’s more like a real person and not a parody. He’s wearing shorts with about a dozen pockets and a polo shirt, and his limbs and scalp have reddened from the sun.
zh_text: 從房子看起來，心理醫生的收入還不錯。他家應該有四五間臥室，屋齡最多兩年，要是除了孩子來訪的時間以外，巴羅都只有一個人，住在這裡一定很孤單。巴羅領他走進書房，裡面的書按著大小和顏色排列，從凸窗看出去，外面有座裝了栅門的游泳池，蓋游泳池的資金想必也來自那些心理碰到障礙的人。外面的陽光依舊毒辣。他聽到屋裡似乎有兩個孩子的笑聲，也有電視的聲音。巴羅跟上次看起來不一樣，今天比較像眞人，而不像諷刺劇裡的人物。他身上的短褲有十幾個口袋，上半身配了一件馬球衫，四肢和頭皮都被太陽曬紅了。

en_text: “Take a seat,” Barlow says, and Schroder notices the study is laid out the same way he imagines Barlow’s office in town must be laid out. Barlow takes a seat behind the desk and leans back in his leather office chair. He picks up a pad and a pen, seems to realize his mistake, and puts them back down. He interlocks his fingers and rests his hands on his knees. Schroder sits opposite him in another leather office chair—thankfully not a couch. There are a couple of diplomas on the wall and some expensive-looking art. There’s a manual typewriter in the middle of an oak desk, both of which are perhaps from the fifties. There’s a closed laptop up on a shelf behind Barlow and a small cactus plant next to it.
zh_text: 「請坐。」巴羅說，施羅德注意到書房的擺設正符合他心目中想像巴羅城裡辦公室的樣子。巴羅坐到書桌後，靠在皮質辦公椅上。拿起紙筆後，似乎發現不安，又放下了紙筆。他十指交扣，把手放在膝蓋上。施羅德在他對面的皮質辦公椅上坐下——還好他不需要躺在沙發上。牆上有兩張證書和一些看似價格高昂的畫作。橡木書桌上有台打字機，桌子跟機器或許都來自五〇年代。巴羅背後的架子上有台闔起來的筆記型電腦，旁邊放了一小盆仙人掌。

en_text: “This is no doubt about Edward Hunter?” Barlow asks.
zh_text: 「你來，一定是因爲艾德華·杭特的關係吧？」巴羅問。

en_text: “You’ve been listening to the news?”
zh_text: 「你看新聞了嗎？」

en_text: “Yes. I heard what happened. He helped his father escape from the hospital, though I’m not sure why he would do such a thing. Edward despises his father.”
zh_text: 「看了，我知道發生了什麼事。他幫他父親逃出醫院，不過我不確定是爲了什麼理由。艾德華痛恨他父親。」

en_text: “Edward Hunter had his daughter kidnapped by the men who killed his wife.”
zh_text: 「殺死艾德華·杭特妻子的人把他女兒綁走了。」

en_text: “Oh dear,” Barlow says. “Oh no, the poor girl. And Hunter helped free his dad because he thought his dad could help find her?”
zh_text: 「噢，我的老天啊，」巴羅說，「太糟了，可憐的小女孩。杭特幫他爸爸逃獄，因爲他覺得老杭特可以幫忙找回女兒？」

en_text:
“Yes.”
“And did they?”
“They found her, but it was already too late,” Schroder says.
zh_text:
「找到了嗎？」
「找到了，但已經太遲了。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Too late? Oh . . . you mean . . . ,” he trails off.
zh_text: 「太遲了？噢···你的意思是···」他接不下去了。

en_text: “She was suffocated.”
zh_text: 「兇手把她扼死了。」

en_text: “You have the men who did it?”
zh_text: 「你找到兇手了嗎？」

en_text: “Jack Hunter found him first. It was just one man who killed her.” “And he killed him?”
zh_text: 「傑克·杭特先找到他。殺小珊的兇手只有一個。」「他殺了他？」

en_text: “Yes. But first he killed a man who used to assault him in prison, and now he’s looking for the rest. We picked up Edward this morning. He had his daughter with him. He had taken her to the cemetery to visit his wife, and then he took her to a motel to protect her. He was acting . . . well, I think he was acting like . . .”
zh_text: 「對。不過他先開槍殺了一個曾在監獄裡欺負他的人，現在他去殺其他人了。今天早上我們找到了艾德華。他把女兒帶在身邊。他帶她去墓地看他妻子，然後把她帶回汽車旅館去，想要保護她。他表現得就像···嗯，我覺得他表現得就像···」

en_text: “Like she was still alive?” Barlow asks.
zh_text: 「像他女兒還活著？」巴羅問。

en_text: “Yeah. I think so.”
zh_text: 「對，我就是這麼認爲。」

en_text: “You have any idea where Jack Hunter is?”
zh_text: 「你知道傑克·杭特跑到哪裡去了？」

en_text: “No. It’s why I’m here. I know you dealt with him all those years ago. Tell me, where do you think he may go?”
zh_text: 「不知道，所以我才來找你，因爲很久以前你也當過他的心理醫生。告訴我，你覺得他會去哪裡？」

en_text: “I think he’ll find the men responsible for killing his grand-daughter.” “Then where?”
zh_text: 「我想他會先去找殺害他孫女兒的同夥。」「然後呢？」

en_text: “I don’t know.”
zh_text: 「我不知道。」

en_text: “He stopped taking his medication.” “What?”
zh_text: 「他已經停止吃藥了。」「什麼？」

en_text: “When we searched his cell we found his meds. He hasn’t been taking them for days.”
zh_text: 「我們去搜牢房的時候，發現他的藥。他已經好幾天沒吃藥了。」

en_text: “Then if he can’t find the men he’s looking for, he’ll move on to what he knows best—killing prostitutes. He’s been in jail a long time, Detective, he’ll have desires. The sickness inside him—it will have desires. The problem is twenty years ago he was living two lives, and one of them he was protecting by killing women he didn’t think anybody would notice going missing. Now he doesn’t have that family life to retreat to, or to hide things from. He may go looking for prostitutes, but it’s doubtful he’ll restrain himself to only them. Anybody is fair game to him now, Detective, because he’s on the run and he knows being free is only a temporary thing. Damn it, why did he have to stop taking his medication!”
zh_text: 「那如果他找不到害死他孫女兒的壤人，他就會重來他的拿手好戲——殺妓女。探長，他坐牢很久了，他一定覺得不滿足。他心裡的病無法不滿足。問題在於，二十年前他過著雙面人的生活，爲了保護家庭生活，他殺死他覺得失蹤了也沒人注意的女人。現在他無法回歸家庭，不需要對家人隱瞞什麼。或许他會去找妓女當作目標，但很有可能他的對象不光是妓女了。任何人都有可能變成他滿足欲望的對象，探長，因爲他在逃亡，他知道自由也只是暫時的。可惡，他爲什麼把藥停了！」

en_text: “He stopped when Jodie Hunter was shot.”
zh_text: 「茱蒂·杭特被槍殺那天，他就停止吃藥了。」

en_text: “Yes, yes, I suppose that makes sense. Detective, don’t doubt that Jack Hunter heard voices, and he was intelligent enough to hide it, and to deal with it. He knew he had a sickness, and he knew if he stopped taking his medication that sickness, that desire, would come back. You may want to look at the man who stabbed Hunter in jail, you might find it was Hunter himself who organized it. Probably on the same day. He probably figured he could use his son to help him escape.”
zh_text: 「對，對，我覺得有道理。探長，不要懷疑，傑克·杭特聽得到聲音，他也很聰明，不告訴别人，想辦法自己處理。他知道他有病，他知道如果停止服藥，他的病，他的欲望就會回來。你可以去調查是誰在監獄裡刺傷了杭特，或许根本就是杭特自己安排的。說不定就在同一天。他早就想到能利用兒子幫他逃獄。」

en_text: “I’ll look into it,” Schroder says, not in the mood to bolster the shrink’s ego by telling him that’s exactly what happened.
zh_text: 「我會去調查。」施羅德說，他可沒心情告訴醫生事情發生的經過，那只會讓巴羅更自命不凡。

en_text: “Hunter is an intelligent man, Detective, and he’s still intelligent even off the meds—the difference is that when medicated, he can be controlled. Right now—well, right now he could be anywhere doing anything. Now that you have Edward Hunter in custody, I strongly suggest you let me see him. I told you he was a danger, and last night proved that. I should see him immediately. I can help him.”
zh_text: 「探長，杭特是聰明人，藥物不會影響他的智力——差別在於，服用藥物後他就能受控制。現在——唉，現在他哪裡都可以去，爱怎樣就怎樣。你現在拘留了艾德華·杭特吧？我建議你一定要讓我見他。我告訴過你，他很危險，昨晚已經證實了。我應該要立刻去跟他談話，我可以幫他。」

en_text: “He’s not in custody.”
zh_text: 「我們沒拘留他。」

en_text: “What do you mean? You said you picked him up with his daughter.” “And then we let him go. He lost his daughter, he was betrayed by his father, we couldn’t keep him after all that. None of this is his fault.” “You need to pick him up.”
zh_text: 「這話是什麼意思？剛才不是說找到他跟他女兒了。」「我們放他走了。他女兒死了，父親背叛他，我們怎麼能把他關在警察局裡？這些都不是他的錯。」「你得把他送回警察局。」

en_text: “Why?”
zh_text: 「爲什麼？」

en_text: “What kind of state was he in when you released him?”
zh_text: 「你讓他走的時候，他看起來怎樣？」

en_text: “He’s a defeated man. We dropped him off at his house. He’s not going anywhere. In fact I’m tempted to put a man on him just to make sure he doesn’t kill himself.”
zh_text: 「他垂頭喪氣。我們送他回家了。他不會出門。事實上我還想派人看著他，免得他自殺。」

en_text: “He’s certainly a candidate for that, but he’s also capable of something else. Edward Hunter is a man who holds grudges, Detective, and he’s a man who can justify those grudges in different ways. He may not go after the men who killed his wife, but what about the others?”
zh_text: 「他很有可能會自殺，但他也幹得出其他的事情。艾德華·杭特滿心怨恨，而且他會爲他的怨恨找到不一樣的理由。或许他不會追殺害死他妻子的人，但其他人呢？」

en_text: “Others?”
zh_text: 「其他人？」

en_text:
“From the bank. The bank tellers, the security guard, the media, even the police—anybody who has let him down could be a target.”
“He went to the security guard’s house.” “What? When?”
zh_text:
「銀行的人。出納員、警衛、媒體，甚至警方——讓他失望的人都有可能變成目標。」
「他去找過那個警衛了。」
「什麼？什麼時候？」

en_text: “Tuesday night. He got drunk and went there but nothing happened.” “And you didn’t think this was important enough to let me know?”
zh_text:
「星期二晚上。他喝醉了，跑到警衛家，就這樣而已。」
「你不覺得這很重要，應該要告訴我嗎？」

en_text: “I just told you.”
zh_text: 「我剛告訴你了。」

en_text: Barlow takes his hands off his knees and leans forward. “Listen to me very carefully, Detective. You have to go and pick him up. Nothing may have happened when he went to the security guard’s house, but his daughter was alive then. This man is a time bomb. Trust me, Detective, if there’s one thing I know about, it’s time bombs, and this one is about to go off.”
zh_text: 巴羅的雙手從膝蓋上抬起，他的身子往前靠。「探長，仔細聽好了。你一定要去把他帶回警察局。他去找警衛的時候或許什麼事都没發生，但那時候他女兒還沒死。這人是個定時炸彈。相信我，探長，要說我懂什麼，就是這些定時炸彈，而且艾德華這顆已經快要爆炸了。」

en_text: It’s evening when I get home. Kids are out playing in the street, riding new bikes and new skateboards, yelling and laughing, all is good in their world, all is right and happy and I envy each one of them.
zh_text: 到家時已是傍晚時分。孩子在街上嬉戲，騎新的腳踏車，溜新的滑板車，喧鬧大笑，他們的世界眞美好，好快樂，每一個人都讓我覺得好嫉妒。

en_text: Nothing has changed at all in the house. It’s more of a tomb than ever. I walk through the rooms touching things, the walls, the furniture, running my fingers over anything in my path. I sit on Sam’s bed for a while and I sit on my bed for a while and I sit in the living room for a while. It’s like last week all over again only worse. The unbelievable thing that could never happen has happened—again. I can’t even cry. I can’t do anything. I sit in the living room with a can of beer but I don’t open it. I stare at the TV but don’t turn it on. I pick at the stitching on a cushion until it comes apart. The kids outside grow quiet. The day gets darker and they all head inside, some of them bored already with their new gifts. I get up to turn on the light and at the same time somebody knocks on my door. I head over to it, part of me not wanting to answer it, but a bigger part hoping it’s the last bank robber, that he’s come armed and with the ability to help me join my wife and daughter.
zh_text: 家裡還是跟原來一樣。愈來愈像一座墳墓。我在房間中遊走，到處撫摸牆壁和家具，邊走邊用手指滑過所有的東西。我在小珊的床上坐了一會兒，在我自己床上坐了一會兒，然後在起居室坐了一會兒。感覺上個星期又重來了一次，而且更糟糕。令人無法相信的事卻一件一件成眞了。我連哭都哭不出來，什麼也不能做。我拿著啤酒坐在起居室裡，也不把啤酒打開。我瞪著電視，卻不想打開電源。我亂摳靠枕上的縫線，直到靠枕裂開。外面的小孩安靜下來了。天色已黑，他們都回家了，有些人已經玩膩了新禮物。我站起來開了燈，同時聽到敲門聲。我走向前門，我不想應門，卻又希望是最後一名銀行搶匪，他帶著武器來，能把我送走，跟我的妻子兒團聚。

en_text: I don’t recognize him. He’s been severely beaten and can hardly stand, but he’s managing to do so by leaning against the wall. My dad is behind him holding the shotgun. He’s still wearing the security guard’s clothes from the hospital, only now there are large bloodstains on them, mostly dry.
zh_text: 我認不出他是誰。他被狠揍一頓，站也站不住，只能靠牆勉強站著。我爹拿著霰彈槍站在他後面，他仍穿著醫院警衛的制服，只是上面沾滿了大塊的血跡，幾乎都乾了。

en_text: “I got you a Christmas present,” Dad says, and he pushes the man forward.
zh_text: 「我帶耶誕禮物給你了。」爹說，把那人推過來。

en_text: I look at my Christmas present, at the blood on it, the torn and bruised wrapping, and I’m sick at the sight of it. I feel no different looking at Dad.
zh_text: 我看著我的耶誕禮物，看著上面的血，看著那撕爛的包裝，我覺得想吐。看到爹的時候，我也覺得想吐。

en_text: “Please, Dad, go away. It doesn’t matter anymore. This is all over. I’ve lost everything and they’re going to put me in jail for setting you free and the truth is, the truth is . . . I just want this to be over. I want everything to be over.”
zh_text: 「爹，拜託你，走吧。我不在乎了。都結束了。我什麼都没有了，而且我把你放走，所以我要去坐牢，事實上，事實上···我只希望趕快結束。我只希望都趕快結束。」

en_text: “This is the man who shot Jodie. This is the man who started it all.”
zh_text: 「茱蒂就是他開槍打死的。這人就是罪魁禍首。」

en_text: I close my eyes for a few seconds and exhale heavily, tilting my head back, focusing on the loss of Jodie and Sam. I remember the way Jodie fell forward, her face before the gun exploded, where she thought the worst thing that was going to happen to her was skinned palms and knees. I can still feel the weight of Sam in my arms, lifting her from the floor of the slaughterhouse and carrying her outside.
zh_text: 我閉上眼睛，停了幾秒，然後重重地吐氣，把頭往後仰，專心思索失去茱蒂和小珊的過程。我記得茱蒂往前倒，槍響前她臉上的表情，她還以爲手掌跟膝蓋磨破皮就是最糟糕的結果了。我仍能感覺到把小珊抱在懷裡，把她從屠宰場的地上抱起來，抱著她走出去。

en_text: Then I focus on the man Dad brought me. An average-looking man I’d never have paid attention to in the past, maybe somebody who works at a gas station or repairs shoes, anything other than the man he truly is. His face has swollen up, his left eye closed, his right eye bloodshot. The edges of the duct tape covering his mouth are stained with blood. Dad pushes him again and he falls onto his knees in my hallway. His hands are tied behind him so tight they’ve turned purple. Dad steps inside and closes the door.
zh_text: 然後我定睛看著爹帶來的人。長相很普通，我以前應該從來不會注意到，或許在加油站工作，或許是鞋匠，而不是開槍殺人的銀行搶匪。他鼻青臉腫，左眼闔上，右眼充血。嘴上貼的膠帶邊緣沾滿了血。爹又推了他一下，他倒在我家的門廊上。他的雙手在背後緊緊綁住，緊到都發紫了。爹走進來，把門關上。

en_text: “I don’t care,” I say.
zh_text: 「我不在乎。」我說。

en_text: “Yes you do.”
zh_text: 「你很在乎。」

en_text: Yes. You do.
zh_text: 對，你在乎。

en_text: “I know,” I say.
zh_text: 「我知道。」我說。

en_text: “I got one of the others,” Dad says. “I made him suffer. I made this guy suffer too. I was going to kill him when, out of nowhere, I realized how selfish that would have been. I’m sorry about what happened to Sam, son, I really am—and Jodie.”
zh_text: 「我已經做掉了另一個人，」爹說，「我狠狠折磨他。這個人也被我搞慘了。我正要殺他，突然發覺我太自私了。兒子，我很難過小珊死了，眞的茱蒂的事也讓我很傷心。」

en_text: “And this will make it better? Killing him will bring her back?” “It’s not about bringing people back, son.”
zh_text: 「那這樣有用嗎？殺了他小珊會復活嗎？」「兒子，當然跟復活沒有關係。」

en_text: “You think it’s about feeding the monster?” “That’s what it’s always about.”
zh_text: 「你以爲怪獸覺得不滿足嗎？」「怪獸一定不會满足。」

en_text: “For you, maybe. But not for me.”
zh_text: 「或許你這麼覺得，但我沒有感覺。」

en_text: “This is the man who shot Jodie! Damn it, son, don’t you get that? This is the man who killed your wife. This is the path he took that got your daughter killed. My granddaughter.” He takes a step back so he’s out of range from the man, reaches into his belt, and drags out a knife about half the length of his forearm and hands it over to me. “Now do something about it!”
zh_text: 「這個人開槍殺了茱蒂！幹，兒子，你還不懂嗎？這人殺了你老婆。他走上這條路，害死了你的女兒，我的孫女。」他退後一步，退到碰不到地上那男人的地方，探手到腰帶裡，拉出有前臂一半長的刀子，然後把刀子遞給我。「快解決他！」

en_text: The man on my floor doesn’t even move. There’s a shotgun pointing at him and two sets of eyes and all he has the strength to do is look down.
zh_text: 地上的男人動也不動。一支槍對著他，兩雙眼睛瞪著他，他還有力氣，也只能讓自己靜靜垂著頭。

en_text: Do it! the monster says.
zh_text: 動手啊！怪獸說。

en_text: “No.”
zh_text: 「我不要。」

en_text: “It’ll help,” Dad says.
zh_text: 「你會覺得好過一點。」爹說。

en_text: Listen to him.
zh_text: 聽他的，動手吧。

en_text: “Listen to the monster,” Dad says, struggling to keep the gun pointed ahead while holding the knife. He starts to lower it. “It’s telling you to do what I say, isn’t it.”
zh_text: 「聽怪獸的話，」爹要舉著槍，又要拿著刀，有點站不穩，舉著刀子的手開始往下掉了。「怪獸要你聽我的話，對吧。」

en_text: “This isn’t the way it’s supposed to be. It’s Christmas Day. I’m going to spend it with Sam and Jodie.”
zh_text: 「結果不應該是這樣。今天是耶誕節，我應該要跟小珊和茱蒂在一起。」

en_text: “This is the way it’s supposed to be. You, him, the monster, none of you are supposed to be here.”
zh_text: 「不應該這樣。你，跟他，還有怪獸，你們都不該來。」

en_text: I step past them and out the door. There aren’t any kids in the street now. Nobody to watch. Christmas lights are flashing from behind windows and from on top of roofs, cars are hidden away in garages and parked up driveways and people are tucking themselves away for the night, tired from too much food, too much sun, too much running around visiting family members and chasing after children. Dad turns toward me. I wonder what Nat and Diana are doing tonight, whether their day has been broken up by small pieces of routine where, for one or two seconds out of every thousand, they forget what happened to Jodie and Sam, only to have it crash back down on them.
zh_text: 我穿過他們身邊，走到門外。街上已經沒有孩子了。沒有人可以看。耶誕節的燈節在窗後跟屋頂上閃閃發光，車子都藏在車庫裡或停在車道上，鄰居也準備好上床休息了，他們覺得累了，吃了太多，曬了太多太陽，到處拜訪親戚和追逐小孩。爹轉身走向我。不知道納森和黛安娜今晚有什麼計畫，他們今天有沒有很多雜事要做，或许會有那麼一瞬間，他們忘記了茱蒂和小珊的悲劇，然後血淋淋的事實又再度打擊他們。

en_text: “It’s in the blood,” Dad says. “Don’t you feel it? We’re the same, son. We’re blood men!”
zh_text: 「這是遺傳，」爹說，「你沒感覺到嗎？兒子，我們一模一樣。我們都是嗜血之人！」

en_text: “I keep telling you, Dad, we really are nothing alike. More than you’ll ever know.”
zh_text: 「爹，我說過了，我們一點也不像。你不懂，就是不像。」

en_text: “You’re wrong,” he says. “Listen to your voice, Edward,” he says, calling me by that name for the first time. “Take the knife. Let the voice guide you,” he says, and I take the knife from him. Killing the man inside, that’s not the way to go about bringing my family back.
zh_text: 「你錯了，聽那個聲音，艾德華，」這還是他第一次叫我艾德華。「把刀拿去，聲音會告诉你要怎麼說。」我接過刀子，殺死躺在地上那個人？也不能把我的家人換回來。

en_text: There’s another way.
zh_text: 還有別的方法。

en_text: He’s not so sure that taking Edward Hunter into custody is the right way to go, and he’s equally unsure whether leaving him alone is the way to go. Barlow warned him a few days ago and even though Schroder didn’t dismiss the man, he certainly could have paid more attention. He can’t ignore the fact that everything that has happened since that meeting, all the deaths, part of the responsibility for that sits with him. Not this time though—he’ll pick Hunter up and, no matter how bad he feels for him, he won’t let emotion get in the way. It’s Christmas Day and he’s about to pick up a man who’s lost his wife and daughter because a psychiatrist with a comb-over and an ex-wife and a nice pool told him so.
zh_text: 他不知道該不该拘留艾德華·杭特，但也不知道該不该丢下他一個人。巴羅幾天前就警告過他了，雖然施羅德把他的話聽進去了，還是應該更小心一點。自從巴羅來找他，就發生了不少事，死了好多人，他也應該要負責任。這次他不會大意了——他要去接杭特，不管他覺得這人有多可憐，也不會讓情感沖昏了頭。耶誕節，他要去把這妻女橫死的人拘留在警察局裡，只因爲梳著條碼頭、和妻子離婚、家有高級游泳池的心理醫生給他的告誡。

en_text: “Jesus,” he mutters. There has to be another way. Barlow agreed that if Schroder could get Hunter into custody, he would come and speak to him tonight and try to get a read on his mental condition. As for where Jack Hunter might go, Barlow had no idea.
zh_text: 「我的天啊，」他喃喃自語。應該有其他的方法吧。巴羅說，如果施羅德能拘留杭特，他同意今晚過來跟他談話，了解他的心理狀態。至於傑克·杭特會去哪裡，巴羅就不知道了。

en_text: “Justify it as not really an arrest,” Barlow had said to him on the way out the door, “but forced therapy. Give me two hours with him and I’ll give you some options. The alternative is to sympathize with him for everything that’s happened and do nothing, and if he kills himself or somebody else tonight then those ghosts are with you.”
zh_text: 「拘留，並不是逮捕，」巴羅送他離開，「還有，強迫他接受心理治療。讓我跟他談兩個小時，我就能建議其他的辦法。不然，你光同情他碰到了這些倒楣事，卻什麼都不做，要是他今晚自殺了，或殺了人，他們的冤魂都要你負責。」

en_text: Schroder is passing over the alternative and heading straight to Hunter’s house. Christmas Day isn’t exactly turning out the way he planned. Thankfully his wife has been good about it. She’s the kind of woman who puts things into perspective—and missing Christmas Day with her husband didn’t amount to much when compared to what Edward Hunter was missing.
zh_text: 施羅德決定聽從巴羅的忠告，直接往杭特家去。耶誕節跟他原本計畫的差了十萬八千里。還好他太太能夠體諒。她懂得顧全大局——老公不回家過耶誕節不算什麼，跟艾德華·杭特失去的一比就差多了。

en_text: There’s not as much traffic on the road as there was last night, but it’s still enough to hold him up as he drives through town. People in their teens and twenties are searching for somewhere to be, the bars and nightclubs catering to them. The streets are lit up with neon and fluorescents, and he can’t imagine anything worse than being nineteen years old again.
zh_text: 街上的車子比昨晚還少，但穿過市中心時他仍耽擱了一下。街上不少十幾二十歲的人無所事事，不知何去何從，也只有酒吧和夜店可以選擇。霓虹燈和日光燈照亮了街道，他心想，世界上最糟糕的事莫過於重回十九歲。

en_text: He reaches Edward’s house. There’s nothing peculiar about the way it looks, no cars parked up the driveway or out front, no broken windows, no open doors, but something about it gives him a bad feeling. Thirty seconds later that bad feeling is confirmed when he steps out of his car and sees the blood on the driveway. It leads toward the door. Two trails of it, one heading one way, the other coming back. He calls for backup. He hasn’t had great experiences of late entering people’s houses, but he goes ahead and enters this one.
zh_text: 到了艾德華家，看起來很正常，車道或外面都没有車子，窗戶好好的，門都關上了，他卻有種不祥的感覺。三十秒後，證實他的感覺沒錯，他下了車，看到車道上有血跡，一路滴到艾德華家門口。血跡有兩條，一條朝著裡面，一條朝著外面。他打電話請求支援。最近他敲別人門的結果總不太好，不過他還是進去了。

en_text: “I first made the newspapers when I was nine years old. I made them in every city across the country, most of them on the first page. I even made them internationally. In them I was black and white, blurred a little, my face turned in to my father’s chest, people surrounding us. From then on I was shown on TV, in magazines, in more and more papers, always the same photo. I never wanted any of it, I tried to avoid it, but the option wasn’t mine.”
zh_text: 「九歲時，我第一次上報。全國各地的報紙都登了我的消息，大多在頭版。我甚至也上了國外的報紙。照片是黑白的，有點模糊，我的臉靠著父親的胸膛，旁邊圍了很多人。然後我還上了電視、雜誌、其他的報紙，都是同一張照片。我根本不想曝光，我很想躲起來，但我無法選擇。」

en_text: I tell her this but she doesn’t seem interested. I tell her about my mum and my sister but the words go through her. Her eyes are closed and there’s blood all over her. Twenty minutes ago her life was much different, twenty minutes ago she was settling in for the night, a pile of DVDs on the coffee table and a Christmas tree full of blazing lights. I take the car toward town, traffic is thin, everywhere is shut. I’m wearing the clothes from the bank again, the ones with Jodie’s blood on them. I picked them up on the way. This is why I kept them, I realize now. For this moment.
zh_text: 我告訴她我的故事，她卻似乎聽不進去。我告訴她我媽媽跟姊姊發生了什麼事，她卻左耳進右耳出。她閉緊了眼睛，身上到處都是血。二十分鐘前，她的生活出現了巨變，二十分鐘前她已經準備好要睡覺了，咖啡桌上有一疊DVD，耶誕樹掛滿了輝煌的燈節。我往城外開去，路上的車子很少，所有的店都關了。我又穿上了銀行搶案那天的衣服，上面有茱蒂的血。出門前我抓了這件襯衫。我現在才明白，爲什麼我一直留著這件衣服，就是爲了這一刻。

en_text: “I was ten years old when the trial began. It was a circus. My mum was still alive, but my sister and me were struggling. Kids would tease us at school. At home, Mum was always yelling at us when she was sober, and crying when she was drunk, and whatever of those two states she was in, you always wished it was the other. Soon the pills and the booze took their toll, but not as quick as she wanted, and when they couldn’t finish the job she used a razor blade. I don’t know how long it took for her to bleed out. She might still even have been alive when we found her. I held my sister’s hand and we watched her pale body, the yelling and the crying gone now.”
zh_text: 「審判在我十歲的時候開始。整個過程吵吵鬧鬧。我媽那時還在，但我跟姊姊的生活很艱難。學校裡的同學會嘲弄我們。媽媽清醒的時候對我們大吼大叫，喝醉的時候就哭個不停，她清醒的時候我們希望她喝醉，喝醉的時候我們卻希望她清醒。藥物跟酒精很快就要奪走她的性命，但速度卻不如她期望的快，最後她覺得吃藥喝酒還不夠，用剃刀刀片自殺。我不知道要花多久血才會流乾。我們發現她的時候她可能還活著。我握住姊姊的手，一起看著母親蒼白的身體，她再也不吼了，再也不哭了。」

en_text: The woman is conscious enough to cry, the tears mingling with the blood. There’s a lot of blood but not a lot of damage. It’s all from a head wound. The thing about head wounds is they bleed. A lot. Blood has soaked into the seat, and the woman has wet herself, making it seem like there is much more blood in the footwell than there really is. I tell her about Belinda, about how my sister became a drug addict and died when she was nineteen.
zh_text: 她仍有知覺，哭了起來，眼涘混合了血漬。流的血雖多，她傷得卻不嚴重。只有頭上一個傷口。頭如果受傷了，就會一直流血。很多血。血滲進了座椅，她緊張到尿濕了，讓腳下的血看起來更多，比實際上還要多。我告訴她貝琳達的生平，我姊姊染上了毒癮，十九歲就死了。

en_text: “I was the last of my family,” I say. “Dad’s monster took them all away.”
zh_text: 「我家就剩我一個了，」我說，「爹的怪獸把他們全帶走了。」

en_text: I keep the car at a constant speed, obeying the law; Edward Hunter was a law-abiding citizen who never did anything wrong in the past and who is now about to correct his future. We reach the center of town. Last time I was here I was running from the police.
zh_text: 我保持平穩的車速，不超過速限；艾德華·杭特是守法的好市民，沒有犯罪紀錄，現在則要糾正他的未來。我們到了市中心。上次我在這裡的時候，正在逃避警方的追捕。

en_text: “There are people who think that I’m destined to be a man of blood too,” I say, “that the same blood runs through both of us. They’re wrong,” I say.
zh_text: 「有些人以爲我也注定要成爲嗜血之人，」我說，「因爲我跟我爹都有同樣的基因。他們錯了。」

en_text: He wasn’t even my father.
zh_text: 他甚至不是我父親。

en_text: And somehow here I am, your very own monster.
zh_text: 不知爲何我還是出現了，我是你創造的怪獸。

en_text: I speed up the car that used to belong to Oliver Church, a nice trajectory ahead now, and I hit the wall of glass and it showers everywhere, it rakes against the car, the world sounds full of screams and the car bounces up off the framework and bounces back down and I slam on the brakes but not before I’ve wedged two desks hard up against the counter. The alarm is instant. The two front tires burst. The front of the car crumples up and the engine stalls. No air bag goes off, but the seat belts stop us from flying out. I look over at my passenger and there are more tears and more blood and I’m pretty sure both of us know that things for her are about to get worse.
zh_text: 這台車本來是奧立佛·丘奇的，我踩下油門，劃出一條漂亮的弧線，撞上了玻璃，碎片如雨點般落下，擦過了車子，尖叫聲此起彼落，車身跳離了車架，又落回來，我用力踩煞車，但我已經把兩張桌子擠到櫃台邊了。警鈴立刻大作。兩個前輪都爆了。車頭變成一團廢鐵，引擎也抛錨了。沒有膨大的安全氣囊，不過我們被安全帶拉住了，沒飛出車子。我看看我的乘客，眼淚更多了，血也更多，我很確定我們兩個都知道，她要受的苦還沒完呢。

en_text: “He’s gone,” Schroder says.
zh_text: 「他不見了。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Maybe . . .”
“And he’s killed,” Schroder adds.
zh_text: 「也殺了人。」施羅德補了一句。

en_text: “Killed who?” Barlow asks.
zh_text: 「殺了誰？」巴羅問。

en_text: Schroder steps back outside. “Do you have an idea where he might go?”
zh_text: 施羅德走回屋外。「你覺得他會去哪裡？」

en_text: There’s silence on the other end of the phone for a few seconds. “The cemetery. It makes perfect sense. He’ll want to be with his wife. Who did he kill, Detective?”
zh_text: 電話那頭沉默了幾秒鐘。「墓地吧。很合理。他想跟妻子在一起。探長，他殺了誰？」

en_text: “I’ll call you back.”
zh_text: 「我再打給你。」

en_text: Schroder calls the station. He organizes a patrol car to go to Gerald Painter’s house, to the homes of the bank tellers, to the cemetery, even to Dean Wellington’s house. He calls Landry and fills him in on the situation. “You think Jack Hunter knew all along which bank teller was involved?”
zh_text: 施羅德打電話回警局，派了巡邏車去傑拉德·潘特家、銀行出納員家、墓地，甚至還派了台車去狄恩·威靈頓家。他撥了藍德里的電話，告诉他發生了什麼事。「你覺得傑克·杭特從一開始就知道出納員也涉案嗎？」

en_text: “Maybe,” Schroder says. “We need to find out.”
zh_text: 「或许吧，」施羅德說，「我們得查出來。」

en_text: The interview Schroder had with the bank teller yesterday was finished off by another detective. Because of all the events last night, nobody had the chance to get around to comparing all the details against each other. Another series of follow-up interviews have taken place over the last six hours, each bank teller difficult to get hold of on Christmas Day, each bank teller reluctant to help out, wanting to spend time with their families instead.
zh_text: 施羅德昨天偵訊銀行出納員到一半就中斷，另一名警探幫他結束了訊問。因爲昨天晚上實在太混亂，大家還來不及比對收集到的詳細資料。過去六小時內，他們又開始另一波偵訊，正值耶誕節，很難找到所有的銀行出納員，找得到的也不願意幫忙，因爲他們要和家人共度節日。

en_text: The problem is none of them can remember who loaded the dye packs.
zh_text: 重點是，沒有人記得誰放了染色包。

en_text: Schroder turns on the sirens and speeds back into town, the houses and cars passing by in a blur. Other police cars come toward him on their way to Hunter’s house. When he reaches the station he runs inside to the interrogation room where, ten minutes earlier, Kelvin Johnson was escorted into.
zh_text: 施羅德打開警笛，一路衝回市中心，路上經過的房子跟車子都變成模糊一片。其其他的警車朝著相反的方向開去，他們要去杭特家。回到警局後，他快步走向偵訊室，凱爾文·強森在十分鐘前就被送進來了。

en_text: “You’ve got one chance here to help yourself,” Schroder says, and Johnson, the only crew member of the gang who robbed the bank in custody—and now the only one still alive—doesn’t even look up from the interrogation table.
zh_text: 「我給你一個機會，你想清楚。」施羅德說，在銀行搶匪中，只有強森被拘留了現在也只有他還活著——強森低頭看著桌子，不肯抬頭。

en_text: “You know everybody else is dead, right? We found Zach Everest a few hours ago, and I just came from looking at Doyle’s butchered corpse,” he says, Lance Doyle being the last name on the list. “There was a lot of rage there, Kelvin, a lot of rage.”
zh_text: 「他們都死了，你知道吧？幾小時前我們找到了查克·艾弗瑞斯特，我剛剛才看到道以爾的屍體，他死得很慘，」道以爾是名單上最後一個人。「有人很氣，強森，他氣炸了。」

en_text: Kelvin says nothing.
zh_text: 強森仍不說話。

en_text: “And we know somebody inside the bank was involved.” “You don’t know anything.”
zh_text: 「我們也知道你們在銀行裡有內線。」

en_text: “Actually I do. I know you’re going to jail. I know that you know Jack Hunter has been running around out there killing off your buddies. You know that he’ll be in jail soon too, right alongside you,” Schroder says, which isn’t quite true. “You know Jack Hunter has connections in there—he’s been there twenty years so he knows how the place works. You know his daughter-in-law and granddaughter are dead because of something you did, and you know that makes you a target. I know you’re going to end up in a jail cell real close to him, and I know your days in there are limited. So both you and I know that the only way you’re ever going to live long enough to see the outside world again is if you talk. You tell me who you had on the inside, and you spend your years in jail somewhere you never have to see Jack or Edward Hunter.”
zh_text: 「你知道個屁。」「我知道，我知道你要去坐牢。我也知道，你知道傑克·杭特正在到處跑，殺死你的同黨。你知道他很快就會回到牢裡，跟你一起吃牢飯，」施羅德信口開河。「你知道，傑克·杭特在牢裡認識不少人——他蹲二十年了，所以他明白坐牢是怎麼一回事。你知道，他媳婦跟孫女死了，都是你們害的，你也知道，你變成他的目標了。我知道，等你去坐牢的時候，你們的牢房就在隔壁，我也知道你坐牢不會坐很久。所以，你知道，我也知道，你想要活得夠久，再出來看外面的世界，就只能跟我說實話。你告訴我內線是誰，你坐牢的時候就不必碰到傑克或艾德華·杭特。」

en_text: “That’s bullshit,” Johnson says.
zh_text: 「聽你在放屁。」強森說。

en_text: “No. What that is is a fact. A one hundred percent fact. So what I’m going to do right now is I’m going to give you thirty seconds to think about it. You’re probably thinking that you’re a tough guy and can handle yourself in jail since you’ve done it before. But what you should be thinking about is the desire of two men in this world who right now want nothing more than to see you dead—men who may not be able to do the job themselves, but at least one of them can afford to pay to have it done.
