Thirty seconds,” Schroder says. “And counting.”
zh_text: 「不，我說的句句屬實。百分之百不騙人。所以我現在要給你三十秒，你好好想一想。或許你覺得自己夠硬氣，反正也坐過牢，你不怕。但你該想想，這世界上有兩個男人，他們很氣，只想置你於死地——或許自己下不了手，但至少有一個人付得起找人幹掉你的價格。三十秒，」施羅德說，「計時開始。」

en_text: “Marcy Croft,” Johnson says, with twenty-eight seconds still remaining. “Bracken paid her off. She was an easy mark. She needed the cash and she was new there and the plan all along was to shoot her anyway. Bracken wanted her taken out onto the street but instead we took that other woman, the wife.”
zh_text: 「瑪西·卡芙特，」還剩二十八秒，強森就吐露了。「布萊肯買通了她。她很容易上鉤。她需要錢，剛到銀行上班，我們本來就打算把她滅口。布萊肯本來要把她帶走，結果我們抓了另外那個女人，那個人的老婆。」

en_text: “Marcy Croft,” Schroder says, and he gets a mental picture of the bank teller. She’s the one who had the shotgun leveled at her. The one Jodie Hunter died for.
zh_text: 「瑪西·卡芙特。」施羅德說，心裡浮現出出納員的面孔。她就是被槍指著的女人。茱蒂。杭特代她犧牲了性命。

en_text: “Did she know people were going to die?”
zh_text: 「她知不知道會搞出人命？」

en_text: “She thought it was a simple thing. We’d go in and get the money and get back out. We told her nobody had to get hurt, and for what it’s worth that’s what I thought too.”
zh_text: 「她以爲很簡單。我們進去丶拿錢丶出來。我們告訴她不會有人受傷，我本來也以爲不需要傷人命的。」

en_text: “So why didn’t anybody try to kill her after the robbery?”
zh_text: 「搶案後怎麼沒人想到把她做掉？」

en_text: “Couldn’t risk it. If we’d touched her after the robbery, you’d have looked into why. You’d have made the connection.”
zh_text: 「太危險了。如果後來我們把她做掉，你們就會調查爲什麼，就會查出來有內線。」

en_text: “You weren’t worried she’d talk to the police?”
zh_text: 「你們不擔心她會透露給警方？」

en_text: “No. Bracken rang her cell phone about ten minutes after the robbery. Told her that if she spoke to the cops he’d kill her and everybody she loves.”
zh_text: 「不。搶完銀行後，布萊肯打她的手機。說如果她敢告訴條子，他就殺了她，還有所有她愛的人。」

en_text: “Did Bracken shoot Jodie Hunter?”
zh_text: 「茱蒂·杭特是布莱肯殺的？」

en_text: “No. Bracken didn’t even say a word in the bank.” “Did you shoot her?”
zh_text: 「不是，布萊肯在銀行裡一個字也沒說。」「你殺的？」

en_text: “No. It was Doyle.”
zh_text: 「不是，是道以爾開的槍。」

en_text: “Okay. That’s good, Kelvin. Real good. You can explain that to Hunter when you see him.”
zh_text: 「OK，很好，強森，非常好。見到杭特的時候，你自己跟他解釋吧。」

en_text: “What? You said . . .” “I lied.”
zh_text: 「什麼？你說過···」「我騙你的。」

en_text: “You son of a bitch,” he says, but Schroder hardly hears him as he closes the interrogation door behind him. He checks the messages on his phone. The cemetery was canvassed and no sign of Hunter. No sign of him at the security guard’s house. No sign of him at any of the bank tellers’ homes. No sign of him at Marcy Croft’s house.
zh_text: 「你個王八蛋。」施羅德早已關上偵訊室的門，沒聽到他的咒罵。他查了查手機訊息。墓地巡過了，沒看到杭特。警衛家也不見杭特蹤影。他沒出現在任何一個銀行出納員家裡。也不在瑪西·卡芙特家。

en_text: He gets in his car and chooses Croft’s house. He calls the detectives who spoke to her earlier today and they say she seemed nervous, but put it down to the events of the last week. There’s a patrol car parked outside her house.
zh_text: 他上了車，决定前往卡芙特家。他打電話給稍早跟她談過話的警探，他們說，她似乎很緊張，應該還受上星期的事件影響。她家門外停了一台巡邏車。

en_text: “Nobody home,” the officers say. “Our orders are to wait till she shows up.”
zh_text: 「家裡沒人，」警官說，「我們收到的命令是等她出現。」

en_text: Schroder knocks on the door anyway. When he finds her he knows she isn’t likely to put up a fight or any fuss. If anything she’ll break down in tears and beg for a forgiveness that isn’t his to offer. He tries the door. It’s unlocked. He opens it.
zh_text: 施羅德還是敲了敲門。等他找到她，他知道她不太可能抵抗。眞有什麼反應，她應該會大哭崩潰，祈求原諒，但他原諒她也沒用。他試試門把，沒鎖，他把門打開了。

en_text: Marcy Croft lives in a small two-bedroom flat with a flat-screen TV and a Christmas tree filling the living room with blood on the carpet and tipped-over furniture.
zh_text: 瑪西·卡芙特住在一間小小的兩房公寓裡，客廳裡有台平面電視和耶誕樹，地毯上有血，家具也倒了。

en_text: “He’s got her,” he says into the phone. “The bank teller.” “Explain it to me,” Barlow says, and Schroder does.
zh_text: 「他把她抓走了，」他對著電話說，「銀行的出納員。」「說清楚一點。」巴羅說，施羅德解釋給他聽。

en_text: “Does Hunter know the bank teller was in on the robbery?” Barlow asks.
zh_text: 「杭特知道出納員跟搶匪一夥的嗎？」巴羅問。

en_text: “Maybe. I don’t know. It’s possible. Jack Hunter may have known. He certainly knew other names.”
zh_text: 「可能知道。我也不曉得。很有可能。傑克·杭特或許已經知道了。他知道其他的搶匪是誰。」

en_text: “It doesn’t make sense,” Barlow says. “If Edward knew she was in on the robbery, he would have killed her already. You said he took her from her home?”
zh_text: 「沒道理啊，」巴羅說，「如果艾德華知道她也涉及搶案，應該早把她殺了。你說他從她家把她帶走了？」

en_text: “There’s sign of a struggle and blood on the carpet. Not much,” he says.
zh_text: 「有挣扎過的痕跡，地毯上有血。不多。」施羅德說。

en_text: “Okay. Let’s assume he didn’t kill her. Let’s assume he took her. What for? If he thought this woman was somehow partly responsible for the death of his wife and daughter, he would have killed her already. No reason for him to take her.”
zh_text: 「好。那我們假設他沒殺出納員。假設他把她帶走了。爲什麼？如果他認爲出納員也要爲他妻子跟女兒的死負責，早就把她殺了。沒理由要把她帶走。」

en_text: “Well, he has her. No doubt there.”
zh_text: 「嗯，他眞的把她帶走了。」

en_text: “Yes, but why? Let me think . . . are you sure Jack Hunter knew about this woman?”
zh_text: 「對，但爲什麼？我想想……你確定傑克·杭特也知道出納員涉案嗎？」

en_text: “I never said I was sure. Could be either way.”
zh_text: 「我沒說過我確定。總有兩種可能。」

en_text: “Interesting,” he says, then doesn’t follow it up. Schroder can almost hear his thinking process. “This woman, he may have taken her for a different reason.”
zh_text: 「有意思，」他卻沒繼續解釋。施羅德感覺得到他正在努力思索。「這個女人，他把她抓走，或许有其他的理由。」

en_text: “What other reason is there?”
zh_text: 「什麼其他的理由？」

en_text: “It all started with her. This is the woman Edward called out to save. Don’t you see? When he saved her, he condemned his wife to death. That in turn condemned his daughter to death. He blames her, Detective, and if he’s in as fragile a state as I believe him to be, then he sees her as the catalyst for everything he’s lost. Maybe . . . yes, yes, maybe he thinks he can right the wrongs that have happened since then.”
zh_text: 「一切都從她起頭。艾德華駁斥搶匪，就是爲了救她。你懂嗎？他救了她，卻爲自己的妻子判了死刑。結果，他女兒也被判死刑。探長，他認爲是她的過錯，如果艾德華眞像我想的如此脆弱，他就會覺得出納員引發了這一連串事故，害他失去了一切。或许對了，對，或許他認爲他能改變这一切，修正所有的錯誤。」

en_text: “Right the wrongs? You mean he thinks that by killing her he can turn back the clock and save his family?”
zh_text: 「修正錯誤？你是說，他以爲殺了她，就可以扭轉時間，救回他的家人？」

en_text: “It’s possible. And if this is the case, then you’ll find he’s taken her to—” “The bank,” Schroder finishes, already running toward his car now. “Exactly.”
zh_text: 「有可能。果眞如此，你會發現他把她帶去···」「銀行。」施羅德接過他的話，立刻拔腿朝車子跑去。「沒錯。」

en_text: “Jesus,” Schroder whispers, and he turns on the sirens and races back into town.
zh_text: 「我的天。」施羅德輕聲說，他打開警笛，火速返回城裡。

en_text: I get out and move around the car. I open the door and drag the woman out. She’s confused. She’s scared. This is nothing new for her—she’s been confused and scared before, in fact she’s been confused and scared in this very place.
zh_text: 我下了車，走到另外一邊。我打開車門，把那女人拖出來。她滿臉疑惑。她很害怕。也不是什麼新鮮事了——她一直都很迷惑很害怕，事實上，就從這裡開始，她就覺得迷惑跟恐懼。

en_text: She stumbles and falls down and cuts her knees on the glass. She tries talking to me but I can’t hear her over the alarm. I can hear a few of the words and can fill in the rest of them myself. She’s telling me over and over that she’s sorry, but it doesn’t matter, not now. Her being sorry isn’t going to fix things. I pick her up and drag her to where she almost died last time. The bank alarm keeps going off, and I wonder if things would have worked out different last week if the alarm had gone off like this when the men came into the bank. I get her standing in the same place but when I let her go she collapses back into a heap. Everything is the same as the last time I saw it, only the people are missing. Same posters advertising low interest rates, pictures of happy people paying off twenty-five-year mortgages or borrowing money to buy a boat. The hole in the ceiling has been repaired, the broken office window replaced, the bullet holes in the wall plastered over and repainted, and all the blood cleaned up. No security guard, no front windows now, nobody with a shotgun. Nobody else to call out wait, to stop this woman getting killed, putting his own family in the firing line, nobody with cell phones to capture footage for the news.
zh_text: 她跌跌撞撞地下了車，倒在地上，被玻璃劃破了膝蓋。她開口說話，但警鈴蓋過了她的聲音。我聽到了幾個字，也能塡得滿空白的地方。她一直對我說她很抱歉，但沒關係了，現在不是道歉的時候。她覺得抱歉，也沒辦法解決問題。我把她拉起來，拖到她之前幾乎喪命的地方。銀行的警鈴響個不停，上禮拜那些男人進來的時候，如果警鈴也這麼吵，不知道結果會不會不一樣。我要她站在同樣的位置，但我一鬆手，她就癱軟在地上。一切看起來都跟上星期一樣，只是沒有人。同幾張廣告低利率的海報，滿臉笑容的人兒付清二十五年的貸款，或借錢買一艘船。天花板上的洞補好了，辦公室破掉的窗子換新了，牆上的彈孔塡了灰泥也重新粉刷，地上的血跡都清掉了。沒有警衛，沒有臨街的玻璃，也沒有拿著霰彈槍的人。沒有人大喊等一下，從搶匪手中救回這女人的性命，卻把自己的家人推上火線，也沒有人拿著手機在旁邊拍攝要賣給電視台的新聞。

en_text: “Try to stand up,” I say, but she doesn’t. I guess it’s okay. I can’t reenact everything. It’s not like I have a shotgun. Just a knife. It’ll all work out the same way. This woman for Jodie. For Sam. The woman is crying, sobbing hard now.
zh_text: 「給我站起來。」但她不肯站起來。沒關係吧，反正我也沒辦法重演所有的細節。我手上也沒有霰彈槍，只有一把刀。還是可以繼續。用這個女人換回茱蒂。換回小珊。她垂頭啜泣，哭個不停。

en_text: “It’s the only way,” I say.
zh_text: 「也只能這樣了。」我說。

en_text: Do it. Feel it. Feed the urge.
zh_text: 動手吧，好好感覺，感覺你的衝動。

en_text: I lean down over her. I hold the knife tightly.
zh_text: 我對著她彎下身子，刀子緊緊抓在手裡。

en_text: Come on, get it done.
zh_text: 来吧，動手吧。

en_text: There are footsteps on the broken glass, loud enough to be heard over the alarm. Detective Schroder comes to within a few meters of us, his palms raised to me. He studies the woman before focusing on the knife in my hand.
zh_text: 踩過碎玻璃的腳步聲響起，吵到連警鈴聲都蓋不住。施羅德探長來了，停在離我們幾公尺遠的地方，舉高手掌對著我。他看看地上的女人，然後又把注意力轉回我手上的刀子。

en_text: “Put the knife down, Edward.” He has to yell to be heard.
zh_text: 「艾德華，把刀放下。」他得放聲大吼，我才能聽得到。

en_text: I move behind her and hold it against her throat. She’s shaking and she’s warm and it’ll be over soon, it’ll be the way it was meant to be.
zh_text: 我移到她後面，用刀抵著她的喉嚨。她身子溫暖，一直顫抖，馬上就要結束了，馬上就要回歸正軌。

en_text: “I can’t,” I yell back.
zh_text: 「不行。」我吼回去。

en_text: “Please, please, help me,” the woman says, but her voice is low and I don’t think Schroder can hear her over the alarm.
zh_text: 「拜託你，拜託你，救我。」女人說，但她的聲音很低，我不覺得施羅德能聽到。

en_text: “Edward, put down the knife.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，把刀放下。」

en_text: “Why are you even here? You weren’t here last time.” “I’m here because I don’t want anybody else to die.”
zh_text: 「你爲什麼在這裡？上次你就不在。」「我在這裡，因爲我不希望再有人死掉。」

en_text: “How come you got here so fast? Last week nobody showed up for five minutes, this week you’re here within seconds. It’s not fair.”
zh_text: 「你怎麼這麼快就到了？上星期等了五分鐘才有人來，這星期你幾秒鐘就到了。不公平。」

en_text: “I know what you’re trying to do,” Schroder says. “And it won’t work. You can’t fix the past, Edward. I know you called out to save this woman and she lived and Jodie died and then Sam died, but you can’t bring them back.”
zh_text: 「我知道你想幹嘛，」施羅德說，「沒用的。沒辦法改正過去的錯誤，艾德華。我知道你見義勇爲，救了這個女人，所以她活下來，茱蒂死了，然後小珊也死了，但你沒辦法把她們換回來。」

en_text: “All I have to do is make sure it never happened,” I say. “All I have to do is never call out.”
zh_text: 「我只能確保這件事從未發生過，」我說，「我只能閉上我自己的嘴巴。」

en_text: “There aren’t any takebacks in this world, Edward. No resets.” “Doing this will make everything the way it was supposed to be.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，這個世界無法重來，不能再來一次。」「我現在動手了，一切就會回復正常。」

en_text: “I wish it were that easy, Eddie, I really do. Life would be so much easier. But it isn’t. It is what it is, and killing her won’t bring Jodie or Sam back.” “I know it won’t. It will stop them from ever being hurt.”
zh_text: 「艾迪，我眞希望有那麼簡單。眞的，我們都會好過一點。但沒辦法。已經這樣了，殺了她也不會讓茱蒂和小珊復生。」「我知道她們不會回來，但她們會覺得快樂一點。」

en_text: “Listen to yourself.”
zh_text: 「你知道你滿口傻話嗎。」

en_text: Listen to me. Kill her. It’s in your nature. It’s who you are.
zh_text: 聽我的。殺了她。你本性如此。你就是這種人。

en_text: “Is this what you want?” he carries on. “To become your dad?”
zh_text: 「你要這樣嗎？」他又說了。「要跟你爹一樣嗎？」

en_text: Daddy’s a ghost.
zh_text: 爸爸變成鬼了。

en_text: “I’m nothing like him.”
zh_text: 「我跟他不一樣。」

en_text: “You keep telling me you hate what he is, that you hate the rest of us for thinking that you’ll become him.”
zh_text: 「你一直說，你恨他殺了那麼多人，你恨大家認爲你會變得跟他一樣。」

en_text: “I’m nothing like him,” I repeat.
zh_text: 「我跟他不一樣。」我又說了一次。

en_text: “Take a look at yourself.”
zh_text: 「看看你自己。」

en_text: “This isn’t about any of that. It’s not about what my dad was.”
zh_text: 「兩件事沒有關係。這跟我爹是誰沒有關係。」

en_text: “You’re right, Edward, you’re absolutely right. This here—this is about you. It’s about what you’re doing, about what you’ve already done. You think you’re nothing like your father, but look at what you’ve done tonight. The man who killed Jodie, you got him, Edward. You really, really got him.”
zh_text: 「艾德華，你說對了，你說得很對。這件事——這件事只跟你有關。看看你在做什麼，还有你做了什麼。你以爲你跟你父親不一樣，但看看今天晚上你做了什麼。那個殺死茱蒂的男人，你把他整死了，艾德華。你眞的讓他死得很慘。」

en_text: “I’m glad I killed him,” I say, and it’s true. I’m a trader in death.
zh_text: 「我很高興我殺了他。」我說，眞的，我就是拿一命換一命

en_text: “And your father? Are you glad you killed him too?”
zh_text: 「那你父親呢？你殺了他也很高興？」

en_text: “He betrayed me,” I say of this man who was never my father either way, certainly not for the last twenty years, and certainly not now. “He used me. He used Jodie. All of my suffering was a tool to him. So yeah, he deserved it too.” I can still feel the knife going into his chest, can still see the look on his face. I can still feel Belinda’s arm around me as we sat on the bathroom floor staring at my mother in the bathtub all those years ago. Blood bubbled up out of my father’s mouth instead of words and I thought I could hear air hissing out of the wound in his chest as he stumbled back from the front door of my house into the hallway, he stumbled and fell, and the darkness my father spent his life with finally claimed him. The man he brought to me looked up, and there was hope in his eyes, keen hope that sparkled as bright as a diamond and then just as quickly faded to coal when I put the same knife that had been inside my father into him as well. I put that knife in over and over and when I wanted to stop I couldn’t, not right away.
zh_text: 「他背叛我，」這人不是我父親，過去二十年來不是，現在當然也不是。「他利用我。他利用茱蒂。我的痛苦，變成他的工具。對，沒錯，他活該。」我仍能體會刀子插進他胸膛的感覺，仍能看到他臉上的表情。就像多年前我跟貝琳達坐在浴室地板上瞪著浴缸中的母親時，她用手臂環著我的感覺仍然不減。血從父親口中咕嚕咕嚕冒出來，他說不出話了，當他從我家前門倒向走廊，我覺得我能聽到空氣從他胸上的傷口嘶嘶逸出，他站不住了，倒下去了，陪伴我父親一輩子的闍黑終於把他帶走了。他帶來的男人抬眼看我，眼神中流露出希望，如鑽石般明亮閃耀的熱切希望，但我把插進我父親身體的同一把刀插在他身上的時候，鑽石很快就褪色成煤炭。我捅了他一刀又一刀，當我想要停下來的時候，我的手卻不聽使喚。

en_text: “It’s over, Edward. You need to let her go and come with us.”
zh_text: 「結束了，艾德華。讓她走吧，跟我回局裡。」

en_text: “I can fix this,” I say, and Schroder goes blurry and I realize I’m crying. “I can fix this.”
zh_text: 「我可以改正這一切，」我說，施羅德的身影變得模糊，我才發現自己哭了。「我可以解決問題。」

en_text: “No. You can’t.”
zh_text: 「不行，你不行。」

en_text: Yes you can, Eddie. Drag that knife back quick and deep and things will be better, much better.
zh_text: 你可以的，艾迪。拿刀子快快劃過去，用力插下去，一切都會變得更美好。

en_text: “Don’t be your father,” he says. “Put down the knife. Let her go. She didn’t do anything to hurt you. You saved her life, you did what nobody else had the courage to do, and the rest of it, none of it is your fault. You didn’t kill Jodie, you didn’t kill Kingsly, you didn’t get Sam killed. You’re a good man trying to do the best he can in a world that’s taken everything away from him. Don’t take everything away from her,” he says, nodding toward the bank teller. “Is this what Jodie would want of you?” he asks.
zh_text: 「不要跟你父親一樣，」他說，「把刀子放下。讓她走吧。她什麼都沒做。你救了她的命，你比其他人都更有勇氣，其他的事情都不是你的錯。茱蒂不是你殺的，金斯理不是你殺的，小珊也不是你害死的。你是好人，你只想盡自己的努力，但這個世界奪走了你的一切。別讓她也失去一切，」他對銀行出納員點點頭。「你覺得，茱蒂會希望你殺了她嗎？」他問。

en_text: My body tightens and I squeeze my eyes shut, only for a second, only long enough to picture my wife falling forward out on the street. In that same second I picture the rest of our lives together, before and after, the life we lived and the life we were supposed to live. I picture Sam.
zh_text: 我全身緊繃，緊緊閉上眼睛，只閉了一秒，只來得及在腦海中描繪我妻子向前倒在街上的樣子。也在那一秒內，我想到事件前後我們的生活，我們曾有過的生活，以及我們規劃的未來。小珊也浮現在我的腦海裡。

en_text: “I really don’t know,” I say.
zh_text: 「我真的不知道。」我說。

en_text: “I don’t think she would,” Schroder says. “I very much doubt she wants you to kill in her name, especially somebody who never hurt you. I think she wants what she always wanted from you—to be nothing like your father.”
zh_text: 「我不認爲她會贊成，」施羅德說，「我眞不覺得她會希望你用她當藉口來殺人，尤其是殺一個從來沒害過你的人。我想她一直對你有個期望不要變成跟你父親一樣。」

en_text: I lower the knife and open my hand.
zh_text: 我垂下刀子，鬆開手掌。

en_text: What are you doing?
zh_text: 你在幹什麼？

en_text: I’m not sure what I’m doing. The blade hits the floor, chips the linoleum, and falls on its side. I step back from the woman. She had no strength earlier, but she finds it now to crawl away from me as fast as she can. Two officers come out of nowhere and scoop her up and help her outside. Another two officers move in right behind Schroder, their guns raised and pointing at me. There are patrol cars outside that I didn’t even notice pull up.
zh_text: 我不知道我在幹什麼。刀鋒撞到塑膠地板，留下了缺口，然後躺在地上。我後退，拉開我跟那女人之間的距離。她剛才一點力氣也沒有，現在卻有力氣盡快從我身邊爬開。兩名警官不知道從哪裡冒出來，将她一把抱到外面去。又有兩名警官出現在施羅德身後，舉槍對著我。外面不知道什麼時候停了好幾台巡邏車。

en_text: There’s another way to be with Sam and Jodie. Pick the knife back up.
zh_text: 還有一個方法能跟小珊和茱蒂團聚。把刀子撿起來。

en_text: “What?”
zh_text: 「什麼？」

en_text: “Huh?” Schroder asks.
zh_text: 「你說什麼？」施羅德問。

en_text: Pick it up and attack them. Make them open fire. You’ll be with Sam and Jodie again. It will all be better. If you’re going to be a pussy for your entire life and ignore everything I want, then put us both out of our misery. Grab that knife.
zh_text: 把刀子撿起來，攻擊他們。讓他們開火。你就能跟小珊還有茱蒂在一起。那就太棒了。如果你一輩子都這麼懦弱，都不管我想要什麼，那乾脆讓我們兩個一起脱離苦海吧。把刀子拿起來。

en_text: I look down at the knife. Schroder watches me look down at it and comes forward.
zh_text: 我低頭看著刀子。施羅德注意到我的視線，大步走過來。

en_text: “Ain’t going to happen,” he says, and he kicks it away. “It’s the easy way out,” he says. “You think it’s what Jodie and Sam would want you to do?”
zh_text: 「想都別想，」他把刀子踼開。「那倒是最簡單的辦法，」他說，「你覺得茱蒂和小珊會贊成嗎？」

en_text: I don’t have an answer. He spins me around and handcuffs me and a minute later I’m in the back of a patrol car heading toward my future. Hell, maybe it was even my destiny. Edward the Hunter. I think of the men who wolf-whistled at me at the prison yesterday, I think of seeing the Christchurch Carver, of meeting Theodore Tate. What’s left of the accountant in me tries to calculate what kind of jail time I’d have to do, but fails. The city should be rewarding my monster for what it did, not locking it away. I watch the bank grow smaller behind me, knowing I’m nothing like my dad, knowing I have a monster of my own, a monster that is growing inside me, making me wonder what it’s going to ask of me when I’m back on the outside again.
zh_text: 我沒有答案。他轉過我的身子，幫我戴上手銬，一分鐘後，我被送上巡邏車後座，奔向我的未來。混蛋，或许這就是我的命運。艾德華獵殺手。我想到昨天在監獄裡對我吹口哨的人，我想到基督城屠夫，或许我會遇見泰奧多·泰特。心中的會計師開始計算我該坐幾年的牢，但算不出來。這座城應該要獎賞我的怪獸，而不是把它關起來。身後的銀行愈來愈小，我知道我跟我爹不一樣，我知道我的怪獸不是來自遺傳，怪獸愈變愈大，讓我忍不住思索，等我出獄後，怪獸會期待我怎麼表現。
